manilla-mt-borah.events: 10th FAI Paragliding World Championship (2007, 150 pilots from 41 countries); Manilla XC Camp (February), state hang gliding championship (February–March), State of Origin (Easter), Weekend Warrior summer series; 335 km world distance record (G. Wenness, 1998)
pros: World-class XC over the plains
Four takeoffs — flyable in almost any wind
School and accommodation right by the mountain
Good for both students and XC pilots
cons: Summer heat and very powerful thermals
Far from big cities
Road closes in the rain
Hardly any flying in winter
manilla-mt-borah.airport: TMW — Tamworth, ~50 min; SYD — Sydney, ~5 h
manilla-mt-borah.tandem_price_note: 30–40 minutes, temporary SAFA membership included; tandems from October to March
school_notes: Tandems, residential PG2 course (9+ days, 2,890 AUD, 2026/27), thermal clinics 770 AUD, cabins by the mountain from 25 AUD a night

stanwell-park-bald-hill.description: Bald Hill above Stanwell Park beach is Australia's legendary coastal takeoff, an hour's drive from Sydney: soaring along the Illawarra cliffs and landing on the sand by the lagoon. This is where Lawrence Hargrave experimented with box kites, and today hang gliders, paragliders and tandems from several schools fly here.
stanwell-park-bald-hill.rating_basis: A world-famous coastal hang gliding and paragliding takeoff above a beach near Sydney; strict club rules, Intermediate rating
stanwell-park-bald-hill.hazards: Rotor off the spurs in strong southerly or easterly wind, cloud forming quickly over takeoff in spring and autumn, strong wind on the downslope takeoff (a spotter is needed), crowded beach at landing, airspace shared with hang gliders
stanwell-park-bald-hill.crowd_note: Crowded at weekends: hang gliders, paragliders and tandems in the same corridor; a flight management plan was introduced after a collision in 2000
stanwell-park-bald-hill.region: Illawarra, New South Wales (40–45 km south of Sydney)
stanwell-park-bald-hill.season: year-round in southerly and easterly winds; more flyable days in spring and autumn; in winter westerly (offshore) winds are common
stanwell-park-bald-hill.transfer: ~50 minutes by car from Sydney airport; Stanwell Park railway station
stanwell-park-bald-hill.takeoffs: The Point — the main grass takeoff in front of the main car park (winds from SSW to ESE); East Launch behind the café — for easterly wind (~190 m). Coordinates are for the top of Bald Hill
stanwell-park-bald-hill.wind_note: Coastal ridge lift in winds from SSW to ESE; ~5–15 knots for paragliders; in strong southerly or easterly wind, rotor off the spurs; in spring and autumn cloud forms quickly over takeoff (“white-out”)
stanwell-park-bald-hill.best_time: Flown throughout the day in a steady sea breeze; on weekends and public holidays a Duty Pilot is on takeoff
stanwell-park-bald-hill.access: By car along Lawrence Hargrave Drive to the Bald Hill Lookout, with parking by the takeoff; ~1 h from central Sydney
stanwell-park-bald-hill.xc_note: Coastal soaring along the Illawarra escarpment; practically no cross-country flying
stanwell-park-bald-hill.rules: Membership of SAFA (full or Visiting Overseas Pilot) and of the FlyStanwell club or another NSWHPA club is mandatory; a briefing from a club or school safety officer is mandatory before your first flight; Intermediate / PG4 site — PG2 pilots only under supervision, with a streamer and a UHF radio (SAFA 2); helmet and connected speed bar are mandatory; tandems land only on the beach, no top landing; no flying over the car park and takeoffs
stanwell-park-bald-hill.landing: Bottom landing “The Chute” — the sand by the northern lagoon between the park and Stanwell Park beach (no landing on the park lawn); emergency landing at the southern end of the beach; top landing for PG4 pilots on “The Strip”, west of the monument
stanwell-park-bald-hill.events: Stanwell Park Festival of Flight (November), honouring aviation pioneer Lawrence Hargrave
pros: Close to Sydney
Beautiful coastal soaring above the beach
Several schools and tandem operators
Drive right up to takeoff
cons: Strict club rules and mandatory SAFA membership
Crowded at weekends
Landing on a busy beach
Needs wind straight off the sea
school_notes: SAFA school, training tandems at Bald Hill and Hill 60, courses
Tandems and PG2–PG5 courses at Bald Hill and Hill 60
School, chief instructor Martin Wysocki
Training south of Sydney

sopot-bulgaria.description: Sopot is Bulgaria's main paragliding centre, on the southern slope of the Stara Planina: a chairlift runs from the landing field by the monastery up to a spacious south-facing takeoff at ~1,400 m. It hosted the 2013 FAI World Championship; in spring and summer pilots fly 100–200 km XC routes along the ridge, and local schools offer inexpensive tandems, training and guiding.
sopot-bulgaria.rating_basis: Bulgaria's most popular site, the 2013 FAI World Championship, a lift to takeoff, a big easy takeoff and XC of up to 200 km; downsides — the lift doesn't always run, and military restrictions
sopot-bulgaria.hazards: Very strong spring thermals, thunderstorms in May, northerly wind over the ridge (rotors), no-landing zones in the valley
sopot-bulgaria.crowd_note: Lots of foreign groups in summer and during competitions, but the takeoff is spacious
sopot-bulgaria.season: The most reliable months are April–October (very strong thermals in spring and thunderstorms in May, gentler in summer); late autumn and winter have some good days, tandems fly on any flyable day of the year
sopot-bulgaria.transfer: Plovdiv ~1 h (60 km), Sofia ~2 h (140 km); buses and trains to Karlovo (5 km) and Sopot
sopot-bulgaria.takeoffs: The main south-facing grass takeoff, ~1,340–1,400 m (easy, plenty of space); the east and west takeoffs are tighter, for experienced pilots. Backup site — Beklemeto (further west; soaring only, in northerly wind)
sopot-bulgaria.wind_note: Flyable in S, E and W wind; strong northerly wind over the Stara Planina makes the takeoff unflyable — then pilots drive to backup sites 1–2 hours away
sopot-bulgaria.best_time: Thermals from late morning; very strong in spring (April–May), 5–6+ m/s, gentler and smoother in summer
sopot-bulgaria.access: Chairlift from the landing meadow by the monastery (~2 km from Sopot) to takeoff; when the lift isn't running, local guides drive you up the road
sopot-bulgaria.xc_note: Routes along the Stara Planina ridge east towards Kazanlak: regular 100+ km triangles and out-and-returns, FAI triangles of up to 200 km, open distance of up to 205 km (to the Black Sea); cloud base ~2,300 m
sopot-bulgaria.rules: No takeoff fees; there's a military air base ~40 km away — in spring and autumn the airspace is sometimes closed for up to a week; the valley sometimes hosts military exercises and has “sensitive zones” where landing is forbidden — check with local pilots. Licence and insurance are mandatory
sopot-bulgaria.landing: Large meadow by the chairlift bottom station and the monastery (~550 m), with parking and a free campsite nearby
sopot-bulgaria.events: 13th FAI Paragliding World Championship (13–26 July 2013, 147 pilots, won by Jérémie Lager); regular open championships and British Paragliding Cup rounds (2023, 2025)
pros: Lift to takeoff
Big, easy takeoff and landing field
100–200 km XC along the ridge
Low prices for accommodation and tandems
cons: The lift sometimes doesn't run
Military air base and exercises in the valley
Strong northerly wind shuts the takeoff
sopot-bulgaria.airport: PDV — Plovdiv, ~1 h; SOF — Sofia, ~2 h
sopot-bulgaria.tandem_price_note: Skynomad: 15–25 min panorama tandem €60, acro €70, XC flight of up to an hour €80; other operators charge ~120 leva for 15 minutes
school_notes: Training, XC guiding (FLARM trackers, retrieves), tandems €60–80
Contact from the Cross Country Magazine guide
Tandems in Sopot and Varna: 120 leva for 15 minutes, acro 140 leva

governador-valadares-ibituruna.description: Pico da Ibituruna is a “black” granite massif 1,123 m high, rising almost 900 m above the Rio Doce and the city of Governador Valadares. It's one of Brazil's top XC sites: World Championships in 1994 and 2005, World Cup Superfinals, gentle wide thermals and a flat valley full of fields to land in.
governador-valadares-ibituruna.rating_basis: The “world capital of free flight”: World Championships in 1994 and 2005, PWC Superfinals, gentle thermals and >80% flyable days
governador-valadares-ibituruna.hazards: Heat and overdevelopment; morning and evening downpours in summer; there have been serious accidents at competitions — care is needed when the air is crowded with pilots
governador-valadares-ibituruna.crowd_note: The takeoffs are big (125 pilots launch in ~30 minutes); crowded only during competitions
governador-valadares-ibituruna.season: Flyable year-round (historically more than 80% flyable days); best for XC and competitions January–May, with a peak in February–March according to AVLI; the dry winter (June–August) is more stable and cooler, but thermals are weaker
governador-valadares-ibituruna.transfer: The city airport has daily Azul flights; 320–340 km (~4–5 h) from Belo Horizonte on the BR-381/BR-116, and there's a Belo Horizonte–Vitória train and intercity buses; 35 minutes from the city to takeoff
governador-valadares-ibituruna.takeoffs: Two big grass takeoffs on the summit — north and south (plus wooden ramps); chosen by wind, they work in almost any direction
governador-valadares-ibituruna.wind_note: Wind is usually light, 8–12 km/h; the N/NE and S/SE takeoffs suit almost any direction. Thermals are wide and smooth, rarely stronger than 3–4 m/s; hot sunny days with little turbulence
governador-valadares-ibituruna.best_time: XC pilots launch closer to midday; tandems fly from morning to evening
governador-valadares-ibituruna.access: 16 km (~35 minutes) from the city centre on a paved road — any car will make it; hotels and restaurants along the road
governador-valadares-ibituruna.xc_note: Competition tasks average ~75 km; the claimed site record is around 250 km (almost to the Rio de Janeiro state border); PWC Superfinals have had more than 90% flyable days
governador-valadares-ibituruna.rules: The takeoff is run by the Ibituruna Free Flight Association (AVLI), while the city council manages the area and flight control in the city; visiting pilots should contact AVLI and have a licence and insurance
governador-valadares-ibituruna.landing: The official city landing field Feira da Paz (144 m) by the Rio Doce, plus the Municipal Park (168 m) and the Carrapato and Geraldo Farias fields; plenty of fields along XC routes
governador-valadares-ibituruna.events: FAI Hang Gliding World Championship (1994), FAI Paragliding World Championship (2005), PWC Superfinals (2014 and 2017), a PWC round (April 2026); regular Brazilian Championship rounds since 1983
pros: Flyable almost year-round
North and south takeoffs — almost any wind works
Gentle thermals, easy landings
Paved road to takeoff
cons: Hot (30–35 °C in summer)
Far from major international airports
Little information in English
governador-valadares-ibituruna.airport: GVR — Governador Valadares, ~20–30 min; CNF — Belo Horizonte, ~4–5 h
governador-valadares-ibituruna.tandem_price_note: Price on an aggregator (operator Voar 360): ~15 minutes, transfer, insurance and 360° video; booking directly with local pilots is usually cheaper
school_notes: Tandems with transfer, insurance and 360° video
The local club that runs the takeoff

quixada-urucum.description: Quixadá, in the arid sertão of Ceará state, is the world capital of straight-line distance: granite inselbergs, a strong trade wind and cloud base up to 3,500 m let pilots fly 200–300 km downwind to the west. World tandem records and FAI records have been set here, but conditions on takeoff are tough — this is a site for experienced XC pilots.
quixada-urucum.rating_basis: A legendary site for world distance records (Cross Country: “record arena”), but the tough conditions are for experienced pilots only
quixada-urucum.hazards: Gusts of more than 50 km/h on takeoff and landing; landing far from roads in the hot sertão (water, a hat and sunscreen are a must); boggy green fields and sharp stubble in harvested ones; poor phone coverage
quixada-urucum.crowd_note: Outside the record season (November) there are few pilots — in December you can fly almost alone
quixada-urucum.season: Dry season July–December; best for record distances October–November (strongest wind, cloud base ~3,500 m), December is gentler; June–July bring shorter routes and calmer flights; February–April is the rainy season
quixada-urucum.transfer: ~160 km (~2.5–3 h) from Fortaleza, two buses a day; after a long XC flight pilots often spend the night where they landed and return by bus
quixada-urucum.takeoffs: The competition takeoff on Urucum mountain by the Nossa Senhora Imaculada sanctuary (~470 m; a wooden ramp for hang gliders and a dirt area for paragliders) and the Pedra dos Ventos takeoff (~537 m) above the hotel of the same name, ~15 km away
quixada-urucum.wind_note: Strong E–SE trade wind: in October–December gusts regularly exceed 50 km/h; pilots launch with helpers in short 10–20-second lulls. After 15:00 the wind eases, and in the evening there's sunset soaring. From September to January the wind on takeoff can be too strong
quixada-urucum.best_time: Record flights launch early in the morning (hotel breakfast from 5:00); after 15:00 ~100 km is still realistic; calm soaring in the evening
quixada-urucum.access: The ramp is ~12 km from Quixadá along a partly cobbled, partly paved road up the mountain; the Pedra dos Ventos hotel drives its guests to takeoff for free
quixada-urucum.xc_note: The world's arena for straight-line distance: typical flights of 200–300 km west along the roads (Quixadá–Quixeramobim–Tauá–Picos or Quixadá–Nova Russas–Pedro II); FAI record of 285.4 km (free distance via 3 turnpoints, Frank Brown, 7 August 2025); world tandem record of 335.4 km to a declared goal (1 November 2015)
quixada-urucum.rules: The launch window is set by the launch director; a SPOT tracker is recommended (the hotel owner keeps track of pilots during the day); hire a helper on takeoff (a few dollars a day) and a retrieve driver. Experienced pilots only
quixada-urucum.landing: Landing near takeoff/in the valley (~300 m); along the route, sertão fields: green fields may be swamp, harvested ones have sharp corn stalks; strong wind on landing too
quixada-urucum.events: Annual record camps in October–November (X-Ceará / Mundial de Voo Livre); national competitions since the 1990s; world tandem records and FAI records
pros: Flights of hundreds of kilometres almost every day in season
Record-flying infrastructure: pilots' hotel, helpers, retrieves
Few people outside November
cons: Very strong wind on takeoff — experienced pilots only
Heat up to 40 °C, remote semi-desert terrain
Poor roads and long retrieves
Few tandems and schools
quixada-urucum.tandem_price_note: According to the local press (2022), around R$200 for a “try a flight” at the ramp by the sanctuary; tandems are rare here, so check in advance
school_notes: Pilots' hotel by the takeoff, owned by a hang glider pilot; breakfast from 5:00, free rides to takeoff, tracker monitoring
Pilot tours for the record season
Local free flight organisation

rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.description: The Pedra Bonita takeoff at ~520 m in Tijuca National Park is a classic Rio postcard: a flight over the rainforest to São Conrado beach with views of Pedra da Gávea and the city. It's one of the world's busiest tandem sites, while pilots get the rare but legendary days of the “route to the Christ statue”.
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.rating_basis: One of the most famous views in paragliding — a flight over Rio, the beach and the Tijuca forest; a huge stream of tandems, but for pilots only local flights and strict rules
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.hazards: Low cloud at takeoff; limited landing options; wires if flying low over the city; rotor behind apartment buildings; heavy tandem traffic and jostling on takeoff
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.crowd_note: In high season more than 200 tourist tandems a day; marshals manage the queue on takeoff, and tandems often push in
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.region: São Conrado, Rio de Janeiro — Tijuca National Park
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.season: Flyable year-round; the dry half of the year (April–October) has more stable flyable days, summer (December–March) is hotter with more thunderstorms and rain; the best conditions come right after cold fronts
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.transfer: ~45–60 minutes from Galeão airport, ~30–40 minutes from Santos Dumont to São Conrado; many operators pick you up from your hotel
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.takeoffs: A wooden ramp for hang gliders above the paraglider launch area (~507–520 m); there are no other takeoffs
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.wind_note: The takeoff faces the ocean above São Conrado beach and works on the sea breeze and slope thermals; the best conditions are usually from 9:00 to 14:00 and right after cold fronts pass through (often in cloudy weather). The “route to the Christ” needs easterly wind and cloud base of at least 800 m
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.best_time: Tandems from 8:00 to ~16:00, most often in the morning; local soaring over the beach all day when the wind is right
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.access: 20 minutes by taxi or bus from Ipanema/Copacabana to São Conrado; you drive up to takeoff on the road through the Tijuca forest (pilots get a lift from the club by the landing field); parking at takeoff, with a trail to the summit of Pedra Bonita nearby
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.xc_note: The classic is the technical ~30 km out-and-return “to the Christ”: along the mountains above Rocinha and Leblon to Corcovado and back to the beach; it works on about 30 days a year, mostly in spring and summer after a cold front. Cloud base is usually 800–1,500 m
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.rules: Visiting pilots must register with the São Conrado Free Flight Club (CSCVL, office by the landing field), show their licence and pay for temporary (day) membership; documents are also checked on takeoff. ABVL rules for visitors: a limited number of visiting pilots per day (20 each for paragliders and hang gliders), mandatory insurance, access to takeoff by ticket and a strict queue
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.landing: Praia do Pepino beach (São Conrado) right in front of takeoff, at sea level; paragliders can also land on the grass area to the right of the beach, next to the club office where you get your day pass. Backups — the racecourse or other beaches; there are few landing options
pros: Incredible views of Rio, the ocean and the forest
Landing on a city beach
Flyable year-round
Lots of certified tandem pilots
cons: Expensive tandems by South American standards
Queues and crowds of tandems
Strict rules and limits for visiting pilots
Few landing fields
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.airport: GIG — Rio de Janeiro (Galeão), ~45–60 min; SDU — Santos Dumont, ~30–40 min
rio-de-janeiro-pedra-bonita.tandem_price_note: Around R$880–999 with photos and video, plus an R$100 São Conrado club fee; hotel transfer often included. The flight itself lasts 7–15 minutes
school_notes: The club that runs the takeoff and landing field: visiting pilot registration, weather station
The association that certifies tandem pilots at Pedra Bonita

golden-mount-seven.description: Mount 7 above Golden is Canada's best-known XC site: a takeoff almost 1,200 m above the Columbia Valley, powerful summer thermals and long flights down the valley between the Rockies and the Purcell Mountains. Every summer it hosts the Canadian championships and the legendary Willi competition.
golden-mount-seven.rating_basis: Cross Country and the local club: Canada's top XC site — high cloud base, 100–230 km routes down the valley, national championships and the long-running Willi competition
golden-mount-seven.hazards: Thunderstorm gust fronts of up to 70 km/h far down the valley; strong southerly wind can stop you reaching the landing field; landing in a neighbouring valley can mean a two-day walk out; trees around the takeoffs
golden-mount-seven.crowd_note: Busy only in July, during the championships and the Willi
golden-mount-seven.region: Golden, British Columbia — Columbia Valley between the Rockies and the Purcell Mountains
golden-mount-seven.season: May–October (sometimes into November): the lower takeoff in May, Lookout from June; peak July–September; in winter the site is practically closed (snowmobile access only)
golden-mount-seven.transfer: ~260 km (~3 h) from Calgary on the Trans-Canada Highway; rental car or intercity bus; ~14 km uphill from Golden to takeoff
golden-mount-seven.takeoffs: Lookout (1,942 m, the main one): north dirt takeoff facing NW, west ramp facing SW, south dirt takeoff facing SE; lower takeoff “9k” (1,560 m) — in spring, mostly for hang gliders; upper takeoff (2,310 m) — ~40 minutes on foot, opens later in summer; heli-drops to remote takeoffs
golden-mount-seven.wind_note: Strong mountain thermals — up to 8–12 m/s in summer, average cloud base ~4,000 m with surrounding peaks at 2,600–2,900 m; XC flights run 2,500–3,000 m above the valley floor. The mountain microclimate makes forecasting tricky; strong southerly wind can stop you reaching the landing field
golden-mount-seven.best_time: In summer, during the day in thermals; gentle soaring in the evening. Thunderstorms with gust fronts of up to 70 km/h in the afternoon
golden-mount-seven.access: The main takeoff is ~14 km up a logging road from Golden, passable for 2WD (usually opens in June once the snow has gone); no regular shuttle — pilots give each other lifts, and in summer you can hitchhike
golden-mount-seven.xc_note: Most flights head south down the valley: the classic is 146 km to Canal Flats, XC beginners manage 60–80 km; the site's flight log shows 231 km (July 2023); only a handful of pilots have crossed the Rockies past Lake Louise and Banff to Canmore. No airspace restrictions below 5,500 m
golden-mount-seven.rules: Landing at the Nicholson fields requires signing a waiver and the rules, plus valid HPAC (Hang Gliding & Paragliding Association of Canada) insurance for all pilots and tandem instructors; retrieve box key $25 and a $25 contribution to the reserve fund; a radio and a 30 m rope for tree extractions are recommended
golden-mount-seven.landing: The main landing field is the Golden Riverfront campground (Nicholson, LZ #1, 790 m), ~10 minutes from Golden, private with a full campground; LZ #2 — Skyview ranch (commercial tandems by permission); backup — the gravel pit
golden-mount-seven.events: The “Willi”, Canada's longest-running XC competition (the 30th edition — 26 July–3 August 2026); Canadian Paragliding Championship (4–8 July 2026) and Hang Gliding Championship (18–25 July 2026)
pros: 100–230 km XC routes down a scenic valley
High cloud base and no airspace restrictions below 5,500 m
Takeoff reachable in an ordinary car
Landing field at a campground
cons: Short season
Strong, rough thermals, thunderstorms
No schools in Golden — tandems only
Tricky forecasting due to the mountain microclimate
golden-mount-seven.tandem_price_note: Altitude Adventures / Golden Tandem Paragliding: tandem with photos and transfer to takeoff; flights from late May to October
school_notes: Tandems from Mount 7 from late May to October, transfer and photos included
Takeoff and landing coordinates, rules, fees, competition calendar

fiesch-kuehboden.description: Fiesch in the upper Rhône valley is one of the best XC sites in the Alps. A gondola takes you up to Kühboden (2,100–2,250 m), right below the Eggishorn and the Aletsch Glacier, and the long Rhône valley allows huge triangles of up to 300 km. Tandems fly here year-round, while solo pilots get powerful alpine thermals and strong valley wind.
fiesch-kuehboden.rating_basis: World-class XC (Cross Country calls the valleys around Fiesch “highways”, triangles of 200–330 km), a gondola to takeoff, views of the Aletsch Glacier; a bit too demanding for beginners
fiesch-kuehboden.hazards: Powerful (“nuclear”) summer thermals, strong valley wind on landing, foehn and bise, rotors behind spurs on the western section, northerly wind from the Grimsel, airspace of the Sion and Münster airfields
fiesch-kuehboden.crowd_note: On good days in May–July lots of XC pilots on takeoff and in the air; queues at the gondola for hang gliders
fiesch-kuehboden.region: Upper Valais (Oberwallis), Aletsch Arena, Rhône valley
fiesch-kuehboden.season: Tandems year-round; XC season May–August (best May–July); in winter, tandems from the ski slopes
fiesch-kuehboden.transfer: By train ~3 h from Zurich, ~3 h from Geneva, ~2 h from Bern (via Brig); ~2.5 h from Milan Malpensa via the Simplon
fiesch-kuehboden.takeoffs: Kühboden: Heimat ~2,140–2,250 m (morning, ~10 min from the gondola), Galfera 2,170 m (afternoon, 10–15 min), Kühboden Chalet 2,197 m (tandems only); nearby Riederalp 1,900 m, Bettmeralp, Bellwald — Steibenkreuz 2,400 m
fiesch-kuehboden.wind_note: South-facing slope above the Rhône valley; no flying in bise (NE) or foehn (S); strong valley wind in the afternoon (often >20 km/h); heading east, you're hampered by northerly wind from the Grimsel Pass (the “Grimselschlange”)
fiesch-kuehboden.best_time: In the morning, the Heimat takeoff and calm tandems; XC pilots launch around midday; in the afternoon, Galfera and strong thermals, with rough valley wind on landing
fiesch-kuehboden.access: Fiesch–Fiescheralp gondola to Kühboden station, then a 10–20-minute walk; hang gliders go up in a separate cargo cabin (queues possible)
fiesch-kuehboden.xc_note: One of the main XC sites in the Alps: “highways” along the Rhône valley west towards Sion and east towards Goms; on the best days, FAI triangles of 200–300+ km (up to ~330 km according to Cross Country); popular for the 200 km triangle league
fiesch-kuehboden.rules: Switzerland: national licence/IPPI card and mandatory liability insurance. Landing field maintenance fee — CHF 5 a day or CHF 20 a year (you also get a rules brochure). Ceiling 3,950 m when the military zone is active (MIL on), 4,500 m when inactive; heading west, the Sion airfield TMA (request clearance by radio), heading east, the Münster airfield rules for gliders; up-to-date info at flyland.ch and skybriefing.com
fiesch-kuehboden.landing: The official landing field in Fiesch (~1,050 m) by the Rhône valley; strong, gusty valley wind during the day — come in with height to spare
fiesch-kuehboden.events: According to Cross Country, Fiesch has hosted world championships
pros: World-class XC flying
Gondola to takeoff, several takeoffs for different times of day
Views of the Aletsch Glacier
Tandems year-round
cons: Strong thermals and valley wind — not for beginners
Complex airspace
Expensive and far from airports
fiesch-kuehboden.airport: ZRH — Zurich, ~3 h; GVA — Geneva, ~3 h; MXP — Milan Malpensa, ~2.5 h
fiesch-kuehboden.tandem_price_note: Flyingcenter Oberwallis: 15/30/45 min, from CHF 150 excluding the gondola ticket; Aletsch Arena from CHF 130; flights year-round
school_notes: Tandems from Fiescheralp, Bettmeralp, Riederalp and Bellwald, year-round
Tandems over the Aletsch Arena

interlaken-amisbuehl.description: Interlaken is the world capital of tandem flying: takeoffs above the village of Beatenberg, a flight over Lakes Thun and Brienz with views of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, and a landing on the Höhematte meadow right in the centre of town. Tandems fly year-round, and there are dozens of operators. Solo pilots get several takeoffs at 1,100–1,950 m, but strict local rules and complex airspace.
interlaken-amisbuehl.rating_basis: One of the world's most popular tandem sites: landing in the centre of the resort, views of the Jungfrau, Eiger and Mönch, dozens of tandem pilots and flights year-round
interlaken-amisbuehl.hazards: Helicopter routes and heliport zones; strong valley wind during the day; afternoon thunderstorms in summer; heavy tandem traffic; a shooting range by the Lehn landing field
interlaken-amisbuehl.crowd_note: Book ahead in July–August; on a clear day there are 5–20 paragliders over the valley at once, and tandems and solo pilots share the takeoff according to the rules
interlaken-amisbuehl.region: Bernese Oberland, between Lakes Thun and Brienz
interlaken-amisbuehl.season: Tandems year-round; best season May–September (September is one of the best months); fewer flights in winter, only on good days
interlaken-amisbuehl.transfer: Zurich–Interlaken by train ~2 h; Bern ~50 min; Geneva ~2 h 45 min; operators pick you up from hotels in Interlaken
interlaken-amisbuehl.takeoffs: Above Beatenberg: Amisbühl upper 1,325 m and lower 1,310 m, Chalet 1,310 m, Bergbo 1,290 m, Hohwald 1,585 m, Luegibrüggli 1,060 m; Niederhorn 1,953 m (funicular + gondola, light wind only); Breitlauenen 1,580 m (Schynige Platte railway)
interlaken-amisbuehl.wind_note: The slope above Interlaken faces south; flown in light wind and in thermals during the day; strong upper wind and NW wind mean turbulence, and in strong bise don't launch on the lee side; during the day, unstable NW conditions bring strong valley wind
interlaken-amisbuehl.best_time: Tandems all day (calmer in the morning; in summer morning slots are better, as thunderstorms come in the afternoon); in winter flights are mostly in the middle of the day, around 15:00
interlaken-amisbuehl.access: PostBus from Interlaken to the Waldegg stop (Beatenberg), then a ~20-minute walk; tandem operators drive passengers up; Niederhorn — Beatenberg funicular and gondola
interlaken-amisbuehl.xc_note: XC routes along Lakes Thun and Brienz and towards Grindelwald are possible in summer, but the airspace is complex (helicopter routes, Meiringen air base)
interlaken-amisbuehl.rules: Switzerland: foreigners need a national licence/IPPI card and mandatory liability insurance. The Amisbühl takeoff has a “special rule”: tandems only by PGI and Deltaclub Interlaken (DCI) schools; Friday to Sunday, solo pilots have priority; solo pilots use the left launch strip, tandems and hang gliders the right. Visiting schools register on the DCI website (CHF 40 a day). The Lehn landing field costs CHF 2 for non-DCI members. Stay out of the purple zones and helicopter corridors (Interlaken and Gsteigwiler heliports); Meiringen zone status on 0800 496 347
interlaken-amisbuehl.landing: Höhematte (568 m) — a big meadow right in the centre of Interlaken, between the hotels; backups — the airfield (the field with four white dots; clear the field immediately) and Lehn (565 m, by the shooting range)
pros: Views of the Jungfrau and two lakes
Landing in the centre of town, everything close by
Tandems year-round, wide choice of operators
Easy takeoffs
cons: Expensive (it's Switzerland)
Crowded in summer, booking needed
Complex airspace and rules for solo pilots
Afternoon thunderstorms in summer
interlaken-amisbuehl.airport: ZRH — Zurich, ~2 h by train; BRN — Bern, ~50 min
interlaken-amisbuehl.tandem_price_note: Standard flight of 10–20 min with transfer (Paragliding Interlaken, Skywings); photos/video ~CHF 40, double flight time +CHF 90
school_notes: Tandems from Amisbühl from CHF 190, landing on the Höhematte; they fly in winter too
Tandems from CHF 190
Tandems
Tandems

iquique-alto-hospicio.description: Iquique is a port city in the Atacama Desert, squeezed between the ocean and a 500-metre coastal escarpment: a steady Pacific breeze and dry weather give almost 360 flyable days a year. The classic is a flight from Alto Hospicio over the city and its high-rises, landing on Cavancha beach.
iquique-alto-hospicio.rating_basis: Cross Country: around 360 flyable days a year, laminar breeze, a beach landing in the city centre; regular FAI-2 competitions
iquique-alto-hospicio.hazards: Wind and thermals strengthen after midday; late in the day you may not make it over the Cerro Dragón dune; rotors near the mountains along XC routes; northerly wind; airport no-fly zone; heat (~30 °C) if you have to walk back across the dune
iquique-alto-hospicio.crowd_note: The takeoff is big (room for ~150 pilots), and the air is usually uncrowded except during competitions
iquique-alto-hospicio.season: Year-round — on average only about 7 unflyable days a year; best October–March (southern summer); in winter (June–August) thermals are weaker, but people still fly and even go cross-country
iquique-alto-hospicio.transfer: Diego Aracena airport is ~40 km south, ~40 minutes to the city by taxi or shuttle; ~15 minutes from the centre to takeoff
iquique-alto-hospicio.takeoffs: Alto Hospicio (490 m) — the main takeoff on the edge of the coastal range above the city; the Cerro Dragón dune (~175–220 m) right in the city — soaring and training; further south, Patillos (170 m, ~45 min) and Alto San Marcos (602 m, ~1.5 h), plus beach dunes for ground handling (Palo Buque)
iquique-alto-hospicio.wind_note: West-facing takeoffs working on the Pacific breeze and slope thermals; wind is usually 8–25 km/h and picks up along with the thermals by 13:00. Don't fly in northerly wind; don't fly if you can see waves breaking far out to sea
iquique-alto-hospicio.best_time: Beginners and tandems as early in the morning as possible; experienced and XC pilots during the day and towards evening; people fly until sunset. Thermals 2–6 m/s; in October–December flights of 7–10 hours are possible
iquique-alto-hospicio.access: The takeoff is ~15 minutes from the centre: city bus 121 or 3B from the market on Barros Arana street, or a shuttle; parking at the top
iquique-alto-hospicio.xc_note: XC routes north and south along the coastal escarpment, as long as the rotors near the mountains allow; in 2025 a 123.8 km FAI triangle (almost 7 hours) was flown from Alto Hospicio
iquique-alto-hospicio.rules: The Diego Aracena airport zone south of the city is closed to flying; don't fly in northerly wind; ask local pilots about the current takeoff situation (the takeoff was temporarily closed in 2019)
iquique-alto-hospicio.landing: Prepared landing fields on the city beaches of Playa Brava and Cavancha; in the desert outside the city you can land almost anywhere, and there are almost 4 km of options on the Cerro Dragón dune
iquique-alto-hospicio.events: Open Iquique (FAI-2, October–November; a Pre-PWC in 2022); Pre-SRS Iquique 2026
pros: Flyable almost every day, year-round
Flight over the city with a beach landing
Laminar conditions, good for learning
Takeoff easy to reach by city bus
cons: Desert: heat and sand, little shade
Wind and thermals pick up noticeably after lunch
A long way to get there (via Santiago)
iquique-alto-hospicio.tandem_price_note: Usually 50,000–80,000 CLP; 10–30 minutes over the city with a beach landing, photos and video often included
school_notes: Flight park with accommodation south of the city, courses and a base for pilots
Tandems and training at a surf hostel, lead pilot Miguel Hernández

medellin-san-felix.description: San Félix is a mountain village on the ridge above the city of Bello and the Aburrá Valley, and the main tandem site near Medellín. An east-facing takeoff with a view over the whole city, 15–20-minute flights; flyable practically year-round.
medellin-san-felix.rating_basis: Colombia's most popular tandem spot, with views of Medellín and dozens of operators; for pilots, mostly local flights
medellin-san-felix.hazards: Wind that picks up quickly and gusts, rotor behind takeoff, venturi to the left; in January 2026 rescuers had to bring two pilots down from the slope after strong gusts, and in September 2026 there was a fatal tandem accident in strong wind. Choose reputable operators and fly in the morning
medellin-san-felix.crowd_note: Lots of tourist tandems, especially at weekends and on public holidays
medellin-san-felix.region: Bello (San Félix), Antioquia — above the Aburrá Valley
medellin-san-felix.season: Flyable year-round; drier and more stable December–March and June–July; April–May and October–November bring rain; August–September are windy, so people fly in the morning and evening
medellin-san-felix.transfer: ~1–1.5 h from Medellín airport (Rionegro); ~45 minutes from central Medellín
medellin-san-felix.wind_note: A big, safe east-facing takeoff above the Aburrá Valley and Medellín; rotor behind takeoff, a slight venturi effect to the left. From October to July wind is usually up to 30 km/h, in August–September up to 50 km/h — then people fly early in the morning or towards evening. Strong wind can build very quickly
medellin-san-felix.best_time: Book tandems for the morning — it's calmer and leaves time to reschedule; thermals and gusts during the day
medellin-san-felix.access: ~40–45 minutes from Medellín on the road to San Pedro de los Milagros: taxi/Uber or bus from the Terminal del Norte (Caribe metro station), get off at the El Voladero restaurant; many operators pick you up in the city
medellin-san-felix.xc_note: Mostly local soaring and thermalling over the slope; cloud base around 3,300 m, local XC is possible, but to the east there are restrictions due to air traffic over Medellín
medellin-san-felix.rules: Because of air traffic (Medellín airport), you may not fly east beyond the set boundaries; check the SIATA forecast before flying
medellin-san-felix.landing: A top landing by the takeoff (convenient) and the bottom landing at El Trapiche in Bello (~1,450 m); staying at the bottom landing after dusk is not recommended — the area is unsafe
pros: Close to Medellín, easy to get to
Inexpensive tandems
Views of the city and valley
Flyable almost year-round
cons: Wind can pick up sharply, gusts
Lots of tandems
There are more interesting places for XC (Roldanillo)
medellin-san-felix.tandem_price_note: From 200,000–220,000 COP for 15–20 minutes, photos and video usually included; transfer from Medellín costs extra
school_notes: Tandems of ~20 minutes, group transfer from Medellín
Office at takeoff (Estadero El Voladero, 2nd floor), airport transfer
Over 10 years in business, 15-minute tandems with photos and video

roldanillo-los-tanques.description: Roldanillo is a small town in the Cauca Valley, one of South America's top XC sites and host of the 2015 World Championship and a World Cup Superfinal. Gentle thermals, a flat valley with sugarcane fields to land in and an almost year-round season make it a favourite winter destination for pilots from Europe and the US.
roldanillo-los-tanques.rating_basis: Host of the 2015 FAI World Championship and a World Cup Superfinal; Cross Country: 100 km almost every day in season, gentle thermals and easy landings
roldanillo-los-tanques.hazards: Accidents every year from launching too early or in tailwind; power lines below takeoff; turbulence when the sea breeze arrives and rotors behind the mountains; smoke and turbulence over burning sugarcane fields; a quarry to the south with strong, rough climbs; flooding of the Cauca river
roldanillo-los-tanques.crowd_note: At peak season and during competitions, 100+ pilots at Los Tanques; the other takeoffs are quieter
roldanillo-los-tanques.season: Flyable year-round; the best windows are December–March and July–September; in the rainy seasons (April–May, October–November) about 60% of days are flyable
roldanillo-los-tanques.transfer: ~1.5 h by taxi from Pereira or Armenia (~€40); from Cali ~1.5 h by taxi or ~2 h by bus
roldanillo-los-tanques.takeoffs: Los Tanques (~1,800–1,900 m, the “competition” takeoff, jeep access only); El Pico (~1,850 m) and La Tulia — closer to town, by bus to the trail and a 15-minute walk, more often used by locals and tandems; a separate takeoff for hang gliders
roldanillo-los-tanques.wind_note: East-facing takeoff working on the anabatic flow (the thermal breeze reaches takeoff around 9:00). The background wind is usually light, from the N or S; in the morning there may be a westerly tailwind — wait for a steady upslope breeze. In the afternoon the Pacific breeze arrives from the west with gusts of up to 25–30 km/h
roldanillo-los-tanques.best_time: Launches from ~10–11 am; climbs up to 3–4 m/s, cloud base 1,800–2,300 m; once the sea breeze arrives, keep away from the western mountains
roldanillo-los-tanques.access: Los Tanques is ~45 minutes by jeep on a dirt road from the main square towards El Dovio; shared Willys jeeps leave from the Central Park around 8:45, once full. To El Pico and La Tulia, scheduled jeeps to the trailhead and a ~15-minute walk
roldanillo-los-tanques.xc_note: In season, ~100 km flights are realistic almost every day: “cat's cradle”, out-and-returns and triangles across the Cauca Valley; site record around 200 km; 2015 FAI World Championship and 2024/25 World Cup Superfinal
roldanillo-los-tanques.rules: Fly by international rules, with a helmet, radio and phone. Airspace limits: ~2,700 m (9,000 ft) to the south-east / south of Tuluá and ~3,000 m (10,000 ft) to the north. Don't land on vineyards or military bases
roldanillo-los-tanques.landing: The official landing field is the Roldanillo stadium / landing field (~950 m) by the town; the valley is flat sugarcane fields, so you can land almost anywhere; after rain the Cauca river can flood the fields
roldanillo-los-tanques.events: 2015 FAI Paragliding World Championship; Paragliding World Cup Superfinal (February 2025); regular FAI-2 open championships and national competitions
pros: Flyable almost year-round
100 km flights almost daily in season
Gentle climbs and easy landings in fields
Cheap accommodation (€15–30 a night)
cons: Afternoon Pacific breeze and turbulence near the western mountains
Limited airspace ceiling
Smoke from sugarcane burning
Modest tourist infrastructure
roldanillo-los-tanques.airport: PEI — Pereira or AXM — Armenia, ~1.5 h; CLO — Cali, ~1.5–2 h
roldanillo-los-tanques.tandem_price_note: From 190,000 COP for a tandem with a certified pilot from the La Tulia takeoff (April 2025)
school_notes: Pilots' hostel, daily rides to takeoff, local information
School and tours around Colombia
Tours and guiding for pilots
XC courses from Piedechinche (45 minutes from Roldanillo)

tegelberg-schwangau.description: Tegelberg above Schwangau is one of Germany's most popular flying sites: a cable car takes you up to ~1,720 m, and the flight passes over the fairy-tale Neuschwanstein Castle, Hohenschwangau and Lake Forggensee. There are several schools and tandem companies, and visiting pilots must follow clear local rules, including a mandatory briefing.
tegelberg-schwangau.rating_basis: The main takeoff has 5 stars on Paraglidingmap; a flight over Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau castles and Lake Forggensee; cable car to takeoff, several schools; strict local rules
tegelberg-schwangau.hazards: Rotor and a rock wall at the lower takeoff; the cable car wire close to takeoff (keep 150 m away); heavy tandem traffic
tegelberg-schwangau.crowd_note: A very touristy place: FLY Royal alone has around 4,000 tandem slots a year; lots of pilots on summer weekends
tegelberg-schwangau.season: Main season April–October; the cable car also runs in winter (except for maintenance from November to mid-December)
tegelberg-schwangau.transfer: Memmingen ~1 h; Munich ~2 h; Innsbruck ~1 h 30 min; train to Füssen, then bus to Schwangau
tegelberg-schwangau.takeoffs: The main takeoff by the Tegelbergbahn top station (~1,707–1,720 m): the upper one mostly faces NW, and in steady NE wind there's a NE option (after consulting the locals); the lower one is a narrow chute with rotor and a rock wall on the right; outside the ski season, takeoffs on the slopes of Grüble (1,507 m) and Rohrkopfsattel (1,308 m)
tegelberg-schwangau.wind_note: The northern edge of the Alps: the main takeoff faces NW, with a NE option in steady NE wind; check the wind and webcam on the Holfuy “Tegelberg Startplatz” weather station
tegelberg-schwangau.best_time: Tandems daily from about 10:30 to 15:30 in good weather; in good thermals, flights of 30 minutes or longer
tegelberg-schwangau.access: Tegelbergbahn cable car from Schwangau to the summit; the takeoff is by the top station; the cable car is closed for maintenance from 9 November to 17 December 2026
tegelberg-schwangau.xc_note: XC routes along the northern edge of the Alps through the Allgäu and towards the Tannheimer Tal in Tyrol on good spring and summer days
tegelberg-schwangau.rules: The Tegelberg flight rules (Flugbetriebsordnung) apply: visiting pilots need a briefing “green card” (issued by FLY Royal Paragliding) and must show their licence and liability insurance at the bottom station; after launching, stay at least 150 m from the cable car and the takeoff area; at least 10 m above roads; private (non-commercial) tandems are banned. At nearby Buchenberg, liability insurance of at least €1.5 million is required
tegelberg-schwangau.landing: The landing field is right by the access road to the Tegelbergbahn bottom station, with separate areas for paragliders and hang gliders; traffic is managed from the FLY Royal base, which has a bar by the landing field
tegelberg-schwangau.events: National and international hang gliding championships have been held here
pros: Flight over Neuschwanstein Castle
Cable car to takeoff
Good infrastructure: schools, bar at the landing field
Easy to reach from Munich
cons: Crowded in season
Mandatory briefing and document checks for visitors
The lower takeoff is technically demanding
tegelberg-schwangau.airport: FMM — Memmingen, ~1 h; MUC — Munich, ~2 h
tegelberg-schwangau.tandem_price_note: 15–30 min (Flugschule Tegelberg); FLY Royal charges €199; views of Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau castles
school_notes: Tandems €199, daily April–October; base with a bar by the landing field; issues the visitors' “green cards”; German, English, Spanish, French
Tandems from €169, paragliding and hang gliding courses; office in the bottom station

ager-montsec.description: The village of Àger below the Montsec ridge in the Catalan Pre-Pyrenees is one of Europe's top XC sites. From the main Coll d'Ares takeoff (around 1,550 m), pilots set off on long flights along the limestone ridges, and the valley has plenty of fields to land in. International paragliding and hang gliding competitions are held here regularly.
ager-montsec.rating_basis: The main Coll d'Ares takeoff has 5 stars on Paraglidingmap; Cross Country ranks Àger among Europe's best XC sites; regular international competitions
ager-montsec.hazards: Rotor at Coll d'Ares in easterly wind; westerly wind at Sant Alís and Gabriel·ló; strong summer thermals; limestone cliffs
ager-montsec.crowd_note: Lots of XC pilots and school groups in spring and summer; crowded during competitions
ager-montsec.season: Flyable most of the year; best XC season spring and summer (March–September), short flights on clear days in winter
ager-montsec.transfer: Barcelona — under 3 h by car; Lleida ~1 h
ager-montsec.takeoffs: The Montsec ridge above the Àger valley: the main upper takeoff Coll d'Ares (~960 m above Àger, S, very big, paved road, used for competitions); Sant Alís 1,586 m (SE, by the fire lookout); Raudoral 1,225 m (S, the lowest — the first to catch the valley breeze); Gabriel·ló (S, technical); Tablones 1,301 m — the backup when there's a northerly up high
ager-montsec.wind_note: South-facing takeoffs above the valley; Coll d'Ares tolerates a little westerly wind, but easterly brings rotor; don't use Sant Alís or Gabriel·ló in westerly wind; with a northerly up high, use the Tablones takeoff
ager-montsec.best_time: XC pilots launch around midday; calm flights in the morning and evening; Raudoral starts working on the valley breeze earlier than the others
ager-montsec.access: Paved road from Àger to the main Coll d'Ares takeoff; local schools and shuttles drive pilots up
ager-montsec.xc_note: One of Europe's best XC sites (Cross Country calls it one of the best places in Europe for hang gliding): the limestone ridges of the Pre-Pyrenees, legendary long-distance flights and numerous competitions
ager-montsec.rules: Spain: foreigners need a national licence/IPPI card and third-party liability insurance; respect airspace boundaries when going cross-country
ager-montsec.landing: Landing field by the campsite in the Àger valley (~500 m below the Raudoral takeoff); the valley has lots of fields for landing on XC flights
ager-montsec.events: Numerous hang gliding and paragliding competitions, including the Ager Women's Paragliding Open (2011)
pros: World-class XC
Big main takeoff with a paved road
Several takeoffs for different heights and winds
Open valley with fields to land in
cons: Car needed, far from major airports
Rough thermals in summer
Little information for tourist tandems

algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.description: The white village of Algodonales by Sierra de Líjar is Europe's main winter base for paraglider pilots. Four takeoffs at 890–1,000 m face almost every direction, so you can fly most of the year, and the mild Andalusian winter draws schools and national teams. It has hosted world championships, the World Air Games and a 2025 World Cup round.
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.rating_basis: One of the main flying centres in Spain and Europe (PWCA, Andalucía.org): over 30 years of history, takeoffs in every direction, lots of flyable days in winter, World Cup rounds and world championships
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.hazards: Rough summer thermals; rocks and bushes in front of the north takeoff; power lines by the landing field near the bullring; in strong wind, move to sheltered sites
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.crowd_note: In winter and spring, lots of groups from northern Europe and national team training camps, but the several takeoffs spread pilots out
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.season: Year-round; best in autumn, winter and spring (March–May, September–October); in summer, very strong thermals — for experienced pilots
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.transfer: Seville ~1 h 15 min; Málaga ~1 h 25 min; Jerez ~1 h
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.takeoffs: The free flight station on Sierra de Líjar has four takeoffs: South 990 m (S) and East 1,000 m (SE) behind the fire tower; West 890 m (SW); North 909 m (NW); all have weather stations and windsocks; nearby alternatives — El Bosque (W/NW, 658 m), Teba, Ronda la Vieja (private, by arrangement with the schools)
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.wind_note: Takeoffs face almost every direction (except NE), so there are lots of flyable days; in strong wind (levante / poniente) people fly at sheltered sites like El Bosque; ridge lift and thermals
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.best_time: In autumn, winter and spring, thermals during the day and tandems all day; in summer the thermals are very rough — beginners and tandems in the morning and evening
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.access: Road up Sierra de Líjar to the takeoffs (each has roadside parking); schools and tandem pilots drive you up themselves
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.xc_note: XC routes across the Sierra de Cádiz towards Ronda and Olvera; from El Bosque you can add 10–15 km; hosts PWC World Cup rounds (May 2025)
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.rules: Spain: foreigners need a national licence/IPPI card and third-party liability insurance; no takeoff fee is listed; the private Ronda la Vieja takeoff only by arrangement with FlySpain or Zero Gravity; near Teba, active airspace on the approaches to Málaga
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.landing: For South and East — a field on the El Imperio estate opposite the takeoffs (440 m, windsock, no obstacles); for West and North — by the bullring at the CA-9101 / A-8126 junction (474 m, power lines nearby); a separate landing field for hang gliders (242 m)
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.events: PWC Spain Paragliding World Cup round (10–17 May 2025); previously the World Air Games, a Hang Gliding World Championship, the Sierra de Cádiz Open, Spanish and Andalusian championships; national team training camps
pros: Flyable almost year-round, especially good in winter and spring
Takeoffs in every direction — lots of flyable days
Good infrastructure: weather stations, parking, landing fields
Inexpensive tandems and accommodation
cons: Very rough thermals and heat in summer
Car needed
Strong levante / poniente winds on some days
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.airport: SVQ — Seville, ~1 h 15 min; AGP — Málaga, ~1 h 25 min
algodonales-sierra-de-lijar.tandem_price_note: ~20–30 min flight, year-round, takeoff chosen by wind (Líjar or El Bosque), via Picuco; acro and long flights cost more
school_notes: Tandems from €90, year-round
School and pilot tours in Algodonales
Tandems and courses

tenerife-taucho.description: Tenerife is the main “winter” destination for European paraglider pilots: from November to April there are thermals, and tandems fly year-round. The classic is the Taucho takeoff above Adeje at ~770 m with a landing on La Caleta beach, while the highest takeoffs are at around 2,200 m. The island demands care: two airports, a no-fly zone over Teide and small landing fields.
tenerife-taucho.rating_basis: Taucho has 5 stars on Paraglidingmap; Cross Country calls Tenerife an early-season favourite for pilots escaping the northern winter; a landing on a resort beach; downsides — complex airspace and small landing fields
tenerife-taucho.hazards: Inversion and different winds at different heights; rough conditions in the afternoon; wind at the ends of the beaches; sink behind the Los Pinos takeoff; small landing fields; CTR and national park no-fly zones
tenerife-taucho.crowd_note: In winter, lots of pilots from northern Europe and tandems at Taucho
tenerife-taucho.season: Thermal and XC season November–April (high season is winter, when pilots “escape” the northern winter); tandems fly year-round, and the weather is more stable in spring and summer
tenerife-taucho.transfer: Tenerife South airport ~20–25 min to Adeje; Tenerife North ~1 h
tenerife-taucho.takeoffs: Taucho 768 m (SW, carpeted, upper and lower windsocks); Taucho — Corona Forestal (Los Pinos) 925 m — experts only; Ifonche 950–1,007 m (afternoons in light NE); Jama ~970 m; soaring at Diego Hernández beach; the island has around 15–30 takeoffs, the highest at ~2,200 m (Izaña, flights to the north and over Güímar)
tenerife-taucho.wind_note: The trade wind blows from the NE down low, with a SW flow often on top; in the south-west of the island (Adeje), the sea breeze and thermals do the work; there can be a strong inversion — you need to get above it, otherwise it's just a sled ride; the best conditions come with an active air mass above ~1,500 m
tenerife-taucho.best_time: Tandems all day; thermals from late morning, conditions turn “rough” in the afternoon; guides usually meet around 10:00 and fly until sunset
tenerife-taucho.access: Taucho — taxi from La Caleta beach ~€4, shuttle ~€10; operators pick you up from hotels in Costa Adeje
tenerife-taucho.xc_note: XC is limited by the complex airspace of the two airports; the island record is around 90 km; on good days thermals reach ~3,500 m
tenerife-taucho.rules: Spain: licence/IPPI card and liability insurance. Two airports mean complex airspace (Tenerife South and Tenerife North CTRs): the Los Cristianos ridge and Montaña Roja (El Médano) are no-fly zones, with fines of up to thousands of euros for violators; flying over Teide National Park, the volcano and the Izaña observatory is forbidden; some of the northern sites are inside the CTR; land only on permitted beaches. Pilot guiding €70–90 a day (Para42, Paraholic, November–March)
tenerife-taucho.landing: La Caleta beach (Costa Adeje) by the ocean; the landing spots are small — an accurate approach is needed; away from the beaches, lots of cacti
tenerife-taucho.events: Pre-PWC events and Spanish league rounds have been held here
pros: Flying in winter, when it's off-season in Europe
Landing on a resort beach
Lots of takeoffs for different winds
Guides and transfers for pilots
cons: Complex airspace around two airports
Small landing fields, cacti everywhere
Not a place for beginners
Limited XC (~90 km record)
tenerife-taucho.airport: TFS — Tenerife South, ~20 min; TFN — Tenerife North, ~1 h
tenerife-taucho.tandem_price_note: Long 45–60 min tandem with some XC and acro (Paraholic Tenerife); short tourist flights with other operators are usually cheaper
school_notes: Long tandems €180, guiding €80–90/day, coaching €200/day; November–March
Guiding on Tenerife since 2008 from €70/day, SIV and XC courses; November–March

annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.description: The Col de la Forclaz above the eastern shore of Lake Annecy is one of the most visited paragliding sites in the world. The takeoff looks out over the turquoise lake and the Alps, and the landing field is by the southern shore in Doussard. There are dozens of schools and tandem companies, and pilots get reliable thermals and XC routes into the Pre-Alps.
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known and most visited paragliding centres: ~2,000 launches a day in season, ~170 professional instructors around the lake, the famous lake view
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.hazards: Heavy traffic in the air and on the landing field; rotors in northerly and strong southerly wind; the breeze switching direction on the landing field towards evening; strong summer afternoon thermals; no low flying over the nature reserve
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.crowd_note: At peak season up to ~1,400 launches a day from the Forclaz and ~600 from Planfait; in 2023 more than 170,000 people used the takeoff — queues at takeoff and crowded skies
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.season: Flyable year-round: thermal season April–September (best May–July), in winter tandems and sled rides on clear days
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.transfer: Geneva ~1 h to Annecy, ~1 h 15 min to Doussard; from Annecy to the Doussard landing field ~25 min (bus 51)
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.takeoffs: The main Montmin takeoff (Col de la Forclaz) 1,240 m, W; the neighbouring Coche Cabane 1,180 m, W (backup when it's crowded); Planfait 960 m above Talloires, W
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.wind_note: West-facing takeoffs: they work in light westerly wind / the lake breeze; no flying in strong northerly (bise) or strong southerly wind — rotors
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.best_time: Tandems from morning to evening; calm in the morning (for beginners), thermals roughly from 11:00 to 17:00; gentle “sunset” flights in the evening
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.access: Road up to the Col de la Forclaz from Talloires or Doussard; ~10 minutes on foot from the car park; cars may drive to takeoff only with a paid badge; in summer, shuttles from the Doussard landing field, and tandem operators drive you up themselves (~25 min). There's no cable car
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.xc_note: Classic routes around the lake and to the Tournette, crossings towards the Aravis and Mont Blanc; on good days, triangles of 100+ km
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.rules: In France you need third-party liability insurance (RC) to fly; an FFVL licence isn't mandatory but is recommended; an IPPI card for wing rental. In summer and on weekends from May to September, a controller and a patrol work on takeoff and may stop a poorly prepared pilot from launching. Stay at least 200 m above ground over the Bout du Lac nature reserve, where landing is forbidden. Driving to takeoff requires a badge (issued at the Montmin and Talloires town halls)
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.landing: Doussard (460 m) by the southern shore of the lake: a big official field, but very busy; towards evening the breeze switches from N to S — risk of landing short of or past the field
pros: Breathtaking view of Lake Annecy
Huge choice of schools and tandems
Easy takeoff, reliable conditions
Flyable almost year-round
cons: Very crowded in summer — queues and busy skies
Overloaded landing field in Doussard
Paid access to takeoff, difficult parking
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.airport: GVA — Geneva, ~1 h 15 min; LYS — Lyon, ~1 h 45 min
annecy-col-de-la-forclaz.tandem_price_note: Classic 10–15 min flight from €100; 30–45 min “performance” flight from €135; photos/video +€30 (Takamaka)
school_notes: Tandems from the Forclaz from €100, flights for children, courses
Tandems and “progression” flights for pilots
Tandems and courses

chamonix-planpraz.description: Chamonix is the Alpine capital of paragliding: a gondola takes you up to the Planpraz takeoff at 2,000 m, and you fly right opposite Mont Blanc and the Bossons Glacier. Tandems fly almost year-round, while strong pilots set off from here on the classic XC routes to Annecy and Switzerland. Conditions are high-mountain: strong thermals, valley wind and restrictions around Mont Blanc in summer.
chamonix-planpraz.rating_basis: An iconic site: flying face to face with Mont Blanc and the glaciers, a gondola to takeoff, classic Alpine XC routes; Cross Country and travel guides list it as a must-fly
chamonix-planpraz.hazards: The Brévent gondola cables in front of takeoff (turn right and pass under them); lee rotors in northerly wind; strong valley wind in the afternoon; cable car wires in the Lachenal cirque (~1,700 m) when heading for the Flégère; helicopters; no-fly zones
chamonix-planpraz.crowd_note: Lots of tandems and pilots at Planpraz in summer; airspace shared with rescue and tourist helicopters
chamonix-planpraz.season: Main season June–September (thermals from March); in winter, tandems from the lifts on clear days; between seasons (May, October–November) the Brévent gondola is closed
chamonix-planpraz.transfer: Geneva ~1 h 15 min (direct shuttles to Chamonix); Turin/Milan ~2–3 h via the Mont Blanc Tunnel
chamonix-planpraz.takeoffs: Planpraz 2,032 m (SE, the main one); Plan de l'Aiguille ~2,300 m (NW, works after ~15:00, closed in July–August); Grands Montets above Argentière; Aiguille du Midi 3,700 m — for experienced alpine pilots; Plaine Joux — by the road
chamonix-planpraz.wind_note: The takeoff faces south-east, towards Mont Blanc; W and N winds stronger than 20 km/h at 2,000 m mean lee side and turbulence — don't fly
chamonix-planpraz.best_time: Planpraz works from the morning (~8–10 am) until early afternoon; during the day, strong thermals and turbulent valley wind — for experienced pilots; tandems all day
chamonix-planpraz.access: Brévent gondola from central Chamonix to Planpraz (~€18.50 one way); tandem operators may or may not include the ticket — check
chamonix-planpraz.xc_note: The classics are Chamonix–Annecy and back (~100 km), the “Rhone Rider” into Switzerland along the Rhône valley to the Furka Pass, and a tour around Mont Blanc; in summer, the occasional top landing on the summit of Mont Blanc (needs cloud base at ~5,000 m)
chamonix-planpraz.rules: Third-party liability insurance is mandatory. From 1 July to 31 August, flying over the Mont Blanc massif (the Mont Blanc side from Prarion to the Mer de Glace) is banned — fines and confiscation of the wing; the Plan de l'Aiguille takeoff is closed in July–August because of helicopters. Over the Aiguilles Rouges nature reserve behind the Brévent ridge, stay at least 1,000 m above ground. While the ski runs are open, landing at Le Bouchet and Les Savoy is banned — use Bois du Bouchet only
chamonix-planpraz.landing: Bois du Bouchet (~1,030 m) near central Chamonix: surrounded by forest, not visible from takeoff, very turbulent during the day — locate it in advance; backup — Les Savoy
pros: Flying face to face with Mont Blanc and the glaciers
Lift to takeoff
Tandems in winter too
Classic Alpine XC routes
cons: Turbulent landing field enclosed by forest
Summer bans on flying over the Mont Blanc massif
Expensive tandems and lifts
Not the best place to learn
chamonix-planpraz.tandem_price_note: “Discovery” ~20 min €148, children's flight €120, long flights of 30–60 min €190–270; lift ticket usually not included (Kailash Adventure)
school_notes: Tandems from Planpraz, 20–60 min

dune-du-pilat.description: The Dune du Pilat on the Arcachon Bay is Europe's highest sand dune (about 107 m) and a classic French coastal soaring site. Pilots ridge-soar the sandy slope in the sea wind, with views of the ocean and the pine forest. Tandems are short but spectacular; for pilots it's a great place to practise wing handling in wind.
dune-du-pilat.rating_basis: Europe's highest dune and one of France's best-known soaring sites; beautiful views of the Arcachon Bay and the ocean; strict rules and zone restrictions
dune-du-pilat.hazards: Wind that's too strong (blowing you back over the dune into the forest); sink behind the crest; tourists on the slope; collisions when ridge soaring is crowded (the pilot with the slope on their right has priority); no-fly zones over the beaches
dune-du-pilat.crowd_note: In summer it's crowded both on the dune (tourists) and in the air; hence the zones and daily pilot limits
dune-du-pilat.season: April–October (tandems); pilots also fly off-season when there's a suitable westerly
dune-du-pilat.transfer: Bordeaux-Mérignac ~1 h by car; by train Bordeaux–Arcachon ~50 min, then ~15 min to the dune
dune-du-pilat.takeoffs: Takeoff and landing are allowed only in the Gaillouneys sector (southern part of the dune, by Petit Nice beach): the western hollow in front of the bunkers or the northern one just behind them, depending on the wind; the dune itself is ~107 m high (2018); there's also the Sabloney — Robinson takeoff by the Pyla campsite
dune-du-pilat.wind_note: Ridge soaring in onshore wind off the Atlantic, best in a W–NW sea breeze; according to the weather station, the workable wind is ~14–23 km/h; in wind stronger than ~20 km/h, don't fly over the dune
dune-du-pilat.best_time: Flying mostly happens in the afternoon, once the sea breeze fills in (tandems usually from 14:00)
dune-du-pilat.access: By car via the A63/A660 and D259 to the Petit Nice car park, then a ~10-minute walk along the beach; ~1 h from Bordeaux; in summer, the Dune Express bus from Arcachon station
dune-du-pilat.xc_note: No XC — only soaring along the dune (300 m altitude limit)
dune-du-pilat.rules: Aviation liability insurance (RCA) and a helmet are mandatory; pilots and groups must pre-register at parapilat.com (groups of up to 10 pilots, no more than 14 days a year, no more than 50 pilots a day); maximum altitude 300 m; speedriding and paramotors are banned. From 15 June to 15 September, flying is allowed only between a point 200 m south of the Corniche lifeguard post and 50 m north of Petit Nice beach; flying over residential areas and supervised beaches is banned; don't launch in the marram grass (oyat) plantings. Safety frequency 143.9875 MHz
dune-du-pilat.landing: Top landing on the dune or in the permitted areas of the Gaillouneys sector; in summer, landing on the beach outside the designated areas is not allowed
pros: Unique scenery: the dune, the ocean, the Arcachon Bay
Laminar sea wind — good for practising ground handling and soaring
Close to Bordeaux
cons: Strict rules, zones and registration
Crowded in summer
No XC — soaring only
Depends on wind direction and strength
dune-du-pilat.tandem_price_note: 10 min with photos and 360° video via an aggregator (Sport Découverte); 20 min — €215; booking directly with schools can be cheaper
school_notes: Tandems of ~30 min over the dune
Local school: tandems and training
5-day course on wing handling in strong wind and soaring, €699

saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.description: A quiet village by Lake Castillon in Haute-Provence, known as one of Europe's best XC sites. Mont Chalvet has takeoffs facing every direction, and a summer cloud base of 3,000–4,000 m allows 100 km flights over the Southern Alps. It hosted the 2012 European Championship, and the long-established Aérogliss school operates by the lake.
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.rating_basis: One of Europe's main XC centres (Cross Country, Ultimate France): high cloud base, takeoffs in every direction, the 2012 European Championship; the Aérogliss school has been running since 1982
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.hazards: Summer thermal turbulence; the main takeoff gets “blown out” in the afternoon; the valley wind on the landing field can swing round 180°; turbulence in N/NW wind
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.crowd_note: Busy on takeoff and on the landing field in summer, noticeably quieter in September
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.season: April–October (best May–September; June–August for big XC, September is calmer and less crowded); in winter people fly on clear days, but the takeoffs may be snowed in
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.transfer: Nice 105 km (~1 h 45 min by car; the scenic Train des Pignes ~2.5 h); Marseille ~2 h
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.takeoffs: Mont Chalvet (1,609 m) has several takeoffs at ~1,540 m: south-west/west (the main one, steep, thermic from midday), a wide gentle south-east/south one (mornings, suitable for beginners) and a north-facing one for early-morning launches
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.wind_note: In the morning, the SE takeoff; after ~11:00, when the valley wind arrives from the Digne side, the SW takeoff; by midday the main takeoff can get blown out (the SW one as early as 13:30); in the evening there's often ridge soaring until dark
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.best_time: Calm air in the morning (tandems, beginners); thermals from ~11:00; gentle soaring and sunset flights in the evening
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.access: Paved road up to the takeoffs (~15 min); in summer (mid-June to mid-September), the ASAVL club shuttle runs from the Aérogliss base 8:00–13:00 and after 17:00, leaving once 4 pilots are on board; alternatively, a taxi
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.xc_note: The classic is a 50 km triangle via Cheval Blanc and Montagne de Coupe; the “100 km” goes via Cheval Blanc, Tête de l'Estrop and Dormillouse; in summer cloud base is 3,000–4,000 m; a venue for FAI Category 1 competitions
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.rules: France: third-party liability insurance is mandatory; an FFVL licence isn't required but is recommended (it includes insurance); IPPI card for wing rental and guiding. No takeoff fees. Free access to the takeoffs; respect landing etiquette (clear your wing off the field quickly)
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.landing: The big Aérogliss field (880 m) at the northern end of Lake Castillon, three windsocks; thermic during the day, turbulent in N/NW wind; the valley wind on the landing field can swing round 180° in seconds. Backup — Moriez (Le Pastaire campsite), 3 km away
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.events: FAI European Paragliding Championship (September 2012), regular FAI Category 1 competitions
pros: Takeoffs facing different directions — lots of flyable days
Strong XC thermals and high cloud base
Big landing field by the lake
Gentle takeoff for students
cons: Few operators, far from the airport
Rough thermals during summer days
Abrupt valley wind shifts on the landing field
saint-andre-les-alpes-chalvet.airport: NCE — Nice, ~1 h 45 min; MRS — Marseille, ~2 h
school_notes: School by the landing field since 1982: tandems (from age 4), courses, guiding, weather briefings, bar

gudauri-paragliding.description: Gudauri is Georgia's main tandem spot and one of the most popular with Russians: in summer, takeoffs are by the Friendship Monument on the Georgian Military Road (~2,300 m), with 20–30-minute flights over the Aragvi gorge; in winter, straight from the slopes of the ski resort at almost 3,000 m. Lots of operators and Russian-speaking pilots, flights almost year-round.
gudauri-paragliding.rating_basis: The most popular tandem spot in Georgia and the Caucasus: flights over the Aragvi gorge and snowy peaks, year-round, lots of Russian-speaking pilots; for independent pilots, serious high-mountain conditions
gudauri-paragliding.hazards: Strong wind on the pass, rapid weather changes, high altitude, deep gorges — there have been fatal accidents involving falls into the gorge; stay within the approved flying zone
gudauri-paragliding.crowd_note: In season and on holidays, dozens of tandems by the viewpoint and queues of tourists
gudauri-paragliding.season: Year-round: in winter (December–March), tandems from the resort slopes; in summer and early autumn (June–September), long flights from the viewpoint; between seasons (April–May, November) there's less flying
gudauri-paragliding.transfer: Tbilisi (airport) ~2–2.5 h along the Georgian Military Road, taxi ~$70; from Vladikavkaz via Upper Lars ~2 h (longer with the border crossing)
gudauri-paragliding.takeoffs: The summer takeoff by the viewpoint and the Friendship Monument on the Georgian Military Road (~2,245–2,350 m), landing in the Tetri Aragvi valley; in winter, from the ski resort slopes: Mount Kudebi 2,987 m and Bidara 2,960 m (up by cable car, landing by the first station, ~10–20-minute flights)
gudauri-paragliding.wind_note: The takeoffs on the slopes above the Aragvi valley work in light valley wind and daytime thermals; flights are cancelled when the wind on the pass is strong
gudauri-paragliding.best_time: Tandems from morning to midday; in summer, 20–35-minute flights over the Aragvi gorge, in winter 10–15 minutes over the ski runs
gudauri-paragliding.access: In summer, a lift from Gudauri along the Georgian Military Road to the viewpoint (5–10 minutes); in winter, the resort's cable cars
gudauri-paragliding.xc_note: Mostly tandems and acro (winter acro camps); XC flights are possible between Kazbegi and Gudauri, but the mountains are high and landing options are few
gudauri-paragliding.rules: Flights within the government-approved zone above Gudauri (Civil Aviation Agency, 2023) under NOTAM rules; around Kazbegi, class G airspace with notification to Tbilisi Control. Insurance and a reserve parachute are mandatory. Russians don't need a visa; the border with Russia (Upper Lars) is nearby — don't fly towards it
gudauri-paragliding.landing: In summer, a prepared landing field in the Tetri Aragvi valley below the viewpoint; in winter, by the first cable car station next to the Time-Out restaurant
gudauri-paragliding.events: Winter acro camps and shows (SkyAtlantida); Georgian competitions, Sakartvelo Open (2026)
pros: Flights over the Caucasus year-round
In winter, easy to combine with skiing
Lots of Russian-speaking pilots
Visa-free for Russians
cons: High altitude: cold, rapid weather changes
Little information for independent pilots
Crowds of tourists at the viewpoint
gudauri-paragliding.tandem_price_note: $129–169 for a 15-minute flight through aggregators; long summer flights cost more than winter ones; booking directly with local pilots is usually cheaper
school_notes: Certifies Gudauri tandem pilots (according to georgia.travel)
Tandems and XC in the Gudauri mountains, operating for 7+ years
Tandems, acro, accommodation and transfers; refresher courses for novice pilots
15-minute flight, winter and summer, Russian and English

bali-timbis.description: The southern coast of the Bukit Peninsula on Bali is a line of limestone cliffs above the Indian Ocean, along which tandems soar in the south-east trade wind during the dry season. Timbis by Pandawa beach is the best-known takeoff for tourist flights; Riug in Nusa Dua and Nyang Nyang near Uluwatu operate nearby.
bali-timbis.rating_basis: Popular tourist tandems over the ocean in the dry season; for pilots, short coastal soaring with no XC, little information about schools
bali-timbis.hazards: Landing near the cliff edge, turbulence behind the cliff edge as the wind picks up, flying over water
bali-timbis.crowd_note: Several tandems at once along the cliffs; the stream of tourists depends on the wind
bali-timbis.season: dry season with the south-east trade wind: April–October, best May–September; November–March is the rainy season, with westerly winds
bali-timbis.transfer: ~30–40 minutes from Denpasar airport; 15–25 minutes from Nusa Dua and Uluwatu
bali-timbis.takeoffs: Other coastal takeoffs on the Bukit: Riug (Sawangan, Nusa Dua) and Nyang Nyang (Uluwatu) — they work in the same trade wind; in the mountains, the Batur thermal takeoff (~1,575 m). Coordinates for Timbis are given for the beach below the cliff
bali-timbis.wind_note: Ridge soaring along the cliffs in the dry-season south-east trade wind; in the rainy season the wind is westerly, and there's practically no flying on the south coast
bali-timbis.best_time: Usually from midday to evening, once a steady sea wind sets in
bali-timbis.access: Drive to the cliff via the Pandawa beach area (Kutuh); there's an entrance fee (~8,000 IDR, 2024)
bali-timbis.xc_note: Almost no XC potential — soaring along the Bukit cliffs
bali-timbis.rules: Little information on formal rules for foreign pilots; flights are arranged with the operators at the takeoffs; a pilot rating (IPPI card) and insurance are required
bali-timbis.landing: Top landing on the clifftop by the takeoff, or on the beach below the cliffs
pros: Flight over the ocean and beaches
Close to the Nusa Dua and Uluwatu resorts
Easy coastal soaring
cons: Flights only in the dry season
Short flights of ~15 minutes
Little information for independent pilots
No XC
bali-timbis.tandem_price_note: About 15 minutes of flying; online prices 860,000–925,000 IDR, on site 1,000,000–1,100,000 IDR; hotel transfer extra
school_notes: The main tandem operator on the Timbis cliffs

bir-billing.description: Bir Billing in Himachal Pradesh is India's paragliding capital and one of the world's best XC areas: the high Billing takeoff above the Kangra Valley, strong Himalayan thermals and flights along the Dhauladhar range. It has hosted a World Cup round, and in season hundreds of tandems launch from the mountain every day.
bir-billing.rating_basis: One of Asia's top XC areas: 2015 World Cup round, flights of over 250 km, Cross Country guides; downsides — weak rescue services and tandem accidents
bir-billing.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms over the main range; strong spring thermals; terraced fields and power lines in an outlanding; remote mountain terrain with no rescue helicopter; wild animals; dangerous mountain roads
bir-billing.crowd_note: Around 200 launches a day in season (2025 data), queues of tandems on takeoff; in October pilots from all over the world converge here
bir-billing.season: mid-September to early July; best XC months October–early November and March–May; winter is flyable but weaker; July to mid-September is the monsoon, and flying is banned
bir-billing.transfer: Gaggal airport (Dharamshala) ~70 km, about 2 h by taxi; from Delhi, an overnight bus to Bir ~12 h; 45 minutes from Bir to takeoff
bir-billing.takeoffs: The large Billing launch meadow (2,428 m) with E, S and W-facing launch areas; the Chowgan landing field near Bir, 1,410 m
bir-billing.wind_note: Light background wind, usually switching from E to W during the day; thermals off the south-facing slopes; by 16:00 thunderstorms often build over the main range
bir-billing.best_time: Tandems from morning to midday; on XC days, launch around midday; towards evening, keep an eye on storm clouds
bir-billing.access: A narrow winding road from Bir, 14–15 km, about 45 minutes by taxi from the Tibetan Colony taxi stand (≈700 INR as of 2023); a ~4 km footpath from the checkpoint
bir-billing.xc_note: The classic route runs along the ridges west to Palampur and Dharamshala (~45 km) and back; competition tasks of 70–80 km; the record from Billing is 253 km (Debu Choudhury, April 2016)
bir-billing.rules: Foreign pilots need a valid pilot rating and insurance; flying is governed by the Himachal Pradesh Aero Sports Rules and the Kangra district administration — registration / a permit is required (check with the local pilots' association and the tourist office).
