From July to mid-September the authorities ban flying for the monsoon. In 2025, after accidents, document checks for tandem pilots and a limit of 2 tandems per pilot per day were introduced
bir-billing.landing: The Chowgan landing field near Bir — large terraced fields, ~1,410 m; on XC flights, outlandings on terraces with power lines
bir-billing.events: Paragliding World Cup round (PWC, October 2015, the first in India); XC Pre World Cup (FAI CAT 2, 26 October–2 November 2023); Indian Open (2018, 2020) and other competitions
pros: World-class XC flying
Cheap tandems and cost of living
Big takeoff facing several directions
International pilot community vibe in October
cons: Monsoon and flying ban from July to mid-September
Weak rescue services, difficult retrieves from the mountains
High tandem accident rate, chaos on takeoff
Permit bureaucracy
bir-billing.tandem_price_note: Standard 15–25 min tandem; short flights from 2,000–2,500 INR, long and thermal flights of up to an hour cost more; GoPro video +500–1,000 INR
school_notes: Well-known guiding operator for XC pilots (mentioned in Cross Country)
Camp by the Billing takeoff, popular with pilots

kamshet-tower-hill.description: Kamshet in the Western Ghats between Mumbai and Pune is India's main paragliding training area: low grassy hills, ridge soaring on the east face of Tower Hill in winter and thermals on the west-facing takeoffs in spring. There are lots of schools, inexpensive P1–P2 courses and tandems for people from Mumbai and Pune.
kamshet-tower-hill.rating_basis: The “training capital of India” according to Cross Country: lots of schools, gentle conditions, ~10 unflyable days in an eight-month season; modest potential for XC pilots
kamshet-tower-hill.hazards: Rotor on the west face of Tower Hill in south-westerly wind; venturi to the left of the Shelar takeoff in strong wind; the Mumbai–Pune airway passes over the area
kamshet-tower-hill.crowd_note: At weekends, lots of students and tandems from Mumbai and Pune
kamshet-tower-hill.season: mid-October to May; best November–February (Tower Hill, easterly winds), in spring the west-facing takeoffs (Shelar); June–September is the monsoon, no flying
kamshet-tower-hill.transfer: 2–3 h from Mumbai on the Mumbai–Pune Expressway (about 100 km), about 1 h from Pune; Kamshet has a railway station
kamshet-tower-hill.takeoffs: Tower Hill: the east face (857 m), and in the westerly season the west face across the flat summit; Shelar — west face, 720 m (landing 640 m), 10 km away, works in spring
kamshet-tower-hill.wind_note: In winter, a morning easterly gives ridge lift on the east face of Tower Hill; towards the end of winter the wind swings west and flying becomes thermal; in spring the mornings are too windy, so people fly from the afternoon until sunset
kamshet-tower-hill.best_time: In winter, mornings around 10:00 and evenings; in spring, from the afternoon until sunset; a sunset flight on Tower Hill is a classic
kamshet-tower-hill.access: Drive to the foot of the hill and a short walk up; schools drive students and passengers from guesthouses near Kamshet
kamshet-tower-hill.xc_note: Short XC flights of 4–10 km between takeoffs and guesthouses; ceiling usually ~1,800 m (up to 3,000 m); crossings over the Ghats to Karjat; the long-distance goal is Panchgani, ~100 km
kamshet-tower-hill.rules: There's hardly any national licensing system; foreign pilots fly by arrangement with local schools / the club (Nirvana Adventures), with a pilot rating and insurance; the Mumbai–Pune airway passes over the area (aircraft at ~1,800 m)
kamshet-tower-hill.landing: Large landing field at the foot of Tower Hill, ~240 m below takeoff; on XC flights it's easy to land, then back by bus or rickshaw
pros: Excellent for training
Long, stable season
Inexpensive
Close to Mumbai and Pune
cons: Small height difference
Modest XC potential
Hot in spring
Monsoon June–September
kamshet-tower-hill.airport: PNQ — Pune, ~1 h; BOM — Mumbai, 2–3 h
kamshet-tower-hill.tandem_price_note: Classic 8–12 min tandem 2,500–3,200 INR; 15–20 min thermal flight 3,500–4,500 INR; video +500–700 INR
school_notes: The oldest local school (APPI), guesthouse; the place to ask about the rules
APPI school, P1–P3 courses and tandems
Tandems and training

bassano-monte-grappa.description: The slopes of Monte Grappa above Bassano and Semonzo are a classic destination for European clubs and schools. South-facing takeoffs at 700–1,600 m look out over the Venetian plain, all of them lead to one big landing field, and you can fly almost year-round. In spring and autumn the area hosts XC clinics and hundreds of training groups.
bassano-monte-grappa.rating_basis: One of Europe's most popular centres for club and school trips (Cross Country, Italia.it): flyable days almost year-round, a big landing field, “dozens of schools and flying centres”, thousands of pilots a year
bassano-monte-grappa.hazards: Valleys along the ridge unsuitable for landing (cross them with height to spare); air being sucked into the valleys when the mountains overdevelop; tree landings (carry a smoke signal); heavy traffic
bassano-monte-grappa.crowd_note: In season, lots of school groups from all over Europe, especially in spring and autumn; crowded on the popular takeoffs
bassano-monte-grappa.season: Flyable almost year-round; best March–May (stronger, but more bad weather) and September–November (more stable); hot in summer, but lots of XC days
bassano-monte-grappa.transfer: Treviso ~50 min; Venice ~1 h 15 min; Verona ~1 h 30 min; train/bus to Bassano
bassano-monte-grappa.takeoffs: The south face of the Grappa massif, 15–20 min from the landing field: Carraro 3 (910 m, paragliders, SE–SW), Carraro 1–2 (850–870 m, mostly hang gliders), Monte Colombera (1,410 m, room for 2 pilots), Monte Meda (1,610 m, a wide meadow for competitions), Costalunga (720 m), Col Campeggia (1,100 m, not for beginners)
bassano-monte-grappa.wind_note: South-facing takeoffs looking out over the Venetian plain; flown in light southerly wind and in thermals; the massif gives no shelter from strong northerly wind — don't fly then
bassano-monte-grappa.best_time: Tandems all day and at sunset; thermals from late morning; spring and autumn bring the most stable and best XC days
bassano-monte-grappa.access: Shuttles from the Garden Relais car park in Semonzo to the takeoffs, leaving as they fill up (from €8 per person, 2011); tandem operators drive you up themselves (~15 min)
bassano-monte-grappa.xc_note: XC routes along the front range to the east and west, 20–150 km (up to 200 km according to Italy's tourism portal); cloud base 1,500–2,500 m; 100 km out-and-returns have been flown in January, and the XC season starts in mid-February
bassano-monte-grappa.rules: All pilots (Italian and foreign) must buy the local club's FlyCard — a pass for the takeoffs and landing fields (2011: 1 day €8, 3 days €12, 5 days €20, 9 days €25, a year €40); available online or at the Semonzo tourist office, Montegrappa Air Park, or at the Garden Relais landing field after a document check. A green smoke signal is recommended: if you land in a tree or outside a field, use it — otherwise a rescue helicopter will be called out (from €500)
bassano-monte-grappa.landing: Big landing field by the Garden Relais hotel in Semonzo (160 m), reachable from all takeoffs; separate fields for paragliders and hang gliders; B&Bs and campsites nearby
pros: Flyable days almost year-round
Lots of takeoffs at different heights, one big landing field
Shuttles and infrastructure for pilots
Close to Venice and Treviso
cons: Crowded in spring and autumn
Forested slopes — tree landings
Hot and hazy in summer
No shelter from northerly wind
bassano-monte-grappa.airport: TSF — Treviso, ~50 min; VCE — Venice, ~1 h 15 min
bassano-monte-grappa.tandem_price_note: 20–30 minutes of flying, transfer to takeoff included; year-round (Freedome, Borso del Grappa)
school_notes: Tandem aggregator: standard, sunset, acro, “performance”, from the summit of Grappa

garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.description: Monte Baldo above Malcesine is one of Italy's most scenic takeoffs: a cable car takes you up to almost 1,800 m, and the flight goes straight out over Lake Garda with a height difference of about 1,700 m and a beach landing. The site is famous for SIV courses over water and tandems with lake views. Conditions depend on the lake winds, the Peler and the Ora.
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.rating_basis: Paraglidingmap gives the Monte Baldo takeoff 5 stars (“scenic but tricky”); a 1,700 m height difference straight over the lake, a cable car, one of Europe's main venues for SIV courses
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.hazards: Strong lake winds and rapid weather changes; landing by the water (a life jacket is mandatory; if you ditch, get out of your harness immediately); pastures by takeoff; heavy tandem traffic
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.crowd_note: Lots of tandems and SIV groups in summer, queues for the cable car at the peak of the tourist season
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.region: Malcesine, eastern shore of Lake Garda, Verona (Veneto)
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.season: The cable car runs and people fly year-round, even in winter; tandems daily from April to October
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.transfer: Verona ~1 h 15 min; Bergamo ~2 h; Venice ~2 h; ferries on the lake
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.takeoffs: A big launch area at Tratto Spino, ~1 km from the cable car top station: the west takeoff faces out over the lake, the east one the other side of the ridge (thermals for XC); nearby, Prada Costabella 1,820–1,935 m
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.wind_note: The lake wind system: in the morning the northerly Peler (dies down by ~11:00), during the day the southerly Ora, blowing steadily until evening; strong wind is possible in summer — check with the locals
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.best_time: Tandems from morning to evening; after midday the Ora strengthens the wind on the landing field; flights of ~20–30 minutes with a ~1,700 m height difference
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.access: The rotating Malcesine–Monte Baldo cable car (with an intermediate station at San Michele) to Tratto Spino, then ~1 km on foot to takeoff; online “Paragliding” tickets for a specific slot, arrive 10 min early
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.xc_note: The east takeoff gives thermals for XC along the Baldo ridge; the site's main specialty is SIV courses over the lake
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.rules: A licence, insurance and a life jacket are mandatory (you can buy one at the bar by the landing field or at the Ideal hotel); the Paragliding Club Malcesine landing field is free for private pilots and paid for commercial flights; club rules at paraglidingmalcesine.it; takeoff anemometer on +39 366 5944289
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.landing: The beach at Navene, ~2 km north of central Malcesine (by the lake, ~70 m): the wind is hard to judge from the air; in summer the club runs a paid rescue boat; bar by the landing field
pros: ~1,700 m height difference straight over Lake Garda
Cable car to takeoff
SIV courses over water
Flyable year-round
cons: Tricky landing by the water, wind hard to judge
Strong Ora on summer afternoons
Cable car queues in season
Expensive tandems
garda-monte-baldo-malcesine.tandem_price_note: Cable car ticket and video included; 20–30 min flight; April–October (Garda Air Style, Freedome)
school_notes: Tandems from €200 including the cable car ticket and video; English, German
Tandems from Monte Baldo
The local club: runs the landing field, rules and weather

kerio-valley-iten.description: The Elgeyo Escarpment above the Kerio Valley, by the runners' town of Iten, is one of the planet's best XC areas: a 100-kilometre ridge at 2,340 m above sea level, the north-east trade wind and tropical thermals make 200 km out-and-returns possible almost every day in winter. World records are set here, tandem ones included.
kerio-valley-iten.rating_basis: One of the world's best places for ridge XC during the northern winter: 200 km flights daily, world records, Cross Country guides; downsides — remoteness, weak rescue services and little tandem infrastructure
kerio-valley-iten.hazards: Strong wind plus thermals on takeoff, a hot valley floor and long retrieves, limited search and rescue (a French pilot died on an XC flight in 2026), wild animals in the reserves
kerio-valley-iten.crowd_note: In January–February record-chasing groups and tours arrive, and the Kerio View hotel is booked six months ahead, but there's plenty of room in the air
kerio-valley-iten.season: December–February (the best weeks for records are mid-January); March is transitional; the rains start in April
kerio-valley-iten.transfer: From Nairobi, a flight or ~4 h by shuttle to Eldoret, then 50 km by taxi to takeoff
kerio-valley-iten.takeoffs: The main takeoff by the Kerio View hotel (2,340 m); the Kilima Resort takeoff on the same escarpment; the ridge runs for ~100 km
kerio-valley-iten.wind_note: The escarpment faces the winter north-east trade wind (~90% of winds are easterly); ridge lift from 7 am until dark in 15–20 km/h, plus powerful thermals; during the day the wind combined with thermals can make launching impossible
kerio-valley-iten.best_time: Launch early in the morning or towards evening; on XC days start in the morning to fit in a 200+ km out-and-return
kerio-valley-iten.access: The takeoff is right by the Kerio View hotel, 50 km from Eldoret (taxi or matatu); retrieves from the shelf by “piki-piki” motorbike taxi, from the valley floor by car with a driver
kerio-valley-iten.xc_note: The classic is a 200 km out-and-return along the escarpment almost every day; site record 340.7 km on a paraglider (O. Procházka, February 2026); tandem world out-and-return records of up to 250 km (2026); 377 km on a hang glider; ceiling up to 4,000 m
kerio-valley-iten.rules: No published rules for visiting pilots could be found — people fly via local organisers and guides (Kerio View, Kilima Resort, SkyNomad, Fly Kenya); a tracker, radio and water are a must, and report your flights — rescue services are limited; after a pause, flying in Iten was officially restarted by the county in February 2026
kerio-valley-iten.landing: Top landing by takeoff or landing on the shelf 200 m below; the valley floor is ~1,300 m lower — hot, with long retrieves
kerio-valley-iten.events: The record season in January–February: tandem world out-and-return records (since 2011), a 377 km hang gliding record (2026)
pros: World records and 200 km almost daily
A stable season while it's winter in Europe
Hotel right on takeoff
Safaris and reserves nearby
cons: Experienced pilots only
Remote, with limited rescue services
Short season
Little information on rules and tandems
kerio-valley-iten.airport: EDL — Eldoret, ~1 h; NBO — Nairobi, a flight or ~5 h
school_notes: Hotel on takeoff, organises retrieves
Local contact for pilots, accommodation and information
Guided XC tours, January–March
XC tours, tandems and training in the Rift Valley

karakol-issyk-kul.description: On Issyk-Kul, organised tandems could only be confirmed near Karakol: pilots launch from the Karakol ski base at around 3,000 m and land in the valley below the base; flights last 30–40 minutes with views of the Terskey Ala-Too and the lake. They fly in both winter and summer. On the beaches of Cholpon-Ata and Bosteri what's on offer is parasailing behind a boat — that's not paragliding.
karakol-issyk-kul.rating_basis: The only place found on Issyk-Kul with organised tandems: takeoff from a ski base at ~3,000 m with lake views; information is scarce and partly outdated (2017)
karakol-issyk-kul.hazards: High altitude (takeoff at ~3,000 m), cold and wind in winter, mountain-valley winds and daytime turbulence in summer, afternoon thunderstorms over the ranges
karakol-issyk-kul.crowd_note: Few tandems, no queues on takeoff expected
karakol-issyk-kul.region: Issyk-Kul Region, Karakol gorge (Terskey Ala-Too range), eastern end of Issyk-Kul
karakol-issyk-kul.season: Tandems fly in winter, from the ski slope during the ski season (December–March), and in summer; best season June–September; the 7 Nebo club gives its flying season as April–October
karakol-issyk-kul.transfer: Issyk-Kul airport (Tamchy) is ~190 km away, about 3 h along the northern shore; ~6–7 h from Bishkek; from Karakol to the ski base, take the road into the Karakol gorge
karakol-issyk-kul.takeoffs: The point on the map is the lower part of the Karakol ski base (~2,300 m); the tandem takeoff is higher, at ~3,000 m near the top lift stations (the highest skiing point is 3,040 m), exact location not published. Tandems are also sold near Teploklyuchenka outside Karakol (Klook). No organised paragliding could be found in Cholpon-Ata or Bosteri — on the beaches there they offer parasailing behind a boat
karakol-issyk-kul.wind_note: Flight duration depends on wind strength and direction; the air is calmer in the morning than during the day
karakol-issyk-kul.best_time: Morning is the calmest time for a tandem; turbulence is stronger during the day
karakol-issyk-kul.access: Up to takeoff on the ski base chairlifts (the lift also runs in summer); after landing, an off-roader takes you back to the base. The base is ~11 km as the crow flies from central Karakol
karakol-issyk-kul.xc_note: No data on XC flights from Karakol. Big XC routes are possible on the ranges around Issyk-Kul: Advance pilots flew ~50 km along the ridge north of the lake and estimate the potential at up to 250 km, but these are expedition flights with no infrastructure
karakol-issyk-kul.rules: Visiting pilots should make arrangements with local pilots and bring their own gear (there's almost no rental for pilots). Passengers have weight limits (roughly 40–110 kg, check with the pilot). Russians don't need a visa
karakol-issyk-kul.landing: A field about 1.5 km below the ski base; you're driven back to the base in an off-roader
pros: Takeoff at ~3,000 m, by chairlift
Flights in both winter and summer
Russian-speaking pilots, visa-free for Russians
cons: Few operators and little up-to-date information
Far from Bishkek
No schools or rental for pilots
karakol-issyk-kul.airport: IKU — Issyk-Kul (Tamchy), ~3 h; FRU — Bishkek, ~6–7 h
karakol-issyk-kul.tandem_price_note: Sky Trial, winter 2016/17: 3,000 som including GoPro video, 30–40-minute flight. The price is outdated — check; a tandem near Teploklyuchenka via Klook is ~$111 (date not given)
school_notes: Tandems from the Karakol ski base, pilots Sergey Trofimtsev and Murat Kuziev (as of 2017)
Tandems at Chon-Tash near Bishkek, near Karakol and at Toktogul; April–October, 1,200–1,500 som (year not given)
Tandem with a pilot around Karakol, ~2 hours, ~$111

danyang-yangbangsan.description: Danyang is South Korea's tandem capital: a takeoff on Mount Yangbangsan above an S-shaped bend of the Namhan River, an hour and a half by train from Seoul. Some fifteen to twenty tandem companies operate here, and flights over the river and mountains are especially beautiful in spring and during the autumn foliage season.
danyang-yangbangsan.rating_basis: Korea's most popular tandem site: 15–20 companies, views of the river bend, easy to reach from Seoul; for pilots, short local flights
danyang-yangbangsan.hazards: Heavy tandem traffic, summer haze and thunderstorms in the rainy season
danyang-yangbangsan.crowd_note: At weekends, queues of tandems on takeoff and lots of wings in the air
danyang-yangbangsan.season: year-round except the rainy season (late June–July); best April–May and September–October; shorter flights in winter
danyang-yangbangsan.transfer: From Seoul by KTX-Eum train from Cheongnyangni ~1 h 20 min, or by bus from Dong Seoul ~2.5 h; operators pick you up from Danyang station for free
danyang-yangbangsan.takeoffs: The main takeoff is the Yangbangsan viewpoint (664 m); a second takeoff, Dusan (~600 m), is used by tandem companies
danyang-yangbangsan.wind_note: Best in NW wind; the Namhan River valley is partly sheltered from other directions; gentle thermals in spring and autumn, shorter flights in winter
danyang-yangbangsan.best_time: Tandems all day; a standard flight lasts 7–15 minutes over the S-shaped bend of the Namhan River
danyang-yangbangsan.access: A road to the top of Yangbangsan; tandem companies drive you to takeoff (pilots pay for a lift or drive themselves)
danyang-yangbangsan.xc_note: Mostly tandems and local flights; moderate XC potential
danyang-yangbangsan.rules: The takeoff is leased and maintained by the tandem companies — independent pilots need to ask them for permission (usually not a problem); tandem pilots are licensed by the Korean Paragliding Association; according to pilot reports, documents aren't checked on takeoff
danyang-yangbangsan.landing: Spacious, well-kept landing fields on the bank of the Namhan River near Danyang
pros: Quick and easy from Seoul
Beautiful views of the river and mountains
Lots of operators, flights almost year-round
cons: Short 7–15-minute tandems
Crowded takeoff at weekends
Little information for visiting pilots
Rainy season in July
danyang-yangbangsan.tandem_price_note: Basic tandem with GoPro video; “dynamic” with acro ~120,000 KRW, VIP ~150,000 KRW; surcharge for passengers weighing 100–120 kg ~20,000 KRW
school_notes: One of Danyang's big tandem companies
Tandems, transfer from Danyang station

almaty-ushkonyr.description: The Ushkonyr plateau, ~50 km west of Almaty, is Kazakhstan's main paragliding site: its steep north slope is home to the deltadrome, a dedicated flying ground where beginners learn and the main competitions of Kazakhstan and the CIS are held. Tandems fly both from here and from the high mountains of the Trans-Ili Alatau — the Talgar Pass above Shymbulak and Big Almaty Lake; everything happens in Russian.
almaty-ushkonyr.rating_basis: Kazakhstan's main paragliding site: the deltadrome, schools, Kazakh and CIS competitions, close to Almaty; minimal infrastructure and little information for visitors
almaty-ushkonyr.hazards: Strong summer thermals, mountain-valley winds in the Trans-Ili Alatau, high altitude at the Talgar Pass
almaty-ushkonyr.crowd_note: Almaty has around 100 pilots, 30–40 of whom fly regularly — the takeoff is rarely crowded
almaty-ushkonyr.region: Almaty Region, Karasay District, ~50 km west of Almaty
almaty-ushkonyr.season: The main season is the warm part of the year (April–October); people also fly in winter in good weather
almaty-ushkonyr.transfer: Almaty airport ~1–1.5 h to the plateau
almaty-ushkonyr.takeoffs: The main site is the steep north slope of the Ushkonyr plateau with the deltadrome (training slopes for beginners, tandems with a height difference of up to ~1,000 m). Other sites: the Talgar Pass above Shymbulak (up by cable car, high-altitude takeoffs), Big Almaty Lake, Tekeli (precision landing)
almaty-ushkonyr.wind_note: The plateau's north slope works in northerly wind and daytime thermals off the plain; in the Trans-Ili Alatau mountains, mountain-valley circulation
almaty-ushkonyr.best_time: The warm season, thermals during the day; a flight from 300 m lasts about 10 minutes, from 1,000 m longer
almaty-ushkonyr.access: ~1 h by car from Almaty to the plateau; clubs drive students and passengers up. To the Talgar Pass, the Medeu–Shymbulak cable cars
almaty-ushkonyr.xc_note: XC flights of 50, 70 and 100 km; the main competitions of Kazakhstan and the CIS are held here
almaty-ushkonyr.rules: There's no state licensing of paraglider pilots — club sign-offs apply, and the clubs oversee safety; visiting pilots should fly through a local club. Russians don't need a visa
almaty-ushkonyr.landing: Fields at the foot of the plateau's north slope
almaty-ushkonyr.events: The main paragliding competitions of Kazakhstan and the CIS are held at Ushkonyr
pros: Close to Almaty
Training slopes and schools
Russian-speaking community
High-altitude takeoffs nearby (Shymbulak)
cons: Little information for foreign pilots
No state system of pilot ratings
Price data is outdated
almaty-ushkonyr.tandem_price_note: As of 2016–2018: a tandem from Ushkonyr 12,000–15,000 ₸ (special offers 7,000–8,000 ₸), from Shymbulak and Big Almaty Lake up to 35,000 ₸; current prices are higher — check
school_notes: Kazakhstan's oldest flying school (headed by Yevgeny Oreshkin); basic course of 15 flying days, 150,000 ₸ (2016–2018)
Other clubs in the Almaty region

mirleft-nid-daigle.description: The Atlantic coast between Aglou and Mirleft is one of the main winter destinations for soaring: a long ridge 2 km from the ocean with a hotel right on takeoff, a warm breeze almost every day and gentle conditions for students. Nearby are the dunes of Aglou beach and the cliffs of Legzira, but Aglou beach lies in a nature reserve and flying there is only unofficially tolerated.
mirleft-nid-daigle.rating_basis: A classic winter soaring destination for European pilots (Cross Country guide, tours by British and French schools); accommodation right on takeoff; downsides — little XC potential and the unclear legal status of some takeoffs
mirleft-nid-daigle.hazards: Wind from the N or S, katabatic flow at sunset, cacti on takeoff and landing, sown fields, a long way from hospitals
mirleft-nid-daigle.crowd_note: In winter and spring, lots of European school groups, but the ridge is long and pilots spread out
mirleft-nid-daigle.region: Between Aglou Plage and Mirleft, Tiznit Province, Souss-Massa
mirleft-nid-daigle.season: almost year-round; best October–November and February–May; mild in winter (~18 °C), occasional rain in December–January; hot in summer, with more stable air
mirleft-nid-daigle.transfer: About 2 h from Agadir (bus to Tiznit and a “grand taxi”), ~4 h from Marrakesh
mirleft-nid-daigle.takeoffs: A ~5 km ridge 2 km from the ocean: the Nid d'Aigle hotel takeoff (guests only) and the neighbouring former Nigel's Place (~238 m, open to all for ~30 MAD a day); Aglou beach (dunes of 10–100 m) is a bird reserve where flying is officially banned and pilots are merely tolerated; Legzira hill (~350 m) to the south
mirleft-nid-daigle.wind_note: A warm sea breeze off the Atlantic (from the Canaries side) lets you soar all day; best from the NW; dangerous when the wind veers too far N or S; at sunset the wind can turn katabatic; in the midday heat the main takeoffs are sometimes blown out
mirleft-nid-daigle.best_time: Soaring from late morning to evening, once the breeze sets in; in the morning, before the breeze, you can glide down to the beach; weak thermals 20–150 m above the ridge during the day
mirleft-nid-daigle.access: From Tiznit towards Aglou Plage, then turn off towards Mirleft; after ~10 km a paved road leads up the hill; the hotels on takeoff run shuttles for pilots
mirleft-nid-daigle.xc_note: Limited XC potential (few roads for retrieves); short trips along the coast and hops between the Aglou, Mirleft and Legzira takeoffs; getting up to ~900 m is rare
mirleft-nid-daigle.rules: According to a local operator, flying in Morocco formally requires permission from the authorities; the Nid d'Aigle takeoff is private — hotel guests only; the neighbouring takeoff charges ~30 MAD a day (2014); flying on Aglou beach is officially banned (bird reserve)
mirleft-nid-daigle.landing: Landing at the foot of the ridge (~61 m) and top landing by the hotel; watch out for cacti and sown fields; at high tide there's hardly any room left on Aglou beach
pros: Soaring almost every day, warm winter
Accommodation right on takeoff
Good for students and building airtime
Inexpensive cost of living
cons: Little XC
Unclear legal status and permits
Far from medical care
Private takeoff for guests only
school_notes: Hotel on takeoff, tandems (baptême), support for pilots; took over the Nigel's Place training base
Neighbouring takeoff and top landing, advice on flying in the region
British school, brings groups to the Tiznit coast
French school, tours to Morocco

budva-brajici.description: The main tandem spot on the Montenegrin coast: a takeoff by the village of Brajići at ~730 m above the Budva Riviera and a landing right on Bečići beach. Flights of 10–25 minutes with views of old Budva and Sveti Stefan island; some of the pilots speak Russian. The site is of limited use to independent pilots — a cramped takeoff, a tricky summer landing and controlled airspace.
budva-brajici.rating_basis: Montenegro's most popular tandem spot: a ~730 m drop to the beach and views of Budva and Sveti Stefan; for pilots, a cramped takeoff, a tricky summer landing and airspace restrictions
budva-brajici.hazards: Crowded landing beach in summer, a sea breeze that strengthens during the day, bora in winter, controlled airspace over the beach
budva-brajici.crowd_note: Several tandem companies in summer, sometimes a queue on the small takeoff; the landing beach is packed with holidaymakers
budva-brajici.season: Spring to autumn, main tandem season April–October; flying is rare in winter (rain and bora)
budva-brajici.transfer: Tivat airport ~30 minutes, Podgorica ~1 h; 5–10 minutes from Budva to Bečići
budva-brajici.wind_note: The takeoff works in a southerly wind / sea breeze; no flying in strong northerly wind (bora)
budva-brajici.best_time: Tandems from morning to sunset; the calmest flights are in the morning and evening, while summer afternoons bring a strong breeze and thermals
budva-brajici.access: A winding road from Bečići to the village of Brajići; operators drive clients up (~20 minutes); there's no cable car
budva-brajici.xc_note: Short scenic flights down to the sea; almost no XC potential. For XC in Montenegro, there are the mountain takeoffs of Žabljak (Savin Kuk, 2,244 m) and Bijelo Polje
budva-brajici.rules: Independent pilots need a licence and insurance and should contact the Paragliding Association of Montenegro; airspace restrictions over the takeoff and beach (TMA from ~500 m); the takeoff is cramped — a maximum of 2 pilots at a time
budva-brajici.landing: Bečići beach by the meeting point: crowded in summer, a tricky landing (July–August) — experienced pilots only
pros: Views of the Adriatic, Budva and Sveti Stefan
Beach landing
Russian-speaking tandem pilots
Close to Tivat airport
cons: Short flight
Crowded landing in summer
Small takeoff
Airspace restrictions
budva-brajici.airport: TIV — Tivat, ~30 min; TGD — Podgorica, ~1 h
budva-brajici.tandem_price_note: Through aggregators from €95 (Paragliding Montenegro) to €119 (Budva Paragliding); 10–25-minute flight over Bečići, Budva or Sveti Stefan
school_notes: Tandem from 760 m above Bečići, 20–25 minutes, from €119; Russian and English spoken
Tandem from Brajići, from €95

krusevo.description: Kruševo is North Macedonia's highest town and one of the capitals of European XC paragliding: it hosted the 2019 FAI World Championship, several World Cup rounds and, in 2026, the European Championship. The takeoff is on a ridge right by the town, and below lies the flat Pelagonia valley with powerful summer thermals and convergence lines. Tandems (~€86) and local guides are available.
krusevo.rating_basis: 2019 FAI World Championship, four PWC rounds, 2026 European Championship; reliable summer thermals and open airspace; free takeoffs
krusevo.hazards: Strong thermals in July–August, afternoon thunderstorms, drainage ditches in field landings
krusevo.crowd_note: During competitions (July–August) a hundred or more pilots on takeoff; quiet the rest of the time
krusevo.season: April–October (until the first snow), best June–September
krusevo.transfer: Skopje airport ~1.5 h; Ohrid ~1.5 h; Thessaloniki (Greece) ~3 h. Best to book a taxi in advance
krusevo.takeoffs: The main grassy takeoff on the ridge by the town (~1,400–1,420 m) on the east slope; there are takeoffs on the west slope and two more on the east side closer to Prilep (paved)
krusevo.wind_note: Takeoffs on the east and west slopes of the ridge make it flyable in different wind directions; in summer, thermals of 3–7 m/s and convergence lines over the Pelagonia valley
krusevo.best_time: In summer people fly from morning to evening; tandems in the morning and towards evening, XC tasks from midday
krusevo.access: The takeoff is a few minutes' walk/drive from Kruševo, paved all the way; a car isn't essential
krusevo.xc_note: One of Europe's best XC sites: cloud base 2,500–4,000 m, ~90% flyable days in summer; routes south along the ridge to the Greek border, triangles around Prilep (Treskavec monastery), north towards Skopje
krusevo.rules: No fees (“no fees, no hassle”); according to APPI, there's a 3,000 m AMSL limit within ~10 km of takeoff, and the zone is opened for major competitions. Licence and insurance are mandatory
krusevo.landing: A big landing field at the foot of the ridge (~650 m); on XC flights, watch out for drainage ditches in the fields, land near roads and villages
krusevo.events: 16th FAI Paragliding World Championship (5–18 August 2019); Paragliding World Cup rounds in 2012, 2014, 2022 and 2025; in 2026, the 18th FAI European Championship (5–16 August) and the Junior World Championship; the annual Ozone Krushevo Open
pros: World-class XC and reliable summer weather
Takeoff within walking distance of town
No fees
Inexpensive accommodation
cons: No flying in winter
Far from the sea and major airports
Little information in Russian
krusevo.tandem_price_note: ≈€86, 10–20-minute flight from the 1,420 m takeoff, ~2 h including transfer
school_notes: Tandems, guiding, competition organisation
Local operator (tandems, training)
Tandem flights in Kruševo

valle-de-bravo-el-penon.description: Valle de Bravo is a lakeside mountain town 2.5 hours from Mexico City and North America's winter XC “mecca”. In the dry season the high El Peñón takeoff delivers strong thermals and high cloud base almost every day, while tandems mostly fly from La Torre, right above the town.
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.rating_basis: Cross Country and world champions call it one of the best flying sites in the world; the 2009 World Championship and World Cup rounds; over 300 flyable days a year
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.hazards: Strong thermals of 5–6 m/s; after midday the takeoff can get turbulent; don't fly into the saddle behind El Peñón; hidden power lines in the fields and south of the El Piano landing field; heavy traffic in popular thermals
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.crowd_note: In winter, pilots from the US, Canada and Europe “migrate” here; thermals at the popular points along the route get crowded
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.region: Valle de Bravo / Temascaltepec, State of Mexico
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.season: Dry season November–May, best December–March (December–January is gentler, thermals get stronger towards spring); according to the club, ~350 flyable days a year; June–October is the rainy season: low cloud base, a short window, tandems fly in the morning
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.transfer: ~1.5 h by taxi from Toluca; ~2.5–3 h from Mexico City, with daily buses from the bus station; operators meet you at the airport
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.takeoffs: The second takeoff is La Torre (Monte Alto reserve), right above the town and the lake: a steep ramp, evening soaring in ~12 km/h westerly wind; most tourist tandems fly from here
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.wind_note: The takeoff faces south-west; in the lower layer there's almost always (99% of the time, according to local data) a south-westerly, and pilots launch in SW, S or W wind; at sunset the wind often veers westerly; higher up the wind is often northerly. Thermals from ~11:00, strong climbs of 5–6 m/s, cloud base 3,500–4,500 m; towards evening, calm glass-off soaring
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.best_time: Launches usually from 11:00–12:30; in the middle of the day the takeoff can be turbulent; tandems from La Torre in the morning and towards evening
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.access: ~45 minutes by car from town: a signposted dirt road off the Valle de Bravo–Temascaltepec highway; pilots take shared taxis from the Santa María church; you can drive up with a hang glider too
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.xc_note: XC routes along convergences and over the mountains around the lake; from December to March, flights of over 100 km, with site records of more than 200 km; the classic finish is by the lake at the Santa María landing field (~14 km NNW); regular international competitions
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.rules: Before flying, register online with Club Peñón (clubpenon.org) and get a takeoff pass (sold online or at takeoff); rules and landing patterns are posted at takeoff and the landing field. In 2025 the takeoff was resurfaced with artificial turf. An IPPI card and insurance are recommended
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.landing: The official landing field “El Piano” (El Piano Africa) — a big grass field ~2.5 km out in front of takeoff (~1,800 m); thermic at midday, power lines to the south; landing patterns are on the board at takeoff. A popular XC finish is the Santa María landing field by the lake near town (~1,790 m)
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.events: 2009 FAI Paragliding World Championship; the annual Monarca Open and El Peñón Classic; a Paragliding World Cup event (Pre-World Cup / Club Peñón Open, 15–20 December 2025)
pros: Stable dry-season weather — almost every day is flyable
High cloud base and 100+ km XC routes
Lots of schools and guides, good infrastructure in town
A pretty colonial town by the lake
cons: Strong and at times rough thermals in the middle of the day, especially in spring
Crowded skies at peak season
Altitude of 1,800–2,300 m — acclimatisation needed
Rainy season in summer
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.airport: TLC — Toluca, ~1.5 h; MEX — Mexico City, ~2.5–3 h
valle-de-bravo-el-penon.tandem_price_note: Typical tandem price in Valle de Bravo (December 2025); on aggregators, from 1,980 MXN for 25–30 minutes from La Torre, photos and video often included
school_notes: Guides with almost 30 years of experience in Valle, tandems, intensive courses, transfer to takeoff, accommodation by the landing field
US school that runs tours and clinics in Valle de Bravo every year

pokhara-sarangkot.description: Sarangkot above Phewa Lake in Pokhara is the best-known paragliding takeoff in the Himalayas: reliable daily thermals, flights facing Annapurna and Machapuchare and a huge choice of tandem operators. In autumn and winter conditions are gentle for beginners; in spring, powerful thermals and XC routes over the foothills.
pokhara-sarangkot.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known paragliding resorts: a Cross Country guide, hundreds of tandems a day in season, a national championship; views of Annapurna and Machapuchare
pokhara-sarangkot.hazards: The airport nearby and no-fly zones; strong thermals in spring and rotor low on the ridge in valley wind; heavy tandem traffic; no flying over the town and the lake
pokhara-sarangkot.crowd_note: In high season some 150–250 tandems a day launch from Sarangkot, with lots of wings in the air at once
pokhara-sarangkot.season: late September to early May; autumn (October–December) brings gentle thermals and the best visibility, spring (February–April) powerful thermals and XC; June–August is the monsoon
pokhara-sarangkot.transfer: From Kathmandu, a 25-minute flight or 6–8 h by bus / taxi; 20–30 minutes from Lakeside to takeoff
pokhara-sarangkot.takeoffs: The main Sarangkot takeoff (~1,450 m according to competition data; summit 1,592 m); Toripani on the same ridge (commercial tandems during competitions); Dikki Danda 1,520 m at the foot of the Green Wall (best for XC); Korchon 3,100 m (a day's walk to the north)
pokhara-sarangkot.wind_note: A thermal upslope wind from the valley and Phewa Lake, starting as early as 9 am; in spring, on some days, the valley wind strengthens and rotor forms low on the ridge
pokhara-sarangkot.best_time: Tandems from morning to midday; the flying window is roughly 10:00–15:30, shorter in winter; gentle 2–3 m/s thermals in autumn, powerful ones in spring (February–April)
pokhara-sarangkot.access: The road up to Sarangkot, 20–30 minutes by the operators' jeeps or minibuses from Lakeside; taxis from Lakeside and the landing fields
pokhara-sarangkot.xc_note: Cloud base 2,500–5,500 m; the classic routes are the “Korchon loop” and flights over the foothills from Sirkot towards Besisahar (the Manaslu area); the best XC conditions are in March–April, from the Dikki Danda takeoff
pokhara-sarangkot.rules: Solo flying requires a permit from the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN); according to APPI, about 50 USD and 2 photos, valid for 2 weeks (check the current rules). Solo flying was suspended for almost three years after accidents and resumed in 2025. Flying over Lakeside, the town or across the lake is banned; the airport is nearby, with no-fly zones to the S and SE of Sarangkot. Tandem pilots must hold a CAAN licence
pokhara-sarangkot.landing: Several landing fields along the shore of Phewa Lake: Lakeside (~800 m), Pame on the northern shore, at the foot of Sarangkot; the landing fields are clearly marked
pokhara-sarangkot.events: Nepal Open Paragliding Championship (Nepal Air Sports Association; the 21st edition in March 2026); Himalayan Open Cup (FAI CAT 2, 2019; organised by the Russian federation and Himalayan pilots)
pros: Reliable thermals almost every day in season
Views of the Annapurna eight-thousanders
Cheap tandems and cost of living
Lots of schools and operators
cons: Monsoon June–August
Bureaucracy and permits for solo flying
Crowded on takeoff and in the air
Haze in spring
pokhara-sarangkot.airport: KTM — Kathmandu (international), then a domestic flight to Pokhara (PHH, 25 min)
pokhara-sarangkot.tandem_price_note: Standard 20–30 min tandem with transfer; 8,000–12,000 NPR depending on the operator, a 40–60 min XC tandem costs more; photos and video extra
school_notes: Guiding and XC tours for pilots, operating in Pokhara for many years

queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.description: Queenstown is New Zealand's adventure capital and the country's main tandem site: on Bob's Peak you launch right by the gondola top station above Lake Wakatipu, while Coronet Peak has a flight park for pilots and flying year-round — from the ski resort car park in summer and from the summit via the chairlift in winter.
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.rating_basis: New Zealand's best-known tandem site: flights over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables, a gondola to takeoff, operators working year-round; for pilots, the Coronet Peak flight park
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.hazards: Strong north-westerly foehn winds, powerful summer thermals, mountain turbulence, heavy tandem traffic around Bob's Peak
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.crowd_note: In season there's a steady stream of tandems by the gondola on Bob's Peak; Coronet Peak is quieter
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.season: year-round: thermal flights in summer (November–March), in winter tandems from the top of the ski resort; spring (September–October) often brings strong north-westerlies
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.transfer: Queenstown airport is 10–15 minutes from the centre; Coronet Peak ~25 minutes; the Skyline gondola is walking distance from the centre
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.takeoffs: Coronet Peak: in summer, the ski resort's car park no. 4 or a rocky gully (~1,160 m), or walk up to the summit (1,649 m); in winter, from the summit (green gates or the back saddle) via the chairlift. Bob's Peak above town is a tandem takeoff by the Skyline gondola top station (~450 m above Lake Wakatipu). Coordinates are for the Coronet Peak summer takeoff (~1,130 m)
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.wind_note: On Coronet Peak the wind is mostly southerly in summer and mostly northerly in winter (sometimes southerly); strong north-westerlies are common in spring
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.best_time: Tandems from morning to evening (some operators fly every hour and a half from 9:00 to 19:30); strong thermals during summer days
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.access: Coronet Peak — a paved road to the ski resort (~25 min from Queenstown), in winter the chairlift; Bob's Peak — the Skyline gondola from central Queenstown
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.xc_note: In summer, thermals over the ranges around Queenstown and Arrowtown; the sources give no details on XC routes or records
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.rules: The Coronet Peak flight park landing field charges a fee: NZD 5 per landing, NZD 20 a week, NZD 40 a month or NZD 80 a year (park phone 03 442 1586); solo flying in New Zealand requires a pilot rating and membership of the national NZHGPA association (ask about temporary membership for foreigners)
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.landing: The flight park at the foot of Coronet Peak (paid landing); tandems from Bob's Peak land near Queenstown
pros: Incredible alpine views and the lake
Gondola to the tandem takeoff
Flights year-round
Well-developed tourist infrastructure
cons: Expensive
Strong north-westerlies in spring
Little information for visiting pilots
Cold winters
queenstown-coronet-peak-paragliding.tandem_price_note: Tandem from Bob's Peak (GForce, takeoff by the Skyline gondola); summer and winter tandems from Coronet Peak with Wanaka Paragliding, children's flights from NZD 299
school_notes: Tandems from Bob's Peak, office by the Skyline gondola top station
Summer and winter tandems from Coronet Peak, meeting point at 45 Camp Street

wanaka-treble-cone.description: Treble Cone above the Matukituki Valley near Lake Wānaka is a mountain takeoff by the ski resort road, with views of the lake and the Southern Alps. In summer Wanaka Paragliding tandems and local pilots fly from here, and the landing field is right by the meeting point in the valley.
wanaka-treble-cone.rating_basis: A scenic mountain takeoff above the Matukituki Valley near Wānaka with a well-known tandem operator (review rating 4.9/5); little information for pilots
wanaka-treble-cone.hazards: Strong north-westerly winds, mountain turbulence, rapid weather changes in the Southern Alps
wanaka-treble-cone.crowd_note: Only a few tandems at a time, plenty of room on takeoff
wanaka-treble-cone.region: Matukituki Valley near Lake Wānaka, Otago, South Island
wanaka-treble-cone.season: mostly the southern hemisphere warm season — November–March; fewer flyable days in spring and autumn; in winter Treble Cone has snow and the ski season (operators fly winter tandems at Coronet Peak)
wanaka-treble-cone.transfer: ~1 h 10 min from Queenstown to Wānaka, then ~25–30 minutes to Treble Cone
wanaka-treble-cone.takeoffs: The “Pub corner” takeoff, ~500 m before the Treble Cone ski resort, just below the access road, with a windsock (1,080 m). Near Wānaka there are also tandems from Coronet Peak (Queenstown)
wanaka-treble-cone.wind_note: The takeoff works in E–NE and SE wind, above the Matukituki Valley; flights are cancelled in strong north-westerlies
wanaka-treble-cone.best_time: Tandems during the day; flights average 10–20 minutes, longer in good thermals; the whole thing takes about an hour
wanaka-treble-cone.access: Meeting point at the foot of Treble Cone (2083 Wānaka-Mount Aspiring Rd, ~25–30 minutes from Wānaka), up the ski resort road; plenty of parking along the road; the landing field is next to your car
wanaka-treble-cone.xc_note: In summer, thermals over the ranges of the Matukituki Valley; the sources give no details on typical XC routes or records
wanaka-treble-cone.rules: Solo flying in New Zealand requires a pilot rating and NZHGPA membership (ask about temporary membership for foreigners); the takeoff is by the ski resort road — check with local pilots
wanaka-treble-cone.landing: Landing field in the valley at the foot of Treble Cone, next to the meeting point and parking
pros: Views of Lake Wānaka and the Southern Alps
Convenient landing by the meeting point
Uncrowded
cons: Mostly a summer season
Expensive
Little information for visiting pilots
wanaka-treble-cone.tandem_price_note: Wanaka Paragliding tandem; passenger weight 10–120 kg, under-18s need parental consent
school_notes: Tandems from Treble Cone, summer and winter flights from Coronet Peak

cusco-cerro-sacro.description: A flight over the Sacred Valley of the Incas — from a high grassy slope near Chinchero almost 900 m above the Urubamba River, with views of the snow-capped Urubamba range. In the dry season cloud base rises above 6,000 m, and experienced pilots fly from the valley back to Cusco over the ruins of Sacsayhuamán.
cusco-cerro-sacro.rating_basis: Cross Country: “high-altitude flying made easy” in an incredible tourist location; a tandem over the Sacred Valley of the Incas on the way to Machu Picchu
cusco-cerro-sacro.hazards: Altitude sickness (a few days of acclimatisation are recommended, and oxygen if you're prone to it); strong thermals and dust devils from the morning; shifting valley winds near Pisac, where four valleys meet; the evening flow after 16:00; Cusco airport airspace; roots, rocks and telecom masts near takeoff
cusco-cerro-sacro.crowd_note: Lots of tourist tandems in the dry season, but plenty of room in the air
cusco-cerro-sacro.region: Chinchero / Yucay, Sacred Valley of the Incas, Cusco Region
cusco-cerro-sacro.season: Dry season April–November, best May–September (cloud base up to 6,000+ m); December–March is the rainy season
cusco-cerro-sacro.transfer: ~45–60 minutes from Cusco airport to Chinchero and takeoff; operators pick you up from hotels in Cusco
cusco-cerro-sacro.takeoffs: The main takeoff (Cerro Sacro near Chinchero, 3,600–3,860 m depending on the source) is ~900 m above the Urubamba valley, a spacious grassy slope with views of the Urubamba range; the second takeoff, Racchi/Racchi Racchi, is above the same valley; operators also fly from Ancahuasi and the Rahuanqui eco-park (Anta Province)
cusco-cerro-sacro.wind_note: High-altitude thermals: climbs are usually ~8 m/s, with cores of up to 12 m/s; during the day the thermal valley wind is ~20 km/h, stronger with overdevelopment; after 16:00 there's often an evening “restitution” flow. Dust devils are possible from as early as 9 am
cusco-cerro-sacro.best_time: Tandems in the morning and until midday, while thermals are moderate; XC pilots during the day, when cloud base is high
cusco-cerro-sacro.access: ~30 minutes by car from Cusco to takeoff; roads lead to both takeoffs, and operators bring tourists from Cusco
cusco-cerro-sacro.xc_note: Cloud base is usually above 6,000 m (5,000–5,500 m in May, 6,000–6,500 m in August); the classics are the ~30 km “back to Cusco” across the altiplano, landing by the White Christ statue above Sacsayhuamán, and a route east to Pisac
cusco-cerro-sacro.rules: Airspace to the S, SW and over the city of Cusco (airliners approach from the west): enter the city over the ridge between Lake Chinchero and Cusco; don't land in the Sacsayhuamán ruins — only by the White Christ statue
cusco-cerro-sacro.landing: Landing fields on the floor of the Urubamba valley (~2,700–2,900 m); on the altiplano behind takeoff, at around 3,600 m
pros: Incredible views of the Andes and the Sacred Valley
Dry season with high cloud base
Easy to combine with Machu Picchu and Cusco
Takeoffs reachable by car
cons: Altitude of ~3,800 m — acclimatisation needed, risk of altitude sickness
Powerful, turbulent thermals during the day
Rainy season December–March
Little official information on prices
school_notes: Local school: flights from Montaña Sacro (Chinchero), Ancahuasi and the Rahuanqui eco-park
Tandems in Cusco since 2000, on site from May to October

lima-miraflores.description: Paragliders over the Miraflores cliffs are one of Lima's trademarks: from a dedicated paraport in Raimondi Park, tandems soar in the ocean breeze along 80-metre cliffs, past high-rises and the Larcomar mall. After a four-year break, flights resumed in late 2023 under municipal control.
lima-miraflores.rating_basis: Peru's best-known tandem spot: a flight over a big city's seafront almost year-round; for pilots, short soaring in tight conditions
lima-miraflores.hazards: Flying close to buildings, palm trees and the Larcomar mall (there have been landings in palm trees and a crash near Larcomar); a small top landing; if the wind picks up, risk of being blown back over the cliff edge; heavy tandem traffic
lima-miraflores.crowd_note: A small grass takeoff, very crowded at weekends, up to 50–60 tandems a day
lima-miraflores.region: Miraflores, Lima — the Costa Verde coast
lima-miraflores.season: Flyable year-round; according to local guides, the most flyable days are from April to November (steady breeze, but often the grey garúa haze), while summer (December–March) is sunny but the wind is less steady
lima-miraflores.transfer: ~40–60 minutes by taxi from Lima airport to Miraflores, depending on traffic
lima-miraflores.wind_note: Ridge soaring along the 80-metre Costa Verde cliffs in the wind off the Pacific (usually a south-westerly breeze); no launching without enough wind. Flights usually go up to ~250 m, and occasionally a thermal over Barranco takes you up to 500–700 m
lima-miraflores.best_time: During the day, roughly from midday to 16:00, once the breeze sets in; the takeoff's official opening hours are 8:00–18:00
lima-miraflores.access: The paraport in Antonio Raimondi Park next to the Love Park (Malecón Cisneros, entrance from Avenida Jorge Chávez) — right in the city, on foot or by taxi
lima-miraflores.xc_note: Practically no XC — soaring along the cliffs above Miraflores and Barranco, close to buildings and the Larcomar mall
lima-miraflores.rules: Since December 2023, flying has been allowed again under an agreement between the Miraflores municipality and the tandem instructors' (APIPT) and air tourism (APTA) associations: police and municipal staff are on duty at takeoff, and ~40 certified pilots work there. The rules are strict because it's a tourist zone — visiting pilots must arrange flights with the locals
lima-miraflores.landing: Landing back on the paraport at the top of the cliff (top landing, precise approach needed); backup — the beaches and the Costa Verde promenade below
pros: A flight right in the city, no transfer needed
Flyable almost year-round
An inexpensive short tandem with views of the ocean and the city
cons: Short flights (10–15 minutes), no XC
Cramped takeoff and queues at weekends
Grey in winter because of the garúa
lima-miraflores.tandem_price_note: About 10–15 minutes over the seafront; S/180–240 with the operators (often discounted and with video), 50–80 USD through travel agencies
school_notes: Tandems over the Costa Verde daily, courses for pilots (S/1,500 for an intermediate pilot course)

madeira-arco-da-calheta.description: Arco da Calheta on Madeira's sunny south-west coast is the main flying site on the “island of eternal spring”. From a grassy takeoff at ~430 m you fly over the ocean and banana terraces and land on the beach at Calheta or Madalena do Mar. You can fly almost year-round, and a takeoff facing three directions means lots of flyable days.
madeira-arco-da-calheta.rating_basis: The Arco da Calheta 1 takeoff has 5 stars on Paraglidingmap (“Madeira's best and most beautiful takeoff”), 300+ flyable days a year, an easy beach landing; small-scale infrastructure
madeira-arco-da-calheta.hazards: Rapid changes in weather and cloud on the island; wind picking up; landing by the water
madeira-arco-da-calheta.crowd_note: Uncrowded: a few tandem pilots and visiting pilots
madeira-arco-da-calheta.season: Year-round, with 300+ flyable days a year according to local pilots; more fronts and rain in winter
madeira-arco-da-calheta.transfer: Madeira airport (Funchal) ~50 min by car on the expressway
madeira-arco-da-calheta.takeoffs: The main grassy takeoff Arco da Calheta 1 (426 m) — you can launch facing E, S or W; nearby are Arco da Calheta 2, Canhas, Rabaçal (Paul da Serra plateau) and Cabo Girão (537 m)
madeira-arco-da-calheta.wind_note: The takeoff faces three directions, so people fly almost every day; the south coast is sheltered from the northerly trade wind; tandems fly in wind of up to ~35 km/h
madeira-arco-da-calheta.best_time: Flights usually from midday to 18:00; tandems are booked on the day of the flight after 11:00, depending on the weather
madeira-arco-da-calheta.access: Road up to the takeoff at Arco da Calheta (Madeira Paragliding base); the pilots help with transport and car hire
madeira-arco-da-calheta.xc_note: According to Paraglidingmap, Madeira's best takeoff for XC, gaining height, acro and SIV; the takeoff page lists the south coast records; route length is limited by the size of the island
madeira-arco-da-calheta.rules: Portugal: foreign pilots need a national licence/IPPI card and liability insurance; check local rules and the Funchal airport airspace with local pilots (Madeira Paragliding)
madeira-arco-da-calheta.landing: The beaches of Calheta (including an artificial sand beach) or Madalena do Mar by the ocean — an easy landing with no power lines or trees; passengers land seated on a protective cushion
pros: Flyable almost year-round
A flight over the ocean with a beach landing
Takeoff facing three directions
Uncrowded
cons: Few operators, tandems can't be booked in advance
XC limited by the size of the island
More fronts in winter
school_notes: 15–20 min tandems from Arco da Calheta, beach landing; services for pilots, camping; German, English, Portuguese; cash only

chegem-eltyubyu.description: The Chegem Gorge in Kabardino-Balkaria is one of the main mountain tandem sites in the North Caucasus: near the village of Eltyubyu there are several flying sites with takeoffs from 1,500 m, and the flight passes over sheer cliffs, mountain villages and medieval towers. Flights are usually combined with a trip to the Chegem waterfalls from Nalchik or the Caucasian Mineral Waters resorts.
chegem-eltyubyu.rating_basis: A popular tandem excursion from the Caucasian Mineral Waters resorts and Nalchik, with a flight over the cliffs of the Chegem Gorge; little data for independent pilots
chegem-eltyubyu.hazards: A narrow rocky gorge, rotors in wind, limited landing options, rapid weather changes in the mountains
chegem-eltyubyu.crowd_note: A few teams of tandem pilots, usually no queues
chegem-eltyubyu.season: March to November; winter tandems depending on the weather
chegem-eltyubyu.transfer: Nalchik airport ~1.5 h; Mineralnye Vody ~2.5–3 h
chegem-eltyubyu.takeoffs: Several flying sites around the village of Eltyubyu; takeoffs from ~1,500 m, flights up to ~2,500 m above sea level
chegem-eltyubyu.wind_note: A mountain gorge with sheer cliffs: people fly in the daytime valley circulation and thermals when the background wind is light; flights are cancelled when the wind in the gorge is strong
chegem-eltyubyu.best_time: Tandems in the first half of the day and towards evening; thermals are stronger during summer days
chegem-eltyubyu.access: Excursions with a flight from Nalchik (~1.5 h), Pyatigorsk and Kislovodsk (~3 h) on the road past the Chegem waterfalls; takeoffs are reached by off-roader
chegem-eltyubyu.xc_note: A narrow gorge with sheer cliffs: mostly scenic tandems and local club flights; XC potential is limited by the terrain and landing options
chegem-eltyubyu.rules: Flights through the local flying site/club (“Paradrom Chegem”, an APPI school and tandem centre); independent pilots need a pilot rating and insurance and should coordinate with the club; check airspace restrictions in southern Russia
chegem-eltyubyu.landing: Landing fields on the floor of the gorge near the village of Eltyubyu; the terrain is narrow and requires a precise approach
pros: Spectacular mountain scenery and cliffs
Can be combined with the Chegem waterfalls
Season from March to November
Everything in Russian
cons: Far from the Caucasian Mineral Waters resorts (a long excursion)
Narrow gorge, few backup landing options
Scant information for independent pilots
chegem-eltyubyu.airport: NAL — Nalchik, ~1.5 h; MRV — Mineralnye Vody, ~2.5–3 h
chegem-eltyubyu.tandem_price_note: Packages from Pyatigorsk: short flight 10,500 ₽, standard 13,500 ₽, extended 20,000 ₽, winter 23,000 ₽ (with transfer, ~10 h including the waterfalls)
school_notes: Trips from Pyatigorsk, 10,500–23,000 ₽, stopping at the Chegem waterfalls on the way
17,000 ₽ for 1–3 people or 5,500 ₽ per person in a group

krasnaya-polyana.description: Krasnaya Polyana is Sochi's main site for mountain tandems: a cable car takes you up to a launch area at about 2,200 m, from which you fly for 15–20 minutes over the Mzymta valley with views of the snowy Caucasus peaks, landing by the resort's mid-station. Flights are run by the resort and local operators, all in Russian; for independent pilots the site is of little interest.
krasnaya-polyana.rating_basis: Russia's most accessible mountain tandems: a cable car up to 2,200 m and views of the Main Caucasus Range; expensive and almost exclusively commercial flights
krasnaya-polyana.hazards: Rapid weather changes in the mountains, cloud on the ridge, strong wind at altitude, forested slopes with no backup landing options
krasnaya-polyana.crowd_note: In summer and on holidays, book flights in advance; only a few tandems in the air at once
krasnaya-polyana.region: Krasnodar Krai, Sochi — Krasnaya Polyana (Aibga ridge)
krasnaya-polyana.season: Main season May–September; in October–November and in winter, flights are possible depending on the weather and whether the cable cars are running
krasnaya-polyana.transfer: Sochi airport (Adler) ~45–60 minutes; ~1–1.5 h from Sochi; the Lastochka train to Rosa Khutor / Esto-Sadok station
krasnaya-polyana.takeoffs: The official takeoff of the Krasnaya Polyana resort is the Polyana 2200 launch area, landing by Polyana 960; the paraplan-sochi.ru operators give their takeoff as Priyut Vetrov (Alpika, 2,256 m), landing by Solnechny station (1,100 m). Rosa Khutor has no active takeoffs. By the sea, Mount Piket (~600 m) is flown almost year-round
krasnaya-polyana.wind_note: Mountain takeoffs on the north slopes of the ridge above the Mzymta valley; flown in light wind and in the daytime valley circulation; flights are cancelled when the wind on the ridge is strong
krasnaya-polyana.best_time: Tandems from 9:30 to 18:00 by appointment; 15–20-minute flights with a ~1,150–1,250 m height difference
krasnaya-polyana.access: The resort cable car to the 2200 station (a sightseeing ticket of ~1,500 ₽ is paid separately); from Sochi/Adler to Krasnaya Polyana ~1 h by the Lastochka train or by car
krasnaya-polyana.xc_note: Mostly commercial tandems from the ski resorts; solo and XC flying is limited by the high mountains, the forest and the narrow valley
krasnaya-polyana.rules: Flights only with the resort's accredited operators, booked in advance; independent pilots must coordinate with the resort and local clubs and take into account the Sochi airport airspace and restrictions in southern Russia
krasnaya-polyana.landing: Prepared landing fields by the cable car mid-stations (~960–1,100 m)
pros: Cable car to takeoff
Views of the Main Caucasus Range
Everything in Russian, easy to reach from Sochi
Easy to combine with a beach holiday
cons: High price
Tandems only, weight and age limits
Flights depend on the cable cars running
krasnaya-polyana.tandem_price_note: 13,000 ₽ for a 15–20-minute flight (the resort's “Short Flight” tariff and the paraplan-sochi.ru price), video +2,500 ₽, cable car ~1,500 ₽ extra; at the resort, 18+ only, passenger weight up to 100 kg
school_notes: The resort's official service: Polyana 2200 takeoff, Polyana 960 landing, 13,000 ₽
Tandems from the Priyut Vetrov takeoff (2,256 m), 13,000 ₽ for 20 minutes, season May–September

kurai-steppe-altai.description: The Kurai Steppe in south-eastern Altai is a high-mountain area for strong pilots: takeoffs on the south slopes of the Kurai Range at around 2,500 m, long XC routes with big height differences and views of the North Chuya Range glaciers. In summer it hosts Russian Cup rounds and training camps; tandems are available for beginners, but conditions are more serious than at flatland and training sites.
kurai-steppe-altai.rating_basis: A high-mountain XC area that hosts Russian Cup rounds; according to Tripster, one of the best places in the country for advanced pilots; remote, with a short season
kurai-steppe-altai.hazards: High altitude, strong thermals and wind, rapid weather changes, far from rescue services, close to the border zone
kurai-steppe-altai.crowd_note: Busy only during competitions and training camps
kurai-steppe-altai.region: Altai Republic, Kosh-Agachsky District, Chuysky Trakt
kurai-steppe-altai.transfer: Gorno-Altaysk ~6–7 h along the Chuysky Trakt; Barnaul ~9–10 h
kurai-steppe-altai.takeoffs: Takeoffs on the south slopes of the Kurai Range at around 2,500 m above the Kurai Steppe
kurai-steppe-altai.wind_note: The south slopes of the Kurai Range work on daytime thermals and the inflow off the steppe; high-mountain conditions with big height differences
kurai-steppe-altai.best_time: XC flights during the day, when thermals are at their peak; tandems for beginners in the morning and towards evening
kurai-steppe-altai.access: Along the Chuysky Trakt from Gorno-Altaysk, ~6–7 h to the village of Kurai; to the takeoffs by off-roader
kurai-steppe-altai.xc_note: Considered one of the best areas in the country for advanced pilots: long XC routes with big height differences along the ranges, views of the North Chuya Range; Russian Cup rounds and athletes' training camps are held in summer
kurai-steppe-altai.rules: Solo flying only with mountain flying experience; Kosh-Agachsky District borders Mongolia and China — don't fly towards the border zone, and if you travel beyond Kurai you may need a border zone permit; coordinate with the camp organisers
kurai-steppe-altai.landing: The vast, flat Kurai Steppe at the foot of the range
kurai-steppe-altai.events: Russian Paragliding Cup rounds and summer training camps for athletes (July–September)
pros: Powerful XC flights
Views of the North Chuya Range
Russian Cup and training camps — an experienced community
cons: Very far from airports
Short season (July–September)
Little infrastructure and few tandems

yutsa-pyatigorsk.description: Mount Yutsa (973 m) near Pyatigorsk is southern Russia's classic paragliding flying ground: bare slopes with takeoffs facing every direction, a gentle evening breeze and huge fields to land in. Many Russian pilots learn here and national championships are held here, while tourists from the Caucasian Mineral Waters resorts fly tandem with views of Beshtau and Elbrus.
yutsa-pyatigorsk.rating_basis: A classic training and competition site in southern Russia: takeoffs for every wind direction, treeless slopes, easy landings, Russian championships; hot in summer, with more modest XC than the mountain areas
yutsa-pyatigorsk.hazards: Strong summer thermals during the day, the “milk” phenomenon (haze/cloud), gusty wind on the crest
yutsa-pyatigorsk.crowd_note: At weekends and during competitions, lots of students and tandems, but there are several takeoffs
yutsa-pyatigorsk.season: Thermal season from the second half of March to October; tandems and soaring almost year-round in good weather
yutsa-pyatigorsk.transfer: Mineralnye Vody airport ~40 minutes; ~20–30 minutes from Pyatigorsk; bus to the village of Yutsa
yutsa-pyatigorsk.takeoffs: Takeoffs on every side of the mountain (973 m): the main ones are east (a ~350 m drop to the foot, 220 m to the plateau) and west (200 m to the plateau with the landing field, 360 m to the village of Yutsa); north (~180 m; northerly wind is rare); the south one, the “mini-Klementyeva”, is a plateau with a 50–70 m drop, ~2 km long
yutsa-pyatigorsk.wind_note: Easterly and westerly winds prevail; northerly and southerly are rare. In the evening there's a very smooth breeze, “like a sea breeze”, for soaring until sunset; the treeless slope lets you launch anywhere from 20 m up to the summit
yutsa-pyatigorsk.best_time: Thermals during the day from spring to autumn; tandems and training flights in the morning and evening in the soaring breeze; in the second half of summer you can see Elbrus
yutsa-pyatigorsk.access: ~20–30 minutes from Pyatigorsk to the village of Yutsa, then up to takeoff by off-roader or on foot
yutsa-pyatigorsk.xc_note: Thermal XC routes over the Caucasian Mineral Waters plain in spring and summer; the site has hosted Russian XC championships and junior championships (2017–2018, a PWC pre-event in 2017)
yutsa-pyatigorsk.rules: Yutsa flying ground — coordinate flights with the local club/flight director; independent pilots need a pilot rating and insurance. Check the current airspace restrictions in southern Russia
yutsa-pyatigorsk.landing: The landing plateau on the west side and fields at the foot and by the village of Yutsa (~690 m) — big and easy
yutsa-pyatigorsk.events: 2017 Russian Paragliding Championship (Pre-PWC), 2018 Russian Open Junior Championship, 2018 Russian Championship, 2017 Russian Hang Gliding Cup
pros: Takeoffs for any wind direction
Ideal for training
Big, easy landing fields
Close to Mineralnye Vody airport
cons: Small height difference (200–350 m)
Hot in summer
Possible airspace restrictions in southern Russia
yutsa-pyatigorsk.tandem_price_note: 8,000–8,500 ₽ for a 15–20-minute flight (longer when the air is working well), including the ride up the mountain; GoPro video ~1,500 ₽
school_notes: Team of pilots since 2016, 8,490 ₽, meeting point in the village of Yutsa
Tandem on Yutsa, 8,000 ₽, ride up, briefing, video

tolmin-kobala.description: The Soča valley in the southern Julian Alps is one of Europe's best XC areas: gentle thermals, high cloud base and long ridges running into Italy. The main takeoff is the big south-facing Kobala meadow above Tolmin, which hosts FAI championships; further up the valley is the Stol takeoff above Kobarid (1,405 m). There are tandems, club schools and well-developed infrastructure for travelling pilots.
tolmin-kobala.rating_basis: One of Europe's best XC areas (Cross Country Magazine), 5 stars on Paraglidingmap, FAI championships; gentle thermals and infrastructure for pilots
tolmin-kobala.hazards: North-easterly bora, afternoon thunderstorms in summer, tree landings on the forested slopes, the heliport near Tolmin
tolmin-kobala.crowd_note: Lots of pilots on Kobala in summer and during competitions, but the takeoff is big
tolmin-kobala.season: Late March/April–September (sometimes October), once the snow has cleared from the road; best May–early June and late July–September
tolmin-kobala.transfer: Trieste ~45 minutes by car; Ljubljana ~1.5 h; Venice ~2 h
tolmin-kobala.takeoffs: Kobala 1,080 m (Tolmin) — a big grassy south-facing takeoff; Stol 1,405 m (Kobarid, the highest takeoff in the valley, landing at 230 m); nearby, Kobariški Kuk 1,227 m, Matajur/Mrzli vrh 1,304 m (north-facing, for bora days), Sorica 1,470 m (record XC routes), Lijak (flyable year-round)
tolmin-kobala.wind_note: South-facing meadows: pilots usually launch around 13:00 in the westerly thermal breeze, and in the morning it can work from the east. No flying in north-easterly bora (pilots head to the north-facing Matajur)
tolmin-kobala.best_time: Thermals from 11:00–12:00 until evening; gentle climbs of 2–4 m/s, cloud base 2,000–2,800 m
tolmin-kobala.access: Paved/dirt road via Poljubinj and Ljubinj right up to takeoff (~13.6 km from Tolmin); in summer a para-taxi leaves the landing field around 11:00 (≈€8 per person)
tolmin-kobala.xc_note: The classics: the 55 km Kobala–Stol out-and-return, a 100 km triangle via Gemona (Italy), ~120 km via Bohinj. In the region — a 280 km out-and-return (Arduino Persello, 2012) and the 259.7 km women's record (Nicole Fedele, 2013); records are usually set in late July–August
tolmin-kobala.rules: The DPL Posočje club's flying vignette is mandatory: €5 a day, €13 for 3 days, €24 for 10 days; independent pilots need an IPPI card (stage 4). Airspace up to 2,900 m above sea level. Don't land near the heliport. Mountain rescue is free (112)
tolmin-kobala.landing: The main landing field is just past Tolmin (~160 m), the backup is the industrial zone before the town; you can also land by the Sibari and Gabrje campsites
tolmin-kobala.events: A well-known competition venue: the FAI Junior World Championship (Tolmin, August 2024; 90% of tasks from Kobala), regular European and world competitions in the Soča valley
pros: Excellent XC with classic routes
Gentle climbs, good for your first XC flights
Cheap vignettes, free mountain rescue
The emerald Soča and mountain scenery
cons: In winter the roads to the takeoffs are closed by snow
Little information in Russian
Flights are cancelled when the bora blows
tolmin-kobala.airport: TRS — Trieste, ~45 min; LJU — Ljubljana, ~1.5 h
tolmin-kobala.tandem_price_note: A typical tandem in Slovenia costs €120–150 (15–30 min); in Tolmin/Kobarid — Padalc d.o.o., Hostel Kobarid
school_notes: Local club: takeoff, landing field, vignettes, information
Pilot residence, shuttle, school and guiding (Kobarid)
Tandems in Bovec (upper Soča valley)

phuket-nai-harn.description: Nai Harn Bay in southern Phuket is the island's main tandem site: takeoff by the windmill on Promthep Cape or on Black Rock, and soaring over the beach in a westerly breeze. For tourists it's a short flight with views of the Andaman Sea; for pilots, small-scale but beautiful coastal soaring.
phuket-nai-harn.rating_basis: A popular tourist tandem over Nai Harn beach; for pilots, small-scale coastal soaring with a limited landing area
phuket-nai-harn.hazards: Rotors off the islet and Krating Cape when the wind veers from west; little room to land; flying over water
phuket-nai-harn.crowd_note: A few tandem pilots work here, with only a handful of wings in the air
phuket-nai-harn.region: Southern tip of Phuket, Promthep Cape
phuket-nai-harn.season: November–April (dry season, steady breezes), best December–March; from May to October rain and strong wind, flights only now and then
phuket-nai-harn.transfer: About 1 h from Phuket airport; 10–20 minutes from Rawai and Kata
phuket-nai-harn.takeoffs: The takeoff by the windmill (Windmill Viewpoint) at the southern end of the bay — a 10-minute walk from the beach; the second takeoff, Black Rock (Pa Hin Dam), to the north — ~45 minutes on foot through the plantations or via the road to Nui beach
phuket-nai-harn.wind_note: Ridge lift on the slopes above Nai Harn Bay in westerly wind (best when it's due west); in WSW wind there's rotor off the islet, in WNW off Krating Cape at the north end of the bay, and landing on the beach becomes dangerous
phuket-nai-harn.best_time: Tandems usually 14:00–18:00, when the sea breeze kicks in; 15–30-minute flights
phuket-nai-harn.access: By car or tuk-tuk to the viewpoint by the windmill; to Black Rock on foot or via the road to Nui beach; scooter rental ~200 THB a day
phuket-nai-harn.xc_note: Coastal soaring over the bay only, no XC
phuket-nai-harn.rules: The sources give no formal rules for visiting pilots; people fly by arrangement with the local tandem pilots; a pilot rating and insurance are required
phuket-nai-harn.landing: Nai Harn beach — little room down below, a constrained approach; in crosswind, rotors off the headlands
pros: Views of the Andaman Sea and the beaches
Close to the Rawai and Kata resorts
Bookings available in Russian
cons: Expensive by Asian standards
Flyable only in westerly wind
Cramped beach landing
Rainy season May–October
phuket-nai-harn.tandem_price_note: Tandem with transfer; with video — 5,900 THB
school_notes: The main tandem operator at Nai Harn
Booking in Russian through an agency; Promthep Cape

kas-asas.description: A small tandem spot on the slope of Mount Asas right above the little town of Kaş: takeoff at ~600–650 m, 20–30 minutes of flying over the bay with views of the Greek island of Meis, and a landing by the harbour in the centre. A good alternative to crowded Babadağ for those holidaying on the Lycian coast.
kas-asas.rating_basis: A beautiful short tandem with views of the Mediterranean and the island of Meis; a small place with one or two operators, of no interest to independent pilots
kas-asas.hazards: A small landing area by the harbour and the water, the breeze strengthening after lunch
kas-asas.crowd_note: Few tandems, no queues on takeoff
kas-asas.season: Tourist tandems April–October (sometimes March and November in good weather); flights are rare in winter
kas-asas.transfer: Dalaman airport ~2 h 15 min, Antalya ~3–3.5 h; ~30 minutes from Kalkan
kas-asas.wind_note: A south-facing takeoff on the slope of Mount Asas right above the town: works in the daytime sea breeze (from the south)
kas-asas.best_time: Tandems throughout the day in good weather; the calmest flights are in the morning and towards evening
kas-asas.access: The operator drives you up to takeoff from central Kaş (about 15–20 minutes); there's no cable car
kas-asas.xc_note: Purely tourist tandem flights over the town and the bay with views of the Greek island of Meis (Kastellorizo); no XC
kas-asas.rules: Independent pilots need a national licence/IPPI card and insurance and should coordinate with the local operator; the site is small and almost entirely for tandems
kas-asas.landing: Landing by the small harbour in central Kaş — a small area by the water that requires a precise approach
pros: Views of the sea and the island of Meis
Landing right in the town centre
No crowds
cons: Few operators
No schools or rental
Short flight compared with Babadağ
kas-asas.airport: DLM — Dalaman, ~2 h 15 min; AYT — Antalya, ~3.5 h
kas-asas.tandem_price_note: Tandem of ~20–30 minutes; through aggregators from £80 to ~$160; photos and video ~€10 extra
school_notes: TÜRSAB agency; according to them, there's one licensed tandem pilot working in Kaş
20-minute tandem, £80 (2026), harbour landing

oludeniz-babadag.description: Babadağ (1,969 m) towers over the Ölüdeniz lagoon — less than 5 km from summit to sea. It's one of the busiest tandem sites in the world: more than 200,000 flights a year, a cable car to takeoffs at 1,200–1,800 m and a landing right on the beach. It's also a centre for acro and SIV training over water, and hosts the annual Ölüdeniz Air Games festival.
oludeniz-babadag.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known and most visited paragliding spots (200,000+ flights a year), a ~1,700–1,900 m drop to the sea, a cable car; downsides — crowds and commercialism
oludeniz-babadag.hazards: Strong summer thermals after midday, crosswind on takeoff, heavy traffic of tandems and acro pilots, landing over a crowded beach and water; don't take your cue from the tandem pilots — they fly in almost any conditions
oludeniz-babadag.crowd_note: Dozens of tandem companies, a launch every couple of minutes; in summer, dozens of canopies in the air at once, and solo pilots have to wait for a gap between tandems
oludeniz-babadag.season: Flyable almost year-round; main season April–October (tandem peak June–August), the best conditions for pilots are May–June and September–October; in winter people fly on dry days, from the 1,200 m takeoff when there's snow
oludeniz-babadag.transfer: Dalaman airport to Ölüdeniz ~1–1.5 h; ~20 minutes from Fethiye; a few minutes from the landing field to the cable car bottom station
oludeniz-babadag.takeoffs: The main south takeoff at 1,700 m (huge, by the cable car station); west 1,800 m, north/summit 1,900–1,960 m, south 1,200 m (used when the summit is in cloud or snow); a small, tricky takeoff at 300 m (SSW)
oludeniz-babadag.wind_note: The main 1,700 m takeoff faces S/SW, into the sea breeze; in northerly wind the north takeoffs near the summit are used. There can be crosswind on takeoff
