By midday the northerly wind swings round to side-shore from the left, averaging 22–27 knots in summer and 18–25 in winter. Near the shore there's a sandbank with flat, standing-depth water; further out — chop and wind waves for jumping.
soma-bay-safaga.rating_basis: Surf Magazin: an average of 22–27 knots in summer and planing almost every day (June–October), more than 50% windy days in winter; the bay is ~1 Bft windier than Hurghada (CDWS); a large Surfmotion centre, GWA training camps; less well known among Russian-speaking riders
soma-bay-safaga.waves_note: Flat water near the shore and on the sandbank, chop for jumping further out; wind waves up to ~1.5 m about 2 km offshore
soma-bay-safaga.hazards: Offshore wind in the morning, reef banks and corals beyond the sandbank, sea urchins, shallow at low tide; occasional 30–35-knot storms
soma-bay-safaga.gustiness_note: In the morning the wind is slightly offshore and gusty; from midday it swings round to side-shore and blows steadily at full strength; peaks of 30–35 knots only a few times a year
soma-bay-safaga.crowd_note: The bay is spacious, and kiters have a separate lagoon; most of the crowd are German windsurfers
soma-bay-safaga.region: Red Sea, between Hurghada and Safaga
soma-bay-safaga.events: Annual slalom Raceweek at Surfmotion (coach Vincent Langer); the German Windsurfing Association (GWA) winter slalom and foil slalom training camps with a closing regatta on 2–9 January 2027
soma-bay-safaga.launch: Wide sandy beach by the Surfmotion centre (Palm Royale hotel); in front of the centre there's a sheltered standing-depth zone of ~100×150 m (depending on the tide), and at low tide the sandbank creates a smooth speed strip; further out there are reef banks and deep water
soma-bay-safaga.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m² in summer, 5.0–6.2 m² in winter; foil on light days
pros: Wind all year round, almost daily in summer
Standing depth and flat water near the shore, chop for jumping nearby
Windier than Hurghada and roomier than the mass-market resorts
Warm water in winter (around 21–23 °C)
cons: Offshore and gusty wind in the morning
Depth near the shore depends on the tide
Few Russian-speaking centres, a resort zone with no town
soma-bay-safaga.wind_dir: NNW→N–NNE, side-shore from the left by midday; slightly offshore in the morning
school_notes: Peter Müller's large centre by the Palm Royale hotel (~20 staff), zones for beginners and advanced sailors, slalom training
centre in Soma Bay: windsurfing, kite, wing, kids' lessons, rescue boat

costa-teguise-las-cucharas.description: Las Cucharas is the sandy bay of the Costa Teguise resort, enclosed by two stone breakwaters, and Lanzarote's main spot for learning and freeriding. Inside there's flat, shallow water for beginners; further out — a steady trade wind and chop for freeride and slalom, and with a swell a 1–3 m wave works on the reef to the left. The season runs from April to September, peaking in July.
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.rating_basis: One of the best spots in the Canaries for learning and progressing: a sheltered bay, steady trade wind, several centres; for advanced sailors — a reef with waves outside. Downsides — wind shadow from the hotels and summer crowds
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.waves_note: Inside the bay, enclosed by two breakwaters, — flat water and light chop; 500 m from shore it's open sea, with a 1–3 m wave on the reef to the left (biggest in winter, with swell from Los Charcos)
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.hazards: The reef outside the bay: in a winter swell the waves can exceed 3 m — stay inside the bay; stone breakwaters at either end; offshore gusts in a northerly wind; swimmers and students near the shore
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.gustiness_note: Near the shore there's wind shadow from the hotels and gusts; 100–200 m out from the beach the wind is steady. When the wind goes further north than NE, the bay gets gusty and offshore
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.crowd_note: In July–August the inner part of the bay is packed with swimmers and school students; it's best to go out before 11:00 or after 16:00
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.events: In the past the bay hosted windsurfing world championship events (in July)
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.launch: A ~640 m sandy beach in the bay between the breakwaters with a gentle entry; the first ~100 m are chest-deep and in the hotels' wind shadow (the learning zone); exit corridors are marked with buoys. Sometimes a moderate shorebreak — centre staff help you launch
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.sail_note: Usually 4.7–5.8 m² in summer, 4.2–4.5 on strong days; 6–7.5 in winter and in light wind. Beginners use 1–3.5 m² training sails in the sheltered zone
pros: Sheltered shallow zone for beginners and kids
Steady trade wind from April to September
Several good centres with modern rental gear
Reef wave for advanced sailors, with the Los Charcos spot nearby
cons: Wind shadow and gusts near the shore because of the hotels
Crowded in the bay in summer
Less reliable wind in winter
Wetsuit needed from November to April
costa-teguise-las-cucharas.wind_dir: NE trade wind, side-shore / side-offshore from the left
school_notes: 150 m from the water, courses for adults and kids aged 8–12, coaching for advanced sailors
on Las Cucharas beach, sails 3.0–8.2 m², 10-hour rental card, flexible booking from November to March
rental and group/private lessons, Las Cucharas

el-medano.description: El Médano is a town in the south of Tenerife known as the island's windsurf capital: the trade wind accelerates through the channel between Tenerife and Gran Canaria and blows almost all year round, strongest in summer. The long sandy bay is used by beginners, freeriders and slalom sailors (pro racers train here in winter), while wave sailors head to neighbouring El Cabezo; a PWA event is held in August.
el-medano.rating_basis: “Tenerife's windsurf capital”: year-round pro training camps, a PWA Grand Slam event, spots for every level from the learning bay to the El Cabezo wave; downsides — gusts near the shore and lots of kiters
el-medano.waves_note: In the southern part of the bay — chop and small 0.5–1.5 m waves; at neighbouring El Cabezo (the northern end of town) a powerful 1–3 m+ wave in a swell, with side-onshore wind
el-medano.hazards: Rocks on the downwind shore and by the breakwater (current at the northern end of the bay); at El Cabezo — rock slabs with sea urchins and the “Godzilla” rock at low tide; strong gusts in summer
el-medano.gustiness_note: The wind accelerates between the mountains of Tenerife and Gran Canaria; it's gusty near the shore and by the breakwater at the northern end of the bay, steadier further out from the beach
el-medano.crowd_note: The bay is shared with lots of kiters; at El Cabezo there's a packed line-up of local pros when the waves are good
el-medano.events: PWA World Cup event (Tenerife Grand Slam, waves and Slalom X): 1–10 August in 2025
el-medano.launch: The main launch is the town's long sandy beach with a shallow entry and the centres right on the seafront; kiters are usually in the southern part of the bay, windsurfers further upwind. At El Cabezo — entry over rock slabs with sea urchins, shoes needed, experienced sailors only
el-medano.sail_note: Usually 4.5–5.5 m² in summer, 4.0–4.2 on strong days; 5.5–7.0 in winter and the shoulder seasons; slalom sailors train on 6.3–7.8 in winter
pros: Wind almost all year round, warm water at 19–24 °C
Spots for every level: learning bay, freeride, slalom, waves
Strong centres with large gear fleets
Airport 10 minutes away
cons: Gusty near the shore
Lots of kiters in the bay
Expensive rental (€110 a day and up)
The downwind shore is rocky — few places to come ashore
el-medano.wind_dir: NE trade wind, side-shore from the left at the main beach; side-onshore at El Cabezo
el-medano.rental_price_note: TWS: 1 day Wave & Freeride €110 (slalom/foil €140), a week €451 (price list on the centre's website)
school_notes: right on the beach, over 100 boards and 120 sails, slalom rental from November to April, clinics
open 365 days a year, a board reserved for you for your whole stay
courses and rental next to the Duotone Pro Center

fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.description: Sotavento is a beach of sand stretching for kilometres on the southeast of Fuerteventura, with a huge tidal lagoon. The trade wind spills over the Jandía mountains and accelerates to 25–40 kn in summer; a PWA World Cup event has been held here at the René Egli centre since 1986. Beginners learn and freestylers train in the lagoon, while out at sea it's fast freeride and slalom on the chop.
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.rating_basis: A long-standing PWA World Cup venue (slalom, freestyle), one of the world's biggest windsurf centres, strong summer trade wind; downsides — offshore wind and high rental prices
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.waves_note: At sea it's mostly wind chop and a small shorebreak; at high tide a huge shallow flat-water lagoon fills up behind the sand spit; with a swell, waves up to ~2 m on the left side of the beach
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.hazards: Offshore wind: if you break gear or get tired, you're carried out into the open ocean — only sail while the centres' rescue service is operating; gusts up to 40+ kn; part of the lagoon dries out at low tide
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.gustiness_note: The trade wind spills over the Jandía ridge and speeds up (a double Venturi effect) — 30–40 kn is not unusual in summer; the wind is offshore and gusty near the shore, steadier further out to sea
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.crowd_note: Busy by the René Egli centre in summer, but the beach and lagoon stretch for kilometres, so there's plenty of room on the water; kiters have their own section of beach
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.events: A PWA Windsurf World Cup event has been held at the René Egli centre since 1986 (18–27 July in 2025, Slalom X and freestyle); since 2023 also a GWA wingfoil event
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.launch: Kilometres of wide sandy beach with no rocks; the René Egli centre is right in front of the Meliá hotels, with a second centre at Risco del Paso (5–10 minutes south). The lagoon is only usable at high tide; at low tide you have to carry your gear to the water
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.sail_note: In summer most often 4.7–5.3 m² (the most used sizes are 4.8–5.2), 4.0–4.5 on strong days; 5.5–6.5 in winter and spring. Typical boards 85–105 l
pros: Strong, steady summer trade wind
Huge shallow lagoon — ideal for learning and freestyle
Sand with no rocks, a wide beach
Big centres with excellent rental gear and a rescue service
cons: Offshore wind (side-offshore/offshore) — if you break gear, you're carried out to the ocean
Gusty near the shore
Expensive rental at René Egli
The lagoon only works at high tide; the trade wind is weaker in winter
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.wind_dir: N–NE trade wind, side-offshore / offshore from the left
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.airport: FUE — Puerto del Rosario, ~1 h (~75 km)
fuerteventura-sotavento-windsurf.rental_price_note: René Egli Premium: full day €110, a week €502, 1–2 h €90 (price list on the centre's website)
school_notes: one of the world's biggest centres, a PWA venue; licensed to teach in the lagoon, rescue service
centre 7 km south of Costa Calma, shallows and lagoon in front of the station, sails 1.0–7.3 m², shuttle from Costa Calma

pozo-izquierdo.description: Pozo Izquierdo is a legendary wave spot in southeast Gran Canaria and one of the world's “wind capitals”: in summer the trade wind accelerates along the coast to 25–40 kn almost every day. A PWA World Cup event has been held here for more than 30 years, and many champions grew up here. A spot for experienced sailors: jumps, waves and extremely small sails.
pozo-izquierdo.rating_basis: A legendary PWA World Cup spot (more than 30 years), one of the windiest in Europe: a 25–40 kn summer trade wind almost daily; downside — a rocky launch and suitable for experienced sailors only
pozo-izquierdo.waves_note: Without swell — small chop and ramps for jumping (especially at low tide); in a northerly swell the waves are usually 1–3 m, bigger on strong days; a right-hand wave with wind from the left
pozo-izquierdo.hazards: Boulders and rocks in the surf zone (especially at high tide), strong, gusty wind up to 40+ kn, powerful shorebreak in a swell; if you break gear, you drift south along the shore
pozo-izquierdo.gustiness_note: The trade wind accelerates along the east coast (a “deflector” effect), up to 40–50 kn in places; gusty near the shore, and south of Pozo there can be lulls in summer
pozo-izquierdo.crowd_note: In summer the line-up is full of strong riders and local pros (Pozo is the home spot of many world champions); the beach is long, but there are few convenient launch spots
pozo-izquierdo.events: A PWA World Cup event (Gran Canaria Windsurf World Cup) has been held here for more than 30 years; 5–13 July in 2025, wave discipline. The Wind & Waves festival also takes place in summer
pozo-izquierdo.launch: A beach of big black boulders and pebbles: you launch and come in between the rocks, shoes needed; at high tide and in waves getting out is especially tricky — it's easy to smash your gear on the rocks
pozo-izquierdo.sail_note: Usually 3.3–4.5 m² in summer, while riders at PWA events use 2.8–4.0; 4.7–5.3 in winter and on light days. You'll hardly ever need a sail bigger than 5.5
pros: Strong wind almost every day in summer — 3.3–4.5 m²
Great bump & jump, and waves in a swell
World Cup atmosphere, you can watch top riders
Warm water all year round (18–23 °C)
cons: Boulder beach — a tough launch and landing, risk of damaging your gear
Advanced sailors only: strong, gusty wind
Little infrastructure compared with Tarifa or Fuerteventura
Beginners are better off at the calm bays nearby (Bahía de Formas, Salinetas)
pozo-izquierdo.wind_dir: NE (NE–NNE in summer, closer to E in winter), side-onshore from the left
pozo-izquierdo.rental_price_note: LPWS Pozo: full kit for 1 day (2 h €48, a week €270), sails 2.7–7.5 m², boards 69–180 l
school_notes: rental (sails 2.7–7.5 m², boards 69–180 l), courses, repairs, apartments; a second centre at Bahía de Formas
sports complex on the beach: windsurf school, hostel, pool, restaurant; base of the PWA event

tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.description: Tarifa is the southernmost point of continental Europe, where the strait accelerates the easterly Levante and the westerly Poniente. Valdevaqueros is a 4-km sandy beach 10 km from town and Tarifa's main windsurf spot: in summer the Levante brings fast freeride and bump & jump on small sails, while the Poniente and winter bring waves. The big Spin Out and Club Mistral centres are right on the beach.
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.rating_basis: Europe's wind capital: in summer 60–80% of days with Force 4+ wind, two wind regimes, big centres (Spin Out, Club Mistral, Dos Mares); downsides — the gusty offshore Levante and summer crowds
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.waves_note: In a Levante it's almost flat near the shore with chop further out (up to half-mast-high by the Hurricane in spring and summer); in a Poniente, especially from October to April, waves up to 1–2 m and a strong shorebreak
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.hazards: The offshore Levante carries you into the strait (strong current, shipping): a rescue boat operates on the stretch from Campo de Fútbol to Dos Mares — a rescue card costs €50 for three rescues, or €100 per rescue without one; rocks at low tide, strong shorebreak in a Poniente and Sirocco; kiters
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.gustiness_note: The Venturi effect in the strait: the Levante is often stronger than forecast (30+ kn), gusty and offshore; the Poniente is gentler (12–25 kn), steadier and brings waves
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.crowd_note: In summer the beach is packed with holidaymakers and kiters, and zones apply; it's crowded on the water by the centres, but the beach is long
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.region: Andalusia, Costa de la Luz (Strait of Gibraltar)
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.launch: A 4-km sandy beach between Punta Paloma and Punta de la Peña, with rocks showing in places; parking behind the gates (fills up quickly in summer). For beginners — the sheltered section by Las Dunas. In summer there are separate zones for windsurfing and kiting
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 3.7–4.7 m² in a Levante (the most used sizes are 3.0–4.7), 5.0–6.5 in a Poniente; boards 90–106 l
pros: Wind almost all year round, 60–80% windy days in summer
Two wind regimes — spots for every direction
Big centres with large rental fleets, shops and sail repair
Sandy beach, campsites and a lively scene
cons: The Levante is gusty, offshore and often too strong
Very crowded in summer, with kite and windsurf zones
Cool water (15–22 °C), you need a warm wetsuit from October to April
Hard for beginners — the spot is more for intermediates and up
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.wind_dir: E (Levante) — side-offshore from the left; W (Poniente) — side-onshore from the right
tarifa-valdevaqueros-windsurf.airport: XRY — Jerez, ~1 h 30 min; AGP — Málaga, ~2 h; GIB — Gibraltar, ~45 min; SVQ — Seville, ~2 h
school_notes: right on Valdevaqueros (N-340 km 75.5), 140 Tabou boards and 280 Gaastra sails; 2026 season: 23 March – 8 November
two stations — on Valdevaqueros and by the Hurricane hotel; Fanatic/Duotone

hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.description: L'Almanarre is a long beach on the western tombolo linking Hyères to the Giens peninsula, and one of France's most famous windsurf spots. The Mistral from the Rhône valley blows here from autumn to spring, often at 25–35 kn, bringing chop and small waves for jumping, while in an easterly the water turns flat. The peninsula has several spots for different directions (L'Almanarre, La Madrague, La Bergerie), and the shallows at La Bergerie are handy for learning.
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.rating_basis: One of the best-known windsurf spots in France and the Mediterranean, a former PWA World Cup venue; Surf Magazin rates it a spot for confident riders (bump & jump, gybes, first waves), with planing wind on 30–40% of days according to the statistics and more according to locals. Downsides — summer crowds and the gusty Mistral
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.waves_note: In a Mistral (NW) — chop and small wind waves for bump & jump, with a jumping wave by a small reef on the upwind side (not very powerful, a bit weak for riding); in an easterly the water at L'Almanarre is flat — for freestyle and speed; in summer calms there are hardly any waves
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.hazards: Rocks to the right of the launch and a small reef; the strong, gusty Mistral; swimming zones in summer; don't leave valuables or keys in the car
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.gustiness_note: The Mistral is strong (5–9 Bft) and gusty, but at L'Almanarre usually a little weaker than further south at La Madrague; the chop builds as the wind picks up. Summer breezes are gentler and steadier
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.crowd_note: In summer and at weekends with a Mistral it's crowded both on the water and in the car park; noticeably quieter in spring and autumn
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.events: In the past PWA World Cup events were held here regularly. The waters off Hyères (based at the port of Hyères) host the annual Semaine Olympique Française regatta for Olympic classes (April), including iQFOiL windsurfing
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.launch: A long (≈4 km) sand-and-pebble beach on the western tombolo of the Giens peninsula; the main windsurf zone is in the northern part by the Route de l'Almanarre, with centres, rental, cafés and free parking. There are a few rocks to the right of the launch and a small reef at the upwind end; kiters have their own zone further south. Beginners are better off at the shallow La Bergerie spot on the eastern side of the peninsula
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m² in a Mistral, 3.5–4.0 on strong days (small sails are a must); 5.5–7.0 in easterlies and breezes; 5.5–6.5 on a high-volume board for beginners
pros: Lots of windy Mistral days from October to May
Several spots on the peninsula for different wind directions
Free parking, centres, a shop and cafés right on the beach
Toulon-Hyères airport 10 minutes away
cons: Very crowded in summer, with lighter wind
The Mistral is gusty, you need small sails
Water at 13–14 °C in winter — you need a 5/3 wetsuit
Thefts from cars in the car park
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.wind_dir: NW/W (Mistral) — cross-onshore from the right; SW (Libeccio) — onshore; E — along the shore, flat water
hyeres-almanarre-windsurf.airport: TLN — Toulon-Hyères, ~10 minutes (~6 km); NCE — Nice, ~1 h 40 min; MRS — Marseille, ~1 h 15 min
school_notes: on L'Almanarre beach: rental of boards, sails, harnesses and wetsuits, courses from beginner to funboard
Route de l'Almanarre: windsurf and wingfoil courses, board rental; a week-long holiday course €200 (2026)
at Camping International at the southern end of L'Almanarre bay: windsurf lessons for all levels

leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.description: Leucate is one of France's main wind resorts: the Tramontane from the Pyrenees blows here for most of the year, often at 25–40 kn. On La Franqui beach in a Tramontane the water near the shore is flat — perfect for speed and freestyle, while the onshore Marin brings waves. Next door is the huge, shallow Étang de Leucate lagoon with spots for beginners and families; the Mondial du Vent festival has been held here since 1997.
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.rating_basis: One of the windiest spots in France (the Tramontane blows most of the year), a set of sea and lagoon spots for every level, and the historic Mondial du Vent; downsides — gusty offshore wind and cold water in winter
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.waves_note: In a Tramontane (offshore) the sea near the shore smooths out — flat water for speed and freestyle; in the onshore Marin (SE) — 1–2 m waves for wave sailing; in the lagoon (Le Goulet, Leucate-Plage) flat water and chop
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.hazards: The offshore Tramontane carries you out to the open sea (also from Leucate-Plage and Port-Leucate); strong gusts; oyster beds and shallows in the lagoon; in the summer season swimming zones and a kite ban in the channel
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.gustiness_note: The Tramontane is a strong, dry offshore wind (20–40+ kn), gusty near the shore, especially at sea; the summer Marin and sea thermals are lighter and steadier
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.crowd_note: Busy at weekends with a Tramontane and during the Mondial du Vent, but the beaches and lagoon are huge; in summer zones apply, along with a 300-metre strip for swimmers
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.events: Mondial du Vent — an international festival with kite and wingfoil World Cup events, held since 1997 on Le Coussoul / La Franqui beach (during the Easter holidays, in April). The Défi Wind takes place in neighbouring Gruissan (~40 km north), not in Leucate
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.launch: A wide sandy beach by Cap Leucate, heading out via a channel; the windsurf zone is beyond the 300-metre mark and upwind (north) of the kite zone. Next door is the Étang de Leucate lagoon: the Le Goulet spot at the entrance to Leucate (big car park, shallow far out from shore) suits all levels
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.0–5.3 m² in a Tramontane, 3.5–4.0 on the strongest days; 5.5–7.0 in a Marin and summer thermals
pros: A great many windy days, especially in autumn, winter and spring
Sea spots and a shallow lagoon — for every direction and level
Flat water in a Tramontane — speed and freestyle
Close to Perpignan, Barcelona and Montpellier
cons: The Tramontane is offshore and gusty
Cold in winter (water 12–14 °C)
Lighter wind and packed beaches in summer
Oyster farms in the lagoon
leucate-la-franqui-windsurf.airport: PGF — Perpignan, ~30 minutes (~35 km); BZR — Béziers, ~1 h; MPL — Montpellier, ~1 h 30 min
school_notes: Le Goulet spot on the lagoon (Leucate-Village): lessons, rental, storage
La Franqui: windsurfing and wingfoil
La Franqui: windsurfing, wing, SUP
Port-Leucate, FFV school on the lagoon, courses for adults and kids

karpathos-afiartis.description: Afiartis in the south of Karpathos is three neighbouring bays under a powerful Meltemi: Devil's Bay for strong wind and speed, Gun Bay for freeride and Chicken Bay with shallows for learning. At the height of summer the wind blows almost every day, often over 30 knots. In 2009 Devil's Bay hosted the Speed Windsurfing World Championship.
karpathos-afiartis.rating_basis: One of the windiest spots in the Mediterranean: ~90% windy days in July–August (Surf Magazin), the 2009 speed world championship; bays for every level 10 minutes from the airport
karpathos-afiartis.waves_note: Three neighbouring bays: in Devil's Bay it's smooth or lightly choppy near the shore, with steep 0.5–1 m chop further out in a strong Meltemi; Gun Bay is smooth near the shore; Chicken Bay is almost standing water over the shallows
karpathos-afiartis.hazards: Offshore wind: if you break gear, you're carried out to the open sea (rescue only near the centres); rock slabs along the shore of Devil's Bay; squalls of 40+ knots; steep chop beyond the bays
karpathos-afiartis.gustiness_note: Gusty near the shore — the wind rolls down into the bay off the hills; steady further out. Days of 30–40+ knots are not uncommon in July–August
karpathos-afiartis.crowd_note: August is the busiest month (the centres advise booking ahead), but the three bays spread people out; Chicken Bay gets a bit cramped because of the students
karpathos-afiartis.events: ISWC Speed Windsurfing World Championship (Devil's Bay, 31 July – 5 August 2009), and earlier an ISA Speedsurfing Grand Prix event (2007)
karpathos-afiartis.launch: Devil's Bay (Vatha): coarse sand and pebbles, a bay of ~900×500 m, with flat rock slabs near the shore (marked). Gun Bay — an easy pebble entry. Chicken Bay (Makris Gialos) — a knee- to waist-deep sandbank stretching almost 100 m, ideal for learning
karpathos-afiartis.sail_note: Usually 4.0–5.2 m² in summer, 3.3–3.7 m² in a storm — small sails are a must; often 5.0–6.0 m² in May–June and September
pros: About 90% windy days in July–August
Bays for every level within walking distance
Flat water near the shore in strong wind
Airport 10 minutes away
cons: The wind is often too strong, and gusty near the shore
Little infrastructure beyond the centres and tavernas
Side-off — dangerous without a centre's rescue cover
karpathos-afiartis.wind_dir: NW (Meltemi), diagonally offshore from the left (side-off)
karpathos-afiartis.airport: AOK — Karpathos, ~10 minutes (charters from Europe in summer)
school_notes: stations in Devil's Bay and Chicken Bay, Tabou/Goya/Gaastra/Duotone, season 15 May – 1 October
Gun Bay, new gear, wingfoil
by Makris Gialos beach (Chicken Bay)

kos-kefalos.description: Kefalos Bay in southwest Kos is historically the island's main windsurf spot and, according to the local centres, its windiest place. The Meltemi blows cross-offshore, so the two-kilometre bay has flat water for freeride, freestyle and speed; the light morning wind suits beginners. Alternatives on the island are Marmari in the north (cross-onshore, safe) and Psalidi in the east.
kos-kefalos.rating_basis: “The windiest place on Kos” and one of Greece's first big windsurf bases in the 1980s (Boards, Surf Magazin); flat water for freeride and freestyle, but the wind is offshore and few centres are left
kos-kefalos.waves_note: Flat water across the big bay, even far from shore; chop and a small swell by the private Robinson beach and at the mouth of the bay. In winter, southerly winds bring onshore surf for a handful of locals
kos-kefalos.hazards: Cross-off: don't overestimate yourself — if you break gear, you drift out to the open sea (the centres have rescue boats); a marked reef; stronger wind and bigger waves at the mouth of the bay
kos-kefalos.gustiness_note: Offshore wind: right by the beach there are holes and gusts, but further out it's remarkably steady; light in the morning (Force 2–3), Force 4 by midday, Force 4–6 towards evening
kos-kefalos.crowd_note: Two centres are left in the bay, so the water is uncrowded; the neighbouring spots of Marmari and Psalidi are busier
kos-kefalos.launch: The long sand-and-pebble Kamari beach; the bottom drops off steeply and there's almost no shorebreak; for the first ~100 m from the shore the wind is uneven (you have to slog out), then it's steady. The reef is marked with a flag
kos-kefalos.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.0 m² in the afternoon, 4.2–4.7 m² and freestyle boards on strong days; big sails for learning in the morning
pros: Flat water in a big bay
The wind picks up towards evening almost every summer day
Uncrowded on the water
Close to the airport
cons: Offshore wind — uneven by the beach, and if you break gear you drift away from shore
Few centres
Often light wind in the morning
school_notes: centre in Kefalos Bay, F2/Fanatic/Sailloft Hamburg, rescue boats; instructors speak 7 languages (not Russian)
centres in Kefalos and Marmari

naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.description: Mikri Vigla is an open bay in southwest Naxos with sandy beaches on either side of a rocky headland. The summer Meltemi blows side-onshore from the right and accelerates out of the channel between Naxos and Paros, so it's windier here than near the island's capital. A good place for freeride and jumping on the chop, and family-friendly too.
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.rating_basis: Reliable Meltemi and an easy sandy entry (Surf Magazin, windsurf.co.uk, boards.co.uk); Naxos's main backup spot when it's light at Agios Georgios
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.waves_note: Open water with small to medium chop; in a strong Meltemi, a small wind swell for jumping
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.hazards: Rocky stretches of the headland downwind, swimmers and kiters near the shore, debris in the water in onshore wind
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.gustiness_note: The Meltemi blows steadily from morning to sunset; local acceleration out of the channel with Paros makes the spot a few knots stronger than its neighbours
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.crowd_note: In summer windsurfers share the spot with lots of kiters, especially by Parthena beach; swimmers near the shore
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.launch: Sandy beaches on either side of the Mikri Vigla headland: to the south, Mikri Vigla beach with the Flisvos centre; to the north, Parthena (more kiters). Easy sandy entry, with parking and tavernas nearby
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.7–5.8 m² in summer, 4.0–4.5 m² in a strong Meltemi (30+ knots) — it's best to always have a small sail with you
pros: Steady and frequent summer Meltemi
Easy sandy entry, safe side-onshore
Beautiful beaches and a quiet village
Other Naxos spots nearby (Agios Georgios, Plaka)
cons: Lots of kiters at the height of the season
Few windsurf centres, limited rental
A strong Meltemi can blow 30+ knots
naxos-mikri-vigla-windsurf.airport: JNX — Naxos, ~25 minutes; ferries from Piraeus and Rafina
school_notes: station on Mikri Vigla beach, windsurf and kite rental and lessons, rescue boats; the main centre is in Agios Georgios
Parthena beach; small windsurf rental (JP 85–105 l, Duotone sails 3.7–5.8 m²), May–October

paros-new-golden-beach.description: New Golden Beach (Tserdakia) on the southeast coast of Paros is the island's windiest place: the Meltemi accelerates through the channel towards Naxos. There's flat water near the shore and swell for jumping further out, so the spot suits almost everyone — from school students to bump & jump fans. A PWA World Cup event was held here in the 1990s.
paros-new-golden-beach.rating_basis: A classic Cyclades spot and former PWA World Cup venue; Surf Magazin calls it the windiest on Paros (up to 70%+ planing days at the height of summer)
paros-new-golden-beach.waves_note: Flat water near the shore (the wind is slightly offshore), with chop and non-breaking swell further out, wrapping round the rocky headland — good ramps by the marked reef upwind. In winter, southerly storms bring onshore waves up to 2–3 m
paros-new-golden-beach.hazards: The wind is slightly offshore — if you break gear, you drift into the channel; rocks and a reef by the headland upwind; a very strong Meltemi (30+ knots) on some days
paros-new-golden-beach.gustiness_note: Near the shore the offshore wind is gusty; further out in the channel towards Naxos it blows steadily; the nozzle effect makes this the windiest spot on Paros
paros-new-golden-beach.crowd_note: The beach and the water are full in July–August, with lots of holidaymakers and schools; neighbouring Golden Beach has several more centres
paros-new-golden-beach.events: In 1993–2001 PWA World Cup events (Paros Grand Prix) were held here, kicking off the island's windsurf boom
paros-new-golden-beach.launch: Sandy beach that gets deep quickly (within the first 30 m you can already waterstart); the centres are right on the beach. Parking is tight in summer
paros-new-golden-beach.sail_note: Usually 4.7–5.3 m² in July–August, 4.0–4.5 m² in a strong Meltemi; 5.5–6.5 m² in the shoulder seasons
pros: Strong, frequent Meltemi in summer (nozzle effect)
Flat water near the shore and ramps further out
Centres right on the beach
Easy to combine with neighbouring Naxos
cons: The wind near the shore is gusty and offshore
Crowded in summer, little parking
A strong Meltemi can be too rough for beginners
paros-new-golden-beach.wind_dir: N–NNW (Meltemi), side-shore from the left, slightly offshore
paros-new-golden-beach.airport: PAS — Paros, ~20–25 minutes; or a ferry from Piraeus/Rafina (3–6 h)
school_notes: running since 1984, Tabou/Gaastra, rental and lessons, April–September
hotel centre, Goya gear, since 2014

rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.description: Prasonisi is a sandy isthmus at the very southern tip of Rhodes, where the island's terrain accelerates the Meltemi. On one side there's flat water for learning, freestyle and speed; on the other, onshore waves for jumping and wave riding. One of Europe's most reliable summer spots.
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.rating_basis: One of Europe's windiest and best-known windsurf spots: “wind statistics unmatched in Europe” (windsurf.co.uk), detailed reviews in Boards; flat water and waves in one place
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.waves_note: Two sides of the sandy isthmus: the eastern (Mediterranean) side has flat water near the shore and light chop further out; the western (Aegean) side has onshore waves from waist- to head-high, up to mast-high in strong wind, breaking on a sandbar
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.hazards: Side-off on the flat side — if you break gear, you drift out to the open sea (centre rescue); on the wave side — broken gear and rip currents by the isthmus; sand eels in the shallow channel between the beaches; fast slalom sailors
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.gustiness_note: The terrain of Rhodes accelerates the Meltemi, so the wind is usually stronger and steadier than on the rest of the island; on the flat side it's a little gusty near the shore because the wind blows off the land
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.crowd_note: In summer lots of windsurfers from all over Europe (especially Poles on slalom gear) and kiters on the wave side; on the flat side it's crowded at high speeds
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.launch: Sandy beach on the flat side of the isthmus, right by the centres; you cross the isthmus to reach the wave side. Sandy bottom, shallow near the shore on the flat side
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.0 m² in June and September, 4.0–5.0 m² in July–August; there are few calm days — even on light days a 6.5 m² on a freeride board is enough in the afternoon
pros: Very high wind frequency from June to September
Flat water and waves a few minutes apart
Big centres with new gear and rescue
Warm water, sandy bottom
cons: Far from town and the airport (about 90 km), little infrastructure
The wind is often very strong in July–August
Crowded on the water at the height of the season
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.wind_dir: NW (Meltemi): side-off on the flat side, cross-onshore on the wave side
rhodes-prasonisi-windsurf.rental_price_note: ProCenter Kirschner, standard full kit for 1 day; a week costs €353 if booked in advance
school_notes: the best-known centre, on the flat side; JP/NeilPryde, foils, open from May to early November; website available in Russian

vassiliki-lefkada.description: Vassiliki is a famous bay in the south of Lefkada and one of Europe's busiest windsurf bases. The daily pattern is a classic: a light onshore breeze for learning in the morning, then in the afternoon the side-shore thermal “Eric” at 15–25 knots over flat and choppy water. A place for freeriding, practising gybes and freestyle, and great for families.
vassiliki-lefkada.rating_basis: One of Europe's classic windsurf bases (reviews in Boards, Surf Magazin, Windsurf UK); downsides — gustiness and a drop in wind frequency in recent years (≈40% planing days in summer according to Surf Magazin)
vassiliki-lefkada.waves_note: No waves: the bay is enclosed on three sides; in the afternoon it ranges from flat water near the shore to small and medium chop at the mouth of the bay
vassiliki-lefkada.hazards: Gusts and a sudden drop in wind towards evening — you can get stranded in the bay; heavy board traffic; stronger wind and bigger waves at the mouth of the bay
vassiliki-lefkada.gustiness_note: The wind rolls down off the mountains and is noticeably gusty; on strong days gusts exceed 25–30 knots, and it can die off suddenly towards evening
vassiliki-lefkada.crowd_note: In summer there are hundreds of boards from several big clubs in the bay (mostly British), and it's especially crowded near the shore during morning lessons
vassiliki-lefkada.launch: Pebble beach in the northern part of the bay with a sandy bottom; about 50 m from shore there's a waist-deep sandbar — handy for beach starts. The beach is narrow with little rigging space, and several centres with rental line the shore
vassiliki-lefkada.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.0 m² in the afternoon, 4.2–4.7 m² on strong days; training sails and longboards in Force 1–2 in the morning
pros: Reliable pattern: mornings for learning, afternoons for planing
Enclosed bay and centre rescue — safe for beginners
Lots of big clubs with new gear
Warm water in summer, you can sail in boardshorts
cons: The wind is gusty and less consistent in recent years
Crowded on the water in summer
Short season — mainly June–August
Narrow pebble beach
vassiliki-lefkada.wind_dir: W–WSW (the local “Eric” wind), side-shore from the right; a light southerly onshore in the morning
school_notes: the biggest club in the bay, a beachfront hotel, hundreds of kits, RYA courses, package holidays
next to Club Vass, windsurfing and dinghies, package holidays
lessons for all levels and rental

bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.description: Bol on the south coast of Brač is Croatia's main windsurf resort. On summer afternoons the channel between Brač and Hvar accelerates the westerly Maestral thermal to 12–20 knots, blowing side-shore from the right along the famous Zlatni Rat headland. A spot for freeride, slalom and foil; it has hosted PWA World Cup events.
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.rating_basis: Croatia's best-known windsurf spot: a reliable summer thermal (45–60% of days >12 knots according to Surf Magazin), PWA Slalom World Cup events; moderate wind, crowded beach
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.waves_note: Light chop and a small swell depending on the strength of the Maestral; real waves only in a strong southeasterly Sirocco outside the season
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.hazards: Swimmers by Zlatni Rat, rocky shore (shoes), a gusty offshore Bora outside the season
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.gustiness_note: The thermal is boosted by the channel between Brač and Hvar and blows steadily from about 50 m offshore; the Bora (NE) blows offshore here and is very gusty
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.crowd_note: In summer the beach and Zlatni Rat are packed with swimmers; on the water there are several schools and foilers
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.events: PWA Slalom World Cup events in the early 2020s (2021 — Zoo Station Bol PWA World Cup, 2022 — Croatia PWA World Tour, “for the third year running”)
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.launch: Pebble beach between the Zlatni Rat headland and Borak beach (the Rat itself is upwind and mostly for swimmers); deep right from the shore with no standing-depth shallows — fine for long fins and foils. Shoes needed
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 5.5–7.0 m² on big freeride boards in summer, and foils are popular; 5.0 m² on strong days
pros: Predictable afternoon thermal almost every summer day
Warm, clear water, a beautiful resort
Several schools with rental and rescue
Good for foil and slalom
cons: Moderate wind — you need big sails or a foil
No shallows for learning, pebbles
Crowded in summer; in August the wind starts later and dies off by 16:00
bol-zlatni-rat-windsurf.airport: SPU — Split + ferry to Supetar (~50 min) and ~45 min by car; in summer also Brač airport (BWK) near Bol
school_notes: VDWS centre on Borak beach next to Zlatni Rat, about 40 boards, April–November, rental from €25 per hour
station that has hosted PWA events
including a station by the Aloa campsite 2 km upwind

viganj-peljesac-windsurf.description: Viganj in the south of the Pelješac peninsula is a cult campsite village for Central European windsurfers. On summer afternoons a steady 10–20-knot westerly thermal blows side-shore from the right in the channel with Korčula, over water with light chop — good for freeride, freestyle and foil. On sunny spring days the wind can be even stronger than in summer.
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.rating_basis: One of Croatia's most popular thermal spots among Czechs, Slovaks, Poles and Germans (Surf Magazin, Croatia Week): steady wind, 50–70% planing or foiling days in summer; the wind isn't strong
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.waves_note: Mostly light chop in summer, almost flat in neighbouring Kučište; in a southerly Jugo outside the season — chop up to half a metre
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.hazards: Rocks and sea urchins near the shore (shoes), deep water close in, a gusty Bora and stormy Jugo outside the season
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.gustiness_note: The thermal in the channel between Pelješac and Korčula blows steadily and is rarely gusty; there's ~50 m of wind shadow by the headland in the northwest, and the Bora is gusty near the shore
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.crowd_note: In summer the campsites are full of Central European windsurfers, and it's crowded on the water near the shore; noticeably quieter in spring
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.events: Czech international windsurfing championships (since 2020, including slalom and foil slalom in July 2021); according to Croatia Week, Viganj has also hosted a Formula world championship
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.launch: Small pebble-and-rock beaches and concrete piers along ~1 km of campsites (Antony Boy, Maestrale, Liberan, an autocamp by Ponta point); standing depth only for 2–3 m, then it's deep straight away. Shoes needed; a narrow road separates the campsites from the sea
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 5.5–7.5 m² or foil in summer; 5.0–5.6 m² on good days and in spring
pros: Steady, barely gusty thermal almost every summer day
You stay at a campsite a few metres from the water
Good for freestyle and foil
Spring works too
cons: Moderate wind — you need big sails or a foil
Rocky entry, almost no shallows
Far from airports; crowded in summer with little parking
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.wind_dir: W–NW (Maestral thermal), side-shore from the right
viganj-peljesac-windsurf.airport: DBV — Dubrovnik, ~2 hours; or SPU — Split, ~3 hours (via the Ploče – Trpanj ferry)
school_notes: centre by Ponta point, windsurfing and kite, keeps its own wind statistics
at the Liberan and Antony Boy campsites, courses and rental, discounts for campsite guests
Polish school and rental

garda-torbole.description: Torbole at the northern tip of Lake Garda is the cradle of European windsurfing: the mountains act as a wind tunnel, and on sunny days the northerly Pelèr blows in the morning and the southerly Ora at 15–25 kn in the afternoon. Fresh water, centres for every level, regattas and training camps. The season runs from April to October.
garda-torbole.rating_basis: Europe's best-known lake windsurf spot: predictable thermal winds twice a day, a historic windsurfing centre (1980 World Championship), lots of centres and regattas; downsides — summer crowds and traffic jams
garda-torbole.waves_note: Fresh water; in a strong Ora — regular lake chop up to ~1 m, smoother water under the cliffs along the west shore
garda-torbole.hazards: Ferries and hydrofoils (motorboats are banned north of Malcesine, except scheduled services); sheer cliffs on the west shore — nowhere to come ashore; cold water in spring and autumn; heavy traffic of windsurfers and wing foilers
garda-torbole.gustiness_note: The Ora blows from March to October on sunny days from ~12:00–13:00 until evening, 20–25 kn on good days; the northerly morning Pelèr starts at sunrise and dies by midday. In cloudy weather and low pressure the thermal is weak and gusty
garda-torbole.crowd_note: In summer, especially at weekends and in August, it's very crowded in front of Conca d'Oro; it's quieter a few hundred metres upwind (to the south) or near the west shore. In spring the wind is better and there are fewer people
garda-torbole.events: In 1980 Torbole hosted the Windsurfing World Championship; northern Garda regularly hosts international regattas (slalom, foil, European and Italian championships)
garda-torbole.launch: Conca d'Oro beach at the southern edge of Torbole: pebbles and lawn, a bar, platforms for getting into the water, a big car park (you carry your gear from the car); a second launch is by Circolo Surf Torbole and at the Sarca river mouth (Surf Segnana). The water gets deep quickly
garda-torbole.sail_note: 5.0–6.0 m² in a good Ora, 6.5–7.5 (or foil) on light days; 4.5–5.3 in the morning Pelèr on strong days
pros: Predictable thermal winds almost every sunny day
Two winds a day: the morning Pelèr and the afternoon Ora
Lots of centres, schools, shops and regattas
Alpine scenery, easy to reach by car from across Europe
cons: Very crowded in summer, parking is difficult
Almost no wind in winter — the season runs only from spring to autumn
Cold water in spring and autumn (9–16 °C)
The thermal doesn't work in overcast weather
garda-torbole.wind_dir: S (Ora) in the afternoon — side-shore/side-onshore; N (Pelèr / Vento) in the morning — side-shore
garda-torbole.airport: VRN — Verona, ~1 h 15 min (~90 km); BGY — Bergamo, ~1 h 45 min; VCE — Venice, ~2 h
garda-torbole.rental_price_note: Surf Segnana: full kit for a day (1 h €39, 4 h €69, weekly pass €329), JP + NeilPryde
school_notes: the biggest centre, at the Sarca river mouth (Foci del Sarca), JP + NeilPryde, simulators; 2026 season: 9 May – 1 November
Torbole's oldest windsurf club, launch spot by the campsites

porto-pollo.description: Porto Pollo (Isuledda) in northern Sardinia is the island's main windsurf spot and one of the best known in the Mediterranean. The Strait of Bonifacio accelerates the Mistral and westerly winds, and the isthmus leading to Isola dei Gabbiani splits the spot into two bays: flat water on the lee side for freeride and freestyle, and chop for jumping on the windward side. In almost any wind there's land downwind, so it's relaxed for beginners too.
porto-pollo.rating_basis: Sardinia's best-known windsurf spot and one of the main ones in the Mediterranean: Surf Magazin cites “the highest wind yield on the island” thanks to the Strait of Bonifacio, flat water and chop side by side, and centres for all levels; Windfinder calls it one of the Mediterranean's best-known spots. Downside — summer crowds
porto-pollo.waves_note: The isthmus to Isola dei Gabbiani splits the spot into two bays: in the eastern bay, Porto Pollo, the water is flat in a westerly (on the lee side) — for freeride and freestyle; in the western bay, Porto Liscia (Coluccia), a Mistral brings chop and waves up to ~1 m at 30 kn — for jumping, but not for wave riding
porto-pollo.hazards: In a southerly there's no land downwind — you get carried into the strait; gusts on the lee side of the isthmus; lots of kiters and swimmers in summer; a very strong Mistral (30–35 kn)
porto-pollo.gustiness_note: The Strait of Bonifacio accelerates the westerly wind — the windiest spot in Sardinia; in the eastern bay, on the lee side of the isthmus, it's gusty near the shore and steadier further out
porto-pollo.crowd_note: In July–August and at weekends it's crowded on the water and in the car parks, with lots of kiters (kiting is banned in the eastern bay during the day); quieter in spring and autumn
porto-pollo.region: Palau, Gallura, northern Sardinia (Strait of Bonifacio)
porto-pollo.launch: Sandy beaches on both sides of the isthmus; the main zone is the eastern bay by the southeastern end of the isthmus, between the Sporting Club Sardinia and MB Pro Center stations (the wind is steadier there). The main car park is by the centres (paid in summer); in almost any wind there's land downwind
porto-pollo.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m² in a Mistral, 3.7–4.2 on the strongest days (30–35 kn); 6.5–8.0 in light summer wind
pros: Sardinia's windiest spot thanks to the Strait of Bonifacio
Flat water and chop in two bays a few steps apart
Suits all levels, with land downwind almost always
Several big centres, warm water in summer
cons: Very crowded in summer, lots of kiters
Gusty near the shore on the lee side of the isthmus
Paid parking in season
Centres closed in winter
porto-pollo.wind_dir: W–NW (Mistral, Ponente) — best: offshore with flat water in the eastern bay, onshore in the western bay; E (Levante) and N (Tramontana) also work; S — dangerous, no land downwind
porto-pollo.airport: OLB — Olbia, ~1 h (~45 km); AHO — Alghero, ~2 h
school_notes: VDWS centre by the main car park: rental, school from beginner to advanced, storage, bar; open from Easter to early November, 9:30–18:30
by the isthmus: over a hundred rental boards, lessons, bar, help with accommodation
base at the entrance to Isuledda: group courses of up to 4 people per instructor, from waterstart to freestyle

dakhla.description: Dakhla is a huge tidal bay on a peninsula in Western Sahara and one of the windiest and most consistent places in the world: the north-easterly trade wind blows about 300–330 days a year. Windsurfers get flat water and chop in the lagoon, the legendary Speed Spot with perfectly smooth water behind the sand spit at low tide, and several ocean wave spots half an hour's drive away.
dakhla.rating_basis: Surf Magazin and Windsurf Magazine describe Dakhla as one of the most wind-reliable places in the world (~300–330 windy days a year), with the legendary Speed Spot and wave spots nearby; downsides — the dominance of kiters and a strong dependence on the tide
dakhla.waves_note: In the lagoon — flat water near the shore and chop further out; at Speed Spot at low tide, a long strip of smooth water behind the sand spit. Ocean wave spots nearby: Point d'Or (for beginners in waves), Oum Lbouir / West Point (a long point break, cross-off wind from the right) and Lassarga (strong offshore, experienced sailors only)
dakhla.hazards: At Speed Spot, touching the bottom at speed means a catapult; offshore wind behind the spit; shallows at low tide; at the wave spots (Lassarga, West Point) strong offshore wind and rocks by the Oum Lbouir point
dakhla.gustiness_note: The trade wind is very consistent and often blows from sunrise to sunset; in summer (July–August) up to 30 knots, in winter 15–25 knots with occasional lulls lasting several days; at Speed Spot the wind is a couple of knots stronger and steadier, but offshore
dakhla.crowd_note: Kiters have taken over the lagoon and especially Speed Spot, and by local standards it can get crowded; there are noticeably fewer windsurfers. Quieter by the white dunes on the opposite shore and at the wave spots
dakhla.region: Dakhla Bay (PK25, Dakhla Attitude), Western Sahara (administered by Morocco)
dakhla.events: The legendary Windsurf Challenge at the West Point wave spot (2006)
dakhla.launch: Launch right in front of the centres on the western shore of the lagoon (Freak Windsurf Club at the Dakhla Attitude hotel, ION Club at Ocean Vagabond): sandy beach, large shallow areas for learning. The tide is strong: at high water the shallows extend ~200–300 m, while at low tide you have to carry your gear up to ~300 m to the water. Speed Spot is ~15 minutes upwind under your own steam or ~10 minutes by tractor/shuttle; the spit there is exposed for 4–6 hours around low tide
dakhla.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.0 m² in summer (freestyle 4.0–4.8), more often 5.0–6.0 m² in winter; 97–135 l boards for freeride, slalom/speed boards and a small fin at Speed Spot
pros: Wind almost all year round, most often from sunrise to sunset
Speed Spot with perfectly smooth water for speed and freestyle
Flat lagoon for learning plus wave spots nearby
Hotels and camps right on the water, no car needed
cons: Strong tidal dependence — shallow and a long carry at low tide
Lots of kiters, especially at Speed Spot
Remote: flights via Casablanca, little entertainment
Cool water in winter (18–19 °C), you need a wetsuit
dakhla.wind_dir: NNE–NE (trade wind), side-shore from the right; offshore over the spit at Speed Spot
dakhla.airport: VIL — Dakhla, ~30–40 minutes to the camps on the lagoon
school_notes: Centre at the Dakhla Attitude hotel — the best base for Speed Spot; JP / NeilPryde rental, storage, shuttle to Speed Spot for an extra fee
Large Fanatic / Duotone selection; a longer carry at low tide, waist-deep water the rest of the time

essaouira-windsurf.description: Essaouira is an old Atlantic port town and Morocco's “wind city”. From April to September a thermal boosts the northerly trade wind, and over the wide sandy bay south of the medina it blows side-onshore from the right almost every day. Good for learning, freeriding and jumping on the waves; for serious wave sailing people head to nearby Moulay Bouzerktoun and Sidi Kaouki.
essaouira-windsurf.rating_basis: Boards, Sportif and Morocco guides call Essaouira the “wind city”: a consistent summer thermal, a big sandy beach for all levels and waves in the bay; downsides — cold water, summer crowds, and Moulay is better for real wave sailing
essaouira-windsurf.waves_note: The swell wraps between Mogador Island and the shore: small waves near the town, bigger towards the south of the bay (downwind); Atlantic swells in winter, and for wave riding many go to Moulay Bouzerktoun (~20 km north, with the wind a Beaufort force stronger) and Sidi Kaouki
essaouira-windsurf.hazards: Strong wind in the afternoon, hypothermia from the wind and cold water, crowds of schools and kiters at the launch in summer; rocks by the port and the island
essaouira-windsurf.gustiness_note: Often calm in the morning; the thermal builds by lunchtime, peaking roughly from 13:00 to 17:00; up to Force 6–7 in summer, gustier in the southern part of the beach closer to the dunes
essaouira-windsurf.crowd_note: In July–August the launch is crowded with schools, kiters and surfers; there's more room further from the medina
essaouira-windsurf.launch: A long, wide sandy beach south of the medina, with the centres right by the water (ION Club / Ocean Vagabond is ~20 minutes' walk from the medina). The shorebreak is usually small, with no rocks or reefs in the main zone. Crowded at the launch in July
essaouira-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m² in summer (3.7–4.2 on strong days in July–August), 90–106 l boards; 6–7 m² on a wide training board for beginners in spring
pros: Wind almost every day in summer, peaking in July–August
Big sandy beach with no rocks, suits all levels
Atmospheric town with a medina, cheap food
The Moulay and Sidi Kaouki wave spots nearby
cons: Cold water at 17–21 °C, you need a 3/2–4/3 wetsuit
Calm mornings, sailing is mostly in the afternoon
Crowded at the launch in summer
Unreliable wind in winter
essaouira-windsurf.wind_dir: N–NNE (trade wind + thermal), side-shore / side-onshore from the right
essaouira-windsurf.airport: ESU — Essaouira, ~20 minutes; RAK — Marrakesh, ~2.5–3 h
essaouira-windsurf.rental_price_note: day rental “from” according to the Ocean Vagabond / ION Club website (2 hours from €62)
school_notes: Fanatic / Duotone, rental and lessons (2 h private from €147), gear storage
Rental from a trailer on the beach, also a base in Moulay, gear repair (per Boards, 2012)

le-morne-windsurf.description: Le Morne is the southwestern tip of Mauritius by Le Morne Brabant mountain, and one of the best-known windsurf spots in the Indian Ocean. Inside the reef there's a warm, shallow lagoon for learning, freestyle and speed; on the reef — waves from the easy Little Reef and Manawa to the famous barrelling left of One Eye. The south-easterly trade wind blows side-shore from the left, strongest from May to November.
le-morne-windsurf.rating_basis: Windsurf Magazine and Boards rank Le Morne among the world's best windsurf spots: a warm lagoon for learning and freestyle plus the One Eye and Manawa reef waves; downsides — dependence on the tide and inconsistent wind outside the season
le-morne-windsurf.waves_note: Inside the reef — a flat or choppy lagoon (~600–800 m out to the reef); on the reef, Little Reef has small waves, Manawa big waves for experienced sailors, and One Eye is a fast, barrelling world-class left over shallow coral, for experts only and at high tide
le-morne-windsurf.hazards: Shallow, sharp reef and sea urchins at One Eye; a strong current and waves inside the lagoon in a big swell (more often September–November); coral in the shallows; the reef is far out — beginners should go out with a boat
le-morne-windsurf.gustiness_note: The trade wind blows almost all day, lighter in the morning; Le Morne Brabant mountain accelerates the wind by 5–10 knots, but near the mountain and close to the shore there can be gusts and holes
le-morne-windsurf.crowd_note: In high season (July–November) the hotels are full and there's a queue of strong riders and surfers at One Eye; the lagoon is wide, with plenty of room
le-morne-windsurf.events: Annual windsurf clinics with British coaches Peter Hart and Jem Hall (September–November, via Sportif)
le-morne-windsurf.launch: A wide sandy beach with a gentle entry by the ION Club station (in front of the Riu Creole hotel), almost no shorebreak, side-shore wind from the left — an easy launch. The reef waves are far out, so beginners and groups are taken out by boat. At low tide parts of the lagoon are too shallow; One Eye works at high tide
le-morne-windsurf.sail_note: The most used sails are 4.2–5.0 m² with 75–110 l boards; 3.6–4.2 m² on the wave on strong days (small rental sails get snapped up quickly), and heavier riders will want 5.3–5.5 m²
pros: Lagoon and world-class waves in one place
Warm water all year round, a shorty or rash vest is enough
The mountain boosts the trade wind, which often blows all day
Good hotels right on the beach
cons: Strong tidal dependence: the lagoon is shallow at low tide, One Eye works at high tide
One Eye is for experts only, with shallow coral and urchins
Expensive destination, centres close around 16:30
Wind isn't guaranteed: there can be windless weeks even in season
le-morne-windsurf.wind_dir: SE–ESE (trade wind), side-shore from the left; cross / cross-onshore on the outer reefs, cross-offshore at One Eye
le-morne-windsurf.airport: MRU — Mauritius (Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam), ~1 h (60 km)
school_notes: The beach's main windsurf station, the former Club Mistral of The Indian Resort hotel; rental, courses, boat to the reef; according to reviews, open roughly 9:00–16:30
Station on the beach near the St Regis; North/Fanatic, kids' and morning lessons for beginners
An excursion-style offer from a team of Russian-speaking guides, not a station; €235 for 1.5–2 hours (price on the page)

los-barriles.description: Los Barriles is a town on the east coast of Baja (East Cape) where windsurfers from the US and Canada have been coming in winter for decades. From December to March the northerly El Norte blows, boosted by a thermal: 18–30 knots side-shore from the left, over the deep water of the Gulf of California. Ramps near the shore and long swell further out — a great place for bump & jump and freeriding on 4.5–6.5 m² sails.
los-barriles.rating_basis: A classic winter spot for North American windsurfers: Wikipedia calls it the kite and windsurf capital of Baja, and it's covered by Surf Magazin, Sportif and iWindsurf. Steady 18–30-knot side-shore wind, deep water, ramps and swell. Rating lowered for the seasonality (November–March), the windless spells between El Norte episodes and the lack of beginner conditions
los-barriles.waves_note: Chop and ramps for jumping near the shore, and further out a long-period wind swell 1–3 m high, ideal for bump & jump. The waves are smaller in the morning and build by lunchtime. Sometimes a small side-shore shorebreak
los-barriles.hazards: Deep water right from the shore, a side-shore shorebreak, fishing boats and buoys. Rocks on parts of the beach. The wind along the shore pushes you downwind. Cows and goats on the highway at night
los-barriles.gustiness_note: The winter northerly El Norte, boosted by the daytime thermal. It usually blows in spells of 4–8 days, with 2–4 days of light wind in between. Steady, with no wind shadows. Lighter in the morning, picking up towards midday (rarely before 11:00)
los-barriles.crowd_note: The beach is about 15 km long, with plenty of room. In winter regulars from the US and Canada live here; there are more and more kiters, but the water is usually uncrowded
los-barriles.events: Vela–NeilPryde windsurf championship in January (per Sportif, undated — not verified whether it's still held)
los-barriles.launch: Sandy beach in front of the Playa del Sol hotel, where Vela is based; the Palmas de Cortez hotel is about 300 m downwind. The beach is long and open, with deep water right from the shore. Waterstarting is the minimum level: there's practically no beginner zone
los-barriles.sail_note: Usually 4.5–6.5 m²; according to Surf Magazin, 4.7–6.5 for an 85 kg rider. 4.2–4.7 on strong El Norte days
pros: Steady side-shore wind with no wind shadows
Ramps and swell for jumping
Long open beach, uncrowded water
Dry, sunny winter, close to Los Cabos airport
cons: Short season: November to March
El Norte blows in spells, with 2–4 windless days in between
Deep water and waves, tough for beginners
Water around 21 °C in winter, you need a 3/2 wetsuit
los-barriles.wind_dir: N–NNE (El Norte), side-shore from the left
los-barriles.airport: SJD — Los Cabos (San José del Cabo), ~1 hour by car
school_notes: the oldest centre in Los Barriles (about 30 years), based at the Playa del Sol and Palmas de Cortez hotels from November to March: windsurf, kite and foil rental and lessons, packages with accommodation

luderitz-speed-canal.description: A man-made canal about 800 m long in the Second Lagoon near Lüderitz, the world's top speed course. Every year from October to early December it hosts the Lüderitz Speed Challenge, where windsurfers and kiters chase WSSRC records in 40–50 knots of wind. This is where Antoine Albeau raised the windsurf speed world record to 53.49 knots (~99 km/h) in 2024.
luderitz-speed-canal.rating_basis: The world's fastest windsurf course: the current 500 m speed world records (WSSRC) were set here. Rated as a unique speed spot for pros; not suitable for an ordinary holiday, as the canal only operates during the competition
luderitz-speed-canal.waves_note: An artificial narrow canal ~800 m long (the timed section is 500 m) in the lagoon; a wall of sandbags along the windward edge kills the chop, so the water is practically flat
luderitz-speed-canal.hazards: Wipeouts at 90–100 km/h in 30–50 cm of water; very strong, gusty wind and sandstorms; cold water; far from medical help, no water or food on site
luderitz-speed-canal.gustiness_note: The wind accelerates between the hills and is very gusty; runs below ~30 knots are pointless, and record days need 40–45 knots plus the right gust. The strong wind pushes the water out: at the start of the canal the level drops by about 20 cm
luderitz-speed-canal.crowd_note: About 35 participants per season and no more than 15 riders on the canal per day; runs are made one at a time
luderitz-speed-canal.region: Second Lagoon south of Lüderitz, ǁKaras Region
luderitz-speed-canal.events: Lüderitz Speed Challenge — held annually since 2007 (October to early December, ratified by the WSSRC). Windsurf 500 m world records set here: Antoine Albeau — 53.27 kn (2015) and 53.49 kn (December 2024, current), and Jenna Gibson's women's record — 48.02 kn (2024); in total, by 2021, 20 world and 146 national records
luderitz-speed-canal.launch: Start from the starting area at the head of the canal: 30–40 cm deep at the windward edge and about 1 m at the leeward edge, ~0.5 m in the run-up and slow-down zones. After each run riders are driven back to the start by pickup. Access is by sandy road; there's nothing on site except gear containers — bring your own food and water. The canal only operates during the Lüderitz Speed Challenge, with up to 15 riders a day allowed on the water
luderitz-speed-canal.sail_note: Speed sails of 4.5–5.7 m² (Albeau set the 2024 record on a 5.3 m² prototype and a ~40 cm wide speed board), short fin ~21 cm
pros: The world's fastest course, with official WSSRC record ratification
Very strong, frequent wind in the southern hemisphere spring and summer
Not just pros — well-prepared amateurs can take part too (by registration)
cons: The canal only exists during the competition, there's nowhere to sail outside it
Experts only: 40–50 knots and 90+ km/h
Middle of nowhere: no cafés, no infrastructure, cold ocean
No rental or schools — only your own speed gear
luderitz-speed-canal.wind_dir: S–SSW, at ~140° to the course (broad reach), blowing off the land across a plain
luderitz-speed-canal.airport: LUD — Lüderitz, ~15 minutes; ~7–8 h by car from Windhoek (WDH)

brouwersdam-windsurf.description: Brouwersdam is a dam between the North Sea and Lake Grevelingen in Zeeland, and the Netherlands' best-known windsurf spot. On the inner side there's a shallow flat-water basin where beginners learn and World Cup-level freestylers train, with chop further out for freeride and slalom; on the sea side — bump & jump. Atlantic lows bring strong, steady wind, and the centre is open all year round.
brouwersdam-windsurf.rating_basis: The Netherlands' cult spot and one of Europe's main freestyle venues (World Cup pros train here); Surf Magazin named it spot of the month for progressing sailors, citing a huge year-round centre and plenty of options along the dam. Downsides — cold water and planing on only about a quarter of days in summer
brouwersdam-windsurf.waves_note: No waves on Lake Grevelingen (the inner side of the dam): a shallow “pool” behind the pier with flat water for beginners and freestyle, then chop for freeride, slalom and jumping. On the sea side there's hardly any surf (a sandbank ~5 km out breaks up the swell): chop and small waves for bump & jump (the Perry's spot at the southern end of the dam)
brouwersdam-windsurf.hazards: Sharp oyster shells — shoes needed; on the sea side a tidal range of up to ~4 m and a light current on the ebb; lots of beginners in the pool behind the pier; kiting allowed only in designated zones
brouwersdam-windsurf.gustiness_note: Over the flat dam and the lake, onshore sea winds are steady; offshore (E) winds are lighter and gustier
brouwersdam-windsurf.crowd_note: Very busy on windy weekends: thousands of windsurfers from the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium; beginners learn in the pool behind the pier — slalom sailors take care; quieter on weekdays and further along the dam
brouwersdam-windsurf.region: Zeeland / South Holland (Grevelingen and North Sea)
brouwersdam-windsurf.launch: Sandy shore by the Zeil- & Surfcentrum Brouwersdam (Ossenhoek 1, Kabbelaarsbank) on the inner side of the dam; free parking right by the water, usually with enough spaces. The shallow pool behind the pier is the learning and freestyle zone; along the dam there are plenty of launch spots for both the lake and the sea
brouwersdam-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.5 m² (rental freestyle sails 4.8–5.2, freeride 5.5–8.2); 4.0–4.7 in autumn storms; 7–8 or foil in light summer wind
pros: Flat water and shallows — ideal for learning and freestyle
Works in almost any wind direction, two bodies of water to choose from
Centre open all year round, free parking by the water
Easy drive from Germany and Belgium
cons: Cold water: a 3–5 mm wetsuit almost always, full winter kit in winter
Lighter wind in summer, planing on only about a quarter of days
Crowded on windy weekends
Sharp oysters on the lake bed
brouwersdam-windsurf.wind_dir: SW–W (the best and strongest, with lows), NW–N; works in almost any direction, including anticyclonic easterlies
brouwersdam-windsurf.airport: RTM — Rotterdam, ~45 minutes; AMS — Amsterdam Schiphol, ~1 h 30 min; BRU — Brussels, ~1 h 45 min
brouwersdam-windsurf.rental_price_note: full “advanced” kit for a day, with wetsuit/harness; €98 for beginners, €190 for pro, from €22 per hour; prices from the centre's website (November 2026, year not stated)
school_notes: large centre since 1993, open all year round: courses for all levels and for kids, Severne rental, storage, restaurant, accommodation for 140 guests
a few metres north: windsurf, kite and SUP gear shop

paracas-windsurf.description: Paracas is a town by a national reserve on the desert coast, 250 km south of Lima. Almost every afternoon a southerly thermal wind picks up in the bay, and the water is flat, so it hosts Peruvian and international slalom, Formula and Olympic-class races. The most reliable months are September to March, and in December the air warms up to 25–27 °C and the water to 20–21 °C.
paracas-windsurf.rating_basis: Peru's main racing venue: it has hosted the 2012 Formula Experience World Championship, RS:X, Techno and IFCA continental championships and the windsurfing at the 2019 Pan American Games. Organisers call the bay a flat-water “wind machine”. Rating lowered because no windsurf rental for visitors was found, for the windless mornings and the cool water in winter
paracas-windsurf.waves_note: An enclosed U-shaped bay: no waves, flat water or light chop. Noticeable chop in front of the main beach in strong wind. Tides and currents have almost no effect on sailing
paracas-windsurf.hazards: The wind is slightly offshore: if you break gear, you drift to the middle of the bay. Gusts near the shore. Sandstorms in winds over 30 knots (organisers advise bringing ski goggles). Small rays near the shore at times — shuffle your feet as you walk in
paracas-windsurf.gustiness_note: Almost calm in the morning. The southerly wind accelerates over the desert and arrives around 11:00–13:00, peaking around 15:00. In the first hours the direction shifts around; it becomes steadier towards evening. Sometimes it blows into the night and builds to 30+ knots, and then a sandstorm hangs over the bay. The wind is slightly offshore, so it's gusty near the beach
paracas-windsurf.crowd_note: The main beach is mostly kiters from several schools; there are few windsurfers — mainly local racers. The bay is big, with plenty of room
paracas-windsurf.region: Paracas, Ica Region, southern coast of Peru
paracas-windsurf.events: Formula Experience World Championship (17–22 December 2012), RS:X and Techno South American Championship (March 2018), IFCA South & Pan American Slalom Championship (15–19 December 2018), windsurfing at the Lima 2019 Pan American Games
paracas-windsurf.launch: Sandy beach in the southern part of the bay, by the La Reserva condominium on the road to Santo Domingo, a few minutes by taxi from Paracas town. Kite schools use the same beach. Sandy bottom, no shorebreak. The IFCA races were run from the Oasis Bahía de Paracas beach club
paracas-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 5.5–7.0 m² on a slalom or freeride board, 4.7–5.3 on strong days. During the IFCA and Formula Experience races the wind was 12–20 knots, gusting to 25
pros: Flat water and almost daily afternoon wind
Well suited to slalom, freeride and foil
Big, safe bay with a sandy bottom
Sunshine and a desert climate with almost no rain
cons: No windsurf centres or rental for visitors found, you need your own gear
Calm in the morning, sailing only in the afternoon
Cool water (16–18 °C from May to November), you need a wetsuit
Sandstorms in strong wind
paracas-windsurf.airport: LIM — Lima, ~250 km, 3–4 hours by car or bus

boracay-bulabog-windsurf.description: Bulabog is Boracay's windward east-facing beach, sheltered by a reef: from November to April the north-easterly Amihan monsoon blows almost every day, and the waist-deep, warm lagoon makes it easy to learn and freeride. At high tide chop builds inside, and there are waves on the outer reef. From the late 1980s the Boracay International Funboard Cup was held here every year, and in 2012 the RS:One World Championship.
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.rating_basis: Windsurf Magazine (micro guide, 2017), Boards and Langyaw: a reliable Amihan from November to April (~75% of days at Force 4+), a warm, shallow lagoon — a great place for learning and freeriding, and a long history of regattas. Downsides — crowded with kiters, coral at low tide, few windsurf centres
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.waves_note: Inside the reef lagoon (about 2.5 km along the shore), at low and mid tide — waist-deep flat water; at high tide the water rises to 1.2–1.8 m, swell rolls in and there's bump & jump. On the outer reef (~500 m from shore) — waves, up to 2 m in storms, for experienced sailors only
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.hazards: Coral and rocks in the lagoon at low tide (shoes, risk of breaking a fin); waves and current on the outer reef; collisions with kiters and their lines; a narrow beach at high tide; typhoons from June to November
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.gustiness_note: The north-easterly Amihan monsoon blows steadily and almost daily; in December–February it can reach 25 knots and more. The summer south-westerly Habagat is gusty and comes with downpours and typhoons
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.crowd_note: Bulabog is the Philippines' main kite beach: in season the lagoon is packed with kites, especially at low tide; windsurfers tend to go out closer to high tide
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.region: Boracay Island, Aklan Province, Western Visayas
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.events: Boracay International Funboard Cup — an annual regatta in January since the late 1980s (it drew about a hundred Asian windsurfers and was a stop on the Asian Windsurfing Tour); 10–15 December 2012 — the first RS:One class World Championship
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.launch: Sandy beach on the island's east (windward) coast; centres line Bulabog Road, with the Funboard Center windsurf centre in the northern, upwind part of the beach. At high tide the beach becomes narrow and crowded; at low tide there's coral and rocks in parts of the lagoon — protect your fins and feet, shoes needed
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.5 m², 4.2–5.0 on strong days in December–February; big 7+ sails or a foil in the shoulder seasons
pros: Steady Amihan from December to March
Warm, shallow lagoon — ideal for learning
Resort infrastructure nearby (White Beach is a 10-minute walk away)
Outer reef with waves for experienced sailors
cons: The beach and lagoon are overrun with kiters
Shallow at low tide, with coral and rocks
Few windsurf centres, limited rental fleet
May to October is Habagat and typhoon season, with unreliable wind
boracay-bulabog-windsurf.airport: MPH — Caticlan (Godofredo P. Ramos), 10 minutes to the jetty + 15 minutes by boat and ~15 minutes to Bulabog; KLO — Kalibo, ~1.5–2 hours
school_notes: Kite and windsurf school in the northern part of Bulabog; Tabou / Gaastra, instructors from the Philippine national team, café at the station. Listed as “temporarily closed” on Google Maps in 2026 — check before you go

praia-do-guincho-windsurf.description: Guincho is a wild beach between Cascais and Cabo da Roca, and the windiest in Portugal. In summer the northerly Nortada, boosted by the Sintra hills, blows side-shore almost every day, especially in the afternoon, and the northwesterly swell delivers 0.5–2 m waves — a classic wave spot half an hour from Lisbon. In winter the wind drops and swings west, and the waves get too big.
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.rating_basis: Portugal's windiest beach (a Finisterra study: over the two summers of 2009–2010 there were 124 days with good windsurf conditions, i.e. about half of all summer days), a former PWA World Cup venue; Surfertoday calls Guincho Portugal's best windsurf spot. Downsides — uneven, gusty wind, shorebreak and few centres
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.waves_note: In summer 0.5–2 m waves from the northwesterly swell — for wave sailing and jumping, flatter near the shore in places; in winter a 1.5–3 m swell, sometimes over 4 m, with a powerful shorebreak — hardly anyone sails
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.hazards: Strong currents, a powerful shorebreak and quickly changing wind; in a westerly wind and big swell it's almost impossible to get out; rocks at the ends of the beach
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.gustiness_note: The Nortada is strong and frequent but uneven: the Sintra hills accelerate the wind and create gusts; it usually freshens towards evening
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.crowd_note: The beach is wide, and there are few swimmers because of the wind and currents — the water is usually uncrowded; on summer weekends windsurfers and kiters come out from Lisbon
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.events: In the 1990s and 2000s PWA Windsurfing World Cup events were held here
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.launch: A sandy beach about 1 km long with dunes; windsurfers usually launch from the northern part of the beach by Bar do Guincho, where there's parking and space to rig. You need to be able to get out through the shorebreak; in a westerly (onshore) wind with swell getting out is almost impossible
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m² in summer, 3.7–4.2 on strong days; you'll hardly ever need a sail bigger than 5.7
pros: Strong Nortada almost every summer day
Good waves for wave sailing and jumping
Uncrowded water — few swimmers
Half an hour from Lisbon airport
cons: Gusty, uneven wind because of the Sintra hills
Powerful shorebreak and currents
Even in summer the water is 17–18 °C (upwelling) — you need a wetsuit
Few centres and little rental right on the beach
praia-do-guincho-windsurf.wind_dir: N–NNW (Nortada) — side-shore from the right; W — onshore, poor
school_notes: school in Cascais (Rua da Torre): windsurf, kite and wingfoil courses (10-hour package with gear)
yacht club in Cascais bay (~8 km): windsurf courses on calm water

viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.description: Cabedelo beach, across from the town of Viana do Castelo at the mouth of the Lima river, is one of Portugal's best windsurf spots. From late April to September the thermal Nortada blows side-shore from morning to evening, bringing chop and jumping waves, and a westerly swell brings good waves. Nearby in the harbour there's shallow flat water for learning, and in 2018 the spot hosted a PWA Slalom and Freestyle World Cup event.
