viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.rating_basis: Surf Magazin wonders whether this is Portugal's best spot (“as many options as three ordinary spots”); it hosted a PWA World Cup event in 2018; a consistent Nortada from late April to September, conditions for all levels and a sports hotel right by the spot. Downsides — cool water and small waves in summer
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.waves_note: On Cabedelo beach — chop and waves; in a westerly swell over 2 m, quality waves over a firm sandy bottom (weaker as the tide rises, closing out in big swell); in summer the waves are often small. By the harbour's big breakwater — completely flat water for beginners and freeride
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.hazards: A few rocks in the water — watch your fins; current at the Lima river mouth; the waves close out in big swell
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.gustiness_note: The thermal Nortada is consistent, often blows from morning to sunset and strengthens during the day (often 25 kn); gusty in spring with swell
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.crowd_note: Lots of windsurfers and kiters on the water in summer and at weekends, but the beach is big; quieter on weekdays
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.events: In June 2018 — the first PWA World Cup event in Viana (slalom and freestyle) on Cabedelo beach
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.launch: A big horseshoe-shaped sandy beach south of the Lima river mouth; parking behind the breakwater (~400 m to the water); windsurfers usually launch further south, by the campsite and the FeelViana water sports centre. The main zone is watched by lifeguards (boat and jet ski). Beginners learn on the shallow flat water by the harbour breakwater — all year round
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.5–5.5 m² in summer, 4.0–4.2 on strong days; 5.5–6.5 in the mornings and on light days
pros: Reliable Nortada from late April to September, often all day
Several types of water close together: waves, chop and flat water by the breakwater
Suits all levels, lifeguards in the main zone
Sports hotel and water sports centre right at the spot
cons: Cool water (16–18 °C in summer) — you need a wetsuit
The waves are often small in summer
Unreliable wind and rain in winter
Few other centres
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.wind_dir: N–NNW (Nortada) — side-shore / side-offshore from the right
viana-do-castelo-cabedelo-windsurf.airport: OPO — Porto, ~50 minutes (~70 km); VGO — Vigo (Spain), ~1 h
school_notes: water sports centre and sports hotel on Cabedelo beach: courses for all levels, North Sails rental, kite, wing, surfing, SUP

anapa-bugaz-spit.description: The Bugaz Spit near the village of Blagoveshchenskaya, 20 km from Anapa, is the main wind spot on the Black Sea coast around Anapa. A narrow sand spit separates the shallow Bugaz lagoon (liman), where beginners learn and people sail on flat water, from the sea, where onshore winds bring chop and small waves. The best months are May, June and September.
anapa-bugaz-spit.rating_basis: Anapa's main wind spot: a flat-water lagoon for learning and the sea for advanced sailors, ~10 kite schools and 2 windsurf schools (tonkosti); the best months are May, June and September (putevka.com), and the wind can be light in summer
anapa-bugaz-spit.waves_note: On the Bugaz (Kiziltash) lagoon — flat water and light chop; at sea in onshore wind — chop and small waves with a gentle shorebreak
anapa-bugaz-spit.hazards: Lots of kites, the offshore northeasterly (Bora) at sea, weed and shallows in the lagoon, sun with no shade, cold water in spring and October
anapa-bugaz-spit.gustiness_note: The summer sea wind is fairly steady; the northeasterly (Bora) in autumn and winter is strong and gusty — and offshore at sea
anapa-bugaz-spit.crowd_note: About a dozen kite schools: lots of kites on the water at weekends, and the roads to the spit are jammed with cars
anapa-bugaz-spit.launch: A sand spit ~12 km long and 250–300 m wide between the lagoon and the sea: beginners learn on the shallow lagoon (lots of weed), advanced sailors head out to sea, with a gentle entry. Access to the spit is paid (~400 ₽), and the road is sandy — you need a high-clearance car; there's almost no shade or infrastructure
anapa-bugaz-spit.sail_note: Usually 6.0–8.0 m² or foil in summer; 4.5–5.5 m² in strong wind in spring and autumn
pros: Shallow flat-water lagoon for learning right next to the sea
Windier than the other Anapa beaches
Russian-speaking centres and schools
cons: The wind can be light in summer
Weed in the lagoon, no shade or services on the spit
Lots of kites, a bad road and paid access
anapa-bugaz-spit.wind_dir: SW–W (onshore at sea), NE — on the lagoon
anapa-bugaz-spit.airport: KRR — Krasnodar, ~2.5–3 h by car (Anapa airport has been closed to passenger flights since 2022); Anapa railway station ~30 min
school_notes: on the Bugaz Spit: windsurf rental and lessons, for adults and kids
windsurf station right in the village of Blagoveshchenskaya, with parking — no need to drive out to the spit
in Anapa itself, Malaya Bukhta beach: windsurf rental and lessons

dolzhanskaya-kosa.description: The Dolzhanskaya Spit (Dolgaya Spit) by the village of Dolzhanskaya is one of Russia's main windsurfing and kiting places. The narrow sand spit separates Taganrog Bay from the Sea of Azov, so in almost any wind one side is side-shore with shallow, standing-depth water. In summer the wind is more often light; the best season is September.
dolzhanskaya-kosa.rating_basis: One of Russia's main windsurf and kite spots: two sides of the spit for different winds, shallows for learning, centres and the annual “Dolzhanka DA!” festival; the wind is often light in summer, with the best conditions in autumn (make-trip, tonkosti, reviews)
dolzhanskaya-kosa.waves_note: The spit is ~11 km long: flat water on the lee side, chop and short Azov waves of up to 1 m in strong wind on the windward side
dolzhanskaya-kosa.hazards: Shallows (fin/foil hitting the bottom), kiters, jellyfish and algal blooms in summer, squalls with passing fronts, cold water in spring and October
dolzhanskaya-kosa.gustiness_note: Over the steppe and the sea the wind is fairly unobstructed; light breezes blow in summer, while spring and autumn bring stronger, steadier northeasterlies, sometimes with squalls
dolzhanskaya-kosa.crowd_note: Lots of kiters and windsurfers in summer and during the festival, but the spit is long — you can move away from the crowd
dolzhanskaya-kosa.region: Dolzhanskaya village, Yeysk District, Krasnodar Krai (Sea of Azov)
dolzhanskaya-kosa.events: “Dolzhanka DA!” amateur kite and windsurf festival at the Surfpriyut base (traditionally in September; flat-water marathon races)
dolzhanskaya-kosa.launch: A sand spit a few hundred metres wide: Taganrog Bay on one side, the open Sea of Azov on the other; you pick the side according to the wind. Very shallow, with standing-depth water far out from the shore — ideal for learning, but use short fins and take care with a foil
dolzhanskaya-kosa.sail_note: Usually 6.5–8.5 m² on a wide board or foil in summer; 4.5–5.8 m² in a strong northeasterly in autumn and spring
pros: Two sides of the spit — you can sail in different wind directions
Shallow and safe for learning
Russian-speaking centres and schools, warm sea in summer
cons: Often light wind in summer — you need big sails
Very shallow: fins and foils catch the bottom
A long way to get there, lots of kites in summer
dolzhanskaya-kosa.wind_dir: NE–E and SW–W, along/across the spit — you choose the side where the wind is side-shore
dolzhanskaya-kosa.airport: KRR — Krasnodar, ~3.5 h by car (Rostov and Anapa airports have been closed to passenger flights since 2022); train to Yeysk (~40 km)
school_notes: windsurf station at the Surfpriyut base on the Dolgaya Spit: windsurf, kite and wing lessons, rental; operates on both sides of the spit

gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.description: The beaches between Sestroretsk and Solnechnoye on the north shore of the Gulf of Finland are St Petersburg's main wind spot. With westerly and southwesterly lows the wind blows onshore here, and a short wind chop of up to 1–1.5 m builds over the shallow sandy bottom, while in light wind you can learn and sail on big sails. The season runs from May to October; autumn is the windiest period, but the water is cold by then.
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.rating_basis: St Petersburg's main wind beach: a shallow sandy bottom, windsurf and kite stations, wind waves in westerlies (Vokrug Sveta, Delovoy Peterburg); the water is cold, and reliable wind comes mainly in autumn
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.waves_note: Brackish water; in westerly and northwesterly winds, wind waves of up to 1–1.5 m with a short period (4–5 s); flat water and chop in light wind
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.hazards: Cold water (risk of hypothermia in spring and autumn), boulders in the shallows, a sideways current, stormy onshore wind, kiters and surfers nearby
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.gustiness_note: The wind comes in off the open water of the gulf and is fairly steady; good days come with low-pressure systems — more often in autumn, with lighter wind in summer
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.crowd_note: On windy weekends windsurfers, kiters and surfers share the water; uncrowded on weekdays
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.region: Kurortny District of St Petersburg, north shore of the Gulf of Finland
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.launch: A wide sandy beach between Sestroretsky Kurort and Solnechnoye (the former “Dyuny” holiday centre, next to “Laskovy” beach); shallow — chest-deep about 20 m from the shore, with boulders in places. There's a slight sideways current
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.sail_note: Usually 6.5–8.5 m² or foil in summer; 4.5–5.5 m² in stormy southwesterlies and westerlies in autumn
pros: The closest sea spot to St Petersburg, with rental stations
Shallow sandy bottom — easy to learn
Wind waves for jumping in westerlies
cons: Cold water, you need a wetsuit all season
Often light wind in summer
Boulders in places, poor water quality for swimming
gulf-of-finland-solnechnoye.airport: LED — Pulkovo, ~1 h; ~40–60 min from central St Petersburg
school_notes: station on the beach of the former “Dyuny” holiday centre in Sestroretsk: windsurf lessons and rental
station by Primorskoye Highway (km 41), kite and windsurfing

pirogovskoe-reservoir.description: The Pirogovo Reservoir north of Moscow is the main place where Moscow windsurfers sail and learn. The Marabu surf club has been running here for years, with rental, a school and storage, and the Pirogovo yacht club is next door. The wind is mostly light and gusty, so this is a spot for learning, big sails and weekend foiling, rather than a destination in itself.
pirogovskoe-reservoir.rating_basis: The main windsurf venue near Moscow and where many Moscow windsurfers got started; but according to riders (T—Zh), in summer the wind is usually 5–7 m/s and very rarely over 10 m/s, so planing days are few
pirogovskoe-reservoir.waves_note: Fresh water, flat or short chop; small waves in strong wind and from motorboats
pirogovskoe-reservoir.hazards: Motorboats and their wake, yachts during regattas, cold water in May and September, wind holes near the shore, a dilapidated pier deck (according to reviews)
pirogovskoe-reservoir.gustiness_note: The reservoir is surrounded by forest and villages — the wind is light, gusty and patchy; good days come mainly with passing fronts, in spring and September
pirogovskoe-reservoir.crowd_note: Busy at weekends: yachts, motorboats, SUPs and wakeboarding; uncrowded on weekdays
pirogovskoe-reservoir.launch: Launch from the pier and shore by the Marabu surf club in the village of Boltino (Orekhovaya St., 2); there are containers for seasonal gear storage. Paid parking (according to reviews, 500 ₽ at weekends)
pirogovskoe-reservoir.sail_note: Most often 7.5–9.5 m² on wide 130–160 l boards or foil; 5.5–6.5 m² on the rare strong days. 4.7–5.5 m² is enough for learning
pros: The closest windsurf spot to Moscow with rental and a school
Gear storage right by the water
Good for learning and foiling in light wind
cons: Light, gusty wind, planing is rare
Lots of motorboats and yachts at weekends
Short season: May to September, ice in winter
pirogovskoe-reservoir.wind_dir: W, SW, S, N — depends on passing weather systems
pirogovskoe-reservoir.airport: SVO — Sheremetyevo, ~40 min; ~1 h from central Moscow
school_notes: Boltino: windsurf rental and lessons, e-foil, wakeboarding; gear storage in containers
Pirogovo yacht club, which runs a “Windsurf Helmsman” programme
kids' windsurf school (Strogino and the Pirogovo Reservoir), snowkiting in winter

pattaya-jomtien.description: Jomtien and neighbouring Na Jomtien beach south of Pattaya are the centre of Thai national windsurfing and a handy place to combine a beach holiday with sailing. The wind is moderate (8–18 knots on average), so people sail big sails and foils; the best months are July–August with the southwest monsoon. Warm, shallow water and a sandy bottom make the spot good for learning, and Pattaya has long been popular with Russian-speaking tourists.
pattaya-jomtien.rating_basis: Older Gulf of Thailand spot guides, Unplug and Techno293.org: warm, shallow water and a sandy bottom — a good place for learning and big-sail sailing, and the centre of Thai national windsurfing. But the wind is light (8–18 knots) with no clear peak — as a dedicated windsurf destination it falls behind Mui Ne and Boracay
pattaya-jomtien.waves_note: No swell: from flat water to chop and small wind waves in a strong southwesterly in summer
pattaya-jomtien.hazards: In winter the northeasterly is offshore (it can blow you away from the shore); in a strong southwesterly there's a rip near the shore; jet skis and boats at Jomtien; strong sun
pattaya-jomtien.gustiness_note: A light-wind spot: the average wind is 8–18 knots, and the best days come with the summer southwest monsoon (July–August, up to 18–20 knots onshore) and the daytime sea breeze; the winter northeasterly blows offshore and is gusty
pattaya-jomtien.crowd_note: Uncrowded water: several centres, kiters and wing foilers; more locals at weekends
pattaya-jomtien.region: Pattaya, Chonburi Province, Gulf of Thailand (Na Jomtien beach, ~12 km south of the centre)
pattaya-jomtien.events: The Windsurfing Association of Thailand is based here (local races with up to 70 entrants); 25–30 November 2025 — the Techno 293 and Techno 293 Plus Asian Championships on Jomtien beach
pattaya-jomtien.launch: The long (over 4 km) sandy Na Jomtien beach with no rocks, reefs or coral; by the centres (Clubloongchat, Amara Watersports) it's an easy launch straight off the beach, shallow near the shore — handy for learning. The beach is public, with parking, showers and cafés nearby
pattaya-jomtien.sail_note: Main sails 6.0–8.5 m² with wide boards; 5.5–6.5 on the best summer days. A good place for foiling and big freeride kits
pros: Warm water all year round, shallow sandy bottom
Great for learning and foiling
Huge tourist infrastructure and lots of Russian speakers
Close to Bangkok and U-Tapao airport
cons: Light, inconsistent wind, you need 6–8.5 m² sails
The winter northeasterly blows offshore
The water isn't the cleanest
No distinct world-class wind season
pattaya-jomtien.wind_dir: Summer: SW–S, onshore / side-onshore; winter: NE–N, side-offshore (in the mornings), with a side-onshore NW–W sea breeze during the day
pattaya-jomtien.airport: UTP — U-Tapao, ~25–30 km (~35 minutes); BKK — Bangkok Suvarnabhumi, ~125 km (1.5–2 hours)
school_notes: A family-run club now in its third generation, Na Jomtien (Soi 14): windsurf, kite, wing, Hobie Cat; freeride kit rental 700 baht/hour or 1,500 baht/3 hours (price list on the website, checked in November 2026), gear storage
School and shop of Amara, who represented Thailand's national windsurf team for 25 years, on Na Jomtien beach, running for over 30 years; Thailand's biggest windsurf gear supplier, over 100 boards
According to the Holiday Inn Pattaya guide — a school on Jomtien with lessons in English and Russian; check before you go

alacati.description: Alaçatı is a big, shallow bay on the Çeşme peninsula and Turkey's main windsurf resort. The northerly Meltemi blows side-shore from the left and accelerates between the hills, the water is flat, and the shallows stretch for hundreds of metres — paradise for freeride, slalom and learning. PWA World Cup events have been held here.
alacati.rating_basis: One of the Mediterranean's best freeride and slalom spots: PWA World Cup events, up to 70% windy days in summer (Surf Magazin), huge shallows; downside — crowds in July–August
alacati.waves_note: An almost enclosed bay with flat water and light chop; in spring and autumn the southerly Lodos pushes a small wave into the bay
alacati.hazards: The yacht channel to the Port Alaçatı marina, heavy board and foil traffic, shallows and seaweed (dark patches), wind shadow by buildings
alacati.gustiness_note: The Meltemi accelerates between the hills (up to +6 knots on the forecast) and blows fairly steadily, strengthening towards evening; wind shadow in places along the built-up shore
alacati.crowd_note: In July–August the bay is very busy: hundreds of boards, foilers, wingers and students from the big schools
alacati.events: PWA Slalom World Cup events (2006 — together with the IFCA Slalom World Championship, 2010 — Pegasus Airlines PWA World Cup); in October 2023 — the PWA Youth and Junior Slalom World Cup at the Alaçatı Windfest
alacati.launch: Sandy shore on the west side of the bay right by the centres (ASPC and others); standing-depth shallows stretch for ~500 m — ideal for learning and beach starts. Kiters ride in the southeastern part of the bay
alacati.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.5 m² in summer, 4.5 m² on strong days; 7 m² and up in the morning at Force 2–4
pros: Huge flat-water shallows
Steady summer Meltemi that strengthens towards evening
Big schools, including some with Russian-speaking instructors
You can sail almost all year round (in a wetsuit in winter)
cons: Very crowded in July–August
Heavy construction along the shore, wind shadow in places
Often light wind in the morning
alacati.wind_dir: N–NNE (Meltemi / “Poyraz”), side-shore from the left; in spring and autumn the southerly Lodos — side-shore from the right
school_notes: Turkey's biggest centre, JP/Gaastra/NeilPryde, open all year round; instructors speak Russian, and there's a Russian version of the website
geared towards Turkish customers, with English-speaking instructors

bodrum-bitez.description: Bitez is a resort bay 7 km from Bodrum with a gently sloping sandy beach and shallows, long known as a place to learn windsurfing. In the afternoon the summer Meltemi blows with a thermal boost, but the wind comes off the land and is gusty in the bay. A good choice for beginners on a family holiday, not a trip for strong wind.
bodrum-bitez.rating_basis: A long-standing windsurf learning bay on the Bodrum peninsula (beachesforkings, Daily Sabah); for advanced sailors the wind is a bit light and gusty (kite-and-windsurfing-guide)
bodrum-bitez.waves_note: Flat water near the shore in the bay, with wind chop and small jumping waves further out
bodrum-bitez.hazards: Offshore wind — if you break gear, you drift towards the mouth of the bay; swimmers and dinghies; the wind is noticeably stronger at the mouth of the bay
bodrum-bitez.gustiness_note: Offshore wind: gusty and uneven in the bay itself, blowing properly only at the mouth of the bay; light in the morning, strengthening towards evening
bodrum-bitez.crowd_note: A resort bay: swimmers, dinghies and catamarans on the water, so you have to weave between them
bodrum-bitez.launch: A gently sloping beach of sand and fine pebbles with shallows — easy to launch and safe to fall; beach clubs and cafés along the shore
bodrum-bitez.sail_note: You need bigger sails: usually 6.0–7.5 m², 5.0–5.5 m² on windy days
pros: Shallows and flat water for learning
Almost daily afternoon breeze in summer
Well-developed resort infrastructure, close to Bodrum
cons: Offshore wind, gusty and a bit light for advanced sailors
Lots of swimmers and boats
Little information on schools, no big windsurf centres

bird-island-basin.description: Bird Island Basin is the windsurf area of Padre Island National Seashore on the shore of the Laguna Madre, about 40 minutes from Corpus Christi. It's a huge, shallow lagoon with a sandy bottom where you can stand almost everywhere. In spring and summer a steady southeasterly blows in off the Gulf. Kites are not allowed, so the water belongs to windsurfers: from beginners to freeriders and slalom sailors.
bird-island-basin.rating_basis: The National Park Service calls it one of the best windsurf spots in the US. Reviews praise the endless shallow flat water and steady wind. Rated below the top spots because of the lack of waves and modest infrastructure
bird-island-basin.waves_note: No waves: the shallow Laguna Madre, from flat water to moderate chop in strong wind
bird-island-basin.hazards: Oyster shells on the bottom (cuts — water shoes needed), weed on the fin, hurricanes and storms from August to October. Further out in the lagoon — the Intracoastal Waterway shipping channel with barges
bird-island-basin.gustiness_note: The southeasterly off the Gulf of Mexico is generally steady over the flat lagoon. Northerly fronts in winter are stronger and gustier
bird-island-basin.crowd_note: Spacious: a huge lagoon, kites are banned in the National Seashore, and motorboats may not enter the windsurf area
bird-island-basin.launch: Sandy beach in the park's recreation area: rig right on the shore, parking on a gravel lot, toilets, shade shelters, primitive campground nearby. About 1–1.5 m deep over a huge area — you can stand almost everywhere. There are oyster shells on the bottom, so water shoes are needed. From late spring to early autumn a weed fin comes in handy. You need a park entrance pass and a day-use fee
bird-island-basin.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.5 m² in spring, 4.5–5.0 on strong days; 7.0–8.0 in summer and in light wind. Rental sails from 3.4 to 8.2
pros: Shallow flat water over a huge area
Steady wind in spring and summer
Kites banned, no motorboats
Rental right on the shore, boards as small as 76 l and sails as small as 3.4 m²
Warm water from April to October
cons: No waves
Modest infrastructure: toilets, shade shelters, primitive campground
Weed in summer, sharp shells
Late summer and early autumn — light wind and hurricane season
bird-island-basin.wind_dir: SE (prevailing, spring–summer), N with winter fronts; almost all directions work
bird-island-basin.rental_price_note: full rigged kit for a day at Worldwinds, sizes can be swapped; 7 days — $415
school_notes: the park's official concessionaire right at the spot: rental (boards 76–250 l, sails 3.4–8.2), lessons, wingfoil. Open daily from 11:00 to 18:00

cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.description: Canadian Hole (Haulover Day Use Area) is a legendary spot on Pamlico Sound on Hatteras Island, between Avon and Buxton. It was named after the Canadian windsurfers who came here in droves from the 1980s. There's shallow flat water for hundreds of metres, ideal for freeride, freestyle and learning, and across the road there's the ocean with waves. The best time is spring and autumn.
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.rating_basis: The best-known windsurf spot on the US East Coast since the 1980s, covered by Boards and Outer Banks guidebooks. Shallow flat water for freeride and learning, but the wind isn't as reliable as at trade-wind spots
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.waves_note: No waves: this is the Pamlico Sound side, facing the mainland. From 13 knots of wind, 30–60 cm chop builds. On the ocean side of the island, across the road, there are waves for wave sailing in strong wind
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.hazards: Shells and rocks on the bottom (foot cuts), a very shallow bar to the right of the beach, weed, sudden wind shifts with fronts and thunderstorms in summer, hurricanes and storms in autumn. Take care crossing the NC-12 highway, where the speed limit is 88 km/h
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.gustiness_note: The summer southwesterly breeze is steady but often light. In spring and autumn the frontal winds are stronger, with gusts and direction changes
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.crowd_note: In spring and autumn windsurfers flock here from all over the East Coast and Canada, but there's plenty of water. In summer the beach is mostly families
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.region: Hatteras Island, Outer Banks, North Carolina
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.events: OBX-WIND — races (long distance, slalom, freestyle) and a festival in neighbouring Avon behind the OceanAir Sports shop, in October. Results have been published since 2019; in 2026 the races were cancelled because of a storm and evacuation
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.launch: A big free car park by the NC-12 highway, showers and toilets (seasonal, from spring to late autumn), sandy beach. Shallow for hundreds of metres: ankle- or knee-deep near the shore, waist-deep further out. The bottom has shells and rocks in places, so water shoes are needed. There's a very shallow bar to the right of the beach. Pits left on the bottom by sand dredging after the 1960s gave the spot the “Hole” in its name
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.sail_note: Usually 5.0–6.5 m² in spring and autumn, 4.2–5.0 in strong fronts; 6.5–8.0 or foil in the summer breeze
pros: Shallow flat water, you can stand almost everywhere
Ocean waves across the road
Free parking, showers, toilets
Shops and rental nearby in Avon
cons: Less reliable wind than at trade-wind spots
Often light breeze in summer, cold in winter
Sharp shelly bottom, water shoes needed
Hurricane season (August–October) and storms
Far from major airports
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.wind_dir: SW (summer sea breeze) or NE with fronts, side-shore / slightly side-off
cape-hatteras-canadian-hole.airport: ORF — Norfolk, ~3 hours; the small Billy Mitchell airport (HSE) near Frisco is closer
school_notes: Avon, a few minutes away: daily and weekly rental (Ezzy, Severne, North, Goya, Duotone, Pro package available), lessons, shallow water right behind the shop

hood-river-event-site.description: The Event Site is Hood River's main launch on the Columbia River, an hour's drive from Portland. From May to September a strong westerly thermal blows against the current almost every day, so there's chop, river swell and plenty of wind. It's a handy base for dozens of other Gorge spots, from flat water to swell (The Hatchery, The Wall).
hood-river-event-site.rating_basis: Hood River is called the “windsurfing capital of the world”: strong, reliable summer wind, dozens of spots in the Gorge and a well-developed industry. Rating lowered for the gusts, the cold water and the short season
hood-river-event-site.waves_note: The westerly wind blows against the Columbia's current and kicks up river swell. At the Event Site it's small, around 0.5–1 m, with constant chop. At neighbouring Gorge spots (The Hatchery, The Wall) the swell can reach 2 m and more in strong wind
hood-river-event-site.hazards: The river current carries you downstream if the wind drops or your gear breaks. Gusts, cold water in spring, barges and ships in the channel, rocks along the shore outside the sandy entry
hood-river-event-site.gustiness_note: A strong thermal in the Gorge: cool Pacific air is drawn towards the hot desert to the east. The wind is gusty, and 3.7 m² days come more often than you'd expect
hood-river-event-site.crowd_note: The busiest launch in the area, crowded in summer. It's also a social hub where racers and locals hang out
hood-river-event-site.events: Gorge Beach Bash — a festival with gear testing, free clinics and a swap meet (late June; per a 2018 guide)
hood-river-event-site.launch: A big rigging lawn right by downtown Hood River, a small sandy entry, and a rocky shore elsewhere. Paid parking: $2.50 an hour, max $15 a day, with a season pass available (2024 data). Not a spot for your first time: beginners learn nearby in the shallow lagoon at The Hook
hood-river-event-site.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m², 3.7–4.2 on strong days, 5.5–6.5 in light wind. The water is cool, so you need a wetsuit
pros: Strong wind almost every day in summer
Convenient rigging lawn in the middle of town
Lots of Gorge spots to suit every taste
Well-developed windsurf industry: shops, repairs, schools
cons: Short season: cold in winter, with hardly any sailing
Gusty wind and current
Cool water, you need a wetsuit
Paid parking and summer crowds
hood-river-event-site.wind_dir: W, side-shore (along the river, against the current)
hood-river-event-site.rental_price_note: per day of rental at The Hook lagoon (Big Winds), per Club Locarno's 2018 guide; probably more expensive now
school_notes: shop, repairs, rental and lessons at The Hook lagoon
windsurf and other water sports lessons
beginner lessons at The Hook
windsurf shop, daily and multi-day rental

hookipa.description: Ho'okipa on Maui's north shore is the cult spot of wave windsurfing. A steady trade wind blows from the right, and powerful reef waves deliver classic starboard-tack down-the-line riding. Every autumn it hosts the Aloha Classic, the final of the world wave tour. Summer brings more wind and smaller waves; autumn and spring offer the best combination of wind and swell.
hookipa.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known wave spots, home spot of the pros and venue of the Wave World Cup final (Aloha Classic); rating lowered only for the crowds and the risk
hookipa.waves_note: Reef waves: in summer mostly 1–2 m wind swell, from autumn to spring 2–5 m and bigger in a northwesterly swell. The main break is The Point (a right-hander, starboard tack down-the-line); in the rare southwesterly Kona wind people sail at Lanes
hookipa.hazards: Lava rocks and shallow reef (especially at low tide), shorebreak, rips, big waves in winter, no wind on the inside, collisions in the crowd
hookipa.gustiness_note: The trade wind is steady, but near the shore and on the inside it's lighter and patchy, with wind shadow by the cliffs
hookipa.crowd_note: On good days there are dozens of windsurfers at the peak; the bay is small and collisions are frequent. Strict priority on the wave and respect for surfers
hookipa.events: Aloha Classic — the final event of the PWA/IWT Wave World Cup (October; in 2025 it started in mid-October)
hookipa.launch: Not a beach but a small, cramped cove below the park: a short shorebreak, then current. It's surrounded by black lava rocks that wreck a board and rig in seconds. Before your first session ask the locals about getting in, getting out and the currents. Windsurfers only go out after 11:00 — mornings belong to the surfers
hookipa.sail_note: Minimum kit: a wave board and 4.2 and 4.7 m² sails. 3.7–4.2 in a strong trade wind, 5.0–5.3 on light days
pros: World-class waves and a steady trade wind
You can watch the pros on the water — the atmosphere of the wave windsurfing “mecca”
Warm water all year round, you can sail in boardshorts
Paia nearby, with accommodation and windsurf shops
cons: For confident wave sailors only
Very crowded on the water, with a strict pecking order
Lava rocks and a tricky exit, frequent breakages
No rental on the beach itself: gear is rented in Kahului or Paia
Windsurfers can only go out after 11:00
hookipa.wind_dir: E–ENE trade wind, side-shore from the right (starboard tack — down-the-line)

kanaha.description: Kanaha is Maui's main windsurf beach, a few minutes from Kahului airport. It has a handy grassy rigging area and a steady trade wind from the right. Between the shore and the reef there's a channel for freeride and bump & jump, and on the outer reefs, Uppers and Lowers, there are waves, up to 3–5 m in winter. Beginners learn near the shore in the morning, and everyone else goes out in the afternoon.
kanaha.rating_basis: Maui's main windsurf beach according to reviews and guides (Boards, Surf Magazin, Waterwind): an easy launch, steady trade wind, reef waves and freeride in one place. Downsides — crowds and rocks
kanaha.waves_note: The reefs are about 300 m from shore: Uppers is trickier, while at Lowers the wave lines up more cleanly. 0.5–1.5 m waves in summer, 3–5 m in a northerly swell in winter. Between the shore and the reef there's a choppy channel for freeride
kanaha.hazards: Small rocks and coral (foot cuts), reef waves that break gear in a big swell, a current towards the Kahului harbour entrance if you drift downwind, kiters downwind, spiky tree seeds in the rigging area
kanaha.gustiness_note: The trade wind is fairly steady, picking up after 11:00, with the best sessions around 16:00–18:00. Less reliable wind in winter
kanaha.crowd_note: The island's busiest windsurf spot: on good waves, up to 7 people per wave. These days there are lots of wing foilers on the water, and kiters ride downwind at Kite Beach
kanaha.launch: Grassy rigging lawns, sand, showers, toilets, a tap for rinsing gear and a big free car park. On the beach the wind is gentle and the sand doesn't blow. The water is shallow over rocks and coral: don't push off the bottom with your foot when waterstarting. Windsurfers can go out from 11:00, with beginner lessons near the shore from 9:00. If the wind drops, you can come ashore downwind at Kite Beach
kanaha.sail_note: Usually 4.7–5.7 m² in summer, 4.2 on strong days; 5.5–6.5 in winter and in a light trade wind. 4.2–5.0 on the Uppers waves
pros: Steady trade wind, windy almost every day in summer
Convenient facilities: lawn, showers, parking
Something for everyone: from learning near the shore to serious reef waves
Rental and gear shops nearby in Kahului
Warm water all year round
cons: Crowded on the water, lots of wing foilers
Small rocks and coral near the shore
You can only go out from 11:00
Maui is an expensive destination (accommodation, car hire)
kanaha.wind_dir: NE–ENE trade wind, side-shore from the right
kanaha.rental_price_note: board and two sails for a day, Kanaha Kai (per a Seabreeze forum review, 2022)
school_notes: windsurf school at Kanaha since 1998, group and private beginner lessons in the mornings
rental: Starboard boards, Hot Sails Maui sails, car racks included
rental (formerly Neil Pryde Maui): Pryde sails, JP boards

el-yaque-windsurf.description: El Yaque on the south coast of Margarita Island is a legendary spot for freestyle and learning. A steady trade wind blows along the shore, and waist-deep shallow water stretches for hundreds of metres, so you can repeat tricks without waterstarting. The airport is five minutes away. The best wind is from December to July, and the windiest month is March.
el-yaque-windsurf.rating_basis: A long-standing “freestyle mecca” (Boards): shallow flat water and a steady trade wind almost all year round; freestyle stars grew up here, including Ricardo Campello. Rating lowered because of the unstable situation in the country and declining infrastructure
el-yaque-windsurf.waves_note: No waves: this is the island's south coast. Flat, shallow water near the shore, and beyond 400 m chop that builds with the wind
el-yaque-windsurf.hazards: Beyond the shallows there's chop and open sea; don't sail to Coche Island (it's far, and there are sharks). After 17:00 the beach switches over to kiters. Street crime and outages of phone service and fuel — check the current situation before you go
el-yaque-windsurf.gustiness_note: The trade wind is steady, lighter in the morning and building by lunchtime
el-yaque-windsurf.crowd_note: In its heyday it was very crowded in season; now there are noticeably fewer tourists. Kiters have been moved to a separate beach
el-yaque-windsurf.launch: Sandy beach in front of the hotels (the former Club Margarita), about 500 m long up to the fishing pier, with the centres right on the sand. Shallow for about 400 m: you can stand waist-deep and repeat tricks. Sandy bottom. Kiters aren't allowed on the main beach before 17:00 and have their own Kite Beach
el-yaque-windsurf.sail_note: Locals most often sail 4.7, 5.3 and 5.7 m²; rental sails range from 4 to 8 m²
pros: Shallow flat water, you can stand for hundreds of metres
Steady trade wind for most of the year
Airport 5–10 minutes away
Warm water and inexpensive accommodation
Direct flights from Moscow resumed in 2025 (Nordwind, Conviasa)
cons: Unstable political and economic situation, check the safety advice
Infrastructure and choice of centres poorer than in the 2000s
No waves
Light wind in September–November
el-yaque-windsurf.airport: PMV — Margarita (Porlamar), ~5–10 minutes: the beach is right behind the airport

mui-ne-windsurf.description: Mui Ne is Vietnam's main windsurf and kite resort and one of the windiest places in Southeast Asia: from November to March the northeast monsoon delivers 15–30 knots almost every day. Sailing is in the bay along the long sandy Ham Tien beach — strong chop and wind waves, good for bump & jump, freestyle and slalom; a PWA event was held here in 2011. The resort has long been popular with Russian-speaking tourists.
mui-ne-windsurf.rating_basis: Planet Windsurf Holidays, Sportif Travel and local guides: a steady 15–30-knot winter monsoon, warm water, a 2011 PWA event (freestyle and slalom). Downsides — strong chop and shorebreak, kiters have taken over the beach, few windsurf centres
mui-ne-windsurf.waves_note: Hardly any swell — the waves are wind-driven: at the height of the season (December–January) strong chop and short 1–2 m wind waves, with shorebreak near the beach. In the morning the water is smoother by the harbour wall (port wall) west of the main beach. Separate wave spots — Malibu and Suoi Nuoc (onshore, mast-high waves on windy days), Ke Ga (a left by the lighthouse, ~30 km southwest of Phan Thiet)
mui-ne-windsurf.hazards: Shorebreak when going out and coming in; gusts up to 35–40 knots in December–January; lots of kites on the water (risk of collisions and lines); fishermen's basket boats and nets in the bay; on a downwinder towards Phan Thiet — boats and changing conditions; strong sun
mui-ne-windsurf.gustiness_note: The northeast monsoon, boosted by the sea breeze: the wind arrives by late morning and holds until sunset, with gusts up to 35–40 knots in December–January. Right by the shore the wind is lighter and patchy — 200 m out from the beach it's noticeably stronger
mui-ne-windsurf.crowd_note: In season the main beach is packed with kiters in the afternoon (up to a hundred kites), and not everyone follows the right-of-way rules; windsurfers have more room by the harbour wall in the morning and at the neighbouring spots
mui-ne-windsurf.region: Phan Thiet, former Binh Thuan Province (Lam Dong since 2025), Ham Tien beach
mui-ne-windsurf.events: PWA Vietnam Grand Slam — a PWA Freestyle and Slalom World Cup event (February–March 2011)
mui-ne-windsurf.launch: The long sandy Ham Tien beach along Nguyen Dinh Chieu street, with centres right on the beach (Jibe's Beach Club, Surf4you and others). Sandy bottom, with hardly any reefs or rocks, but on windy days there's shorebreak — going out and coming in takes some skill. Beginners are better off in the morning, when the wind is lighter and the water calmer
mui-ne-windsurf.sail_note: Usually 4.2–5.3 m² in December–January, 5.0–6.0 in February–March; in the light morning hours and in summer (10–14-knot southerly) you need a big 6.5–7.5 m² sail or a foil
pros: Reliable wind almost every day from November to March
Warm water all year round (25–29 °C)
Sandy bottom with no reefs at the main beach
Lots of Russian-speaking tourists and services, low cost of living
Wave spots (Malibu, Ke Ga) and Phan Rang nearby
cons: Strong chop and shorebreak — hard for beginners at the height of the season
The beach is packed with kiters
Few windsurf centres, and the gear isn't always new
Light, unreliable wind in summer and the shoulder months (May, October)
Long transfer from Ho Chi Minh City
mui-ne-windsurf.wind_dir: NE–ENE, side-shore / side-onshore from the left (November–April); S–SW and lighter in summer
mui-ne-windsurf.airport: SGN — Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat), ~200 km, 3–4 hours via the expressway; Phan Thiet airport is under construction (civil terminal groundbreaking in 2026)
school_notes: Mui Ne's oldest windsurf centre (since 2000), 90 Nguyen Dinh Chieu; Starboard / Severne, year-round rental, courses, beach bar and restaurant
Surf hotel with a windsurf and wingfoil station and workshop; according to vietnamspot.ru, there are Russian-speaking instructors
10 Nguyen Dinh Chieu; mainly kite, but also windsurfing, surfing and SUP

big-bay-bloubergstrand.description: Big Bay is Cape Town's main windsurf bay, in Bloubergstrand, with a view of Table Mountain. In summer (November–March) the strong south-easterly “Cape Doctor” blows here side-shore / side-onshore: perfect for jumping, freestyle and wave riding. It hosted the Oxbow Big Bay Classic with the IFCA Slalom World Championship, and now hosts Freestyle Pro Tour events.
big-bay-bloubergstrand.rating_basis: Surf Magazin, Windsurfing UK and Boards describe Cape Town as one of the best winter (for Europeans) windsurf destinations, and Big Bay as its hub: strong, steady wind, jumping and waves with a view of Table Mountain; downsides — cold water and almost no rental
big-bay-bloubergstrand.waves_note: The bay is sheltered by rocks, so the water is smoother than at neighbouring Sunset and Doodles: in a small swell, waves up to 1 m (freestyle, jumping), in a medium swell 1.5–2.5 m; winter storms bring big waves
big-bay-bloubergstrand.hazards: Rocks at both ends of the bay; very strong, gusty wind towards evening (up to 40 knots); cold water — hypothermia if you break gear; crime — don't leave valuables in the car; great white sharks are rarely seen on the west coast
big-bay-bloubergstrand.gustiness_note: The south-easterly “Cape Doctor” blows in cycles of 3–4 days with 1–2 calm days in between; moderate in the morning, often 30–40 knots towards evening; slightly lighter at Big Bay than at Sunset Beach
big-bay-bloubergstrand.crowd_note: In December–February there are lots of windsurfers and especially kiters, and the car park is overflowing; in strong wind towards evening it's mostly experienced riders left on the water
big-bay-bloubergstrand.events: Oxbow Big Bay Classic (January 2009: IFCA Slalom World Championship and WSA Open Wave); Freestyle Pro Tour Cape Town events (January 2023–2024, with the sea round at Big Bay / Sunset / KFC depending on conditions)
big-bay-bloubergstrand.launch: Sandy beach by the lifeguard tower and the lawn in front of the promenade with cafés and shops; people rig on the lawn. The bay is bounded by rocks on both sides — keep well away from them; small shorebreak. The car park is jammed on windy days
big-bay-bloubergstrand.sail_note: 4.2–5.0 m² in the morning and for freestyle, 3.4–4.2 m² in the afternoon; on strong days you need your smallest sail; you'll hardly ever need more than 5.5 m²
pros: Strong, frequent wind from November to March
Excellent conditions for jumping and freestyle, with smoother waves in the bay than at the neighbouring spots
Another dozen spots nearby (Sunset, Doodles, Melkbos, Langebaan) — you can pick one to suit the wind
Strong local and visiting community, cafés right by the beach
cons: Cold water at 12–15 °C, you need a 4/3–5/3 wetsuit
Almost no windsurf rental in Cape Town — you need your own gear (there's rental in Langebaan)
Crowded because of the kiters, overflowing car park
In winter (May–September) the wind is rare and stormy

langebaan.description: Langebaan is a big, shallow lagoon 1.5 hours north of Cape Town and the region's best flat water for learning, freestyle and fast freeriding. The summer south-easterly blows side-shore from the left, gentle in the morning and strengthening by midday. The Cape Sports Center on the main beach is effectively the only windsurf rental around Cape Town.
langebaan.rating_basis: Surf Magazin and Sportif call Langebaan the best place in the Cape Town region for flat water and learning, and the Cape Sports Center the only full-fledged windsurf rental in the area; the lagoon is considered one of the most wind-reliable
langebaan.waves_note: For the first ~200 m from shore by the centre the water is almost glassy (the point blocks the waves), with tide-dependent chop further out; in strong westerly and southwesterly swells there can be clean small waves by the points
langebaan.hazards: Currents at the lagoon mouth (especially at low tide), boats near the mouth, shallows at low tide, shells on the beach; the wind picks up quickly in the afternoon
langebaan.gustiness_note: Gentle wind in the morning, building by midday; at the height of the season up to 30–40 knots towards evening, and the weather changes quickly. In SW–NW winds the surrounding hills accelerate the wind
langebaan.crowd_note: Busy in December–February, especially with kiters at neighbouring Shark Bay; by the centre on the main beach there's usually enough room
langebaan.region: Langebaan Lagoon, West Coast, Western Cape
langebaan.launch: Langebaan's main beach by the Cape Sports Center: an even sandy entry with a gently sloping bottom and no shorebreak; at low tide there's a standing-depth area near the shore. There are shells on the beach — better to wear shoes
langebaan.sail_note: 5.5–6.5 m² in the morning (training sails for beginners), 4.5–5.3 m² in the afternoon, 3.7–4.5 m² on strong days; foil sessions in light wind
pros: Flat water near the shore, handy for learning and freestyle
The only proper windsurf rental in the Cape Town region
The lagoon water is warmer than the ocean
Works in a northwesterly when the other Cape Town spots are dead
cons: You need a wetsuit all year round
The wind can get too strong for beginners towards evening
Far from Cape Town, you need a car
Expensive rental by local standards
langebaan.wind_dir: S–SSE (summer south-easterly), side-shore from the left; NW in winter — side-shore from the right
langebaan.airport: CPT — Cape Town, ~1.5 h by car (about 120 km)
langebaan.rental_price_note: board + rig for a day per the Cape Sports Center price list (a week is about 7,800 ZAR)
school_notes: Station right on the beach, rental for all levels and foil, courses (2 h private — 2,200 ZAR, 2026/27 season), rooftop café; open roughly 9:00–17:00

great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.description: Cairns and Port Douglas are the gateway to the largest reef system on the planet. Day boats take even beginners diving and run Open Water courses, but the best of it — the Ribbon Reefs with the giant potato cod of Cod Hole and the shark-patrolled walls of Osprey Reef — is reached on 3–7-night liveaboards. Suits every level; experienced divers should head for the Coral Sea.
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.rating_basis: The world's best-known reef system; the Ribbon Reefs, Cod Hole and Osprey Reef consistently make global top lists (50 Great Dives, DIVE), but the reefs closest to Cairns suffer from coral bleaching and crowds on the tourist pontoons.
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.hazards: Box jellyfish and Irukandji (November–May, a protective stinger suit is a must), cyclones (December–March), currents on the outer walls and in the Coral Sea, depth at Osprey.
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.crowd_note: The inner reefs and pontoons off Cairns and Port Douglas are busy with big day boats; the Ribbon Reefs and Osprey are reachable almost only by liveaboard and are much quieter.
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.region: Queensland, northern Great Barrier Reef (Ribbon Reefs) and the Coral Sea (Osprey Reef)
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.marine_life: Huge, tame potato cod at Cod Hole, Napoleon wrasse, turtles, reef sharks; at Osprey Reef in the Coral Sea — grey reef and silvertip sharks, mantas, occasionally hammerheads and whale sharks.
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.signature_sites: Cod Hole (Ribbon Reef No. 10), Steve's Bommie, Pixie Pinnacle, Osprey Reef — North Horn, Agincourt Reefs (from Port Douglas)
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.chamber: Recompression chamber at Townsville University Hospital (Townsville, ~350 km south of Cairns, 24/7, evacuation by air)
pros: A huge choice of reefs for every level
Cod Hole and Osprey are world-class
Swim-with-minke-whales season (June–July)
Excellent infrastructure and safety
cons: Expensive
The inner reefs have been hit by bleaching
November–May is box jellyfish season (you need a stinger suit) and cyclone season
The best sites are liveaboard-only
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.airport: CNS — Cairns; Cod Hole is ~250 km to the north, liveaboard only (or from Lizard Island)
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.dive_price_note: Outer-reef day trip from Cairns (Silverswift): ~AUD 424 for 2 dives with gear, i.e. ~€120 per dive; plus a fuel levy
great-barrier-reef-cod-hole.course_price_note: PADI Open Water with Pro Dive Cairns: 4 days, 3 days/2 nights of them on a liveaboard, ~AUD 1235 + AUD 125 levy
highlights: Dwarf minke whales (swim-with-whales trips on the Ribbon Reefs)
Humpback whales
Mass coral spawning
Turtles: mating and nesting
Giant potato cod at Cod Hole
Sharks at North Horn, Osprey Reef (grey reef, whitetip, silky)
school_notes: Open Water courses with liveaboard nights, Silverswift day trips
Liveaboards to Cod Hole, the Ribbon Reefs and Osprey Reef, seasonal minke whale trips
3–7-night liveaboards: Ribbon Reefs, Cod Hole, Coral Sea

ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.description: Exmouth is the base for Ningaloo Reef, where the coral comes right up to the shore. The signature dive is the Navy Pier: a shallow (to ~14 m) guided dive among giant schools of fish, sharks and groupers, open to divers fresh out of their Open Water. From March to July people come to swim with whale sharks (snorkel only), and from August for humpback whales and mantas.
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.rating_basis: Ningaloo is one of the best places in the world to meet whale sharks (a UNESCO World Heritage Site); the Navy Pier is on the 50 Great Dives list; downsides — limited visibility at the pier and the remoteness.
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.hazards: Strong tidal currents at the Navy Pier (dive only at slack water), a giant-stride entry from the high pier, Irukandji jellyfish in summer, cyclones (January–March), a long way to the recompression chamber.
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.crowd_note: Only small guided groups are allowed onto the Navy Pier, by arrangement with the military; in whale shark season book boats and tours well ahead.
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.region: Western Australia, North West Cape peninsula, Ningaloo Reef and Exmouth Gulf
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.marine_life: Under the naval pier — more than 200 fish species: schools of barracuda, trevally and wrasse, giant groupers, tasselled wobbegongs, whitetip reef sharks, turtles, nudibranchs; on the outer reef and around the Muiron Islands — mantas, turtles, dugongs.
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.signature_sites: Navy Pier (Point Murat), Muiron Islands, Lighthouse Bay, Turquoise Bay, Ningaloo outer reef
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.chamber: Hyperbaric Medicine Unit, Fiona Stanley Hospital (Perth, ~1,100 km, evacuation by air ambulance)
pros: Guaranteed whale shark encounters (April–July)
The Navy Pier is one of the world's best pier dives
Few people, pristine reef
Suitable for beginners
cons: Very remote and expensive
Visibility at the pier is only 5–10 m
Whale sharks are snorkel-only, no scuba
Summer heat, strong wind and cyclones
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.airport: LEA — Learmonth (Exmouth), ~35 km to town; flights from Perth ~2 h
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.dive_price_note: Navy Pier trip (~6 h, guided): AUD 300 + AUD 50 Defence fee; you won't be let onto the base without a passport or driving licence
ningaloo-exmouth-navy-pier.course_price_note: PADI Open Water at Exmouth Dive & Whalesharks: AUD 795, 2–3 days
highlights: Whale sharks (snorkel-only swims, peak season)
Humpback whales (including swim-with tours)
Manta rays (peak numbers)
Coral spawning
Grey nurse sharks at the Navy Pier
school_notes: Navy Pier, Muiron Islands, PADI courses, whale shark tours; season 1 March – 31 October
Navy Pier dives, office in Exmouth
Whale shark tours and diving

bonaire-salt-pier.description: The world capital of shore diving: dozens of sites marked with yellow stones line the leeward coast, and you can go in on your own at any time. The water is calm, there's almost no current, and the island lies outside the hurricane belt, so diving goes on all year. Great both for an Open Water course and for experienced divers who want to dive a lot and on their own schedule.
bonaire-salt-pier.rating_basis: A long-time leader of Scuba Diving's readers' poll in the shore-diving category; one of the oldest marine parks in the Caribbean (86 sites); reviews praise the freedom — rent a pickup with tanks and dive by yourself
bonaire-salt-pier.hazards: Slippery rocky entries, urchins and fire coral; current at Salt Pier and the northern sites; depth on the walls; break-ins — leave cars unlocked and empty
bonaire-salt-pier.crowd_note: There are so many sites that most have just a couple of cars; Salt Pier is closed while ships are loading
bonaire-salt-pier.region: Leeward Antilles (ABC islands), Bonaire National Marine Park, Caribbean Sea
bonaire-salt-pier.marine_life: Healthy fringing reefs, tarpon, turtles, seahorses, frogfish, squid, sponges and sea fans; the Hilma Hooker wreck.
bonaire-salt-pier.signature_sites: Salt Pier, 1000 Steps, the Hilma Hooker wreck, Klein Bonaire, Oil Slick Leap, Andrea I and II
bonaire-salt-pier.chamber: Recompression chamber at Fundashon Mariadal hospital, Kralendijk
pros: Unguided shore diving with no boats or schedules
Year-round, outside the hurricane belt
Calm sea and almost no current
Healthy reefs, the oldest marine park in the region
cons: Few big pelagics
You need a rental car, entries are over rocks and coral
Not cheap (flights via Amsterdam or Miami)
Some northern sites are closed because of coral disease
bonaire-salt-pier.airport: BON — Bonaire (Kralendijk), ~10 min to Salt Pier
bonaire-salt-pier.dive_price_note: A tank for an unguided shore dive ($23); guided $60, boat dive $67; gear rental and the marine park fee not included
bonaire-salt-pier.course_price_note: PADI Open Water with eLearning, $565 (Dive Friends Bonaire)
highlights: Salt Pier pilings with tarpon, schooling fish and turtles
Seahorses, frogfish and macro on the reefs
school_notes: Several locations on the island; 6 days of unlimited shore diving — $234, Open Water course — $565

bahamas-tiger-beach.description: A shallow sandbank on the Little Bahama Bank where tiger, lemon and reef sharks swim right up to divers at 6–12 m — the world's top spot for cageless shark diving. It's shallow and there's almost no current, but you need solid buoyancy control and strict discipline; many operators ask for 30+ logged dives. In winter, nearby Bimini has its great hammerhead season.
bahamas-tiger-beach.rating_basis: The best place in the world for cageless tiger shark dives; Tiger Beach and Bimini feature in every global shark-diving top list; rated 8.7/10 from reviews on liveaboard.com
bahamas-tiger-beach.hazards: Big predatory sharks around bait — only with an experienced operator, dark gear, keep your hands tucked in; rough boat crossings
bahamas-tiger-beach.crowd_note: 1–3 boats on site at a time (liveaboards from Florida and day boats from Grand Bahama); at Bimini, boat spots in peak hammerhead season sell out in advance
bahamas-tiger-beach.region: Little Bahama Bank, ~30 km northwest of West End (Grand Bahama); Bimini is 80 km from Miami
bahamas-tiger-beach.marine_life: Tiger, lemon, Caribbean reef and nurse sharks over shallow sand; at Bimini — great hammerheads, bull sharks and wild dolphins; groupers, moray eels.
bahamas-tiger-beach.signature_sites: Tiger Beach (sand at 6–12 m), Fish Tales and Mini Wall; off Bimini — the hammerhead sand flats, the Sapona wreck, bull sharks at Bullrun
pros: Tiger sharks and great hammerheads up close
Shallow, no current, excellent visibility
Close to Florida (Palm Beach, Fort Lauderdale)
cons: Shark diving on sand only — little reef
Expensive: liveaboards from ~$2800
Water is 23–24 °C in winter with windy fronts; summer is hurricane season
bahamas-tiger-beach.airport: FPO — Freeport (Grand Bahama), ~40 min to West End + ~1 h by boat; BIM — South Bimini; ferry from Fort Lauderdale
highlights: Tiger sharks (year-round; best October–January, fewest in July–August)
Lemon, Caribbean reef and nurse sharks on the sand
Great hammerheads off Bimini (mostly in winter)
Wild spotted dolphins off Bimini
school_notes: North Bimini: great hammerhead trips, wild dolphins, bull sharks, Tiger Beach expeditions
Departs from Old Bahama Bay (Grand Bahama), $2794–5094 per trip

belize-great-blue-hole.description: The world's second-longest barrier reef and three atolls. Ambergris Caye makes an easy base for the Hol Chan reserve (shallow, lots of nurse sharks and rays — good for beginners), and for a full-day trip to the Great Blue Hole on Lighthouse Reef to tick it off the list: the dive to 40 m among the stalactites requires Advanced and experience. For serious wall diving on the atolls, take a liveaboard.
belize-great-blue-hole.rating_basis: The Great Blue Hole is a bucket-list wonder of the world (Cousteau, Discovery), but as a dive it's often called overrated (deep, little life); the walls of Lighthouse Reef and Hol Chan get far more praise
belize-great-blue-hole.hazards: 40 m depth in the Blue Hole (nitrogen narcosis, short bottom time), open sea on the crossing, boat traffic at Hol Chan
belize-great-blue-hole.crowd_note: Boats from San Pedro and Belize City all arrive at the Blue Hole at the same time in the morning; the other atoll sites are uncrowded
belize-great-blue-hole.region: Lighthouse Reef and the Belize Barrier Reef, Caribbean Sea (trips from San Pedro on Ambergris Caye)
belize-great-blue-hole.marine_life: Caribbean reef and blacktip sharks, nurse sharks, stingrays, eagle rays, turtles, groupers; on the atoll walls (Half Moon Caye, the Aquarium) — sponges and sea fans.
belize-great-blue-hole.signature_sites: Great Blue Hole (to 40 m, stalactites), Half Moon Caye Wall, the Aquarium (Lighthouse), Hol Chan reserve and Shark Ray Alley (off Ambergris), Turneffe Atoll
belize-great-blue-hole.chamber: Recompression chamber in San Pedro (Ambergris Caye)
pros: The legendary Blue Hole
Good reef diving for all levels
English-speaking country, easy to reach from the US
Lots of sharks and rays in the shallows of Hol Chan
cons: The Blue Hole is a deep, short dive with little life
Long crossing (2–2.5 h each way) and an expensive trip
Hurricane season June–November; winter fronts can cancel atoll trips
belize-great-blue-hole.airport: BZE — Belize City, then ~15 min by local flight or ~1.5 h by ferry to Ambergris Caye; ~2–2.5 h by boat to the Blue Hole
highlights: Stalactites under the overhang of the Great Blue Hole at ~40 m
Caribbean reef sharks, nurse sharks and rays (Hol Chan / Shark Ray Alley, Lighthouse)
Spotted eagle rays in the Hol Chan channel
school_notes: Daily 1–3-dive trips, Blue Hole trips (36 miles from Ambergris), Hol Chan

cocos-island.description: An uninhabited island in the open Pacific, 36–48 hours away by liveaboard (10–14-day trips). People come for schooling hammerheads, night hunts by hundreds of whitetip sharks and the chance of a whale shark or tiger shark. Experienced divers only: currents, 25–40 m depths, cold thermoclines and a long ocean crossing. Diving is year-round: the rainy season (June–November) brings more plankton and sharks, the dry season calmer seas and better visibility.
cocos-island.rating_basis: In the world's top three shark destinations alongside the Galápagos and Malpelo; a UNESCO site; Undersea Hunter calls the hammerhead schools here the largest in the world, and reviews back that up
cocos-island.hazards: Strong currents and downcurrents, depth, getting separated from the skiff (an SMB and a locator beacon are mandatory), big sharks (a fatal tiger shark attack at Manuelita in 2017), complete remoteness from medical help
cocos-island.crowd_note: Only a handful of liveaboards make the trip, so it's almost always just your group on site
cocos-island.region: Isla del Coco National Park, Pacific Ocean, ~550 km off the coast of Costa Rica (liveaboard only)
cocos-island.marine_life: Schooling hammerheads at cleaning stations, hundreds of whitetip reef sharks (night hunts), silky and Galápagos sharks, occasional whale and tiger sharks, mantas and eagle rays, marbled rays, turtles, huge schools of jacks.
cocos-island.signature_sites: Bajo Alcyone (seamount, hammerheads), Dirty Rock, Manuelita (whitetip night hunts), Dos Amigos Grande (underwater arch), La Pajara
cocos-island.chamber: No recompression chamber on the island — the mainland is 36–48 h away; insurance with evacuation cover is mandatory
pros: Some of the biggest hammerhead schools in the world
Hardly any other divers — a UNESCO reserve
Year-round season
A wide variety of sharks and pelagics
cons: Very expensive and long (10–14-day liveaboard)
36–48 h crossing on the open ocean
Experienced divers only (Advanced, usually 30–50+ dives, nitrox)
Rain and swell, cold thermoclines
cocos-island.airport: SJO — San José, ~2 h to the port of Puntarenas, then 36–48 h by liveaboard
highlights: The world's largest schools of hammerheads (Bajo Alcyone, Dirty Rock)
Whitetip reef sharks hunting in packs at night (Manuelita)
Whale sharks, mantas, tiger and silky sharks, dolphins
school_notes: 11- and 14-day expeditions, skiffs of 10 divers; DeepSee submersible on board

cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.description: An archipelago of hundreds of mangrove islets 60–80 km off Cuba's south coast, closed to fishing and mass tourism since the 1990s: its reefs are among the healthiest in the Caribbean, and sharks greet divers at almost every site. Diving is only possible with the single operator (Avalon), from a floating hotel or yacht, on an all-inclusive week. Suits divers from Open Water up with good buoyancy; the best months are the dry season, November to May.
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.rating_basis: One of the most pristine reefs in the Caribbean thanks to the reserve and a quota (~3,000 divers a year); reviews and features (Scuba Diving, DIVE) talk of abundant sharks and giant groupers — “the Caribbean as it was 50 years ago”
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.hazards: Sharks at feeds (follow the guide's rules), currents on the outer walls, depth, crocodiles in the mangroves (only with a guide), a long way to a recompression chamber
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.crowd_note: Only Avalon operates here, with no more than ~3,000 divers a year — usually one boat per site
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.region: Jardines de la Reina National Marine Park, south coast of Cuba (Camagüey / Ciego de Ávila), Caribbean Sea
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.marine_life: The reserve's pristine reefs: plenty of Caribbean reef and silky sharks, lemon, blacktip, nurse sharks and great hammerheads, giant groupers, tarpon, turtles; walls with sponges, sea fans and black coral.
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.signature_sites: Black Coral I and II (sharks), Pipín, Farallón, Vicente, Cuevas del Pulpo, mangrove channels with crocodiles
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.chamber: No recompression chamber in the archipelago — evacuation to mainland Cuba; insurance with evacuation cover is mandatory
pros: Pristine reefs and lots of sharks
Hardly any other divers
Giant groupers and snorkelling with crocodiles
Direct flights to Cuba from Moscow
cons: Only one operator — expensive, book well ahead
A long journey: Havana → Júcaro (~6 h) + 3–5 h by boat
Remote from medical help
June–November is hurricane season
cuba-jardines-de-la-reina.airport: HAV — Havana, ~6 h by car to the port of Júcaro + 3–5 h by boat; CMW (Camagüey) is closer
highlights: Dozens of Caribbean reef and silky sharks on every dive
Whale sharks
Goliath groupers up to 180 kg
Snorkelling with American crocodiles in the mangrove channels
school_notes: The only operator in the park: the floating hotel and the Jardines Avalon I–IV yachts; dives under quota

larnaca-zenobia.description: The Zenobia is a 172-metre Swedish ferry that sank in 1980 1.5 km off the Larnaca seafront, along with a cargo of more than a hundred lorries. She lies on her port side at up to 42 m: newly qualified Open Water divers swim along the starboard side at 16–20 m, advanced divers explore the decks with the trucks, and tech divers go into the lower holds and the engine room. People usually do several dives on her in a row.
larnaca-zenobia.rating_basis: The Zenobia regularly makes lists of the world's ten best wrecks (The Times and others) and the top 10 recreational dives; the downside — it's essentially a single site, and there's little reef life around Larnaca.
larnaca-zenobia.hazards: Depth (the decks are at 25–42 m, easy to run into deco), penetrating the hull without training, currents on the descent and ascent, boat traffic in the bay.
larnaca-zenobia.crowd_note: In summer boats from many Larnaca and Ayia Napa centres share the Zenobia's buoys at the same time; it's quieter early in the morning and in winter.
larnaca-zenobia.marine_life: Big groupers, barracuda, amberjacks, sea bream, wrasse and triggerfish around the hull; sponges and nudibranchs on the metal.
larnaca-zenobia.signature_sites: Zenobia: starboard side (16–20 m), the lorry deck and promenade deck, the restaurant and cabins, the lower cargo deck and engine room (for the experienced)
pros: One of the world's best wrecks, 10 minutes from the airport
Suits every level — from Open Water to tech diving
Warm water and year-round diving
Lots of Russian-speaking tourists and services

Crowded on the buoys in summer
Penetrations require training (Deep/Nitrox, Wreck)

galapagos-darwin-wolf.description: Two remote islands in the far north of the Galápagos, reachable only by liveaboard: schools of hammerheads, Galápagos and silky sharks hang in the currents, and from June to November there are huge whale sharks. The warm season (December–May) brings calmer seas and better visibility; the cold season (June–November) brings whale sharks and more plankton. Experienced divers only: strong currents, swell, reef-hook dives.
galapagos-darwin-wolf.rating_basis: Always in the top three of global dive destination rankings (Scuba Diving, DIVE, PADI) — the world's largest concentration of sharks; reviews talk of “walls” of hammerheads and whale sharks
galapagos-darwin-wolf.hazards: Very strong and unpredictable currents, downcurrents, swell when getting back into the boat, getting separated from the group in the open ocean (an SMB and a locator beacon are mandatory), remoteness from medical help
galapagos-darwin-wolf.crowd_note: The number of liveaboards visiting Darwin and Wolf is capped by national park permits; usually 1–2 boats on site
galapagos-darwin-wolf.region: Northern islands of the Galápagos archipelago, Pacific Ocean (marine reserve; we chose the Darwin and Wolf liveaboard rather than day trips to Gordon Rocks)
galapagos-darwin-wolf.marine_life: Huge schools of hammerheads, Galápagos and silky sharks, whale sharks (June–November), dolphins, mantas and eagle rays, green turtles, sea lions, giant schools of jacks and tuna.
galapagos-darwin-wolf.signature_sites: Darwin's Arch / the Theatre (the arch collapsed in 2021, the reef remains), El Arenal, Wolf's east wall, the Pinnacle (Wolf), La Bañera; along the way — Cape Marshall (Isabela), Gordon Rocks
galapagos-darwin-wolf.chamber: No medical help at Darwin and Wolf — the inhabited islands of the archipelago are about a day's sailing away; insurance with evacuation cover is mandatory
pros: One of the biggest concentrations of sharks in the world
Whale sharks June–November, hammerheads year-round
Strictly protected reserve, few boats
Can be combined with land-based Galápagos
cons: Very expensive: 7–8-night liveaboard + national park entry
Experienced divers only (usually Advanced and 30–50+ dives required)
Cold water for the tropics (down to 20–22 °C) and long night crossings
galapagos-darwin-wolf.airport: GPS — Baltra Island or SCY — San Cristóbal (flights from Guayaquil/Quito), then the liveaboard; Darwin is ~a day's sailing away
highlights: Whale sharks (mostly adult pregnant females) at Darwin
Schools of hundreds of hammerheads
Galápagos, silky and blacktip sharks, dolphins, mantas, turtles

brothers-islands-big-brother.description: Two tiny islands in the middle of the Red Sea, reachable only by liveaboard: sheer walls drop into the abyss and sharks patrol all around — from grey reef sharks and threshers in summer to oceanic whitetips in autumn. The Numidia and Aida wrecks lie on the walls of Big Brother. Strictly for experienced divers: operators require AOW and at least 50 logged dives.
brothers-islands-big-brother.rating_basis: The Brothers are one of the world's top shark sites and a perennial highlight of Red Sea liveaboard routes (Divezone, Emperor Divers, liveaboard.com); divers praise the world-class walls and wrecks, but also mention strong currents and unpredictable weather.
brothers-islands-big-brother.hazards: Strong currents and downcurrents, depth, waves in open water, ascents in the blue far from the boat (you need an SMB and drift experience), oceanic sharks near the surface; night dives are banned.
brothers-islands-big-brother.crowd_note: There are no day boats, but in high season several liveaboards moor at Big and Little Brother at the same time; night dives are banned.
brothers-islands-big-brother.region: Open Red Sea, marine park, ~67 km from El Quseir (liveaboard only)
brothers-islands-big-brother.marine_life: Sheer walls covered in soft corals and sea fans, grey reef, whitetip, silky and oceanic whitetip sharks, threshers and hammerheads, occasionally silvertips and whale sharks; schools of tuna, barracuda and jacks.
brothers-islands-big-brother.signature_sites: Big Brother: the Numidia and Aida wrecks, the north and south walls; Little Brother: the north and south plateaus (sharks); BDE routes also take in Daedalus Reef and Elphinstone
brothers-islands-big-brother.chamber: No chamber on the islands; the nearest are in Marsa Alam (Baromedical, Marsa Shagra) and Hurghada (HyperMed); evacuation takes many hours

World-class wrecks and walls
Excellent open-sea visibility
Liveaboard only — no crowds of day boats and snorkellers

Hammerhead sharks
Oceanic whitetip sharks (longimanus)
Aggregations of grey reef sharks in the mating season on Little Brother's plateau
The Numidia (1901) and Aida wrecks on the walls of Big Brother

Brothers, Daedalus, Elphinstone from Hurghada or Port Ghalib, March–November; 7 nights €1350–1700 (2027–2028 dates)
Brothers liveaboards from Hurghada (link from Divezone)

dahab-blue-hole.description: Dahab is a divers' village on the Gulf of Aqaba with dozens of shore sites: you walk straight in off the beach onto coral walls. It suits everyone: total beginners learn at the Lighthouse, the Canyon and the Blue Hole are for advanced divers, and the Blue Hole's arch is a tech-diving classic. The vibe is more relaxed, and cheaper, than in Sharm.
dahab-blue-hole.rating_basis: The Blue Hole features on almost every global top list of dive sites; SSI and Divezone guides praise Dahab for its dozens of shore sites, accessibility and variety — from first dives to tech diving.
dahab-blue-hole.hazards: Depth and the temptation to go beyond your limit at the Blue Hole and the Canyon (the arch is for tech divers only), wind and waves at reef entries, sea urchins, lionfish and scorpionfish, fire coral.
dahab-blue-hole.crowd_note: The Blue Hole and the Canyon fill up with groups from Sharm and Dahab during the day; early mornings and the more distant sites (Gabr el Bint, Abu Galum) are quieter.
dahab-blue-hole.region: South Sinai, Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea
dahab-blue-hole.marine_life: Coral walls and gardens, lionfish, moray eels, turtles, Napoleon wrasse, seahorses and nudibranchs; occasionally eagle rays, dolphins and whale sharks (Gabr el Bint).
dahab-blue-hole.signature_sites: Blue Hole and the Bells, Lighthouse (house reef), the Canyon, the Garden (garden eels), the Islands, Gabr el Bint and Ras Abu Galum (by boat)
dahab-blue-hole.chamber: Recompression chamber in Dahab (Hyperbaric Medical Center); also the Hyperbaric Medical Center in Sharm el-Sheikh

Suits everyone from beginners to tech divers
Warm water and good visibility all year
Laid-back atmosphere, lots of freedivers and scuba divers

hurghada-giftun.description: Hurghada is mainland Egypt's main mass-market dive resort: dozens of reefs 30–60 minutes away by boat, drift dives off Small Giftun, easy coral gardens for training and the famous Abu Nuhas ship graveyard. It's also the departure point for liveaboards north (the Thistlegorm) and south (the Brothers, Daedalus). A great, inexpensive option for a first course and a package holiday.
hurghada-giftun.rating_basis: Divezone and reviews praise the variety (the Giftun reefs, the Abu Nuhas wrecks, dolphins) and low prices, but note the crowded inner reefs and the marks of mass tourism; the sites are a notch below Ras Mohammed and southern Egypt.
hurghada-giftun.hazards: Currents at Small Giftun and on the outer reefs, waves in a northerly wind, heavy boat traffic, penetrating the Abu Nuhas wrecks only with training.
hurghada-giftun.crowd_note: Hundreds of boats leave Hurghada's marinas every day; several groups on the same site at Giftun and Abu Ramada is normal. Abu Nuhas and the outer reefs are quieter.
hurghada-giftun.region: Red Sea Governorate, mainland coast, Red Sea
hurghada-giftun.marine_life: Coral gardens and walls with anthias, lionfish, moray eels, parrotfish; on the outer reefs — turtles, rays, occasionally reef sharks; pods of dolphins on the northern reefs.
hurghada-giftun.signature_sites: Small Giftun (wall drift), Gotta Abu Ramada and Abu Ramada South, El Fanadir, Umm Gamar and Carless Reef, the El Mina wreck, Abu Nuhas (full day)
hurghada-giftun.chamber: Recompression chambers in Hurghada: HyperMed (opposite the airport) and the Naval Hyperbaric Medical Center (Sekalla); Deco International in El Gouna

Lots of easy reefs for training
The Abu Nuhas wrecks and the Thistlegorm on day trips

marsa-alam-elphinstone.description: Marsa Alam is the quiet south of Egypt's coast, with pristine reefs, long shore dives from the bays and the famous Elphinstone: an offshore reef with sheer walls, currents and a chance of oceanic whitetip sharks in autumn. Beginners learn in the bays (Abu Dabbab with its turtles), experienced divers head for Elphinstone, Samadai and Fury Shoals.
marsa-alam-elphinstone.rating_basis: Elphinstone makes top lists of Red Sea shark sites (PADI, Divezone, liveaboard operators' rankings); southern Egypt is praised for less trampled reefs than Hurghada and Sharm, but shark and dugong encounters are never guaranteed.
marsa-alam-elphinstone.hazards: Strong currents and waves at Elphinstone, depth at the plateaus (40 m and deeper), curious oceanic whitetips near the surface — follow the guide's rules; boat traffic in the bays.
marsa-alam-elphinstone.crowd_note: Boats from several marinas and liveaboards all arrive at Elphinstone at once; Abu Dabbab bay fills with snorkellers during the day. The southern offshore reefs are quieter.
marsa-alam-elphinstone.region: Southern Egyptian Red Sea coast (Marsa Alam, Port Ghalib)
marsa-alam-elphinstone.marine_life: Elphinstone's walls covered in soft corals and sea fans, reef and oceanic whitetip sharks, occasionally hammerheads; in the bays — turtles, guitarfish and dugong; on the offshore reefs (Fury Shoals, Samadai) — dolphins and barracuda.
marsa-alam-elphinstone.signature_sites: Elphinstone (north and south plateaus), Abu Dabbab (shore), Sha'ab Samadai (“Dolphin House”), the Fury Shoals reefs, the Hamada wreck, the Marsa Shagra house reefs
marsa-alam-elphinstone.chamber: Baromedical in Marsa Shagra (~22 km north of Marsa Alam) and Deco International in Tondoba Bay (~15 km south of Marsa Alam)

safaga-panorama-reef.description: Safaga is a small port and windsurfing resort an hour south of Hurghada with calmer, better-preserved reefs. The main sites are the walls and plateaus of Panorama and Abu Kafan out in the open sea, the shallow Tobia Arba pillars for beginners and the tragic wreck of the Salem Express ferry. A good choice for anyone who finds Hurghada too crowded.
safaga-panorama-reef.rating_basis: Reviews (Divezone) mention clear water, turtles and reef sharks; Panorama and Abu Kafan are considered the best walls on the central Egyptian coast, and the Salem Express a powerful but ethically controversial wreck.
safaga-panorama-reef.hazards: Currents and waves on the exposed reefs (Abu Kafan), strong northerly wind, depth along the walls; penetrating the Salem Express is banned.
safaga-panorama-reef.crowd_note: Much quieter than Hurghada: usually 1–3 boats at Panorama and Abu Kafan; the Salem Express also gets groups from Hurghada.
safaga-panorama-reef.region: Red Sea Governorate, south of Hurghada (Safaga, Soma Bay)
safaga-panorama-reef.marine_life: Sea fans and soft corals on the walls, Napoleon wrasse, turtles, whitetip reef sharks, seahorses on the shallow reefs; on the whole the reefs are cleaner and quieter than around Hurghada.
safaga-panorama-reef.signature_sites: Panorama (Abu Alama), Abu Kafan, Salem Express, Tobia Arba (Seven Pillars) for beginners, Middle Reef, Shaab Sheer
safaga-panorama-reef.chamber: Deco International at Safaga hospital (per a 2009 list, check); the nearest reliable ones are HyperMed and the naval centre in Hurghada (~60 km)

sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.description: Sharm el-Sheikh is Sinai's largest dive resort and the gateway to Ras Mohammed National Park: the sheer walls at the southern tip of the peninsula, currents and huge summer fish schools. Boats from here also go to the Tiran reefs and the legendary Thistlegorm wreck. Fine for learning from scratch (the Naama Bay shore reefs), but the best sites are for divers with drift experience.
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.rating_basis: Ras Mohammed and the Thistlegorm consistently make global top lists of dive sites (Divezone, Lonely Planet, wreck rankings); reviews praise the walls and fish schools, but complain about crowds of boats.
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.hazards: Strong currents and downcurrents at Shark Observatory and in the Strait of Tiran, depth along the walls (the bottom drops beyond 80 m), waves in winter, boat traffic; on the Thistlegorm — current, and penetration only with training.
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.crowd_note: In season dozens of boats moor at Ras Mohammed and the Thistlegorm, especially towards midday; for the Thistlegorm it's better to take an overnight liveaboard and dive early in the morning.
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.region: South Sinai, Ras Mohammed National Park, Red Sea
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.marine_life: Sheer walls with sea fans and soft corals, schools of snapper, jacks, barracuda and batfish, Napoleon wrasse, turtles, reef sharks; on the Tiran reefs — pelagic fish in the current.
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.signature_sites: Shark & Yolanda (the reef with the Yolanda's toilets), Shark Observatory, Anemone City, Jackfish Alley, the Thistlegorm (~3 h by boat or on a liveaboard), the Tiran reefs (Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse, Gordon)
sharm-el-sheikh-ras-mohammed.chamber: Hyperbaric Medical Center in Sharm el-Sheikh (Sharm el-Maya, by the Travco jetty), DAN Europe network
