el-hierro-la-restinga.description: La Restinga is a fishing village at the southern tip of El Hierro, the smallest and wildest of the Canaries. Its leeward side, the Mar de las Calmas (“Sea of Calms”), is sheltered from the trade winds and the cold Canary Current, so the water here is warmer and calmer than around the neighbouring islands. The reserve is famous for its groupers, volcanic pinnacles, arches and caves; the underwater eruption of the Tagoro volcano happened nearby in 2011. Good for unhurried diving and underwater photography, with conditions for training too.
el-hierro-la-restinga.rating_basis: The Mar de las Calmas has been a marine reserve since 1996, and in 2024 a proposal to make it Spain's first purely marine national park was approved; divers love the groupers, the volcanic topography and the clear, calm water. The downside — remoteness and few big animals compared with the tropics.
el-hierro-la-restinga.hazards: Current at El Bajón and the outer sites, depth along the walls, caves — only with a guide, sea urchins.
el-hierro-la-restinga.crowd_note: The island is small and remote, the boats are small; it only gets busy during the Open Fotosub photo contest and in August.
el-hierro-la-restinga.region: Canary Islands, Punta de La Restinga – Mar de las Calmas marine reserve, Atlantic Ocean
el-hierro-la-restinga.marine_life: Lots of groupers (mero), barracuda, croakers, triggerfish, trumpetfish, garden eels on the sand, moray eels, rays; occasionally mantas and whale sharks, and in summer smalltooth sand tiger sharks (solrayo).
el-hierro-la-restinga.signature_sites: El Bajón, El Desierto, El Salto, Cueva del Diablo, La Herradura
el-hierro-la-restinga.chamber: No recompression chamber on the island; evacuation to Tenerife — check with the dive centre

medes-islands-estartit.description: The Medes are seven islets a kilometre off L'Estartit, an underwater continuation of the Montgrí massif: tunnels, caves, sheer walls and boulder fields. Protection since 1983 has made them one of the fishiest places in the Mediterranean — the groupers here swim right up to you. Diving is only allowed through an accredited dive centre with a permit and briefing; good both for training on the shallow sites and for experienced divers on the walls and in the tunnels.
medes-islands-estartit.rating_basis: The Medes are Spain's best-known marine reserve (protected since 1983, part of the Montgrí, Medes Islands and Baix Ter Natural Park since 2010); L'Estartit is called one of the best places in the Mediterranean for diving thanks to its groupers, caves and sea fans. Downsides — cool water and variable visibility.
medes-islands-estartit.hazards: Currents at the outer sites (Tascó, Carall Bernat), cold thermoclines, tunnels and caves — only with a guide, strong northerly wind (tramontane), boat traffic.
medes-islands-estartit.crowd_note: In summer and at weekends lots of boats work around the islands; there's a daily quota on the number of divers, so it's best to book ahead.
medes-islands-estartit.region: Costa Brava, Catalonia, Medes Islands and Montgrí marine reserve
medes-islands-estartit.marine_life: Big dusky groupers, moray eels, octopus, sea bass, dentex, schools of salema and barracuda; red and yellow sea fans; Posidonia meadows; seasonally — sunfish and eagle rays.
medes-islands-estartit.signature_sites: La Vaca (tunnel), Dofí Nord and Dofí Sud (caves), Carall Bernat, Pedra de Déu, Tascó Gran and Tascó Petit
medes-islands-estartit.chamber: The nearest recompression chamber is the CRIS-UTH hyperbaric therapy unit in the Barcelona area (~1.5–2 h); check the exact evacuation procedure with your dive centre

Crowded in summer, dive quotas
The season is effectively April to October
medes-islands-estartit.airport: GRO — Girona, ~45 min; BCN — Barcelona, ~1.5–2 h
medes-islands-estartit.dive_price_note: ≈€45 per dive: a 2-dive package (1 Medes + 1 Montgrí) is €89.30 including tank, weights, boat and reserve fee; gear and guide extra (Unisub)
medes-islands-estartit.course_price_note: PADI Open Water: online theory, pool, 4 boat dives, gear and insurance (Unisub, 2026 price list)
highlights: Huge, fearless groupers — the reserve's calling card
The tunnel through La Vaca islet and the Dofí caves
Walls covered in sea fans (Pedra de Déu, Carall Bernat)
Sunfish and eagle rays — seasonal visitors
school_notes: L'Estartit, PADI; website in Spanish, English, Catalan and French
L'Estartit, eco-centre; diving, snorkelling, kayaks; website in Catalan, Spanish, English, French and Dutch

fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.description: Pacific Harbour on the south coast of Viti Levu is Fiji's shark-diving capital. On the organised feed at 30 and 16 m, dozens of bull sharks circle the divers, and sometimes a tiger shark turns up too. You need AOW (or at least 10 logged dives); between shark days you can dive the soft corals of Beqa Lagoon.
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.rating_basis: The Beqa shark feed is called one of the world's best shark dives (Lonely Planet, Divernet, DIVE): guaranteed bull sharks and a chance of a tiger; the Shark Reef reserve is managed by the local villages.
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.hazards: Big sharks at the feed — follow the briefing strictly and stay behind the line; 30 m depth (no-deco limits, narcosis), surface chop, cyclones from November to April.
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.crowd_note: Big groups go on the feed (up to 20–25 divers per boat), but the dives are tightly organised; the ordinary lagoon reefs are uncrowded.
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.region: Viti Levu, south coast (Coral Coast), Beqa Passage
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.marine_life: Up to eight shark species on a single dive: bull, tiger, tawny nurse, sicklefin lemon, silvertip, grey reef, whitetip and blacktip reef sharks; away from the feed — soft corals and sea fans.
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.signature_sites: Shark Reef (Beqa Adventure Divers shark feed, “the Arena”), the Bistro (Aqua-Trek feed), Three Nuns (pinnacles with sea fans), Fantasy, Aquarium
fiji-beqa-lagoon-shark-reef.chamber: Recompression chamber in Suva (~50 km by road)
pros: Guaranteed bull sharks up close
Up to eight shark species per dive
The reserve supports the local villages
No current
cons: Experience needed: depth to 30 m, at least AOW/10 dives
The bull sharks leave from November to early January
Surface chop, rainy and cyclone season (November–April)
Far from Nadi airport (~2.5–3 h)

Tiger sharks (irregular visitors)

chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.description: Truk Lagoon is the mecca of wreck diving: in February 1944 American aircraft sank the Japanese fleet here, and dozens of ships and hundreds of aircraft lie on the bottom with their cargo. The Fujikawa Maru sits upright on an even keel at about 42 m, with disassembled Zero fighters in her hold. Plenty of wreckage lies shallower than 15 m, but the best ships are deeper — you need experience, and many are for tech divers.
chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.rating_basis: The Fujikawa Maru is considered the lagoon's best site (Dan Bailey, Klaus Lindemann); The Times included it in the world's top 10 wreck dives, Aquaviews ranks it 4th in the world. Chuuk is the largest underwater war graveyard, with 15–40 m visibility. Coordinates are from Wikipedia's list of the February 1944 shipwrecks (7°20′ N, 151°53′ E, accurate to the minute, ~1–2 km). Seasons are low-confidence: least rain in January–February (driest in February), most rainy days from May to August; peak is set to January–April, the rest are shoulder months.
chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.hazards: Depth and decompression risk, penetrating the wrecks, unexploded ordnance on board; remoteness from medical help.
chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.region: Chuuk State, Caroline Islands, Truk Lagoon
chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.marine_life: The main attraction is the sunken ships and aircraft with their cargo (trucks, ammunition, medical supplies); about 700 fish species live in the lagoon.
chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.signature_sites: Fujikawa Maru (bottom at 42 m), Heian Maru (34 m), Nippo Maru (15–46 m), Hoki Maru, San Francisco Maru (27–64 m, tech diving), the Betty bomber (15 m), the upside-down Zero (18 m)
pros: The world's finest collection of WWII ships and aircraft
The Fujikawa Maru is in the world's top 10 wreck dives
15–40 m visibility, warm water
cons: Remote: United flights via Guam/Honolulu
Deep wrecks (30–60 m) — you need experience or technical training
The wrecks suffer from dynamite fishing
chuuk-lagoon-fujikawa-maru.airport: TKK — Chuuk International Airport on Weno (Moen); United Airlines flights from Guam and Honolulu
highlights: A6M Zero (8) and A5M fighters in the Fujikawa Maru's forward hold
The Fujikawa Maru's 152 mm bow gun
About 60 ships and 400 aircraft — the largest underwater war graveyard in the world (Operation Hailstone, February 1944)

yap-mil-channel.description: Yap is a small island in Micronesia with a resident population of reef mantas. They're seen at shallow cleaning stations all year, and in groups during the mating season (December–April). Mi'l Channel is a sand-bottomed channel with coral walls, dived as a drift on the tide; currents at the change of tide can be strong. The resort takes few divers, so the sites are almost empty.
yap-mil-channel.rating_basis: Yap is known for its resident population of reef mantas, seen at cleaning stations year-round; the Manta Ray Bay dive resort takes only ~1,000 divers a year, so there are no crowds on site. Seasons: peak is the manta mating season from December to April (per Manta Ray Bay Resort); summer brings the calmest seas, but no months are given, and June to October is the wettest period (July–August are the rainiest). The Mi'l Channel coordinates are a rough estimate (the sources give none): the northwestern part of Yap's reef, accurate to within a few km.
yap-mil-channel.hazards: Currents in the channels at the change of tide (up to ~6 km/h), opposing currents at the surface and near the bottom.
yap-mil-channel.crowd_note: Manta Ray Bay Resort reports ~1,000 divers a year and no crowds on site
yap-mil-channel.region: Yap State, Caroline Islands, northwest of Yap's barrier reef
yap-mil-channel.marine_life: Reef mantas, hawksbill turtles, big barracuda, reef sharks, eagle rays, schools of jacks and snapper; on the channel walls — hard and soft corals, soldierfish, bumphead parrotfish, moray eels, spiny lobsters and octopus.
yap-mil-channel.signature_sites: Mi'l Channel (Manta Ridge), Valley of the Rays, Goofnuw Channel (Goofnuw Mini Wall), Yap Caverns, Vertigo, Gilmaan Wall
pros: Mantas year-round, with mating displays in December–April
Hardly any other divers
Warm water ~29 °C
cons: Remote and expensive (~$109 per dive)

yap-mil-channel.airport: Yap International Airport — United Airlines and Pacific Mission Aviation flights
yap-mil-channel.dive_price_note: Yap Divers: one boat dive $109, two — $199 (tanks, weights, guide, boat); gear extra. ≈€95 per dive
yap-mil-channel.course_price_note: Open Water (SSI/PADI, same price) at Yap Divers — $680

Resident reef mantas at shallow cleaning stations — year-round
In summer — Valley of the Rays: drifting with mantas in the channel
school_notes: Dive resort on Yap; manta dives year-round, MantaFest in late August – early September

roatan-west-end.description: An island at the southern end of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef: the walls start a couple of hundred metres from shore, currents are mild and the water is warm all year. One of the best places in the Caribbean for an inexpensive Open Water course and relaxed reef diving; for experienced divers there are wrecks and a shark dive.
roatan-west-end.rating_basis: Reviews praise the walls right off the shore, mild currents and low prices; one of the most popular places in the Caribbean for PADI courses; few big animals
roatan-west-end.hazards: Boat traffic off West End, fire coral, lionfish; hurricane season June–November
roatan-west-end.crowd_note: West End has lots of centres and boats, but there are over 40 sites, so it's usually not crowded; busier on cruise ship days
roatan-west-end.region: Bay Islands (Islas de la Bahía), Caribbean Sea (southern end of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef)
roatan-west-end.marine_life: Walls with huge sponges and sea fans, hawksbill turtles, seahorses, moray eels, rays, Caribbean reef sharks; the El Aguila and Prince Albert wrecks.
roatan-west-end.signature_sites: Half Moon Bay Wall and Blue Channel (West End), Mary's Place (a crevice in the south), the El Aguila wreck, Cara a Cara (sharks), Pelican Point
roatan-west-end.chamber: Recompression chamber at Anthony's Key Resort in Sandy Bay

Mild currents, short boat rides
Walls and reefs right off West End, with shore diving too
Suits beginners and families

vis-teti-wreck.description: Vis is the most remote inhabited island in Central Dalmatia; it was closed to foreigners for decades, so its underwater world is better preserved than along the mainland. The big draw is the wrecks: the steamship Teti is accessible even with Open Water, the B-24 bomber is for advanced divers, and the B-17 and the stern of the Vassilios T. are for tech divers. Ideal for lovers of wrecks and walls; beginners can do the shallow parts of the Teti and Sika 3.
vis-teti-wreck.rating_basis: Vis is considered the best place to dive in Croatia and one of the strongest wreck locations in the Adriatic (DAN Alert Diver, Scuba Diving, PADI): WWII aircraft and steamships, walls with sea fans; marine life is more modest than in the tropics, and visibility depends on the weather.
vis-teti-wreck.hazards: Depth on the B-24 and the Vassilios T. (deco builds up fast), cold upwellings, currents off the outer headlands, the island's exposure to storms from every direction.
vis-teti-wreck.crowd_note: The island is far from the mainland and was a closed military zone until 1989, so the sites aren't overcrowded even in summer; in July–August Komiža is full of yachts.
vis-teti-wreck.region: Vis island (Komiža), Central Dalmatia, Adriatic Sea
vis-teti-wreck.marine_life: Red and yellow sea fans, red coral, anemones, sponges; conger eels, scorpionfish, John Dory, spiny lobsters, moray eels, nudibranchs; schools of fish around the wrecks.
vis-teti-wreck.signature_sites: The Teti wreck, the B-24 Liberator bomber, the Vassilios T., Sika 3 and Sika 6, the Green Cave (Ravnik), the Blue Cave (Biševo)
vis-teti-wreck.chamber: Recompression chamber at the Institute of Maritime Medicine in Split (accepts civilian divers)

Uncrowded, unspoilt nature
Sites for every level, including technical diving

bunaken-lekuan-wall.description: A small island opposite Manado, at the heart of one of Indonesia's oldest marine parks: sheer coral-covered walls dropping 25–50 m start right off the beach, and turtles turn up on almost every dive. Currents are mostly gentle — fine for training too, with drift dives at some sites. Often combined with muck diving in Lembeh.
bunaken-lekuan-wall.rating_basis: One of Indonesia's first marine parks and a fixture of Southeast Asia top lists thanks to its walls and turtles (liveaboard.com, Wikipedia); some divers mention signs of bleaching and rubbish in the rainy season.
bunaken-lekuan-wall.hazards: Deep walls — watch your depth and buoyancy; changeable currents at some sites (Celah-Celah, Sachiko), carry an SMB; choppy crossings from Manado in the west monsoon season. Park fee IDR 50,000 per day (no more than IDR 150,000 per year).
bunaken-lekuan-wall.crowd_note: Boats come from Manado and from the island itself; Lekuan and Sachiko sometimes have several groups at once, but on the whole it's uncrowded
bunaken-lekuan-wall.region: North Sulawesi, Bunaken National Marine Park (Manado Bay)
bunaken-lekuan-wall.marine_life: Walls covered in sponges and sea fans, dozens of turtles, reef sharks, schools of fusiliers and surgeonfish, Napoleon wrasse; macro — pygmy seahorses, ghost pipefish, nudibranchs; occasionally dugongs and dolphins. The park has ~390 coral species and up to 2,000 fish species, and a coelacanth has been filmed off neighbouring Manado Tua.
bunaken-lekuan-wall.signature_sites: Lekuan I–III, Sachiko Point (to 40 m), Celah-Celah, Depan Kampung, Mandolin, Fukui; Manado Tua and Siladen nearby
pros: Spectacular sheer walls right off the shore
Lots of turtles and fish
Suits both beginners and experienced divers
Easy to combine with Lembeh and Tangkoko
cons: In the rainy season, rubbish and poorer visibility from Manado's run-off
The coral has been damaged in places
The depth of the walls tempts divers to go too deep
bunaken-lekuan-wall.airport: MDC — Manado, ~20 min to the port + 30–45 min by boat

Green and hawksbill turtles on almost every dive
Sperm whales in the straits around the park

gili-islands-shark-point.description: Three small car-free islands off northwest Lombok — a classic place for your first certification: warm water, gently sloping reefs and turtles on almost every dive. Around Gili Air and Gili Meno it's calmer and shallower; the outer sites off Trawangan (Shark Point, Deep Turbo) offer drift dives and reef sharks for more experienced divers.
gili-islands-shark-point.rating_basis: One of Asia's most popular places to get certified: cheap, warm, turtles guaranteed. Experienced divers find the reefs more modest than Komodo and Raja Ampat (Wikivoyage, liveaboard.com).
gili-islands-shark-point.hazards: Currents (strong at the outer sites, with occasional downcurrents), boat traffic between the islands, depth to 35 m at Shark Point; in summer cold thermoclines and jellyfish.
gili-islands-shark-point.crowd_note: There are dozens of dive centres, but plenty of sites and small groups; busy in July–August and over Christmas
gili-islands-shark-point.region: Gili Trawangan, Gili Meno, Gili Air — northwest Lombok, Lombok Strait
gili-islands-shark-point.marine_life: Lots of turtles, reef sharks, stingrays and eagle rays, cuttlefish, pygmy seahorses and shrimps on the gentle slopes; occasionally mantas, and mola mola when cold currents come through.
gili-islands-shark-point.signature_sites: Shark Point and Manta Point (Trawangan), Deep Turbo, Turtle Heaven and the Bounty wreck (Meno), Han's Reef / Turtle Rock (Air), a Japanese patrol boat at 45 m (tech diving)
gili-islands-shark-point.chamber: The nearest confirmed recompression chamber is on Bali (Sanglah hospital, Denpasar); ask your dive centre about a chamber on Lombok/the Gilis

Turtles on almost every dive
Good for training and fun diving
Car-free island atmosphere, well-developed tourist infrastructure

Currents at the outer sites — drift is the norm

gili-islands-shark-point.dive_price_note: The standard benchmark price on the Gilis: fun dive IDR 490,000 + a one-off reef fee of IDR 50,000
gili-islands-shark-point.course_price_note: Open Water (PADI/SSI) ≈ IDR 5,500,000, Gili Dive Association benchmark price

Centres on all three Gilis, on Lombok and in Komodo

komodo-batu-bolong.description: A national park between Sumbawa and Flores where the waters of the Pacific and Indian Oceans meet: powerful currents bring plankton, and with it mantas, sharks and huge schools of fish. Batu Bolong is a coral pinnacle in the middle of the strait and one of the most life-packed sites in the world. Beginners can train at the calm sites, but most centres recommend AOW and 30+ dives; diving is from day boats out of Labuan Bajo or from liveaboards.
komodo-batu-bolong.rating_basis: A fixture of global top lists (liveaboard.com, dive magazine readers' polls): ferocious currents, pristine corals and big animals. Downsides — the currents aren't for everyone, and boat numbers keep growing.
komodo-batu-bolong.hazards: Currents up to 8 knots, whirlpools and downcurrents (Batu Bolong, the Cauldron, Castle Rock), getting separated from the group — an SMB is mandatory, sometimes a reef hook; cold thermoclines in the south; boat traffic.
komodo-batu-bolong.crowd_note: In season lots of day boats and liveaboards gather at Batu Bolong and Manta Point; the park has introduced a daily visitor quota and dated e-tickets
komodo-batu-bolong.region: East Nusa Tenggara, Komodo and Rinca islands, Sape Strait; base — Labuan Bajo (Flores)
komodo-batu-bolong.marine_life: One of the richest places in the Coral Triangle: Batu Bolong's pristine corals, mantas, reef sharks, Napoleon wrasse, schools of jacks and fusiliers, turtles, dolphins; in the south — cold water with macro (seahorses, frogfish, nudibranchs), occasionally mola mola and whale sharks.
komodo-batu-bolong.signature_sites: Batu Bolong, Castle Rock and Crystal Rock (north), Manta Point / Karang Makassar, the Cauldron (Shotgun), Tatawa Besar, Yellow Wall and Cannibal Rock (south, Rinca)
komodo-batu-bolong.chamber: Recompression chamber at Siloam Hospitals Labuan Bajo (since 2018, up to 8 people) — 1–2.5 h by boat from the sites; check availability in advance with DAN or your dive centre

Mantas, sharks and big schools on almost every trip
Variety: drifts, pinnacles, macro in the south
Can be combined with the Komodo dragons

National park fees and quotas, rising prices
Crowded at the main sites

komodo-batu-bolong.dive_price_note: Day trip from Labuan Bajo from $142 (Dive Tribe, usually 3 dives) — ~€44 per dive, national park fees not included

Reef sharks, jacks and tuna on the Castle Rock and Crystal Rock pinnacles

lembeh-strait-muck.description: A narrow strait by the town of Bitung in northeast Sulawesi — the world's top place for muck diving: mimic octopus, frogfish and other rare critters live on the shallow black volcanic sand. There's almost no current and the depths are modest, so beginners can dive here too, but the place really comes into its own for underwater photographers and macro lovers.
lembeh-strait-muck.rating_basis: The acknowledged muck-diving capital of the world (liveaboard.com, photography top lists): the best place for underwater macro photography; a bit dull for lovers of reefs and big animals.
lembeh-strait-muck.hazards: Venomous creatures (blue-ringed octopus, scorpionfish, lionfish, stonefish) — touch nothing; sea urchins; visibility drops sharply after heavy rain.
lembeh-strait-muck.crowd_note: The resorts keep groups small, but at the best-known sites (Hairball, TK) you sometimes meet 2–3 boats
lembeh-strait-muck.region: North Sulawesi, Bitung — between Sulawesi and Lembeh Island
lembeh-strait-muck.marine_life: The world capital of muck diving: on the black volcanic sand — mimic octopus, wunderpus, blue-ringed octopus, frogfish of every kind, flamboyant cuttlefish, ghost pipefish, mantis shrimp, Rhinopias scorpionfish; on the reefs and the Japanese Mawali wreck — soft corals and pygmy seahorses.
lembeh-strait-muck.signature_sites: Hairball, TK (Teluk Kembahu) 1–3, Nudi Falls, Angel's Window, the Mawali wreck (15–30 m), Police Pier

Calm water, shallow depths — long dives

nusa-penida-crystal-bay.description: Three islands southeast of Bali — Indonesia's top place to see the ocean sunfish, mola mola (July–October), and reef mantas (year-round). Currents here are strong and changeable, and in mola season the water at depth can be cold: Crystal Bay and Manta Point are fine for beginners with a guide, while the drifts along the north coast are for experienced divers. You dive from boats out of Sanur or stay on Lembongan / Penida.
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.rating_basis: One of the few places in the world where mola mola are reliably seen at recreational depths; mantas year-round. Features in SSI/PADI top lists for Indonesia; liveaboard.com and guides mention strong currents and cold thermoclines.
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.hazards: Strong currents that change direction and downcurrents (especially in the channel between Penida and Ceningan), sudden cold thermoclines, surge at Manta Point, boat traffic. An SMB is a must, and dive with an experienced local guide.
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.crowd_note: In July–September dozens of boats sit at Crystal Bay and Manta Point at the same time; an early start and the north-coast sites help
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.region: Nusa Islands (Penida, Lembongan, Ceningan), southeast Bali, Badung Strait
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.marine_life: Reef mantas year-round; in July–October mola mola rise from the deep to the cleaning stations; turtles, jacks, barracuda, reef and bamboo sharks, rich hard and soft corals (a marine park since 2010, >500 fish species).
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.signature_sites: Crystal Bay, Manta Point, Toyapakeh, SD Point, Ped and Sental (drift along the north coast), Blue Corner (Lembongan)
nusa-penida-crystal-bay.chamber: Recompression chambers on Bali: Sanglah hospital (RSUP Prof. Ngoerah), Denpasar, and Kasih Ibu Saba (Gianyar) — ~40 min by boat to Sanur + 30–60 min overland

Padang Bai; has a Russian-language website, runs trips to Manta Point and Crystal Bay; check the instructors' languages

raja-ampat-cape-kri.description: A remote archipelago off West Papua whose reefs are considered the richest on the planet: at Cape Kri hundreds of fish species have been counted on a single dive. Diving is from liveaboards (main season October–April) or from resorts and homestays on Kri, Mansuar and Arborek. Currents in the Dampier Strait are strong, so it's a place for experienced divers (AOW and a few dozen dives).
raja-ampat-cape-kri.rating_basis: On almost every global top list (liveaboard.com, dive magazines) as the place with the highest reef biodiversity on the planet; downsides — the journey, the cost and the currents.
raja-ampat-cape-kri.hazards: Strong tidal currents and downcurrents in the Dampier Strait, remoteness from medical help (insurance with evacuation cover is mandatory), malaria zone, heat and sun on the boats.
raja-ampat-cape-kri.crowd_note: The area is huge and boats are few; at Cape Kri and Manta Sandy you'll meet several liveaboard groups in season
raja-ampat-cape-kri.region: Southwest Papua, Raja Ampat archipelago (Waigeo, Mansuar, Kri, Misool)
raja-ampat-cape-kri.marine_life: The heart of the Coral Triangle: more than 600 hard coral species and 1,500+ reef fish species; huge schools of jacks, barracuda and fusiliers at Cape Kri, mantas, wobbegongs, reef sharks, turtles, rich macro.
raja-ampat-cape-kri.signature_sites: Cape Kri, Sardine Reef, Blue Magic, Manta Sandy, Mike's Point, Chicken Reef, Melissa's Garden; in the south — Misool (Boo Windows, Magic Mountain)
raja-ampat-cape-kri.chamber: Recompression chamber in Waisai (according to DAN, it was under repair in 2019 and divers were evacuated to Bali) — check in advance whether it's working; otherwise air evacuation from Sorong
pros: The highest reef biodiversity in the world
Few people, pristine corals
Mantas, wobbegongs, huge schools of fish
Options from homestays to premium liveaboards
cons: A long, expensive journey (Sorong + ferry/boat)
Strong currents — not for beginners
Limited medical care, the chamber question
Marine park fee IDR 1,000,000 (≈ $100)
raja-ampat-cape-kri.airport: SOQ — Sorong (flights via Jakarta, Makassar or Manado); ferry to Waisai ~2 h, then a boat to the resort
highlights: Record fish diversity on a single dive (Cape Kri)
Reef mantas at cleaning stations (Manta Sandy, Mansuar)
Wobbegongs (carpet sharks), epaulette “walking” sharks, pygmy seahorses
school_notes: The archipelago's oldest dive resort, right by Cape Kri

tulamben-liberty-wreck.description: A village in northeast Bali that people visit for the USAT Liberty transport ship: she lies 25–30 m off a rocky beach at 3–30 m depth, so you can dive her from shore, and the top of the hull is visible even with a mask. There's almost no current, so the site suits both Open Water courses and experienced divers — with the Drop Off wall and muck diving at Seraya nearby.
tulamben-liberty-wreck.rating_basis: The Liberty is one of the best-known and most accessible shore-dive wrecks in the world; it's in every Bali guide (PADI, SSI, Stingy Nomads). Downside — daytime crowds and the rocky beach.
tulamben-liberty-wreck.hazards: Slippery rocks at the entry and surf in the rainy season; depth to 30 m at the stern; penetrating the hull — only with a guide and training; the current sometimes picks up towards evening.
tulamben-liberty-wreck.crowd_note: In high season the Liberty gets up to ~100 divers a day; it's best to stay in Tulamben and dive at dawn, before the groups from southern Bali arrive
tulamben-liberty-wreck.marine_life: A hull overgrown with soft corals and sea fans, schools of glassfish and jacks, barracuda, bumphead parrotfish, Napoleon wrasse, turtles; at the neighbouring sites — pygmy seahorses, frogfish, mimic octopus, harlequin shrimp.
tulamben-liberty-wreck.signature_sites: The USAT Liberty wreck, Drop Off (wall), Coral Garden (underwater temple at ~15 m), Seraya Secret (muck diving), Kubu, Batu Kelebit
tulamben-liberty-wreck.chamber: Recompression chambers in Denpasar (Sanglah hospital / RSUP Prof. Ngoerah) and at Kasih Ibu Saba hospital (Gianyar), ~2–2.5 h by road
pros: A famous wreck from shore, no boat needed
Almost no current — suits beginners and training
Reef, wall and muck diving in one bay
Night dives on the Liberty
cons: Daytime crowds of groups from southern Bali
A beach of big cobbles — an awkward entry (porters help)
Far from the airport (~2.5–3 h), no ATMs in the village
tulamben-liberty-wreck.dive_price_note: Guided shore dive with gear (Tulamben Wreck Divers, IDR 495,000)
tulamben-liberty-wreck.course_price_note: PADI Open Water, 3–4 days, 4 dives on the Liberty (IDR ~5,075,000)
highlights: The USAT Liberty transport ship (120 m), 30 m from shore
Schools of bumphead parrotfish at dawn
Macro: pygmy seahorses, ghost pipefish, mimic octopus (Drop Off, Seraya Secret)
school_notes: Tulamben; Russian-language website “Diving in Bali with a Russian instructor”; on Baliforum (2026) people praise the Russian-speaking instructor Oleg
Tulamben; Russian is listed in its PADI profile, and try dives and OWD in Russian are sold through it
Local centre right by the Liberty, Balinese guides; transparent prices
Dive resort with its own centre, trips all over Bali

eilat-coral-beach.description: Eilat is Israel's resort at the northernmost tip of the Red Sea: a short strip of reefs along the south coast with entries straight off the beach, calm water with no current and strong dive infrastructure. A good place for an Open Water course and relaxed dives; seasoned divers will quickly find it too small.
eilat-coral-beach.rating_basis: Divezone and reviews value Eilat for its easy shore dives, good infrastructure and training, but the reefs are small and trampled in places, and there are few big fish — a level below the Egyptian resorts.
eilat-coral-beach.hazards: Sea urchins and fire coral in the shallows, lionfish; walking on the reef is banned (entries via jetties only), waves in a southerly wind; Israeli rules require a check dive and insurance.
eilat-coral-beach.crowd_note: At weekends (Friday–Saturday) and on Israeli holidays the shore sites fill with groups and snorkellers; quiet on winter weekdays.
eilat-coral-beach.region: Eilat's south coast, Gulf of Aqaba (Gulf of Eilat), Red Sea
eilat-coral-beach.marine_life: Branching and table corals, anemones with clownfish, reef fish, octopus, moray eels, spotted rays; occasionally turtles. Big animals are rare visitors.
eilat-coral-beach.signature_sites: Japanese Gardens, Moses Rock, Coral Beach (reserve), Neptune's Tables, the Satil wreck, Three Sisters, Veronica
eilat-coral-beach.chamber: Recompression chamber at Yoseftal Medical Center, Eilat
pros: Calm water and easy shore entries
Well-developed infrastructure, lots of centres, some Russian-speaking
Recompression chamber in town
Direct flights to Ramon, year-round season
cons: The reefs are small and damaged in places
Expensive compared with Egypt
Water ~21 °C in winter
Crowded at weekends and on holidays
eilat-coral-beach.course_price_note: Manta: 5-day Open Water course ₪1400 (theory and 6 dives); special offer ₪1150 from November to February

The Satil wreck (an Israeli Navy ship) at ~24 m
Moses Rock and the Coral Beach reserve — easy shore dives via jetties

havelock-dixons-pinnacle.description: Havelock (officially Swaraj Dweep) is the main dive island of India's Andaman Islands, with a season from November to April. It has easy reefs for an Open Water course and advanced pinnacles at 20–30 m with schooling fish, reef sharks and currents. For those who want off-the-beaten-track diving at Indian prices and are ready for a long journey via Port Blair.
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.rating_basis: The best place to dive in India according to guides and dive centres: pinnacles with sharks and big fish, few boats. The coral has been bleached in places; a level below the nearby Similan Islands and Mergui.
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.hazards: Strong currents at Jackson's Bar and by Peel lighthouse around the new and full moon; saltwater crocodiles live in the Andamans (a snorkeller was killed on Havelock in 2010) — swim and shore dive only in permitted areas
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.crowd_note: Few boats on the sites even in season; most of the traffic is snorkelling at Elephant Beach
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.region: Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andaman Sea
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.marine_life: Three pinnacles covered in soft corals with Napoleon wrasse, groupers, reef sharks, rays and turtles; on the walls — octopus, cuttlefish, moray eels, scorpionfish; at the more distant sites — schools of barracuda, jacks and tuna. Whale sharks occasionally pass through.
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.signature_sites: Dixon's Pinnacle (20–30 m), Johnny's Gorge (25–30 m), Jackson's Bar (25–30 m, strong currents), The Wall (10–55 m), Nemo Reef (5–15 m, for beginners), the SS Inchkett wreck (6–18 m)
pros: Few boats and divers on the sites
Pinnacles with big fish and sharks
Easy sites for training
Radhanagar beach and the island's relaxed atmosphere
cons: A long journey: flight to Port Blair and a ferry
June to September is the southwest monsoon, with poor visibility
No recompression chamber on the island (according to the sources we found)
The coral has partly suffered from bleaching
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.airport: IXZ — Port Blair, then a ferry to Havelock ~1.5–2.5 h
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.dive_price_note: Nearby sites: 2 dives a day for ₹6,500 with full gear and guide (more distant ones ₹8,000–10,000)
havelock-dixons-pinnacle.course_price_note: PADI Open Water at DIVEIndia, ₹36,000 all-inclusive, from 4 days
highlights: Reef sharks, rays, turtles and big groupers on the pinnacles
Whale sharks (occasionally) at Dixon's Pinnacle
Schools of jacks, barracuda and tuna at Johnny's Gorge and Jackson's Bar
school_notes: Havelock's oldest dive centre (since 2003–2004), Beach No. 5; discovered The Wall; operates year-round, weather permitting
PADI Dive Center on Havelock, courses and internships

silfra-thingvellir.description: Silfra is a flooded fissure in the Thingvellir rift zone, where the North American and Eurasian plates pull apart. It's fed by glacial meltwater filtered through lava for decades, so it's clear to 100 m and beyond, with a year-round temperature of 2–4 °C. It's a single dive to 18 m with an instructor; you need Open Water and a drysuit certification (or 10 drysuit dives in the last two years). It's not about fish — it's about the feeling of flying over a rift.
silfra-thingvellir.rating_basis: Silfra is a constant on lists of the world's most unusual and best dive sites: a dive between continental plates in water with over 100 m visibility. Downsides — almost no life, 2–4 °C water, a high price for one short dive.
silfra-thingvellir.hazards: Hypothermia and regulator freezing, drysuit and buoyancy problems; going head-down through the “Toilet” tunnel is forbidden because it's unstable; strict health requirements (60+ need a doctor's certificate).
silfra-thingvellir.crowd_note: In summer there are queues of diver and snorkeller groups from Reykjavík at the entry platform; quieter in the morning and in winter.
silfra-thingvellir.region: Thingvellir National Park, Lake Thingvallavatn, southwest Iceland
silfra-thingvellir.marine_life: Almost no life: bright green algae (“troll hair”) on the bottom and walls, occasionally a dwarf Arctic char.
silfra-thingvellir.signature_sites: Big Crack, Silfra Hall, the Cathedral, the Lagoon; nearby — the Davíðsgjá fissure
silfra-thingvellir.chamber: Recompression chamber at Landspítali University Hospital in Reykjavík (~1 h)
pros: Unique: a dive between continental plates
Visibility over 100 m
Year-round, easy to reach from Reykjavík
Can be combined with the Golden Circle
cons: Water at 2–4 °C, you need drysuit experience
Almost no underwater life
Expensive: ~€245 for a single dive
Lots of groups in summer
silfra-thingvellir.airport: KEF — Keflavík, ~1.5 h; ~45–60 min from Reykjavík
silfra-thingvellir.dive_price_note: ≈€245: from ISK 35,999 for one dive with an instructor, all gear (drysuit) and the Silfra entrance fee (DIVE.IS)
highlights: The fissure between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates
Glacial water with over 100 m visibility

school_notes: Daily tours year-round, transfer from Reykjavík; a 2-day “drysuit course + Silfra” combo (ISK 99,980)

ustica-scoglio-del-medico.description: Ustica is a small volcanic island 60 km north of Palermo and Italy's first marine reserve. Black lava walls drop to 40–50 m, the water is exceptionally clear, and fearless groupers and schools of barracuda live in the protected zone in the northwest. There are sites for training, but the best of it — the banks and walls — is for confident divers.
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.rating_basis: Ustica is Italy's first marine reserve (1986) and one of the Mediterranean's classic dive destinations: clear water, volcanic walls, lots of groupers and barracuda. Downsides — a short season and expensive dives.
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.hazards: Currents on the exposed banks (Colombara, Secchitello), depth on the walls, caves — only with the appropriate training, rough seas in northerly winds.
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.crowd_note: The island is small and there aren't many boats; lots of Italians come in August, but the outer banks are still uncrowded.
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.region: Ustica island, Tyrrhenian Sea, north of Palermo (Sicily)
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.marine_life: Dusky and white groupers, barracuda, dentex, amberjacks, croakers, salema; occasionally tuna; spiny lobsters and lobsters; red and yellow sea fans, rare pink sponges.
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.signature_sites: Scoglio del Medico, Secca della Colombara, Secchitello (24–50 m, for the experienced), Punta San Paolo, Secca d'Africa, Grotta dei Gamberi (Shrimp Cave)
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.chamber: No recompression chamber on the island; the nearest is in Palermo (helicopter evacuation) — check with your dive centre
pros: A reserve since 1986: lots of groupers and barracuda
Very clear water
Volcanic topography: walls, canyons, grottoes
A quiet island with no mass tourism
cons: Reached by ferry/hydrofoil from Palermo
The season is effectively May to October
Expensive dives (≈€65)
The best sites are deep and have currents
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.airport: PMO — Palermo, ~2.5–3 h (road to the port + hydrofoil or ferry to Ustica)
ustica-scoglio-del-medico.dive_price_note: One dive with your own gear; with rental €85, a 10-dive package €450 (Altamarea Diving Center)

aqaba-cedar-pride.description: Aqaba is Jordan's outlet to the Red Sea: calm water at the northern end of the gulf, shore dives onto coral gardens and a collection of wrecks — from the Cedar Pride to a tank, aircraft and an entire underwater military museum. Great for a first course, current-free wreck diving and a trip combined with Petra and Wadi Rum.
aqaba-cedar-pride.rating_basis: Divezone and reviews praise the easy shore dives, the Cedar Pride and the unusual artificial reefs (tank, aircraft, military museum), as well as the calm water; few big fish, and the reefs are more modest than Egypt's.
aqaba-cedar-pride.hazards: Sea urchins and fire coral in the shallows, lionfish and scorpionfish, boat traffic near the port; wreck penetration only with training.
aqaba-cedar-pride.crowd_note: The shore sites on the south coast are usually quiet; more locals and snorkellers at weekends and on holidays.
aqaba-cedar-pride.region: Aqaba's south coast, Aqaba Marine Park, Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea
aqaba-cedar-pride.marine_life: Coral gardens with soft corals, macro life (frogfish, pipefish, shrimps, nudibranchs), lionfish and moray eels; turtles and rays are a nice bonus but not guaranteed.
aqaba-cedar-pride.signature_sites: Cedar Pride, Japanese Garden, the M42 tank, the C-130 Hercules, the TriStar L-1011, the Underwater Military Museum, Seventh Heaven
aqaba-cedar-pride.chamber: We couldn't confirm a recompression chamber in Aqaba itself; the nearest confirmed one is at Yoseftal hospital in Eilat (~15 km, across the border)

Wrecks and artificial reefs at shallow depths
30–40 m visibility most of the year
Easy to combine with Petra and Wadi Rum

Water ~21 °C in winter
Prices higher than in Egypt
Russian-speaking centres not confirmed

kerama-islands-zamami.description: The Kerama Islands, 35–70 minutes by ferry from Naha, are Okinawa's top dive area, with clear water and national park reefs. The villages on Zamami, Aka and Tokashiki live off diving and snorkelling. In summer and autumn the water is warm; in winter and early spring it's cooler (~22 °C), but you can see humpback whales around the islands.
kerama-islands-zamami.rating_basis: Kerama's reefs have been a national park since 2014, and two areas are Ramsar wetlands (248 coral species); on Zamami and Aka the economy runs almost entirely on diving and snorkelling. This is a cautious rating: no specific dive sites, visibility, currents or prices were found in the available sources. Seasons are low-confidence: peak is June–October (water 27–29 °C, high season per Wikivoyage), December–April has 22–23 °C water but whales; the typhoon season isn't described in the sources. Coordinates are an estimate: the channel between Zamami and Aka, south of Zamami village.
kerama-islands-zamami.crowd_note: During Golden Week (late April – early May), in summer and in August–October, book ferries and accommodation in advance
kerama-islands-zamami.region: Okinawa Prefecture, Kerama Shotō National Park, west of Naha
kerama-islands-zamami.marine_life: Coral reefs with 248 coral species (mostly Acropora) and lots of reef fish; humpback whales around the islands from late December to early April.
kerama-islands-zamami.signature_sites: The reefs around Zamami, Aka, Tokashiki and Geruma; Furuzamami and Ama beaches (snorkelling)

Quick to reach from Naha (fast ferry 35–70 min)

hikkaduwa-coral-garden.description: Hikkaduwa is the main dive resort on Sri Lanka's southwest coast, with a season from November to April. It has easy reefs and rocks at 6–20 m for beginners, turtles right off the beach and around twenty historic wrecks within an hour by boat, including the Conch tanker. A good place for an inexpensive Open Water course with a Russian-speaking instructor, but not for those looking for pristine coral and great visibility.
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.rating_basis: Sri Lanka's best-known dive resort and the capital of local diving (Lonely Planet, PADI, DiveSriLanka): lots of historic wrecks and turtles, but the reef was badly damaged by the 1998 bleaching and the 2004 tsunami, and visibility is modest. Not on global top lists.
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.hazards: Surf and strong surge on the shallow rocks, boat traffic, currents at Kiralagala, sea urchins, lionfish
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.crowd_note: The reserve reef off the beach is busy with snorkellers and glass-bottom boats; the wrecks and outer rocks are quieter
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.region: Southern Province, southwest coast, Indian Ocean
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.marine_life: Turtles almost guaranteed, moray eels, groupers, hawkfish, anthias, lobsters, octopus, nudibranchs; at Kiralagala — schools of jacks, fusiliers and redtooth triggerfish, black coral.
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.signature_sites: Coral Garden (6–18 m), the SS Conch tanker wreck (21 m), Earl of Shaftesbury (12–14 m), Goda Gala (22 m), Kiralagala (to 40 m — AOW/Deep only), Black Coral Point (30 m)
hikkaduwa-coral-garden.chamber: The nearest confirmed recompression chamber is the Sri Lanka Navy's in Trincomalee (~7–8 h); in 2022 divers from the southwest coast (Unawatuna) were taken there

Interesting historic wrecks

English- and German-speaking instructors

trincomalee-pigeon-island.description: Trincomalee and Nilaveli beach are Sri Lanka's main dive destination in the summer months, when the southwest of the island is shut down by the monsoon. The shallow reef of Pigeon Island National Park, with reef sharks and turtles, suits first dives and Open Water courses, and historic wrecks lie in the deep Trincomalee harbour. In spring people also come here for blue whale trips.
trincomalee-pigeon-island.rating_basis: Sri Lanka's main summer dive destination (PADI/SSI guides, DiveSriLanka); the Pigeon Island reef is easy and pretty but suffers from tourist crowds, and the region's strengths are its historic wrecks and whales. Not on global top lists.
trincomalee-pigeon-island.hazards: Boat traffic around Pigeon Island, currents in places at the outer sites, sea urchins and lionfish; great depth on the technical wrecks
trincomalee-pigeon-island.crowd_note: Pigeon Island gets lots of snorkelling boats with tourists during the day; divers are better off going out early in the morning, and the sites in Trincomalee harbour are quieter
trincomalee-pigeon-island.region: Eastern Province, Nilaveli, Bay of Bengal
trincomalee-pigeon-island.marine_life: A shallow Acropora reef around Pigeon Island with blacktip reef sharks, turtles, moray eels and schools of reef fish; in Trincomalee harbour — 19th–20th-century wrecks, rays, groupers. In spring and summer boats go out from Trincomalee to see blue whales and sperm whales.
trincomalee-pigeon-island.signature_sites: Pigeon Island (national park), Swami Rock by the Koneswaram temple, Sithanampara, Coral Island, the sunken Admiralty Floating Dock 23 (15–40 m), the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes off Batticaloa (53 m — tech divers only)
trincomalee-pigeon-island.chamber: The Sri Lanka Navy recompression chamber (Command Diving & Salvage Unit, Eastern Naval Command) in Trincomalee — according to DiveSriLanka, the only one in the country; civilian divers are treated for a fee

A shallow, calm reef — suits beginners and snorkellers

PADI centre in Trincomalee

herceg-novi-mamula.description: The entrance to the Bay of Kotor by Herceg Novi is Montenegro's main dive area: merchant and naval ships have sunk here for centuries, so a small stretch of water holds steamships, torpedo boats, a patrol boat and even a British Spitfire. Luštica has the Blue Cave and underwater grottoes, and Žanjic bay offers easy dives for beginners. A good choice for wreck lovers combining diving with a beach holiday.
herceg-novi-mamula.rating_basis: Montenegro is valued for its WWII and Austro-Hungarian-era wrecks at the entrance to the Boka, the Luštica caves and 15–35 m visibility along the coast (PADI); its marine life and corals can't compete with the tropics or the Mediterranean reserves.
herceg-novi-mamula.hazards: Depth on most wrecks (30–41 m), penetrations and caves — only with a guide, boat traffic and tour boats at the Blue Cave and Mamula.
herceg-novi-mamula.crowd_note: Few dive boats, uncrowded sites; in summer the Blue Cave is packed with excursion boats full of snorkellers.
herceg-novi-mamula.region: Entrance to the Bay of Kotor, Luštica peninsula, Adriatic Sea
herceg-novi-mamula.marine_life: Typical Adriatic life: octopus, moray eels, conger eels, scorpionfish, spiny lobsters, wrasse and schools of salema; sponges and sea fans on the wrecks.
herceg-novi-mamula.signature_sites: The PBR 512 patrol boat (Žanjic), the 76T Golešnica torpedo boat (32–35 m), the Tihany steamship off Mamula, the Blue Cave, “Poseidon's City”, the Spitfire
pros: Lots of wrecks from different eras in a small area
The caves and grottoes of Luštica
Calm water in the Boka with almost no current
Lots of Russian-speaking tourists and residents
cons: Poor marine life by tropical standards
The interesting wrecks are deep (30–40 m)
Visibility inside the bay is worse than in the open sea
Water 14 °C in winter
herceg-novi-mamula.airport: TIV — Tivat, ~40 min; DBV — Dubrovnik, ~45–60 min (with a border crossing)
herceg-novi-mamula.dive_price_note: ≈€60 per dive: a 2-dive boat day is €120, gear included (Adriatic Blue)
herceg-novi-mamula.course_price_note: SSI Open Water with gear; PADI Open Water — €600 (Adriatic Blue)
highlights: The PBR 512 patrol boat at the entrance to Žanjic bay (24 m) — one of Montenegro's most visited wrecks
The Tihany steamship (1912) off Mamula island, ~40 m — the country's largest accessible wreck
The Blue Cave on Luštica (7–25 m) and other grottoes
A British Spitfire fighter (1944, ~31 m) and torpedo boats in the Boka
school_notes: Herceg Novi, Škver harbour; since 2003, SSI/PADI/CMAS, diving year-round; the website doesn't list languages
Budva (~1 h drive); Russian and Ukrainian are listed in its PADI profile

nosy-be-tanikely.description: Nosy Be is a tropical island off northwest Madagascar and the country's main dive base. The best-known site is the marine reserve around Tanikely island, with excellent snorkelling and shallow reefs; experienced divers dive the deep banks and take liveaboard trips to the Mitsio archipelago.
nosy-be-tanikely.rating_basis: Madagascar's main dive resort: the Tanikely marine reserve with world-class snorkelling (Wikivoyage), and the Mitsio islands are famous for diving. Fact-check (November 2026): the whale shark and humpback whale months, turtles and the absence of a recompression chamber weren't confirmed by sources — removed or zeroed. Seasons are low-confidence: according to Wikipedia the rainy season runs from October to early May, with a short dry season until September and strong northeasterly winds sometimes in August; no dive season is given anywhere, so all months are shoulder months. Coordinates not verified (no coordinates for Tanikely in open sources) — left as an estimate.
nosy-be-tanikely.hazards: Currents on the outer banks, cyclones in January–March, remoteness from medical help
nosy-be-tanikely.crowd_note: Tanikely is a popular snorkelling excursion with lots of boats during the day; the outer sites are empty
nosy-be-tanikely.marine_life: In the Tanikely reserve — turtles, clownfish, lionfish, moray eels, schools of reef fish in the shallows; on the outer banks (Grand Banc) — groupers, barracuda, rays. A notable population of Omura's whales lives in the waters around Nosy Be.
nosy-be-tanikely.signature_sites: Nosy Tanikely marine reserve, Grand Banc, Nosy Sakatia, longer trips to the Mitsio archipelago
pros: World-class snorkelling at Tanikely
Calm water, suits beginners
Warm water year-round
Can be combined with a Madagascar safari
cons: The rainy season runs from October to early May; strong northeasterly winds sometimes in August
Tricky logistics and poor medical care
The inner reefs have degraded in places
nosy-be-tanikely.airport: NOS — Nosy Be (Fascene), ~30–40 min to Ambatoloaka
highlights: Tanikely marine reserve — world-class snorkelling, popular with divers too
The Mitsio islands (Nosy Tsarabanjina) — “world-famous” for diving
Omura's whales — a notable population in the waters around Nosy Be

mergui-archipelago-black-rock.description: The Mergui Archipelago is more than 800 almost uninhabited islands in southern Myanmar, visited only by liveaboards from Ranong in Thailand (usually 4–8 days). The draw is the wilderness and the big animals: sharks on the Burma Banks, mantas at Black Rock, and the Western Rocky tunnel with nurse sharks. Suits experienced divers ready for currents, swell and variable visibility.
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.rating_basis: A wild, remote archipelago that only opened to foreigners in 1997: sharks on the Burma Banks and mantas at Black Rock (liveaboard.com, Ranong operators). Reviews from 2019–2025 mention variable visibility, strong currents and swell.
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.hazards: Strong currents and swell on the Burma Banks and at Black Rock, remoteness from medical help and a recompression chamber, depth
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.crowd_note: Almost deserted: usually one boat on site, and just a few liveaboards on the whole route per season
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.region: Tanintharyi, Andaman Sea (liveaboards from Ranong, Thailand)
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.marine_life: Rocks and underwater banks on the edge of the continental shelf with silvertip, whitetip and blacktip sharks, mantas and rays; at Western Rocky — a tunnel with nurse sharks, guitarfish, harlequin shrimp and seahorses. Mantas and whale sharks visit from February to May.
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.signature_sites: Black Rock (~100 miles northwest of Kawthaung; mantas, sharks), the Burma Banks — Silvertip, Rainbow, Roe, Heckford (sharks, experienced divers only), Western Rocky (a swim-through tunnel), Shark Cave, North Twin
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.chamber: The nearest is the SSS Recompression Chamber on Phuket (hundreds of kilometres away; evacuation from a liveaboard takes many hours)
pros: Almost nobody on the sites
Sharks, mantas and whale sharks (February–May)
A mix of big fish and macro
Easy to combine with Richelieu Rock and the Similans
cons: Liveaboard only, expensive: ~USD 200–220 a day and up
Strong currents and swell, not for beginners
Variable visibility; the reefs have been damaged by fishing in places
A long way to a recompression chamber
Myanmar entry formalities (handled by the operator)
mergui-archipelago-black-rock.airport: UNN — Ranong (direct flights from Bangkok); liveaboards depart from Ranong, some from Khao Lak/Phuket (HKT)
highlights: Manta rays and whale sharks
Silvertip, whitetip and blacktip sharks (Black Rock, the Burma Banks)
Tawny nurse sharks in the Western Rocky tunnel
Macro: harlequin shrimp, toadfish, seahorses
school_notes: Liveaboards from Ranong to Mergui and Richelieu Rock; English, French, Thai; 8 days/25 dives — from THB 54,000

gozo-blue-hole.description: Gozo is one of the best dive islands in the Mediterranean: almost every dive is a shore dive, and the water is clear all year. The Blue Hole at Dwejra is a natural well with an arch leading out to a wall in the open sea; nearby are the Inland Sea tunnel and the reef formed by the collapsed Azure Window. There are shallow bays for training, and wrecks, caves and walls to 40 m for experienced divers.
gozo-blue-hole.rating_basis: Gozo consistently ranks among the top dive destinations in Europe and the Mediterranean (PADI, Scuba Diving, DIVE): clear water, topography with caves and arches, lots of shore sites and wrecks; the downside — marine life is rather sparse by tropical standards.
gozo-blue-hole.hazards: Rough water at the Blue Hole exit in a northwesterly wind; boats in the Inland Sea tunnel; depth along the walls (quickly drops past 30–40 m); slippery rocks at the entry; caves and swim-throughs — only with a guide.
gozo-blue-hole.crowd_note: In summer Dwejra is the island's most popular site, with lots of groups and snorkellers at the Blue Hole entry at the same time; early mornings and the off-season are noticeably quieter.
gozo-blue-hole.region: Gozo island, west coast, Mediterranean Sea
gozo-blue-hole.marine_life: Groupers, dentex, sea bass, octopus, moray eels, spiny lobsters, nudibranchs and sea hares; occasionally tuna, barracuda and amberjacks over the drop-offs.
gozo-blue-hole.signature_sites: Blue Hole, Azure Reef, the Inland Sea and tunnel, Coral Cave, Fungus Rock (by boat), the MV Karwela wreck off Xatt l-Aħmar
gozo-blue-hole.chamber: Recompression chamber at Gozo General Hospital (Victoria, Gozo; a new multiplace chamber since 2026) and the hyperbaric unit at Mater Dei Hospital on Malta
pros: Shore diving — flexible and inexpensive
Excellent visibility, especially in winter
Caves, arches, tunnels and wrecks on one small island
Year-round diving, lots of dive centres
Recompression chamber on the island itself
cons: Sparser marine life than in the tropics
Water 15 °C in winter; Dwejra is closed in westerly storms
Rocky entries carrying heavy gear
Crowded at the Blue Hole in summer
gozo-blue-hole.airport: MLA — Malta, ~1.5–2 h (road to Ċirkewwa + 25-min ferry to Mġarr)
gozo-blue-hole.dive_price_note: Guided shore dive: tank, weights and jeep transfer, no gear (rental +€12); boat dive +€27.50
gozo-blue-hole.course_price_note: PADI Open Water with eLearning, gear and certification (Atlantis Gozo)
highlights: The Blue Hole: a well in the rock with an arch opening onto the open sea
The Inland Sea tunnel — ~80 m to the wall
The reef on the rubble of the Azure Window arch (collapsed in 2017)
Scuttled wrecks off the coast: MV Karwela, Cominoland, Xlendi
school_notes: Marsalforn, 5* PADI IDC; instructors speak German, Polish, French, Italian and English
Marsalforn, SSI centre
Marsalforn, SSI centre

mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.description: Flic-en-Flac on the sheltered west coast is Mauritius's most popular dive area: it's the calmest part of the island in the trade-wind season, and the island's best sites are close by — the arch of La Cathédrale, Rempart Serpent and several wrecks. Currents are usually mild, so it suits both training and relaxed dives for experienced divers.
mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.rating_basis: La Cathédrale is Mauritius's best-known dive site; reviews praise the topography, the wrecks and the easy conditions, but note there are fewer fish and less coral than in the Maldives or the Red Sea. Fact-check (November 2026): Wikivoyage confirms La Cathédrale is one of the best-known sites and that the best time to dive is November to April (very good visibility); cyclones are possible from November to April, most often from late December to March. Humpback whales, sperm whales and a recompression chamber at Victoria hospital weren't confirmed by sources — removed. Coordinates not verified (no coordinates for the site in open sources): a point on the outer reef southwest of Flic-en-Flac is left as an estimate.
mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.hazards: Stonefish and scorpionfish (don't touch the bottom), swell beyond the reef, cyclones in January–March
mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.crowd_note: Flic-en-Flac has lots of hotel dive centres; La Cathédrale sometimes has several groups in high season
mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.region: West coast of Mauritius, Indian Ocean
mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.marine_life: Arches and grottoes with batfish and soldierfish, moray eels, scorpionfish, stonefish, lionfish, turtles, schools of reef fish; dolphins off the west coast.
mauritius-flic-en-flac-cathedral.signature_sites: La Cathédrale (arch and grotto at 18–25 m), Rempart Serpent, Couline Bambou, the Kei Sei 113 and Tug II wrecks
pros: Sheltered coast — calm even in the trade-wind season
Arches, grottoes and wrecks close together
Lots of hotel dive centres
Dolphins off the west coast
cons: November–April — cyclones possible (most often from late December to March)
In winter (July–September) the water is around 23 °C
Fewer fish than in the Maldives
Hotel diving isn't cheap
highlights: The La Cathédrale arch — one of Mauritius's best-known and most popular sites
Dolphins off the west coast (dolphin tours)
Moray eels, scorpionfish and stonefish at Rempart Serpent

maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.description: Baa Atoll (a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 2011) is famous for Hanifaru Bay: when the tide pushes plankton into it, dozens and sometimes up to a hundred mantas gather here, and whale sharks show up too. The waters around Dharavandhoo island — Dharavandhoo Thila and Hanifaru — are known to divers worldwide and are protected. You stay at resorts or on local islands (Dharavandhoo, Thulhaadhoo).
maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.rating_basis: Hanifaru is one of the world's largest manta aggregation sites (up to 100 individuals); Baa Atoll is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve (2011), with ~350,000 tourists a year. Fact-check (November 2026): the manta and whale shark season months, the “snorkel only” rule, visitor limits and recompression chambers weren't confirmed by sources — zeroed. All months are shoulder months (conservatively) until there's a source on the manta season. Coordinates not verified — estimated at ~2.5 km north-northeast of Dharavandhoo (island coordinates 5°09′30″ N, 73°07′50″ E per Wikipedia).
maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.hazards: Swell and currents in the monsoon season, boat traffic at Hanifaru; keep your distance from the mantas and don't dive down onto them from above
maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.region: Baa Atoll (UNESCO Biosphere Reserve), northwest of Malé
maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.marine_life: When the tide pushes plankton into Hanifaru Bay, dozens and sometimes up to a hundred mantas gather there, and whale sharks show up (mostly young males). On the atoll's thilas — turtles, reef sharks, eagle rays, moray eels, soft corals.
maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.signature_sites: Hanifaru Bay (snorkel only), Dhigu Thila, Dhonfanu Thila, Nelivaru Thila, manta cleaning stations on the atoll's thilas
pros: One of the world's largest manta aggregations
UNESCO Biosphere Reserve
Its own airport at Dharavandhoo (since 2012)
cons: Manta aggregations depend on the tides and plankton — not guaranteed
June–November is the southwest monsoon: rain, strong wind, storms
Resorts are expensive
The manta season by month isn't confirmed in the available sources — check with dive centres
maldives-baa-hanifaru-bay.airport: DRV — Dharavandhoo (domestic flight from Malé ~35 min) or seaplane from MLE — Malé, ~35–45 min
highlights: Reef manta aggregations in Hanifaru Bay — up to a hundred individuals when the tide pushes plankton into the bay
Whale sharks at Hanifaru (mostly young males)
Turtles, bottlenose dolphins, reef sharks on the thilas

maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.description: Fuvahmulah is a single-island atoll with no lagoon, right out in the open ocean, known for the world's largest aggregation of tiger sharks — they're seen at the harbour mouth on the island's southeastern tip. Divers also go down at dawn for thresher sharks, and hammerheads, oceanic mantas and whale sharks turn up in the blue. A place for experienced divers: negative entries, currents, swell and depth.
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.rating_basis: In recent years it has become one of the most talked-about shark-diving destinations: according to research cited by Wikipedia, Fuvahmulah has the largest known aggregation of tiger sharks in the world, and the island's waters suit pregnant females. Fact-check (November 2026): the year-round presence of tiger sharks, threshers, hammerheads, mantas and whale sharks weren't confirmed by sources; no recompression chamber was found. Seasons are low-confidence: the southwest monsoon in the Maldives runs from early June to late November (rain, strong wind, storms), with the changeover in April–May; on Fuvahmulah the rainiest months are November, October and May, the driest February. Peak is December–March, the rest are shoulder months. Coordinates are an estimate: at the harbour mouth on the island's southeastern tip (the harbour is there per Wikipedia; island coordinates 0°17′36″ S, 73°25′25″ E).
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.hazards: Strong currents and ocean swell, negative entries, 30+ m depth for the threshers, big tiger sharks — follow the briefing strictly and stay close to the bottom
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.crowd_note: Several dive centres work Tiger Harbour at the same time in the morning; the outer sites are quieter
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.region: Fuvahmulah single-island atoll (Gnaviyani), south of the equator
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.marine_life: Tiger sharks at the harbour mouth are seen on almost every dive; there are also thresher and grey reef sharks, silvertips, oceanic whitetips, hammerheads, oceanic mantas, whale sharks, tuna and sailfish. The coral is modest — people come for the big animals.
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.signature_sites: Tiger Harbour (tiger sharks, 10–15 m), Farikede (thresher sharks at dawn), the island's outer walls with drifts in the blue
pros: Tiger sharks on almost every dive
Thresher sharks and other pelagic species
Inexpensive guesthouses on an inhabited island
Few non-diving tourists
cons: AOW and experience needed: currents, negative entries, ocean swell
Almost no coral or lagoon — little for a beach holiday
No resorts, only guesthouses (local rules — no alcohol)
Weather rules: trips are cancelled in the monsoon
maldives-fuvahmulah-tiger-harbour.airport: FVM — Fuvahmulah (domestic flight from Malé, ~1 h)
highlights: Tiger sharks — the largest known aggregation in the world (by the harbour)
Thresher sharks at dawn, at about 30 m
Hammerheads, oceanic mantas, whale sharks, silvertips (seasonal and with luck)

maldives-south-ari-maamigili.description: South Ari is the Maldives' top whale shark area: young males patrol the outer reef between Maamigili and Dhigurah all year. You dive from resorts, local islands (Dhigurah, Maamigili, Dhangethi) and liveaboards; there are calm reefs for training and channels with strong currents for experienced divers.
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.rating_basis: One of the few places in the world where whale sharks are seen year-round (Wikipedia: permanent residents of Alif Dhaal Atoll, including off Dhigurah). The downside in reviews — crowds of boats around the whale sharks. Fact-check (November 2026): the manta months at Rangali Madivaru and a recompression chamber weren't confirmed by sources — zeroed. Seasons: the southwest monsoon runs from early June to late November (rain, strong wind, storms), with the changeover in April–May; peak is the dry northeast monsoon (December–March), with whale sharks year-round, the rest are shoulder months. Coordinates are an estimate: the outer reef ~2 km south-southeast of Maamigili (island coordinates 3.475° N, 72.8375° E — from a link in the Wikipedia article; the airport is on the island's southern edge).
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.hazards: Strong currents in the channels and on the thilas, negative entries and drifts in the blue, boat traffic around the whale sharks
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.crowd_note: In the morning lots of boats full of snorkellers from hotels and local islands gather at the whale shark reef
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.region: South Ari Atoll (Alifu Dhaalu), SAMPA marine protected area
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.marine_life: Young whale sharks patrol the outer reef in the south of the atoll year-round; mantas at cleaning stations, grey reef and whitetip sharks, turtles, eagle rays, big schools of fish on the thilas (underwater pinnacles) and in the channels.
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.signature_sites: The Maamigili–Dhigurah whale shark reef (SAMPA), Rangali Madivaru (mantas), Kudarah Thila, Broken Rock, the Dhigurah arches
pros: Whale sharks year-round
Reefs for every level
Lots of options: resorts, guesthouses, liveaboards
cons: Very crowded around the whale sharks
June–November is the southwest monsoon: rain, strong wind and storms
Strong currents in the channels
Resorts are expensive
maldives-south-ari-maamigili.airport: MLE — Malé (Velana), ~25 min by seaplane or ~2 h by speedboat; VAM — Maamigili, domestic flight
highlights: Whale sharks — permanent residents of Alif Dhaal Atoll, year-round (Maamigili–Dhigurah outer reef)
Mantas at the Rangali Madivaru cleaning station
Grey reef sharks and turtles in the channels

cozumel-palancar.description: Mexico's best-known dive destination: the mainland-facing walls and coral massifs of the island's southwest, swept by a current, so almost every dive is a drift. The shallow reefs (Paradise, Chankanaab) suit Open Water courses, while the Santa Rosa and Punta Sur walls are for experienced divers. Easy to combine with the cenotes on the mainland (ferry from Playa del Carmen ~45 min).
cozumel-palancar.rating_basis: A Caribbean classic: consistently in the Scuba Diving Readers' Choice top lists and PADI/SSI guides; reviews praise the wall drifts, 30+ m visibility and abundant sponges
cozumel-palancar.hazards: Strong and changeable currents on the walls (drift, separation from the group), depth on the walls >40 m, boat traffic; guided dives only — national park rules
cozumel-palancar.crowd_note: Lots of boats and cruise tourists at Palancar and Colombia in peak months; the more distant sites (Punta Sur, Maracaibo) are quieter
cozumel-palancar.region: Quintana Roo, Cozumel island, Caribbean Sea (Mesoamerican Barrier Reef)
cozumel-palancar.marine_life: Huge sponges and coral “fingers” with grottoes, turtles, moray eels, nurse sharks, barracuda, lobsters; the endemic splendid toadfish (Sanopus splendidus); in winter — eagle rays on the walls.
cozumel-palancar.signature_sites: Palancar (Gardens, Horseshoe, Caves), Santa Rosa Wall, Colombia, Punta Sur (Devil's Throat — for the experienced), Chankanaab and Paradise (shallow, for beginners)
cozumel-palancar.chamber: Recompression chamber on the island: the Costamed hospital hyperbaric centre in San Miguel
pros: 25–40 m visibility and warm water year-round
Easy drifts — you see a lot of reef effortlessly
A huge choice of centres, hotels and direct flights
Suits both beginners and experienced divers

Crowds and cruise ships at peak times

cozumel-palancar.dive_price_note: From a “2 boat dives” package at $115 + national park fee ~225 pesos/day; gear extra
cozumel-palancar.course_price_note: PADI Open Water with eLearning, ~$495 (Cozumel Dive Academy)
highlights: Spotted eagle rays on the walls in the south of the island
Turtles, nurse sharks, the endemic splendid toadfish

Hotel dive centre in the south of the island, closest to Palancar

la-paz-los-islotes.description: From La Paz, boats head to the rocky islands of Espíritu Santo and La Partida: the star attraction is the Los Islotes sea lion colony, where curious pups play with divers at 5–15 m. There are easy sites and wrecks for beginners and the El Bajo seamount with currents for experienced divers. The water is warm in summer and autumn; in winter it's 20 °C and windy.
la-paz-los-islotes.rating_basis: Jacques-Yves Cousteau called the Sea of Cortez “the aquarium of the world”; diving with the playful sea lions of Los Islotes is one of the most loved experiences in reviews; there are noticeably fewer big sharks at El Bajo these days
la-paz-los-islotes.hazards: Currents at El Bajo and around the outer islands; bull sea lions can be aggressive — don't approach the haul-out; sun and dehydration in summer
la-paz-los-islotes.crowd_note: Several boats with snorkellers and divers sometimes visit the sea lion colony at once; the outer sites are uncrowded
la-paz-los-islotes.region: Baja California Sur, Espíritu Santo archipelago, Gulf of California (Sea of Cortez)
la-paz-los-islotes.marine_life: A sea lion colony, huge schools of jacks and snapper, moray eels, rays, turtles, occasionally mantas and hammerheads at El Bajo; whale sharks in the bay in winter.
la-paz-los-islotes.signature_sites: Los Islotes (sea lions), El Bajo seamount, the Salvatierra ferry wreck, La Reina (Cerralvo), San Francisco island/La Partida
pros: Playing with sea lions — a unique experience
Huge schools of fish and a chance of big animals
Whale sharks and whales in winter
Suits beginners: shallow, sheltered coves

Cold in winter (20 °C) with a strong northerly wind, “El Norte”
Visibility more modest than in the Caribbean

Whale sharks in La Paz bay
Mobulas (schools of rays)

riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.description: The flooded freshwater caves of the Yucatán Peninsula: cenote dives are shore dives with no current and visibility of tens of metres. Guided cavern tours of Dos Ojos (5–10 m) are open to Open Water divers with good buoyancy, while The Pit and Angelita need Advanced (depths to 30–40 m). They run year-round and save the holiday when the nortes close the sea.
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.rating_basis: Freshwater cave diving unlike anywhere else in the world; Dos Ojos and The Pit appear on almost every list of the world's best dives, and reviews are rapturous
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.hazards: An overhead environment (no direct ascent) — only with a certified guide and along a guideline; entering a true cave without cave certification is deadly dangerous; depth and the hydrogen sulphide cloud at The Pit/Angelita
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.crowd_note: Dos Ojos fills with snorkellers and dive groups during the day; go to The Pit and the more distant cenotes early in the morning
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.region: Quintana Roo, Yucatán Peninsula, between Playa del Carmen and Tulum (freshwater karst caves)
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.marine_life: Little life (small fish near the entrances, blind cave shrimps) — people come for the cave chambers, stalactites, light beams, the halocline and the hydrogen sulphide cloud at The Pit.
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.signature_sites: Dos Ojos (Barbie Line and Bat Cave routes, 5–10 m), The Pit (to 30–40 m, halocline), Angelita (hydrogen sulphide “river”), Gran Cenote, Chac Mool, Taj Mahal
riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.chamber: The nearest recompression chambers are in Playa del Carmen and on Cozumel (Costamed hyperbaric centre)

No currents or waves — you can dive in any weather
Unique cave scenery and light beams
Easy to combine with Cozumel and the Playa del Carmen reefs

Solid buoyancy needed, not suitable for first dives

riviera-maya-cenotes-dos-ojos.airport: TQO — Tulum, ~1 h; CUN — Cancún, ~1.5–2 h
