Stalactites and stalagmites in the cave chambers of Dos Ojos
school_notes: Cenote dives in Russian, groups of up to 4, ~$260 per day (8 h)
Large cave and technical diving centre; from 2026 operates only in Tulum

socorro-revillagigedo.description: Remote volcanic islands in the open Pacific, reachable only by liveaboard (a day's sailing from Cabo San Lucas). People come for the giant mantas that approach divers of their own accord, dolphins, whales and sharks. This is a destination for experienced divers: ocean swell, currents, depth and blue-water dives.
socorro-revillagigedo.rating_basis: One of the best pelagic routes in the world: the “Mexican Galápagos”, always in the global top 10 liveaboard lists; reviews talk of mantas circling divers for hours
socorro-revillagigedo.hazards: Strong currents and swell, depth, separation from the boat in the open ocean (you need an SMB and a beacon/radio), remoteness from medical help and a recompression chamber
socorro-revillagigedo.crowd_note: The number of boats and divers is capped by national park permits; usually one or two boats on site
socorro-revillagigedo.region: Revillagigedo Islands, Pacific Ocean, ~450 km south of Cabo San Lucas (liveaboard only)
socorro-revillagigedo.marine_life: Giant mantas, friendly bottlenose dolphins, humpback whales, hammerhead, Galápagos, silky, whitetip reef and silvertip sharks, tuna, wahoo; occasionally whale sharks and orcas.
socorro-revillagigedo.signature_sites: The Boiler (mantas), the Canyon (hammerheads), Roca Partida (a rock in the open ocean — schooling sharks), Cabo Pearce and Punta Tosca (Socorro), Red Rocks
socorro-revillagigedo.chamber: No recompression chamber on the islands — the nearest help is in Cabo San Lucas (24–30 h away); insurance with evacuation cover is mandatory
pros: Giant mantas, dolphins and humpback whales on one trip
Few divers — national park quotas
North America's largest marine reserve, with fishing banned
cons: Liveaboard only: expensive (from ~$3200 + national park fee ~$200 per dive day)
24–30 h crossing on the open ocean — seasickness
Not for beginners; the water is cooler than people expect (21–24 °C in winter)
socorro-revillagigedo.airport: SJD — Los Cabos, ~40 min to the port of Cabo San Lucas, then 24–30 h by liveaboard
highlights: Giant oceanic mantas that swim up to divers (peak January–April)
Humpback whales (you can hear them singing underwater)
Whale sharks
Bait balls with sharks, tuna and wahoo
Bottlenose dolphins seeking contact with divers
Hammerhead, silky, Galápagos and silvertip sharks
school_notes: 8–10-night liveaboards from Cabo San Lucas, season November–July, US$3195–5845 + national park fee

perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.description: The Perhentians are two small islands with white beaches off the northeast coast of Peninsular Malaysia — a popular, inexpensive place for an Open Water course. Easy reefs with turtles and reef sharks, a few wrecks, and the Tokong Laut pinnacle for experienced divers. The season runs from mid-March to late October; in winter the islands all but close because of the monsoon.
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.rating_basis: One of Malaysia's most popular budget dive resorts for training: easy reefs, turtles, sharks and wrecks, inexpensive courses. The sites are good for the region, but a long way off Sipadan's level.
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.hazards: Boat traffic off the beaches, currents on the outer pinnacles, depth on the Secret Wreck (38 m), jellyfish
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.crowd_note: July and August are the busiest months, with several boats at the popular sites; quieter in September–October
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.region: Terengganu, northeast Peninsular Malaysia, South China Sea
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.marine_life: Granite pinnacles covered in soft corals and sea fans, turtles, blacktip reef and bamboo sharks, rays, schools of barracuda and jacks; on the Sugar Wreck — lionfish, scorpionfish and groupers. Whale sharks are occasionally seen at Tokong Laut.
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.signature_sites: Tokong Laut — Temple of the Sea (pinnacle), Sugar Wreck (an easy wreck), Terumbu Tiga (Three Brothers), Tanjung Butung, Secret Reef, Police Wreck
pros: Inexpensive courses, lots of schools
Turtles and reef sharks in the shallows
Wrecks for different levels
Beautiful beaches and excellent snorkelling
cons: November to February is monsoon season — hotels and ferries shut down
Average visibility
No doctor or recompression chamber on the islands
Crowds in July–August
perhentian-temple-of-the-sea.airport: KBR — Kota Bharu, ~1 h to Kuala Besut jetty, then 30–40 min by speedboat
highlights: Turtles and blacktip reef sharks
Wrecks: Sugar Wreck, Police Wreck (18 m), Secret Wreck (38 m)
Whale sharks at Tokong Laut (occasionally)
school_notes: Long Beach, Perhentian Kecil; season from mid-March to late October
Teluk Dalam, Perhentian Besar; trips to Tokong Laut, the Sugar Wreck and also Redang

sipadan-barracuda-point.description: Sipadan is an oceanic seamount island off Borneo and one of the most famous sites in the world: the wall drops 600 m, schools of barracuda and jacks circle around, and turtles are seen by the dozen. Access to the island itself is by limited permits only; divers stay on Mabul, Kapalai or in Semporna. Suits experienced divers; beginners can train on Mabul and visit Sipadan after the course.
sipadan-barracuda-point.rating_basis: A classic of global top lists (Jacques Cousteau called Sipadan “an untouched piece of art”; consistently in the world top 10 of magazines and liveaboard.com): the wall, barracuda and turtles are guaranteed. The downside — a strict permit quota.
sipadan-barracuda-point.hazards: Strong and changeable currents (including downcurrents) at Barracuda Point and South Point, great depth along the wall, Turtle Tomb — only with a cave guide
sipadan-barracuda-point.crowd_note: Diver numbers are capped (about 176 permits a day), so there are no crowds, but permits sell out in advance and are usually only issued with a package of 3 days/2 nights or more
sipadan-barracuda-point.marine_life: A sheer 600 m wall with huge schools of barracuda and jacks, dozens of turtles, reef sharks and bumpheads; occasionally hammerheads, eagle rays, mantas and whale sharks. On neighbouring Mabul and Kapalai — macro on the sand (muck diving).
sipadan-barracuda-point.signature_sites: Barracuda Point, South Point (strong currents), the Drop-Off by the jetty, Turtle Tomb (only with a cave guide), Hanging Gardens, White-Tip Avenue; macro sites on Mabul
pros: One of the world's best walls, with guaranteed barracuda and turtles
Permit quota — no crowds on the sites
An almost year-round season
Macro diving on Mabul and Kapalai nearby
cons: Permits are limited and have to be booked in advance with a package
Expensive compared with Thailand
No overnight stays on Sipadan; the islands are guarded by ESSCOM security forces
Currents at Barracuda Point and South Point — experience needed
sipadan-barracuda-point.airport: TWU — Tawau, ~1–1.5 h to Semporna, then 40–60 min by boat
highlights: Barracuda “tornadoes” and schools of jacks at Barracuda Point
Green and hawksbill turtles — on almost every dive
Bumphead parrotfish (early in the morning), whitetip and grey reef sharks
Hammerheads, mantas, whale sharks (occasionally)
school_notes: Large operator in Semporna and on Mabul; Sipadan permits guaranteed with a package of 3 days/2 nights or more

tioman-renggis.description: Tioman is a large green island off the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia with easy reef diving from March to October. Shallow reefs with turtles and reef sharks such as Renggis suit Open Water courses, while the outer islets of Chebeh, Labas and Tiger Reef are for certified divers. From November to February the northeast monsoon blows: many hotels and dive centres close, and ferries run irregularly.
tioman-renggis.rating_basis: An island popular with Singaporeans and Malaysians for training and easy reef dives; corals and visibility are average, and it's not on global top lists.
tioman-renggis.hazards: Boat traffic off Tekek, sea urchins, jellyfish at certain times, currents around the outer islets
tioman-renggis.crowd_note: Renggis has lots of snorkellers from the Tekek and Berjaya hotels during the day, the outer islets are uncrowded; weekend influx from Singapore
tioman-renggis.region: Pahang, east coast of Peninsular Malaysia, South China Sea
tioman-renggis.marine_life: Shallow coral reefs and boulders with turtles, blacktip reef sharks, rays, moray eels and schools of reef fish; the outer islets (Chebeh, Labas, Tiger Reef) have more fish and soft corals.
tioman-renggis.signature_sites: Renggis (off Tekek — for beginners and snorkelling), Tiger Reef, Chebeh island, Labas island, Magicienne Rock, wrecks around the island
pros: Easy reefs for training and snorkelling
Turtles and reef sharks right off the shore
A quiet jungle island
Relatively inexpensive
cons: November to February is monsoon season — the season is closed
Average visibility and coral
A long journey: ferry from Mersing, no scheduled flights to the island (as of 2024)
tioman-renggis.airport: SIN — Singapore (~3 h to Mersing) or KUL — Kuala Lumpur (~5 h), then a ferry ~1.5–2 h
highlights: Turtles and blacktip reef sharks at Renggis island
Wrecks (more than 20 sites, including wreckage near the island)
school_notes: At Papaya Resort, Tekek village; 22+ sites, including wrecks

tofo-manta-reef.description: Tofo is Mozambique's top megafauna spot: mantas at cleaning stations and whale sharks are seen year-round, and humpback whales pass by in winter. The best sites are offshore reefs at 18–30 m with a gentle drift, reached by RIB launched through the surf. Best suited to AOW divers and above; beginners train on the shallow inshore reefs.
tofo-manta-reef.rating_basis: Features in global megafauna top lists: mantas and whale sharks year-round, and the Marine Megafauna Foundation is based here. Downsides in reviews — variable visibility, surf launches and remoteness.
tofo-manta-reef.hazards: Launching and landing the boat through the surf, swell and surge, variable currents on the offshore reefs, 25–30 m depth; a long way to a recompression chamber; cyclones in January–March
tofo-manta-reef.crowd_note: Few boats — usually one or two groups at Manta Reef; busier during the South African December–January and Easter holidays
tofo-manta-reef.marine_life: Reef and giant mantas at cleaning stations, whale sharks in the blue on the way to the reefs, humpback whales in winter; turtles, big groupers, moray eels, stingrays, dolphins. Macro on the inshore reefs, seahorses in the Barra lagoon.
tofo-manta-reef.signature_sites: Manta Reef (three cleaning stations), Giant's Castle, the Office (pinnacle), Amazon, the shallow inshore reefs Salon and Crock Rock
tofo-manta-reef.chamber: No recompression chamber nearby; in case of DCS — evacuation, usually to South Africa. You need insurance with evacuation cover (DAN or similar)
pros: Mantas and whale sharks year-round
Humpback whales from June to October
Few boats and divers on the sites
A surfer village, inexpensive compared with island resorts
cons: Visibility varies a lot from day to day
RIB launches through the surf, a bumpy ride
No recompression chamber nearby
January–March is cyclone and rainy season
tofo-manta-reef.airport: INH — Inhambane, ~30 min; MPM — Maputo, ~7 h by car
tofo-manta-reef.dive_price_note: Boat dive with gear, usually €45–65; the more distant megafauna sites €60–90
tofo-manta-reef.course_price_note: PADI Open Water, 3–4 days; €370–530 depending on the centre (~$490 at Tofo Scuba)

Reef and giant mantas at cleaning stations
Humpback whales

PADI; Marine Megafauna Foundation researchers join the trips
Small family-run dive resort in Tofo

poor-knights-northern-arch.description: The Poor Knights Islands off the coast of the North Island are one of the world's best-known marine reserves: arches, caves, kelp forests and surprisingly subtropical marine life. The trip from Tutukaka is about an hour by boat, usually two dives at 12–25 m chosen by the skipper. You need Open Water certification; summer is warmer and sometimes brings mantas, winter is colder but has better visibility.
poor-knights-northern-arch.rating_basis: Wikipedia calls the Poor Knights Marine Reserve (1981, a full fishing ban since 1998) one of the ten most popular dive sites in the world; arches, Rikoriko Cave and subtropical marine life. Seasons: trips run year-round; peak is summer (December–March, water 20–23 °C, mantas); winter has the best visibility but ~15 °C water — a shoulder season. Coordinates are an estimate: the northern tip of Tawhiti Rahi island (the sources give only general coordinates for the group, 35°30′ S, 174°45′ E), accurate to ~1 km.
poor-knights-northern-arch.hazards: Cold water, open-ocean swell, weather can cancel trips.
poor-knights-northern-arch.region: North Island, Poor Knights Islands Marine Reserve; trips from Tutukaka (~1 h by boat)
poor-knights-northern-arch.marine_life: Kelp forests with subtropical marine life, snapper and masses of fish in the no-take reserve; in summer — mantas and whale sharks, in winter — whales and fur seals.
poor-knights-northern-arch.signature_sites: Northern Arch, Middle Arch, Maomao Arch — all on Tawhiti Rahi island; Rikoriko Cave (the largest sea cave by volume in the Southern Hemisphere)
pros: One of the world's most famous marine reserves
Arches, caves and kelp forests
Mantas and whale sharks in summer, whales and fur seals in winter
Year-round trips
cons: Cold water: 20–23 °C in summer, ~15 °C in winter — you need a thick wetsuit
Expensive (NZ$399 per day)

poor-knights-northern-arch.airport: Whangārei airport (nearest); boats to the islands leave from Tutukaka (~1 h)
poor-knights-northern-arch.dive_price_note: Dive! Tutukaka: a day at the Poor Knights, 2 guided dives with full gear rental — NZ$399, i.e. ~NZ$200 ≈ €100 per dive
poor-knights-northern-arch.course_price_note: PADI Open Water at Dive! Tutukaka — from NZ$699 + eLearning, 3 days

Whales, albatrosses and New Zealand fur seals (in winter)
Subtropical marine life in the kelp forests, arches and Rikoriko sea cave
Snapper — their numbers have soared since the full fishing ban (1998)
school_notes: Running since 1998, daily trips to the Poor Knights year-round, PADI courses, nitrox on request

muscat-daymaniyat-islands.description: A reserve of nine small islands in the Gulf of Oman, 18 km off the coast at Barka and ~45 minutes by boat from Muscat's marinas. Calm coral gardens with turtles and leopard sharks suit even first dives, and whale sharks visit the islands in season. Winter brings comfortable water and mild weather; summer brings heat and plankton.
muscat-daymaniyat-islands.rating_basis: The Daymaniyat Islands are Oman's main dive destination: a protected reserve with coral gardens, turtles and leopard sharks; visibility isn't world-class, but the reefs are uncrowded.
muscat-daymaniyat-islands.hazards: Currents at the drift sites (Police Run), summer thermoclines and heat, boat traffic; touching turtles and landing on the islands without a permit are banned.
muscat-daymaniyat-islands.crowd_note: Visitor numbers are capped by ministry permits (groups of up to 12), and on weekdays there are usually 1–3 boats on the sites; busier at weekends (Friday–Saturday).
muscat-daymaniyat-islands.region: Gulf of Oman, Daymaniyat Islands reserve (18 km off Barka, Seeb wilayat)
muscat-daymaniyat-islands.marine_life: Coral gardens (including rare coral species), turtles, leopard sharks, rays, moray eels, schools of fish; seasonally — whale sharks. Green and hawksbill turtles and seabirds nest on the islands.
muscat-daymaniyat-islands.signature_sites: Aquarium, Police Run (drift), Three Sisters and other reefs around the nine islands
pros: Uncrowded reefs in a protected reserve
Turtles and leopard sharks — frequent encounters
Suits beginners
Easy to combine with Oman's cities and desert

Whale sharks — seasonal visitors to the islands

fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.description: The Tumakohua south pass by the hamlet of Tetamanu is the legendary “wall of sharks”: hundreds of grey reef sharks hang in the current in a narrow, shallow pass. The currents here are gentler than in the Garuae north pass, and according to TOPDIVE the pass suits divers of all levels. The best time is June and July, when thousands of groupers spawn at the full moon and the sharks hunt them.
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.rating_basis: Fakarava's south pass is known for the world's highest density of grey reef sharks (700+, research by the Gombessa expedition) and for the grouper spawning in June–July; the atoll is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve (2016), and diving is the backbone of the local economy. Coordinates are a rough estimate (the sources give none for the pass): a point at the southern tip of the atoll, possibly off by several km. Seasons: peak is set by the grouper spawning (the June and July full moons), the other months are shoulder months on a conservative reading; the Tuamotus have no pronounced seasons.
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.hazards: Tidal currents in the passes (strong in the Garuae north pass), large numbers of sharks (no danger if you behave correctly), remoteness from medical help.
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.region: Tuamotu Archipelago, south of Fakarava atoll (Tetamanu); UNESCO Biosphere Reserve
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.marine_life: Hundreds of grey reef sharks (fully protected since 2008), blacktip and whitetip sharks, Napoleon wrasse, spotted eagle rays, groupers; in June–July — mass spawning of camouflage groupers. In the Garuae north pass — mantas, barracuda, turtles and dolphins.
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.signature_sites: Tumakohua south pass (Tetamanu), Maiuru; in the north — Garuae pass (the widest in Polynesia, ~1.4–1.6 km), Ohotu reef, Pufana reef in the lagoon

Grouper spawning at the June and July full moons

Gentler current than in the north pass

Expensive
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.airport: Fakarava airfield in the north of the atoll (1.4 km runway), flights via Rangiroa or Manihi several days a week
fakarava-south-pass-tumakohua.dive_price_note: TOPDIVE 6 inter-island package — 6 dives for XPF 58,800 (2026 rates), ~€82 per dive (€1 ≈ XPF 119.33); a trip to the south pass from the north is a separate day trip
highlights: Camouflage grouper (Epinephelus polyphekadion) spawning at the mouth of the Tumakohua pass — over two full moons
The “wall of sharks”: more than 700 grey reef sharks — the highest density in the world
Napoleon wrasse, eagle rays, blacktip sharks, camouflage groupers

rangiroa-tiputa-pass.description: Rangiroa is one of the largest atolls in the world, and Tiputa Pass is a cult spot for drift dives on the incoming tide: schools of grey sharks, dolphins, mantas and, from December to March, hammerheads. There are sites for every level (Tiputa reef, the lagoon by motu Nuhi Nuhi), but the best drifts in the pass call for experience in currents and good buoyancy. There isn't much coral or macro — people come for the big animals.
rangiroa-tiputa-pass.rating_basis: Wikipedia calls Rangiroa one of the world's top dive destinations and Tiputa Pass a world-famous site for drifting with sharks and mantas; Wikivoyage: “for big thrills, Rangiroa is the place”, but coral and macro lovers may be disappointed. Coordinates are an estimate: the point is placed at the mouth of the pass by Tiputa village (using the village's coordinates from Wikipedia), accurate to ~0.5–1 km. Seasons: the Tuamotus have no pronounced seasons (water 27–29 °C year-round); peak is set by the hammerhead and tiger shark season (December–March), the other months are shoulder months on a conservative reading.
rangiroa-tiputa-pass.hazards: Strong tidal currents in the passes (in on the incoming tide, out on the outgoing), downcurrents and depth on the outer walls; sharks (safe if you behave correctly).
rangiroa-tiputa-pass.region: Tuamotu Archipelago, northeast of Rangiroa atoll, between motu Avatoru and Tiputa village
rangiroa-tiputa-pass.marine_life: Grey reef, whitetip, blacktip and silvertip sharks, bottlenose dolphins, mantas, eagle rays, barracuda, tuna, Napoleon wrasse and turtles; from December to March great hammerheads and tiger sharks appear in the pass.
rangiroa-tiputa-pass.signature_sites: Tiputa Pass (Tiputa Reef, The Canyons, The Angle, The Blue), Avatoru Pass (Little Pass, Mahuta), The Wall (The Fault, 11–50 m), the Blue Lagoon (snorkelling with blacktip sharks)

Hammerheads and tiger sharks from December to March

rangiroa-tiputa-pass.airport: Rangiroa airport on motu Avatoru — flights from Tahiti and other Polynesian atolls

Aggregations of stingrays in Tiputa Pass and the hammerheads that hunt them
A school of grey reef sharks — up to ~200 at the mouth of the pass at ~50 m on the incoming current
Resident bottlenose dolphins playing in the pass
Mantas, eagle rays, Napoleon wrasse, green turtles
school_notes: Centres on Reporepo beach and at the Kia Ora hotel; dives at 08:00, 10:00, 14:00 and at sunset; free nitrox

anilao-twin-rocks.description: The coast of the Calumpan Peninsula in Batangas province is the closest dive area to Manila: dozens of small dive resorts along the shore, short bangka rides and one of the richest places in the world for macro and nudibranchs. There are reefs with current (Twin Rocks, Mainit Point) and calm sandy slopes for training; at night there's blackwater diving for photographers.
anilao-twin-rocks.rating_basis: The Philippines' top place for macro and nudibranchs, popular with underwater photographers (liveaboard.com, guides); the reef scenery and big animals are more modest than in the Visayas and Palawan.
anilao-twin-rocks.hazards: Strong currents at Mainit Point and Twin Rocks (drift), boat traffic, venomous macro critters (blue-ringed octopus, scorpionfish), typhoons in summer–autumn.
anilao-twin-rocks.crowd_note: Lots of divers from Manila (2.5–3 h drive) at weekends; noticeably quieter on weekdays
anilao-twin-rocks.region: Batangas (Luzon), Calumpan Peninsula, Balayan Bay and Maricaban Strait
anilao-twin-rocks.marine_life: The Philippines' acknowledged nudibranch capital: hundreds of nudibranch species, frogfish, blue-ringed octopus, ghost pipefish and shrimps on the sand; at Twin Rocks — schools of jacks and barracuda, a sunken barge covered in soft corals; at Mainit Point — reef sharks in the grottoes and a strong drift.
anilao-twin-rocks.signature_sites: Twin Rocks (with the sunken barge), Cathedral Rock, Mainit Point, Secret Bay (muck), Sombrero and Maricaban islands, Betchy (blackwater)

2.5–3 h from Manila — good for short trips

coron-wwii-wrecks.description: A bay off Busuanga island where American aircraft sank a Japanese convoy on 24 September 1944: more than a dozen ships lie at 10–40 m, with an average dive depth of ~25 m. Some of the ships (Nanshin Maru, Olympia Maru) are accessible even to Open Water divers, while penetration and the deep Irako and Akitsushima require AOW, nitrox and a Wreck course. Between dives — Coron's lagoons and Barracuda Lake.
coron-wwii-wrecks.rating_basis: Features in global wreck-diving top lists (liveaboard.com calls the Irako the best wreck in the Philippines); reviews are mixed about the visibility.
coron-wwii-wrecks.hazards: Penetrating the hulls — only with a Wreck course and a guide (silt-outs, sharp edges, entanglement); depth to 40 m on the Irako and Akitsushima; a thermocline up to 38 °C in Barracuda Lake; typhoons in the rainy season.
coron-wwii-wrecks.crowd_note: On the popular wrecks and at Barracuda Lake you'll meet several groups during the day; the more distant wrecks (Irako, Akitsushima) are quieter
coron-wwii-wrecks.region: Northern Palawan, Busuanga island, Coron and Gutob bays (Calamian Islands)
coron-wwii-wrecks.marine_life: The hulls are overgrown with corals and sponges, surrounded by schools of fusiliers, barracuda, lionfish, scorpionfish, turtles; the real attraction is the ships themselves and their interiors. Barracuda Lake has hardly any fish but spectacular underwater scenery.
coron-wwii-wrecks.signature_sites: Akitsushima, Irako (a refrigerated supply ship, the best wreck in the Philippines), Olympia Maru, Taiei Maru, Nanshin Maru, Okikawa Maru, Barracuda Lake

malapascua-monad-shoal.description: A small island off the northern tip of Cebu that people visit for thresher sharks: at dawn they rise from the deep to the cleaning stations on Monad Shoal (around 25–30 m). It's a dive for divers with AOW and nitrox; during the day there's Gato Island with its cave and reef sharks, muck diving, wrecks and mandarinfish at sunset, and in December–May a chance of hammerheads at Kimud.
malapascua-monad-shoal.rating_basis: The only place in the world where thresher sharks are seen almost guaranteed at recreational depth every day; features in top lists for shark encounters. liveaboard.com reviews: the daytime reefs and macro are more modest, and Monad can get lots of boats.
malapascua-monad-shoal.hazards: Depth and no-deco limits at Monad (nitrox recommended), distance rules at the cleaning stations (no strobes), currents on the outer shoals, typhoons in the rainy season (July–December).
malapascua-monad-shoal.crowd_note: The morning thresher trips — lots of boats from every centre on the island at once; groups must stay behind the rope at the cleaning station
malapascua-monad-shoal.marine_life: Pelagic thresher sharks rising at dawn to cleaning stations on the edge of a 200 m drop-off; in December–May schools of hammerheads at Kimud, mantas and mobulas; around Gato Island — whitetip reef sharks in the cave, banded sea snakes, pygmy seahorses; mandarinfish and muck at Bantigi.
malapascua-monad-shoal.signature_sites: Monad Shoal (Shark Point, Shark Wall), Kimud Shoal, Gato Island (cave, Whitetip Alley), Lighthouse (mandarinfish), the Dona Marilyn and Tapilon wrecks, Lapus Lapus
malapascua-monad-shoal.chamber: The nearest recompression chamber is the military hospital in Lahug (Cebu City), ~4–5 h including the boat to Maya
pros: Thresher sharks almost every morning, year-round
Hammerheads in winter–spring
Variety: the Gato caves, wrecks, muck, mandarinfish
An atmospheric car-free island
cons: Getting up around 4:30–5:00 for the sharks
25–30 m depth — you need AOW, ideally nitrox
Crowds of boats at Monad
A long journey from Cebu (bus + boat)
malapascua-monad-shoal.airport: CEB — Mactan-Cebu, 3.5–4 h by car/bus to Maya + 30 min by boat
highlights: Thresher sharks at cleaning stations at dawn (Monad, Kimud)
Schools of hammerheads on Kimud Shoal
Mantas and mobulas at Monad
Mandarinfish at sunset by the lighthouse
school_notes: Bounty Beach; trips to Kimud (threshers daily) and Monad

moalboal-sardine-run.description: A resort village on the west coast of Cebu, famous for the enormous sardine school that hangs right by the reef off Panagsama beach — you can see it even with a mask, and on scuba you can go in from shore. Twenty minutes away by boat is Pescador Island, with its walls and the “Cathedral” cave. Warm water, gentle currents and cheap dives make it suitable for all levels.
moalboal-sardine-run.rating_basis: The sardine ball is one of the Philippines' great wow moments and a social-media hit; liveaboard.com calls it the country's best sardine run. The downside — crowds of snorkellers at Panagsama.
moalboal-sardine-run.hazards: Boat traffic over the reef at Panagsama, currents at Pescador, deep walls; typhoon risk (usually October–December), sea urchins and lionfish.
moalboal-sardine-run.crowd_note: The sardines at Panagsama attract lots of snorkellers and divers during the day; early mornings and night dives are quieter
moalboal-sardine-run.marine_life: A giant school of sardines that stays by the Panagsama reef year-round (it used to be at Pescador), hunted by tuna and occasionally thresher sharks; turtles on the reef, Pescador's walls with soft corals, groupers, barracuda, rich macro and night dives.
moalboal-sardine-run.signature_sites: The sardine ball off Panagsama Beach, Pescador Island (walls and the “Cathedral” cave), Turtle Bay, White Beach, Talisay Wall
moalboal-sardine-run.chamber: The nearest recompression chamber is the military hospital in Lahug (Cebu City), ~3 h by car
pros: The sardine ball year-round, right off the shore
Suits snorkellers and beginners alike
Inexpensive accommodation and dives
Can be combined with the whale sharks at Oslob and Kawasan Falls
cons: Crowds of snorkellers at the sardines
Southwest monsoon and typhoon season — July–December
Far from the airport (~3 h)
highlights: Millions of sardines off Panagsama beach (a few metres from shore)
The walls and “Cathedral” of Pescador Island
Occasional thresher and whale sharks hunting the sardines
school_notes: Moalboal's oldest centre, multilingual team; liveaboards October–May

tubbataha-reefs.description: Two ring atolls and Jessie Beazley Reef in the middle of the Sulu Sea — the most remote and most pristine reef in the Philippines. It's reachable only by liveaboard from Puerto Princesa (a ~10–12 h crossing) in a short window from mid-March to mid-June; trips cost ~€280–500 per night. Most boats accept Open Water divers with experience, but the open ocean and currents are better suited to AOW divers.
tubbataha-reefs.rating_basis: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a consistent leader of dive rankings for the Philippines and Asia (liveaboard.com, Wikipedia): pristine walls, sharks, whale sharks; accessible only ~3 months a year.
tubbataha-reefs.hazards: Currents and surf on the exposed atolls (Washing Machine, Jessie Beazley), deep walls, remoteness from medical care and a recompression chamber — strict boat safety rules and a mandatory SMB.
tubbataha-reefs.crowd_note: Visits are strictly limited: liveaboards only, under park permits; usually one or two boats on site
tubbataha-reefs.region: Sulu Sea, ~150 km southeast of Puerto Princesa (Palawan); UNESCO site
tubbataha-reefs.marine_life: Sheer walls with pristine hard corals (~360 species), ~600 fish species and 11 shark species: grey reef, whitetip, blacktip, silky, occasionally hammerheads and tigers; whale sharks, mantas, huge schools of jacks and barracuda, turtles, pygmy seahorses.
tubbataha-reefs.signature_sites: Amos Rock, Washing Machine (North Atoll), Shark Airport, Delsan Wreck, Black Rock (South Atoll), Jessie Beazley Reef
tubbataha-reefs.chamber: No recompression chamber at the reef; the nearest land is 10–12 h away — you need insurance with evacuation cover
pros: Pristine walls and some of the best coral in Asia
Lots of sharks, whale sharks, mantas
Excellent visibility (up to 30–40 m)
Minimal crowds thanks to quotas
cons: Open only from mid-March to mid-June
Expensive liveaboards only; places sell out in advance
A long overnight crossing on the open sea
No medical help nearby
tubbataha-reefs.airport: PPS — Puerto Princesa (Palawan), then a ~10–12 h overnight crossing by liveaboard
highlights: Grey reef, whitetip and blacktip sharks; occasionally hammerheads and tigers
Whale sharks (Shark Airport, Jessie Beazley)
Mantas at the North and South Atolls
Nesting hawksbill and green turtles

santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.description: Santa Maria is the southernmost and sunniest of the Azores, and out in the open ocean nearby lie seamounts where schools of giant devil rays (mobulas) arrive in summer. At Ambrósio there can be more than a dozen per dive, in blue water with good visibility. Longer trips to the Formigas islets and Dollabarat reef (about 2 hours by boat) offer a chance of groupers, pelagics and, in a good year, a whale shark. Suits confident divers who are comfortable in open water and current.
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.rating_basis: Dive centres call Ambrósio one of the best places in the world for diving with mobulas; the Formigas have been a nature reserve since 1988 and are a Ramsar site. Downsides — a short season, changeable weather and long open-water crossings.
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.hazards: Currents on the exposed banks, blue-water dives with no visual reference, swell and seasickness on the long crossings, depth along the walls.
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.crowd_note: The island is small and there are few boats, but in summer places sell out fast — book early, even before your flights.
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.region: Azores, Santa Maria island, Atlantic Ocean
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.marine_life: Giant devil rays and mantas, tuna, amberjacks, barracuda, groupers, wrasse, parrotfish; at the Formigas — big groupers and pelagics, occasionally whale sharks.
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.signature_sites: Ambrósio bank, João Lopes bank, the Formigas and Dollabarat reef (~2 h by RIB), Gruta Azul, Ilhéu da Vila, Calçada do Gigante
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.chamber: No recompression chamber on Santa Maria; the nearest is in Ponta Delgada (São Miguel) — check the evacuation plan with your dive centre
pros: One of the best places in Europe to meet mobulas
Clear blue water and good visibility in summer
Untouched banks and the Formigas reserve
Few divers
cons: Short season: June to October
Open ocean: swell, seasickness, cancelled trips
Expensive and remote (flights via Lisbon or Ponta Delgada)
Animal encounters aren't guaranteed
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.airport: SMA — Santa Maria, ~10 min to Vila do Porto (flights from Lisbon and Ponta Delgada)
santa-maria-azores-ambrosio.dive_price_note: ≈€70 per dive: a 2-dive package is €140 with a 12 l tank and weights; trips to Ambrósio and the Formigas carry a supplement paid on site (Wahoo Diving)
highlights: Schools of giant devil rays (Mobula tarapacana) on Ambrósio bank — sometimes more than a dozen at once
Dollabarat reef and the Formigas islets: groupers, pelagic predators, mantas; occasionally whale sharks
Volcanic grottoes along the coast (Gruta Azul, Gruta dos Camarões)
school_notes: Vila do Porto (Colombo hotel); season June to October; trips to Ambrósio and the Formigas
Vila do Porto, German-run base; website in German, English and French

palau-blue-corner.description: Blue Corner is a triangular promontory of the barrier reef with sheer walls, where sharks gather in the current along the reef edge. It's one of the best-known dives in the world; the current can be strong, so the site is for experienced divers (usually AOW). Nearby are the Blue Holes and the German and Ulong channels, and in the lagoon there's Jellyfish Lake for snorkelling.
palau-blue-corner.rating_basis: Wikivoyage calls Blue Corner one of the best-known dive sites in the world — “sharks all the time and strong current”; diving and snorkelling are Palau's main tourist draw, and the Rock Islands lagoon is a UNESCO site. Coordinates are from Wikipedia (the Blue Corner article). Seasons are low-confidence: typhoons are rare, it rains year-round, more often from June to October; peak is set to January–April (the lowest rainfall in Koror's climate table), the rest are shoulder months.
palau-blue-corner.hazards: Strong and changeable currents at the corner of the reef, depth on the walls to 30 m and beyond.
palau-blue-corner.region: Palau's barrier reef south of Koror, Rock Islands area
palau-blue-corner.marine_life: Reef sharks at the corner of the reef in the current, a great variety of corals and reef life on the sheer walls; WWII wrecks in the lagoon.
palau-blue-corner.signature_sites: Blue Corner, Blue Holes, German Channel, Ulong Channel; Jellyfish Lake — snorkelling only
pros: One of the world's most famous sites, with guaranteed sharks
The entire country's waters are a shark sanctuary
Lots of top sites nearby: Blue Holes, German Channel, Ulong
Warm water ~29 °C year-round, typhoons are rare
cons: Strong currents — not for beginners
Expensive (~$150 for 2 dives)
Lots of rain, especially from June to October
palau-blue-corner.airport: ROR — Palau airport (Airai, Babeldaob island), near Koror
palau-blue-corner.dive_price_note: About US$150 for a 2-dive trip (Wikivoyage, year not stated), i.e. ~$75 ≈ €65 per dive
highlights: Sharks — “all the time” at Blue Corner (Palau became the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009)
Blue Holes — a large underwater cave in the northern part of the site
Jellyfish Lake — snorkelling only (scuba is banned)
school_notes: PADI 5 Star IDC, Ocean Hunter liveaboard; EAN32 nitrox for the price of air

baikal-listvyanka.description: Listvyanka, an hour's drive from Irkutsk, is the most accessible place to dive Lake Baikal. Drop-offs and canyons covered in sponges start 20–30 m from shore and plunge for tens of metres. In summer the surface water is +8…16 °C, while below 10–15 m it's +3…4 °C all year. The water is clearest in June, after the ice breaks up; by August visibility falls to 10–12 m. The main season is February to March: under-ice dives at Listvyanka and expeditions to the clear ice of the Small Sea by Olkhon. You need solid drysuit experience; AOW is recommended, and Ice Diver for under-ice dives.
baikal-listvyanka.rating_basis: Baikal features in every Russian roundup of the best dive destinations (RG, Vokrug Sveta, Trip.com, the PADI blog). Divers praise the clear water, especially under the ice (30–40 m), and the endemic fauna. Downsides — icy water year-round and sparse life compared with the seas.
baikal-listvyanka.hazards: Very cold water (+3…4 °C at depth), risk of regulator freezing. Steep drop-offs to 100 m and more start tens of metres from shore, so it's easy to go deeper than planned. Strong winds in April–May and November, summer storms with waves up to 4.5 m, cracks and open leads in the ice in winter.
baikal-listvyanka.crowd_note: Listvyanka is Baikal's most touristy village, but there aren't many dives; in February–March lots of groups work on the ice of the Small Sea
baikal-listvyanka.region: Irkutsk Oblast, southwest shore of Baikal, at the source of the Angara (in winter, expeditions also go to the Small Sea and Olkhon)
baikal-listvyanka.marine_life: Baikal's freshwater endemics: branching sponges on the rocks, colourful amphipods (gammarids), flatworms, Baikal sculpins; in the Small Sea, colonies of flatworms and white amphipods. The Baikal seal (nerpa) is rarely seen — spotting one underwater is a stroke of luck.
baikal-listvyanka.signature_sites: The drop-offs, canyons and grottoes of Listvyanka, Bolshiye Koty, the Circum-Baikal Railway; in the Small Sea — Sennaya Bay, “Planarians” and the under-ice cracks; the Ushkany Islands (liveaboard)
pros: Unique under-ice diving in clear water
Endemic fauna found nowhere else
Close to Irkutsk, diving almost year-round
Deep drop-offs right off the shore, tech diving available
cons: Icy water year-round, you need a drysuit
At Listvyanka visibility is usually 10–15 m; storms and murky water in August
Sparse underwater life compared with the seas
The Small Sea is 5–6 h by road from Irkutsk
baikal-listvyanka.airport: IKT — Irkutsk, ~1 h by car (70 km); ~5–6 h to the Small Sea
baikal-listvyanka.course_price_note: SDI Open Water at BaikalTek: theory, pool and 4 dives in Baikal with drysuit rental, 35,000 ₽ (groups of 2 or more)
highlights: Under-ice diving at Listvyanka (ice camp, daily dives)
The clear ice and ice cracks of the Small Sea (Olkhon expeditions)
Ice ridges and Baikal seals in Northern and Central Baikal (expeditions)
Endemics: branching sponges, amphipods, flatworms, sculpins
school_notes: Club in Irkutsk. Under-ice diving at Listvyanka from January to April (from 1 day), expeditions to Olkhon in February–March and to Northern Baikal from 25 March to 20 April. Liveaboard dive safaris in summer. A dive at Listvyanka from ~1,000 ₽ without guide, rental or transfer; a dive day on the boat — 15,000 ₽

black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.description: Bolshoy Utrish is a rocky stretch of coast between Anapa and Novorossiysk. Unlike Anapa's sandy beaches, here the rocky bottom falls away in drop-offs to 30–40 m. Anapa's dive centres bring divers here by boat, and there are plenty of WWII wrecks at 5–18 m in the area. The season runs from May to September, with summer water at +22…26 °C. It's a good place for first dives and courses; experienced divers will find the wrecks more interesting.
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.rating_basis: In Russian guides (RG, Trip.com, the PADI blog) the Black Sea is the country's warmest and most accessible sea, “the cradle of Soviet diving”. It's praised for its wrecks and easy training conditions, but the marine life is noticeably poorer than in the Mediterranean. Utrish is considered one of the best spots near Anapa thanks to its rocky drop-offs.
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.hazards: Boat traffic off the beaches, summer upwellings (sudden drops in water temperature), jellyfish. There's still ammunition in the hold of the Gorgippia — don't go inside.
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.crowd_note: In summer the shallow sites near Anapa are busy with try dives and courses; fewer groups go to Utrish and the more distant wrecks
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.region: Krasnodar Krai, the coast between Anapa and Novorossiysk, Black Sea
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.marine_life: Rocks and drop-offs covered in mussels, big rapa whelks, crabs, Black Sea fish. Compared with the Mediterranean the marine life is poor, but the wrecks barely get overgrown and are well preserved.
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.signature_sites: The Bolshoy Utrish drop-offs (20–40 m), the Gorgippia barge sitting upright (18 m), the Underwater Museum, the tanker Valerian Kuibyshev (8–13 m, off Blagoveshchenskaya), the tug Odessky Gorsovet (5–7 m, off Vityazevo), an Il-2 attack aircraft
pros: Warm water in summer — a 5–7 mm wetsuit is enough
Accessible and inexpensive, convenient for training
Wrecks at shallow depths
Can be combined with a beach holiday in Anapa
cons: Poor marine life compared with the tropics
Visibility usually 5–15 m; algal blooms and cold upwellings in summer
Short season: dive centres operate from May to September
The Anapa coast was hit by the December 2024 fuel oil spill in the Kerch Strait — check the current situation
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.airport: AAQ — Anapa (Vityazevo), ~40 min; the airport has been closed since 2022, check its status. Alternatively, take the train to Anapa or Novorossiysk
black-sea-bolshoy-utrish.dive_price_note: Guided boat dive at Bolshoy Utrish or the Gorgippia — 6,000 ₽ without rental (full kit +500 ₽); shore dive 3,500 ₽ (Morskaya Zvezda, prices for the 1 May – 30 September 2026 season)
highlights: The Bolshoy Utrish drop-offs: mussel-covered rocks, big rapa whelks and crabs
WWII wrecks off the Anapa coast
school_notes: PADI Dive Resort and NDL 5 Star in Anapa. Dives from Maly Utrish to Taman: Bolshoy Utrish, the Gorgippia, the Underwater Museum, wrecks. Try dive 5,000 ₽, PADI Open Water course with 4 sea dives

kamchatka-avacha-bay.description: Avacha Bay by Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky and the coast of the Avacha Gulf offer expedition-style cold-water diving on the edge of the Pacific. Underwater there's volcanic topography, huge starfish, anemones, crabs and octopus, and in Zheleznaya Bay you can dive with Steller sea lions. The water is cold even in summer: according to Rossiyskaya Gazeta, around +5 °C already at shallow depth. You need a drysuit and experience. The season runs from July to September. The weather often scuppers trips, so allow at least two weeks for the journey.
kamchatka-avacha-bay.rating_basis: Russian guides (RG, Trip.com, the PADI blog) mention Kamchatka as a wild, little-explored destination: volcanic topography, Steller sea lions, orcas, big cold-water fauna. But it's expensive, heavily weather-dependent and has almost no dive infrastructure. There are few reviews or detailed guides.
kamchatka-avacha-bay.hazards: Icy water and hypothermia, sudden weather changes, fog and ocean swell at the mouth of the bay. Steller sea lions are big and can be aggressive. The base is far from everything — you can rely only on yourself and the organiser.
kamchatka-avacha-bay.crowd_note: Only a handful of divers; dives are run expedition-style in small groups
kamchatka-avacha-bay.region: Kamchatka Krai, Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, entrance to Avacha Bay (Avacha Gulf, Pacific Ocean)
kamchatka-avacha-bay.marine_life: Huge starfish, colourful anemones, crabs, octopus, molluscs and fish, volcanic topography and kelp. At the surface — seals, Steller sea lions, tufted puffins and cormorants; orcas sometimes visit the gulf.
kamchatka-avacha-bay.signature_sites: Zheleznaya Bay (Steller sea lions), the Three Brothers rocks at the entrance to Avacha Bay, Russkaya Bay, Starichkov Island
pros: Wild nature: Steller sea lions, orcas, seals, seabird colonies
Volcanic underwater topography and big cold-water fauna
Hardly any other divers
Can be combined with volcanoes, geysers and fishing
cons: Very expensive: expeditions from 150,000 ₽ excluding flights
Cold water — you need a drysuit and experience
Weather often cancels dives: fog, storms, ocean swell
Few dive centres and almost no information about them online
kamchatka-avacha-bay.airport: PKC — Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky (Yelizovo), ~40 min to the city and the piers
highlights: Dives with Steller sea lions (Zheleznaya Bay)
Giant starfish, crabs, octopus, colourful anemones
Orcas, seals, tufted puffins and cormorants at the surface

ladoga-valaam-skerries.description: Northern Ladoga — the skerries, the Valaam archipelago and the granite islands near Lahdenpohja and Sortavala — is the best-known freshwater dive destination in northwest Russia. St Petersburg clubs bring groups here by boat from Priozersk. Underwater, granite walls drop for tens of metres, and there are grottoes and sunken barges and steamships. In summer the surface water reaches +20…24 °C, but at 9 m it's about +12 °C and below 20 m only +3…5 °C, so you need a drysuit. The best time is early summer and early autumn.
ladoga-valaam-skerries.rating_basis: RG and Trip.com call Ladoga the main freshwater destination in northwest Russia: wrecks, granite skerries, with Ruskeala nearby. Medium difficulty, drysuit required. It's mostly St Petersburg clubs coming for the weekend; Ladoga has no international reputation.
ladoga-valaam-skerries.hazards: Cold at depth and a sharp thermocline, sudden storms on Ladoga, darkness and poor visibility below 15–20 m, fishing nets, danger inside the wrecks.
ladoga-valaam-skerries.crowd_note: Small club groups on boats from Priozersk; there are almost never other divers on the sites
ladoga-valaam-skerries.region: Karelia, northern Lake Ladoga: the Valaam archipelago, the Lahdenpohja skerries, Ladoga Skerries National Park
ladoga-valaam-skerries.marine_life: A freshwater lake where the main attractions are the topography and the wrecks: granite walls and grottoes in amber-coloured water. Few fish; the Ladoga ringed seal is occasionally seen.
ladoga-valaam-skerries.signature_sites: The Lahdenpohja skerry, the islands of the Valaam archipelago, Putsaari island, sunken barges and steamships; nearby — the Ruskeala marble quarry (a separate site, suitable for beginners too)
pros: Close to St Petersburg, easy for a weekend trip
Wrecks and dramatic granite topography
Beautiful scenery above water: the skerries, Valaam
Can be combined with the Ruskeala marble quarry
cons: Cold water at depth (+3…5 °C), you need a drysuit
Dark, amber water with modest visibility
Hardly any wildlife
The programme depends heavily on the weather on the lake
ladoga-valaam-skerries.airport: LED — St Petersburg, ~2.5 h by car to Priozersk (boarding point for the boats); ~4 h to Sortavala
highlights: Sunken barges and paddle steamers
Granite walls, grottoes and the rocky labyrinths of the skerries
The Ladoga ringed seal (if you're lucky)
school_notes: Mini-liveaboard from Priozersk on the expedition vessel Grifon in late May: 3 days, 37,000 ₽ including cabin, meals and 1–2 dives a day. Drysuit rental 1,500 ₽/day; Dry Suit and AOWD courses available on board
“Northern Ladoga” weekends in September (Lahdenpohja skerry, Valaam, Putsaari): 3–4 dives, from 21,000 ₽. OWD (ideally AOWD) and a drysuit required

primorye-vityaz-andreevka.description: The Gamov Peninsula in southern Primorye, with the bays of Vityaz, Andreyevka and Troitsa, is the main dive area of the Russian Far East. In July–August the surface water warms to +20…22 °C, while below the thermocline at 15 m it's about +13…15 °C. Visibility reaches 30 m. Underwater there are rock walls at 20–40 m covered in anemones and kelp, grottoes and wrecks; giant octopus turn up on almost every dive, and spotted seals near their haul-outs. Suits OWD divers, preferably in a drysuit or a 7 mm wetsuit.
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.rating_basis: Russian guides (RG, Trip.com, Vokrug Sveta, the PADI blog) rank southern Primorye among the best dive destinations in the country. It's the warmest sea in the Far East, with octopus, seals and big cold-water fauna. Downsides — a short season, summer fogs and average visibility.
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.hazards: A cold thermocline (+15 °C and below) under the warm surface layer, fogs and typhoons in late summer, lots of boats at the popular bays, sea urchins.
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.crowd_note: In July–August boats from several bases head for the popular headlands, but there are lots of sites and they're spread out; quieter in September
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.region: Primorsky Krai, Khasansky District, Gamov Peninsula, Peter the Great Gulf (Sea of Japan)
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.marine_life: Giant octopus, starfish and sea urchins, sea cucumbers (trepang), scallops, red sea squirts, anemones and soft corals, nudibranchs, shrimps, wolffish and pufferfish, kelp forests. Spotted seals haul out on the rocks, and spiny dogfish are seen around Stenin Island in spring and autumn.
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.signature_sites: Cape Gamov, the mouth of Vityaz Bay, the Tarantsev Islands (octopus), Stenin Island, Klerk Island (grotto), Kamen Opasnosti, the schooner Lakhtak (8–16 m), Putyatin Island (Steller sea lions)
pros: The warmest water in the Russian Far East in July–September
Octopus, spotted seals, rich cold-water fauna
Lots of varied sites: drop-offs, grottoes, wrecks
Can be combined with a beach holiday in Vityaz and Andreyevka
cons: Short season: June–October
Fogs, algal blooms and typhoons in summer; visibility varies
A long, expensive flight from European Russia
Some islands are part of a marine reserve and need a pass
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.airport: VVO — Vladivostok, about 4 h by car to Andreyevka and Vityaz
primorye-vityaz-andreevka.dive_price_note: Day boat trip, 2 dives — 5,000 ₽ (about 2,500 ₽ per dive), gear rental 3,000 ₽; try dive 6,000 ₽ (Nautilus dive centre, Andreyevka)
highlights: Giant Pacific octopus (a colony around the Tarantsev Islands)
Steller sea lions at Putyatin Island
Spotted seal haul-outs
Spiny dogfish at Stenin Island (spring and autumn)
school_notes: Dive base with accommodation on the shore of Troitsa Bay (Andreyevka), season from 5 June to 30 October. 18 m boat, 2 dives a day — 5,000 ₽. Of the PADI courses, it only runs continuing education

Group tours to the Dem Club base in late July – early August: 6 days of diving, octopus, spotted seals, a dive with Steller sea lions. From 195,000 ₽ excluding flights. OWD minimum, Dry Suit preferred
Group tour in July: 11 days, 5 of them diving, 125,000 ₽ excluding flights

white-sea-nilmoguba.description: The Karelian shore of the Kandalaksha Gulf by the Arctic Circle is Russia's top place for under-ice diving on sea ice. From February to April dives are made through holes cut in ice a metre and a half thick: the water is −1.5 °C, visibility up to 30–40 m, with ice ridges and icicles hanging over fields of soft corals and anemones. In summer and autumn you dive from boats along rock walls and through kelp forests. A place for certified divers with drysuit experience.
white-sea-nilmoguba.rating_basis: X-Ray Mag, Scuba Diving, Sport Diver and UW Photography Guide call the White Sea one of the best places in the world for ice diving, and the PADI blog calls it “perhaps the best ice diving on sea ice”. In summer it's cold-water diving with moderate visibility, an acquired taste.
white-sea-nilmoguba.hazards: Hypothermia and regulator freezing; dives only on a safety line through the ice hole. Tides of about 2 m move the ice floes and create currents in the straits. Some sites have a hydrogen sulphide layer. The base is remote, a long way from hospitals and recompression chambers.
white-sea-nilmoguba.crowd_note: Almost all tourist dives run from a single base in small groups; there are no other divers on the sites
white-sea-nilmoguba.region: Karelia, Louhi District, Kandalaksha Gulf of the White Sea (by the Arctic Circle, 6 km from Moscow State University's White Sea Biological Station)
white-sea-nilmoguba.marine_life: Soft corals, fields of anemones, sponges, hydroids, multi-armed starfish and basket stars, kelp forests, nudibranchs, crabs, wolffish and cod; occasionally seals, bearded seals and belugas.
white-sea-nilmoguba.signature_sites: Stone Garden and Miracle Stone (by Krestovy Island), Biofilter Bay, Beluga Rock, Kamenny Lob and Ludushka (by Kasyan Island)

Very clear water in winter, up to 30–40 m

seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.description: Northwest Mahé by Beau Vallon is the Seychelles' main dive area: granite boulders covered in coral, wrecks and lots of big rays. Beginners learn in the bay and on the shallow reefs, while Shark Bank and the Ennerdale tanker at 25–30 m are for experienced divers. From May to November the southeast trade wind blows steadily.
seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.rating_basis: Beautiful granite dive sites and clear water in the shoulder seasons; reviews praise the variety and the lack of crowds, but mention the high prices and the coral damaged by the 1998 bleaching (some reefs, for example around Silhouette, have recovered). Fact-check (November 2026): Shark Bank is on Big Blue Divers' list of sites (longer trips), but with no description, depth or season; the whale shark months, the best shoulder seasons and a recompression chamber in Victoria weren't confirmed by sources — removed. Seasons are low-confidence: according to Wikipedia the southeast trade wind blows from May to November, and the hot, humid months are December–April; no dive season is given anywhere, so all months are shoulder months. Coordinates not verified — left as an estimate (the bank northwest of Beau Vallon).
seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.hazards: Currents at the exposed sites (Shark Bank), depth to 30 m on the wrecks, swell in the trade-wind season, boat traffic off Beau Vallon
seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.crowd_note: Small groups; rarely more than one or two boats on a site
seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.region: Northwest Mahé, Beau Vallon bay, Indian Ocean
seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.marine_life: Granite boulders covered in corals and sponges: big stingrays and eagle rays, barracuda, batfish, turtles, reef sharks, moray eels, huge schools of fish.
seychelles-mahe-shark-bank.signature_sites: Shark Bank (a granite plateau at 18–30 m), Brissare Rocks, the Ennerdale tanker wreck, L'Ilot, Sainte Anne; on Praslin — Ave Maria Rocks and Marianne Island

Granite topography unlike any other reef
Rays, turtles, reef sharks
Easy to combine with a holiday on Praslin and La Digue

koh-lanta-hin-daeng.description: Koh Lanta is a laid-back island in Krabi province and the departure point for two remote pinnacles in the open sea — Hin Daeng and Hin Muang, among the best sites in Thailand. These are deep walls with currents for experienced divers, with a chance of mantas and whale sharks in February–April. For beginners there are easy bays and caves in the Koh Haa archipelago.
koh-lanta-hin-daeng.rating_basis: Hin Daeng and Hin Muang are called the best sites in Thailand's southern Andaman Sea (liveaboard.com, Lanta dive centres): deep walls covered in soft corals and a chance of mantas and whale sharks; the sites are remote and uncrowded.
koh-lanta-hin-daeng.hazards: Strong currents and depth at Hin Muang and Hin Daeng, rough crossings, lionfish and scorpionfish
koh-lanta-hin-daeng.crowd_note: Hin Daeng is ~2 h away by speedboat, so there are few boats; Koh Haa sometimes has several boats from Lanta and Phi Phi during the day
koh-lanta-hin-daeng.region: Krabi, Mu Ko Lanta National Park, Andaman Sea
koh-lanta-hin-daeng.marine_life: The sheer walls of Hin Muang and Hin Daeng covered in purple and red soft corals, grey reef and leopard sharks, barracuda, tuna, jacks; in February–April — mantas and whale sharks. Around the Koh Haa islands — caves, turtles and reef fish.
koh-lanta-hin-daeng.signature_sites: Hin Daeng (“Red Rock”, 5–40 m), Hin Muang (“Purple Rock”, a deep wall), Koh Haa (the Cathedral, the lagoon, caves), Koh Rok, Koh Bida Nok off Phi Phi

Few boats on the sites

koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.description: Koh Tao is a small island in the Gulf of Thailand where people come above all to learn: its Open Water courses are among the cheapest in the world, and there are dozens of schools. The season runs almost year-round, apart from the November–December monsoon. For certified divers the highlights are the granite pinnacles of Chumphon and Sail Rock, with schooling fish and a chance of whale sharks in March–May and September–October.
koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.rating_basis: One of the world's biggest dive-training hubs: cheap courses, dozens of schools, warm calm water. Chumphon Pinnacle and Sail Rock are considered the best sites in the Gulf of Thailand, but the coral and visibility can't match the Andaman Sea (the Similans).
koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.hazards: Titan triggerfish bite during the nesting season, boat traffic, currents on the pinnacles, rough crossings in the monsoon; jellyfish occur in the Gulf of Thailand
koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.crowd_note: Lots of training groups at Japanese Gardens and the island's inshore sites at the same time; several boats sit at Chumphon and Sail Rock in the morning — quieter on early trips and in September–October
koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.marine_life: Granite pinnacles carpeted in anemones, with giant groupers, barracuda, batfish, tuna and jacks; whale sharks visit in season. Right by the island — turtles, reef sharks in Shark Bay, titan triggerfish.
koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.signature_sites: Chumphon Pinnacle (to 36 m, for AOW), Sail Rock / Hin Bai (between Koh Tao and Koh Phangan), Southwest Pinnacle, Shark Island, Japanese Gardens by Nang Yuan, the scuttled Navy ship HTMS Sattakut (~30 m)
koh-tao-chumphon-pinnacle.chamber: SSS Recompression Chamber on Koh Tao (24/7)
pros: Cheap courses and dives, a huge choice of schools
Warm, calm water, an almost year-round season
A chance of meeting a whale shark

similan-elephant-head-rock.description: The Similan Islands are a marine national park 70 km from Khao Lak and Thailand's premier diving; the park is open from 15 October to 15 May. Granite boulders, swim-throughs and clear water suit both beginners (the sheltered bays of the east coast) and experienced divers (currents in the west and at Koh Bon and Koh Tachai to the north). Best of all is a 3–5-day liveaboard that takes in Richelieu Rock, where whale sharks and mantas come in February–April.
similan-elephant-head-rock.rating_basis: Thailand's best diving: the Similans and Richelieu Rock consistently make Asian top lists (liveaboard.com, PADI, magazines), with clear water and mantas/whale sharks in spring. Downsides — crowds of day speedboats and signs of coral bleaching.
similan-elephant-head-rock.hazards: Strong and changeable currents at the western sites, Elephant Head, Koh Bon and Richelieu Rock; boat traffic; lionfish and stonefish
similan-elephant-head-rock.crowd_note: The national park is capped at 3,850 visitors a day; islands No. 4 and No. 8 get lots of speedboats from Khao Lak during the day, and several liveaboards sit at Richelieu Rock at once. Quieter on a liveaboard with early dives
similan-elephant-head-rock.region: Phang Nga, Andaman Sea (trips from Khao Lak and Phuket)
similan-elephant-head-rock.marine_life: Granite boulders and canyons covered in soft and hard corals, schools of reef fish, turtles, leopard and reef sharks, bluespotted rays; from February to April — mantas and whale sharks. Richelieu Rock in the Surin park is famous for both big fish and macro.
similan-elephant-head-rock.signature_sites: Elephant Head Rock — Hin Pusar (Island No. 7, swim-throughs, strong currents), Christmas Point, Shark Fin Reef, Anita's Reef (for beginners), Koh Bon (mantas), Richelieu Rock (a 5–35 m pinnacle in the Surin park)

Mantas and whale sharks in February–April
A choice of day speedboats from Khao Lak or liveaboards

similan-elephant-head-rock.course_price_note: PADI Open Water on Phuket (Sea Bees Nai Yang), 16,000 baht

Whale sharks (Richelieu Rock, Koh Tachai)
Macro at Richelieu Rock: seahorses, harlequin shrimp, toadfish

kas-canyon.description: Kaş is Turkey's top dive resort: a quiet town on the Lycian coast opposite the Greek island of Meis (Kastellorizo), with about 28 sites 5–30 minutes away by boat. Clear water, topography with canyons and caves, sunken aircraft and ships, ancient amphorae. Suits both a first course (calm bays with almost no current) and technical diving.
kas-canyon.rating_basis: Kaş is called Turkey's diving capital (Hürriyet, Daily Sabah, X-Ray Mag, Go Türkiye): water clear to 40 m, canyons, caves, aircraft and ancient amphorae; fewer fish than in the Red Sea.
kas-canyon.hazards: The deep sites (amphorae, Dimitri, SM.79) can easily take you past 40 m; boat traffic near the harbour; sea urchins and stinging hydroids; caves and tunnels — only with a guide.
kas-canyon.crowd_note: About 17 dive schools in Kaş itself; in summer you'll meet several boats at the popular sites (the Canyon, the DC-3); quieter in autumn.
kas-canyon.region: Lycian coast, Antalya Province, Mediterranean Sea
kas-canyon.marine_life: Groupers, barracuda, amberjacks, moray eels, octopus, wrasse, nudibranchs, seahorses in the Posidonia meadows; turtles are common, and very rarely a Mediterranean monk seal.
kas-canyon.signature_sites: The Canyon and the Tunnel, the DC-3 Dakota aircraft, the Dimitri wreck, Flying Fish (an Italian SM.79 bomber at 71 m — for tech divers), Beşmi island, Limanağzı (night dives)
kas-canyon.chamber: No recompression chamber in Kaş; the nearest hyperbaric medicine centres are in Antalya (~3.5 h) — check the evacuation plan with your dive centre

mafia-island-chole-bay.description: Mafia is a quiet island south of Zanzibar with Tanzania's oldest and largest marine reserve. The sites in sheltered Chole Bay are accessible year-round and suit training, while the outer reefs (October to March only, to 26 m, unpredictable currents) are for AOW divers. From October to February you can snorkel with resident whale sharks; all dives are tied to the tides.
mafia-island-chole-bay.rating_basis: Mafia is famous for its resident whale shark population (Wikipedia), and the marine park is Tanzania's oldest and largest (founded in 1995). Fact-check (November 2026): the months for whale sharks (October–February), humpback whales (August–September) and turtle hatchlings (June–September) are from the Mafia Island Diving website; the Chole Bay sites operate year-round, those outside it only from October to March. So peak is October–February, the other months are shoulder months (lodge closures in April–May weren't confirmed by sources). Kinasi Pass isn't mentioned in the sources. Coordinates are an estimate: the point was moved into Chole Bay north of Chole island (using the island's coordinates from Wikipedia), accurate to ~1 km.
mafia-island-chole-bay.hazards: Strong tidal currents in Kinasi Pass, swell outside the bay in the southeast trade-wind season (June–September), remoteness from medical care
mafia-island-chole-bay.crowd_note: A few small lodges — usually only your boat on the sites
mafia-island-chole-bay.region: Mafia Island Marine Park, south of Zanzibar, Indian Ocean
mafia-island-chole-bay.marine_life: The Chole Bay reefs with giant groupers and Napoleon wrasse; on the outer reefs — green turtles, groupers and rays. A resident population of whale sharks lives off the island (snorkelling from October to February); humpback whales pass by in August–September.
mafia-island-chole-bay.signature_sites: Kinasi Pass (drift), Chole Wall, Main Reef, the Coral Garden in Chole Bay; snorkelling with whale sharks off Kilindoni

zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.description: Mnemba is a private island 3 km off Zanzibar's northeast coast, ringed by the reef of the MIMCA marine conservation area. Shallow coral gardens and walls with a gentle drift suit both first dives and experienced divers; dolphins and turtles are often seen along the way. You dive from Matemwe (15–20 minutes by boat), Nungwi and Kendwa.
zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.rating_basis: The most popular dive site in Zanzibar and Tanzania: warm water, good visibility, dolphins and turtles; reviews praise how easy and beautiful the reefs are, but complain about the crowds of snorkelling boats. Fact-check (November 2026): Wikipedia confirms the MIMCA reserve, three dolphin species, ~600 reef fish species and green turtle nesting from February to September; One Ocean's sites range from 2–15 m (Kichwani, Sand Banks — for beginners) to walls at 12–50 m (Big Wall — only in calm conditions). Whale sharks and a dive season weren't confirmed by sources: according to Wikipedia the main rains are March–May, the short rains November–December, with the least rainfall in July, but the northeast monsoon brings a strong breeze to the northeast coast — so all months are shoulder months. Coordinates not verified (Wikipedia only says “~3 km off the northeast coast of Unguja, opposite Muyuni”) — left as an estimate.
zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.hazards: Light to moderate currents on the outer walls, boat traffic around the atoll, sea urchins and lionfish, sun
zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.crowd_note: Lots of boats with snorkellers and dolphin tours around Mnemba during the day; divers are better off going out in the morning
zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.region: Northeast Unguja (Matemwe, Nungwi, Kendwa), Indian Ocean
zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.marine_life: A ring reef around Mnemba island: corals, turtles, moray eels, rays, lionfish, Napoleon wrasse, big schools of reef fish; dolphins (three species) are seen often, and there are about 600 reef fish species.
zanzibar-mnemba-atoll.signature_sites: Wattabomi, Kichwani, Aquarium, the Coral Garden on Mnemba Atoll; nearby — Leven Bank off Nungwi for experienced divers

kona-manta-night-dive.description: The Kona manta night dive is one of the best-known dives in the world: divers settle on the sand at ~10 m and shine their torches upwards, and mantas loop overhead, feeding on plankton. The dive is easy and suits beginners with Open Water certification; non-certified visitors can watch the mantas from the surface on snorkel. A trip is usually two dives: a reef at sunset and the night manta dive.
kona-manta-night-dive.rating_basis: The Kona manta night dive is a “world-famous” dive (Kona Honu Divers); Wikivoyage: an easy dive for beginners, 1–20 mantas a night, with night snorkelling for the non-certified. Seasons: the mantas feed every night year-round, so every month is peak; Kona Honu calls September the best month for diving in Kona. Coordinates are an estimate: a point at Garden Eel Cove near Kona airport (the sources give no coordinates for the site), accurate to within ~1 km.
kona-manta-night-dive.hazards: Night dive; in a swell the dive is done deeper (~17 m).
kona-manta-night-dive.region: Hawaii, west (Kona) coast of the Big Island
kona-manta-night-dive.marine_life: Reef mantas feeding on plankton at night in the torchlight; by day — green turtles, schools of fish, lava arches, sometimes dolphins, and humpback whales in winter.
kona-manta-night-dive.signature_sites: Garden Eel Cove (Manta Heaven) — night mantas; lava arches and caves along the Kona coast; Pelagic Magic — a night drift in the open ocean

nha-trang-hon-mun.description: Nha Trang is Vietnam's main beach resort and the most popular place to dive in the country, much loved by Russian-speaking tourists. Dives take place in the Hon Mun marine reserve, 30–40 minutes away by boat: calm water, swim-throughs at Madonna Rock and lots of macro. It's a place for try dives and an inexpensive course with a Russian-speaking instructor, not for big fish.
nha-trang-hon-mun.rating_basis: The most popular dive destination in Vietnam and one of the first IUCN-recognised marine reserves, but the reefs have suffered badly from overfishing and tourism; good for inexpensive training and macro, not on global top lists.
nha-trang-hon-mun.hazards: Boat traffic at Hon Mun, sea urchins, lionfish and scorpionfish; storms and typhoons in the rainy season
nha-trang-hon-mun.crowd_note: Dozens of excursion boats with snorkellers and try dives gather at Hon Mun during the day; dive boats try to get there early in the morning
nha-trang-hon-mun.region: Khanh Hoa, Nha Trang Bay, South China Sea
nha-trang-hon-mun.marine_life: Hard and soft corals in the Hon Mun marine reserve, clownfish, lionfish, moray eels, rays, cuttlefish and lots of macro — nudibranchs and shrimps. Few big fish because of years of overfishing.
nha-trang-hon-mun.signature_sites: Madonna Rock (swim-throughs), Moray Beach, Coral Garden, Lobster Cave, Dam Bay, a wreck in the bay

Calm water with no current — ideal for beginners
