Visibility usually 10–20 m
nha-trang-hon-mun.airport: CXR — Cam Ranh, ~28 km (~40 min) to Nha Trang
nha-trang-hon-mun.dive_price_note: 1-day package: 3 dives (Madonna, Dam Bay, Lobster Cave, the wreck) — USD 100, Sailing Club Divers
highlights: Macro: nudibranchs, shrimps, clownfish in anemones
Swim-throughs and grottoes at Madonna Rock
school_notes: Vietnam's oldest operator (Nha Trang and Whale Island); training and guides in Russian, a separate Russian-language phone number
Speaks English, Korean, Russian, French and Vietnamese; daily trips year-round

aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.description: Aliwal Shoal is a fossilised dune 5 km offshore, a marine protected area and one of the world's best sites for cageless shark diving: in winter and spring hundreds of ragged-tooth sharks come here to mate, and in summer tiger sharks and hammerheads. Depths are modest (6–27 m), but the RIB launch through the surf and the Agulhas Current call for solid skills; you can do your Open Water here, but the site really comes into its own for AOW divers.
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known shark-diving sites: raggies in winter and tiger sharks in summer, all cageless; often features in global top lists. Downsides — surf launches, currents and highly variable visibility.
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.hazards: The Agulhas Current (drift dives), surge, waves when launching and boarding through the surf, big sharks on baited dives — follow the briefing strictly
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.crowd_note: No more than 10 divers per boat (by law); in raggie season and on South African holidays there can be several boats at Cathedral at once
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.region: KwaZulu-Natal, south coast near Durban, Indian Ocean
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.marine_life: In winter — hundreds of ragged-tooth sharks in the reef's caves and gullies; in summer — tiger and bull sharks, hammerheads and occasionally mantas; year-round, oceanic blacktip sharks, turtles, rays, big schools of fish. The reef is an ancient fossilised dune with pinnacles, caves and soft corals.
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.signature_sites: Cathedral, Raggie's Cave, Shark Alley, the MV Produce (32 m) and SS Nebo (27 m) wrecks, a baited blue-water shark dive
aliwal-shoal-umkomaas.chamber: The nearest recompression chambers are in Durban (~50 km)
pros: Guaranteed shark encounters almost year-round
Two wrecks next to the reef
The sardine run and humpback whales in winter
An hour's drive from Durban airport
cons: Surf launches, a bumpy RIB ride
Visibility swings from 5 to 40 m, murkier in summer because of the rivers
Water around 20 °C in winter — you need a 5–7 mm wetsuit
A marine protected area permit is required
highlights: Ragged-tooth sharks (raggies) gathering to mate
Tiger sharks (baited dives)
Hammerheads
The sardine run: dolphins, whales, gannets
Humpback whales
Oceanic blacktip sharks on baited dives
school_notes: Dive centre in Umkomaas, boats go out daily; baited shark dives
Guesthouse with diving in Umkomaas

sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.description: Sodwana Bay is South Africa's main dive resort, in the iSimangaliso reserve: Africa's southernmost coral reefs, warm water and easy 9–20 m depths make it one of the country's best places for training and first dives. Two Mile Reef, 3–4 km from the boat launch, is the most popular; the more distant reefs (Five, Seven, Nine Mile) are deeper and more interesting for experienced divers.
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.rating_basis: South Africa's main dive resort (~35,000 divers a year), the country's best coral reefs and a popular training spot; in international top lists it trails Aliwal Shoal and the megafauna sites. Fact-check (November 2026): Wikipedia confirms ~35,000 divers a year, Two Mile depths from 9 to 30+ m, raggies at Quarter Mile in January–February, humpback whales in winter–spring (no months given), whale sharks (no months given) and coelacanths; the water is usually above 20 °C, up to 29 °C in summer. Mantas, turtle nesting months, the best diving months and a recompression chamber weren't confirmed by sources — removed. Peak is January–February only (raggies), the rest are shoulder months. Coordinates are an estimate: ~3 km north of Jesser Point and ~1 km offshore, consistent with the bay's coordinates on Wikipedia (27°32′ S, 32°41′ E) and the distances to Five Mile (8 km) and Seven Mile (11 km).
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.hazards: RIB launches through the surf from the beach, current on the outer edges of the reefs, boat traffic at Jesser Point
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.crowd_note: On South African holidays (Easter, December–January) Two Mile Reef is busy with boats and training groups; uncrowded on weekdays outside the school holidays
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.region: KwaZulu-Natal, iSimangaliso Wetland Park, Indian Ocean
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.marine_life: Africa's southernmost coral reefs: hard and soft corals (branching, table and plate corals at Five Mile), turtles, moray eels, rays; in January–February ragged-tooth sharks gather at Quarter Mile, whale sharks are seen in the reserve, and humpback whales pass by in winter and spring. Loggerhead and leatherback turtles live in the park. Coelacanths live in the deep canyons (tech divers with a permit only).
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.signature_sites: Two Mile Reef (Chain, Pinnacles, Antons, Caves & Overhangs), Quarter Mile, Stringer, Five Mile, Seven Mile, Nine Mile
pros: A good place for Open Water and first dives
Warm water and rich corals
Lots of dive centres and campsites
Humpback whales in winter and spring, raggies in January–February
cons: Boats launch straight off the beach through the surf — it's bumpy
Crowded on South African holidays
A reserve permit is required
Far from the big cities (~5 h from Durban)
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.airport: DUR — Durban (King Shaka), ~4.5–5 h by car
sodwana-bay-two-mile-reef.course_price_note: PADI Open Water at Coral Divers: R6360–7950 depending on the season (rates 01.02.2026–31.01.2027, “tbc”), park fees not included; ≈€320–400
highlights: Pregnant ragged-tooth sharks (raggies) on Quarter Mile reef
Migrating humpback whales (winter–spring)
Whale sharks
Coelacanths in the underwater canyons — tech diving only, deeper than 100 m, with trimix and a special permit
Leatherback and loggerhead turtles, a huge variety of reef fish
school_notes: PADI 5 Star resort and dive centre inside the park, free shuttle to the beach

antigua-jolly-harbour.description: An island of regattas and the historic Nelson's Dockyard, with dozens of bays around its shores and flat, coral-fringed Barbuda 30 miles to the north. Passages are longer and the seas bigger than in the BVI — an area for crews with bareboat experience.
antigua-jolly-harbour.rating_basis: The yachting capital of the Eastern Caribbean: Nelson's Dockyard, world-class regattas, “365 beaches”, deserted Barbuda; Moorings and Sunsail rate the area Level 2 (harder than the BVI), and reviews mention big seas on the windward side.
antigua-jolly-harbour.hazards: Coral reefs along the north and east coasts and around Barbuda (some areas are off-limits to charter boats), northerly swell in Barbuda's anchorages in winter, big Atlantic seas on the east side, hurricanes June to November (Irma devastated Barbuda in 2017); 5 kn speed limit in harbours.
antigua-jolly-harbour.crowd_note: Generally quiet; Falmouth and English Harbour are packed with superyachts and regatta crews in April–May (Classic Regatta, Sailing Week) and at Christmas.
antigua-jolly-harbour.region: Caribbean, Leeward Islands: Antigua (English Harbour, Falmouth, Nonsuch Bay, Green Island), Barbuda; further afield Nevis and St Kitts
antigua-jolly-harbour.wind_desc: Trade winds: December–May east to north-east 15–20 kn, most stable January–May; June–November east to south-east 10–25 kn, less settled weather, squalls, hurricane season; in winter northerly swell works into some anchorages, especially on Barbuda.
antigua-jolly-harbour.route: Jolly Harbour — Deep Bay — Barbuda (Cocoa Point, ~30 miles) — back to Antigua (Five Islands) — Falmouth and English Harbour (Nelson's Dockyard) — Green Island / Nonsuch Bay from the south — Carlisle Bay — Jolly Harbour, about 110–120 miles in a week
antigua-jolly-harbour.mooring: Mooring buoys in Falmouth and Jolly Harbour $15–30 a night, a marina berth about $0.5–1 per foot per day; the first and last nights at the Dream Yacht base are free; in most bays you anchor on sand, and dinghy docks are few. No customs formalities between Antigua and Barbuda.
antigua-jolly-harbour.licence: No official licence required; your sailing CV is what counts. Sunsail asks for Level 2 — at least 10 days or 200 miles as skipper on a similar yacht (the area is considered harder than the BVI); if in doubt, a paid skipper becomes mandatory. Minimum crew of 2, no night sailing; the passage along the north-east coast between North Sound and Nonsuch Bay, the north of Barbuda and Spanish Point are closed to charter yachts because of reefs.
pros: Nelson's Dockyard and the regatta atmosphere
Plenty of empty bays and beaches, Barbuda's pink sand
Direct flights from London to ANU
No customs between Antigua and Barbuda
cons: Swell and wind on the windward (east) side
Reefs in the north and east; Barbuda is low and seen late — daylight navigation only
Expensive marinas in regatta season
Hurricane season; Sunsail/Moorings bases close July to October
antigua-jolly-harbour.airport: ANU — V. C. Bird, ~30–45 min to Jolly Harbour or English Harbour
antigua-jolly-harbour.charter_price_note: Bareboat Dufour 412 GL (41 ft, 3 cabins) per week: February–March ~$4,800–5,400 / June–October ~$2,400–2,700 (12knots, Jolly Harbour), converted from euros; up to $6,600 at Christmas
antigua-jolly-harbour.skipper_price_note: $240–311 per day (Moorings / Dream Yacht), plus food
highlights: RORC Caribbean 600 — a race around 11 islands starting in Antigua
Antigua Classic Yacht Regatta (English Harbour)
Antigua Sailing Week
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator (website and support in Russian), Dream Yacht boats in Jolly Harbour
Base in Nelson's Dockyard (English Harbour), open November to June
Bareboat and skippered charters from English Harbour
Base in Jolly Harbour Marina (dock D)

airlie-beach-whitsundays.description: Seventy-odd islands inside the Great Barrier Reef: the white sand of Whitehaven, the coral bays of Hook Island, whales in winter. One of the best places for a first bareboat week — no licence needed, short hops, daily radio contact with the base; the best season is June to October.
airlie-beach-whitsundays.rating_basis: Australia's main bareboat cruising ground: 74 islands, Whitehaven Beach, reefs and whales; no licence, short passages in sheltered water and strong base support. Downsides: steep Australian prices, stinger jellyfish and the cyclone season.
airlie-beach-whitsundays.hazards: Tropical cyclones (peak January–March), venomous stinger jellyfish October–May, reefs around the islands (move in good light with a lookout on the bow), shallow inlet entrances accessible only on the tide (Gulnare Inlet), bullets of wind in the bays in strong south-easterlies, the 300 m rule for whales.
airlie-beach-whitsundays.crowd_note: By day Whitehaven and Blue Pearl Bay are busy with tour boats (the buoys are taken until midday); in the evening there is plenty of room in Nara Inlet and Cid Harbour. Crowded during Australian school holidays.
airlie-beach-whitsundays.region: Queensland, Great Barrier Reef: the Whitsundays — Hook, Hamilton, Hayman and South Molle islands, Whitehaven Beach
airlie-beach-whitsundays.wind_desc: March–May are the windiest months: the south-east trade wind returns at 15–25 kn. June–July — brisk but steady trades. August–October — the driest and best season; from the second half of September the wind eases. December–March — the wet season with heat, thunderstorms and tropical cyclones.
airlie-beach-whitsundays.route: Airlie Beach (Coral Sea Marina, formerly Abell Point) — Nara Inlet — Cid Harbour / Gulnare Inlet — Hamilton Island Marina — Whitehaven Beach (Hill Inlet lookout) — Cateran Bay — Butterfly Bay — South Molle (Bauer Bay) — Airlie Beach, 7 nights
airlie-beach-whitsundays.mooring: The main base is Coral Sea Marina (formerly Abell Point) in Airlie Beach. Out on the water you anchor or use free public moorings; near the reefs (Hook's northern bays, Blue Pearl Bay) moorings have a 2-hour limit, and anchoring is allowed only outside the reef protection markers. Hamilton Island Marina is for water, rubbish and provisions; resort moorings ~A$50 a night. Great Barrier Reef Marine Park environmental charge ~A$24 per person.
airlie-beach-whitsundays.licence: No licence required: you need experience handling a sailing yacht (anchoring, reefing, chart work). A compulsory briefing before departure, then daily radio contact with the base; bareboats may not go out to the outer Barrier Reef. No experience — take a sail guide (skipper).
pros: Bareboat without a licence, good briefing and base support
Short passages in sheltered water
Whitehaven Beach, reefs, whales June–September
Wide choice of monohulls and catamarans
cons: Expensive (prices in Australian dollars plus fees)
Stinger jellyfish October–May — swim only in a stinger suit
January–March — wet season and cyclones
March–May — fresh trades up to 25 kn
airlie-beach-whitsundays.airport: PPP — Whitsunday Coast (Proserpine), ~40 min; HTI — Hamilton Island
airlie-beach-whitsundays.charter_price_note: 41–44 ft monohull (Dufour 412, Jeanneau 44i) from A$670–775 a night, 5-night minimum ≈ A$4,700–5,400 a week; in low season a “7 nights for the price of 5” deal. Plus insurance A$250–550, fuel and the environmental charge; 40–44 ft catamarans from A$835–2,000 a night
airlie-beach-whitsundays.skipper_price_note: Sail guide (skipper) A$650 per day (half day A$300); cook/host A$550 per day
highlights: Humpback whale season (keep at least 300 m away)
Hamilton Island Race Week
school_notes: Bareboat without a licence, sail guides; base at Coral Sea Marina, Airlie Beach

angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.description: Ilha Grande Bay between Rio and São Paulo: hundreds of rainforest-covered islands, beaches, fishing villages and floating restaurants. Short hops in warm, calm water, but not much wind — more a leisurely tropical cruise than a sailing workout. Good for a family holiday and a first bareboat; beginners should take a skipper.
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.rating_basis: Hundreds of islands, rainforest and sheltered bays; 12 Knots rates the route from Paraty as easy. The international charter fleet is small (about 8 boats in Angra and 27 in Paraty) and reviews are few. Downsides: light winds, summer rain and thunderstorms, crowds of motorboats at popular beaches.
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.hazards: Squalls and sudden wind shifts as cold fronts pass; summer thunderstorms; heavy traffic of speedboats and tourist schooners; tricky approaches to some bays (Praia dos Meros); tankers at the oil terminal and a shipyard near Angra.
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.crowd_note: During Brazilian holidays (December–February, Carnival) and at weekends Abraão, Praia do Dentista and Frade are busy with motorboats and tourist schooners; on weekdays and from April to November it is quiet.
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.region: Rio de Janeiro state: Ilha Grande Bay, the islands of Angra, Paraty
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.wind_desc: The bay is shielded by mountains and Ilha Grande, so the wind is usually light to moderate: a sea breeze by day, calm in the morning and at night, lots of motoring. Cold fronts, mostly May to September, bring a sudden south-westerly with squalls and rain for 1–2 days. Summer (December–March) is hot and humid, with afternoon thunderstorms.
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.route: Angra (BR Marinas Verolme) — Abraão on Ilha Grande — Saco do Céu — Lagoa Verde — Provetá — Sítio Forte — Praia do Dentista — Angra, ~70–90 miles in a week; from Paraty add the Saco do Mamanguá fjord
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.mooring: Marinas in Angra: BR Marinas Verolme, Bracuhy, Piratas, Angra dos Reis Marina Clube; several marinas in Paraty. Around Ilha Grande you spend the night at anchor in sheltered bays (Saco do Céu, Lagoa Verde, Abraão); floating restaurants and villages have fresh water. Berthing prices not found.
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.licence: Charter companies (per 12 Knots' terms) require a valid international certificate for bareboat: ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper or ASA 104 with an IPC; the document is uploaded in advance for checking. Check with the charter company what the Brazilian authorities require of foreign skippers.
pros: Short passages and sheltered anchorages
Warm water year-round, rainforest and beaches
No hurricane season, sailing all year
The colonial town of Paraty nearby
cons: Light winds, lots of motoring
Summer heat, humidity, thunderstorms and rain
Small charter fleet, mostly catamarans
Heavy motorboat traffic at popular beaches
A long flight from Europe
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.airport: GIG — Rio de Janeiro, ~2.5–3 h by car
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.charter_price_note: Dufour 410 (41 ft, 3 cabins) from Verolme marina per week: New Year and March / August ($5,960 / $4,335), other months $4,550–5,400; plus $335 cleaning. Most of the fleet is catamarans
angra-dos-reis-ilha-grande.skipper_price_note: Skipper $168 per day, plus food and a separate cabin
school_notes: Aggregator with a Russian version of the site: boats in Angra (Verolme, Bracuhy), Paraty and Rio

comox-desolation-sound.description: British Columbia's fjords 30–40 miles from Comox: sheer mountains, waterfalls, deep coves where you stern-tie to shore, and water that warms up to swimming temperature in summer. The Gulf Islands to the south are gentler and more settled, with farmers' markets and marinas. For crews seeking wilderness who don't mind a lot of motoring; tidal navigation experience required.
comox-desolation-sound.rating_basis: SAIL and Cruising World describe Desolation Sound and the Salish Sea as one of the best cruising grounds in North America: fjords, waterfalls, deep coves, wildlife, and water that is warm for these latitudes. Downsides — light summer winds and a short season.
comox-desolation-sound.hazards: Tidal currents in narrow passes (over 10 kn in places — the rapids north of Desolation Sound), big tides; seas on the Strait of Georgia crossing; depths close to shore make anchoring without a stern line difficult; driftwood and deadheads; cold water outside the summer months.
comox-desolation-sound.crowd_note: In July–August popular coves such as Prideaux Haven are full, with boats packed in on stern lines; in early June and September you may have just one or two boats per cove.
comox-desolation-sound.region: British Columbia, Strait of Georgia: Desolation Sound, Cortes Island, the Gulf Islands
comox-desolation-sound.wind_desc: In summer the mountains kill the wind in Desolation Sound itself, and boats motor up to 70% of the time. Crossing the Strait of Georgia you can get a brisk north-westerly or westerly of 10–20 kn in the afternoon. In autumn and winter fronts bring south-easterly gales.
comox-desolation-sound.route: Comox — across the Strait of Georgia to Lund or Savary Island — Prideaux Haven — Pendrell Sound — Teakerne Arm (Cassel Lake falls) — Cortes Island — Comox, ~130 miles in a week. The Gulf Islands are better started from Vancouver, Nanaimo or Sidney
comox-desolation-sound.mooring: In the fjords of Desolation Sound Marine Park you anchor, often with a stern line ashore; marinas are few (Lund, Refuge Cove, Gorge Harbour on Cortes). In Comox — the Comox Valley Harbour Authority harbour. Berthing prices not found.
comox-desolation-sound.licence: Canada requires no official licence for bareboat: the charter company assesses your sailing CV (chart work and tidal-water experience) and does an on-water checkout after the briefing. To operate a rented powerboat in Canada you complete a rental boat safety checklist instead of a PCOC card. Crossing from and back to the US requires reporting to customs.
pros: Fjords, waterfalls and mountains, wildlife
Warm water for the north in Pendrell Sound and Desolation Sound
Quiet coves in June and September
Easy to combine with the Gulf Islands and San Juans
cons: Light winds in summer, lots of motoring
Short season: June–September
Few charter companies and boats
A long flight and expensive
comox-desolation-sound.airport: YQQ — Comox, ~15 min; YVR — Vancouver (ferry or local flight)
comox-desolation-sound.charter_price_note: Jeanneau 42 DS at Desolation Sound Yacht Charters: 6,300–7,500 Canadian dollars for 6 nights plus 12% tax; high season 15 June – 15 September
highlights: The warmest water north of Mexico in Pendrell Sound — swimming is possible
school_notes: Comox's main charter company: 30–50 ft sailing and motor yachts, bareboat and skippered; IYT and CRYA training centre
From Bellingham (USA): 14-day flotillas in Desolation Sound and 10-day ones along the Sunshine Coast

turku-archipelago-sea-aland.description: A maze of thousands of granite islands between Turku and Åland: short hops along well-marked channels, fishing villages, guest harbours with saunas and white nights. Calm, tide-free water — a good choice for a first bareboat week in the Baltic.
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.rating_basis: One of the world's largest archipelagos (tens of thousands of islands) with excellent navigation marks and guest harbours with saunas; downsides — a season of just three months (12knots: charter in Finland runs June–August), light winds and a small charter fleet.
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.hazards: Countless rocks and shallows — stay in the channels; large Turku — Mariehamn — Stockholm ferries pass through the archipelago in narrow channels; summer thunderstorms with squalls; cold water in spring and autumn.
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.crowd_note: In July, the Finnish holiday season, guest harbours on popular islands (Nagu, Korpo, Kökar) fill up by evening; June and August are quiet.
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.region: Baltic: Turku, Naantali, Nagu, Korpo, Utö, Kökar; west to Mariehamn (Åland Islands)
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.wind_desc: In summer usually south-westerlies of 6–14 kn, a sea breeze by day and often calm at night; summer thunderstorms with squalls occur. Inside the archipelago there is almost no sea, but crossing open stretches to Åland (the Åland Sea) brings a short, steep chop. From September the wind is stronger and colder.
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.route: Turku — Nagu — Korpo — Kökar (Åland) — Utö — Nagu — Turku, ~130 miles in a week; a variant with a stop in Mariehamn
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.mooring: Guest harbours (vierasvenesatama) on almost every inhabited island, usually with a sauna and showers; plenty of natural moorings bow-to a rock with a stern anchor under the right of public access. In Mariehamn — the large Västerhamn and Österhamn harbours. No tides.
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.licence: Finland requires no separate licence for a pleasure-yacht skipper beyond the flag state's requirements; the ICC is recognised (Resolution 40). For bareboat, charter companies require a sailing qualification and experience — check with the charter company.
pros: A vast choice of islands and coves, 10–25-mile passages
No tides, almost no sea inside the archipelago
Saunas in guest harbours, peace and unspoilt nature
Åland — a special autonomy with its own maritime history (the barque Pommern in Mariehamn)
cons: The season is effectively June–August
Light winds and calms, lots of motoring
Rocks and shallows outside the channels
Few charter yachts, expensive restaurants
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.airport: TKU — Turku, ~15 min; HEL — Helsinki, ~2 h by car
turku-archipelago-sea-aland.charter_price_note: 12knots' average weekly price for 40–50 ft yachts in Finland: July / September (~€3,800 in June, ~€3,100 in August, ~€2,800 in May); the fleet is small
highlights: Juhannus — the Midsummer festival, bonfires on the islands
White nights
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator, the few charter yachts available in Finland

athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.description: The Saronic islands begin 15 miles from Athens: Aegina, Poros with its narrow strait, car-free Hydra, Spetses, and beyond them the quiet Argolic Gulf with Nafplio. The gulf is sheltered from the strong meltemi and passages are short — handy for a first charter, a short week after Athens, or a course.
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.rating_basis: The Saronic is Greece's most accessible area: the base is 40 minutes from Athens airport, passages are short and navigation simple (12 Knots rates the route easy; YACHT notes few shallows and well-marked entrances). Navily reviews mention overcrowded harbours in Hydra, Poros and Aegina and ferry wash.
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.hazards: Heavy ferry traffic from Piraeus and ship wash at Poros, Hydra and Aegina (at night too); anchors get crossed in cramped harbours — use a trip line; sudden strong northerly or southerly winds when a low passes in spring and autumn.
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.crowd_note: On high-season weekends local yachts join the Athens charters: Hydra, Poros and Aegina are packed, and a berth in Hydra means arriving early in the morning. The further west you go (Argolis, Nafplio), the quieter it gets.
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.region: Aegean Sea: Aegina, Poros, Hydra, Spetses, Methana, Epidavros, Nafplio
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.wind_desc: The gulf is sheltered from the strong meltemi: in July–August a north-easterly blows off Aegina, usually light to moderate, gusting up to force 6; off Poros there is often a thermal southerly, between Hydra and Spetses an easterly. Towards Nafplio it is calmer, with calms in spring and autumn; passing lows bring strong northerly or southerly winds.
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.route: Alimos — Methana — Hydra — Spetses — Poros — Aegina (Perdika) — Alimos, ~120 miles in a week; in two weeks you can add the Argolic Gulf (Nafplio, Ermioni)
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.mooring: Alimos (~1,080 berths) is Greece's largest charter base and overcrowded in summer. On the islands — town quays, stern-to with your anchor; few facilities but cheap (sometimes under €10 for 42 ft, water and electricity extra). In Hydra boats moor several deep — only with experience and a calm forecast; plenty of anchorage bays (Dokos, Agios Ioannis by Hydra).
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, a second experienced crew member (in Alimos you may be asked for a signed declaration) and a sailing CV. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: Base 40 minutes from Athens airport, X96 bus to the marina
Shelter from the strong meltemi, easy navigation
Cheap town quays
Easy to combine with Athens, Epidavros and Nafplio
cons: Very crowded at weekends and in August
Tricky multi-row mooring in Hydra
Wash from ferries and water taxis
Less “wild” nature than the Ionian
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.course_price_note: IYT Bareboat Skipper, a week aboard from Athens with a Russian-speaking instructor (InSailing, September 2026): €1,450 per person with 3 trainees, €1,900 with 2, plus €100 shared expenses
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.charter_price_note: List price without discounts for an Oceanis 41.1 from Alimos per week: 25 July — 15 August / from November to early April (~€1,900 in late October); ~€3,400 in June–July and late August
athens-saronic-argolic-gulf.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food
highlights: Spetses Classic Yacht Regatta — a classic yacht regatta on Spetses (every June)
school_notes: Sailing-trip platform with Russian-speaking skippers; IYT course in Russian and English
Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian website: yachts in Alimos and Lavrio
Large charter base in Alimos: bareboat, catamarans, cabin charters

corfu-north-ionian.description: The northern Ionian: green Corfu with its Venetian fortress, little Paxos and Antipaxos with turquoise coves, and the Epirus mainland coast with Parga and Sivota. Short hops and moderate winds — a good choice for a first charter and a family holiday, though the leg to Paxos is open to the swell.
corfu-north-ionian.rating_basis: Corfu is one of the Ionian's main bases: easy passages, green islands and the coves of Paxos and Antipaxos, a large marina close to the airport; charter companies and Sunsail rate the area easy. Downside — an expensive marina and crowds in Lakka and Parga in summer.
corfu-north-ionian.hazards: The border with Albania runs through the Corfu Strait — don't enter Albanian waters without clearance; ferry traffic off Corfu Town and Igoumenitsa; swell on the open passage to Paxos in north-westerlies; spring and autumn thunderstorms.
corfu-north-ionian.crowd_note: In July–August Lakka, Gaios and Parga fill up by evening, and berths below Corfu's Old Fortress are taken in the morning; May, June and September are calmer.
corfu-north-ionian.region: Ionian Sea: Corfu, Paxos, Antipaxos, mainland Sivota and Parga
corfu-north-ionian.wind_desc: In summer a north-westerly of force 3–5 prevails: it blows from late morning until sunset and dies down by evening. The Corfu — Paxos passage and the mainland coast are open to north-westerly swell; in spring and autumn there are southerly winds and thunderstorms.
corfu-north-ionian.route: Gouvia — Sivota (mainland) — Paxos (Lakka) — Antipaxos (day stop) — Parga — Plataria — Gouvia, ~95 miles in a week; a variant with a night below Corfu's Old Fortress (Mandraki)
corfu-north-ionian.mooring: D-Marin Gouvia (~1,200 berths) is a large and not cheap marina; book ahead in summer; anchoring in Gouvia bay is prohibited (the alternative is Kommeno bay). On Paxos and the mainland — town quays with lazy lines or your own anchor; in Lakka and Parga arrive early in summer.
corfu-north-ionian.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, a second experienced crew member and a sailing CV. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: Corfu airport 15–20 minutes from the marina, many direct flights
Short passages, moderate wind
The turquoise coves of Paxos and Antipaxos
A large full-service marina
cons: Gouvia marina is expensive, anchoring in the bay is prohibited
Crowds and a shortage of berths in Lakka and Parga in summer
Fewer islands nearby than around Lefkada
corfu-north-ionian.charter_price_note: List price without discounts for an Oceanis 41.1 (2018) from Gouvia per week: 8–22 August / from mid-October until May; ~€3,500 in June — early August, ~€2,000 in May
corfu-north-ionian.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food
highlights: Brindisi — Corfu Regatta (the 40th in 2026): start on 7 June in Italy, finish and party at Gouvia marina
Ionian International Sailing Week — a week of racing off Corfu (3–11 August in 2024)
school_notes: Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian website: yachts in Corfu, cabin cruises
Base at Gouvia marina: bareboat, one-week routes

kos-dodecanese.description: Kos is a handy base for the northern Dodecanese — rocky Kalymnos, Leros, holy Patmos and tiny Lipsi — or south to volcanic Nisyros. The islands are close together, but the summer wind is fresh and some passages are exposed — an area for experienced skippers or crews with a hired skipper.
kos-dodecanese.rating_basis: Kos is one of the Dodecanese's two main bases (together with Rhodes ~576 yachts): nearby, little-touristed Kalymnos, Leros, Patmos and Lipsi. Charter guides rate the area intermediate because of the meltemi and exposed passages, and don't recommend it for a first bareboat charter in July–August.
kos-dodecanese.hazards: Meltemi up to force 7 and gusts off the high islands; some bays are open to southerlies; the Turkish coast (Bodrum) is close — enter Turkish waters only with border clearance and the charter company's consent; ferry traffic.
kos-dodecanese.crowd_note: Kos Marina is busy with charters at weekends; on the northern islands (Leros, Lipsi, Patmos) you can usually find a berth even in August, though Patmos and Pali on Nisyros can get crowded.
kos-dodecanese.region: Aegean Sea: Kos, Pserimos, Kalymnos, Leros, Patmos, Lipsi, Nisyros
kos-dodecanese.wind_desc: The afternoon wind is noticeably stronger than in the Ionian. The westerly to north-westerly meltemi is strongest from late July to late August — up to force 7, making upwind passages hard; in spring the wind is force 3–5. Late spring and early autumn are gentler and less crowded.
kos-dodecanese.route: Kos — Pserimos — Kalymnos — Leros — Patmos — Lipsi — Kalymnos — Kos (northern Dodecanese), or Kos — Nisyros — Tilos — Symi to the south; in 10–14 days you can do both the northern and southern parts
kos-dodecanese.mooring: Kos Marina (~250–265 berths, plus ~80 in the old Mandraki harbour) is the main base and full of charters at weekends. On the islands — town quays, stern-to with your anchor (in Greece ~€20–70 a night, often less), many anchorage bays, but in a meltemi you need shelter from the north and west.
kos-dodecanese.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, a second experienced crew member and a sailing CV. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: Kos airport ~30 minutes from the marina
Nearby islands with authentic villages
Fewer charter crowds than the Saronic and Cyclades
A fresh, steady wind for proper sailing
cons: Strong meltemi in late July — August
Upwind passages on the way back
Few marinas — mostly town quays and anchoring
kos-dodecanese.charter_price_note: Typical range in Greece for 40–45 ft per week: high season €4,000–5,500, low season €2,500–4,000; in Kos an Oceanis 40.1/41.1 or Sun Odyssey 410 from ~$210–270 a day in cheap weeks, peak prices in July
kos-dodecanese.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food
school_notes: Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian website: yachts at Kos Marina

lavrio-cyclades.description: From Lavrio, half an hour from Athens airport, crews head into the western and central Cyclades: Kea, Kythnos, Syros, Paros, Sifnos. This is open sea with long passages and a strong summer meltemi — an area for experienced skippers or crews with a hired skipper; the wind is gentler in June and September.
lavrio-cyclades.rating_basis: The Cyclades are Greece's most iconic sailing area (whitewashed villages, long sailing legs), and Lavrio is the country's second-largest base (~480 yachts). Charter guides rate the route intermediate to difficult and don't recommend it for a first bareboat charter because of the meltemi.
lavrio-cyclades.hazards: A strong meltemi that accelerates in the channels between islands, with steep seas; ferries and fast craft in channels and ports; gusts off the lee slopes of high islands; some ports are open to swell in strong winds.
lavrio-cyclades.crowd_note: Paros (Parikia, Naoussa) and Syros are packed with charters at weekends; in July–August quay berths must be claimed before lunch; Kea and Kythnos are quieter.
lavrio-cyclades.region: Aegean Sea: Kea, Kythnos, Syros, Paros, Antiparos, Sifnos, Serifos
lavrio-cyclades.wind_desc: From June to September the meltemi blows — a northerly to north-westerly, usually 20–25 kn, gusting 30 kn and more in the channels between islands, seas up to 3–4 m; the peak is mid-July to mid-August, and the wind can last several days. Weaker in the morning, easing in the evening. In May, June and September it is gentler — the best time for less experienced crews.
lavrio-cyclades.route: Lavrio — Kea — Syros (Ermoupoli) — Paros — Sifnos — Kythnos — Lavrio, ~155 miles in a week; in 10–14 days you can go deeper into the Cyclades
lavrio-cyclades.mooring: Olympic Marine (680 berths) is the main base, 30 minutes from Athens airport. On the islands — town quays, stern-to with your anchor (in Greece ~€20–70 a night, often less): Ermoupoli suffers heavy ferry wash, Naoussa (Paros) is free but cramped, and Kamares (Sifnos) draws complaints about unexpected fees. For anchoring in a meltemi you need bays sheltered from the north.
lavrio-cyclades.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, a second experienced crew member and a sailing CV; for the Cyclades the charter company may check experience more strictly. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: Base 30 minutes from Athens airport
Classic Cycladic villages and beaches
Good steady wind for real sailing
Plenty of islands for 1–2-week routes
cons: Meltemi of 20–30 kn in July–August: days stuck in port and hard upwind passages
Long 25–30-mile passages
Ferry wash in ports, cramped quays on Paros
Few bays sheltered from the north wind
lavrio-cyclades.charter_price_note: Typical range in Greece for 40–45 ft per week: high season €4,000–5,500, low season €2,500–4,000; in Lavrio a Sun Odyssey 410 from ~$300 a day in cheap weeks
lavrio-cyclades.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food
school_notes: Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian website: yachts in Lavrio, a 7-day Cyclades route

lefkada-ionian-islands.description: Lefkada is linked to the mainland by a swing bridge, and to its east lie a dozen nearby islands: Meganisi, Ithaca, Kefalonia, Kalamos, Kastos. Short hops, water sheltered from the open sea, moderate and predictable wind — the best place in Greece for a first bareboat charter, a flotilla or a holiday with children.
lefkada-ionian-islands.rating_basis: The Ionian around Lefkada is the classic cruising ground for a first bareboat and flotillas: Sunsail rates the base Level 1 (for beginners), and Yachting Monthly calls Lefkas one of Greece's best islands; downside — overcrowded quays in summer.
lefkada-ionian-islands.hazards: Sudden afternoon gusts off Vasiliki (up to force 7), squalls off the mountains in spring and autumn, poor holding (ploughed mud) off Lefkas, the private island of Skorpios — keep your distance, the strait between Skorpios and Sparti is closed; earthquakes.
lefkada-ionian-islands.crowd_note: In July–August Nidri, Sivota and Fiskardo are packed by evening, and flotillas line the quays of Kalamos; May, June and September are much quieter. Lefkas marina is overflowing with charters on Saturdays.
lefkada-ionian-islands.region: Ionian Sea: Lefkada, Meganisi, Ithaca, Kefalonia, Kalamos, Kastos
lefkada-ionian-islands.wind_desc: From May to September the “maestro” — a north-westerly breeze of force 2–5 (8–18 kn): almost calm in the morning, the wind picks up after lunch and dies down by evening. Spring and autumn bring squalls off the mountains and occasionally a southerly sirocco. Off Vasiliki the afternoon wind can rise from force 2 to 7 within 10 minutes.
lefkada-ionian-islands.route: Lefkas — Kalamos — Port Atheni and Meganisi (Vathi) — Ithaca (Kioni) — Kefalonia (Fiskardo) — Vasiliki — Sivota — Nidri — Lefkas, ~100 miles in a week
lefkada-ionian-islands.mooring: D-Marin Lefkas (620 berths) is the main base, overflowing with charters in summer (per 2018 reviews ~€60 a night for 42 ft, more for catamarans); town quays on the islands are cheap or free (in Sivota water and electricity are free if you dine at the taverna), and there are many sheltered bays for anchoring with a line ashore.
lefkada-ionian-islands.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, one more experienced crew member and a sailing CV. RYA Day Skipper without an ICC has not been accepted since 2019. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: Short passages and calm water
A gentle, predictable afternoon maestro
Huge choice of yachts and flotillas
Lots of cosy coves and quayside tavernas
Preveza airport ~25 minutes from the marina
cons: Overcrowded quays and popular coves in summer
Not much wind for those who want to “race”
The Lefkas bridge opens on the hour — timing needs planning
lefkada-ionian-islands.charter_price_note: List price without discounts for an Oceanis 41 (2015) from Lefkas marina per week: late July — mid-August / until 25 April and from late September; ~€3,300–3,600 in June and September
lefkada-ionian-islands.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food

school_notes: Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian website: yachts in Lefkas, cabin cruises around the Ionian
