rhodes-dodecanese-symi.description: Rhodes with its Knights' Old Town and neighbouring Symi with colourful houses above the harbour make a beautiful but windy start to a southern Dodecanese route: Tilos, Halki, volcanic Nisyros. Passages are long and exposed, so the area suits experienced skippers; beginners should take a hired skipper or do a short loop to Symi.
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.rating_basis: Rhodes and Symi are the Dodecanese's most beautiful harbours, but 12 Knots rates the area intermediate: long exposed passages and the meltemi, not recommended for a first bareboat charter in July–August. Navily reviews: Rhodes marina is well run but expensive; Symi is cramped and pricey; Pedi and Pali are quiet.
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.hazards: Meltemi and southerlies in unprotected bays; northerly swell at Rhodes marina; ferry wash in Symi and on Nisyros; a shallow entrance to Pali harbour (keep close to the breakwater); Turkish waters are close — don't enter without clearance.
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.crowd_note: Cramped in Symi harbour (tour boats from Rhodes by day) and on the small quays of Tilos and Halki; Rhodes marina is full of charters at weekends.
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.region: Aegean Sea: Rhodes, Symi, Tilos, Halki, Nisyros, Kos
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.wind_desc: From mid-May to mid-September the meltemi blows — a dry northerly to north-westerly that usually eases by evening but can last several days; strong and gusty in July–August. The Rhodes → Kos leg is almost always upwind — allow spare time. Some bays are open to southerlies.
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.route: Rhodes (Mandraki) — Symi — Nisyros — Kos — Tilos — Halki — Rhodes, ~170 miles in a week; calmer — a short loop Rhodes — Symi (Pedi, the bays) — Rhodes
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.mooring: Rhodes Marina (~600 berths) is modern but expensive and windy, and far from the Old Town; part of the fleet is based in Mandraki. On Symi — mooring buoys on the town quay (cramped, ferry wash, expensive) or quiet Pedi marina; on Tilos and Halki berths are scarce and you sometimes have to anchor.
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, a second experienced crew member and a sailing CV. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: Airport 14 km from the marina, many direct flights
Rhodes Old Town and Symi harbour
Uncrowded Tilos and Halki
Long season, warm water until October
cons: Long exposed passages (20–36 miles)
Strong meltemi in July–August, an upwind leg to Kos
Expensive Rhodes marina and cramped Symi harbour
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.charter_price_note: Typical range in Greece for 40–45 ft per week: high season €4,000–5,500, low season €2,500–4,000; in Rhodes a Dufour 430 GL from ~$290 a day and a Bavaria 46 from ~$310 a day in cheap weeks; cheapest in March, most expensive in June–August
rhodes-dodecanese-symi.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food
school_notes: Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian version of the site: yachts at Rhodes Marina and Mandraki, a one-week route

volos-skiathos-sporades.description: From Volos, across the calm Pagasetic Gulf, crews sail to the Northern Sporades — green Skiathos, Skopelos and Alonissos with its marine park. The wind is usually moderate, the islands close together and coves plentiful — a good area for a relaxed week and a first charter, though the meltemi can be fresh in July–August.
volos-skiathos-sporades.rating_basis: The Northern Sporades are loved for their pine-clad green islands, beaches and the Alonissos National Marine Park; 12 Knots describes Volos as a suitable base for inexperienced skippers (moderate wind, simple navigation), with a warning about the meltemi in July–August. The area is less hyped than the Ionian and Cyclades.
volos-skiathos-sporades.hazards: Meltemi gusts under the high islands and Mount Pelion; in the Alonissos National Marine Park entry and mooring are restricted in certain zones — check with the charter company; ferries and fast craft off Skiathos and Skopelos.
volos-skiathos-sporades.crowd_note: Skiathos harbour and Skopelos town are busy in summer; the coves of Alonissos and the Pagasetic Gulf are much quieter.
volos-skiathos-sporades.region: Aegean Sea: Pagasetic Gulf, Skiathos, Skopelos, Alonissos
volos-skiathos-sporades.wind_desc: The Pagasetic Gulf usually has force 3–4 and calm water. In summer the meltemi blows around the Sporades — a north-easterly of force 4–7, gentler than in the Cyclades but gusty under the high islands and the mainland; in July–August it can be hard going for the inexperienced. In spring and autumn the wind is lighter and the air cooler.
volos-skiathos-sporades.route: Volos — Pagasetic Gulf (Trikeri) — Skiathos — Skopelos (Panormos, Loutraki) — Alonissos (Steni Vala, Patitiri) — Skopelos town — Skiathos — Volos
volos-skiathos-sporades.mooring: The fleet is based in Volos harbour and on Skiathos (Skiathos has no marina as such — it's the town port). On the islands — town quays, stern-to with your anchor (in Greece ~€20–70 a night, often less), and lots of green coves for anchoring with a line ashore.
volos-skiathos-sporades.licence: For bareboat: ICC, RYA or IYT Coastal Skipper or higher, or a national licence (EU licences with a certified translation; non-EU licences, including Russian ones, subject to the charter company's agreement). You need the original certificate, a VHF certificate, a second experienced crew member and a sailing CV. IYT Bareboat Skipper and other certificates are at the charter company's discretion.
pros: The calm Pagasetic Gulf for the first days
Green islands with pines and beaches
Alonissos marine park, a chance to see dolphins
Fewer charter crowds than in the Saronic
cons: Awkward logistics: Volos airport has few flights, ~2.5 h from Thessaloniki
Gusty meltemi in July–August
Short season, water cooler than in southern Greece
volos-skiathos-sporades.airport: VOL — Volos (Nea Anchialos), ~30 min; SKG — Thessaloniki, ~2.5 h
volos-skiathos-sporades.charter_price_note: Typical range in Greece for 40–45 ft per week: high season €4,000–5,500, low season €2,500–4,000; in Volos a Sun Odyssey 410 from ~$360 a day, on Skiathos an Oceanis 41.1 from ~$230 a day in cheap weeks
volos-skiathos-sporades.skipper_price_note: Skipper in Greece €1,200–1,800 a week (~€170–260 a day) plus food
school_notes: Charter aggregator and sailing school with a Russian website and Russian phone number: yachts in Volos (~215), Skiathos and Skopelos

dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.description: Croatia's southernmost charter area: from Komolac near Dubrovnik you reach the Elaphiti Islands in an hour, then Mljet with the saltwater lakes of its national park, medieval Korčula and Ston on Pelješac. Passages are short, but the legs to Mljet and Korčula cross open water. Suits a first week and anyone who wants to combine sailing with old towns.
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.rating_basis: Guides and aggregators (12 Knots, Borrow a Boat) call the Dubrovnik — Elaphiti — Mljet — Korčula route easy and one of the most scenic in Croatia: Mljet National Park and the old towns of Dubrovnik, Korčula and Ston. 12 Knots lists about 325 boats in Dubrovnik. Downsides — expensive marinas near Dubrovnik and cruise-ship crowds in town.
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.hazards: Jugo with big seas on the passages to Mljet and Lastovo; bora off Pelješac; ferries and cruise liners off Gruž and Dubrovnik; in Mljet National Park anchor only in designated places; to Montenegro only after clearing out (Cavtat) and clearing in.
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.crowd_note: In July–August it is cramped near Dubrovnik, in Polače and Pomena on Mljet and in Korčula — claim a spot before midday; Šipan and Lopud are calmer.
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.region: Southern Dalmatia: the Elaphiti Islands (Koločep, Lopud, Šipan), Mljet, Korčula, Pelješac (Ston), Cavtat
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.wind_desc: In summer the maestral (north-west) in the afternoon, stronger in the channels off Pelješac. In the southern Adriatic the jugo (south-east) blows more often than in the north: warm and humid, it builds over a day and can last several days, in autumn up to 40–50 kn with big seas. The bora can be fierce off Pelješac, mostly outside summer.
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.route: Dubrovnik (Komolac) — Šipan (Šipanska Luka) — Mljet (Polače, national park) — Korčula — Ston (Pelješac) — Lopud or Koločep — Dubrovnik, ~115 miles in a week
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.mooring: ACI Dubrovnik in Komolac about €187 a night for 13 m (2026), Frapa in Gruž €133. On Mljet: Pomena marina €80–100 for 12 m, often including the national park ticket; buoys in Polače €60–80; national park entry about €25 per person per day. On Šipan, Lopud and in Okuklje restaurant buoys are free if you dine.
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence on the official list of the Croatian Ministry of the Sea — ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and higher, many national licences; Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licences are on the list (sailing categories — yachts up to 100 GT in the Adriatic). Plus a VHF radio operator's certificate (VHF SRC): all charter boats carry a radio. Without a licence — skippered only.
pros: Dubrovnik, Korčula and Ston — old towns straight from the water
Mljet National Park: lakes, forest, quiet coves
Restaurant buoys on the Elaphiti and Mljet
The route can be extended to Montenegro
cons: Expensive marinas near Dubrovnik (about €190 a night)
Smaller fleet than in Split — book ahead
The jugo kicks up seas on open passages
Russian citizens need a Schengen visa
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.charter_price_note: Guide price for 40–45 ft per week at 2026 Croatian prices (July–August / May or October); no separate statistics for Dubrovnik. The fleet is smaller than in Split — book ahead for summer
dubrovnik-elaphiti-mljet.skipper_price_note: Skipper €150–250 a day, plus their food
highlights: Dubrovnik Summer Festival: theatre and concerts in the Old Town
school_notes: Aggregator with Russian-speaking support: about 325 boats in Dubrovnik, skippers, a one-week route
Charter based at ACI Dubrovnik, ISPA sailing school

murter-kornati.description: Murter is the gateway to Kornati National Park: about 90 bare stone islands with restaurants by their jetties, plus Telašćica Nature Park and the Krka waterfalls at Skradin nearby. Passages are short, but rocks are many and infrastructure scarce: water, shops and fuel are only available in marinas and villages. For those seeking peace and nature; for a first week, take a skipper or navigate carefully.
murter-kornati.rating_basis: The Kornati are one of the Adriatic's great nature routes: the national park's deserted stone archipelago, restaurant jetties, with Telašćica and the Krka waterfalls nearby. 12 Knots lists about 200 boats on Murter. Aggregators note fewer crowds than around Split and low off-season prices; downsides — few shops and little water, paid park entry.
murter-kornati.hazards: Many exposed and submerged rocks and shoals between the Kornati islands — careful chart navigation needed; the bora strikes suddenly in gusts; steep seas on the outer side of the archipelago in a jugo; the swing bridge in the canal at Tisno opens on a schedule.
murter-kornati.crowd_note: The fleet is smaller than in Split; in July–August claim restaurant buoys and berths at ACI Piškera and Žut before evening; June and September are quiet.
murter-kornati.region: Adriatic: Kornati, Žut, Telašćica (Dugi Otok), the Šibenik archipelago, Krka
murter-kornati.wind_desc: In summer the maestral — a north-westerly afternoon breeze that dies down by sunset, calm in the morning. The bora (north-east) arrives suddenly and in gusts, mostly in spring, autumn and winter, in summer usually for 1–2 days. The autumn jugo (south-east) drives open-sea swell onto the outer side of the Kornati.
murter-kornati.route: Murter (Hramina) — Žut — Telašćica (Dugi Otok, Mir salt lake) — Sali — Piškera (Kornati) — Kaprije or Zlarin — Skradin (Krka river) — Murter, ~100 miles in a week
murter-kornati.mooring: In the Kornati — ACI Piškera and Žut marinas (€124–136 a night for 13 m, 2024), restaurant jetties and buoys in the bays. Kornati National Park charges a per-boat entry ticket — roughly €40–80 a day depending on length and season. On Murter — Hramina, Betina and Jezera marinas; Telašćica has buoys and a nature park entry fee.
murter-kornati.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence on the official list of the Croatian Ministry of the Sea — ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and higher, many national licences; Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licences are on the list (sailing categories — yachts up to 100 GT in the Adriatic). Plus a VHF radio operator's certificate (VHF SRC): all charter boats carry a radio. Without a licence — skippered only.
pros: The wild Kornati landscape and quiet coves
Short passages and plenty of shelter
Cheaper than Split, especially in May and October
Krka and Telašćica nearby
cons: Paid entry to Kornati National Park and Telašćica
Few shops, little water and fuel in the archipelago
Restaurant jetties assume you'll dine at the restaurant
Russian citizens need a Schengen visa
murter-kornati.airport: ZAD — Zadar, ~1 h; SPU — Split, ~1 h 15 min
murter-kornati.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: July–August / May. Example: Sun Odyssey 410 (2021) from Hramina marina — €1,250–1,450 October to April, €1,700–2,050 in May, €3,000–3,500 in summer
murter-kornati.skipper_price_note: Skipper €150–250 a day, plus their food
school_notes: Aggregator with Russian-speaking support: about 200 boats on Murter, skippers
Charter company based at Hramina marina
Russian-language sailing course platform: IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and Coastal Skipper starting in Pirovac (10 km from Murter)

pula-istria-kvarner.description: The southern tip of Istria and the Kvarner islands: Cres, Lošinj, Unije, Susak, Ilovik. Passages are longer than in Dalmatia, some across the open Kvarner, but the coves are quieter and prices lower. Suits experienced crews and those driving down from Europe; beginners should take a skipper.
pula-istria-kvarner.rating_basis: A less hyped but peaceful area: 12 Knots lists about 370 boats in Pula, and off-season prices are among the lowest in Croatia. Pluses — Lošinj, Susak and Cres, quiet coves, an easy drive from Central Europe; minuses — the bora in the Kvarner, long open passages and cool water at the start and end of the season.
pula-istria-kvarner.hazards: The bora in the Kvarner and Kvarnerić — the strongest in the Adriatic, and gusty; tramontana with cold fronts; open passages from Istria to Unije and Cres; the autumn jugo with big seas.
pula-istria-kvarner.crowd_note: Even in August it is quieter than Dalmatia; Istria's busiest period is June to mid-September.
pula-istria-kvarner.region: Northern Adriatic: southern Istria (Medulin, Kamenjak), Kvarner — Cres, Lošinj, Unije, Susak, Ilovik
pula-istria-kvarner.wind_desc: In summer a moderate north-westerly maestral by day and a light land breeze at night. The Kvarner has the Adriatic's strongest bora: the north-easterly strikes suddenly and in gusts, lasting up to a week in winter and usually 1–2 days in summer. Cold fronts bring tramontana; in autumn the jugo, up to 40–50 kn, builds big seas.
pula-istria-kvarner.route: Pula (Veruda) — Medulin / Cape Kamenjak — Unije — Mali Lošinj — Ilovik — Susak — Cres (Osor) — Rabac — Pula, ~130 miles in a week
pula-istria-kvarner.mooring: In Pula — Veruda marina and ACI Pula (€98–114 a night for 13 m, 2024); Istria's ACI marinas average €110–250 in 2026 (Rovinj is the most expensive), Kvarner's €100–137 (Cres). On the islands — town quays in Mali Lošinj, Unije, Susak and Ilovik (€3.5–5.5/m) and paid buoys in the bays.
pula-istria-kvarner.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence on the official list of the Croatian Ministry of the Sea — ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and higher, many national licences; Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licences are on the list (sailing categories — yachts up to 100 GT in the Adriatic). Plus a VHF radio operator's certificate (VHF SRC): all charter boats carry a radio. Without a licence — skippered only.
pros: Low off-season prices (from €1,200 a week)
Fewer crowds than in Dalmatia
Lošinj, Susak, Cres — quiet islands and coves
Pula airport 15 minutes away, easy to reach by car
cons: The Kvarner bora is strong and sudden
Longer open-water passages
Cooler water in May and October
Russian citizens need a Schengen visa
pula-istria-kvarner.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: July–August / May. Example: Sun Odyssey 410 (2019) from Veruda marina — €1,200 October to April, €1,600–1,900 in May, €3,300–3,600 in summer
pula-istria-kvarner.skipper_price_note: Skipper €150–250 a day, plus their food
highlights: Film festival in Pula's Roman amphitheatre
school_notes: Aggregator with Russian-speaking support: about 370 boats in Pula, skippers
Charter based at ACI Pomer near Pula, ISPA sailing school

split-central-dalmatia.description: The Adriatic's main charter area: from Split and Kaštela it takes 2–4 hours to reach Brač, Hvar, the Pakleni Islands, Šolta and Vis. Hops between islands are short, the summer maestral is predictable, and marinas, town quays and buoyed coves are plentiful. Suits a first bareboat week, a course or a skippered cruise; experienced crews can head out to Vis and Biševo.
split-central-dalmatia.rating_basis: Croatia's most popular charter area: 12 Knots lists more than 1,800 boats in Split, Kaštela and Trogir combined. Guides and aggregators (12 Knots, Borrow a Boat, Skippercity) call the Brač — Hvar — Vis loop the classic first week: short passages, a steady maestral, plenty of marinas and coves. Reviews complain about crowds and prices in July–August.
split-central-dalmatia.hazards: Ferries and fast catamarans in the Split and Hvar channels; the bora with sudden gusts in spring and autumn; the autumn jugo with big seas; overcrowded coves in summer — easy to snag someone else's anchor chain.
split-central-dalmatia.crowd_note: In July–August berths in Hvar, Palmižana and Komiža are taken by midday, and there is a queue at the Blue Cave from the morning; June and September are much quieter.
split-central-dalmatia.region: Adriatic: Brač, Hvar, the Pakleni Islands, Vis, Šolta, Korčula
split-central-dalmatia.wind_desc: In summer the maestral — a north-westerly breeze that builds towards midday and dies at sunset, usually 10–20 kn, stronger in the channels off Brač and Hvar; often calm in the morning, and August can be light. In spring and autumn the bora (north-east, sudden gusts) and the jugo (south-east, builds over 2–3 days, up to 40–50 kn with big seas in autumn) are more common. Off the outer islands of Vis and Biševo a strong maestral raises steep seas.
split-central-dalmatia.route: Split — Brač (Pučišća or Milna) — Hvar (Vrboska, Stari Grad) — Vis (Komiža, Blue Cave on Biševo) — Vis town — Šolta (Stomorska or Maslinica) — Split, ~125 miles in a week; a variant via the Pakleni Islands and Korčula
split-central-dalmatia.mooring: ACI and private marinas: ACI Split about €190 a night for 13 m in the 2026 season, Central Dalmatia's ACI marinas average €130–190; Hvar town from €120 for 40 ft in summer. Town quays €3.5–5.5/m, paid buoys in the bays €2–4/m (up to €60 in Komiža), restaurant buoys free if you dine. Catamarans usually pay double.
split-central-dalmatia.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence on the official list of the Croatian Ministry of the Sea — ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and higher, many national licences; Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licences are on the list (sailing categories — yachts up to 100 GT in the Adriatic). Plus a VHF radio operator's certificate (VHF SRC): all charter boats carry a radio. Without a licence — skippered only.
pros: Short passages, islands within sight of each other
A predictable daytime maestral in summer
Huge choice of boats, airport 30 minutes away
Plenty of marinas, town quays and buoyed coves
Russian GIMS licences are on the official recognised list
cons: Crowds and expensive marinas in July–August (ACI Split about €190 a night)
You pay almost everywhere: buoys, town quays, concession anchorages
August is often calm, with more motoring
Russian citizens need a Schengen visa
split-central-dalmatia.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: July–August / May or October. Example: Sun Odyssey 410 (2025) at ACI Split — €2,570 off-season, €3,140 in May, €4,200–4,700 in summer; older boats are cheaper. Plus a mandatory package (cleaning, linen, tourist tax) of €100–400
split-central-dalmatia.skipper_price_note: Skipper €150–250 a day, plus their food
highlights: Split Summer Festival: opera and theatre in Diocletian's Palace
school_notes: Aggregator with Russian-speaking support: about 530 boats in Split, 380 in Kaštela, 900 in Trogir; skippers, routes
Charter from Split (ACI Split, Trogir), ISPA sailing school
International charter company in Marina near Trogir, one-week routes

zadar-northern-dalmatia.description: Sukošan near Zadar is one of the Adriatic's largest charter bases, 15 minutes from the airport. From here crews head into the Zadar archipelago: Ugljan, Pašman, Dugi Otok with Telašćica bay, the quiet car-free islands of Silba, Olib and Molat, and south to the Kornati. Suits a relaxed first week and anyone looking for fewer crowds than around Split.
zadar-northern-dalmatia.rating_basis: Croatia's second-largest charter zone: 12 Knots lists about 540 boats in Sukošan and about 200 in Zadar. Routes are calmer and cheaper than around Split, with the Kornati and Telašćica nearby and northern islands (Silba, Olib, Molat) free of cars and crowds. Downsides — fewer famous towns and less nightlife, the bora off the Velebit.
zadar-northern-dalmatia.hazards: The bora at Maslenica, in Nin bay and under the Velebit; current and short chop in the Zadar Channel in a jugo; ferries between Zadar and the islands; rocks and shoals off the outer islands and in the Kornati.
zadar-northern-dalmatia.crowd_note: Even in August you can usually find a spot on the northern islands and in Telašćica; it gets cramped in the Kornati and at Sali in peak weeks.
zadar-northern-dalmatia.region: Adriatic: Ugljan, Pašman, Dugi Otok (Telašćica), Molat, Silba, Olib, Kornati
zadar-northern-dalmatia.wind_desc: In summer the maestral (north-west) in the afternoon, calm in the morning. The bora off the Velebit is strongest at Maslenica and in Nin bay, with sudden gusts; mostly in spring, autumn and winter, in summer usually for 1–2 days. In a jugo (south-east) the Zadar Channel has a strong current and short chop.
zadar-northern-dalmatia.route: Sukošan — Pašman — Telašćica (Dugi Otok) — Sali — Božava — Silba or Olib — Molat — Zadar — Sukošan, ~110 miles in a week; a southern variant — the Kornati and Žut
zadar-northern-dalmatia.mooring: D-Marin Dalmacija is Croatia's largest marina (about 1,200 berths), €105–140 a night for 13 m (2024); marinas in Zadar, Biograd and on Ugljan. Town quays in Sali, Božava and on Silba €3.5–5.5/m, buoys in the bays €2–4/m; park entry fees in Telašćica and the Kornati.
zadar-northern-dalmatia.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence on the official list of the Croatian Ministry of the Sea — ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and higher, many national licences; Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licences are on the list (sailing categories — yachts up to 100 GT in the Adriatic). Plus a VHF radio operator's certificate (VHF SRC): all charter boats carry a radio. Without a licence — skippered only.
pros: Wide choice of boats, airport 15 minutes away
Calm channels and many sheltered coves
Northern islands without cars or crowds
The Kornati and Telašćica nearby
cons: The bora off the Velebit — sudden gusts
Less nightlife and fewer famous towns
Entry fees for the Kornati and Telašćica
Russian citizens need a Schengen visa
zadar-northern-dalmatia.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: July–August / May or October. Example: Sun Odyssey 410 (2023) in nearby Biograd — €1,700–1,900 in October, €2,000–3,000 in May, €4,400–4,900 in July–August; older boats are cheaper
zadar-northern-dalmatia.skipper_price_note: Skipper €150–250 a day, plus their food
school_notes: Aggregator with Russian-speaking support: about 540 boats in Sukošan and 200 in Zadar, skippers
Russian-language sailing course platform: introductory IYT courses starting in Zadar, RYA Start Yachting in Biograd

tivat-bay-of-kotor.description: The Bay of Kotor (Boka Kotorska) is a winding bay among mountains with Kotor, Perast and Herceg Novi; the base is Porto Montenegro marina in Tivat, 5 minutes from the airport. Inside the bay the water is calm — handy for training and family sailing; outside lie Luštica, Budva and the open coast, and you can reach Dubrovnik. Russian citizens don't need a visa (up to 30 days).
tivat-bay-of-kotor.rating_basis: A small but growing area: 12 Knots lists about 73 boats in Montenegro, 47 of them in Tivat. Sailors praise the fjord-like scenery of the Boka, Kotor and Perast, duty-free fuel and calm water for training; downsides — few one-week routes, expensive marinas, an exposed coast outside the bay with few harbours.
tivat-bay-of-kotor.hazards: Speed limit of 12 kn in the Boka and 8 kn in the Kumbor and Verige straits; cruise liners turn off Kotor; military and border boats call on channel 16 — you must answer; crossing from Croatia only with border clearance (clear out in Cavtat, clear in at Zelenika, Tivat, Kotor or Bar); jugo and swell on the open coast.
tivat-bay-of-kotor.crowd_note: In July–August it is cramped off Kotor (cruise liners) and Perast; the coves of Luštica and Herceg Novi are quieter. May, June and September are calm and cheaper.
tivat-bay-of-kotor.region: Southern Adriatic: Bay of Kotor (Kotor, Perast, Herceg Novi), Luštica, the Budva Riviera
tivat-bay-of-kotor.wind_desc: Inside the bay summer brings light variable breezes, often calm in the morning, and little wind in August. In spring and autumn the bora (north) or jugo (south-east), which usually ease after midday — the best time for regattas; in the narrows at Verige and Kotor gusts can exceed 30 kn in a storm. Outside the bay it is open sea, with steep seas in a jugo. November–January are the wettest months.
tivat-bay-of-kotor.route: Tivat — Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks (Gospa od Škrpjela) — Kotor — Herceg Novi or Rose bay — Luštica coves — Budva — Bigova — Tivat, ~90 miles in a week; a variant — Cavtat and Dubrovnik with border clearance
tivat-bay-of-kotor.mooring: Porto Montenegro is a superyacht marina, from €100 a night according to sailors' reports; Kotor marina €50–70 per 2017–2023 reports (catamaran +50%); quays in Prčanj and Herceg Novi, buoys in Rose, Portonovi and Luštica Bay marinas. Outside the bay shelter is scarce — Budva, Bar. A yacht needs a vignette (cruising permit; €27–98 a week according to reports) — check with the charter company whether it is included. Duty-free diesel about €1.1–1.4 a litre.
tivat-bay-of-kotor.licence: For bareboat, charter companies require an international licence: ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper and higher, or a recognised national licence, plus a VHF radio operator's certificate (VHF SRC). Whether Russian GIMS licences are accepted — check with the charter company. Without a licence — skippered only.
pros: Visa-free for Russian citizens (up to 30 days)
Calm water inside the bay — good for training
Kotor, Perast and the mountains straight from the water
Duty-free diesel
Russian-speaking skippers and schools
cons: A small area: few one-week routes
Expensive marinas, the vignette and border formalities when visiting Croatia
Few sheltered harbours outside the bay
Hot with little wind in summer
tivat-bay-of-kotor.airport: TIV — Tivat, ~5 min; DBV — Dubrovnik, ~1 h + border; TGD — Podgorica, ~1.5 h
tivat-bay-of-kotor.course_price_note: IYT Bareboat Skipper (sail) at Sail Band school, Porto Montenegro: 10 days living aboard, taught in Russian or English
tivat-bay-of-kotor.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: July–August / spring and autumn. Example: Oceanis 45 and Bavaria C42 in Montenegro — €1,840 off-season, €3,750–4,750 at peak; Lucia 40 catamaran — €2,300–5,600
highlights: Fašinada at Perast: a procession of boats to Our Lady of the Rocks and a regatta (22 July)
school_notes: Russian-language school: IYT Bareboat Skipper practical in Montenegro (10 days); charter of about 73 boats
IYT school in Porto Montenegro, taught in Russian and English; the link goes to an Adriacom review, the school's own website not verified
Marina yacht club: RYA Powerboat Level 2 courses, regattas

saint-martin-marigot.description: A triangle of three islands and three jurisdictions: French and Dutch St Martin, glamorous St Barths and quiet Anguilla with its white beaches. 15–20-mile open-sea passages with Atlantic swell — for experienced crews who find the BVI a bit tame.
saint-martin-marigot.rating_basis: Valued for three countries and three cuisines in a week, St Barths and Anguilla's empty beaches (Sail Magazine, All At Sea, Moorings); passages are longer and more exposed than in the BVI, plus customs and Anguilla's expensive permit — hence rated slightly below the BVI.
saint-martin-marigot.hazards: Hurricanes (June–November, peak August–October), northerly swell in winter in the open bays of Anguilla and Marigot, reefs off Tintamarre and shallows around Anguilla, Atlantic seas in the St Barths channel, night sailing prohibited; the bridges near the airport and into Simpson Bay Lagoon open on a schedule.
saint-martin-marigot.crowd_note: Gustavia and Colombier fill up in December–March, especially over the holidays and during regattas; Anguilla and Tintamarre are much quieter.
saint-martin-marigot.region: Caribbean, Leeward Islands: Saint-Martin / Sint Maarten, Anguilla, Saint-Barthélemy (St Barths), Tintamarre
saint-martin-marigot.wind_desc: North-east to east trades of 10–25 kn; most steady from December to April (winter brings 20–25 kn “Christmas winds” and northerly swell); in summer the wind is lighter and gustier in squalls; September–October is the peak of hurricane season.
saint-martin-marigot.route: Marigot — Orient Bay / Pinel — Tintamarre — Gustavia (St Barths) — Anse de Colombier — Philipsburg — Anguilla (Road Bay, Crocus Bay, Prickly Pear) — Marigot, ~80 miles in a week
saint-martin-marigot.mooring: Fort Louis marina (150 berths; about €47 a night for 14 m, seasonal rates), Anse Marcel; in St Barths the Gustavia outer anchorage ~€40 a night, buoys at Colombier ~€10; in Anguilla clear in at Road Bay first, then a paid cruising permit is required (by tonnage, per day/week); marine park buoys are included in the permit.
saint-martin-marigot.licence: On the French side no official licence is required for sailing bareboat: Dream Yacht Charter states plainly that no licence is needed — your CV and the briefing decide; some agencies ask for ICC/RYA/ASA — check with the charter company. Night passages are prohibited. Saint-Martin, Sint Maarten, Anguilla and St Barths are separate jurisdictions: customs clearance and passports on every crossing.
pros: Variety: French cuisine, St Barths, Anguilla's empty beaches
Direct flights from Europe (Paris) and the US to SXM
Steady trades in winter
Colombier bay with turtles and snorkelling
cons: Open-sea passages with swell — not for a first charter
Customs on every island, Anguilla's expensive cruising permit
Pricey St Barths
Hurricane season July–November (Irma devastated the island in 2017)
saint-martin-marigot.airport: SXM — Princess Juliana (Sint Maarten), ~25–30 min to Marigot / Anse Marcel
saint-martin-marigot.charter_price_note: Bareboat monohull per week: December–April / September–November, converted from $2,500–5,000 (WiYachts, base price without fees); at 12knots 41–46 ft boats from ~$340–450 a day
highlights: St. Maarten Heineken Regatta
Les Voiles de Saint-Barth
New Year in Gustavia roads — a gathering of superyachts
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~100 boats in Anse Marcel and Marigot, prices by month
Moorings and Sunsail base at Fort Louis marina (Marigot)
Base at Anse Marcel marina, bareboat and cabin cruises to St Barths

nosy-be-madagascar.description: The tropical islands of north-west Madagascar: empty beaches, fishing villages, lemurs and corals, 10–35-mile passages. This is expedition chartering for an experienced crew or a group with a skipper; the season is the dry months from May to October.
nosy-be-madagascar.rating_basis: Wild and exotic: empty islands, villages, lemurs, corals and hardly any other yachts. Fleets are small and charter companies few; guides warn about poor navigation marks, unreliable forecasts and currents, and advise taking a skipper.
nosy-be-madagascar.hazards: Reefs and shallows with almost no navigation marks, inaccurate charts, strong currents and at times heavy swell, unreliable forecasts; tropical cyclones in the rainy season; malaria — prophylaxis needed.
nosy-be-madagascar.crowd_note: Hardly any other yachts even in the dry season.
nosy-be-madagascar.region: North-west Madagascar: Nosy Komba, Tanikely, Iranja, the Mitsio and Radama archipelagos
nosy-be-madagascar.wind_desc: Dry season May–October: the easterly trades gradually strengthen to 15–20 kn; the Tsaratanana massif partly shelters Nosy Be from strong north-easterlies. November–April is the hot, rainy season (300–390 mm of rain in December–March), with light variable winds, thunderstorms and a risk of tropical cyclones.
nosy-be-madagascar.route: Hell-Ville (Nosy Be) — Nosy Tanikely — Mamoko — Russian Bay — Nosy Iranja — Nosy Kalakajoro — Radama archipelago (Nosy Antsanimora) — Baramahamay Bay — Nosy Be; to the north Nosy Komba and the Mitsio archipelago
nosy-be-madagascar.mooring: There are no proper marinas: charter boats are based in Hell-Ville harbour and Crater Bay (Marina Crater); beyond that it's anchoring only, off empty islands and villages; fuel, water and provisions in Hell-Ville. Buoys and navigation marks are almost non-existent.
nosy-be-madagascar.licence: For bareboat, charter companies require a valid yacht skipper's certificate (Madagascar is on the list of countries where a licence is needed, not just a sailing CV). Because of the poor navigation infrastructure many take a skipper or a crewed yacht.
pros: Hardly any other yachts
Wildlife: lemurs, corals, whales in the channel
Dry season with steady trades May–October
Cheap ashore
cons: Few charter companies and a small fleet
Almost no buoys or lighthouses, unreliable forecasts
Rainy and cyclone season December–March
Malaria, limited medical care, a long flight
nosy-be-madagascar.charter_price_note: 12 Knots' average weekly price for a 40–50 ft yacht in Nosy Be: May–July / November–March; the fleet is mostly catamarans, bareboat from ~$470 a day, many boats crewed only
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: crewed catamarans and yachts in Nosy Be, cabin cruises

la-paz-sea-of-cortez.description: Desert islands in the Gulf of California, 30 minutes' sail from La Paz: red cliffs, white sand coves, the sea lion colony at Los Islotes, dolphins and whale sharks. There are no marinas outside town, every night is spent at anchor and there is almost no phone signal. For crews who want wildlife and silence rather than waterfront restaurants; beginners should take a skipper.
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.rating_basis: SAIL, Cruising World and Yachting praise the deserted coves, desert scenery and marine life (sea lions, whale sharks, dolphins). In 2025 The Moorings arrived alongside Dream Yacht. Reviews mention no signal or shops, harsh northers in winter and summer heat.
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.hazards: Northerly “nortes” with steep seas; unmarked reefs and shoals around the islands (especially further north, near Agua Verde); hurricanes July–October (Odile in 2014 and Norma in 2023 damaged marinas); night passages prohibited; port closures in strong winds; aggressive bull sea lions when snorkelling; stingrays in the shallows.
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.crowd_note: Lots of coves and a small fleet (a few dozen boats, mostly catamarans); it only gets crowded at Balandra and Los Islotes by day, when tour boats arrive.
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.region: Gulf of California: Espíritu Santo, Partida, San Francisco, San José
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.wind_desc: From November to April the northerly “nortes” blow: usually 10–20 kn, but several times each winter they hold at 20–30 kn for 2–3 days with a short, steep sea. Spring winds are moderate, summer winds light, with a southerly “coromuel” in the evenings. July–October brings heat above 35 °C and the Pacific hurricane season.
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.route: La Paz (CostaBaja) — Ensenada Grande (Partida) — San Evaristo — Isla San Francisco — San José (Amortajada) — Espíritu Santo — Balandra — La Paz, ~120 miles in a week
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.mooring: Marinas only in La Paz (CostaBaja, Marina de La Paz, Palmira, Cortez). The islands have no marinas or buoys: you spend the night at anchor in sandy coves, free of charge. Espíritu Santo National Park requires a permit (about $9 per person per day, arranged by the charter company). Overnight anchoring in Balandra bay is prohibited. In a strong norte the harbour master closes the port.
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.licence: Mexico requires no licence for bareboat: charter companies ask for a sailing CV covering the last 2–3 years (independent skippering experience). Night passages are prohibited, and the float plan is filed with the harbour master through the charter company. Fishing requires a Mexican fishing licence (issued online).
pros: Deserted coves, all stops at anchor and free
Marine life: sea lions, dolphins, whale sharks, snorkelling
Warm water and a dry climate, little rain November to June
Bareboat without a mandatory licence — a CV is enough
cons: Winter nortes of 20–30 kn lasting several days
July–October — heat and hurricanes
No signal in about 70% of the area, no shops or marinas outside La Paz
Few monohulls, the fleet is mostly catamarans
A long and expensive flight from Europe
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.airport: LAP — La Paz, ~30 min; SJD — Los Cabos, 2.5–3 h
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.charter_price_note: 44 ft bareboat (Sun Odyssey 449) per week: March–April / June–September (about $5,800 / $2,960); plus mandatory fees of about $530. Most of the fleet is catamarans
la-paz-sea-of-cortez.skipper_price_note: Skipper about $196 a day, plus food and a separate cabin
highlights: Whale sharks in La Paz Bay
school_notes: La Paz's largest charter company, based at CostaBaja marina: bareboat, skippers, cabin cruises
Aggregator with Russian-speaking support: about 34 boats in La Paz, routes
Charter agency, boats from various operators

noumea-southern-lagoon.description: A vast coral lagoon in southern New Caledonia: white-sand islets off Nouméa, the quiet Baie de Prony, araucaria pines and the coves of the Île des Pins. Suits an experienced crew on a catamaran looking for empty anchorages; the best months are May–June and September–November.
noumea-southern-lagoon.rating_basis: One of the largest lagoons in the world (UNESCO, 2008): sheltered water, the empty coves of Prony and the white sand of the Île des Pins; Dream Yacht has a base in Nouméa. Downsides according to guides — inaccurate charts in remote areas, fresh trades, few charter boats and an expensive flight.
noumea-southern-lagoon.hazards: Coral reefs and heads in the lagoon, inaccurate electronic charts and Google Maps coordinates in remote areas, tricky reef passes, fresh trades on open stretches, tropical cyclones December–April, rules for approaching whales.
noumea-southern-lagoon.crowd_note: Few yachts — it only gets crowded in Nouméa roads and at Îlot Maître and Amédée at weekends, when local boats head out.
noumea-southern-lagoon.region: Southern Lagoon (UNESCO site): Îlot Maître and Amédée, Baie de Prony, Île Ouen, Île des Pins
noumea-southern-lagoon.wind_desc: A south-east trade wind blows almost all year; on open stretches of the lagoon it can be fresh. June–August is the cool dry season (air 23–24 °C), with occasional fronts. September–October are the driest months. December–April is the hot, humid season and cyclone season (winds over 100 km/h; the most recent was Niran in March 2021).
noumea-southern-lagoon.route: Nouméa (Port Moselle) — Îlot Maître or Amédée lighthouse — Baie de Prony — Île Ouen — Île des Pins (Kuto and Kanumera bays) — back via Prony to Nouméa
noumea-southern-lagoon.mooring: Port Moselle in central Nouméa (depths up to 8 m; no advance bookings — call Port Moselle Control on channel 67 on approach; the anchorage in front of the marina is full of buoys) and Port du Sud; in the lagoon — anchorages sheltered from any wind (Prony, Ouen) and buoys at popular islets.
noumea-southern-lagoon.licence: No special official certificate is usually required for a sailing yacht (as in Oceania generally) — the charter company assesses your experience from your sailing CV. Check Dream Yacht's and local companies' requirements when booking.
pros: A huge sheltered lagoon with anchorages for any wind
Few yachts, empty coves
Île des Pins with white beaches and araucarias
Whales in July–September
cons: December–April — cyclone season
Fresh trades on open stretches of the lagoon
A small charter fleet, mostly catamarans
An expensive flight and prices in Pacific francs
noumea-southern-lagoon.charter_price_note: 12 Knots' average weekly price for a 40–50 ft yacht (mostly catamarans): October / February; Bali 4.1 from $672 a day; few monohulls
highlights: Humpback whales in the Southern Lagoon (approach only at the required distance)
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: catamarans at Port Moselle, Nouméa

linton-bay-san-blas.description: More than 300 low, palm-fringed coral islets off Panama's Caribbean coast, governed by the Guna people: turquoise lagoons, reefs, stilt villages, and no hotels or restaurants. Boats go out almost exclusively with crew — the skipper threads the boat between the reefs, the hostess cooks. For anyone after “desert islands” and snorkelling; the best time is the dry season, December to April.
linton-bay-san-blas.rating_basis: San Blas is known as one of the most unspoilt archipelagos in the Caribbean: hundreds of palm-topped coral islets and Guna culture. 12 Knots names December–April as the best months (safest in February–March). Reviews mention almost no bareboat or infrastructure, and rain and thunderstorms from May to November.
linton-bay-san-blas.hazards: Reefs and shoals, charts offset in places — eyeball navigation with the sun high and local pilot guides; strong trades and swell outside the reefs in December–February; lightning storms and squalls in the rainy season; no medical help on the islands; lobster catching and fishing are banned without Guna permission.
linton-bay-san-blas.crowd_note: Yachts are few, but the Cayos Holandeses and Chichime get busy by day with tour boats from Cartí; at the outer islands you can have an anchorage to yourself.
linton-bay-san-blas.region: Panama's Caribbean coast: San Blas archipelago, the Guna autonomy — Chichime, Cayos Holandeses, Coco Bandero, Cayos Limón
linton-bay-san-blas.wind_desc: In the dry season (December–April) the north-east trades blow at 8–18 kn, sometimes 20–25 kn in December–February with big swell outside the reefs. May to November is the rainy season: light, variable winds, thunderstorms and squalls with downpours, with 19–22 rainy days a month by October–November. Hurricanes almost never reach this far.
linton-bay-san-blas.route: Linton Bay — a ~40-mile passage east to Chichime — Cayos Holandeses (“the Swimming Pool”) — Coco Bandero — Cayos Limón — Porvenir — Linton Bay, ~100 miles in a week; crewed boats often meet guests right on the islands (Cartí, Porvenir)
linton-bay-san-blas.mooring: There is one marina — Linton Bay Marina (80+ berths, hurricane-sheltered) on the mainland; San Blas has no marinas, and you spend nights at anchor behind the reefs off uninhabited islets. The Guna charge an entry fee for Guna Yala and a small anchoring fee at some islands (check amounts with the charter company). Water, fuel and provisions on the mainland only; the Guna sell fish and lobster from their boats.
linton-bay-san-blas.licence: Bareboat is rare here: almost the entire fleet is chartered with crew only (skipper and hostess, food and fuel included). Check licence requirements for the rare bareboats with the charter company.

Guna culture, fresh lobster and fish from fishermen's boats
Short passages behind the reefs, warm water year-round
Outside the hurricane belt
cons: Almost no bareboat — crewed only
No marinas, shops or phone signal on the islands
Rain, thunderstorms and light winds from May to November
Reefs and inaccurate charts, sail only in good light
Getting there from Panama City means a drive or a small plane
linton-bay-san-blas.airport: PTY — Panama City, ~2 h by car to Linton Bay; local flights from PAC (Albrook) to Porvenir
linton-bay-san-blas.charter_price_note: Crewed Sun Odyssey 44i (skipper and hostess), food and fuel included: about $5,750 a week in November–January. Most of the fleet is crewed catamarans, with cabin charters sometimes available
school_notes: Aggregator with a Russian version of the site: about 20 boats in Panama, mostly crewed catamarans
Fleet of crewed boats (Guna or international crew), whole-boat and cabin cruises; site in Spanish, English and French

listvyanka-lake-baikal.description: Sailing on Baikal is rugged and stunningly beautiful: along mountainous shores to the Maloye More strait and Olkhon. Yachts are kept at clubs on the Irkutsk Reservoir and reach Baikal down the Angara via Listvyanka. Suits trips with a local captain and experienced skippers ready for cold water and sudden storms.
listvyanka-lake-baikal.rating_basis: A unique cruising ground — the world's deepest lake, with mountains, cliffs and crystal-clear water; there are sailing schools and regattas, summer cruises and ice yachting in winter. But the water is icy (rarely above +15 °C), storms are sudden and violent, and marinas and services are almost non-existent.
listvyanka-lake-baikal.hazards: Sudden squalls and storms with waves up to 4 m (sarma, kultuk, barguzin, verkhovik), icy water — hypothermia within minutes, few shelters and little mobile signal away from villages, fog; the ice only breaks up in May–June.
listvyanka-lake-baikal.crowd_note: Sailing yachts are a rarity; it only gets busy around Listvyanka and Khuzhir in July–August because of tourist boats.
listvyanka-lake-baikal.region: Southern and Central Baikal: the Irkutsk Reservoir and the Angara, Listvyanka, Bolshiye Koty, Peschanaya Bay, Maloye More, Olkhon
listvyanka-lake-baikal.wind_desc: In settled summer weather the wind is light, but conditions can change within an hour: local winds include the kultuk (from the south-west), the verkhovik (along the lake from the north) and the barguzin; in Maloye More — the sarma, a hurricane-force north-westerly, especially in late summer and autumn. In a storm waves reach 4 m.
listvyanka-lake-baikal.route: Irkutsk — up the Angara — Listvyanka — Bolshiye Koty — Peschanaya Bay — Maloye More — Olkhon (Khuzhir, Cape Burkhan, Shamanka) — Ogoy — and back; that's a lot for a week, and part of the trip is long passages along the rocky shore
listvyanka-lake-baikal.mooring: Yacht clubs on the Irkutsk Reservoir (Irkut yacht club and others), piers in Listvyanka; on Baikal itself there are almost no marinas — anchorages in bays (Peschanaya, Maloye More) and mooring to the shore. Part of the coast is Pribaikalsky National Park.
listvyanka-lake-baikal.licence: Without a captain — with a Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licence for a small sailing or sail-and-motor vessel (Baikal and the Angara are inland waterways, the “VVP” category). Sailing trips on Baikal almost always go with a local captain.

Olkhon, Maloye More and bays unreachable by land
Hardly any other yachts
Ice yachting in winter
cons: Icy water even in August
Sudden violent storms, the sarma in Maloye More
Almost no marinas — you need to be self-sufficient
Short season: July–August, at a stretch June and September
highlights: Ice yachting and winter sailing on Baikal's transparent ice
school_notes: School at the Irkut yacht club (Irkutsk, 111 Rzhanova St): summer cruises and regattas on Baikal, skipper school, ice yachts in winter
Irkutsk: courses from helmsman to skipper, practice on a cruising yacht

moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.description: The nearest big water to Moscow: a chain of reservoirs on the Moscow Canal 10 km from the MKAD ring road, with dozens of yacht clubs. A place for first lessons, weekend regattas and day rentals; from here you can also cruise down the canal to the Moscow Sea.
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.rating_basis: Moscow's main sailing venue since 1938: it has hosted the 49er (2005), Micro (2009) and Finn (2011) world championships, with many schools and regattas. But these are narrow reservoirs with light winds — a place for training and racing, not cruising.
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.hazards: The Moscow Canal shipping lane with passenger ships and barges, shallows near the shore, heavy small-craft traffic at weekends, thunderstorm squalls in summer.
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.crowd_note: On summer weekends there are dozens of sails on the water, plus motorboats and jet skis; weekdays are quiet.
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.region: Moscow region: the Moscow Canal — Pirogovo, Klyazma, Pestovo; cruises as far as Dubna and the Ivankovo Reservoir (the Moscow Sea)
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.wind_desc: Summer winds are light and variable, 4–10 kn, often calm in hot weather; fresher in spring and autumn. The reservoirs are narrow, with wind shadows from the wooded shores — a good school for tacking and short-course racing.
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.route: Usually day sails and weekend regattas; for a week-long cruise: Pirogovo — the Moscow Canal (locks) — Dubna — the Ivankovo Reservoir (Konakovo) — and back
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.mooring: Dozens of yacht clubs along the shores (Pirogovo, Uletai Pirogovo, Orekhovaya Bukhta, Spartak in Dolgoprudny, Burevestnik and others): guarded piers with water and electricity, winter storage in hangars; few guest berths, prices on request.
moscow-pirogovo-klyazma.licence: Without a captain — with a Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licence for a small sailing or sail-and-motor vessel; the Moscow Canal reservoirs are inland waterways (the “VVP” category). Clubs usually rent a yacht without a captain after a few training sessions or a skills check; in the canal follow the inland waterway navigation and locking rules.
pros: 10–15 km from the MKAD, handy after work and at weekends
Many schools, training sessions from 3 hours, regattas for beginners
Warm water in summer (up to 20–23 °C)
Sheltered water with no waves
cons: Light, variable summer winds
Crowded at weekends: motorboats, jet skis, passenger ships
No cruising scene — mostly day sails
Season from May to October

school_notes: School and practice at Pirogovo (Orekhovaya Bukhta) and Klyazma (Spartak yacht club), regattas, ICC theory
J/70 training at the Uletai Pirogovo yacht club, 8,000 ₽/h per crew of up to 4, regattas on Saturdays
Training at Klyazma and Pirogovo, GIMS courses, cruises
Training at Klyazma and Pirogovo

priozersk-lake-ladoga.description: Europe's largest lake, with its northern skerries — hundreds of rocky islands and fjords between Sortavala and Priozersk. Week-long trips with nights in coves and on islands, plus Valaam and Konevets. Suits trips with a captain and skippers experienced in northern waters.
priozersk-lake-ladoga.rating_basis: The best inland cruising ground in north-west Russia according to sailors and tour operators: ~650 skerry islands over ~100 km, Valaam, wild nature and nights on the islands; downsides — a short season, cold water and sudden storms on open water.
priozersk-lake-ladoga.hazards: Submerged rocks and reefs in the skerries (navigate by chart, preferably with a local skipper), sudden storms on open Ladoga, cold water, few places to refuel and resupply; the national park's strict reserve zones are closed.
priozersk-lake-ladoga.crowd_note: Yachts are few; popular trip dates in July–August sell out in advance, and the bays of Valaam and Kocherga get busy with motorboats at weekends.
priozersk-lake-ladoga.region: Leningrad Region and Karelia: the Ladoga Skerries, Valaam, Konevets, Sortavala
priozersk-lake-ladoga.wind_desc: Moderate summer winds of 8–15 kn; in the skerries it's calm and you can sail in almost any weather; on open Ladoga storms strike suddenly and quickly build a steep sea. From late August the wind is stronger and colder.
priozersk-lake-ladoga.route: Priozersk — Konevets — the skerries (Kocherga Bay) — Valaam (Monastery Bay) — Sortavala or Winter's Dacha — Putsaari — Kukhka / Honkasalo islands — Priozersk, 7–8 days; the passage to Valaam is ~25 miles, 5–7 hours
priozersk-lake-ladoga.mooring: The bases are the yacht clubs of Priozersk and Berezovo (beyond Priozersk); in the skerries you anchor or moor to the rocks in coves and spend nights on uninhabited islands around a campfire; on Valaam — Monastery Bay. In Ladoga Skerries National Park you pay 50–1,000 ₽ a day per boat plus a visitor fee (about 350 ₽ per person per day).
priozersk-lake-ladoga.licence: Without a captain — with a Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licence for a small sailing or sail-and-motor vessel (the “VVP” category); clubs rent bareboats only to certified skippers. Ladoga Skerries National Park requires a boat permit in advance: apply to oopt@parkladoga.ru with your route and crew list, preferably 1–2 days ahead; landing on strict reserve islands is prohibited.

Valaam and Konevets from the water
White nights in June
~2.5 h from St Petersburg to the base
cons: Season only June — early September, cold water
Sudden storms and steep seas on the open lake
Few marinas and services — you need to be self-sufficient
Paid national park and a boat permit
priozersk-lake-ladoga.airport: LED — Pulkovo, ~2.5–3 h by car to Priozersk
priozersk-lake-ladoga.charter_price_note: 30 ft bareboat (6 berths) — 95,000 ₽ a week, with a captain — 190,000 ₽ (August–September); a 44 ft yacht with a captain and mate for 5 days — 201,600–223,200 ₽; a cabin berth — 55,000–74,000 ₽ per person for 5–7 days; euro figures are an approximate conversion
highlights: White nights — long, light passages through the skerries
school_notes: 3–7-day skerry trips from Berezovo, bareboat for skippers with papers
5–6-day trips on a 44 ft yacht from Priozersk, June — early September
Week-long Priozersk — Valaam — Sortavala trip, GIMS courses

saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.description: The city with Russia's oldest sailing tradition: yacht clubs at the mouth of the Neva, outings into the Neva Bay beyond the flood barrier, to Kronstadt and the forts. Best suited to training, short sails and trips with a captain; longer passages to Vyborg and the islands require experience and an approved route.
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.rating_basis: Russia's main Baltic sailing centre: the oldest yacht clubs, dozens of schools and regattas, white nights. But the season is short, the water cold, the gulf shallow and busy with shipping, and longer routes are restricted by the border regime; it doesn't feature in international top lists.
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.hazards: Shallows and banks outside the channels, the Sea Channel with large ships and ferries, passage through the flood barrier's navigation openings, a short steep sea and fast-building westerly gales, cold water.
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.crowd_note: Plenty of room at sea; what's scarce is berths for cruising yachts in the city: in 2025–2026 the fleet from Petrovskaya Kosa is moving to Kronstadt, Krestovsky Island and other clubs.
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.region: Baltic: the Neva Bay, Kronstadt and the forts, the gulf's north shore to Vysotsk and Vyborg
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.wind_desc: In summer westerlies and south-westerlies of 8–15 kn are most common, with some calm days in hot weather; from September the wind is stronger and westerly gales more frequent. The gulf is shallow, so the sea is short and steep, and the weather changes quickly.
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.route: Petrovskaya Kosa / Krestovsky Island — Kronstadt and the forts — Vysotsk — Vyborg — back via Kronstadt; passages of up to 60 miles, the route depends on the weather and the border regime
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.mooring: Yacht clubs at the mouth of the Neva (Petrovskaya Kosa, Krestovsky Island, the Rowing Canal, Smolenka harbour), Kronstadt (Fort Konstantin); guest berths by arrangement with the club, prices on request. The historic club on Petrovskaya Kosa is being vacated for reconstruction from 2025 (until 2029), and part of the fleet has moved to Kronstadt and Martynova Embankment.
saint-petersburg-gulf-of-finland.licence: Without a captain — only with a Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licence for a small sailing or sail-and-motor vessel with the “MP” category (internal sea waters and territorial sea), and “VVP” for the Neva. Most outings and trips go with a captain-instructor. Sailing to the islands and towards Vyborg is subject to the border regime — agree the route with your club.

White nights in June
The Kronstadt forts and the city from the water
Easy to reach — you start right in the city

Shallows and heavy shipping
The border regime restricts routes to the islands and Vyborg

White nights — night passages with almost no darkness
Kronstadt Sails festival at Island of Forts, business regattas during SPIEF

Skippered yacht rental and training, outings from Krestovsky and Petrovskaya Kosa
Outings into the gulf with a captain-instructor, up to 10 guests, regattas

sochi-black-sea-coast.description: Sochi's Black Sea coast is the only place in Russia where you can sail almost all year round. The bases are the marina in Sochi seaport and Imeretinsky port in Sirius. Good for training, regattas and pleasure sails; for a cruise there is a passage along the exposed coast to Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk.
sochi-black-sea-coast.rating_basis: Russia's warmest sea for sailing: two modern marinas, schools and regattas year-round. But the coast is straight and exposed, harbours are few and summer is often calm — weak for week-long cruises, mainly day sails and regattas.
sochi-black-sea-coast.hazards: Open sea with no shelter for dozens of miles, autumn and winter south-westerly gales, the bora around Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk, heavy motorboat traffic off Sochi; to the south, the state border along the Psou River.
sochi-black-sea-coast.crowd_note: At the height of summer the marinas are full of pleasure boats and yachts for hourly hire; sailing yachts for cruising are few.
sochi-black-sea-coast.region: Black Sea: Sochi, Sirius (Imeretinsky port), the coast to Tuapse, Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk
sochi-black-sea-coast.wind_desc: Light summer winds and a daytime breeze of 5–12 kn, with dead calms in hot weather — part of the way is under motor; fresher in autumn and winter, with south-westerly gales, and around Gelendzhik and Novorossiysk the bora (nord-ost) with hurricane-force gusts.
sochi-black-sea-coast.route: Usually day sails from Sochi or Sirius; a one-way cruise: Sochi — Tuapse — Kiselyov Rock — Parus Rock (Gelendzhik) — Novorossiysk, about 110 miles
sochi-black-sea-coast.mooring: Modern marinas: Sochi Grand Marina in Sochi seaport and Imeretinsky port in Sirius; further along the coast harbours are few (Tuapse is a commercial port, Gelendzhik, Novorossiysk), the shore is open to the swell, and there are almost no sheltered anchorages. Prices on request.
sochi-black-sea-coast.licence: Without a captain — with a Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licence for a small sailing or sail-and-motor vessel with the “MP” category (sea waters). In practice yachts are mostly rented with a captain. South of Sirius is the state border along the Psou River — do not sail towards Abkhazia.

Almost year-round season, winter regattas
Modern marinas, direct flights to Sochi
Dolphins near the yachts
cons: A straight, exposed coast with no islands or sheltered bays
Light winds and calms in summer
Few harbours, passages of 30–50 miles
Few yachts available for week-long charter
sochi-black-sea-coast.airport: AER — Sochi (Adler): ~40 min to Sochi seaport, ~15 min to Imeretinsky port
highlights: Weekend winter regattas — in Sochi people sail all year round
Amateur Sunday regattas at Imeretinsky port, open to beginners
school_notes: School at Imeretinsky port (Sirius): a 2-hour masterclass for 14,000 ₽ per boat for up to 5 people, intro course, Sunday regattas
Training in the waters of Sochi seaport and Imeretinsky port

vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.description: The indented shore of Peter the Great Gulf with dozens of islands an hour or two from Vladivostok: Russky Island, the Empress Eugénie Archipelago, Putyatin and Askold. A city with a strong sailing school and regattas; cruises go with a captain, best in August–September.
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.rating_basis: A strong sailing centre in the Russian Far East: a large yacht club, schools and dozens of regattas, with dozens of islands nearby offering coves and marine life. Downsides — fog in early summer, typhoons, a short warm season and closed border zones.
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.hazards: Fog, typhoons in late summer, cold water in spring, heavy shipping around Vladivostok's ports and in the Eastern Bosphorus strait, closed military and border areas.
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.crowd_note: Yachts are few and the island coves quiet; it only gets busy at the city beaches and during regattas.
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.region: Sea of Japan: Amur and Ussuri bays, Russky Island, the Empress Eugénie Archipelago, Putyatin, Askold
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.wind_desc: In summer a south-easterly monsoon of 8–14 kn, with frequent fog and drizzle in June–July; August–September are the warmest and sunniest months, but typhoons are possible; from October a cold north-westerly monsoon, fresh and clear; in winter Amur Bay freezes over.
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.route: Vladivostok — Russky Island — Reineke and Rikord (a spotted seal colony) — Minonosok Bay — Cape Bruce — the Five Fingers rocks between Putyatin and Askold — and back
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.mooring: The Sem Futov (Seven Feet) yacht club is the largest in the Far East (about 30 VLADMORE school yachts), plus other Vladivostok clubs; there are no marinas in the Empress Eugénie Archipelago or around Putyatin — anchorages in the bays, and Minonosok Bay is almost always calm.
vladivostok-peter-the-great-gulf.licence: Without a captain — with a Russian GIMS (EMERCOM) licence for a small sailing or sail-and-motor vessel with the “MP” category. Some islands and bays are in the border zone or are closed military sites requiring a permit; agree the route with your club.
pros: Dozens of islands and coves close to the city
Spotted seals, clean water, seafood
Warm sea in August–September (up to 22 °C)
A strong yacht club and plenty of regattas
cons: Fog in June–July, typhoons in August–September
Short warm season, the bay freezes in winter
Border zones and closed military sites
Few yachts available for week-long charter
highlights: Regatta season at Sem Futov — more than 50 regattas a year (Platu 25, MX700, cruising yachts)
school_notes: School based at the Sem Futov yacht club: training April–October, about 30 yachts, regattas, children's sea school
MX700 training from 2,500 ₽ for 2 hours, based at the Sem Futov yacht club

phuket-phang-nga-bay.description: Hundreds of karst islands in Phang Nga Bay, the beaches of Krabi and Phi Phi, warm water year-round and short hops in sheltered water. A good choice for a first bareboat week in the tropics or a group with a skipper; the season is November to April, in the north-east monsoon.
phuket-phang-nga-bay.rating_basis: South-East Asia's main charter area: bases of Sunsail, The Moorings, Dream Yacht and dozens of local fleets. Sail Magazine praises the scenery, good holding and cheap food, but notes light winds at the end of the monsoon, heat and ~3 m tides. Reviews complain about crowds of tour boats at Phi Phi.
phuket-phang-nga-bay.hazards: Tides up to 2–3 m and shallows in Phang Nga Bay, coral banks, unlit fish traps and nets, heavy longtail and speedboat traffic, squalls in the south-west monsoon, swell on the west coast; moving between provinces requires a domestic clearance stamp (fines up to 10,000 baht).
phuket-phang-nga-bay.crowd_note: Marinas are few but usually have space; by day Phi Phi, Koh Hong and Racha are swarming with tour boats and speedboats — better to anchor towards evening when they leave. For New Year berths and yachts are booked 6–12 months ahead.
phuket-phang-nga-bay.region: Andaman Sea: Phang Nga Bay, Koh Yao, Krabi (Ao Nang, Railay), Phi Phi, Racha
phuket-phang-nga-bay.wind_desc: November–April — the north-east monsoon: dry, a steady NE 8–18 kn; by March–April the wind eases and it gets hot. May–October — the south-west monsoon: downpours, squalls, winds up to 20–30 kn and swell on the west coast; charter companies offer discounts, but boats mostly stay inside Phang Nga Bay.
phuket-phang-nga-bay.route: Ao Po — Koh Naka Yai — Koh Yao Noi — Ao Nang/Railay (Krabi) — Phi Phi Don — Koh Racha Yai — Koh Rang Yai — Ao Po, ~110 miles in a week
phuket-phang-nga-bay.mooring: Mostly anchorages and buoys in bays; marinas only on Phuket (Ao Po Grand, Yacht Haven, Boat Lagoon, Royal Phuket) — Sunsail's own yachts berth free at Ao Po, other marinas charge ~1,250–1,900 baht a day for 12 m. National parks (Phang Nga, Phi Phi, Similan) charge entry and mooring fees; never drop anchor on coral, and buoys are mandatory in places.
phuket-phang-nga-bay.licence: For bareboat, charter companies require a recognised yacht skipper's certificate (ICC, IYT, RYA, etc.) and a sailing CV; Sunsail requires Level 2 experience (≈10 days or 200 miles as skipper). Without papers — skippered only. Check requirements for Russian documents with the charter company.
pros: Dry season with a steady moderate wind November–April
Short passages, many sheltered anchorages
Large charter bases and plenty of catamarans
Water 28–30 °C, cheap food ashore
cons: May–October — monsoon with downpours and squalls
Crowds of tour boats at Phi Phi and Koh Hong
National park fees and mandatory buoys, tidal shallows in the bay
Hot and often calm in March–April — lots of motoring
phuket-phang-nga-bay.charter_price_note: 40–42 ft bareboat (3 cabins) per week: December–January / May–October; +30–50% at Christmas and New Year, 20–40% discounts off-season
phuket-phang-nga-bay.skipper_price_note: Sunsail skipper — £155 a day, plus food
highlights: Phuket King's Cup Regatta (Kata Beach)
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: bareboats on Phuket (Yacht Haven) and catamaran cabin cruises
Bareboat and skippers, based at Ao Po Grand Marina
Bareboat from Ao Po Grand Marina, routes for both monsoons
Announcement of an IYT Bareboat Skipper course on Phuket in Russian and English

neiafu-vavau-tonga.description: Dozens of forested islands around the Port of Refuge harbour: 3–15-mile hops within sheltered waters, caves and humpback whales you can swim with. Suits a relaxed week and a first taste of the Pacific — but it's a rare destination with a small local fleet, and the season is May to October only.
neiafu-vavau-tonga.rating_basis: A well-known stop for circumnavigators and one of the most sheltered cruising grounds in the Pacific: short passages, caves, whales from June to October. The big chains (The Moorings, Dream Yacht) don't list Tonga among their bases; the fleet is small and local, and information on prices and requirements is scarce.
neiafu-vavau-tonga.hazards: Tropical cyclones November–April, coral reefs and heads (move in good light), rules for approaching whales.
neiafu-vavau-tonga.crowd_note: In season many circumnavigators' yachts lie in Neiafu (about 500 a season); the island anchorages are quiet.
neiafu-vavau-tonga.region: Northern Tonga: the Vava'u group — Port of Refuge, Kapa, Nuapapu, Kenutu and ~40 more islands
neiafu-vavau-tonga.wind_desc: May–October is the dry season with south-east trades, and the water inside the group is calm: the southern islands form one of the most sheltered natural harbours in the Pacific. November–April is the official cyclone season: heat, downpours, storms and flood risk; yachts leave for New Zealand.
neiafu-vavau-tonga.route: Neiafu (Port of Refuge) — Port Maurelle and Swallows' Cave (Kapa) — Mariner's Cave (Nuapapu) — the southern islands — Kenutu by the eastern reef — Neiafu; short passages in sheltered water
neiafu-vavau-tonga.mooring: In Neiafu — a mooring field and anchorage in the deep-water Port of Refuge harbour (about 500 yachts call each season); among the islands — anchoring in sheltered bays. Port fees are paid on departure.
neiafu-vavau-tonga.licence: No official requirements could be found; in Oceania special certificates usually aren't needed — the charter company assesses your sailing experience. Check with the local company.
pros: Very sheltered water and short passages
Humpback whales June–October
Caves, reefs and empty anchorages
The circumnavigators' scene in Neiafu
cons: November–April — cyclone season
A small local charter fleet, little information
A long, expensive flight (via Tongatapu)
neiafu-vavau-tonga.airport: VAV — Vava'u, ~15 min (flights from Tongatapu, TBU)
highlights: Humpback whales: whale watching and guided swims with whales

anacortes-san-juan-islands.description: An archipelago of hundreds of forested islands between Seattle and Vancouver: short hops, marine state parks with mooring buoys, orcas and bald eagles, and the towns of Friday Harbor and Roche Harbor. The main challenges are tidal currents in the passes and cold water. Suits skippers with tidal navigation experience; beginners should take a skipper or join a flotilla. From Anacortes the Canadian Gulf Islands are easy to reach.
anacortes-san-juan-islands.rating_basis: Cruising World calls the Salish Sea (the San Juans and Gulf Islands) one of the best cruising grounds in North America; SAIL and Discover Boating include the San Juans among the top US charter destinations. Praise goes to the nature, orcas and state parks with buoys; downsides — cold water, light summer winds and currents.
anacortes-san-juan-islands.hazards: Tidal currents of 2–5 kn (Cattle Pass, Obstruction Pass, San Juan Channel), 7–8 kn in Deception Pass; standing waves when wind is against tide; morning fog; cold water; floating logs and deadheads; rocks and kelp near shore; ferries and shipping lanes in Haro and Rosario straits; a limited number of fuel docks.
anacortes-san-juan-islands.crowd_note: In July–August popular coves (Sucia, Roche Harbor, Friday Harbor) fill up by midday and boats are booked 3–6 months ahead; September is much quieter.
anacortes-san-juan-islands.region: Salish Sea, Washington State: San Juan, Orcas, Lopez, Sucia, Stuart
anacortes-san-juan-islands.wind_desc: In summer the wind between the islands is often light and boats motor a lot. In the afternoon a north-westerly of 10–20 kn fills in the straits (Haro, Rosario, Juan de Fuca), easing by night; fog in the mornings. In autumn and winter fronts bring south-easterly gales, and in winter there can be a cold north-easterly.
anacortes-san-juan-islands.route: Anacortes — Sucia (28 miles) — Orcas (Deer Harbor) — Friday Harbor — Roche Harbor — Stuart (Reid or Prevost Harbor) — Blakely — Anacortes, ~115 miles in a week
anacortes-san-juan-islands.mooring: Washington marine state park buoys — $23 a night (Sucia has 48 of them), park docks — $1 per foot; anchoring is free. Marinas at Friday Harbor, Roche Harbor, Deer Harbor and Rosario: Friday Harbor charges $1.95 per foot in summer (about $80 for 42 ft). In July–August coves and buoys are taken by midday.
anacortes-san-juan-islands.licence: The US has no official yacht licence: the charter company looks at your CV (recent skippering experience on a similar boat and in tidal waters). They usually ask for ASA 104 / US Sailing Bareboat Cruising level or equivalent (RYA Day Skipper, ICC) and always do a checkout with an instructor; if experience is lacking, they assign paid extra training. Entering Canadian waters requires passports and visas and a phone report to CBSA (1-888-226-7277).
pros: Beautiful northern nature, orcas, seals, eagles
A network of marine state parks with buoys and docks at $23 a night
Short passages between islands, sheltered waters
Easy to combine with the Canadian Gulf Islands
cons: Short season: July–September
Often calm in summer, lots of motoring
Cold water of 10–13 °C, swimming barely possible
Expensive charter and few boats compared with the Mediterranean
Crowded coves in July–August
anacortes-san-juan-islands.airport: SEA — Seattle, ~1.5–2 h by car; BLI — Bellingham, ~45 min
anacortes-san-juan-islands.charter_price_note: 42 ft bareboat (Catalina) at Anacortes Yacht Charters: $800–1,025 a night depending on season, i.e. $5,600–7,200 a week; 40 ft boats from $665 a night. Seasonal rates for 2027
anacortes-san-juan-islands.skipper_price_note: Captain $300–500 a day on top of the rental (sea.net estimate)
highlights: Orcas and humpbacks in the straits
Wooden Boat Festival in Port Townsend
school_notes: Anacortes's largest charter company: 27–70 ft sailboats and catamarans, bareboat and skippered
Charter company and ASA school in Bellingham, flotillas in the San Juans, Gulf Islands and Desolation Sound
ASA school and charter in the region

bvi-tortola.description: The Caribbean's best-known “training” cruising ground: dozens of islands around the Sir Francis Drake Channel, 5–15-mile hops, reliable trades and mooring buoys in almost every bay. Suits a first bareboat charter, families and groups on a catamaran; seasoned sailors may find it too easy and too crowded.
bvi-tortola.rating_basis: The bareboat classic and one of the world's most popular areas: short line-of-sight passages, the sheltered Sir Francis Drake Channel, an extensive buoy network; tops the “best place for a first charter” lists at Moorings, Sunsail and 12knots; downsides — prices and crowds.
bvi-tortola.hazards: Hurricanes June–November (Irma in 2017), Christmas winds of 25+ kn in December–January, northerly swell in winter in north-facing bays (Jost Van Dyke, Cane Garden Bay), reefs and coral heads — especially Horseshoe Reef off Anegada (enter only via the channel and by day); charter companies prohibit night sailing.
bvi-tortola.crowd_note: In high season the bookable Boatyball buoys sell out by 7 a.m., and first-come buoys in popular bays (Norman, Cooper, Jost Van Dyke) are taken by midday; summer is quieter, and some bars and restaurants close in September–October.
bvi-tortola.region: Caribbean, Virgin Islands: Tortola, Virgin Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, Norman, Cooper, Anegada
bvi-tortola.wind_desc: Easterly trades all year: December–April north-easterly 15–25 kn (“Christmas winds” of 25+ kn in December–January), May–August south-easterly 15–20 kn, September–October lighter at 5–15 kn and hurricane season.
bvi-tortola.route: Road Town — Norman (The Bight) — Jost Van Dyke (Great Harbour, White Bay) — Cane Garden Bay — Anegada — Virgin Gorda (North Sound, The Baths) — Cooper — Road Town, ~90 miles in a week
bvi-tortola.mooring: Mostly paid buoys in the bays: about $45 a night on white first-come buoys, $55–65 on bookable Boatyball buoys (booked on the day of arrival, often sold out by 7 a.m.); marinas cost more; national park day buoys (The Baths, the Indians, the Caves) are for daytime use only with a national park permit, which, along with the cruising tax, is included in the charter bill.
bvi-tortola.licence: No official licence needed: charter companies check your experience against your sailing CV (Sunsail, for example, asks for at least 9 days and 100 miles as skipper on a similar yacht); the base may test your skills and, if in doubt, insist on a paid skipper; minimum crew of 2, night passages prohibited. To visit the USVI you must clear out with BVI customs.
pros: Short passages in sheltered waters, islands always in sight
Steady trades of 12–20 kn
Huge choice of boats and bases, buoys almost everywhere
Beach bars, snorkelling, The Baths
cons: Expensive: charter, buoys, restaurants
Crowded in high season — you have to hunt for buoys
Hurricane season June–November, peak August–October
Connecting flights (via St Thomas, Antigua or Puerto Rico)
bvi-tortola.airport: EIS — Beef Island (Tortola), ~30 min; or STT — St Thomas (USVI) + ~1 h ferry
bvi-tortola.charter_price_note: 40–42 ft bareboat per week: winter (December–April) / summer; converted from USD (Dream Yacht charges roughly $1,600–2,800 in summer and $3,900–8,100 in winter), plus mandatory packages, cruising tax and fuel
bvi-tortola.skipper_price_note: $264–308 a day plus food and tips (Dream Yacht Charter BVI)
highlights: BVI Spring Regatta & Sailing Festival (Nanny Cay)
The “Christmas winds” — the strongest trades of the season
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: bareboat, skippers, cabin cruises in the BVI
Flagship base in Road Town (Wickhams Cay II), bareboat and crewed
Base in Road Town, flotillas, rules and fees
Base at Hodges Creek (Tortola), seasonal prices from broker Virgin Island Sailing

hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.description: Rope jumping from the rim of Hell's Canyon: about 4 seconds of free fall, then a big pendulum swing in a climbing harness. The same team also runs a 120-metre jump in Dragon Canyon (Vayots Dzor) and canyoning trips. Easy to combine with a visit to Khor Virap.
hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.rating_basis: The only regular commercial jump in Armenia we could confirm; the red cliffs of the Aratso canyon; the team has been operating for more than 13 years
hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.hazards: This is rope jumping on a static rope with a pendulum swing, not bungee — ask the team about the rigging and equipment certification. Contraindications: blood pressure, heart conditions, spine problems, pregnancy. The canyon is near the border with Nakhchivan — don't stray from the route. Jumps are cancelled in rain and strong wind.
hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.crowd_note: Small groups by appointment, no queues
hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.region: Ararat Province, the Aratso river canyon near the village of Tigranashen, ~80 km from Yerevan (approximate coordinates)
hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.booking: Book by phone with the operator (+374 93 835959), 30% deposit; jumps mostly at weekends. At most sites the usual limits are 18+ (younger with parental consent) and a weight of roughly 45–100 kg
pros: Cheap: ~€56 per jump
Red cliffs and views of Ararat on the way
A 120 m option for experienced jumpers
cons: No website of its own, booking by phone
Mostly at weekends
The Ararat Valley is hot in summer — May–June and September–October are better
hells-canyon-armenia-rope-jump.price_note: 25,000 drams (~€56 at ~450 AMD/€) for the 65 m jump. The flagship 120 m jump in Dragon Canyon (Vayots Dzor, ~2 h from Yerevan) — 40,000 drams (~€89). 30% deposit; transfer from Yerevan extra
school_notes: Description, prices and the operator's phone number; also canyoning at Devil's Bridge (Syunik)
