europabruecke.description: A jump from a platform in the middle of the A13 motorway bridge on the Brenner Pass route — one of the highest bridges in Europe — over the Sill valley. 192 m of free flight, after which you're hauled back up to the bridge. Just 20 minutes from Innsbruck.
europabruecke.rating_basis: No. 5 in CNN's top 15 highest jumps in the world; 5/5 from 48 reviews on Manawa; operating since 1993
europabruecke.hazards: The operator's rules exclude people with high blood pressure, heart and vascular disease, skull injuries, epilepsy, glaucoma, osteoporosis, a pacemaker, thrombosis, pregnancy or mental illness. Strictly 0.0 per mille alcohol. No jumps in bad weather.
europabruecke.crowd_note: Around 60 days a year and only at weekends — slots are booked in advance, and there can be a wait on the bridge
europabruecke.region: Tyrol, the Wipptal valley near Schönberg, ~20 minutes from Innsbruck
europabruecke.booking: Saturdays and Sundays only, roughly from late May to late October (22 May – 23 October announced for 2027), main hours 10:00–16:00. Advance booking is mandatory. Strictly 0.0 per mille alcohol on the bridge. In bad weather the jump is moved to another date; no refunds.
europabruecke.record: One of the highest bridge jumps in Europe — 192 m; Rupert Hirner made the first jump on 3 October 1993
pros: 192 m — one of the highest sites in Europe
Innsbruck and its airport are close by
Cheaper online: €199 instead of €239
cons: Weekends only, around 60 days a year
The bridge is a working motorway, with traffic noise all around
Strict limits: 50–105 kg, age 16+
europabruecke.airport: INN — Innsbruck, ~20 min; MUC — Munich, ~2 h
europabruecke.price_note: €199 when booked online, €239 on site; video — €31 online (€34 on site), a companion to the jump point — €9 online
school_notes: Operator; cheaper online than on site. Website in German, English and Italian
Aggregator, from €239

koelnbrein-dam.description: A jump from the crest of Austria's highest dam at about 1,900 m above sea level, among the peaks of the Hohe Tauern. 165 m of free fall alongside the concrete wall. Nearby there's a skywalk viewing platform over the drop and a high-altitude reservoir.
koelnbrein-dam.rating_basis: No. 8 in CNN's top 15 highest jumps in the world (listed there as 169 m); high-alpine views of the Hohe Tauern
koelnbrein-dam.hazards: The same contraindications as at the Europabrücke: high blood pressure, heart disease, epilepsy, glaucoma, osteoporosis, thrombosis, pregnancy, etc. At altitude the weather changes fast: in a thunderstorm, wind or fog the jump is postponed.
koelnbrein-dam.crowd_note: Jumps run on just 4 days a year — everyone comes on those days, so book ahead
koelnbrein-dam.region: Carinthia, the Malta valley, at the end of the Malta Hochalmstraße mountain road
koelnbrein-dam.booking: Jumps happen on only a few weekends a year: 31 July – 1 August and 7–8 August announced for 2027, from 9:00. Online booking is mandatory. The road to the dam is open roughly from May to the end of October. In bad weather the jump is postponed; no refunds.
koelnbrein-dam.record: Austria's highest dam (200 m); the operator calls it the highest-altitude bungee site in the world — over 2,000 m above sea level; jumps since 1998
pros: High-alpine site with Alpine views
165 m of free fall
The Malta Hochalmstraße road is a sight in itself
cons: Only a couple of weekends a year
Far from major cities
Chilly at 1,900 m even in August
koelnbrein-dam.airport: KLU — Klagenfurt, ~1 h 45 min; SZG — Salzburg, ~2 h
koelnbrein-dam.price_note: €199 when booked online, €229 on site; the Malta Hochalmstraße road toll is extra
school_notes: Operator (the same as at the Europabrücke); website in German, English and Italian

skypark-cairns.description: An AJ Hackett tower on a rainforest-covered hillside (a UNESCO site), 20 minutes from Cairns: 50 m of free fall and 16 jump styles, including a water-touch option. Next to it are a giant swing reaching up to 120 km/h and the highest viewing deck in Cairns. Easy to combine with a trip to the Great Barrier Reef.
skypark-cairns.rating_basis: The country's only bungee and 30+ years of operation (Tourism Queensland), 16 jump styles; the height and the view are more modest than at the New Zealand sites
skypark-cairns.hazards: The usual contraindications: pregnancy, heart conditions, blood pressure, back problems. In the wet season jumps may be cancelled because of thunderstorms and cyclones; summer is hot and very humid — drink plenty of water.
skypark-cairns.crowd_note: Queues are rare; busiest in the dry season (June–October) and during school holidays
skypark-cairns.region: Queensland, Smithfield (end of McGregor Road), ~20 min north of Cairns
skypark-cairns.booking: Book online at book.skyparkcairns.com or by phone on (07) 4057 7188; open daily roughly 10:00–17:00, last slots at 16:00. Free transfers from Cairns and the Northern Beaches by prior arrangement
skypark-cairns.record: The only bungee jump in Australia; a tower above the rainforest with views of the coast
pros: The only bungee in Australia
Free transfer from Cairns
Tandems and 16 jump styles
Close to the reef and Palm Cove
cons: Low compared with New Zealand
In the wet season (December–March) it's hot and humid, and cyclones are possible
skypark-cairns.price_note: Jump from AUD 189 (with a media package via partners ~AUD 229); giant swing from AUD 109, bungee + swing combo from AUD 269; free transfer from Cairns and the Northern Beaches
school_notes: Official website: bungee, giant swing, viewing deck

great-canadian-bungee.description: A 61 m jump (about 20 storeys) over a spring-fed lagoon in the flooded Morrison limestone quarry, half an hour from Ottawa. On request the jump master can set the cord so that you touch the water with your head or dip in up to your waist. Nearby are the ~310 m RIPRIDE zipline starting from 200 feet up, a beach and a picnic area.
great-canadian-bungee.rating_basis: Canada's highest jump, over a turquoise lagoon in a limestone quarry, with the rare chance of a water dip; 35th season in 2026
great-canadian-bungee.hazards: Contraindications: pregnancy, hypertension, epilepsy, severe asthma, joint, ligament and spine problems, being under the influence of alcohol. Jumps are suspended during thunderstorms.
great-canadian-bungee.crowd_note: Summer weekends draw lots of people from Ottawa and Montreal — book ahead
great-canadian-bungee.region: Quebec, Chelsea (Outaouais), ~30 min north of Ottawa
great-canadian-bungee.booking: Book online or by phone; the season runs from late April – early May to early November, with jumps almost every day; under-18s need parental consent
great-canadian-bungee.record: Canada's highest bungee (61 m); according to the operator, the only jump in the Americas where you can dunk your head in the water; Prime Minister Justin Trudeau jumped here in 2022
pros: Canada's highest bungee
You can dip into the water
A beautiful turquoise lagoon
Close to Ottawa
cons: Open only from May to early November
A water touch isn't guaranteed
Pricier than most jumps in Latin America
great-canadian-bungee.price_note: First jump CAD 178.30 + taxes; a repeat jump the same day CAD 89.58; zipline CAD 34.79; entry to the Morrison quarry is extra
school_notes: Official website: bungee and the RIPRIDE zipline over the lagoon

whistler-bungee.description: A jump from a 50 m footbridge over the glacial Cheakamus River, in a canyon of basalt columns and old-growth conifer forest. The site is 15 minutes' drive from Whistler and open year-round — in winter you can jump between ski days. Tandem jumps are possible if the combined weight is up to 136 kg.
whistler-bungee.rating_basis: High review scores (around 4.8 out of 5 on aggregator sites), a beautiful canyon with basalt cliffs and a view of the Black Tusk; mid-range in terms of height
whistler-bungee.hazards: Contraindications: heart, blood pressure, back and neck problems, pregnancy. Jumps are cancelled during thunderstorms; in winter the path to the bridge can be icy.
whistler-bungee.crowd_note: In summer and at weekends slots go early — book a few days ahead
whistler-bungee.region: British Columbia, 15 km south of Whistler Village
whistler-bungee.booking: Online booking at least 3–4 days ahead, after that by phone; open every day year-round, roughly 12:00–17:00 in summer and 12:00–15:00 in winter
whistler-bungee.record: The higher of British Columbia's two bungee jumps; voted by locals “Whistler's most extreme activity”
pros: Open every day, year-round
A very beautiful canyon and mountain views
Close to the Whistler ski resort
Tandem jumps available
cons: The height is modest next to the world record-holders
Cold in winter, with short opening hours
Online booking only a few days ahead
whistler-bungee.airport: YVR — Vancouver, ~2 h via the Sea-to-Sky Highway
whistler-bungee.price_note: A single jump from CAD 141 (per Tourism Whistler); 15% off when booked 15+ days ahead; photos CAD 45
school_notes: The operator's official website, online booking
Booking via the Whistler tourism portal

wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.description: A 46 m bridge over the Nanaimo River on Vancouver Island — North America's first legal bridge built specifically for bungee. There are 16 jump styles across six difficulty levels, and next door the Primal Swing giant swing reaching up to 140 km/h and ziplines over the canyon. Every February there's a charity naked bungee jump.
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.rating_basis: North America's historic first bungee bridge and a big adventure park; average height, forest-canyon scenery
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.hazards: Contraindications: heart disease, high blood pressure, back and neck injuries, pregnancy. Operation depends on the weather — jumps stop in thunderstorms and strong wind.
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.crowd_note: Queues only on summer weekends; usually quiet on weekdays
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.region: British Columbia, Vancouver Island, ~10 km south of Nanaimo
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.booking: You can turn up without booking, but an online booking guarantees a slot; open daily in summer (July – early September), almost every day in June and September, Fri–Mon in October, Sat–Sun from November to mid-December; closed in winter
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.record: North America's first legal bridge built specifically for bungee; more than 265,000 people have jumped from it
pros: A historic site
Lots of jump styles and activities in one park
No advance booking needed
Handy on a Vancouver Island road trip
cons: A low jump by world standards
Closed in winter, weekends only in spring and autumn
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.airport: YCD — Nanaimo, ~10 min; ferry from Vancouver to Nanaimo ~1 h 40 min
wildplay-nanaimo-bungy.price_note: A single jump CAD 139.99–164.99 (cheaper in the morning and late in the day); jump + Primal Swing combo from CAD 199.99
school_notes: Official website: bungee, Primal Swing, ziplines, ropes courses

niouc-bridge.description: A narrow — just 50 cm wide — pedestrian suspension bridge from 1922, strung across a gorge at the entrance to the Val d'Anniviers. It's 190 m to the bottom, and the bridge itself sways underfoot, so the fear starts on the walk out. The site is a whole park: a pendulum swing, rope jumping, a zipline and a bar above the abyss.
niouc-bridge.rating_basis: No. 6 in CNN's top 15 highest jumps in the world; a rare format — a swaying suspension bridge; lots of activities at one site
niouc-bridge.hazards: The bridge sways in the wind and as people walk. Contraindications: pregnancy, heart disease and blood pressure, spinal injuries, epilepsy; over-60s need a doctor's certificate. Jumps are suspended in thunderstorms and strong wind.
niouc-bridge.crowd_note: Queues on summer weekends; on weekdays the site isn't always open
niouc-bridge.region: Valais, the entrance to the Val d'Anniviers, ~15 minutes from Sierre
niouc-bridge.booking: 2026 season — 4 April to 31 October: at least every weekend, 10:00–18:00, with more days in summer — see the calendar on the website. Extra days are opened for groups of 5+ by phone. Over-60s need a medical certificate.
niouc-bridge.record: One of the highest bridge jumps in the world (190 m, CNN top 15); a narrow pedestrian suspension bridge from 1922, with jumps since 1997
pros: 190 m — one of the highest bridge jumps in the world
Pendulum swing, rope jumping and zipline at one site
The sunny, dry climate of Valais
cons: Prices aren't published on the website
Age 16+ only
Mostly at weekends
niouc-bridge.airport: GVA — Geneva, ~2 h; SIR — Sion, ~30 min (few flights)
niouc-bridge.price_note: CHF 210 per jump (≈€221) according to a 2023 SwitzerLanding review; the operator's website doesn't publish prices — check when booking
school_notes: Website in French, German and English; besides bungee — solo and tandem pendulum swing, rope jumping, zipline and the “Le Perchoir” bar

stockhorn-cable-car.description: Not a bridge jump but a jump from the open cabin of the Stockhorn cable car: 134 m of free fall above the mountain lake Hinterstockensee. The package includes the cable-car ride and transfer from Interlaken, and after the jump a drink and views of the Bernese Alps.
stockhorn-cable-car.rating_basis: The best-known jump in the Interlaken area, featured in round-ups of Switzerland's best bungee; an unusual setting — a cable-car cabin above a lake
stockhorn-cable-car.hazards: Standard contraindications: pregnancy, heart disease and blood pressure, back and neck injuries, epilepsy. Mountain weather changes fast: in strong wind, a thunderstorm or low cloud the trip is postponed.
stockhorn-cable-car.crowd_note: Fixed departures in small groups — no queues, but weekend places are best booked ahead
stockhorn-cable-car.region: Bernese Oberland, above the Hinterstockensee; the valley station is in Erlenbach, ~40 minutes from Interlaken
stockhorn-cable-car.booking: April–October, departure at 15:45 on Mondays, Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays (in peak season also at 18:30 on Saturdays). Meeting point at the OUTDOOR base in Wilderswil (Interlaken) or at the cable car's valley station in Erlenbach. The whole programme takes about 5 hours from Interlaken. Up to two spectators can come along as far as the middle station. Age 14+, no exceptions.
stockhorn-cable-car.record: A jump from an open cable-car cabin above a mountain lake at ~1,600 m — a rare format in Europe
pros: An unusual format — jumping from a cable-car cabin
Cable car and transfer from Interlaken included
A mountain lake and Alpine views
cons: Only 4 days a week, one or two departures a day
Strictly 14+
The programme takes half a day
stockhorn-cable-car.airport: BRN — Bern, ~40 min; ZRH — Zurich, ~1 h 45 min
stockhorn-cable-car.price_note: CHF 239 per person (≈€251), groups of 10+ — CHF 215; includes the cable car, equipment, transfer from Interlaken and a drink. Photos — CHF 49, video — CHF 59, both — CHF 99; spectator — CHF 60
school_notes: Operator; guides speak German and English
Booking site with a Russian-language interface, from CHF 239; briefing in English or German

verzasca-dam.description: The very jump from the opening of the film GoldenEye: 220 m of free flight down the concrete wall of an arch dam above the Verzasca gorge. After the jump you're hauled back up to the crest. Nearby are the emerald Verzasca river and the village of Lavertezzo with its old stone bridge.
verzasca-dam.rating_basis: No. 2 in CNN's top 15 highest jumps in the world (after the Macau Tower); a Guinness record for the GoldenEye stunt; the operator counts more than 10,000 jumps
verzasca-dam.hazards: Not allowed with pregnancy, high blood pressure, heart disease, epilepsy, musculoskeletal injuries, neurological disorders, glaucoma, recent eye surgery or chronic ear conditions; no one under the influence of alcohol is allowed to jump. Jumps are suspended in thunderstorms, thick fog and when water is released from the dam.
verzasca-dam.crowd_note: On summer weekends slots sell out in advance and people wait their turn on the dam crest; weekday afternoons are quieter
verzasca-dam.region: Ticino, the Verzasca valley, ~15 minutes from Locarno
verzasca-dam.booking: The season runs from Easter to 31 October, with jumps in the afternoons only. In 2026 — Wednesday to Sunday; announced for 2027: April — Sat–Sun, May–October — Fri–Sun, June – mid-September — Wed–Sun. Summer weekends sell out early, so book online. There's no minimum age (what matters is a weight of 45 kg+); under-18s need parental consent, over-65s a doctor's certificate. Night jumps run for groups of 10+; the backwards jump is available from your second jump, the “Ultimo” from your third.
verzasca-dam.record: James Bond's jump in GoldenEye (1995) — according to Guinness World Records, the highest bungee jump from a structure in a film; one of the highest commercial jumps in the world
pros: One of the highest jumps in the world — 220 m
A legendary location from a Bond film
15 minutes from Locarno, close to Lake Maggiore
Can be combined with canyoning with the same operator
cons: Expensive: from CHF 255
Afternoon jumps only, and not every day
Closed from November to March
verzasca-dam.airport: MXP — Milan Malpensa, ~1 h 30 min; ZRH — Zurich, ~2 h 30 min
verzasca-dam.price_note: Classic jump — CHF 255 for 1–2 people (≈€268), in a group of 3+ — CHF 235, under-19s and students — CHF 195. A second jump the same day — CHF 125, GoPro video — CHF 39. The price includes the briefing, a drink and a certificate
school_notes: The only operator on the dam; website in German, English, French and Italian. “Bungee + canyoning” packages available

zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.description: A jump from the middle of the 430-metre glass bridge over the Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon — 260 m to the bottom of the gorge. The platform opened at the end of 2020 and is China's highest bungee. The jump is easy to combine with a walk across the glass bridge, a zipline and a trip to the “Avatar” pillars of Wulingyuan.
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.rating_basis: One of the highest bungee sites in the world, above a canyon in the Wulingyuan UNESCO area; few reviews from foreigners
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.hazards: Not allowed with heart disease, blood pressure or back problems, or pregnancy; age 16+ only. The bridge closes in thunderstorms, strong wind and icy conditions; June brings the meiyu rains.
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.crowd_note: Few people jump (~20 jumps a day in 2021), but the bridge itself is packed with Chinese tourists on holidays (1 May, 1–7 October) and in summer
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.region: Hunan, Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon (Cili County), ~40 km from Zhangjiajie city
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.booking: Jump tickets are bought on site or via Chinese services (Ctrip/Trip.com); the platform operates year-round, 9:00–16:00. The bridge closes in bad weather — check the day before
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.record: 260 m — China's highest bungee and, according to the operator, the world's highest jump from a footbridge (higher than the 233 m Macau Tower)
pros: One of the highest bungee points on the planet
A spectacular glass bridge and canyon
Can be combined with Wulingyuan park
cons: Expensive: ~CNY 2,000 plus canyon entry
Little information in English, no official website for foreigners
Heat and crowds on the bridge in summer
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.airport: DYG — Zhangjiajie Hehua, ~1 h by car
zhangjiajie-glass-bridge-bungee.price_note: CNY 1,998 (≈€241) per jump; the entry ticket to the canyon with the bridge (route B) is another CNY 175

san-gil-colombia-bungee.description: A 70 m jump from a crane basket over the Fonce river, 10 minutes from San Gil — Colombia's capital of rafting, paragliding and caving. Operating since 2007; tandem jumps are possible and photos are included in the price. When the river is high you can get a light dip at the bottom.
san-gil-colombia-bungee.rating_basis: Excellent reviews (4.9 out of 5 from 1,500+ Google reviews), a very low price; average height, the platform is a crane over the river
san-gil-colombia-bungee.hazards: Not open to pregnant women or people with recent injuries or heart disease; contraindicated with hypertension and back problems. In the rainy seasons (April–May, October–November) jumps are suspended for thunderstorms.
san-gil-colombia-bungee.crowd_note: One platform, ~15 minutes per person — at weekends and on Colombian public holidays you may have to wait
san-gil-colombia-bungee.region: Santander, 2 km from San Gil on the road to Charalá
san-gil-colombia-bungee.booking: You can take a taxi from San Gil (~10 min) without booking or book through a hostel/agency; open 8:30–16:30, except Wednesdays; there's only one platform — allow time for the queue
san-gil-colombia-bungee.record: Colombia's highest bungee tower according to the operator; San Gil is the country's “adventure capital”
pros: Very cheap
Excellent service according to reviews
Easy to combine with rafting and paragliding in San Gil
Warm climate year-round
cons: A crane, not a bridge or a gorge
One platform — queues happen
Closed on Wednesdays
san-gil-colombia-bungee.airport: BGA — Bucaramanga, ~3 h via the Chicamocha Canyon
san-gil-colombia-bungee.price_note: A single jump from COP 90,000 (≈EUR 19; COP 80,000 was quoted in 2025); photos included, video extra
school_notes: Official website, booking for solo and tandem jumps
Online booking from COP 90,000

monteverde-extremo-bungee.description: A small cable-car gondola carries you out to the middle of a canyon above the Monteverde cloud forest — it's 143 m to the bottom, with about 60 m of free fall. It's the highest bungee in Costa Rica and, according to the park, in all of Central America. The same park has one of the world's highest Tarzan swings and 4 km of ziplines, including the “Superman” line.
monteverde-extremo-bungee.rating_basis: The highest jump in the region, an unusual gondola platform above the cloud forest; excellent reviews (5/5 on Manawa)
monteverde-extremo-bungee.hazards: Contraindications: pregnancy, back and neck injuries, heart and vascular disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, epilepsy, recent surgery. Jumps stop in strong wind and thunderstorms; in the rainy season (May–November) there are often afternoon downpours.
monteverde-extremo-bungee.crowd_note: In the dry season and on holidays there can be queues for the gondola — arrive at opening time
monteverde-extremo-bungee.region: Puntarenas, Monteverde, ~3 km northwest of Santa Elena
monteverde-extremo-bungee.booking: Book via the park's website, Monteverde hotels or aggregators; better to go in the morning — in the afternoon cloud and wind can stop the jumps; the whole thing takes ~45 minutes
monteverde-extremo-bungee.record: The highest bungee in Central America (according to the park): a jump from a gondola above a 143 m-deep canyon
pros: The highest jump in Central America
A jump above the cloud forest
Tarzan swing and ziplines in the same park
Open year-round
cons: The free fall is noticeably shorter than the advertised 143 m
Frequent cloud and wind, especially in the afternoon
The road to Monteverde is slow and partly unpaved
monteverde-extremo-bungee.airport: LIR — Liberia, ~2.5 h; SJO — San José, ~3.5 h
monteverde-extremo-bungee.price_note: From EUR 98 on the Manawa aggregator, ~USD 100 on local sites; photos and video +USD 40
school_notes: Official website: bungee, mega Tarzan swing, 4 km of ziplines
Online booking with prices in euros
Marketplace of the Monteverde Chamber of Tourism

banos-san-francisco-bridge.description: Puenting — a pendulum jump on safety ropes from the San Francisco road bridge over the Pastaza river gorge, right by the town. The height is about 80 m; the jump is short but very sharp. It's a Baños classic alongside the “Swing at the End of the World”, rafting, canyoning and ziplines.
banos-san-francisco-bridge.rating_basis: Popular with backpackers for its low price and the Pastaza gorge; it's a pendulum jump on ropes, not classic bungee, and the safety standards are more basic
banos-san-francisco-bridge.hazards: Choose an agency with good reviews and check the equipment. The pendulum puts a heavy load on the back and neck — contraindicated with injuries, heart and blood pressure problems, pregnancy. The town is at ~1,800 m and the active Tungurahua volcano is nearby — keep an eye on the bulletins.
banos-san-francisco-bridge.crowd_note: Queues at weekends and on holidays, when tourists come from Quito
banos-san-francisco-bridge.region: Tungurahua, the northern edge of Baños de Agua Santa, above the Pastaza river
banos-san-francisco-bridge.booking: Book at any agency on the streets of Baños or online via Civitatis; the jump itself takes ~20 minutes, and you walk to the bridge from the centre
banos-san-francisco-bridge.record: One of the most affordable bridge jumps; Baños is called Ecuador's adventure capital
pros: Very cheap
The bridge is within walking distance of the centre
Lots of other activities in town, plus hot springs
cons: It's a pendulum jump on ropes, not an elastic bungee
Many small operators — equipment quality varies
Frequent rain and fog
banos-san-francisco-bridge.airport: UIO — Quito, ~3.5 h by bus or car
banos-san-francisco-bridge.price_note: From USD 27 on Civitatis (≈EUR 24 on Central de Reservas); agencies in town charge similar prices, photos and video extra
school_notes: Online booking from USD 27, the instructor speaks Spanish and English
Listing with a description (temporarily unavailable when checked)

artuby-bridge.description: An arch bridge over the Artuby gorge right by the Grand Canyon du Verdon — 182 m to the bottom. A jump with a view of limestone walls, followed by a 30-minute hike back up the trail. A classic of French bungee that's easy to combine with a trip around Provence.
artuby-bridge.rating_basis: France's highest jump, in every French round-up of the best bungee; the famous scenery of the Verdon Gorge
artuby-bridge.hazards: The climb out of the gorge is on a trail — you need comfortable shoes and water, and it's hot in summer; the winch lift is only for up to 90 kg. Standard contraindications: heart, blood pressure, back, pregnancy; from 55 a medical certificate is required. Jumps depend on the weather.
artuby-bridge.crowd_note: People jump in turn all day and a fast pass is sold for an extra fee — in season the wait stretches to hours
artuby-bridge.region: Var, Grand Canyon du Verdon, near the Balcons de la Mescla (Aiguines)
artuby-bridge.booking: April to mid-November. From April to mid-June and from mid-September to mid-November — Sundays only; from mid-June to mid-September — weekends; from mid-July to mid-August — Fri–Sun. It's a full-day event: check-in 9:00–12:00, and after the jump a 30-minute walk out of the canyon. Under-18s need parental permission, from 55 a medical certificate.
artuby-bridge.record: One of the highest jumps in Europe — 182 m above a tributary of the Verdon by the Grand Canyon
pros: One of the highest jumps in Europe — 182 m
Grand Canyon du Verdon scenery
Cheaper than in Switzerland and Austria
cons: Takes a whole day, long waits
A hike out of the canyon after the jump
Sundays only in spring and autumn
artuby-bridge.airport: NCE — Nice, ~2 h; MRS — Marseille, ~2 h 15 min
artuby-bridge.price_note: €140 per jump according to the Provence tourist office (rate valid until 2027), discount for groups of 4+; on Manawa — from €105, fast pass and video — €30 each
school_notes: Operator; briefing in French and English
Aggregator, from €105

ponsonnas-bridge.description: A 1941 stone arch bridge over the Drac river gorge — 103 m to the water. One of Europe's first permanent bungee sites, operating since 1988. Affordable, tandem jumps are possible, and every jump is filmed.
ponsonnas-bridge.rating_basis: A historic site (since 1988); 4.9/5 from 206 reviews on Funbooker and 4.95/5 from 75 reviews on Cap Adrénaline
ponsonnas-bridge.hazards: Standard contraindications: heart, blood pressure, back injuries, pregnancy; from 55 a medical certificate is required, over-60s are not accepted. Jumps depend on the weather.
ponsonnas-bridge.crowd_note: Small groups, rarely queues; few dates in 2026 because of repairs
ponsonnas-bridge.region: Isère, the Matheysine plateau near La Mure, ~40 km south of Grenoble
ponsonnas-bridge.booking: Usually April–November at weekends, almost daily in July–August (in 2026 — Mon, Wed, Thu and weekends, 10:00–17:00). The bridge is under repair in 2026: some dates are cancelled and full reopening is expected in 2027 — 2027 dates are already open on aggregators. Ages 13–60; from 55 a medical certificate is required.
ponsonnas-bridge.record: One of Europe's oldest bungee sites: jumps here since 1988
pros: One of Europe's oldest sites
Inexpensive — €98
Tandem jumps
From age 13
cons: Bridge repairs in 2026 — few dates
The height is modest next to the Alpine giants
Strict weight limit for women
ponsonnas-bridge.airport: LYS — Lyon-Saint Exupéry, ~1 h 45 min; GNB — Grenoble-Isère, ~1 h 15 min
ponsonnas-bridge.price_note: €98 per jump; tandem — €214 for two; groups of 4+ — €88, of 10+ — €75; video — €28
school_notes: Booking, prices and group discounts
Booking; warns about the bridge repairs in 2026

souleuvre-viaduct.description: The stone piers of a viaduct designed by Gustave Eiffel are all that's left of a 19th-century railway. AJ Hackett built a platform on the tallest of them: 61 m above the Souleuvre river, and you can ask for a water dip. Nearby are a giant swing, a pendulum swing, a 400 m zipline and a glass cube above the valley.
souleuvre-viaduct.rating_basis: A historic AJ Hackett site; 5/5 from 25 reviews on Manawa; not very high, but lots of activities
souleuvre-viaduct.hazards: Standard contraindications: heart disease and blood pressure, back and neck injuries, pregnancy, epilepsy. Jumps stop in strong wind and thunderstorms. The water touch is optional — the water is cold.
souleuvre-viaduct.crowd_note: Lots of families and groups in summer and at weekends — book a slot ahead
souleuvre-viaduct.booking: 2026 season — 4 April to 30 November: in spring and autumn at weekends and on public holidays 10:00–17:00, from 13 June to 31 August — daily 10:00–18:00. Online booking. Minors need written parental permission.
souleuvre-viaduct.record: AJ Hackett's first site in Europe (1990) — on a pier of a viaduct built to a design by Gustave Eiffel in 1887–1889
pros: The legendary operator AJ Hackett
You can touch the water
Swing, pendulum and zipline for the whole group
From age 12
cons: Not high — 61 m
Expensive for the height: €179
Changeable Normandy weather
souleuvre-viaduct.airport: CFR — Caen-Carpiquet, ~45 min; CDG — Paris, ~3 h 30 min
souleuvre-viaduct.price_note: €179 solo; students and under-18s — €119; a repeat jump — €99; tandem — from €198; photos or video — €40 each
school_notes: Operator; website in French

jumpin-heights-rishikesh.description: A jump from a cantilever platform jutting out 25 m over the cliff edge of the Hiunl river gorge in the Himalayan foothills — 83 m down to the rocky riverbed. It's India's main bungee site and a must after rafting and yoga in Rishikesh. The same site has a giant swing over the gorge and a flying fox almost a kilometre long.
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.rating_basis: India's best-known site, with an average rating of 4.7–4.8 from thousands of reviews; average height by world standards
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.hazards: Not allowed with heart disease, hypertension, back and neck problems, epilepsy or pregnancy. In the monsoon operations stop because of downpours, floods and wind; the mountain road gets washed out.
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.crowd_note: Very popular with Indian tourists: at weekends, on holidays and in May–June the wait can be several hours; a weekday morning is the best bet
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.region: Uttarakhand, Mohan Chatti village, ~25 km (45 min) from Tapovan in Rishikesh
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.booking: Online booking on the website is mandatory; at weekends and on holidays places go early. Shuttle from the Tapovan office at 9:15 and 13:15. Ages 12–45; under-18s only with a parent. Usually closed on Tuesdays — check
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.record: India's highest bungee from a fixed platform (83 m); operating since 2010 to New Zealand standards
pros: A professional operator with New Zealand standards
Inexpensive
Three attractions in one place
Easy to combine with rafting and yoga in Rishikesh
cons: Long queues at weekends and on holidays
Age limit of 45
Closed at the height of the monsoon (roughly mid-July to mid-September)
Heat of up to 37 °C in May–June
jumpin-heights-rishikesh.price_note: INR 3,700 (≈€36) including GST; giant swing — INR 3,700, flying fox INR 2,000–3,500, video from INR 900, shuttle from Tapovan INR 500, spectator entry INR 100
school_notes: Official website and online booking; also a site in Goa (~60 m)

ponte-colossus.description: A 152 m concrete viaduct above a valley in the Alpine foothills near Biella — Italy's first permanent bungee centre. About 5 seconds of free fall at up to 110 km/h, after which you're lowered to the valley floor. They jump even in the rain — only a strong crosswind cancels it.
ponte-colossus.rating_basis: CNN top 15; Italy's oldest permanent centre; 4.9/5 on Manawa
ponte-colossus.hazards: Not recommended with serious heart disease, neurological or joint problems, retinal disease, epilepsy, recurrent shoulder dislocation, pregnancy, or recent injuries and surgery. Weight 45–120 kg clothed.
ponte-colossus.crowd_note: Summer weekends fill up early, especially with groups
ponte-colossus.region: Piedmont, province of Biella, Veglio — ~1 h from Milan and Turin
ponte-colossus.booking: Jumps run at weekends from spring to autumn (April–October according to the Biella tourist office); the calendar on the website covers March to December. Booking is mandatory, online until 8:00 on the day of the jump. Minors need written parental consent, over-60s a medical certificate in advance. After the jump you're lowered to the valley floor and walk back up a trail; the whole programme takes ~1.5 h.
ponte-colossus.record: Italy's first permanent bungee centre (since the mid-1990s), No. 10 in CNN's top 15 highest jumps in the world
pros: 152 m — one of the highest jumps in Europe
Inexpensive — €110
They jump even in the rain
An hour's drive from Milan and Turin
cons: Weekends only
A walk back up after the jump, no lift
No public transport to the bridge — you need a shuttle or a car
ponte-colossus.airport: MXP — Milan Malpensa, ~1 h 15 min; TRN — Turin, ~1 h 15 min
ponte-colossus.price_note: €110 per jump; a repeat jump (with a Bungee Card or certificate) — €90; for groups of 7+ one jump is free; video — €20–30
school_notes: Operator; calendar and prices, website in Italian and English

valgadena-bridge.description: A 1990 concrete bridge on the Asiago plateau over the deep Valgadena gorge: according to the operator, at 175 m it's the highest bridge jump in Italy. It's a club-association, not an attraction: jumps run to a schedule, payment is in cash, and you need a medical certificate. In return, it's cheaper than in Switzerland and Austria.
valgadena-bridge.rating_basis: CNN top 15; 4.9/5 from 63 reviews on CheckYeti; the site has been running for more than 20 years
valgadena-bridge.hazards: Contraindications are listed on the operator's website (heart, blood pressure, back, etc.); no one is allowed to jump without a medical certificate. Weather on the plateau is changeable: in thunderstorms and strong wind jumps are postponed.
valgadena-bridge.crowd_note: Jumps run to a schedule, with small groups on jump dates
valgadena-bridge.region: Veneto, the Asiago plateau (Sette Comuni), between Enego and Foza
valgadena-bridge.booking: Jumps on fixed dates, mostly at weekends from mid-March to November (about 45 dates in 2026). An application via the form on the website is confirmed only after contact on WhatsApp. On the day of the jump you need a medical certificate of fitness for sport. Under-18s need a parent present or their written permission.
valgadena-bridge.record: According to the operator, Italy's highest bridge; No. 7 in CNN's top 15 highest jumps in the world (175 m)
pros: One of the highest jumps in Europe
Inexpensive — about €110 including the membership fee
High ratings on aggregators
cons: You need a medical certificate of fitness for sport
Cash only, and confirmation via WhatsApp
Fixed dates, mostly at weekends
valgadena-bridge.airport: VCE — Venice, ~1 h 45 min; VRN — Verona, ~1 h 45 min
valgadena-bridge.price_note: €90 per jump + €20 association membership fee; photos or video — €15, both — €25; cash only
school_notes: Operator (an association); dates and application form, website in Italian and English
Aggregator, 4.9/5 from 63 reviews

gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.description: A jump from the 462 m Shin-Tabisoko road bridge, spanning the Tabisoko river valley in the Gifu mountains at a height of about 200 m — 215 m of free flight. It's Japan's highest bungee, opened in 2020. It's easiest to get there by car from Nagoya; from the car park you walk through a tunnel to the check-in desk.
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.rating_basis: 215 m — a Japanese record and among the world's top bridge jumps; a bridge ~200 m above a gorge, operated by Bungy Japan
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.hazards: Health restrictions: heart, blood pressure, back, pregnancy. Operations are suspended in bad weather — thunderstorms, typhoons (August–October), strong wind.
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.crowd_note: Bookings in hourly blocks; at weekends and on Japanese public holidays slots sell out in advance
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.region: Gifu Prefecture, Yaotsu, the Shin-Tabisoko Bridge over the Tabisoko river valley; ~1.5–2 h from Nagoya
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.booking: Book online or by phone on 0278-72-8133, in 60-minute blocks. Cancelling the day before costs 50%, on the day of the jump 100%. Open year-round: April–September 9:00–17:30, October–March 8:30–17:00. ~700 m on foot from the car park through a tunnel
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.record: Japan's highest bungee (215 m, opened in August 2020) and one of the highest bridge jumps in the world
pros: A Japanese-record 215 m
Open year-round
A scenic mountain gorge
A discount if you've already jumped from another Bungy Japan bridge
cons: Expensive — JPY 28,000
Hard without a car: train to Mino-Ōta and a ~30-minute taxi
Strict cancellation rules
Weight limit of 100 kg
gifu-bungy-shin-tabisoko.price_note: First jump JPY 28,000 (≈€161), a second the same day JPY 13,000, for “regular jumpers” with a certificate — JPY 18,000; JPY 1,000 off if you've already jumped at another Bungy Japan site. Cash only
school_notes: Website in English and Japanese

minakami-suwakyo-bungy.description: A jump from the Suwakyo Bridge, 42 m above the Tone river right in the middle of Minakami — Japan's rafting and canyoning capital. You can get there from Tokyo in 1.5 hours by shinkansen plus a bus. On the same day you can also jump from the operator's second bridge — Sarugakyo (62 m), a 20-minute drive away.
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.rating_basis: A low but scenic jump over the Tone river in the middle of an outdoor-activity resort; a Bungy Japan classic
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.hazards: Health restrictions: heart, blood pressure, back, pregnancy. Jumps stop when the river is high (snowmelt, the tsuyu rains in June) and during typhoons.
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.crowd_note: Open only 2 days a week, so at weekends and on holidays slots go early; without a booking you can wait for hours
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.region: Gunma Prefecture, Minakami town, ~1 km south of Minakami station; ~2 h from Tokyo
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.booking: Booking online or by phone on 0278-72-8133 is essential for a convenient time. 2026 season: April – 31 October, Fridays and Saturdays only; 9:00–17:30 (until 17:00 in October). Under-18s with a parent or signed consent
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.record: Japan's oldest operating bridge bungee site (since 2007)
pros: Easy to reach from Tokyo
Can be combined with rafting and canyoning in Minakami
A combo with the higher Sarugakyo Bridge
cons: Only 42 m
Open only April–October, and only on Fridays and Saturdays
Cash only
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.airport: HND / NRT — Tokyo, ~2.5–3 h by train
minakami-suwakyo-bungy.price_note: First jump JPY 12,000 (≈€69), a second the same day JPY 6,000, a repeat on another day JPY 7,000; combo with the Sarugakyo Bridge (62 m) on the same day — JPY 19,000. Cash only
school_notes: Website in English and Japanese

ryujin-bridge-bungy.description: A jump from the middle of the 375 m Ryujin suspension bridge in Ibaraki Prefecture — 100 m down to a reservoir in a wooded gorge. For a long time it was Japan's highest bungee; after the jump an electric winch hauls you back up to the bridge. In autumn the gorge turns red with maples, and that's the most beautiful time to jump.
ryujin-bridge-bungy.rating_basis: 100 m above a lake in a wooded gorge, more than 10,000 jumps a year; especially beautiful in November during the maple season
ryujin-bridge-bungy.hazards: Health restrictions: heart, blood pressure, back, pregnancy. Jumps stop during typhoons (August–October) and thunderstorms; in winter the bridge is cold and windy.
ryujin-bridge-bungy.crowd_note: More than 10,000 jumpers a year: at weekends, on holidays and in the red-maple season (November) the wait without a booking is up to 3 hours
ryujin-bridge-bungy.region: Ibaraki Prefecture, Hitachiota city, the Ryujin Great Suspension Bridge over a reservoir; ~2.5 h from Tokyo
ryujin-bridge-bungy.booking: Booking is essential, especially for weekends and holidays: without one the wait is up to 3 hours. Open year-round, 9:00–11:00 and 12:00–17:30; check operating days by phone on 0278-72-8133. One companion can watch from the platform for an extra fee
ryujin-bridge-bungy.record: 100 m — Japan's second-highest permanent bungee (after Gifu, 215 m); the 375 m bridge is one of the country's longest pedestrian suspension bridges
pros: 100 m of free flight
A beautiful gorge, especially in November
Open year-round
GoPro video included
cons: Awkward without a car: the bus from Hitachiota station runs 3–4 times a day
Queues at weekends
Cash only
ryujin-bridge-bungy.airport: IBR — Ibaraki, ~1.5 h by car; NRT / HND — Tokyo, ~2.5 h
ryujin-bridge-bungy.price_note: First jump JPY 19,000 (≈€109), a second the same day JPY 8,000, a repeat on another day JPY 11,000; GoPro video included. Cash only
school_notes: Website in English and Japanese

macau-tower.description: A jump from the outer rim of the Macau Tower at 233 m — about 4–5 seconds of free fall at up to 200 km/h, braking 30 m above the ground. Guide cables secure the fall, so the jump is both extreme and very high-tech. The same platform offers the SkyJump (a cable-controlled descent), the SkyWalk around the edge and a climb up the tower's mast.
macau-tower.rating_basis: A Guinness record, consistently in the top 3 highest commercial bungee jumps in the world, the legendary operator AJ Hackett
macau-tower.hazards: Not allowed with heart or blood pressure problems, epilepsy, pregnancy, recent surgery and injuries, or a history of dislocations. Jumps stop in typhoons, strong wind, thunderstorms and downpours — typhoon season is June–October.
macau-tower.crowd_note: Queues on the platform at weekends and on Chinese holidays; weekday mornings are quieter (there's a discount for early slots)
macau-tower.region: Macau Peninsula, the Macau Tower, platform at 233 m
macau-tower.booking: Book on the Skypark website or via aggregators (Klook, LocalTours in Russian); open daily: Mon–Fri 11:00–19:00, Sat–Sun 10:30–19:30. Under-18s only with a parent, who signs a liability waiver
macau-tower.record: Guinness record: the highest commercial bungee jump from a building (233 m); one of the highest bungee jumps in the world
pros: One of the highest bungee jumps in the world
Open daily, year-round
Can be combined with the SkyWalk and the mast climb
Easy to reach from Hong Kong by ferry or via the bridge
cons: Expensive: ≈€330 without photos and video
Views of the city and construction sites, not nature
Heat, thunderstorms and typhoons in summer — jumps get suspended
macau-tower.airport: MFM — Macau, ~15 min; HKG — Hong Kong, ~45 min via the HZMB bridge
macau-tower.price_note: Solo jump MOP 3,088 (≈€330): tower entry ticket, T-shirt, e-certificate; photos and video as a separate package. Tandem MOP 5,488, SkyJump MOP 2,188, SkyWalk MOP 788, Tower Climb MOP 2,688
school_notes: Official operator, website in English and Chinese
Russian-language ticket reseller; staff on site speak English and Chinese

kushma-bungee.description: A jump from a 520 m suspension bridge 228 m above the Kali Gandaki gorge between Kushma and Balewa — according to the operator, the second-highest bungee on the planet after Macau. The free fall lasts about 5–7 seconds. The Cliff site also has a giant swing, a “sky cycle” on a cable, a café above the abyss and overnight stays in tents and cottages.
kushma-bungee.rating_basis: 228 m — according to the operator and Wikipedia, the second-highest jump in the world after Macau; popular on social media, around 300 visitors a day
kushma-bungee.hazards: Not allowed with heart disease, blood pressure or back problems, or pregnancy. Operations stop in thunderstorms and strong wind; in the monsoon (June–September) landslides wash out the Pokhara–Kushma road.
kushma-bungee.crowd_note: Up to 300 visitors a day, busiest at weekends and during Nepali festivals (Dashain, Tihar); arrive at opening time
kushma-bungee.region: Parbat, the Kali Gandaki river gorge, 62 km from Pokhara
kushma-bungee.booking: Book by phone/WhatsApp or through agencies in Pokhara (a day tour with transfer). No tandem jumps; there are tents and cottages nearby for an overnight stay
kushma-bungee.record: The second-highest bungee jump in the world (228 m) and the highest in Nepal; the same bridge has the “world's highest swing”
pros: Near-record height for next to nothing
The wild Kali Gandaki gorge
A day trip from Pokhara
A swing and other attractions on the same bridge
cons: Age 18+ and up to 105 kg only
~2 hours from Pokhara on a mountain road
No tandem jumps
Fog and landslides in the monsoon
kushma-bungee.price_note: NPR 8,000 (≈€49) — the same price for Nepalis and foreigners; photos, video and T-shirt extra; a repeat jump the same day NPR 4,000. Press reports from 2023 quoted NPR 7,500
school_notes: Prices, rules and contacts (WhatsApp/Viber)

last-resort-bhote-koshi.description: A jump from a 166 m pedestrian suspension bridge strung across the Bhote Koshi river gorge right by the Tibetan border: 160 m and about 5 seconds of free fall towards the churning water. It's Nepal's first and best-known bungee site. Nearby are a canyon swing, a tandem swing, canyoning and rafting, and on the riverbank a tented camp where you can stay the night.
last-resort-bhote-koshi.rating_basis: A Nepal classic: 160 m above a wild river in a narrow gorge, a Swiss-designed bridge, good reviews on safety; features on lists of the highest bridge jumps
last-resort-bhote-koshi.hazards: Not allowed with heart disease, hypertension, epilepsy, asthma, recent surgery, orthopaedic or neurological problems, pregnancy, or when intoxicated. In the monsoon (June–September) landslides block the Araniko Highway, and the trip can drag on or fall through: in August 2025 the highway was closed by landslides for 11 days.
last-resort-bhote-koshi.crowd_note: People jump in groups on the day-tour schedule; queues are short, but in October–November tours from Kathmandu are best booked ahead
last-resort-bhote-koshi.region: Sindhupalchok, the Araniko Highway, ~100 km from Kathmandu and ~12 km from the Tibetan border
last-resort-bhote-koshi.booking: Book on the website or at the office on Mandala Street in Thamel (pay at least 3 days ahead); the bus leaves Thamel around 6:00 and the drive takes 3.5–4.5 hours. You can stay overnight in the tented camp by the bridge. Under-18s with a parent
last-resort-bhote-koshi.record: Nepal's first bungee site; 160 m above the river — one of the highest bridge jumps in the world, and the same site has one of the longest canyon swings
pros: A very high jump in a real mountain gorge
Inexpensive for the height
Can be combined with the canyon swing, canyoning and rafting
Overnight stay in the camp by the bridge
cons: A long drive from Kathmandu on a mountain road
Strict bungee weight limit — up to 98 kg
Monsoon in summer: fog, downpours and landslides on the Araniko Highway
last-resort-bhote-koshi.price_note: Jump only USD 92 (≈€79); a day tour from Kathmandu with transfer and lunch — USD 108, bungee + canyon swing — USD 137, a second jump or swing — USD 55
school_notes: Official operator, prices in USD, website in English

pokhara-highground-bungee.description: A jump from an 80 m cantilever tower in the Hemja valley near Pokhara (guidebooks quote 70–75 m of flight), with views of Himalayan peaks. It's the easiest way to jump in Nepal without a long drive: the transfer from Lakeside takes 20 minutes. Tandems are available, and the same operator runs the ZipFlyer from Sarangkot and paragliding flights.
pokhara-highground-bungee.rating_basis: A modest cantilever tower, but with views of Annapurna and Machapuchare and just 20 minutes from Pokhara; good reviews as a “first bungee”
pokhara-highground-bungee.hazards: Health restrictions: heart, blood pressure, back, pregnancy, recent surgery. Jumps stop in thunderstorms and downpours; Pokhara is Nepal's rainiest city (June–September).
pokhara-highground-bungee.crowd_note: Slots by booking, usually no queues; more tourists in October–November
pokhara-highground-bungee.booking: Instant online booking on the website or at the office on Lakeside Road (Barahi Chowk); photo ID required. Open daily; closed-toe shoes are mandatory, skirts and flip-flops are not allowed
pokhara-highground-bungee.record: The only tower bungee site in Nepal
pros: 20 minutes from Pokhara
Cheap
Views of Annapurna in clear weather
Tandem jumps available
cons: Modest height for Nepal
A tower, not a gorge
In the monsoon clouds hide the mountains, frequent downpours
pokhara-highground-bungee.price_note: From NPR 5,000 (≈€31) for a solo jump per the operator's website; tandem NPR 9,500 with transfer from Lakeside. Older guidebooks quote NPR 8,700–13,000 depending on nationality — check
school_notes: Tower operator; also ZipFlyer, paragliding and quad bikes

auckland-harbour-bridge.description: A jump from a pod under the deck of Auckland Harbour Bridge — 40 m down to the waters of the Waitematā Harbour. You can ask to dunk your head in the ocean (depending on the tide) or jump in tandem. The jump is easy to combine with the Bridge Climb tour.
auckland-harbour-bridge.rating_basis: A city jump with a panorama of Auckland and the harbour, plus an ocean touch; low, but convenient for travellers passing through
auckland-harbour-bridge.hazards: The usual contraindications: pregnancy, photosensitive epilepsy, heart, blood pressure, back. In windy and rainy weather (especially in winter) jumps may be rescheduled.
auckland-harbour-bridge.crowd_note: Usually no queues; more groups on summer weekends
auckland-harbour-bridge.region: Auckland, the bridge over the Waitematā Harbour; starts at Westhaven Marina, 5–10 min from the centre
auckland-harbour-bridge.booking: Book on bungy.co.nz; meeting point at 105 Curran Street, Westhaven Marina (free parking). Open daily 9:00–16:30, except Christmas Day. For a water touch, ask the jump master at check-in
auckland-harbour-bridge.record: Auckland's only bungee — a jump towards the sea from the city's main bridge
pros: Within the city, handy before a flight out of Auckland
An ocean water touch
Tandem jumps
Combo with the Bridge Climb tour
cons: Only 40 m
A water touch isn't guaranteed — it depends on the tide
auckland-harbour-bridge.price_note: A single jump from NZD 260 (child from NZD 220), photos, video and T-shirt included when booked direct; combo with the Bridge Climb — NZD 325; spectators — NZD 20
school_notes: Official booking; combo with the Bridge Climb

kawarau-bridge.description: A historic 1880 suspension bridge over the emerald Kawarau River — this is where the world's first commercial bungee site opened in 1988. It's 43 m to the water; you can ask for a river touch (depending on the water level, not guaranteed) or jump in tandem. Nearby are a swing over the gorge, a short zipline and the wineries of the Gibbston Valley.
kawarau-bridge.rating_basis: The “home of bungee” and the first commercial site (Wikipedia, AJ Hackett), the turquoise Kawarau River, a must-do in Queenstown
kawarau-bridge.hazards: Not for pregnant women or people with photosensitive epilepsy; with osteoporosis, scoliosis or a recent concussion you need a doctor's certificate. It's cold by the river in winter — bring a jacket. With a water touch your head and shoulders may go into the cold river.
kawarau-bridge.crowd_note: In summer and on holidays there's a queue on the bridge and lots of spectators; morning slots are quieter
kawarau-bridge.region: Otago, the Gibbston Valley, 23 km from Queenstown on SH6
kawarau-bridge.booking: Book direct on bungy.co.nz; in summer (December–February) a few days ahead. Allow 1.5 h if you drive yourself, 2.5 h by bus from central Queenstown. Hours: October–April 8:30–17:00, May–September 9:00–16:30, daily except Christmas Day. Spectators watch for free
kawarau-bridge.record: The world's first commercial bungee site — AJ Hackett opened it in 1988
pros: A historic site — the “home of bungee”
Water touch and tandem jumps
Photos and video included when booked direct
20–25 minutes from Queenstown, reachable under your own steam
cons: Expensive for 43 m
Crowded in summer
When the water is high the weight limit drops to 130 kg
kawarau-bridge.price_note: A single jump from NZD 320 (child from NZD 280); booking direct includes photos and video, a T-shirt and the bus from Queenstown. Swing NZD 240, zipline NZD 50
school_notes: Official booking; combo with the Nevis available

ledge-bungy.description: A platform above the slope near the top of the Skyline gondola, 400 m above Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu. Here you jump with a run-up in a waist harness — you can dive, do a flip or simply step off. The most spectacular option is an evening jump into the darkness above the city lights.
ledge-bungy.rating_basis: The best view of Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu, evening jumps above the city lights; not very high
ledge-bungy.hazards: The usual contraindications: pregnancy, heart, back and blood pressure problems. On winter evenings it's cold and windy at the top; the walking tracks up Bob's Peak aren't recommended in winter.
ledge-bungy.crowd_note: Usually no long queues; the Skyline gondola can have queues in summer
ledge-bungy.region: Queenstown, Bob's Peak by the top station of the Skyline gondola, 400 m above the town
ledge-bungy.booking: The site is temporarily closed because of staff shortages; AJ Hackett promises to reopen it in summer 2026/27 (newzealand.com says “from November 2026”), for now booking is via a waiting list. Normally open daily 13:00–20:00; up via the Skyline gondola from Brecon St
ledge-bungy.record: Run-up bungee in a waist harness above the lights of Queenstown; the jump closest to the town centre
pros: Five minutes' walk from the centre plus the gondola
You can jump with a run-up and freestyle
Evening jumps above the lights of Queenstown
Open in the afternoon until 20:00
cons: Temporarily closed — check the status before you go
The gondola is paid for separately
Only 47 m
ledge-bungy.airport: ZQN — Queenstown, ~20 min to the gondola's bottom station
ledge-bungy.price_note: A single jump NZD 240; the Skyline gondola ticket isn't included and is bought separately; swing NZD 210
school_notes: Official page; currently a waiting list until it reopens

nevis-bungy.description: A pod cabin hangs on cables above the Nevis River canyon, and you reach it in a small cable car. 134 m and 8.5 seconds of fall — the highest jump in New Zealand. The same site has the Nevis Swing (the world's biggest swing) and a catapult, and the road there crosses private land in an off-road bus.
nevis-bungy.rating_basis: The country's highest jump and one of the highest bungee platforms in the world (Wikipedia), a wild canyon, cult status among Queenstown visitors
nevis-bungy.hazards: Not for pregnant women or people with photosensitive epilepsy; with osteoporosis, scoliosis or a recent concussion — a doctor's certificate. Glasses come off (free protective goggles with prescription lenses are provided). Closed-toe shoes required, warm layers in winter. May be cancelled in strong wind.
nevis-bungy.crowd_note: The flow is regulated by the buses, so there's little queuing, but in summer places go early
nevis-bungy.region: Otago, the Nevis River valley, ~45 min by bus from Queenstown
nevis-bungy.booking: Booking only (changes and cancellations up to 48 h ahead). You can't drive there yourself: a 4×4 bus from the Queenstown Bungy Centre (corner of Shotover and Camp St); the whole trip takes about 4 hours. Departures vary by season — in August 2026 the bus ran Thursday–Monday at 8:40, 10:00 and 12:00
nevis-bungy.record: New Zealand's highest bungee jump — 134 m and 8.5 seconds of flight; also home to the world's biggest swing and the first catapult
pros: The highest jump in the country
A wild mountain canyon without crowds of spectators
Transfer, photos and video included
You can do the “trilogy”: jump, swing and catapult
cons: Expensive
Minimum age 13, weight from 45 kg
The trip takes about 4 hours
Fewer departures and cold in winter
nevis-bungy.airport: ZQN — Queenstown, ~20 min to the centre, then ~45 min by bus
nevis-bungy.price_note: A single jump NZD 395 (same price for adults and children); includes the 4×4 bus from Queenstown, photos and video, T-shirt. Swing NZD 325, catapult NZD 295, combo of all three — NZD 805
school_notes: Official booking; combos with the swing, catapult and Kawarau
Booking via a Russian-language interface; service on site in English

taupo-bungy.description: A cantilever platform juts out from a cliff above the Waikato River a few minutes from Lake Taupō: 47 m down to turquoise water. You can ask for a river touch or jump in tandem, and next door there's a swing over the same gorge. A good option for those travelling around the North Island who won't make it to Queenstown.
taupo-bungy.rating_basis: A beautiful turquoise river, a water touch, easy to combine with other Taupō activities (skydiving, jetboating)
taupo-bungy.hazards: The usual contraindications: pregnancy, photosensitive epilepsy, heart, blood pressure, back. Chilly in winter; in strong wind jumps may be rescheduled.
taupo-bungy.crowd_note: Busy in summer and during school holidays, but there are usually no long queues
taupo-bungy.region: Taupō, North Island, a cliff above the Waikato River (202 Spa Road), 5–10 min from the centre
taupo-bungy.booking: Book on bungy.co.nz; free cancellation up to 48 h ahead. In autumn 2026 the site closed for rebuilding — the bungee reopens on 12 November, the swing on 5 November. Hours: weekdays 9:30–16:00, weekends until 17:00 (until 17:00 in summer), closed on Christmas Day
taupo-bungy.record: New Zealand's only cliff-edge bungee — a cantilever platform above the turquoise Waikato
pros: Water touch and tandem jumps
Within the town, close to skydiving and jetboating
A beautiful turquoise gorge
cons: The height of a city site
A water touch isn't guaranteed
Check the schedule after the autumn 2026 rebuild
taupo-bungy.airport: TUO — Taupō, ~15 min; AKL — Auckland, ~3.5 h by car
taupo-bungy.price_note: A single jump from NZD 275 (child from NZD 235), photos, video and T-shirt when booked direct; swing NZD 240; combos with jetboating, rafting or skydiving NZD 361–785
school_notes: Official booking, combos with the swing and skydiving
Prices, hours, family rate NZD 785 (2 adults + 2 children aged 10–14)

action-valley-cusco.description: An adventure park in the valley near Poroy, 20 minutes from Cusco: a platform jump with 122 m of free fall — one of the highest in South America. The same park has the Slingshot catapult, which launches you up to 130 m in 4 seconds, a swing and a “sky bike”. Easy to combine with a trip to Machu Picchu.
action-valley-cusco.rating_basis: One of the highest jumps on the continent, at 3,600 m above sea level near Cusco and Machu Picchu; 4.6 out of 5 in Google reviews (117 reviews)
action-valley-cusco.hazards: Acclimatise in Cusco for 1–2 days first: the 3,600 m altitude puts extra strain on the heart. Not open to pregnant women or people with epilepsy; with osteoporosis, scoliosis or a recent concussion you need a doctor's certificate; also contraindicated with heart disease and hypertension. In the rainy season thunderstorms and cancellations are possible.
action-valley-cusco.crowd_note: Short queues; more groups from Cusco in the dry season (June–August)
action-valley-cusco.region: Cusco, Poroy district, 11 km (~20 min) from central Cusco
action-valley-cusco.booking: Book at the Action Valley office at Calle Santa Teresa 325 in Cusco or through agencies; departure in the morning (~9:00), the whole thing takes about 3 hours
action-valley-cusco.record: Latin America's highest bungee according to the operator: 122 m of free fall; the park has been running since 2001, with more than 500,000 jumps
pros: A huge free-fall height
20 minutes from Cusco
The Slingshot catapult — a rare attraction
Inexpensive for the height
cons: 3,600 m altitude — acclimatisation needed
Rain from November to March
Its own website has no online price list
action-valley-cusco.price_note: Bungee only ~USD 74, bungee + catapult USD 105–120 (Civitatis, Nomades) or PEN 600 with Condor Xtreme; transfer from Cusco PEN 40, photos and video USD 20
school_notes: The park's official website: bungee, Slingshot catapult, “sky bike”
Cusco agency: bungee + catapult with transfer, PEN 600
Online booking for bungee with catapult from USD 105, with transfer

skypark-sochi-bungy-207.description: A jump from a pod in the middle of the Skybridge suspension bridge, 207 m above the Akhshtyr Gorge — about 7 seconds of free fall. The same park has Bungy 69 from the start of the bridge (age 10+, tandem available), Bungy 207 PRO from the roof of the pod, the SochiSwing over the abyss, a zipline and the MegaTroll trolley at up to 120 km/h.
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.rating_basis: One of the highest bungee jumps in the world and the highest in Russia; views of the Akhshtyr Gorge, the Mzymta valley and the sea; Russia's best-known jump site (Lenta.ru)
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.hazards: Contraindications: blood pressure, heart, spine, recent injuries and surgery, pregnancy (full list on the park's website). Jumps are suspended in strong wind and thunderstorms, and in bad weather the weight limit may be tightened. In winter the walkways are slippery — wear shoes with good soles.
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.crowd_note: Peak season is July–September; the bridge is narrow, so it's best to arrive at opening time. The jump time is assigned by the instructor; online booking is essential in season
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.region: Krasnodar Krai, Sochi, Kazachiy Brod village, the Akhshtyr Gorge (on the road to Krasnaya Polyana)
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.booking: Tickets online, by phone or by e-mail (online until the day before); arrive at least 30 minutes early. Attractions operate Wed–Sun 10:30–17:00 with a lunch break; jumps are suspended in strong wind and thunderstorms
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.record: Russia's highest bungee jump (207 m, according to the operator); the 439 m Skybridge is one of the longest pedestrian suspension bridges in the world
pros: Russia's highest bungee, ~7 s of free fall
Everything in Russian, online booking
Open year-round, 30–40 minutes from Sochi airport
Lots of other attractions in the same park
cons: Expensive: 24,000 ₽ plus the entry ticket and video
Age 18+ only
Closed Mon–Tue, a break in the middle of the day
In winter attractions close during snowfall and wind
skypark-sochi-bungy-207.price_note: Bungy 207 — 24,000 ₽ (~€250 at ~95 ₽/€) + a compulsory park entry ticket; media package 3,000 ₽ if prepaid or 3,500 ₽ after the jump. Bungy 207 PRO from the pod roof (210 m, only after a classic jump) — 15,000 ₽; Bungy 69 from the start of the bridge — 12,000 ₽ (ages 14–17 8,000 ₽, ages 10–13 5,000 ₽); SochiSwing — 9,000 ₽
school_notes: Official jump page, prices and rules in Russian
A 69 m jump from the start of the bridge, age 10+, tandem available

sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.description: A jump over the Sulak Canyon — one of the deepest in Europe — at the former Nokhyo tunnel complex, where caves are linked by a 70 m suspension bridge. Nearby are a giant swing over the abyss and a 500 m zipline with a 250 m drop. Check the format (elastic cord or rope with a pendulum swing) and the height on site.
sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.rating_basis: The Sulak Canyon is one of Dagestan's main sights, and the Nokhyo complex is very popular with tourists; the jump height and operator aren't publicly documented
sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.hazards: No public data on equipment certification; in 2021 two tourists in Dagestan fell from a faulty swing above the canyon (they miraculously survived) — check the gear and ask about insurance. Contraindications as for bungee: blood pressure, heart, spine, pregnancy. Operations are suspended in rain and strong wind.
sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.crowd_note: At weekends and in the middle of the day the queue for the Tarzan swing and the swings is several hours; for double the price you can skip the queue
sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.region: Dagestan, the Sulak Canyon near the village of Dubki, ~70 km from Makhachkala (approximate coordinates)
sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.booking: Pay on site; arrive at opening time or on a weekday — at weekends and in the middle of the day the queue is several hours. Usually part of “Sulak Canyon and Nokhyo caves” excursions from Makhachkala, Kaspiysk, Izberbash and Derbent (the boat trip through the canyon is extra)
pros: A spectacular view of the turquoise Sulak in a deep canyon
Easy to combine with a boat trip, the zipline and the viewpoints at Dubki
Everything in Russian, 1.5 hours from Makhachkala
cons: Queues lasting hours in season
No official website, no age or weight rules and no data on the height
Hot in the canyon in summer — April–May and September–October are better
sulak-canyon-nokhyo-tarzanka.price_note: Tarzan swing from 7,000 ₽ (~€74 at ~95 ₽/€), queue-skip ~14,000 ₽; giant swing over the abyss from 5,000 ₽ (queue-skip 10,000 ₽); entry to the Nokhyo cave complex 500 ₽; insurance and a helmet are compulsory

tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.description: Rope jumping (a jump on an ordinary rope with climbing shock absorbers, not an elastic cord) from the edge of the Tsolotl Canyon next to the Tobot waterfall. First about 70 m of free fall, then a pendulum swing over the abyss. There's also a swing over the cliff nearby.
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.rating_basis: A high jump next to a 70 m waterfall on the edge of a huge canyon; a popular stop on tours of mountainous Dagestan; the operator and rules aren't publicly documented
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.hazards: No public information on equipment certification — choose an organiser with reviews and ask about insurance. Contraindications as for bungee: blood pressure, heart, spine, pregnancy. Don't jump in rain or strong wind; the mountain road is dangerous after downpours.
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.crowd_note: Most visitors are summer tour groups in the daytime; early mornings and weekdays are quieter
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.region: Dagestan, Khunzakh District, the edge of the Tsolotl Canyon near the village of Arani, ~3 km from Khunzakh, ~140 km from Makhachkala (approximate coordinates)
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.booking: Pay and jump on site, usually as part of an excursion from Makhachkala, Kaspiysk or Izberbash to Khunzakh and Matlas; it's a mountain road, and after rain there can be restrictions because of landslides
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.record: Dagestan's highest Tarzan swing: a jump from a 100 m cliff with a fall of about 70–75 m (according to T—Zh)
pros: One of the most spectacular jumps in the Caucasus: a waterfall and a canyon
Easy to combine with an excursion to Khunzakh and the Matlas plateau
Everything in Russian
cons: No official website and no published age or weight rules
Far from Makhachkala: ~3 hours on a mountain road
Operating season not confirmed — check before you go
tobot-waterfall-tarzanka.price_note: From 10,000 ₽ (~€105 at ~95 ₽/€), according to nashaplaneta.net; check the price and operator on site. There's a similar rope-jumping site on the neighbouring Matlas plateau (Tarzan swing from 5,000 ₽)

solkan-bridge.description: A jump from a 55 m road bridge over the emerald Soča — right next to the stone Solkan Bridge. Not high, but cheap and very photogenic. Easy to combine with kayaking on the Soča and a trip to neighbouring Gorizia in Italy.
solkan-bridge.rating_basis: A low jump, but a very scenic location: the emerald Soča and the famous stone bridge
solkan-bridge.hazards: You need to be in good health: standard contraindications (heart, blood pressure, back, pregnancy). Jumps are cancelled in thunderstorms and strong wind.
solkan-bridge.crowd_note: Almost no queues, but it operates only at weekends
solkan-bridge.region: Goriška, the Soča valley, on the outskirts of Nova Gorica
solkan-bridge.booking: Mid-May to mid-October, Saturdays and Sundays only (according to Yumping, 10:00–15:30). Advance booking required; the next date on the operator's website is May 2027. Minors need a parent's signature.
solkan-bridge.record: Slovenia's only bungee operator, running since 1993; next door is the Solkan Bridge, with the world's largest stone railway arch (85 m)
pros: Inexpensive — about €70
The emerald Soča and a view of the stone bridge
Kayaking and an adventure park nearby
cons: Only 55 m
Weekends only, May to October
Little information and no online prices on the website
solkan-bridge.airport: TRS — Trieste, ~45 min; LJU — Ljubljana, ~1 h 15 min
solkan-bridge.price_note: €70 per jump according to the Vipava Valley tourism portal; a gift voucher on Yumping — from €150
school_notes: Operator; website in Slovenian, English and Italian

chiang-mai-x-centre.description: A jump from a 50 m tower over a pond in the green Mae Rim valley near Chiang Mai. You can choose whether or not to touch the water. The site has been running since 1992 and is considered the most “jungly” in Thailand; easy to combine with a trip to the waterfalls and elephant parks on the road to Samoeng.
chiang-mai-x-centre.rating_basis: A well-run site with good reviews, but only 50 m above a pond; valued for its safety and the greenery around it
chiang-mai-x-centre.hazards: Not allowed with pregnancy, hypertension, heart disease, neurological disorders, epilepsy, asthma, a history of shoulder dislocation, or after drinking alcohol. In March–April there's heavy smog (field-burning season); in the rainy season jumps are suspended during thunderstorms.
chiang-mai-x-centre.crowd_note: Almost no queues; busier in December–January and over Chinese New Year
chiang-mai-x-centre.region: Chiang Mai, Mae Rim district, the Mae Rim – Samoeng road, ~30 min from the centre
chiang-mai-x-centre.booking: Online via aggregators (Pelago, Ticket2Attraction) or at Chiang Mai tour agencies; daily 9:00–18:00, the jump itself with the briefing takes 20–30 minutes. Transfer from town extra
chiang-mai-x-centre.record: Chiang Mai's only bungee; operating since 1992 to New Zealand standards
pros: A beautiful green valley
You can touch the water
Inexpensive, often discounted online
Close to the waterfalls and parks of Mae Rim
cons: Only 50 m
Transfer costs extra
February–April — haze from forest fires, May–October — rain
chiang-mai-x-centre.price_note: THB 2,500 (≈€66) list price, discounted by online agents from THB 1,990: jump, insurance, certificate; transfer not included
school_notes: Online booking; instructors speak English
Discounted tickets, contact via WhatsApp/Line

pattaya-xbungy.description: A jump from a 60 m platform over a lake on the outskirts of Pattaya — the highest bungee in Thailand. Tandem jumps are possible, and next door Sanook park has a human slingshot, paintball and go-karts. A handy way to “jump between beach days”: 15–20 minutes by taxi from the centre.
pattaya-xbungy.rating_basis: The highest in Thailand, 4.5/5 from ~400 Google reviews; but it's a jump over an artificial lake in a city amusement park
pattaya-xbungy.hazards: Not allowed with pregnancy, hypertension, heart disease, epilepsy, asthma, neck, back or eye injuries, or when intoxicated; don't eat a heavy meal before jumping. Jumps are suspended during thunderstorms.
pattaya-xbungy.crowd_note: Hardly ever any queues; busier at weekends and in December–February
pattaya-xbungy.region: Pattaya, Thepprasit Road, Soi 9, Sanook Park
pattaya-xbungy.booking: You can turn up without booking or buy online; daily from 10:00, last jump at 17:30. You need your passport for the insurance. Under-16s with an adult
pattaya-xbungy.record: Thailand's highest bungee (60 m); the site has been running since 1989 according to the operator
pros: Thailand's highest bungee
Video and certificate included in the price
Tandem jumps available
Close to central Pattaya
cons: An urban view of a lake and construction sites
Downpours and thunderstorms from May to October
Hotel transfer not included
pattaya-xbungy.airport: UTP — U-Tapao, ~40 min; BKK — Bangkok Suvarnabhumi, ~1.5 h
pattaya-xbungy.price_note: THB 2,500 (≈€66): jump, video, certificate and insurance; human slingshot (2 launches) — THB 1,400. Hotel transfer not included
school_notes: Official website, online purchase
Russian-language aggregator page; tickets temporarily unavailable when checked

phuket-jungle-bungy.description: A jump from a 50 m platform over the green lagoon of a former tin mine in the Kathu jungle, 10 minutes from Patong. The operator has been running since 1992 to New Zealand standards; after the jump you're lowered into a boat. Besides the classic jump there are tandems, a backwards jump, a “catapult” and a water-touch jump.
phuket-jungle-bungy.rating_basis: A reliable, long-established operator with good reviews, but the height is modest (50 m) and the jump is over the artificial lagoon of a former tin mine
phuket-jungle-bungy.hazards: Not allowed with heart, blood pressure, back or neck problems, pregnancy or epilepsy. In the rainy season (May–October) jumps are suspended for thunderstorms.
phuket-jungle-bungy.crowd_note: Usually no queues; more tour-agency groups in December–February
phuket-jungle-bungy.region: Phuket, Kathu district, Wichitsongkram Road — ~10 min from Patong
phuket-jungle-bungy.booking: You can turn up without booking or book through a tour agency with transfer (not included in the price). Daily 9:00–18:00, last jumps around 17:30. Under-18s need parental consent
phuket-jungle-bungy.record: Thailand's oldest bungee: since 1992, a New Zealand team, more than 25 years without a fatality
pros: Close to Patong
The oldest and most experienced operator
You can touch the water, jump in tandem or backwards
Open year-round
cons: Low by world standards
Transfer and video cost extra
May to October — southwest monsoon and downpours
phuket-jungle-bungy.price_note: From THB 2,200 (≈€58) per jump with certificate and insurance; packages with T-shirt, photos and video — up to ~THB 3,000; according to 2026 guides a solo jump is ~THB 2,800–3,200. A second jump the same day is cheaper
school_notes: Online booking; no official website found, phone +66 76 321 351

jinja-nile-bungee.description: A 44 m tower on the bank of the White Nile at Kalagala Falls, not far from Jinja — the town where the Nile flows out of Lake Victoria. You can choose a water-touch jump or jump in tandem. Bungee is usually combined with some of the world's best grade 5 rafting.
jinja-nile-bungee.rating_basis: A unique location above the White Nile, a water touch, popular with overlanders and rafters; modest height
jinja-nile-bungee.hazards: Not allowed with pregnancy, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma or back problems; you must be sober. No jumps in thunderstorms or strong wind. The ankle harness straps can chafe. Malaria zone — prophylaxis needed.
jinja-nile-bungee.crowd_note: Hardly ever any queues; most jumpers are rafting clients and camp guests
jinja-nile-bungee.region: Kalagala Falls, Kangulumira, ~30 km north of Jinja (on the bank of the White Nile)
jinja-nile-bungee.booking: Book ahead through Adrift; arrive 30 minutes before your jump. Open 7 days a week year-round, except in gale-force wind and thunderstorms. Usually combined with grade 5 rafting on the Nile and a night at the Kalagala Falls camp
jinja-nile-bungee.record: The only purpose-built bungee tower in East Africa — a jump towards the source of the Nile
pros: A Nile water touch
Tandem jumps
Inexpensive by world standards
Combines perfectly with rafting and a night by the river
cons: Modest height
Far from the capital: 3+ hours from Entebbe airport
Information on the jump location varies (the tower used to stand near Jinja) — check when booking
jinja-nile-bungee.price_note: A single jump USD 115 for foreigners (cheaper for East African residents); “rafting + bungee” combos available
school_notes: Online booking; tandems and water touches are its signature
Tour operator with transfers from Jinja/Kampala

bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.description: A 1936 concrete arch bridge over the gorge of the East Fork of the San Gabriel River: the road to it was washed away by the 1938 flood, and now you reach it on a hike of about 8 km up the canyon with river crossings. From the bridge you jump 37 m down towards the river. It's really a day hike with a jump: you can jump several times, there are advanced styles (backflip, “the lumberjack”) and overnight trips with night jumps.
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.rating_basis: A cult location: an abandoned arch bridge in a gorge, accessible only on foot; the jump isn't high, but the whole trip is an adventure
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.hazards: River crossings knee-deep and deeper: after rain and in spring the water can be fast and dangerous (people have drowned on the trail). Summer heat up to 35 °C — you need 2–3 litres of water. The trail was closed after the 2024 Bridge Fire and reopened in summer 2025; check the status with Angeles National Forest before you go. Standard bungee contraindications.
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.crowd_note: Groups are large and you can spend several hours in the queue on the bridge — bring lunch and water
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.region: California, Angeles National Forest, ~1.5 h from Los Angeles + 8 km on foot
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.booking: Advance booking on the website only; trips on Saturdays and Sundays year-round, weekdays for groups from USD 1,000; ~8 km (about 2 h) on foot to the bridge with 6+ river crossings
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.record: An abandoned 1936 bridge in the middle of the wilderness: the road to it was washed away by the 1938 flood
pros: A unique atmosphere: a bridge in the middle of the wilderness
Cheap repeat jumps
A beautiful canyon hike
Close to Los Angeles
cons: Weekends only
8 km on foot each way with river crossings
Intense summer heat and wildfire risk
A low jump
bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.airport: LAX — Los Angeles, ~1.5 h to the East Fork car park; ONT — Ontario, ~1 h
