bridge-to-nowhere-bungee.price_note: A single jump USD 150; each additional jump +USD 50, a 4-jump package USD 240; spectators USD 20; parking — Forest Adventure Pass ~USD 5
school_notes: The only operator; booking at reservations.bungeeamerica.com

bloukrans-bridge.description: A jump from the middle of the arch bridge over the Bloukrans River gorge on the N2 — 216 m to the valley floor, on a pendulum bungee. You reach the jump point via a zipline and a mesh walkway under the road deck, and after the jump a winch hauls you back up. All around are the forests and canyons of Tsitsikamma National Park, and the bridge itself is the Garden Route's top adrenaline attraction.
bloukrans-bridge.rating_basis: The height record for bridge jumps (Wikipedia, TheTravel), a must-stop on the Garden Route, lots of rave reviews
bloukrans-bridge.hazards: Contraindications: heart, blood pressure and back problems, pregnancy, recent surgery. Jumps stop in gale-force wind and thunderstorms. The mesh walkway under the road deck is unnerving for anyone afraid of heights — bring a warm top, as it's cool and windy on the bridge.
bloukrans-bridge.crowd_note: In December–January (South African school holidays) and at weekends there are queues on the bridge and at the video shop; quiet on winter weekdays
bloukrans-bridge.region: Garden Route, Eastern Cape, ~40 km east of Plettenberg Bay
bloukrans-bridge.booking: Book ahead online or via WhatsApp; arrive an hour before your slot (for the first jump at 09:00 — by 08:30). Open daily year-round; there's an “all in one day” package: jump + zipline + SkyWalk + Hangout
bloukrans-bridge.record: The highest commercial bridge bungee jump in the world — 216 m, operating since 1997
pros: The highest bridge jump in the world
Open every day, year-round
Easy to combine with a Garden Route road trip
You can do the SkyWalk along the bridge separately without jumping
cons: Minimum age 14
Photos and video cost extra
Spectators can't go onto the bridge itself without a SkyWalk ticket
bloukrans-bridge.airport: GRJ — George, ~1 h 45 min (≈130 km); PLZ — Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth), ~2 h
bloukrans-bridge.price_note: A single jump ~ZAR 1,899 (the regular price per a FOMO voucher; the operator's website doesn't give a price). Includes the zipline to the arch and the winch back up; photos and video extra
school_notes: Official website; online booking via bloukransbungy.activitar.com, tel. +27 42 281 1458
Full Adventure package; SkyWalk separately — ZAR 400

victoria-falls-bridge.description: A head-first jump from the middle of the historic bridge across the Batoka Gorge — right over the Zimbabwe–Zambia border, 111 m above the churning Zambezi and a couple of hundred metres from Victoria Falls. About four seconds of free fall, then you're hauled back up to the bridge. The same site has a gorge swing and a zipline on the Zambian side.
victoria-falls-bridge.rating_basis: A legendary location next to Victoria Falls (a UNESCO site), a regular on lists of the most scenic bungee jumps, lots of reviews
victoria-falls-bridge.hazards: Contraindications: heart disease, back problems, high blood pressure, pregnancy. Jumps stop in rain and strong wind — in the rainy season (December–March) there may be breaks for thunderstorms. Heat up to 33 °C in October–November. There's a known 2011 incident in which the cord snapped under the previous operator.
victoria-falls-bridge.crowd_note: Peak tourist season is July–October; short queues in the morning, groups from the lodges by lunchtime
victoria-falls-bridge.region: Zimbabwe–Zambia border, the Batoka Gorge, ~3 km from the town of Victoria Falls
victoria-falls-bridge.booking: Check in at the Shearwater office by the bridge on the Zimbabwean side; you need your passport — the border post issues a Bridge Pass, and no visa is needed to go onto the bridge. The bridge is open 9:00–17:00 with a break from 13:00 to 14:00
victoria-falls-bridge.record: One of the most famous jumps in the world: a 1905 bridge 111 m above the Zambezi with a view of Victoria Falls
pros: Views of Victoria Falls and rainbows in the spray
Swing, zipline and a bridge tour at one site
Easy to combine with a safari and rafting on the Zambezi
cons: Expensive for 111 m
Solo only, no tandem bungee (tandems only on the swing and zipline)
You have to go through border control even without entering the neighbouring country
Lunch break 13:00–14:00
victoria-falls-bridge.airport: VFA — Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe), ~25 min; LVI — Livingstone (Zambia), ~20 min
victoria-falls-bridge.price_note: A single jump USD 194 per the Shearwater price list (a USD 160 promotion has been seen); Big Air package (bungee + zipline + swing) USD 250; swing USD 137, zipline USD 58
school_notes: Official operator of the bungee, swing and zipline on the bridge
Booking from the Zambian side (Livingstone)

jebel-jais-via-ferrata.description: About 1 km of cables, rungs and ladders in a wadi below the summit of Jebel Jais, with three ziplines and bridges. Three routes to choose from — from an easy walk along ledges to 120 m of near-vertical climbing on Julphar Scare. Only with the operator's guides; suitable for beginners and for teenagers from 12 with their parents (height from 122 cm, weight 40–120 kg).
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.rating_basis: An official attraction of the Ras Al Khaimah Tourism Development Authority (RAKTDA), popular with tourists from Dubai; on the mountain it is ~10 °C cooler than on the coast
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.hazards: Heat and sun from May to September — bring water and sun protection; loose stones on the trails; closed sports shoes with good tread are mandatory
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Groups of up to 20 people, one at a time on the ziplines; busier and more expensive at weekends (Fri–Sat)
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.region: Ras Al Khaimah, Jebel Jais (Hajar Mountains), Bear Grylls Explorers Camp
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.approach: By car or taxi up the Jebel Jais mountain road to Bear Grylls Explorers Camp, ~25 minutes from central Ras Al Khaimah; briefing and gear handout at the camp
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.descent: By zipline back down into the wadi (the longest is 300 m, over the Jebel Jais road)
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: A via ferrata on the UAE's highest mountain: three ziplines of 50, 60 and 300 m, swinging bridges, rungs and ladders above the wadi
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.grade_local: No formal grade: 3 routes — Ledge Walk (easy), Middle Path (technical), Julphar Scare (the hardest, 120 m of vertical rungs)
pros: An easy day trip from Dubai
All gear and guides included
Open in winter too — the best season is October to April
cons: An attraction rather than a mountain route
Hot in summer even at altitude
Can't be done independently
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.airport: RKT — Ras Al Khaimah, ~1 h; DXB — Dubai, ~2 h
jebel-jais-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: October–March: 220 dirhams (≈€51) on weekdays, 275 on Fri–Sat; April, May, September — 175/220; June–August — 130/165; cheaper for children; guide and gear included
school_notes: Official operator, online booking, gear included

dachstein-superferrata.description: The longest and most serious via ferrata day on the Dachstein: “Anna” and “Johann” up the south face to the Seethaler hut, then the “Schulter” to the 2,995 m summit. Only for experienced and very fit climbers, with crampons and an ice axe at the start and end of the season; “Anna” or “Johann” can also be done on their own.
dachstein-superferrata.rating_basis: An Alpine classic in reviews by the Alpenverein (DAV), Bergwelten and bergsteigen.com; Johann is one of Austria's best-known hard “sport” routes
dachstein-superferrata.hazards: Rockfall in the upper section, steep snowfields and ice (crampons and an ice axe needed in early summer and after autumn snowfalls), glacier crevasses and the randkluft, fog on the glacier, thunderstorms at 3,000 m; you have to make the last cable car down
dachstein-superferrata.crowd_note: Queues on the Schulter near the summit because of inexperienced groups coming up from the glacier; on summer weekends Johann gets busy too — start at dawn
dachstein-superferrata.region: Styria, Schladming-Dachstein, Ramsau — the Dachstein south face
dachstein-superferrata.approach: Toll panoramic road from Ramsau to the Dachstein-Gletscherbahn valley station (Türlwand), then about 20 minutes on the trail to the Dachstein-Südwandhütte (1,871 m); the “Anna” via ferrata starts just below the hut
dachstein-superferrata.descent: From the summit of the Hoher Dachstein (2,995 m) down the Schulter and across the Hallstatt Glacier past the Seethalerhütte to the Hunerkogel top station (2,687 m), then 10 minutes down by cable car; there are large crevasses on the glacier
dachstein-superferrata.vf_highlights: Three via ferratas in a row up the whole Dachstein south face to the highest point of Upper Austria and Styria (2,995 m); Ramsau is regarded as the cradle of via ferrata in Austria
dachstein-superferrata.grade_local: D/E overall (Austrian A–E scale): Anna C/D–D, Johann D/E (the overhanging start is E), Schulter B–C
pros: Reach the region's highest summit on almost continuous via ferrata
A huge 1,200 m of vertical on cables
Descent by the Hunerkogel cable car instead of a long walk
cons: A very long and hard day, with D/E and E sections
Snowfields and ice on the link between “Anna” and “Johann”
A crevassed glacier and the randkluft at the Schulter
dachstein-superferrata.airport: SZG — Salzburg, ~1.5 h; GRZ — Graz, ~2.5 h; MUC — Munich, ~3 h
dachstein-superferrata.fee_note: The route is free; the toll road to the Gletscherbahn costs €20 per car (free if you buy a cable car ticket and validate it at the machine at the top station); the cable car is paid
school_notes: The region's official via ferrata guide with contacts for mountain schools

donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.description: The most famous via ferrata in the Salzkammergut: up a rocky ridge to the Großer Donnerkogel (2,054 m), crossing a swaying 40-metre ladder over the void. For people who already have via ferrata experience: the route is long, with vertical C/D sections and no intermediate exits.
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.rating_basis: 4.5 out of 5 from ~4,000 ratings on ferrataguide.com, 4.2 out of 5 on via-ferrata.de; featured by National Geographic and Euronews as one of the most spectacular ladders in the Alps
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms (the cable acts as a lightning conductor), lingering snow in spring and early summer, wet rock makes the route noticeably harder; the ladder swings a lot in the wind; the descent by the normal route takes effort
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.crowd_note: On sunny weekends in July–August there are jams at the ladder; better to start with the first gondola (around 8:00) or stay overnight at the Gablonzer Hütte
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.approach: Gosaukammbahn cable car from Lake Gosausee, then 20–30 minutes on trail no. 611 to the Törleck saddle; on foot from the lake without the lift — about 1.5–1.75 hours
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.descent: From the summit of the Großer Donnerkogel on trail no. 628 to the Törleck saddle and on no. 611 to the Gosaukammbahn top station, about 1.5–2 hours
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.vf_highlights: The 40-metre “Stairway to Heaven” (Himmelsleiter), strung between two rock towers over the void, with views of the Dachstein glacier and Lake Gosausee
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.grade_local: C/D (Austrian Schall scale, some sections A/B)
pros: The iconic “stairway to heaven” and huge exposure
Views of the Dachstein, the Gosaukamm and Lake Gosausee
The lift shortens the approach
The easy Laserer Alpin practice via ferrata by the lake nearby
cons: Not for beginners: C/D sections and no escape before the summit
Queues at the ladder at weekends
A long 1.5–2-hour descent on foot
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.airport: SZG — Salzburg, ~1.5 h; LNZ — Linz, ~2 h; MUC — Munich, ~2.5 h
donnerkogel-himmelsleiter.fee_note: The route is free; the Gosaukammbahn cable car is paid, parking at the local rate
school_notes: Alpine school: via ferrata courses, gear rental (~$20 a day), prices on request
Guide for the Donnerkogel, 5–6 h, gear free of charge; lift ticket not included

innsbrucker-klettersteig.description: A long high-alpine via ferrata along the Nordkette ridge from the Hafelekar to the Frau Hitt saddle: short walls, traverses and summits up to 2,480 m with views of Innsbruck and the Karwendel. For fit hikers with via ferrata experience; the first section (about 4 hours) is easier and shorter than the full traverse.
innsbrucker-klettersteig.rating_basis: A Tyrolean classic in the topos of bergsteigen.com, via-ferrata.de (3.8 out of 5 from 6 reviews) and on the Tirol Werbung website; one of the few high-alpine via ferratas reachable straight from a big city
innsbrucker-klettersteig.hazards: Thunderstorms and fog from the Inn valley; snow on the north slopes until July (the route opens depending on snow); wet rock after rain; scree and loose stones on the Schmidhubersteig path; the lifts close for maintenance in November
innsbrucker-klettersteig.crowd_note: At weekends there are hold-ups in the first section because of inexperienced groups; arrive for the first gondola to the Hafelekar (around 9:00)
innsbrucker-klettersteig.approach: From central Innsbruck take the Hungerburgbahn funicular, then the Seegrubenbahn and Hafelekarbahn cable cars to Hafelekar station (2,269 m); 5–10 minutes from the station to the start
innsbrucker-klettersteig.descent: Via the Langer Sattel (after section 1) or the Frau Hitt saddle (after section 2), then down the steep scree path Schmidhubersteig to Seegrube station (1,905 m), 1–1.5 hours, and down by lift
innsbrucker-klettersteig.vf_highlights: A ridge via ferrata over a string of summits right above Innsbruck: 2,000 m of air above the Inn valley, ibex, and a cable car ride up from the city centre
innsbrucker-klettersteig.grade_local: B–C, in places C/D (Austrian A–E scale)
pros: The start is 30 minutes from central Innsbruck by cable car
Panoramic views of Innsbruck and the Karwendel all day
You can shorten the route by leaving at the Langer Sattel
Gear rental right at the station
cons: A long high-alpine day with no official emergency descents
A steep scree descent with no cables
You must make the last gondola from Seegrube (18:30 in summer)
innsbrucker-klettersteig.airport: INN — Innsbruck, ~20 min to the valley station; MUC — Munich, ~2 h
innsbrucker-klettersteig.fee_note: The route is free; the Nordkette cable cars are paid (there is a special via ferrata ticket); full set rental is €25 a day at the shop at Seegrube station, book online the day before
school_notes: Set rental €25/day with online booking, information on route opening

lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.description: A compact waterfall via ferrata in Längenfeld with two finishes of different difficulty: the right one suits a first taste of via ferrata and teenagers with a guide, while the left one — with an E section and a suspension bridge — is a serious test of arm strength. Easy to combine with the Aqua Dome thermal spa in the same village.
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.rating_basis: A route recommended by the Ötztal tourist office; a handy alternative to the overcrowded Stuibenfall in the same valley
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.hazards: Wet rock by the waterfall, steep exposed sections with small holds, a D overhang on the right finish; don't go in thunderstorms or high water
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.crowd_note: On summer weekends and on rainy days guided groups arrive in the afternoon; quieter in the morning
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.approach: A few minutes to the waterfall from the paid car park south of the local heritage museum in Längenfeld (Lehn district); to the Ötztal by train to Ötztal station and then by bus
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.descent: On foot along the trail back to Lehn; from the right finish you can cross to the left variant by trail or a 35-metre suspension bridge
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.vf_highlights: A short via ferrata along the Lehner waterfall right in Längenfeld: the right variant is for families and beginners, the left one with an E section and a 35-metre suspension bridge is for strong climbers
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.grade_local: Right (classic) finish B–C with a short D overhang (can be bypassed on the left); left variant with an E section (Austrian A–E scale)
pros: Two difficulty options on one route
Starts right from the village, no lift needed
Done in half a day, with the thermal spa in the evening
cons: A short route
Slippery rock in the waterfall spray
The left variant is very hard (E) and not for children
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.airport: INN — Innsbruck, ~1 h; MUC — Munich, ~2.75 h
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.guide_price_note: CANKICK (via Manawa): from €85 per person, per the price table €60 per person for groups of 1–6; half a day, guide, helmet and harness included, from age 10
lehner-wasserfall-laengenfeld.fee_note: The route is free; parking is paid
school_notes: Guided tour of the Lehner, from €85 per person, gear included

seewand-hallstatt.description: A long and very hard via ferrata up the wall above Lake Hallstatt: vertical walls, small overhangs, an exposed ledge and a final 100-metre pillar. Only for experienced and fit climbers: there are no emergency exits, and the whole day takes 7–9 hours.
seewand-hallstatt.rating_basis: 4.5 out of 5 from ~860 ratings on ferrataguide.com; a Salzkammergut classic in the bergsteigen.com topos and on the Dachstein Salzkammergut tourist office website
seewand-hallstatt.hazards: A thunderstorm is a deadly danger — start only in settled weather; after rain the grassy middle section and the rock are slippery; loose rock in places and stones near the bivouac; snow on the exit towards the Gjaidalm until early summer; mountain rescue brings down inexperienced climbers every year
seewand-hallstatt.crowd_note: Its difficulty means there are hardly any queues; people start early, before 9:00, to make the last lift down
seewand-hallstatt.region: Salzkammergut, Lake Hallstatt, between Hallstatt and Obertraun
seewand-hallstatt.approach: From the large car park at Kessel beach (510 m) between Hallstatt and Obertraun, on the trail via the Hirschau alm, about 1 hour
seewand-hallstatt.descent: From the top about 40 minutes across the Dachstein plateau to the Gjaidalm hut, then down by the Krippenstein cable car (last descent at 16:50, from July to mid-September at 18:50) and 2 km along the road to the car park; on foot without the lift — 3.5–4 hours
seewand-hallstatt.vf_highlights: Almost 800 m of vertical straight above Lake Hallstatt with views of Hallstatt; one of the longest and hardest sport via ferratas in Austria
seewand-hallstatt.grade_local: D/E (Austrian Schall A–E scale), the crux is the “100-metre pillar”
pros: Incredible views of Hallstatt and the lake
A serious sporting challenge over 800 m of vertical
Descent by lift from the Dachstein plateau
cons: For experienced climbers only: D/E sections and no escape routes
A very long day with a strict last-lift deadline
Grassy sections are slippery after rain
seewand-hallstatt.airport: SZG — Salzburg, ~1.5 h; LNZ — Linz, ~1.75 h; VIE — Vienna, ~3.5 h
seewand-hallstatt.fee_note: The route is free; the descent by the Krippenstein cable car is paid
school_notes: Guides for the Seewand, recommended by the Hallstatt tourist office; prices on request
Alpine school, via ferrata gear rental, ~25 km away

stuibenfall-umhausen.description: A short but spectacular via ferrata on the rocks beside the Stuibenfall, a waterfall about 160 m high: a rope bridge, traverses above the torrent and a suspension bridge in a cloud of spray. A good choice for a first independent via ferrata once you have some experience, or for teenagers with a guide.
stuibenfall-umhausen.rating_basis: 4.6 out of 5 from 17 reviews on via-ferrata.de; one of Tyrol's most popular “waterfall” routes, included in a Euronews round-up
stuibenfall-umhausen.hazards: Wet, slippery rock and waterfall spray, exposed traverses, heat on the south-west-facing wall in summer; the route is closed after severe thunderstorms (damage in July 2023)
stuibenfall-umhausen.crowd_note: In summer and at weekends queues at the bridges of up to 30 minutes; better to come at the start of the day or after 16:00
stuibenfall-umhausen.approach: From the paid car park in Umhausen (at Ötzidorf or the Umhauser Badesee lake) 20–30 minutes on a forest road or the Waalweg trail to the waterfall; put your harness on before the rope bridge at the start
stuibenfall-umhausen.descent: Down the new staircase (about 700 steps) and suspension bridge along the waterfall, 40–45 minutes; you can stop at the Gasthof Stuibenfall (+15 minutes)
stuibenfall-umhausen.vf_highlights: A route alongside Tyrol's largest waterfall: a rope bridge across the torrent at the start and a suspension bridge right above the waterfall's spray
stuibenfall-umhausen.grade_local: C (Hüsler A–E scale); the left variant of the upper bridge is easier
pros: Spectacular bridges with the waterfall right beside you
A short approach and a quick descent by staircase
Easy to combine with rafting and the other Ötztal via ferratas
cons: Long queues in summer
You will definitely get wet by the waterfall
Slippery rock in the spray
stuibenfall-umhausen.airport: INN — Innsbruck, ~50 min; MUC — Munich, ~2.5 h; ZRH — Zurich, ~3 h
stuibenfall-umhausen.guide_price_note: CANKICK (via Manawa): from €85 per person, half a day, guide and gear included
stuibenfall-umhausen.fee_note: The route is free; parking is paid (about €5 a day according to a 2024 review)
school_notes: Guides for the Stuibenfall and Lehner, from €85 per person, gear included, from age 10

pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.description: Historic iron “ladders” on the granite rock of Pedra do Baú, installed around 1942 — about 600 rungs over 200 m of vertical to the 1,950 m summit. Technically easy but very exposed; a harness and lanyard are mandatory and a guide is recommended. A good weekend trip from São Paulo (~3 hours).
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.rating_basis: Brazil's most famous and oldest via ferrata; a Mantiqueira classic (SummitPost, Viaja Que Passa)
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.hazards: Thunderstorms and downpours from December to March — iron rungs are dangerous in lightning; wet, slippery granite; cold on the summit in winter; groups coming the other way on the same line
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.crowd_note: In winter (June–August) and at weekends there are many groups on the rungs — you have to pass each other at narrow spots; weekdays are better
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.region: São Paulo, Serra da Mantiqueira, São Bento do Sapucaí (near Campos do Jordão)
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.approach: From the Pedra do Baú complex (the last ~5 km is a dirt road) about an hour on the trail, gaining ~360 m, to the foot of the rung ladder; trail access by advance booking
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.descent: The same way down the rungs, then along the trail to the car park; the whole trail is ~2 km each way
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: About 600 iron rungs driven into the sheer granite rock back in the 1940s; a 1,950 m summit with views of the Serra da Mantiqueira
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.grade_local: No official grade: historic iron “ladders” of rungs, ~200 m of vertical
pros: A historic via ferrata dating from the 1940s
Superb panorama of the Mantiqueira mountains
Inexpensive
cons: Descent by the same rungs — two-way traffic
Downpours and thunderstorms in summer
Dirt road to the car park
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.airport: GRU — São Paulo, ~3 h; SJK — São José dos Campos, ~1.5 h
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Armazém Aventura (via Airbnb Experiences): ~70 Canadian dollars per person for 5 hours, entry ticket and gear included; a guide is recommended
pedra-do-bau-via-ferrata.fee_note: Entry to the Pedra do Baú complex is R$18; the summit trail requires online booking
school_notes: Via ferrata guide in Portuguese, gear and ticket included

kicking-horse-via-ferrata.description: Three guided routes on the north face of Terminator Peak above Kicking Horse ski resort: the one-hour Pioneer with a suspension bridge for first-timers, the two-hour Discovery and the technical Ascension to the summit. Up by gondola, all gear included, ages 12 and up.
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.rating_basis: A high-alpine via ferrata by a ski resort gondola; often mentioned in Canadian Rockies guides (Kootenay Rockies, Vacay.ca)
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.hazards: Thunderstorms and sudden cold at altitude, snow on the face in June; participant weight 40–120 kg; routes are closed in bad weather
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Only scheduled guided groups of up to 8 people — no queues
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.region: British Columbia, Purcell Mountains, Kicking Horse resort near Golden
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.approach: Golden Eagle Express gondola from the resort base (15 km from Golden) to ~2,300 m; meet at the Eagle's Eye restaurant, a few minutes from there to the cables
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.descent: Loop routes on the north face of Terminator Peak, returning to the gondola top station and down by gondola
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: The Hanging Glory suspension bridge and the “Guts Bridge”, and the summit of Terminator Peak with views of the Purcells and the Rockies
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.grade_local: French scale: Pioneer — PD+, Discovery — AD+, Ascension — D/D+
pros: High alpine terrain without a long approach — up by gondola
Routes from very easy to hard
The package includes the resort's trails and grizzly bear refuge
cons: Can't be done independently
Short summer season
Cold and windy at 2,300–2,400 m
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.airport: YYC — Calgary, ~3 h; YLW — Kelowna, ~4 h
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Guided only (up to 8 people), prices in Canadian dollars per person excluding tax: Pioneer up to 1 h — $104, Discovery up to 2 h — $169, Ascension up to 3 h — $215; teens 13–17 pay less; gondola and gear included
kicking-horse-via-ferrata.fee_note: Included in the tour price together with the gondola (Adventure Pass)
school_notes: Route operator: guide, gondola, gear

mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.description: About 2.5 km of cables on Mount Nimbus in the Purcell Mountains, built by CMH guides in 2007. The only way in is by helicopter as part of a stay at the Bobbie Burns lodge, but no mountaineering experience is needed — good fitness is enough. The climax is a suspension bridge leading to the summit.
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.rating_basis: On the Canadian Bucket List, featured by Daily Hive, Matador Network and WorldAtlas; unique heli access and a bridge over the void
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.hazards: Fast-changing mountain weather and thunderstorms, cold and wind on the ridge, helicopter flights are cancelled in poor visibility; huge exposure on the bridge
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Only small groups of lodge guests with guides — no queues
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.region: British Columbia, Purcell Mountains, Golden area — helicopter access only
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.approach: For CMH Bobbie Burns lodge guests only: the helicopter drops the group in the valley at the start of the route
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.descent: From the summit to the landing spot where the helicopter picks the group up
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: North America's longest and highest via ferrata: knife-edge ridges, rungs on the walls and a 60-metre suspension bridge ~600 m above the ground — the only way to the 2,651 m summit
pros: A real mountaineering summit without the experience
Helicopter, wilderness, glaciers
No crowds
cons: Very expensive: multi-day package only
The season is just two months
Age and weight restrictions apply
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.airport: YYC — Calgary, ~3 h to Golden (then by helicopter); YLW — Kelowna, ~4 h
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Only as part of a stay at the Bobbie Burns lodge (2–6 nights) with CMH guides, helicopter and meals; in 2019 — from 3,275 Canadian dollars
mount-nimbus-via-ferrata.fee_note: Not sold separately — part of the lodge package
school_notes: The only operator: lodge, helicopter, guides and gear

mt-norquay-via-ferrata.description: Five commercial guided routes on the slope of Mount Norquay right above Banff: from the 2-hour introductory Explorer (ages 12+) to the 6-hour Summiteer to the summit, with lunch. No experience needed; all gear and even boots are provided free.
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.rating_basis: The main via ferrata in the Canadian Rockies: Ski Big 3 and Banff Bound blogs, sold by big aggregators (Expedia, Trip.com)
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.hazards: Colder than in town and often windy; summer afternoon thunderstorms; snow on the ridge at the start and end of the season; wildfire smoke in August
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Only scheduled guided groups — no queues on the cables, but in July–August tours sell out a few days ahead
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.region: Alberta, Rocky Mountains, Banff National Park
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.approach: From the Norquay ski base, 10 minutes' drive from Banff; the guided group walks up to the start of the route (by the Cliffhouse Bistro)
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.descent: On foot along the ridge and trail to the Cliffhouse Bistro and down to the base; the short routes are loops
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: A ridge above Banff with views of Cascade Mountain and the Bow Valley; a 55-metre suspension bridge on the Skyline route and a three-cable bridge over a couloir on the Summiteer
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.grade_local: No official grade: 5 routes from the introductory Explorer to the hard Summiteer (overhanging ladder, bridges)
pros: 10 minutes from Banff
Options for any level of fitness
Stunning views of Banff National Park
cons: Can't be done independently
Fairly expensive
Season only from mid-June to mid-October
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Only with an ACMG guide, prices in Canadian dollars per person: Explorer 2–2.5 h — $199, Ridgewalker — $269, Alpinist — $295, Skyline — $325, Summiteer 5.5–6 h — $399 (with lunch); gear, boots and backpack free
mt-norquay-via-ferrata.fee_note: No separate fee — included in the tour
school_notes: Route operator, ACMG guides, 5 options, gear included

sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.description: A short (1–1.5-hour) guided via ferrata by the top station of the Sea to Sky Gondola in Squamish: rungs, suspension bridges and granite slabs above the fjord. No experience needed, children from age 8. Easy to combine with a drive from Vancouver to Whistler.
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.rating_basis: The gondola's website cites a No. 1 ranking from Explore Magazine; a short but scenic route by a popular gondola
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.hazards: Rainy coastal climate: wet, slippery granite from October to April; the gondola closes in strong winds
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Scheduled guided groups — no queues on the cable, but the gondola itself is busy at summer weekends
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.region: British Columbia, Squamish, Howe Sound — between Vancouver and Whistler
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.approach: Sea to Sky Gondola from Highway 99 by Shannon Falls to the top station; gear is handed out at the Summit Shelter, then a short guided walk to the start
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.descent: The route ends at the Summit Lodge viewing deck; down by gondola
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: Granite slabs, bridges and catwalks high above Howe Sound with views of the ocean and snowy peaks; the finish is right at the viewing deck
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.grade_local: No official grade; per the operator: for beginners with no experience
pros: An hour from Vancouver
Suitable for children from 8 and beginners
Views of the fjord and ocean
cons: Very short
Guided only
The gondola is paid separately
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Only with a Mountain Skills Academy guide, prices in Canadian dollars: adults $114 (weekdays) / $129 (weekends), with a gondola ticket $184 / $199; children 8–15 — from $89; private group of up to 8 — $699–749
sea-to-sky-gondola-via-ferrata.fee_note: A Sea to Sky Gondola ticket is required (can be bought together with the tour); parking at the gondola is paid from May to October
school_notes: Route operator: guide, gear, gondola ticket optional

allmenalp-kandersteg.description: A short but steep and varied via ferrata straight from Kandersteg: vertical walls on rungs beside a waterfall, ladders, Nepalese bridges and Tyrolean traverses. For people who already have experience and arm strength; the cable car descent makes it a handy half-day activity.
allmenalp-kandersteg.rating_basis: One of the most spectacular via ferratas in the Bernese Oberland according to BLS, Interlaken Tourismus and Bergwelten; promoted by MySwitzerland
allmenalp-kandersteg.hazards: Wet rock by the waterfall, high water in early summer, vertical sections that demand arm strength, thunderstorms; the route is open only while the cable car is running
allmenalp-kandersteg.crowd_note: On summer weekends there can be waits at the bridges; the route is short, better to start before noon
allmenalp-kandersteg.approach: From Kandersteg station 10 minutes to the Allmenalpbahn valley station, then on a waymarked trail along the right bank of the Allmibach stream to the start (~1,250 m)
allmenalp-kandersteg.descent: From the exit at the Undere Allme top station (1,723 m, restaurant) down by the Allmenalpbahn or on foot via Ryharts and Schneitböde in 1 h 15 min; you can also fly down on a tandem paraglider
allmenalp-kandersteg.vf_highlights: A via ferrata along the Allmibach waterfall: 880 rungs, 4 ladders, 2 Nepalese bridges and 2 Tyrolean traverses (50 and 110 m), finishing at a restaurant overlooking Kandersteg
pros: Lots of features on a short route
The start is 10–20 minutes from Kandersteg station
Rental right by the lift
Descent by cable car or paraglider
cons: Steep and physically demanding (K4–K5)
The 110-metre traverse is guided only
Rock wet from the waterfall spray
allmenalp-kandersteg.airport: BRN — Bern, ~1 h; ZRH — Zurich, ~2 h; GVA — Geneva, ~2.5 h
allmenalp-kandersteg.guide_price_note: Private tour from the Kandersteg-Allmenalp cable car via MySwitzerland: from CHF 160 (≈€170); the 110-metre Tyrolean traverse is guided only
allmenalp-kandersteg.fee_note: The route is free; Allmenalpbahn down CHF 18 (return CHF 24); set rental CHF 25 a day at the valley station or in Kandersteg shops
school_notes: Private guided tour from CHF 160
Cable car timetable and prices, rental CHF 25

daubenhorn-leukerbad.description: A very long and hard sport via ferrata to the summit of the Daubenhorn: vertical walls, long overhanging ladders, a chimney and a cave. Only for experienced and very fit climbers; beginners should do just the short part with its intermediate exit, or a different route altogether.
daubenhorn-leukerbad.rating_basis: Billed by Valais/Wallis Tourismus and the Leukerbad tourist office as Switzerland's longest via ferrata; described on the SAC route portal and in the bergsteigen.com topos
daubenhorn-leukerbad.hazards: Rockfall (helmet mandatory), thunderstorms, meltwater in the big couloir early in the season, old snow and a small glacier on the descent, exposed sections without cable; the intermediate descent is dangerous when wet
daubenhorn-leukerbad.crowd_note: Hardly any queues because of the difficulty; people start with the first gondola to beat the thunderstorms
daubenhorn-leukerbad.approach: From Leukerbad take the Gemmibahn cable car to the Gemmi Pass (2,346 m), then 20–45 minutes down the old trade path to the grassy terrace of Untere Schmitte (~2,060 m) with a big information board; on foot from Leukerbad it takes an hour longer
daubenhorn-leukerbad.descent: From the exit follow the white-blue-white markings to the edge of the small Daubenhorn glacier, onto the Lämmerenboden plain and back to the Gemmibahn station, about 1.75 hours; after the short via ferrata (≈2 h) there is an intermediate descent to Leukerbad, dangerous when wet
daubenhorn-leukerbad.vf_highlights: Switzerland's longest via ferrata: about 2 km of cable, 216 m of ladders (some overhanging; the chimney ladder is about 100 m) and a 2,941 m summit above the Leukerbad thermal spa resort
daubenhorn-leukerbad.grade_local: K5–K6 (Swiss SAC scale); short via ferrata K4–K5, long via ferrata K5–K6, cave variant E
pros: Switzerland's longest via ferrata and a summit of almost 3,000 m
Cable car access from Leukerbad
Leukerbad's thermal pools after the route
Intermediate exit after the first third
cons: Experienced climbers only: K5–K6
Short season, usually from July
A very long day, 8+ hours
daubenhorn-leukerbad.airport: GVA — Geneva, ~2.5 h; ZRH — Zurich, ~3 h; BRN — Bern, ~1.75 h
daubenhorn-leukerbad.fee_note: The route is free; the Gemmibahn cable car is paid
school_notes: Route description; rental in Leukerbad sports shops and at the Gemmibahn

fuerenwand-engelberg.description: A long and physically demanding via ferrata up the huge Fürenwand: T-shaped rungs, a wet traverse, smooth slabs and, at the end, a swinging ladder. Experienced climbers only: arm strength and stamina are essential, and there is no emergency exit.
fuerenwand-engelberg.rating_basis: 5.0 out of 5 from 280 ratings on ferrataguide.com, 4.6 out of 5 on via-ferrata.de; one of the best-known sport via ferratas in Central Switzerland
fuerenwand-engelberg.hazards: No emergency exit, arm fatigue; wet sections with dripping water and polished rock; stones and wet rock after the spring snowmelt; summer heat; thunderstorms
fuerenwand-engelberg.crowd_note: After the bench halfway up the wall groups catch each other up and queues form; better to start in the morning on a weekday
fuerenwand-engelberg.approach: From the Fürenalpbahn valley station (Herrenrüti, ~1,080 m; by bus from Engelberg) 20–30 minutes along a paved road to the foot of the wall
fuerenwand-engelberg.descent: From the exit at the Fürenalp restaurant (1,840 m) down by the Fürenalpbahn cable car or on foot on the trail to the valley, about 1.5 hours
fuerenwand-engelberg.vf_highlights: A near-vertical 600-metre wall above the Engelberg valley with views of the Titlis, and a final swinging cable ladder, the “Himmelsleiter”, about 20 m high
pros: A tremendous wall and views of the Titlis
Gear rental right by the lift
Descent by cable car, restaurant at the exit
Long season: late May to October
cons: No emergency exit — if you run out of strength, it's a helicopter
The wide spacing between rungs is awkward for shorter people
Hot on the wall in summer
fuerenwand-engelberg.airport: ZRH — Zurich, ~1.5 h; BSL — Basel, ~1.75 h
fuerenwand-engelberg.fee_note: The route is free; the descent by the Fürenalpbahn is paid; parking at the valley station about CHF 5; set rental at the valley station CHF 25 (lanyards only — CHF 15), booking advisable
school_notes: Set rental CHF 25, book by phone on +41 41 637 20 94

muerren-gimmelwald.description: The famous “descending” via ferrata along the edge of the sheer cliffs between the villages of Mürren and Gimmelwald: rungs over the void, ladders, cable traverses and a long suspension bridge. Technically moderate (K3) but very exposed — beginners are better off with a guide.
muerren-gimmelwald.rating_basis: One of Switzerland's best-known via ferratas: recommended by Rick Steves, Earth Trekkers and many travel blogs; 4.0 out of 5 on ferrataguide.com (~850 ascents)
muerren-gimmelwald.hazards: The metal rungs are very slippery in the rain — don't go when it's raining or thunderstorms threaten; huge exposure above the drop; the bridge sways under a group; stepping onto the BASE jumpers' platform is prohibited
muerren-gimmelwald.crowd_note: In August in good weather there can be jams on the rungs and the wobbly bridge; better to start at opening time, 9:00
muerren-gimmelwald.approach: To Mürren by cable car from Lauterbrunnen to Grütschalp and train, or by cable car from Stechelberg; the start is 5–10 minutes from the Sportchalet Mürren, through a tunnel under the tennis court retaining wall
muerren-gimmelwald.descent: The route mostly goes downhill and ends in Gimmelwald; back to Mürren (or down to Stechelberg) by the Schilthornbahn cable car
muerren-gimmelwald.vf_highlights: A traverse on rungs above the 600-metre drop of the Lauterbrunnen valley with views of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau, an 80-metre “Nepalese” bridge and a 60-metre zipline (guided only)
pros: Views of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau and the Lauterbrunnen waterfalls
Gear rental in Mürren near the start
Easy logistics: back by cable car
Zipline and Nepalese bridge with a guide
cons: Open only from 1 June to 31 October, 9:00–18:00
Very strong exposure
Switzerland is expensive: cable cars, rental and guide
muerren-gimmelwald.airport: ZRH — Zurich, ~2.5 h; BRN — Bern, ~1.5 h; GVA — Geneva, ~3 h
muerren-gimmelwald.guide_price_note: Outdoor Interlaken: from CHF 135 (≈€145) per person, UIAGM guide, gear (fitted at Stäger Sport in Mürren) and zipline included
muerren-gimmelwald.fee_note: The route is free (you can make a voluntary donation on the website); cable cars and gear rental are paid
school_notes: Tour with a UIAGM guide from CHF 135, gear and zipline included
Opening hours, rules, guide booking

pinut-flims.description: An ancient via ferrata that locals used for centuries to reach the Flimserstein pastures, and since 2007 a fully renovated route with wide ladders and a continuous cable. Technically easy (K2), suitable for beginners and children from 12, but it takes stamina: 700 m of ascent.
pinut-flims.rating_basis: 4.9 out of 5 from 4 reviews on via-ferrata.de; promoted by MySwitzerland and Graubünden as one of the highlight adventures of Flims Laax; unique for its history
pinut-flims.hazards: Thunderstorms and wet rock; the cave is always damp and stones can fall from its floor onto people below; large loose boulders on the descent; exposed ladders
pinut-flims.crowd_note: Busy at weekends in high summer; seats on the bus and gondola are limited — better to buy tickets in advance
pinut-flims.region: Graubünden, Flims Laax, Fidaz — the Flimserstein wall
pinut-flims.approach: From Flims take the PostAuto bus towards Fidaz to the “Pinut” stop (or walk from Flims Dorf, 45 minutes), then 30 minutes and 200 m of ascent to the gearing-up spot below the Flimserstein wall; Stenna car park at the valley station in Flims
pinut-flims.descent: From the exit along the historic Scala Mola path to the Bargis alp (1,549 m), about 1 hour, then by PostAuto bus to Flims; alternatively the Crap da Flem gondola to Fidaz (tickets in advance)
pinut-flims.vf_highlights: Switzerland's oldest surviving via ferrata (first written mention in 1739): wide iron ladders, bridges, a cave and tunnels on the three sheer tiers of the Flimserstein
pinut-flims.grade_local: K2 (Swiss SAC K1–K6 scale), “moderate”; C on via-ferrata.de
pros: Historic atmosphere and a unique character
Technically easy, good for a first time
Guided tours at a fixed price
A beautiful descent on the Scala Mola path
cons: Long approach and descent — you need to be fit
A wet, dripping cave with loose stones
Season only from mid-May to late October
pinut-flims.airport: ZRH — Zurich, ~2 h; FDH — Friedrichshafen, ~2 h
pinut-flims.guide_price_note: Group tour by the Flims Laax Falera tourist office: CHF 150 (≈€160) per person, CHF 20 off with the guest card, minimum 4 people; gear and the bus from Bargis included
pinut-flims.fee_note: Free; paid parking at the bottom
school_notes: Group tours with a mountain guide, CHF 150; rental via Sport Beat and LAAX Rental in Flims
Beginners' tour, booking via Graubünden

huashan-plank-walk.description: Not a classic via ferrata but a short stretch of Taoist path below the South Peak of Huashan (2,154 m): down on rungs and along about 20 m of planks on a sheer wall, with a harness and two carabiners on a chain mandatory. It's a dead end — you have to turn round and pass others on the same planks. For anyone without a fear of heights; the main difficulty is the queues.
huashan-plank-walk.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known exposed routes, in top lists of “the most dangerous trails”; according to reviews the danger is mostly psychological
huashan-plank-walk.hazards: Exposure above the drop, passing people coming the other way on the planks; the mountain closes in strong wind and snowfall, ice in winter; thunderstorms in summer
huashan-plank-walk.crowd_note: Up to 30,000 visitors a day on the mountain, a 2–3-hour queue for the planks in summer and on national holidays; better to take the cable car up by 7–8 am or stay overnight on the mountain
huashan-plank-walk.region: Shaanxi Province, Huayin, Mount Hua — South Peak
huashan-plank-walk.approach: High-speed train Xi'an — Huashan North ~40 minutes, bus to the West Peak cable car, then on foot along the ridge to the South Peak
huashan-plank-walk.descent: Back the same way along the planks (dead-end route), then along the ridge to the North Peak and down by cable car
huashan-plank-walk.vf_highlights: The world's most famous “terrifying trail”: about 20 m of 30 cm-wide planks fixed to the sheer wall below the South Peak, reached by climbing down iron rungs
huashan-plank-walk.grade_local: No formal grade; technically easy, the main thing is the exposure above the drop
pros: A famous and very photogenic spot
Technically easy, harnesses issued on site
An easy day trip from Xi'an
cons: Huge queues and crowds
A very short section
Two-way traffic on narrow planks
huashan-plank-walk.airport: XIY — Xi'an, ~2 hours (40-minute train from Xi'an North)
huashan-plank-walk.fee_note: Mountain entry 160 yuan (≈€21, March–November, valid 2 days) + rental of the mandatory harness ~30 yuan; cable cars extra: 140 up and 80 down

yandangshan-via-ferrata.description: A commercial via ferrata park on the cliffs of Taping Peak in the Yandang Mountains: a short introductory route C, route A of 400 m with three cable bridges, and the long route B of 900 m with a 48-metre cable bridge and a 33-metre wooden bridge. Open year-round from 7:30 to 17:00, gear provided on site. A good option for beginners if you are in Zhejiang.
yandangshan-via-ferrata.rating_basis: A popular commercial route covered by Chinese and international media (a traffic jam on the rock on the 1 May holiday)
yandangshan-via-ferrata.hazards: Queues and waiting on the rock during holidays; heat, downpours and typhoons June–September; wet rungs after rain
yandangshan-via-ferrata.crowd_note: On Chinese holidays (1 May, 1 October) jams on the rock of over an hour; quiet on weekdays
yandangshan-via-ferrata.region: Zhejiang Province, Wenzhou, Yueqing — Yandang Mountains, Xianxi town, Taping Peak (沓屏峰)
yandangshan-via-ferrata.approach: From the entrance of the “雁荡山飞拉达” via ferrata park by Taping Peak, Xianxi town, Yueqing
yandangshan-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: One of China's best-known via ferratas: cable bridges over the void (the longest is 48 m) and a 33-metre wooden suspension bridge
yandangshan-via-ferrata.grade_local: No formal grade; 3 routes: A (400 m), B (900 m), C (70 m, introductory)
pros: Open year-round
Inexpensive, gear on site
Spectacular bridges over the void
cons: Jams on the route during Chinese holidays
Information in Chinese only
Hot and humid in summer, typhoon season
yandangshan-via-ferrata.fee_note: Tickets from 65 yuan (≈€8) according to a ticket aggregator; price depends on the route

alpspitz-ferrata.description: An easy, superbly equipped via ferrata up the north face to the summit of the Alpspitze: rungs, steps and cables with almost no vertical sections. Ideal as a first high-alpine via ferrata and for teenagers with an experienced adult, but it takes stamina and sure-footedness on the descent.
alpspitz-ferrata.rating_basis: 4.2 out of 5 from 32 reviews on via-ferrata.de; a Bavarian classic on bergsteigen.com, Bergzeit and in DAV guidebooks
alpspitz-ferrata.hazards: Rockfall in the middle section and the summit couloir, thunderstorms and sudden weather changes, slippery rock in the rain, snow on the cables and descents in June and autumn; in winter — guided only
alpspitz-ferrata.crowd_note: On summer weekends “very overcrowded”: queues double the ascent time, people overtaking without clipping in; go on a weekday with the first gondola and don't descend the via ferrata against the flow
alpspitz-ferrata.approach: Alpspitzbahn cable car from Garmisch to the Osterfelderkopf (about 2,050 m, AlpspiX viewing platform), then 20 minutes following signs for “Alpspitz-Ferrata / Nordwandsteig”
alpspitz-ferrata.descent: Recommended: along the east ridge (A/B sections) into the Oberkar cirque and along the Nordwandsteig path with its tunnels back to the Osterfelderkopf, about 2 hours. Long option: the Matheisenkarsteig (B/C) to the Höllentalangerhütte and through the Höllentalklamm gorge to the valley, about 4 hours
alpspitz-ferrata.vf_highlights: Bavaria's most popular “first” via ferrata: an easy climb up the Alpspitze pyramid (2,628 m) with views of the Zugspitze and Garmisch
pros: Technically easy (A/B) and well equipped
Quick cable car access from Garmisch
A real 2,628 m summit with views of the Zugspitze
A loop via the Nordwandsteig with its tunnels
cons: Badly overcrowded at weekends
Rockfall in the summit couloir from groups above
Snow on the north face until mid-June
alpspitz-ferrata.airport: MUC — Munich, ~1.5 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~1 h
alpspitz-ferrata.guide_price_note: Bergschule Kleinwalsertal: 2 days (Alpspitze + Zugspitze via the Höllental), €445 per person, groups of 4–5, gear provided
alpspitz-ferrata.fee_note: The route is free; an Alpspitzbahn return ticket is €37 (2025)
school_notes: 2-day Alpspitze + Zugspitze programme, €445, gear for the duration of the tour

gruenstein-koenigssee.description: A short sport via ferrata on the south face of the Grünstein above the Königssee with several variants: the easy Isidor (C) suits beginners with an experienced companion, while the Räuberleiter and Gipfelwand (D/E–E) are for strong climbers. The season is longer than on high-alpine routes — from spring to early November.
gruenstein-koenigssee.rating_basis: 4.5 out of 5 on ferrataguide.com (~930 ascents), 4.5 out of 5 from 18 reviews on via-ferrata.de; one of the most visited via ferratas in Bavaria
gruenstein-koenigssee.hazards: Thunderstorms (lightning once struck a group on the cable), heat and sun on the south face, slippery earthy sections after rain; the cables on the suspension bridge hang high for shorter people; closed from November to March
gruenstein-koenigssee.crowd_note: At weekends “absolutely overcrowded”, with queues at the start by 8:30; get to the car park by 7:00–7:30 or go on a weekday
gruenstein-koenigssee.region: Bavaria, Berchtesgadener Land, Schönau am Königssee
gruenstein-koenigssee.approach: From the large Königssee car park (604 m) along the road beside the bobsleigh track to the start above the Kunsteisbahn, 35–45 minutes
gruenstein-koenigssee.descent: From the summit to the Grünsteinhütte, then steeply down trail AV 445 to Hammerstiel or the Klingerweg (AV 443) to the Königssee car park, about 1–1.25 hours; descending the via ferrata itself is prohibited
gruenstein-koenigssee.vf_highlights: A “pick your grade” via ferrata from C to E above the Königssee: a long, wobbly suspension bridge, an overhanging start and a view of the Watzmann from the summit
gruenstein-koenigssee.grade_local: C (Isidor variant, B/C in places); variants Hotelroute D, Räuberleiter D/E, Renoth-Gipfelwand exit D+/E (Hüsler scale)
pros: Options for every level from C to E
A short approach from the Königssee
Long season: May–October
Views of the Königssee and the Watzmann
cons: Badly overcrowded at weekends
Hot on the south face in summer, with almost no breeze
No emergency exit after the start
gruenstein-koenigssee.airport: SZG — Salzburg, ~40 min; MUC — Munich, ~2.5 h
gruenstein-koenigssee.fee_note: The route is free; parking at the Königssee is paid

mindelheimer-klettersteig.description: A long, moderately difficult ridge via ferrata over the summits of the Schafalpenköpfe: short vertical walls, a ladder bridge and plenty of ridge walking. Suits fit hikers with basic experience; easiest with a night at the Fiderepasshütte.
mindelheimer-klettersteig.rating_basis: 4.9 out of 5 from 9 reviews on via-ferrata.de; one of the most popular via ferratas in the Allgäu according to Bergzeit; guided by the Kleinwalsertal mountain schools
mindelheimer-klettersteig.hazards: Fast-changing weather and thunderstorms on the ridge, snowfields until late June and in places later, the steep Kemptner Scharte couloir with rockfall, no water along the way, some sections without cable
mindelheimer-klettersteig.crowd_note: At weekends in good weather there are queues and hold-ups at the ladders; on weekdays the route is almost empty
mindelheimer-klettersteig.region: Allgäu Alps, German–Austrian border: Oberstdorf / Kleinwalsertal
mindelheimer-klettersteig.approach: From Mittelberg (Kleinwalsertal, paid parking) up the Wildental valley to the Fiderepasshütte (2,067 m), 2–3 hours, then about 30 minutes steeply up to the Fiderescharte saddle; it's convenient to spend the night before at the hut. Alternatively, the Kanzelwandbahn lift and a traverse over the Hammerspitzen
mindelheimer-klettersteig.descent: From the summit of the Kemptner Köpfle down to the Kemptner Scharte saddle (a steep scree couloir), then via the Hintere Wildenalpe and Fluchtalpe to Mittelberg, 1.5–2 hours; you can drop in at the Mindelheimer Hütte (+15–20 minutes)
mindelheimer-klettersteig.vf_highlights: A classic Allgäu ridge traverse over the three summits of the Schafalpenköpfe with a ladder bridge across a cleft and views of Oberstdorf and the Kleinwalsertal
mindelheimer-klettersteig.grade_local: B/C, occasional C sections (Hüsler A–E scale)
pros: Not too technical, but very scenic
Huts at the start and end of the route
Can be done with a mountain school from the Kleinwalsertal
cons: A very long day: 8–10 hours including the approach
No emergency exits from the ridge
A steep scree descent with rockfall
mindelheimer-klettersteig.airport: FMM — Memmingen, ~1.5 h; MUC — Munich, ~2.5 h; ZRH — Zurich, ~2.5 h
mindelheimer-klettersteig.guide_price_note: Bergschule Kleinwalsertal: €120 per person, groups of 4–6, start at the Fiderepasshütte at 8:00; gear provided; from age 12
mindelheimer-klettersteig.fee_note: The route is free; paid parking at Mittelberg / Alpe Schwendle
school_notes: Group trips on the Mindelheimer, €120 per person, gear for the duration of the tour

canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.description: A short but demanding via ferrata on the south face of Montserrat along the Artiga Baixa gully: four cabled sections, rungs up an overhang and a steep final couloir. For people with arm strength and experience; beginners only with a guide. Best from September to June — in summer the wall is scorching.
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.rating_basis: Montserrat's best-known via ferrata, guided by the main Barcelona guiding companies; hard and physical
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.hazards: Heat and sun on the south face from June to September; slippery polished rock; the overhang takes arm strength; after rain, debris and stones on the first section
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.crowd_note: Lots of local groups at weekends in spring and autumn; quiet on weekdays
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.region: Catalonia, south face of Montserrat between Collbató and El Bruc, ~50 minutes from Barcelona
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.approach: From the Vinya Nova restaurant car park (exit 575 off the A2 past Collbató) 20–25 minutes on a forest trail to the foot of the wall
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.descent: On foot up the gully bed to the Pollegons col and down to the Clot de la Mònica, or via the Artiga Alta gorge, 30–60 minutes
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.vf_highlights: A steep “sport” route on Montserrat's famous conglomerate walls with views of the olive groves of the Bruc plain
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.grade_local: K4 / K4+ (Spanish scale; D+ on the French scale)
pros: Close to Barcelona — easily done in half a day
Views of the plain and the Montserrat cliffs
Season almost year-round
Free
cons: Polished rock, few footholds
Bent rungs in places and only a chain
Very hot on the south face in summer
canal-de-les-dames-montserrat.guide_price_note: Pyrenees Extrem — from €40 (gear, insurance, aperitif); Guies de Muntanya de Montserrat — from €80; from age 12–15
school_notes: Guide, gear included; Catalan, Spanish, English
Guide, gear included; English, French, Spanish

tajo-de-ronda.description: A short historic via ferrata up the wall of the Tajo gorge right below Ronda's famous bridge: large wrought-iron rungs set in concrete, originally for the hydroelectric plant workers. A good first taste of via ferrata on a trip around Andalusia; the neighbouring “La Sevillana” route has been closed since 2023.
tajo-de-ronda.rating_basis: A famous spot, but the via ferrata itself is short and “technical” (concrete and rungs); rated 2.5 out of 5 on via-ferrata.de
tajo-de-ronda.hazards: Summer heat up to +34 °C; wet rungs after rain; rockfalls happen in the old town — the walls are inspected regularly; the neighbouring route II is closed
tajo-de-ronda.crowd_note: Guides bring tourists from Málaga and Marbella almost every day; lots of hikers on the path in the gorge
tajo-de-ronda.region: Andalusia, Ronda, the Tajo gorge below the Puente Nuevo
tajo-de-ronda.approach: From the Old Town on foot through the Puerta del Viento and Puerta de los Molinos gates down into the gorge, 20–30 minutes; better to leave the car outside the old town
tajo-de-ronda.descent: The exit comes out on the path; 7–10 minutes to the fork at the Puerta del Viento, or climb up to the Old Town
tajo-de-ronda.vf_highlights: An old early-20th-century “staircase of death” for the hydroelectric plant workers — a climb up the Tajo wall with views of the 100-metre Puente Nuevo bridge
tajo-de-ronda.grade_local: K2 (A/B; C in places according to a 2026 review)
pros: A view of the Puente Nuevo from below that ordinary tourists never get
Short — easy to combine with sightseeing in Ronda
Suitable for beginners with a guide
cons: Very short (~80 m of cable)
Lots of concrete and old structures instead of rock
Hot in the gorge in summer
tajo-de-ronda.airport: AGP — Málaga, ~1.5 h; SVQ — Seville, ~2 h; GIB — Gibraltar, ~1.5 h
tajo-de-ronda.guide_price_note: Sport Mountain via Yumping: 2 hours, guide, gear and insurance; groups of 2–12 people
school_notes: Guide, gear
Guide, gear, photo report; a circuit of 3 via ferratas
Aggregator of via ferrata tours in Andalusia

diable-aussois.description: A complex of seven independent sections totalling 3.76 km above the Arc gorge between the Esseillon forts. You can do one short section in an hour or link the lot into a 6–8-hour loop. Suits beginners with children (Angelots, Diablotins) as well as experienced climbers (Rois Mages, Purgatoire — TD).
diable-aussois.rating_basis: One of the longest via ferrata complexes in France (3.76 km), the main summer attraction of the Haute-Maurienne; guides run trips year-round
diable-aussois.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms in summer; ice and snow in winter; rockfall from groups above; children under 1.4 m and under 40 kg need a rope belay
diable-aussois.crowd_note: In July–August lots of families and groups on “Diablotins” and “Montée au Ciel”; the hard sections (Rois Mages, Purgatoire) are quieter
diable-aussois.region: Savoie, Maurienne valley, the Esseillon forts near Aussois
diable-aussois.approach: From the Fort Victor-Emmanuel car park (D215 road from Aussois) or from the Redoute Marie-Thérèse on the D1006; 5–10 minutes to the start
diable-aussois.descent: On foot along the paths between the forts and over the Pont du Diable, 10–20 minutes
diable-aussois.vf_highlights: Seven sections above the Arc gorge between 19th-century forts: from the children's “Angelots” to the three suspension bridges of “Rois Mages” (TD)
pros: Free and open year-round
A choice from F to TD in one place, 5 minutes from the car park
19th-century forts, bridges and the Nant waterfall
Gear rental in Aussois and La Norma
cons: Low altitude (1,300 m) — none of the alpine panoramas of the summit routes
Hot in the gorge in summer
From February to June eagle owls nest on the cliffs — please keep quiet near the galleries
diable-aussois.airport: TRN — Turin, ~1.5 h; CMF — Chambéry, ~1.5 h; LYS — Lyon, ~2.5 h; GVA — Geneva, ~2.5 h
diable-aussois.guide_price_note: Savoie Maurienne guides' office: “Les Diablotins” half a day — from €45 per person in a group, “Montée au Ciel” — from €47; gear included
school_notes: Guides, gear included; from age 8

evettes-flegere-chamonix.description: A short AD via ferrata on the Flégère slope with one of the best views of the Mont Blanc massif. Suits beginners with a guide and families with teenagers; can be done in half a day including the lift. Experienced climbers can carry on to the second part — more of a bolted rock route.
evettes-flegere-chamonix.rating_basis: Chamonix's main “introductory” via ferrata, guided by the Compagnie des Guides de Chamonix and Evolution 2; Mont Blanc panorama
evettes-flegere-chamonix.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms in summer; snow early in the season; at ~2,000 m it gets cold quickly; a rope is recommended for children and beginners
evettes-flegere-chamonix.crowd_note: In July–August lots of guided groups from 10 am to 2 pm; better to take the first lift
evettes-flegere-chamonix.region: Haute-Savoie, Chamonix, the Flégère slope opposite Mont Blanc
evettes-flegere-chamonix.approach: Flégère lift from Les Praz (Chamonix), then ~20 minutes on foot following the green markings
evettes-flegere-chamonix.descent: On foot from the top, 20 minutes back to the Flégère station and down by lift
evettes-flegere-chamonix.vf_highlights: A short via ferrata with a Himalayan bridge and close-up views of Mont Blanc, the Aiguille du Midi and the Mer de Glace glacier
pros: Panorama of Mont Blanc and the Aiguille du Midi
A short approach from the lift
Plenty of guides and rental shops in Chamonix
Free (only the lift is paid)
cons: The season depends on the lift — roughly mid-June to late October
Short (150 m of ascent)
Expensive with a guide
evettes-flegere-chamonix.airport: GVA — Geneva, ~1 h; LYS — Lyon, ~2.5 h; TRN — Turin, ~2 h
evettes-flegere-chamonix.guide_price_note: Evolution 2: €79 per person in a group of 4–6, private €320 for 1–4 people + €5 rental; the lift (~€24 return) is not included; from age 12 and 150 cm tall
evettes-flegere-chamonix.fee_note: Free; only the Flégère lift is paid
school_notes: Groups and private, gear rental
Chamonix's oldest guides' office

freissinieres-grande-falaise.description: A short but very airy via ferrata on the south face above the Freissinières valley, built in 1988. Two parts (K2/K3 and K3+) with an escape route between them; there are few rungs, so you have to use hands and feet on the rock. Good in spring and autumn, when the high Alps are still under snow.
freissinieres-grande-falaise.rating_basis: A historic route — the first via ferrata in France; praised for its airiness and the quality of the cable
freissinieres-grande-falaise.hazards: Slippery polished rock, great exposure; heat on the south face on summer afternoons; peregrine falcons nest on the cliffs from February to June
freissinieres-grande-falaise.crowd_note: Usually quiet; groups on mornings in July–August
freissinieres-grande-falaise.approach: From the village of Freissinières along the road towards the Anon pass to the car park on a hairpin bend (signposted), then ~30 minutes on a waymarked trail to the western end of the cliff
freissinieres-grande-falaise.descent: On a waymarked trail via Clos du Puy (1,660 m) and through the forest back to the car park, about 1 hour
freissinieres-grande-falaise.vf_highlights: France's first via ferrata (1988): airy traverses on the south face above the valley, minimal rungs — plenty of real rock climbing
pros: France's historic first via ferrata
South-facing — season from spring to November
Free, close to the car park
Escape route after the first part
cons: Polished, slippery rock in places
No bridges or ladders — a bit dull if you like “thrill-ride” features
Check the status before you go: the Écrins National Park website carried a fire warning and a sector closure notice
freissinieres-grande-falaise.airport: TRN — Turin, ~2.5 h; GNB — Grenoble, ~2.5 h; MRS — Marseille, ~3 h

gorges-de-la-durance.description: A paid via ferrata park in the narrow Durance gorge: four routes totalling over 2 km — from a children's route (from age 4) to a black TD with an overhang and five bridges. Ideal for families and a first via ferrata, while strong climbers can add giant ziplines.
gorges-de-la-durance.rating_basis: A popular family via ferrata park in the Briançonnais; the black route is considered one of the hardest in the area
gorges-de-la-durance.hazards: Heat in the gorge in July–August; thunderstorms; the black route takes arm strength (~10 m overhang)
gorges-de-la-durance.crowd_note: In July–August lots of families and summer camps on the orange and green routes; the black one is quieter
gorges-de-la-durance.region: Hautes-Alpes, Durance gorge between Briançon and L'Argentière-la-Bessée
gorges-de-la-durance.approach: Car park by the Gamonet bridge (turn-off before La Bâtie-des-Vigneaux on the road to Vallouise), 5–10 minutes along the Durance to the start of the cables
gorges-de-la-durance.descent: 10–15 minutes on foot along the penstock and over the big bridge to the car park
gorges-de-la-durance.vf_highlights: Five suspension bridges up to 55 m above the river on the black route and two ~500 m ziplines across the gorge
gorges-de-la-durance.grade_local: F – TD (4 routes: orange, green, red, black TD)
pros: Routes for the whole family, children from age 4
Gear rental right at the start
~500 m ziplines across the gorge
Short approach and descent, a café on the riverbank
cons: Paid
Low altitude — no alpine panoramas
Open only from April to October
gorges-de-la-durance.airport: TRN — Turin, ~2 h; GNB — Grenoble, ~2.5 h; MRS — Marseille, ~3 h
gorges-de-la-durance.fee_note: Roc Aventure: via ferrata €10 (group/family €8), gear rental €14; a day with two giant ziplines and rental — €45
school_notes: Park operator: tickets, rental, ziplines

mines-du-grand-clot.description: A long and physically demanding via ferrata on the south-facing gneiss wall above La Grave: a tunnel, a chimney with rungs, an overhang on iron rungs and the old mine adits. For people who already have experience of D routes and good stamina; beginners only with a guide.
mines-du-grand-clot.rating_basis: One of the longest and most “sporty” via ferratas in France, a Hautes-Alpes classic; views of the Meije glaciers
mines-du-grand-clot.hazards: Heat and afternoon thunderstorms in summer; rockfall; possible snow on the descent in April–May and October; the waymarking on the approach has faded in places
mines-du-grand-clot.crowd_note: Even in August queues are rare — the route is long and hard
mines-du-grand-clot.region: Hautes-Alpes, La Grave, opposite the Meije massif (Écrins)
mines-du-grand-clot.approach: From the D1091 road by the former Grand Clot mines (between La Grave and Les Fréaux) 10–30 minutes up the spoil heap to the adit
mines-du-grand-clot.descent: On foot along the mule track via La Puyat to the village of Le Chazelet (1,797 m) and down to the road, 1.5–2.5 hours; it's handy to leave a second car in Le Chazelet
mines-du-grand-clot.vf_highlights: 750 m of ascent up the south face past the old adits of lead mines, with views of the Meije glaciers (3,983 m)
mines-du-grand-clot.grade_local: D (French scale; C/D on the Hüsler scale)
pros: Big ascent (750 m) and an alpine atmosphere
Views of the Meije glaciers
Few people
Free
cons: A long 1.5–2.5-hour descent, or you need a second car
South-facing — hot in July–August
Not for beginners
mines-du-grand-clot.airport: GNB — Grenoble, ~2 h; TRN — Turin, ~2 h; LYS — Lyon, ~2.5 h

sveri-georgia.description: Two routes on the cliffs by the village of Sveri near Chiatura — an easy one and a harder one, with cables and iron ladders, about 2–2.5 hours of climbing. Usually sold as a day tour from Kutaisi with lunch at the camp, a stop at the Katskhi Pillar and a swim at the waterfalls. Suits beginners and families with children from 10–12.
sveri-georgia.rating_basis: Georgia's only well-known commercial via ferrata, sold by the national tourism portal georgia.to and local agencies
sveri-georgia.hazards: Heat in July–August, slippery rock after rain
sveri-georgia.region: Imereti, Chiatura municipality, Sveri village — Sveri Adventure Camp
sveri-georgia.approach: About 20 minutes on foot from Sveri Adventure Camp; small caves along the way
sveri-georgia.vf_highlights: Billed as the first via ferrata in the Caucasus; the programme includes the Katskhi Pillar and a swim in a waterfall pool on the Sadzaliskevi river
sveri-georgia.grade_local: No formal grade: an easy route for beginners and a harder one
pros: Simple logistics from Kutaisi, all-inclusive
Suits beginners and children
The Katskhi Pillar and waterfalls on the same trip
cons: Route length and height gain not published
Season only April–October
Hot in Imereti in summer
sveri-georgia.airport: KUT — Kutaisi, ~2 hours; TBS — Tbilisi, ~3 hours
sveri-georgia.guide_price_note: Day tour: from 420 lari per person in a group of 8 to 990 lari for one person (from ~$160); guide, gear, lunch and dinner, and entry included
school_notes: Day tour, English-speaking guide, from age 12
Tour from Kutaisi, from age 10 with an adult

meteora-great-saint.description: A short rock route up one of Meteora's “suspended” rocks above Kastraki. It is a via cordata: instead of a continuous cable there are bolts, a rope belay and multi-pitch technique, so it's for climbers only if done independently, and for tourists with a guide. Technically easy, suitable for beginners in reasonable shape.
meteora-great-saint.rating_basis: Meteora is a UNESCO site and one of Greece's top destinations; the Visit Meteora tour is rated 4.9 out of 5 from 47 reviews; 4.0 on ferrataguide.com
meteora-great-saint.hazards: Heat up to +33 °C in July–August; smooth conglomerate, wet after rain; no protection at the summit cross
meteora-great-saint.crowd_note: Small guided groups; the tourist crowds are at the monasteries, not on the rock
meteora-great-saint.region: Thessaly, the Meteora rocks above the village of Kastraki near Kalambaka
meteora-great-saint.approach: From the free car park by the Church of Saints Peter and Paul in Kastraki up through the village streets past the Church of St Nicholas and along a forest path, ~35 minutes
meteora-great-saint.vf_highlights: A climb up one of the Meteora rocks to a cross with views of the monasteries, the Thessalian plain and the Pindus mountains
meteora-great-saint.grade_local: B (via cordata: rope belay on bolts, not a continuous cable)
pros: Views of the Meteora monasteries and the Pindus
Short and easy — half a day together with a monastery visit
Highly rated guided tours
cons: Not a classic via ferrata: you need a rope and a guide
Very hot in summer
Protection points are far apart, and there is none at the cross
meteora-great-saint.airport: SKG — Thessaloniki, ~3 h; ATH — Athens, ~4 h; VOL — Volos, ~2 h
meteora-great-saint.guide_price_note: Visit Meteora — from €65 per person, ~3 hours, the guide provides harness, helmet and lanyard; rated 4.9 out of 5 from 47 reviews
school_notes: Guide and gear, ~3 hours

fortica-omis.description: An easy via ferrata right above the seaside resort of Omiš: cables, ladders and metal bridges lead up the cliffs to a 16th-century fortress with views of the Cetina estuary and the islands. A good first experience for a family with children from 8 during a holiday in Dalmatia.
fortica-omis.rating_basis: Rated 4.0 on via-ferrata.de; a popular excursion for holidaymakers in Split and Makarska
fortica-omis.hazards: Heat and sun in July–August; scree on the short descent; the bora (strong wind) in winter; some loose holds
fortica-omis.crowd_note: Guided groups on summer mornings; almost nobody during the midday heat
fortica-omis.region: Dalmatia, Omiš at the mouth of the Cetina river, 25 km from Split
fortica-omis.approach: From the public car park by the tunnel at the entrance to Omiš (about €5 a day) on the path to the left of the tunnel, 5–10 minutes to the start sign
fortica-omis.descent: On foot to Omiš along an easy path, ~45 minutes, or a shorter route down steep scree to the car park
fortica-omis.vf_highlights: A climb up the cliffs straight from town to the medieval Fortica fortress (Starigrad) with views of Omiš, the Cetina canyon and the islands of Brač and Hvar
pros: Starts within the town, close to the sea
Technically easy, suits beginners and children
Views of the Cetina and the Adriatic
You can just rent the gear
cons: Very hot in summer — set off early in the morning
Three short sections without cable
There were reports (2022) of loose rungs and holds
fortica-omis.guide_price_note: MOCO Adventures: guided €60 (gear, fortress ticket, insurance, photos, minimum 2 people); independent with gear rental — €35; from age 8
fortica-omis.fee_note: The via ferrata itself is free (private; according to 2021 data no registration is needed); entry to the Fortica fortress is a small fee
school_notes: Guide or gear rental; Croatian, English

averau.description: A short, easy via ferrata to the summit of the Averau above the Rifugio Averau: a traverse, a couple of metres of vertical and a stepped chimney, then a panorama over half the Dolomites. A great first experience, including for teenagers with a guide; easy to combine with the Nuvolau, Ra Gusela and the open-air museum at the Cinque Torri.
averau.rating_basis: Cortina's classic “first via ferrata”: the tourist office calls it family-friendly and guides sell half-day outings; reviews praise the panorama, though the route itself is short
averau.hazards: Stones knocked down by groups above in the couloir, snow in the north-east couloir in June, afternoon thunderstorms; in summer the road to the Cinque Torri hut is closed to cars from 10:00 to 17:00.
averau.crowd_note: Lots of families and guided groups in summer — the chimney can jam up; quieter in the morning and in September
averau.region: Dolomites, Cinque Torri / Passo Falzarego, Cortina d'Ampezzo
averau.approach: Bai de Dones car park (Cortina — Falzarego road), chairlift to the Rifugio Scoiattoli (2,255 m), trail no. 439 to the Rifugio Averau (2,413 m) and ~15 min over scree to the start of the cable in the north-east couloir; on foot from Passo Falzarego on trails 441/419, ~1.5 h to the hut
averau.descent: The same way down the via ferrata (there is an easy A/B variant) to the Rifugio Averau, then to the Scoiattoli and down by chairlift, ~1 h
averau.vf_highlights: A short, easy via ferrata to a 2,649 m summit with a panorama of the Tofane, Cristallo, Civetta and Marmolada; nearby are the open-air First World War museum at the Cinque Torri and the oldest hut, the Nuvolau (1883)
averau.grade_local: A/B – B/C (bergsteigen.com: A/B, chimney variant B; via-ferrata.de: B/C)
pros: Almost the whole approach is by lift
Technically easy — suits beginners and families
A 2,649 m summit with a 360° panorama
The Averau and Nuvolau huts close by
cons: Very short — the via ferrata itself takes ~30 min
Jams in the chimney in summer
The last 20 min to the summit are unmarked easy scrambling
averau.airport: VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h; TSF — Treviso, ~2 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h
averau.guide_price_note: Half a day, “from” price per person for a group of 6 on Explore-Share (IFMGA-UIAGM guide from Cortina)
averau.fee_note: Free; the Cinque Torri chairlift is paid
school_notes: Half-day trip up the Averau from €119/person
Guide from Cortina, from $157/person; set rental on site €15

bocchette-centrali.description: The heart of the Via delle Bocchette: a traverse along narrow ledges with cables and ladders between the Bocca degli Armi and the Bocca di Brenta, around the legendary Campanile Basso tower. Technically easy (B) but very exposed and high, with a 4-hour approach — the classic plan is 2 days with a night at the Brentei, Alimonta or Pedrotti hut.
bocchette-centrali.rating_basis: One of the most famous via ferratas in the Alps; Planetmountain notes its great popularity, and reviews call it very scenic and “airy”
bocchette-centrali.hazards: Hard snow and ice on the Sfulmini glacier in the mornings (crampons and an ice axe needed early in the season), snow hides the cable at the Campanile Basso bocchetta, strong wind in the cols, thunderstorms — go only in settled weather.
bocchette-centrali.crowd_note: On clear days in July–August it's very crowded: a jam at the step up to the Bocca degli Armi, and it's hard to pass people coming the other way on the narrow ledges
bocchette-centrali.approach: From Madonna di Campiglio by car or taxi to the Rifugio Vallesinella (1,513 m), on trails no. 317/318 via the Rifugio Casinei to the Rifugio Brentei (2,182 m), ~2.5 h, then trail no. 323 past the Rifugio Alimonta across the Sfulmini glacier to the Bocca degli Armi (2,749 m), ~1.5 h
bocchette-centrali.descent: From the Bocca di Brenta on trail no. 318 through the Val Brenta Alta to the Rifugio Brentei (~1 h) and on to Vallesinella (~2 h); or 15 min to the Rifugio Pedrotti-Tosa (2,491 m) and on to Molveno
bocchette-centrali.vf_highlights: The famous narrow ledges (50 cm in places) above the void around the Campanile Basso and Brenta Alta — the best-known part of the Via delle Bocchette, the Brenta's signature route
bocchette-centrali.grade_local: B, variant B/C (bergsteigen.com); “moderate but very exposed” (Planetmountain)
pros: Iconic ledges and views of the Campanile Basso
Technically easy for an experienced hiker
Huts at the start and finish
cons: A long approach — effectively 2 days
Crowded in summer, hard to pass on the ledges
No emergency descents from the middle
bocchette-centrali.airport: VRN — Verona, ~2.5 h; BGY — Bergamo, ~2.5 h; VCE — Venice, ~3.5 h
bocchette-centrali.fee_note: Free; taxi/shuttle to Vallesinella and hut stays extra
school_notes: Multi-day guided Brenta traverse with hut stays

brigata-tridentina.description: A Dolomites classic on the north face of the Sella massif: from the Pisciadù waterfall up ladders and rungs to the ridge of the Exner tower and across a suspension bridge to the Rifugio Pisciadù. Technically moderate (C) with a short approach from the road — the ideal first “real” via ferrata with a guide for sporty beginners.
brigata-tridentina.rating_basis: The best-known via ferrata in the Dolomites: in almost every top list (Garmont, BMC, Planetmountain), with pages on the Alta Badia and Val Gardena tourist office websites
brigata-tridentina.hazards: Rockfall from groups above, afternoon thunderstorms in summer, snowfields on descent no. 666 early in the season (sometimes until late August); north-facing — cold in the shade.
brigata-tridentina.crowd_note: One of the busiest via ferratas in the Alps: in July–August and at weekends there are queues at the ladders and the bridge; the tourist office advises starting at dawn and avoiding weekends
brigata-tridentina.region: Dolomites, Sella massif, Passo Gardena (Alta Badia)
brigata-tridentina.approach: 5–15 minutes from the car park by the former quarry (1,956 m) on the Colfosco — Passo Gardena road, ~2.3 km east of the pass
