brigata-tridentina.descent: From the Rifugio Pisciadù (2,585 m) on trail no. 666 down the Val Setus gully to Passo Gardena and the car park, ~1.5–2 hours; alternatively trail no. 676 through the Val Mesdì to Colfosco
brigata-tridentina.vf_highlights: A suspension bridge between the Exner and Brunico towers over the void, ladders by the Pisciadù waterfall and a lake by the hut at the finish
pros: A 5–15-minute approach from the car
The famous bridge and a hut with a lake at the finish
Emergency exit by the waterfall
Easy to find a guide in Corvara and Val Gardena
cons: Very crowded in summer and at weekends
A long scree descent
Snowfields on the Val Setus descent until August
brigata-tridentina.airport: VCE — Venice, ~2.5–3 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2 h; BZO — Bolzano, ~1 h
brigata-tridentina.guide_price_note: “From” price per person for a group of 5 on Explore-Share (IFMGA guide, guiding fee only); more expensive for 1–2 people
school_notes: Alta Badia mountain guides (Corvara, Colfosco), group trips on the Tridentina
Private IFMGA guide, May–October

cesare-piazzetta.description: A short but very strenuous via ferrata to the highest point of the Sella massif: the first 30 metres are a near-vertical wall where you haul yourself up the cable, then a chimney, a bridge and an unprotected ridge to the 3,152 m summit. Only for experienced and strong climbers; not for beginners.
cesare-piazzetta.rating_basis: Known as one of the hardest via ferratas in the Dolomites (Dolomite Mountains, Planetmountain), with good reviews on Summitpost and Komoot for the summit view; a niche audience
cesare-piazzetta.hazards: Ice and cold at 2,700–3,150 m even in summer, afternoon thunderstorms, an unprotected loose ridge to the summit, rockfall; in June, snow on the descent in the Forcella Pordoi couloir.
cesare-piazzetta.crowd_note: Few people on the via ferrata itself because of the difficulty; the crowds are on the summit of Piz Boè and at the Sass Pordoi cable car
cesare-piazzetta.region: Dolomites, Sella massif, Passo Pordoi (Arabba / Canazei)
cesare-piazzetta.approach: From Passo Pordoi (car park, arrive before 9:00) past the German war memorial and up a steep path on the south slope, 1–1.5 h; alternatively the Boè / Vallon lifts from Corvara and trail no. 638 from Passo Campolongo
cesare-piazzetta.descent: From the summit of Piz Boè (3,152 m) on trail no. 638 to the Forcella Pordoi, then down the steep couloir to Passo Pordoi (~1.5 h), or from the Forcella Pordoi climb up to the Sass Pordoi cable car and ride down
cesare-piazzetta.vf_highlights: One of the most strenuous via ferratas in the Dolomites — a vertical starting wall and chimney, a small suspension bridge and the summit of Piz Boè (3,152 m), the highest point of the Sella
cesare-piazzetta.grade_local: Very difficult (Planetmountain); the vertical starting wall is up to 5+ on the rock scale according to reviews, the final ridge without cable is UIAA II
pros: A 3,000-metre summit with a panorama of the Marmolada
Few people on the via ferrata itself
The Sass Pordoi cable car can make the descent easier
cons: A very hard start — you need arm strength
Final ridge without cable (II)
Scree descent to the Pordoi
cesare-piazzetta.airport: VCE — Venice, ~3 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h; BZO — Bolzano, ~1.5 h
cesare-piazzetta.fee_note: Free; the Sass Pordoi cable car is paid
school_notes: Private IFMGA guide, meeting at Passo Pordoi at 8:30, May–September; bring your own gear

cima-capi-susatti.description: A panoramic ridge via ferrata above Riva del Garda: short steep steps with rungs, an exposed traverse round a boulder below the summit and First World War trenches, with the descent down a second via ferrata, the Foletti. Technically easy (B), but 5 hours and 500+ m of ascent make it a good full day for fit beginners; children should be on a rope.
cima-capi-susatti.rating_basis: Often called the most beautiful via ferrata on Lake Garda: 360 Garda Life gives it 5/5 for scenery and experience; the route was renovated in 2009; included in Arco guides' programmes
cima-capi-susatti.hazards: Heat and sun on the south slopes in summer (bring plenty of water), a narrow exposed summit ridge, short unprotected sections, ice and snow in winter; rockfall from groups.
cima-capi-susatti.crowd_note: In high season “very crowded and hot” — start early and avoid the midday heat
cima-capi-susatti.region: Trentino, northern shore of Lake Garda — Riva del Garda / Biacesa (Ledro)
cima-capi-susatti.approach: From Riva del Garda along the road to the Val di Ledro through the tunnels to Biacesa (418 m, ~7 km), parking by the playground (or bus no. 2); on SAT trails 470 (Sentiero del Bech) and 405 to the start of the cable on the ridge
cima-capi-susatti.descent: From the summit of Cima Capi (909 m) down the north slope (easy but exposed) to the saddle before Cima Rocca, then down the Mario Foletti via ferrata (SAT 460, A/B) to the Bivacco Arcioni by the church of San Giovanni and by path/road to Biacesa, ~1.5 h
cima-capi-susatti.vf_highlights: A ridge right above Lake Garda with views of Monte Baldo, Riva and the Sarca and Ledro valleys; Austrian First World War trenches and concrete passages, a flag and summit book at the top
cima-capi-susatti.grade_local: B (bergsteigen.com); EEA on the CAI scale; the descent via the Foletti via ferrata is A/B
pros: The best Lake Garda views of any via ferrata
A loop combining two via ferratas
Doable almost year-round
First World War trenches and passages
cons: Hot and crowded in summer
A narrow exposed ridge near the summit, some sections without cable
Approach ~1–1.5 h
cima-capi-susatti.airport: VRN — Verona, ~1.2 h; BGY — Bergamo, ~2 h; VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h
cima-capi-susatti.guide_price_note: Mmove: “Via ferrata Cima Capi” from €100, ~6 hours, starting from Arco
school_notes: Guide, from €100
Guided trip from Riva/Arco

colodri-arco.description: A short, easy via ferrata on Monte Colodri straight from Arco: cable and rungs up a smooth wall, a vertical section on rungs at the end, and at the top a panorama of the Sarca valley and Lake Garda. Ideal for a first time and for children with their parents or a guide; doable almost year-round.
colodri-arco.rating_basis: Arco's classic training via ferrata (built by the S.A.T. in 1981), sold as a family outing by every guiding office around Garda; short in itself
colodri-arco.hazards: Rockfall from groups above (put your gear on before approaching the wall), heat in summer, ice on cold winter days; slippery polished rock when damp.
colodri-arco.crowd_note: Very crowded, especially at weekends and on holidays: guided groups and families; a weekday and early morning are better
colodri-arco.region: Trentino, northern shore of Lake Garda — Arco (Prabi)
colodri-arco.approach: Car park by the Arco campsite / municipal swimming pool in Prabi (next to the Rock Master climbing wall), ~5 minutes from the road on trail no. 431b to the start of the cable
colodri-arco.descent: From the summit of Monte Colodri along the Sentiero dei Lecci to the church of Santa Maria di Laghel (drinking fountain) and into central Arco, then on foot to Prabi, ~1 h; the variant via Monte Colt is exposed and needs a full set
colodri-arco.vf_highlights: The most accessible “first via ferrata” in the Garda area: rungs and cable up the wall right above Arco, with views of the Sarca valley and the northern tip of Lake Garda; year-round
colodri-arco.grade_local: A/B (Garda Trentino / Visit Trentino); EEA on the CAI scale
pros: The start is 5 minutes from the car park
Doable almost year-round
Plenty of guides and gear rental in Arco
Suitable for children
cons: Very crowded
Hot in summer — go in the morning
The via ferrata itself is short
colodri-arco.airport: VRN — Verona, ~1 h; BGY — Bergamo, ~2 h; VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h
school_notes: Guide, from €65
Guided family outing
Private guide from Arco

ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.description: A via ferrata on the summit of the Paganella with a lift right to the start: 1 km of cable along the cliffs of the “eagle” face, cable bridges, a spiral staircase and a long exposed ledge, with strictly one-way traffic. A good option for a first time with a guide and for teenagers aged 12–14+, with Lake Molveno and Andalo nearby.
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.rating_basis: A new “sporty-touristy” via ferrata with bridges and a lift to the start: sold by several agencies at once (Trentino Wild, LOLgarda, Manawa, CheckYeti); Trentino family guides recommend it for teenagers
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms (the summit is exposed, and the route is officially dangerous in rain), slippery rock when damp, exposed ledges; keep your distance — one person per 2–3 anchors.
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.crowd_note: Lots of guided groups in summer; one-way traffic helps, but there can be waits at the bridges — better with the first lifts
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.region: Trentino, Paganella plateau — Andalo (between the Brenta Dolomites and Trento)
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.approach: From Andalo by the Andalo — Doss Pelà gondola and the lift to the summit of the Paganella (or from Fai della Paganella by the “Paganella 2001” cable car); a few minutes from the top station to the start at the Battisti couloir
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.descent: One-way traffic only — from the Battisti couloir to the “Eagle's Throne”; back to the lift on the Aquile or Botanico trail, ~30–45 min, and down by lift
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.vf_highlights: Cable bridges, a spiral staircase and a long exposed ledge above the drop with views of the Adige valley, Lake Molveno and the Brenta; a lift right to the start
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.grade_local: A–C for the classic line; variants D–E (official Paganella website)
pros: Lift right to the start
Bridges and ladders — lots of features in 2 hours
Plenty of guided trips with gear rental
One-way traffic
cons: Open only while the summer lifts are running
Lift fare to pay
Dangerous in rain and thunderstorms — it closes
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.airport: VRN — Verona, ~1.5 h; VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h; BGY — Bergamo, ~2.5 h
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.guide_price_note: Group trip with a Trentino Wild guide, gear and gloves included, lift extra; from age 14 (height from 1.40 m), July to mid-September
ferrata-delle-aquile-paganella.fee_note: Free; the Paganella lifts are paid
school_notes: Group trip, €100/person, gear included
Guide and gear, from age 12; guides speak 6 languages (Russian not among them)

giovanni-lipella.description: A long high-alpine via ferrata on the Tofana di Rozes: in through the wartime Castelletto tunnel, then ladders, ledges and walls up the west face to the ridge at 3,000 m and on foot to the 3,225 m summit. You need to be fit and have experience of C via ferratas — this is a full mountain day, not a stroll.
giovanni-lipella.rating_basis: A Cortina classic: Planetmountain calls it one of the most popular and historically significant via ferratas; 4.5/5 on via-ferrata.de
giovanni-lipella.hazards: Snow and ice in the upper section and on the descent in June and after snowfalls, rockfall from groups and during the thaw, afternoon thunderstorms on a long route; the tunnel is slippery and dark — a headtorch is essential.
giovanni-lipella.crowd_note: Busy in summer, but the route is long and groups spread out; start early to beat the thunderstorms
giovanni-lipella.approach: By car from Cortina along the Passo Falzarego road to the car park at the Rifugio Dibona (2,037 m), then on trails no. 442/404 west below the south face of the Tofana to the entrance of the Castelletto gallery, ~1–1.5 h
giovanni-lipella.descent: From the summit back along the ridge and down the normal route (blue markings, scree) to the Rifugio Giussani (2,580 m), then on trail no. 403 to the Rifugio Dibona, ~2.5 h. Emergency exit at the Tre Dita (2,694 m) towards the Rifugio Giussani
giovanni-lipella.vf_highlights: The start through the dark 500-metre Castelletto gallery, dug by the Alpini in 1916, and the climb to the 3,000-metre summit of the Tofana di Rozes (3,225 m)
giovanni-lipella.grade_local: C (Hüsler scale, via-ferrata.de); some C/D sections (mountain topos, hoehenrausch.de)
pros: A First World War tunnel and a 3,225 m summit
Huge views of Cortina and the Fanes
Emergency exit halfway (Tre Dita)
cons: 8–9 hours and ~1,300 m of ascent including the approach
A slippery dark tunnel — you need a headtorch
A tiring scree descent
giovanni-lipella.airport: VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h; TSF — Treviso, ~2 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h
school_notes: Private IFMGA guide from Cortina

ivano-dibona.description: A long high-alpine traverse of the Cristallo massif along First World War positions: technically easy (B) but with partly unprotected ledges, scree and 10+ hours on the go, including the walk up to Staunies. For fit, experienced hikers; beginners only with a guide and in good weather.
ivano-dibona.rating_basis: A legendary traverse with the bridge from “Cliffhanger”, 4.2/5 on via-ferrata.de; without the upper lift it has become noticeably harder and is done less often
ivano-dibona.hazards: Snow and ice early in the season (in June 2023 hikers were turning back), thunderstorms on a long ridge with no quick escapes, unprotected ledges near the Vecchio del Forame, steep scree below the Forcella Alta; rescue options are limited — start early.
ivano-dibona.crowd_note: Since the Staunies gondola closed there are few people; there can be groups at the bridge at the start, but the ridge is almost empty
ivano-dibona.approach: Rio Gere chairlift (Passo Tre Croci road) to the Rifugio Son Forca (2,215 m), then on foot up steep scree to the Forcella Staunies and the Rifugio Lorenzi (2,932 m), 2.5–3 h and ~700 m of ascent. The Son Forca — Staunies gondola has been out of service since 2016; 2026 reviews mention preparations for a new lift, but no date has been announced
ivano-dibona.descent: The route is a ridge traverse heading downhill almost the whole time: via the Forcella Grande and the Bivacco Buffa di Perrero to the Col dei Stombi (2,168 m) and along the old military path down the Val Grande to Ospitale (SS51 road), ~8–8.5 h from Staunies; back to Cortina by bus or taxi. Returning to Tre Croci on trail 203 means another ~400 m of ascent
ivano-dibona.vf_highlights: The 30-metre “Ponte Cristallo” suspension bridge at the start (where Stallone's “Cliffhanger” was filmed), First World War tunnels and fortifications on the ridge with views of the Tre Cime and Misurina
ivano-dibona.grade_local: B (Hüsler scale, via-ferrata.de); the dolomiti.it tourist office rates it D because of its length: a long high-alpine traverse
pros: The “Cliffhanger” bridge and views of the Tre Cime
First World War history at every step
Hardly any queues
cons: The upper lift has been closed since 2016 — a hard 2.5–3-hour climb up scree
A very long day, and the finish is far from the start — you need a transfer
Partly without cable: ledges and scree
ivano-dibona.airport: VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h; TSF — Treviso, ~2 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h
ivano-dibona.fee_note: Free; the Rio Gere — Son Forca chairlift is paid
school_notes: Directory of IFMGA guides in Cortina; the Dibona on request

marmolada-cresta-ovest.description: A via ferrata up the west ridge to Punta Penia (3,343 m), the highest point of the Dolomites: an approach from Passo Fedaia across a small glacier, then polished slabs and 450 m of cable above the huge south face. A serious 8–10-hour high-alpine day; without experience, only with a guide and with crampons.
marmolada-cresta-ovest.rating_basis: The only via ferrata on the “Queen of the Dolomites”; according to guides (Explore-Share, 2025) it is now the most common option for a guided ascent of Punta Penia
marmolada-cresta-ovest.hazards: Crevasses and instability of the Marmolada glacier (serac collapse on 3 July 2022, 11 dead; areas were closed by order of the mayor of Canazei), ice and snow on the ridge, thunderstorms on the open ridge, altitude of 3,300+ m. Check the current restrictions before setting out.
marmolada-cresta-ovest.crowd_note: In July–August you meet groups coming the other way on the ridge — passing places were added after 2022; people start at 6–7 am
marmolada-cresta-ovest.region: Dolomites, Marmolada — the highest point of the Dolomites, Passo Fedaia / Val di Fassa (Canazei)
marmolada-cresta-ovest.approach: From Passo Fedaia (2,057 m) on foot to Pian dei Fiacconi (2,722 m), past the Gran Vernel and across a small glacier to the Forcella Marmolada (2,910 m), where the cable starts; alternatively from Alba di Canazei via the Rifugio Contrin on trail no. 606 (often with an overnight stay)
marmolada-cresta-ovest.descent: The same way back along the ridge or, if the guides consider the glacier passable, by the normal route across the Marmolada glacier to Pian dei Fiacconi and Fedaia (crampons, ice axe, rope); in 2022, after the collapse, descent was allowed only by the ascent route
marmolada-cresta-ovest.vf_highlights: A via ferrata to the highest point of the Dolomites — Punta Penia (3,343 m) above the 800-metre south face; there is a hut, the Capanna Punta Penia, right on the summit
marmolada-cresta-ovest.grade_local: Difficult: “grade 4” per the Veneto region's guides, “experienced only” (Dolomite Mountains); plus a small glacier crossing — crampons
pros: The Dolomites' No. 1 summit
An incredible ridge above the south face
You can stay overnight in a hut on the summit itself
cons: Glacier on the approach/descent — you need crampons and the skills
A very long day, ~1,350 m of ascent
Route status depends on the glacier — decided at the last minute
marmolada-cresta-ovest.airport: VCE — Venice, ~3 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h; BZO — Bolzano, ~1.5 h
marmolada-cresta-ovest.guide_price_note: “From” price on Explore-Share (guide Renato, 2025); with the guides “Filippo e Francesco” (Veneto region website) — €190/person for groups of 3+, departures on Fridays at 7:00 from Fedaia
marmolada-cresta-ovest.fee_note: Free; staying overnight at the Capanna Punta Penia on the summit requires a booking
school_notes: IFMGA guides; west ridge or normal route over the glacier depending on conditions
Group trip on Fridays, €190/person

punta-anna-olivieri.description: A steep and very exposed via ferrata up the south ridge of Punta Anna above Cortina: vertical sections straight away, lots of arm work, excellent rock. For people who have done C via ferratas and want the next level; with the lift to Pomedes the start is just 30 minutes away.
punta-anna-olivieri.rating_basis: One of Cortina's most popular hard via ferratas: several guides sell it as a separate tour; 4.7/5 on via-ferrata.de for the Olivieri + Aglio combination
punta-anna-olivieri.hazards: Big exposure and friction sections, afternoon thunderstorms, snow on the descent via the Bus de Tofana early in the season, ice on the Aglio continuation; rockfall from groups above.
punta-anna-olivieri.crowd_note: In summer lots of groups arrive with the first chairs — it gets crowded on the steep sections; reviews recommend an early start
punta-anna-olivieri.approach: From the Pie Tofana car park (Cortina) by two chairlifts to the Rifugio Pomedes (2,303 m), then ~30 min to the start below the Punta Anna ridge; without the lift — from the Rifugio Dibona on trail no. 421, ~1 h
punta-anna-olivieri.descent: From Punta Anna: down the scree of the Bus de Tofana and Vallon de Tofana to the Rifugio Giussani and on trail no. 403 to the Dibona (for experienced hikers); or to the Ra Valles cable car mid-station and along the easy Sentiero Olivieri to Pomedes, then down by chairlift. To continue — the Aglio via ferrata to the Tofana di Mezzo (3,244 m) and down by cable car
punta-anna-olivieri.vf_highlights: A steep, airy south ridge right above Cortina, a 360° panorama from Punta Anna, and the option of continuing to the summit of the Tofana di Mezzo (3,244 m)
punta-anna-olivieri.grade_local: D (Hüsler scale, via-ferrata.de); “for experts” according to the Cortina tourist office
pros: A lift almost to the start
A steep, “proper” route on good rock
Can be extended to the 3,000-metre Tofana di Mezzo
cons: Hard from the very first metres — not for beginners without a guide
A tough scree descent
No water or huts on the route
punta-anna-olivieri.airport: VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h; TSF — Treviso, ~2 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h
punta-anna-olivieri.guide_price_note: “From” price per person for a group of 5 on Explore-Share (guide Renato); other guides — from €152
punta-anna-olivieri.fee_note: Free; the Pie Tofana — Pomedes chairlifts and the Tofana cable car are paid
school_notes: Tours of Punta Anna from €119–152/person (group of 5)
Tofana cable car: lifts and via ferrata descriptions

rino-pisetta.description: A very hard, strenuous via ferrata on the south face of Monte Garzolet above Lake Toblino: smooth polished slabs with almost nothing to stand on, and the hardest part (D/E) right at the start. Only for experienced and very strong climbers; if the start feels too hard, take the bypass on the right. The season is almost year-round, except in heat or when the rock is wet.
rino-pisetta.rating_basis: The cult “hardest via ferrata” of the Garda area; 2024–2026 reviews on via-ferrata.de give 4.5–5 out of 5 (“extremely hard and beautiful”)
rino-pisetta.hazards: Heat and sun on the south face in summer, slippery slabs after rain, big exposure on the final slab traverse, rockfall: because of a rockfall risk the route was closed from 15 October 2025 and reopened on 24 April 2026 (at your own risk) — check the status before you go.
rino-pisetta.crowd_note: Few people, but there can be a bottleneck at the hard start — many get stuck there; busier at weekends in spring and autumn
rino-pisetta.region: Trentino, Sarca valley by Lake Toblino (Sarche), 20 km north of Lake Garda
rino-pisetta.approach: From the public car park in the centre of Sarche (259 m, big “Picol Dain” sign) up a faintly marked path and across scree to the sign at the start, ~45 min
rino-pisetta.descent: From the summit of the Dain Piccolo (971 m) on a marked trail towards Ranzo, then along a wide track past the chapel of San Vigilio back to Sarche, ~1.5 h; alternatively through the Val Busa gorge to Lake Toblino. Descending the via ferrata is not allowed
rino-pisetta.vf_highlights: Built in 1982 and long considered the hardest via ferrata in the Eastern Alps: a smooth south face with almost no footholds, where you hang on the cable above Lake Toblino and the Sarca valley
rino-pisetta.grade_local: E (Hüsler scale; D start with an E section)
pros: Doable almost year-round (Mediterranean climate)
A legendary test of arm strength
Views of Lake Toblino and the Sarca valley
cons: Not for beginners — the hardest section is right at the start
In summer the south face bakes (shade only after 15:00)
The slabs are polished and very slippery when damp
rino-pisetta.airport: VRN — Verona, ~1.5 h; BGY — Bergamo, ~2 h; VCE — Venice, ~2.5 h

via-delle-trincee.description: A ridge via ferrata along the Padon chain with a panorama of the Marmolada glacier: right by the cable car there is a steep, smooth 30-metre wall (the hardest part), then the ridge, a bridge and First World War tunnels. A good second or third route after the easy via ferratas; beginners with a guide.
via-delle-trincee.rating_basis: In most top lists of Dolomites via ferratas (Planetmountain, Dolomite Mountains, sportoutdoor24); the best views of the Marmolada, First World War history
via-delle-trincee.hazards: Slippery, smooth volcanic rock on the starting wall (especially in wet weather), exposure on the ridge, afternoon thunderstorms; the tunnels are dark — you need a torch, and there is a fork in the last tunnel.
via-delle-trincee.crowd_note: In summer a queue forms at the starting wall with the first cable cars; better to go up at opening time or walk in from Fedaia
via-delle-trincee.region: Dolomites, Padon ridge opposite the Marmolada, Arabba / Passo Fedaia
via-delle-trincee.approach: Arabba — Porta Vescovo cable car (2,478 m), a few minutes along the path from the top station; on foot from Passo Fedaia on trail no. 698, ~45 min – 1.5 h
via-delle-trincee.descent: From the ridge via the Bivacco Bontadini (2,550 m) to the Rifugio Padon (2,390 m), then along the path below the south slope back to Porta Vescovo (a short climb at the end) or down trail no. 699 to Lake Fedaia, ~1.5 h
via-delle-trincee.vf_highlights: Dark volcanic rock, a ridge facing the Marmolada glacier, a suspension bridge and First World War tunnels and trenches
via-delle-trincee.grade_local: C/D (Hüsler scale; the smooth 30-metre starting wall is D)
pros: A lift almost to the start
The best views of the Marmolada and the Sella
First World War tunnels and trenches
An intermediate emergency exit
cons: The hardest section comes right at the start, before you've warmed up
Queues at the wall in summer
You need a torch for the tunnels
via-delle-trincee.airport: VCE — Venice, ~3 h; INN — Innsbruck, ~2.5 h; BZO — Bolzano, ~1.5 h
via-delle-trincee.guide_price_note: “From” price per person for a group of 4 on Explore-Share (GAI guide from Arabba)
via-delle-trincee.fee_note: Free; the Arabba — Porta Vescovo cable car is paid
school_notes: GAI guide, departure from Arabba

todra-gorge-via-ferrata.description: A short, easy via ferrata (200 m, about an hour) on the sheer walls of the Todra Gorge — a popular stop on the way from Marrakech to the Sahara (Merzouga). Suits beginners and children with a guide; gear can be rented at a shop at the entrance to the gorge.
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.rating_basis: 4.0/5 from 36 people who have done it on ferrataguide.com; a short route, but in a very spectacular setting; the cables are rated as in average condition
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.hazards: Heat in July–August — go in the morning while it's in shade; rockfall from the gorge walls; flash floods in the riverbed in autumn and spring; check gear from local rental outfits
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Few people on the cables, but the gorge itself fills with tour buses during the day — come in the morning
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.approach: 5 minutes from the car park in the narrowest part of the gorge (≈15 km from Tinghir): cross the road and the dry riverbed
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.descent: On foot back down the path, ~15 minutes
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: Cables and rungs on the 300-metre limestone walls of the narrowest point of the Todra Gorge — one of Morocco's top natural sights; a rare via ferrata in Africa
pros: Easy to fit into a Marrakech — Sahara tour
Spectacular gorge walls
Doable year-round
cons: Very short
Cables in average condition
Hot in the gorge in summer
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.airport: OZZ — Ouarzazate, ~3 h; ERH — Errachidia, ~2.5 h; RAK — Marrakech, ~7 h
todra-gorge-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: DesertTrail Adventures via Expedia/Wotif: ~80 Australian dollars per person for 1.5 hours, guide, helmet and harness included; prices with local guides in the gorge are negotiable
school_notes: Guide and gear, meeting point in Ait Lahbib, optional horse ride

via-ferrata-kotor.description: A short via ferrata (about 200 m of cable) right above Kotor's Old Town, opened in 2018. Technically easy, done with a guide who is also a trained rescuer, gear provided; a good way to see the Bay of Kotor from above in a couple of hours during a beach holiday.
via-ferrata-kotor.rating_basis: A popular excursion from cruise ships and from Budva; a short route, but with a picture-postcard view of Kotor
via-ferrata-kotor.hazards: Heat in July–August; heavy rain and wet rock in winter; stones dislodged by people above
via-ferrata-kotor.crowd_note: Only small guided groups; busier on days when cruise ships are in port
via-ferrata-kotor.region: Bay of Kotor (Boka Kotorska), at the mouth of the Škurda canyon next to Kotor's Old Town
via-ferrata-kotor.approach: 10 minutes on foot from Kotor's Old Town to the mouth of the Škurda canyon (Tabačina); the start is about 100 m behind the “Vodovod” building
via-ferrata-kotor.descent: On foot down the path to Kotor, about 30 minutes
via-ferrata-kotor.vf_highlights: Montenegro's first via ferrata (2018): a short climb up the cliffs with views of the Old Town, the Bay of Kotor and the Fortress of St John
pros: The start is 10 minutes from the Old Town
Views of Kotor and the bay
Open year-round
Suitable for beginners
cons: Very short
Hot in summer — better in the morning
November–January are the rainiest months in the Boka
via-ferrata-kotor.airport: TIV — Tivat, ~15 minutes; TGD — Podgorica, ~1.5 h; DBV — Dubrovnik, ~1.5 h
school_notes: Guide, helmet, harness, gloves; year-round
Guide and gear, ~2 hours

barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.description: A short via ferrata in an adventure park on the rim of the Copper Canyon by Divisadero station: first a 45 m abseil down the wall, then rungs, a suspension bridge and a “Tarzan jump”. Done with a park instructor, no experience required. It makes sense to combine it with the “Chepe” train, the zipline and the cable car.
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.rating_basis: A small via ferrata, but in one of Mexico's most spectacular places; the park is described by México Desconocido and Programa Destinos México
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.hazards: Altitude ~2,200 m; summer thunderstorms in the rainy season (July–September); cold mornings and occasional snow in winter; the park sometimes closes for cable car maintenance
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.crowd_note: The main flow is “Chepe” train passengers around midday; quiet in the morning
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.region: Chihuahua, Sierra Tarahumara, Copper Canyon — Divisadero
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.approach: The park is by Divisadero station on the “Chepe” (Chihuahua–Pacífico) railway and the Piedra Volada viewpoint; sign up on site at the park
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.descent: The route starts with a 45-metre abseil down the canyon wall and climbs back up via rungs and bridges
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: An abseil, rungs, a suspension bridge and a “Tarzan jump” on the rim of the Copper Canyon — a canyon system deeper than the Grand Canyon; nearby are 7 zipline runs (4.1 km), a ZipRider and a 3-kilometre cable car
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.grade_local: No official grade; doable by anyone in good physical shape
pros: Views of the Copper Canyon
Inexpensive
A whole adventure park next door
cons: The route is short
A long way to get there — by train or a long drive from Chihuahua
Little precise information about the route
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.airport: CUU — Chihuahua, ~5 h by car; LMM — Los Mochis (“Chepe” train)
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: With a park instructor: about 600–800 Mexican pesos per person, gear included (earlier sources give 450 pesos)
barrancas-del-cobre-via-ferrata.fee_note: No separate park entry ticket found; the cable car and ziplines are paid separately
school_notes: Park operator: instructors, gear, ziplines and cable car

kinabalu-mountain-torq.description: A system of about 1.2 km of cables on the Panalaban granite wall between 3,400 and 3,800 m, built by Mountain Torq in 2007. There are two options: the introductory Walk the Torq (PD) and the longer Low's Peak Circuit (AD) with a suspension bridge. Done on the second day of the Kinabalu climb, after sunrise on the summit; LPC from age 10.
kinabalu-mountain-torq.rating_basis: Asia's best-known via ferrata, “the highest in the world” according to the operator; sold by every agency in Sabah together with the climb to Borneo's highest point
kinabalu-mountain-torq.hazards: Altitude of 3,800 m — altitude sickness is possible after the night ascent; cold, rain and fog, especially November–January; the granite is slippery in wet weather
kinabalu-mountain-torq.crowd_note: Climber numbers are limited by permits, and the groups on the cables are small; permits and hut places sell out months ahead
kinabalu-mountain-torq.region: Sabah (Borneo), Kinabalu National Park, Panalaban rock face
kinabalu-mountain-torq.approach: Day 1: 4–5 hours on foot from Timpohon Gate to the hut at Panalaban (3,289 m), mandatory briefing; day 2: set off at 2:30 for sunrise on Low's Peak (4,095 m), then meet the instructor at the Sayat-Sayat hut (3,668 m)
kinabalu-mountain-torq.descent: The route leads down to the Panalaban huts; after breakfast, descend on foot to Timpohon Gate, 5–6 hours
kinabalu-mountain-torq.vf_highlights: The world's highest via ferrata according to the operator (opened in 2007): up to 3,800 m on Kinabalu's granite wall, a 22-metre suspension bridge at 3,600 m, sunrise on Low's Peak
kinabalu-mountain-torq.grade_local: Low's Peak Circuit — AD (French scale); Walk the Torq — PD
pros: Unique altitude and a 4,095 m summit on the same trip
All-inclusive: guide, hut, gear
Suitable for beginners (Walk the Torq)
cons: Expensive and only as a 2–3-day package
You have to book months ahead
In bad weather the route is cancelled with no refund
kinabalu-mountain-torq.airport: BKI — Kota Kinabalu, ~2 hours to the park
kinabalu-mountain-torq.guide_price_note: 2-day/1-night package with Walk the Torq for foreigners: 3,090–3,790 ringgit (MYR 3,290 in a group of 2–3, ≈€660); guide, instructor, hut, meals, permit, park fee, transfers
kinabalu-mountain-torq.fee_note: The park fee and climbing permit are included in the package; you can't go up the mountain without one
school_notes: 2–3-day packages, via ferrata instructor included
Packages with the Pendant Hut

queenstown-via-ferrata.description: A half-day guided via ferrata on the cliffs right above Queenstown: ladders, rungs and paths between the walls, over 300 m of vertical. No experience needed, ages 12 and up. A good option if you have half a day free in Queenstown between a bungee jump and a trip to Milford Sound.
queenstown-via-ferrata.rating_basis: 5.0 from 7 reviews on BookMe, write-ups by Atlas & Boots and Destinationless Travel; a handy half-day route in the adventure capital
queenstown-via-ferrata.hazards: Sudden weather changes, cold wind and frost on the rock in winter (June–August); strong sun in summer
queenstown-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Small groups of up to 4 people per guide — no queues
queenstown-via-ferrata.region: South Island, Otago, Queenstown — cliffs above Lake Wakatipu by Queenstown Hill
queenstown-via-ferrata.approach: Meet at the Adventure Centre (39 Camp Street) in central Queenstown, about 5 minutes' drive to the start of the route
queenstown-via-ferrata.descent: On foot down with the guide; optionally a zipline descent through the pine forest towards Queenstown Hill
queenstown-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: New Zealand's first via ferrata: rungs and ladders on glacier-polished rock right above Queenstown, with views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables
queenstown-via-ferrata.grade_local: No official grade: two options of different difficulty, no experience needed
pros: 5 minutes from central Queenstown
Beautiful lake views
Small groups
cons: Guided only
Pricey for 2 hours of climbing
Less well known than Wildwire in Wanaka
queenstown-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Only with a Canyon Explorers guide (up to 4 people per guide): 189 New Zealand dollars per person for 3.5 hours, gear included; starts at 9:15 and 13:30
queenstown-via-ferrata.fee_note: No separate fee — only as part of a tour
school_notes: The only via ferrata operator in Queenstown, gear included

wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.description: A via ferrata alongside the double Twin Falls near Wanaka, billed as the world's highest waterfall via ferrata. The short Level 1 (from age 10) suits beginners, while the full Level 3 is a day of climbing on rungs, bridges and an overhang, with lunch at the top and a helicopter ride down. Guided only.
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.rating_basis: TripAdvisor 5.0 from 1,452 reviews, Qualmark Gold quality mark; articles in Smithsonian and The Manual
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.hazards: Spray and wet rock by the waterfall, cold and wind in spring and autumn, helicopter cancellations in bad weather; the overhang in the upper section takes arm strength
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.crowd_note: Small guided groups (from 2 people) — no queues; in summer book a few days ahead
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.region: South Island, Otago, Wanaka — Mount Aspiring Road
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.approach: 20 minutes' drive from Wanaka (11 km from Wanaka Airport), transfer from the town centre; from the base to the foot of Twin Falls
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.descent: Level 1 — 20 minutes down on foot; Level 3 — by helicopter from the top to the valley
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.vf_highlights: The world's highest waterfall via ferrata: ~2,500 rungs and 450 m of vertical alongside Twin Falls, 7 bridges, a passage behind a 60-metre waterfall and a helicopter from the top
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.grade_local: Operator's levels 1–3: Level 1 — the lower part for beginners, Level 2 — intermediate, Level 3 — the whole route including the overhang
pros: A world record and views of the Southern Alps
Options from 2 to 7 hours
Helicopter descent
cons: Expensive, especially Level 3
Closed in June–July
Weight limit 40–100 kg
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.airport: ZQN — Queenstown, ~1 h; WKA — Wanaka (domestic flights)
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.guide_price_note: Only with a Wildwire guide, New Zealand dollars: Level 1 (≈1 h on the cables, 4 bridges) — $205; Level 3 with lunch and helicopter — $750–769; gear included
wildwire-wanaka-lord-of-the-rungs.fee_note: No separate fee — only as part of a tour
school_notes: The only operator: guide, gear, transfer from Wanaka, helicopter on Level 3

jebel-shams-via-ferrata.description: A short but exposed via ferrata on the top 200 m of the Wadi Ghul canyon wall: from the abandoned village of As Sab, cables and rungs lead back up to the rim of the plateau. Takes 1–2 hours as part of a loop with the Balcony Walk trail. Guided only: suits people in good shape with no fear of heights.
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.rating_basis: Oman's best-known mountain route (the Balcony Walk) plus a via ferrata in many Muscat tour operators' programmes; an Oman Observer article
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.hazards: Sun and heat with no shade from May to September — carry plenty of water; big exposure above the canyon; on winter nights it can be around zero at the rim
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.region: Ad Dakhiliyah, Al Hamra, Jebel Shams plateau — the rim of the Wadi Ghul canyon by the abandoned village of As Sab
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.approach: From the village of Al Khitaym along the Balcony Walk trail on the canyon rim to the abandoned village of As Sab (Sab Bani Khamis), about 2 km
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.descent: The route tops out on the canyon rim, then back on foot to Al Khitaym — a loop
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: A wall above Wadi Ghul, the “Grand Canyon of Oman”: cables and rungs on the top 200 m of the cliff after the classic Balcony Walk trail
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.grade_local: Moderate to difficult lower section (per local press descriptions); no formal grade
pros: Views of one of Arabia's deepest canyons
Can be combined with the Balcony Walk and a night on the plateau
Comfortable in winter: 14–20 °C during the day
cons: Hard to find and do the route without a guide
Hot with no shade in summer
A long drive from Muscat (~3.5 h)
jebel-shams-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Guided tour, ~5 h — from $150 (≈€130) per person, gear included; from age 14
school_notes: 5-hour tour from the Cliff Café, from $150
3 days from Muscat with camping, from age 15
Day trip from Muscat, Balcony Walk + via ferrata

skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.description: South America's most famous via ferrata: a climb on rungs up a sheer wall in the Sacred Valley to the transparent pods of the Skylodge hotel, then lunch or an overnight stay and a descent by zipline. No experience needed, children from age 8. The main difficulty is the altitude of ~3,000 m above sea level.
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.rating_basis: A world-famous attraction thanks to the Skylodge pod hotel (Traveller, Malay Mail, Original Travel, Scott Dunn); very popular with tourists in Cusco
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.hazards: Altitude sickness in the first days; strong high-altitude sun; in the rainy season (December–March) wet rock and afternoon downpours; hypothermia in the wind
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.crowd_note: Natura Vive groups start in the morning; in the dry season (June–August) several groups are on the wall one after another
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.region: Cusco, Sacred Valley of the Incas, Pachar — between Urubamba and Ollantaytambo
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.approach: About an hour by car from Cusco to Pachar (Urubamba — Ollantaytambo road), a few minutes from the road to the wall
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.descent: Down by 6 zipline runs from 100 to 500–700 m (~2 km in total), ~35 minutes' walk to the first line; in the short version — an abseil and a walk down
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.vf_highlights: A climb on rungs and bridges up a sheer ~300–400 m wall to Skylodge's transparent pod rooms hanging on the cliff above the Sacred Valley; a descent by 6 zipline runs
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.grade_local: No official grade; per the operators: Moderate–Demanding
pros: A unique sight — pod rooms on a cliff
Easy to combine with Machu Picchu and Cusco
Season almost year-round
cons: Expensive
Altitude ~3,000 m — you need to acclimatise in Cusco
Only as part of a tour
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.guide_price_note: “Via ferrata + zipline + 4-course lunch at Skylodge” package with transfer from Cusco — ~$278 via Civitatis; a night in a Skylodge pod is a separate, expensive package. Gear and guide (English/Spanish) included
skylodge-via-ferrata-sacred-valley.fee_note: Only as part of a Natura Vive tour
school_notes: Owner of the route and Skylodge: guides, gear
Full-day tour with transfer from Cusco
Page in Russian; the guide's language is not specified

aktru-kanyon.description: A 700 m route up a canyon on the south-east slope of Kyzyltash peak, built in 2019–2020 by the Aktru mountaineering camp. Sections called “Ledges”, “Canyon”, “Ridge”, “Big Tower” and “Final Push”, with rungs on the hard bits, rest platforms and views of the glaciers. Suits people with basic experience and their own set; beginners should go with a camp instructor.
aktru-kanyon.rating_basis: A detailed guide by the Russian Mountaineering Federation, a mention in a scientific paper on the development of via ferratas in Russia; a well-known but remote location
aktru-kanyon.hazards: Sudden weather changes and snow in June and September, cold at altitude; a via ferrata set with an energy absorber (EN 958) and a helmet are mandatory; wet grass on the descent via the Sukhoy Log gully is slippery
aktru-kanyon.crowd_note: No queues: the only people in the valley are mountaineering camp guests and hikers
aktru-kanyon.region: Altai Republic, North Chuya Range, Aktru valley, slope of Kyzyltash peak
aktru-kanyon.approach: About 25 minutes from the Aktru mountaineering camp: past the climbers' memorial, through the Siberian pine forest and up a grassy slope to the rocks, on a red-marked path
aktru-kanyon.descent: On foot via the Sukhoy Log gully to the camp, 20–25 minutes (scree and steep grass), or up the path to Lake Tronova, 40–50 minutes; you can also descend via the easy “Forest” via ferrata across a suspension bridge
aktru-kanyon.vf_highlights: Siberia's highest via ferrata: a canyon above the glacial Aktru valley with views of the North Chuya Range glaciers; nearby are three more easy routes — “Forest”, “Dome” and “Children's”
aktru-kanyon.grade_local: Moderate (the guide author's own rating; no formal scale)
pros: High mountains at 2,300–2,600 m with glaciers nearby
Free, no queues
Can be combined with Lake Tronova and the easy routes nearby
cons: A long journey: the Chuya Highway and a dirt road by 4x4
Short season — effectively July–August
Gear rental and guide prices are not published
aktru-kanyon.airport: RGK — Gorno-Altaysk, then along the Chuya Highway to Kurai and by dirt road to Aktru in a 4x4 (a full day's travel)
aktru-kanyon.fee_note: Free (according to the “Aktru Via Ferratas” guide)

mishoko-adygea.description: A small via ferrata in a canyon near Khadzhokh: a southern family route with bridges and a shorter, steep one with an overhanging ladder. Led by park instructors, with European-brand gear provided on site. Good for a first try and for children with an instructor; ziplines, canyoning and jeep tours nearby.
mishoko-adygea.rating_basis: A detailed review by a family with children (2020); a simple park route in the popular Khadzhokh tourist area
mishoko-adygea.hazards: The overhanging ladder on the steep variant throws off the unprepared; children and light people need a top rope or an adult alongside; hot in summer
mishoko-adygea.crowd_note: Done with park instructors in small groups
mishoko-adygea.region: Republic of Adygea, Kamennomostsky village (Khadzhokh), a canyon on the Belaya river
mishoko-adygea.approach: The start is from the park's platform on the north side of the canyon, a few minutes on foot
mishoko-adygea.descent: From the top of the route back across the canyon by zipline
mishoko-adygea.vf_highlights: Bridges over the canyon, a zipline across its widest point and a return to the start on a second zipline
mishoko-adygea.grade_local: No formal grade: a family route and a short steep one with an overhanging ladder
pros: Suitable for children and beginners
Zipline across the canyon included
The Khadzhokh gorge, Lago-Naki and other attractions nearby
cons: Short routes, modest height
Length, prices and opening hours are not published — check with the park
The northern route is sometimes closed
mishoko-adygea.fee_note: Paid: routes are sold as packages at the park, prices not published

rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.description: A short 300 m route with 100 m of height gain on the north-east slope of the Aibga ridge, by the top station of the “Kavkazsky Express” lift. Guests are clipped to the cable with a lanyard that can't be unclipped and are led by an instructor; helmet and gloves provided. Suits anyone who wants to try via ferrata for the first time, from age 14.
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.rating_basis: A resort attraction: a short route, but easy lift access and a Caucasus panorama; launched in July 2024
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.hazards: Fog, wind and thunderstorms at 2,300 m; closed in bad weather together with the lift
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.crowd_note: Done in small groups with an instructor; there may be a wait at the height of summer
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.region: Krasnodar Krai, Sochi, Krasnaya Polyana — Rosa Khutor resort, Aibga ridge
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.approach: By the resort's cable cars to the “Kavkazsky Express” top station; the start is next to the station
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.descent: To the “Kavkazsky Express” top station and down by lift
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.vf_highlights: Russia's most accessible via ferrata: 20–40 minutes on the rocks of the Aibga ridge at 2,300 m with views of the Main Caucasus Range
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.grade_local: Grade not published; an easy route for beginners with an instructor
pros: Up by cable car, no long approach
Instructor and gear on site
Can be combined with walks around Rosa Peak
cons: A very short route
Ages 14 and up only
A lift ticket is required; the price of the route is not published
rosa-khutor-vereskovaya-tropa.airport: AER — Sochi (Adler), ~1 hour to Rosa Khutor

sochi-orlinye-skaly.description: About 1 km of rock route with cable, rungs, steps and ladders on the Eagle Rocks (Orlinye Skaly) above the Agura gorge, 250 m of it on rock. Guided only, gear provided. Suits fit beginners and families with children from 12; the route runs year-round, weather permitting.
sochi-orlinye-skaly.rating_basis: Reviews on Tripster: 5.0 (30 reviews for one guide, 5 for another); the guiding team describe themselves as the creators of the first via ferrata in Russia
sochi-orlinye-skaly.hazards: Slippery rock and mud after rain, heat and humidity in summer; you need proper shoes with tread (not canvas sneakers)
sochi-orlinye-skaly.crowd_note: Done in small guided groups; no queues on the cables
sochi-orlinye-skaly.region: Krasnodar Krai, Sochi, Khosta — Agura gorge, Sochi National Park
sochi-orlinye-skaly.approach: Meet at the entrance to the Agura gorge, then walk up the path along the Agura river to the rocks
sochi-orlinye-skaly.descent: From the Eagle Rocks viewpoint on foot through the relict forest, from 40 minutes to 2 hours
sochi-orlinye-skaly.vf_highlights: A rock route above the Agura gorge topping out at the Eagle Rocks viewpoint, with a view of the sea
pros: Within Sochi city limits, 30–40 minutes from the airport
Open year-round
Russian-speaking guides, all gear included
cons: Guided only, can't be done independently
Hard in places without basic fitness
Hot and humid in summer
sochi-orlinye-skaly.guide_price_note: 8,000–8,500 ₽ per person (≈€85) on a guided group excursion; helmet, harness and lanyard included
sochi-orlinye-skaly.fee_note: Entry to Sochi National Park is extra, according to tourists' reviews
school_notes: Up to 4 people, UIAA gear
Groups of up to 20 people, children from 12

triglav-tominskova-pot.description: The most popular protected route up Triglav from the north: rungs and cables up the wall above the Vrata valley, then a night at Kredarica and the cabled summit ridge. Technically easy (A/B), but the route is long, with about 1,900 m of ascent from the car park and some sections without cable. Suits fit hikers with mountain experience; in Slovenia's high mountains only IFMGA guides are allowed to work as guides.
triglav-tominskova-pot.rating_basis: Slovenia's national symbol; an average rating of 4.0 from 557 ascents on ferrataguide.com; the classic route up Triglav from the north
triglav-tominskova-pot.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms — be on the summit or in a hut by 14:00; snow and ice on the route until late June (crampons and an ice axe needed); polished rock; rockfall; sudden cold and wind on the ridge
triglav-tominskova-pot.crowd_note: In July–August there are queues on the summit ridge from Kredarica between 8 and 11 am, and the huts fill up — book ahead
triglav-tominskova-pot.region: Julian Alps, Triglav National Park, Vrata valley near Mojstrana
triglav-tominskova-pot.approach: From the car park by the Aljažev dom hut in the Vrata valley (990 m), past the giant carabiner memorial, along a dry riverbed and through the forest, 1.5 hours
triglav-tominskova-pot.descent: From the summit along the protected ridge to the Triglavski dom hut on Kredarica (2,515 m), then down the Tominšek Trail or the Čez Prag trail to the Vrata valley, 3.5–4 hours; usually with a night at Kredarica
triglav-tominskova-pot.vf_highlights: A climb to Slovenia's highest point (2,864 m) with views of Triglav's north face — one of the highest walls in the Eastern Alps
pros: Slovenia's highest summit
Views of Triglav's north face
A night at the high-mountain Kredarica hut
Technically easy
cons: A very long day, better done in 2 days
In places only pegs without cable, and scree
Huts open only from June to October
triglav-tominskova-pot.airport: LJU — Ljubljana, ~1 h; KLU — Klagenfurt, ~1 h; TRS — Trieste, ~2 h
triglav-tominskova-pot.fee_note: Free; hut stays are paid, cash only, book ahead
school_notes: Official list of Slovenia's IFMGA mountain guides

kemaliye-egin-gabani.description: A route on the Eğin Gabanı wall above the Euphrates, built in 2017 by the Kemaliye authorities and the local KEMAV foundation; the climb takes about 2 hours. It is usually done on guided club tours, together with the “Stone Road” along the Dark Canyon and a boat trip. For people who are fit and have no fear of heights.
kemaliye-egin-gabani.rating_basis: NTV news coverage of the Kemaliye festival and tours by Istanbul clubs; few reviews and no topo
kemaliye-egin-gabani.hazards: Heat and sun in summer, a high wall with big exposure, rockfall; check the condition of the route's hardware with local guides
kemaliye-egin-gabani.crowd_note: Only occasional groups; busy only during the Kemaliye festival
kemaliye-egin-gabani.region: Eastern Anatolia, Erzincan Province, Kemaliye — above the Dark Canyon (Karanlık) of the Euphrates
kemaliye-egin-gabani.approach: From the town of Kemaliye to the Eğin Gabanı rock wall
kemaliye-egin-gabani.vf_highlights: Turkey's first via ferrata, on a wall about 470 m high above the Dark Canyon of the Euphrates; originally a path to a wingsuit jumping point
kemaliye-egin-gabani.grade_local: Moderate (per the tour organisers' description); no formal grade
pros: The impressive Euphrates canyon and the Stone Road nearby
Hardly any tourists
Can be combined with the extreme sports festival
cons: Far away and hard to reach
No published topo, length or prices
Very hot in summer
kemaliye-egin-gabani.airport: ERC — Erzincan, ~160 km by mountain road
school_notes: 3-day tour: via ferrata, Stone Road, boat trip through the canyon; gear from the guides

nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.description: A route along two vertical quartzite ridges in a private preserve within the Monongahela National Forest: rungs, traverses and the famous suspension bridge between the rock “fins”. Done only with the operator's guides, which makes it convenient for beginners. Ages 13 and up, weight 40–120 kg.
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.rating_basis: The best-known via ferrata in the eastern US, articles by Atlas Obscura, Blue Ridge Outdoors and WV Living; 4.5/5 on ferrataguide.com
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.hazards: Summer afternoon thunderstorms, humid heat in July–August; slippery rock after rain; exposed sections above the drop
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.crowd_note: Only organised guided groups of up to 14 people — hardly any queues; book ahead, weekend slots sell out
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.region: West Virginia, Allegheny Mountains, Circleville (Monongahela National Forest)
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.approach: 15 minutes on foot from the NROCKS base (141 Nelson Gap Road, Circleville)
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.descent: A loop route: ~30 minutes down the trail back to the base
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: A ~60 m-long suspension bridge ~45 m up between two quartzite rock “fins”; the longest via ferrata on the US East Coast
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.grade_local: C/D (per ferrataguide.com); the operator calls the route “moderate”
pros: Guide and gear included — ideal for a first time
A spectacular suspension bridge
Beautiful autumn foliage in October
cons: Can't be done independently
Remote: 3–4 hours from Washington
Children only from age 13
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.airport: IAD — Washington Dulles, ~3.5 h; SHD — Staunton (Shenandoah), ~1.5 h
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: Only with an NROCKS guide: $80–125 per person, gear included; full-moon night climb ~$150 (only for those who have already done the route)
nelson-rocks-via-ferrata.fee_note: No separate fee — included in the guide price; independent climbing is not allowed
school_notes: The only operator: guide, gear, plus a zipline tour

ouray-via-ferrata.description: About 1.2 km of cables and rungs on the walls of the Uncompahgre Gorge right on the edge of Ouray. Downstream is the easy beginners' option with two bridges; Upstream is harder, with a suspended ladder and a “leap” across the whole gorge. Free, but only with certified gear — it can be rented in town.
ouray-via-ferrata.rating_basis: One of Colorado's two best-known via ferratas; free, with a ranger at the entrance; RopeWiki 3.9/5 (13 ratings), lots of guides
ouray-via-ferrata.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms in July–August; slippery wet rock by the river; closures in bad weather; there is only one emergency exit — before the Skyladder
ouray-via-ferrata.crowd_note: A steady stream of people in summer, with no more than two people per cable span — it takes longer at the height of the season; the route is open 8:00–16:00
ouray-via-ferrata.region: Colorado, San Juan Mountains, Ouray — the “Switzerland of America”
ouray-via-ferrata.approach: About 800 m from Camp Bird Road (on the edge of Ouray, by the Ouray Ice Park), crossing the river to the route gate; at the start a ranger checks your gear and gives a briefing
ouray-via-ferrata.descent: The route is one-way from south to north; you exit up one of two ~60 m technical walls straight to the road and car park, 5–10 minutes
ouray-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: The Sky Bridge (~23 m, at a 35° angle) and the suspended Skyladder right above the churning Uncompahgre River; the famous ice park is opposite
ouray-via-ferrata.grade_local: 4B on the Fletcher–Smith scale (per SJMG; Telluride is 2B on the same scale); Downstream — beginner to intermediate, Upstream — intermediate to difficult
pros: Free, 10 minutes from town
Two routes of different difficulty
The river and bridges — very photogenic
cons: Short — 2–4 hours
Open only May–October and only 8:00–16:00
Restrictions: reach with arm extended at least 157 cm, weight 41–120 kg without extra belay
ouray-via-ferrata.airport: MTJ — Montrose, ~45 min; DEN — Denver, ~5.5 h
ouray-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: San Juan Mountain Guides: $179 (group of 5) – $299 (two people) per person, $449 private; Petzl gear included. Also Mountain Trip, Basecamp Ouray, Cirque Guides, Moxie Mountain Guides
ouray-via-ferrata.fee_note: Free; mandatory check-in with the ranger at the entrance and inspection of certified gear (EN 958)
school_notes: AMGA guides, starts at 7:30/8:30/10:00, gear included
Guides for Ouray and Telluride

tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.description: A commercial via ferrata on the granite Tram Face of the Palisades Tahoe ski resort (formerly Squaw Valley). Three options: a 2-hour loop a third of the way up the wall, a 3-hour route to a viewpoint, and the 4-hour Sundial Arête and Skyline Traverse to the very top. No experience needed — you just have to be comfortable climbing a ladder and walking a trail for an hour.
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.rating_basis: According to the operator, one of Tahoe's most popular summer activities; a short commercial route for beginners
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.hazards: Strong sun and heat on the south-facing wall in July–August; occasional summer thunderstorms; snow on the wall in May and early June; wildfire smoke in late summer
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.crowd_note: Only scheduled guided groups — no queues, but summer weekends sell out in advance
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.region: California, Sierra Nevada, Olympic Valley near Lake Tahoe
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.approach: Meet in Olympic Valley village, then ride up to the start of the route in the guides' all-terrain vehicle, “The Beast”
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.descent: From the top of the wall at the Tram Tower 1 cable car pylon — a short trail and a ride down in the all-terrain vehicle; the short options are loops
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.vf_highlights: A ~240 m granite wall right above the resort, the “Monkey in the Middle” cable bridges and the 15-metre “Super Monkey Bridge”, views of the valley and the tram
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.grade_local: No official grade; the operator pitches it from beginner (2-hour) to intermediate (4-hour Skyline Traverse)
pros: Suitable for complete beginners and families
Guide, gear and the all-terrain shuttle up included
Lake Tahoe nearby — easy to combine with a holiday
cons: Expensive for a short route
Can't be done independently
Height from 120 cm; weight 40–120 kg in a mixed group
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.airport: RNO — Reno, ~1 h; SMF — Sacramento, ~2 h; SFO — San Francisco, ~3.5 h
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.guide_price_note: Only with an Alpenglow Expeditions guide: 2 h — $199–209, 3 h — $230–251, 4 h — $269–299 per person (weekdays/weekends), gear and transfer included
tahoe-via-ferrata-palisades.fee_note: No separate fee — only as part of a tour
school_notes: The only operator: 2/3/4-hour tours, gear included

telluride-via-ferrata.description: About 3 km of traverse along the south wall of the Telluride box canyon, built by local climbers in 2007. Around 30% of the route is cabled; the rest is a narrow path above the drop; the climax is the Main Event section, with rungs on a sheer wall. Suits fit beginners with no fear of heights.
telluride-via-ferrata.rating_basis: The best-known via ferrata in the US: articles by National Geographic, Out There Colorado and Bearfoot Theory; several AMGA guiding schools
telluride-via-ferrata.hazards: Afternoon thunderstorms from early July to mid-August — start early; avalanche danger in spring while there is snow above the route; drops of up to 150 m; altitude ~3,000 m — altitude sickness for those arriving from the lowlands
telluride-via-ferrata.crowd_note: At weekends in summer and September there are jams at the Main Event — the route can stretch to 4–6 hours; set off early
telluride-via-ferrata.region: Colorado, San Juan Mountains, Telluride canyon
telluride-via-ferrata.approach: From the car park by Bridal Veil Falls (the east end of the canyon) about 1.6 km up the road and trail, ~260 m of ascent; the start is at a switchback bend beyond the falls, unsignposted
telluride-via-ferrata.descent: The route is one-way from east to west; it exits onto the trail into the Marshall Creek valley and back down to the Bridal Veil road, ~40 minutes
telluride-via-ferrata.vf_highlights: A traverse along the sheer canyon wall up to 150–180 m above the forest with views of Telluride and Bridal Veil Falls; the Main Event section is rung after rung up bare rock
telluride-via-ferrata.grade_local: C/D (per climbing.place); local guides call the route moderate
pros: Views of Telluride and the 110-metre Bridal Veil Falls
Free, no booking needed
Can be done with a guide from town in half a day
cons: No escape routes — once on, you can't get off until the end
Altitude around 3,000 m: acclimatisation needed
Jams in high season
telluride-via-ferrata.airport: TEX — Telluride, ~15 min; MTJ — Montrose, ~1.5 h; DEN — Denver, ~6 h
telluride-via-ferrata.guide_price_note: San Juan Mountain Guides: from $179 (group of 5) to $449 (private) per person; Mountain Trip: $249 in a mixed group 16+; gear and transfer from town included
telluride-via-ferrata.fee_note: Free; voluntary donations to the route maintenance fund
school_notes: AMGA guides, private and groups of up to 5, gear included
Mixed groups 16+ and private trips, start at 8:00

bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.description: A chain of barrier cays along Great Abaco forms the Sea of Abaco — a shallow, sheltered lagoon with short hops, the Hope Town lighthouse and New England-style villages. Good for a relaxed first charter, but you need to watch depths and tides; Marsh Harbour was badly hit by Hurricane Dorian in 2019.
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.rating_basis: The Sea of Abaco behind its barrier of cays is a sheltered shallow cruising ground with 1–2-hour hops (12knots: “moderate” level, wind 5–20 kn); sailors love the calm water and colonial villages; downsides — shallows, winter fronts and the aftermath of Hurricane Dorian (2019).
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.hazards: Shallows, banks and coral heads; the “rage” — dangerous swell in the Whale Cay Passage when a northerly sea is running (go only in calm weather); cold fronts with 20–30 kn north-westerlies in winter; tidal currents in the cuts; hurricanes (Dorian, Category 5, destroyed Marsh Harbour in September 2019).
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.crowd_note: Uncrowded; in Hope Town the buoys may be taken in season and during the July regattas.
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.region: Bahamas, Abaco: the Sea of Abaco — Elbow Cay (Hope Town), Man-O-War, Great Guana, Green Turtle, Little Harbour
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.wind_desc: November–April — easterly trades of 10–15 kn, but every 1–2 weeks cold fronts swing the wind round to the north-west–north at 20–30 kn, and winter is cool (water ~22–23 °C); May–August the wind is lighter, 8–12 kn, with heat and thunderstorms; September–October is the peak of hurricane season.
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.route: Marsh Harbour — Hope Town (Elbow Cay) — Tilloo Cay / Little Harbour — Man-O-War Cay — Great Guana Cay — Green Turtle Cay (via the Whale Cay Passage, calm weather only) — Marsh Harbour, ~70–90 miles in a week (12knots' 10-day route is 116 miles)
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.mooring: Marinas in Marsh Harbour (Conch Inn, Boat Harbour); in the island harbours — rental mooring buoys and small marinas, plus plenty of free anchorages on sand; harbour entrances are shallow, so time your entry with the tide.
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.licence: The Bahamas has no official licence for pleasure yachts: charter companies look at your sailing CV, and some ask for a certificate under their own rules — check in advance. Charter companies do not allow night passages.
pros: Sheltered water behind the barrier cays, short hops
Easy line-of-sight navigation
Colourful villages: Hope Town, Man-O-War, Green Turtle
Direct flights from Florida
cons: Shallows of 2–4 m and shallow harbour entrances — tides must be taken into account
Winter cold fronts, water 22–23 °C
Connecting flights from Europe
Hurricane season June–November, Dorian's aftermath
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.airport: MHH — Marsh Harbour, ~10 min; flights from Florida and Nassau
bahamas-abacos-marsh-harbour.charter_price_note: There are almost no 40–45 ft monohulls for charter in the Abacos (the fleet is mostly catamarans). Benchmark — a Dufour 37 (2023, 35 ft, 3 cabins) from Marsh Harbour per week: Christmas and late February–April ~$5,770 (≈€4,900) / January–mid-February ~$5,100 (≈€4,300), summer and autumn ~$5,300–5,600. Plus a mandatory 4% charter tax and 10% Bahamas tax, cleaning $400; skipper $220 a day plus food and a separate cabin
highlights: Regatta Time in Abaco — a week of inter-island regattas
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~70 boats in Marsh Harbour (Conch Inn, Boat Harbour), a 10-day Abaco route

bahamas-exumas-nassau.description: A chain of hundreds of cays south-east of Nassau with turquoise banks 2–5 m deep, sandbars and the Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park, where fishing is banned. Eyeball navigation by water colour, tidal currents in the cuts and an open-water passage from Nassau make it an area for experienced crews.
bahamas-exumas-nassau.rating_basis: The Exumas are one of the most spectacular sailing areas for water colour alone: shallow banks, sandbars, the Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park, swimming pigs; 12knots names Nassau as the main base for Exuma trips (about 70 boats); downsides — the open-water passage, shallows and winter fronts.
bahamas-exumas-nassau.hazards: Shallow banks and coral heads (Yellow Bank) — navigate by day only, with the sun high; strong tidal currents and steep seas in the cuts when wind is against tide; winter cold fronts of 20–30 kn; hurricanes June–November; no fishing or collecting in the Exuma park.
bahamas-exumas-nassau.crowd_note: Most anchorages are empty; it gets busy at Big Major's Spot and Staniel Cay (tour boats), and the Warderick Wells buoys are taken by midday in season.
bahamas-exumas-nassau.region: Bahamas: New Providence and the Exuma Cays — Allan's Cay, Normans Cay, Shroud Cay, Warderick Wells (Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park), Staniel Cay
bahamas-exumas-nassau.wind_desc: November–April — steady easterly trades of 10–15 kn, warm and dry, but in winter cold fronts regularly pass through, swinging the wind to the north-west–north at up to 20–30 kn; May–August the wind is lighter, 8–12 kn, with heat and thunderstorms; September–October is the peak of hurricane season.
bahamas-exumas-nassau.route: Nassau — Allan's Cay (~35 miles across the Yellow Bank) — Normans Cay / Shroud Cay — Warderick Wells (Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park) — Staniel Cay (Thunderball Grotto, swimming pigs at Big Major's Spot) — Compass Cay — Nassau, ~135 miles in a week
bahamas-exumas-nassau.mooring: In the Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park — first-come mooring buoys, $36.36 a night for 40–49 ft yachts + 10% VAT, plus $14 per person per day for charter yachts; anchoring in the park costs $0.45 per foot; outside the park mostly free anchorages on sand, with marinas at Staniel Cay and Compass Cay.
bahamas-exumas-nassau.licence: The Bahamas has no official licence for pleasure yachts: charter companies look at your sailing CV, and some ask for a certificate under their own rules — check in advance; 12knots rates the Nassau — Exumas route as “experienced” because of the open-water passage and shallows. Night passages are prohibited.
pros: Incredible water colour and empty sandbars
Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park — snorkelling, turtles, iguanas
Staniel Cay: Thunderball Grotto and the swimming pigs
Plenty of free anchorages
cons: Shallows and coral heads — navigate only in good sunlight
A 30–35-mile open-water passage from Nassau
Cold fronts in winter, water 24 °C
Expensive provisions, few shops
bahamas-exumas-nassau.airport: NAS — Nassau (Lynden Pindling), ~40 min to Palm Cay
bahamas-exumas-nassau.charter_price_note: Sun Odyssey 410 (2022, 41 ft, 3 cabins) from Palm Cay Marina (Nassau) per week: mid-March–April $7,000–8,900 (≈€6,800), February $6,500–7,500, New Year up to $7,200–9,000 / late August–mid-October $2,400–2,750 (≈€2,300, hurricane season), June–July ~$4,150–4,500. Plus a mandatory 4% charter tax, a $460 service package with cleaning and a $40 fee; skipper $380 a day plus food and a separate cabin
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~70 boats in Nassau (Palm Cay Marina), a 7-day Nassau — Exumas route

belize-placencia.description: Sailing inside the Belize Barrier Reef: hundreds of tiny palm-fringed cayes, mangroves, manatees and reef snorkelling a couple of miles from your anchorage. There is hardly any swell, but reef navigation with old charts and no marks, plus a mandatory local certificate, make it an area for experienced skippers or skippered crews.
belize-placencia.rating_basis: The world's second-longest barrier reef, hundreds of deserted cayes and almost no other yachts; Sunsail puts the area in its toughest category (Level 3) because of the reefs, old charts (surveyed in 1989) and missing navigation marks; 12knots rates the route as “experienced”.
belize-placencia.hazards: Coral reefs and heads; charts have not been updated since 1989 and many lights and marks are missing — sail by day only, in good light; north-westerly fronts in winter, summer squalls up to 60 kn, hurricanes (peaking in August–September); fines for reef damage; closed lobster season 14 February–15 June.
belize-placencia.crowd_note: Almost no other yachts even in high season; busy only at popular day-trip snorkelling spots (Laughing Bird Caye).
belize-placencia.region: Central America, Caribbean Sea: the southern Belize Barrier Reef — Laughing Bird Caye, Pelican Cays, South Water Caye, Tobacco Caye, Ranguana Caye
belize-placencia.wind_desc: Easterly trades of 10–20 kn for most of the year (11–15 kn on average); from October to April, most often in December–February, cold fronts bring 20–25 kn north-westerlies; in summer short but violent squalls (“bayamas”) of up to ~60 kn, heralded by a dark sky to the south; hurricanes are most likely in August–September.
belize-placencia.route: Placencia — Laughing Bird Caye (national park) — Pelican Cays — South Water Caye / Tobacco Caye — Ranguana Caye — Placencia, ~90 miles in a week inside the reef; Glover's Reef, Lighthouse Reef and Turneffe atolls lie outside the reef — only with a local skipper
belize-placencia.mooring: Marine reserves charge $10 per person per day (buoys extra): ~$20 a night at Pelican Cays, ~$15 at Ray Caye; some reserves require a guide (~$50–150); elsewhere you anchor on sand behind the reef off deserted cayes; departure tax $56 per person.
belize-placencia.licence: For bareboat you need a temporary certificate of competence issued by the Belize Port Authority (apply about 2 weeks ahead; the charter company usually handles it). Sunsail requires a recognised licence or a Level 3 sailing CV (at least 20 days or 400 miles as skipper). Sailing only inside the reef, no night sailing; reef damage is fined, up to confiscation of your passport.
pros: Barrier reef and deserted cayes, almost no other yachts
Water sheltered from ocean swell
World-class snorkelling and diving
Can be combined with jungle and Maya ruins
cons: Tricky reef navigation, old charts, no marks
A temporary certificate from the port authority is required
Reserve fees and departure tax
Long journey: flight to Belize City + a local flight or 3 hours by shuttle
belize-placencia.airport: BZE — Belize City, then a local flight to PLJ (Placencia, ~45 min) and 5 min by taxi; shuttle from Belize City 2.5–3 h
belize-placencia.charter_price_note: There are virtually no monohulls in Placencia — the fleet is catamarans. Benchmark — a Leopard 42 (2024, 42 ft, 3 cabins) per week: February–March $11,000–12,300 (≈€9,700), January and April ~$9,500–10,000, Christmas up to $14,500–15,500 / August–September ~$5,300–5,600 (≈€4,500, hurricane season), early October discounted to ~$3,600. Cleaning, linen and a full tank included; deposit ~$8,500 (insurance at $134 a day reduces it); skipper $207 a day plus food and a cabin
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator (website and support in Russian): ~20 boats in Placencia
Base at Laru Beya marina on the Placencia peninsula; reserve rules and certificate paperwork

cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.description: Cuba's south coast — the deserted coral cayos of the Canarreos Archipelago with white sand, and colonial Cienfuegos at the start. Exotic sailing for those ready for long passages, Cuban bureaucracy, landing restrictions and scarce supplies.
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.rating_basis: Cruisers on Noonsite praise the professional clearance, empty cayos and colonial Cienfuegos, but complain about shortages of food and spares, cash-only payments, landing restrictions and theft; the charter fleet is small and reviews are few.
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.hazards: Reefs, shallows and poorly marked passes in the Canarreos Archipelago — daylight navigation only; hurricanes June–November (peak August–October); winter cold fronts; theft (a dinghy outboard was stolen in Cienfuegos) — lock your dinghy; limited supplies — bring food and spares with you.
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.crowd_note: Almost no other yachts; only the Cienfuegos marina itself is busy with charter boats.
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.region: Caribbean Sea, southern Cuba: Cienfuegos Bay, the Canarreos Archipelago (Cayo Largo, Cayo Rosario, Cayo Cantiles); further east — Jardines de la Reina
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.wind_desc: East–north-easterly trades of 10–15 kn in the dry season (December–April); in winter cold fronts (“nortes”) pass through, swinging the wind to the north; summer is lighter, hot, with thunderstorms; August–October is the peak of hurricane season.
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.route: Cienfuegos — Cayo Largo (~70 miles, a day passage leaving at dawn) — the cayos of the Canarreos Archipelago (Cayo Rosario, Cayo Cantiles) — Cayo Largo — Cienfuegos, ~180–200 miles in a week; Jardines de la Reina lies 80–150 miles to the east and, according to cruisers (2019), is closed to foreign yachts
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.mooring: The marina in Cienfuegos is small and taken up by charter companies (about $0.7 per foot per day); at the cayos — anchorages; on Cayo Largo there is a state-run marina at the resort (no drinking water, bottled only; US cards not accepted).
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.licence: Skipper requirements are set by the charter company — check in advance. A foreign yacht may only enter and leave through ports of entry (Cienfuegos and Cayo Largo among them); landing is not allowed everywhere and may need permission from the border guards; US citizens need an OFAC licence.
pros: Empty cayos and reefs with hardly any other yachts
Colonial Cienfuegos and Trinidad close to the base
Snorkelling and fishing (outside reserves)
Warm water all year round
cons: Long passages (~70 miles to Cayo Largo)
Bureaucracy, landing not allowed everywhere
Shortages of food and spares, cash needed, US cards don't work
Jardines de la Reina reportedly closed to foreign yachts
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.airport: HAV — Havana, ~3.5–4 h by car to Cienfuegos; VRA — Varadero, ~3 h
cuba-cienfuegos-cayo-largo.charter_price_note: There are almost no monohulls for charter in Cuba — the Cienfuegos fleet is catamarans. Benchmark — a Lagoon 421 (2010, 43 ft, 5 cabins) per week: mid-January–April ~€5,900, holidays ~€6,500 / late October–mid-December ~€4,100. Cleaning and linen included; mandatory cruising fee ~€12 per person per day (paid at the base in dollars), deposit €3,000; skipper ~€80 a day plus food

svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.description: Dozens of low green islands south of Funen, sheltered from the open sea: 5–15-mile hops, well-kept harbours and medieval towns such as Ærøskøbing. Suits a first bareboat week and family holidays, as long as you stick carefully to the fairways.
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.rating_basis: One of Denmark's most popular sailing holiday areas (the “Danish South Seas”): sheltered water, short passages, old harbour towns; downsides — shallows outside the fairways, packed harbours in July, cool water.
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.hazards: Shallows and banks outside the fairways (especially around Strynø and Birkholm), the narrow Svendborgsund and Thurø Sund with current and ferries to Ærø, wind-driven changes in water level.
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.crowd_note: In July, during the Danish and German school holidays, the harbours of Ærøskøbing, Marstal and the small islands fill up by evening — best to arrive before lunch; June and late August are quieter.
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.region: Baltic: the South Funen Archipelago (Det Sydfynske Øhav) — Ærø, Tåsinge, Thurø, Lyø, Strynø, Avernakø, Faaborg
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.wind_desc: In summer westerlies of 8–16 kn prevail; in hot weather a daytime breeze that dies in the evening; the sea is slight, and the low islands shelter you from swell. In spring and September fresh westerlies and rain are more common.
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.route: Svendborg — Ærøskøbing — Marstal — Strynø — Faaborg — Lyø — Drejø — Svendborg, ~80–100 miles in a week
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.mooring: About 55 islands and lots of small harbours (Ærøskøbing, Marstal, Faaborg, Lyø, Drejø): berthing in boxes between piles, bow or stern to the pier, with the nightly fee paid at a machine or via an app; there are anchorages, but many shallows.
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.licence: Denmark imposes no requirements on foreign-flagged yachts beyond those of the flag state; a Danish certificate is only compulsory for some Danish-flagged motorboats. Charter companies require a sailing licence (ICC or similar) and experience for bareboat — check with the charter company.
pros: Very short hops in sheltered water
Picturesque harbours and towns: Ærøskøbing, Marstal, Faaborg
No significant tides or big seas
Easy to reach by train from Copenhagen
cons: Shallows and narrow fairways — careful navigation needed
Crowded harbours in July
Short season and cool water
Little charter information in Russian
svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.airport: CPH — Copenhagen, ~2–2.5 h by train via Odense; BLL — Billund, ~1 h 45 min by car
