svendborg-south-funen-archipelago.charter_price_note: There are no large charter bases in Svendborg itself; the nearest on the aggregators is Juelsminde (eastern Jutland, 1–2 days' sail from the archipelago). A Hanse 418 or Bavaria Cruiser 41 (2022, ~40 ft, 3 cabins) from there costs ~€2,150 per week from October to December; summer prices are not published (on Yachtico the same Bavaria 41 starts at ~€4,100 including mandatory fees). Plus final cleaning ~€195, linen ~€45 per person; skipper ~€180 a day plus food. Scandinavia is expensive because of taxes
highlights: Sankt Hans — bonfires on the shore on the night of 23–24 June

ibiza-formentera.description: Short hops between Ibiza and Formentera: the turquoise lagoons of Ses Illetes, the Es Vedrà rock, quiet coves on the north coast and parties in town. Easy navigation for a first week; the key is choosing your anchorage according to wind and swell direction.
ibiza-formentera.rating_basis: Formentera's lagoons with Caribbean-coloured water and short hops make this a popular “beach” charter (~100 yachts on Ibiza according to 12knots); 12knots recommends June and September, and a skipper for beginners in peak weeks. Downsides — prices, crowds and motorboat noise in July–August.
ibiza-formentera.hazards: Easterly swell (levante) and northerly winds quickly make exposed anchorages uncomfortable; shallows and rocks in the Es Freus strait between Ibiza and Formentera; a ban on anchoring on Posidonia, with patrols; heavy motorboat and ferry traffic.
ibiza-formentera.crowd_note: In July–August hundreds of yachts and motorboats crowd Ses Illetes and Espalmador, and buoys and marina berths must be booked in advance; June and September are calmer.
ibiza-formentera.region: Balearic Islands (Pityuses): Ibiza, Formentera, Espalmador; bases — Ibiza town, San Antonio, Santa Eulalia
ibiza-formentera.wind_desc: Summer winds are light to moderate: a daytime sea breeze of 6–15 kn, often calm in the morning. The easterly levante sends swell onto the east coast, northerlies (tramontana, the tail end of the mistral) onto the north coast; pick your anchorage by the forecast. Storms in autumn and spring.
ibiza-formentera.route: Ibiza — Formentera (Ses Illetes, Espalmador) — La Savina — Cala d'Hort (view of Es Vedrà) — San Antonio — Portinatx — Santa Eulalia — Ibiza, ~80–100 miles in a week
ibiza-formentera.mooring: Ibiza town's marinas are among the most expensive in the Mediterranean, and on Formentera (La Savina) berths are scarce in summer, so book ahead. Off Ses Illetes and Espalmador there are seasonal eco-buoys bookable in advance; anchoring on Posidonia is banned throughout Spain (Formentera enforces it especially strictly). Ports IB is opening new buoy fields off Ibiza (Porroig, Cala d'Hort, Talamanca).
ibiza-formentera.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence appropriate to the yacht and area (ICC or a national licence from your country of citizenship/residence in the EEA or a recognised country; IYT and Russian licences — check with the charter company in advance) + VHF; in Europe Day Skipper / ICC and VHF are usually requested.
pros: Caribbean-coloured water off Formentera
Short hops, everything close together
Plenty of flights to Ibiza airport
cons: Very expensive marinas
Crowds of motorboats and noise in July–August
Strict anchoring restrictions (Posidonia)
ibiza-formentera.charter_price_note: Estimate for 40–45 ft per week based on 12knots statistics for Spain (40–50 ft average: €7,000 in August, €4,000–4,400 in February–April); prices on Ibiza are higher than on Mallorca (from ~$1,900 per week for the smallest yachts); a catamaran costs roughly ×2
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: bases in San Antonio and Santa Eulalia
Charter agency: Balearic yachts with or without a skipper, routes to Ibiza and Formentera from Palma, Barcelona, Valencia or Alicante; advice in Russian
Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking yacht company and school: helps with charters and organises sailing trips around the Balearics — Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, Formentera

palma-mallorca-balearics.description: The Balearics' biggest charter hub: from Palma you can cruise the southern calas and Cabrera or sail right round the island, including the mountainous north coast. The south and east are calm — fine for a first week; a full circuit with the Tramuntana coast is for an experienced crew.
palma-mallorca-balearics.rating_basis: One of the Mediterranean's main charter hubs (~310 yachts on Mallorca according to 12knots): the Tramuntana mountains, turquoise calas, a convenient airport; the best months are June and September. Reviews complain about expensive marinas, crowded calas and new anchoring restrictions.
palma-mallorca-balearics.hazards: Northerly winds and swell along the Tramuntana coast (Sóller is open to the swell), easterly seas in the calas (Cala Figuera), a ban on anchoring on Posidonia enforced by patrol boats, jet skis and motorboats in the calas, an open-sea crossing to Menorca.
palma-mallorca-balearics.crowd_note: In July–August the calas of the east and south coasts are packed, and berths in the Palma and Andratx marinas are booked well ahead; the north is quieter, but has more wind and swell.
palma-mallorca-balearics.region: Balearic Islands: Mallorca (Bay of Palma, Andratx, Sóller, Pollença, the eastern calas), Cabrera; crossing to Menorca
palma-mallorca-balearics.wind_desc: In summer a daytime sea breeze (in the Bay of Palma the south-westerly “embat”) of 8–15 kn, calm in the morning. The north and west coasts are open to northerlies (tramontana) and swell — with a residual mistral it can blow 25+ kn there while the south is calm; easterlies push into the calas of the east coast. Storms in spring and autumn.
palma-mallorca-balearics.route: Palma — Port d'Andratx — Port de Sóller — Pollença — Cala Ratjada — Cala Figuera — Palma, ~169 miles in a week (round the island); calmer — Palma — Cabrera — the eastern calas and back
palma-mallorca-balearics.mooring: The Palma and Andratx marinas are expensive, Ports IB harbour berths (Sóller, Cala Ratjada) are cheaper; book summer berths in advance. Since March 2026 anchoring on Posidonia has been banned throughout Spain — drop anchor on sand only or use eco-buoys (Ports IB buoy fields); fines are €1,800–6,000; in Cabrera National Park — by permit only.
palma-mallorca-balearics.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence appropriate to the yacht and area (ICC or a national licence from your country of citizenship/residence in the EEA or a recognised country; IYT and Russian licences — check with the charter company in advance) + VHF; according to 12knots, in Europe Day Skipper / ICC and VHF are usually requested.
pros: Huge choice of yachts and direct flights to Palma
Turquoise calas and the Tramuntana mountains
You can sail to Menorca or Cabrera
cons: Expensive marinas, crowds in July–August
Strict Posidonia anchoring ban and fines
North coast exposed to wind and swell
palma-mallorca-balearics.charter_price_note: Estimate for 40–45 ft per week: from ~$3,150 in spring/autumn (Bavaria Cruiser 46, from $451 a day); the 12knots average for 40–50 ft in Spain is €7,000 in August and €4,000–4,400 in February–April; a catamaran costs roughly ×2
highlights: The Copa del Rey MAPFRE regatta in Palma
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: round-the-island route and yachts in Palma
Bases in Palma, Ibiza, Santa Eulalia, the Canaries
Moscow-based charter agency: Balearic yachts with or without a skipper (starting from Palma or Mahón), routes round Mallorca and to Ibiza and Formentera, transfers; advice in Russian
Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking yacht company and school: helps with charters and organises sailing trips around the Balearics — Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, Formentera

san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.description: Atlantic trades, volcanic islands and whales 15–30 miles off southern Tenerife. These are not Mediterranean lagoons: passages are open, the wind is fresh and there is always swell — a good choice for winter sailing and honing ocean skills; beginners are better off with a skipper.
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.rating_basis: Europe's only warm year-round charter area: +22 °C in winter, volcanic islands and whales; but 12knots rates the route as “intermediate–advanced” because of the trades, acceleration zones and ocean swell, and marinas and sheltered coves are few.
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.hazards: Wind acceleration zones off the headlands and between the islands, ocean swell and surf at marina entrances (Los Gigantes), sudden wind shifts when leaving an island's wind shadow, ferries and fast craft between Los Cristianos and La Gomera, whales and dolphins in your path.
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.crowd_note: Marinas are small: Los Gigantes and Las Galletas are cramped, while San Sebastián de La Gomera and La Palma usually have space; anchorages are empty.
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.region: Canary Islands, Atlantic: southern Tenerife, Los Gigantes, La Gomera, La Palma, El Hierro
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.wind_desc: North-easterly trades of 12–20 kn all year; between the high islands there are acceleration zones (off Tenerife's south-west tip, in the channel to La Gomera) with gusts of 25–35 kn, especially in summer when the trades are stronger. Calm in the islands' wind shadow. In winter the trades are lighter, and Atlantic lows occasionally bring south-westerlies; ocean swell in any month.
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.route: San Miguel — Los Gigantes — Santa Cruz de La Palma (a day ashore) — Valle Gran Rey (La Gomera) — San Sebastián de La Gomera — San Miguel, ~167 miles in a week; shorter — Tenerife — La Gomera and back (16–30-mile passages)
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.mooring: Marinas are few: San Miguel (sheltered, but far from shops), Los Gigantes (narrow shallow entrance, swell, crowded with tour boats), Las Galletas (few berths), San Sebastián de La Gomera and two marinas in Santa Cruz de La Palma. There are few well-sheltered anchorages; in Valle Gran Rey you moor at the quay or anchor in the bay.
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence appropriate to the yacht and area (ICC or a national licence from your country of citizenship/residence in the EEA or a recognised country; IYT and Russian licences — check with the charter company); the charter company may ask for VHF and proven ocean experience — 12knots advises beginners to take a skipper.
pros: Year-round sailing, warm in winter
Steady wind and ocean practice
Pilot whales and dolphins, volcanoes and Teide
cons: Trade-wind acceleration zones of up to 30–35 kn and ocean swell
Few marinas and sheltered coves
Long passages to La Palma and El Hierro
san-miguel-tenerife-la-gomera.charter_price_note: Sun Odyssey 410 (2022, 41 ft, 3 cabins) from Las Galletas (Marina del Sur, next to San Miguel) per week: €2,675–2,800 all year round; a Sun Odyssey 419 (2017) from Santa Cruz — €2,700 from April to October and €2,500 from November to March. Little seasonality, slightly more expensive at Christmas and in February. Plus final cleaning €100–190, marina fee €5–10 per person, gas; skipper ~€1,650 a week plus food
highlights: Pilot whales and dolphins in the channel between Tenerife and La Gomera
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: route and yachts at San Miguel marina
A week by the cabin from Tenerife from $824 per person
Russian-speaking club and ISSA school (Gdańsk): one-week skippered catamaran trips from San Miguel marina — Los Gigantes, La Gomera, La Palma; in winter the ISSA Inshore Skipper course on Tenerife
Charter agency: yachts on Tenerife (Radazul and Santa Cruz bases), Gran Canaria and Lanzarote with or without a skipper, advice in Russian

ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.description: Corsica's west and south coasts: granite cliffs, deep gulfs and medieval Bonifacio perched above its fjord. 20–30-mile passages along an exposed coast and the mistral in the strait make this an area for an experienced or skippered crew.
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.rating_basis: Wild red cliffs, turquoise coves and clifftop Bonifacio — one of the Mediterranean's most beautiful areas in charter aggregator reviews and routes (12knots, Navily); reviews complain about expensive, overcrowded marinas in Bonifacio and Porto Pollo, and strong winds.
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.hazards: Mistral and libeccio with big seas, wind acceleration in the Strait of Bonifacio (a marine reserve with passage rules), rocks and shoals off the Lavezzi Islands and Roccapina, ferries in Ajaccio and Bonifacio.
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.crowd_note: In July–August Bonifacio and the Lavezzi Islands are packed — book marina berths and arrive early; the gulfs of Ajaccio and Valinco are quieter.
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.region: Corsica: Gulf of Ajaccio, Gulf of Valinco (Propriano), Roccapina, Bonifacio, the Lavezzi Islands; nearby — La Maddalena (Sardinia)
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.wind_desc: In summer daytime breezes of 10–15 kn on the west coast; the mistral (W–NW) and libeccio (SW) blow for several days at 25–35 kn with big seas, the wind accelerates to 40 kn in the Strait of Bonifacio, and an easterly makes Bonifacio uncomfortable. October–April — frequent storms.
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.route: Ajaccio — Gulf of Valinco (Porto Pollo / Propriano) — Bonifacio — Lavezzi Islands — Roccapina bay — Propriano — Ajaccio, ~127 miles in a week; in good weather, a detour to La Maddalena
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.mooring: Bonifacio charges €60–120 a night for 40–45 ft, berths are scarce in summer and service is slow; it's cheaper to anchor at Anse de la Catena and take the dinghy in. Ajaccio has two marinas (Charles Ornano near the centre, Tino Rossi — noisy from the ferries). In the Lavezzi and Strait of Bonifacio reserve there are mooring rules and paid buoys; buoys in Porto Pollo are expensive.
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.licence: Under French rules no licence is needed for a sailing yacht, but the charter company requires proven experience (a sailing CV) and usually an ICC or national licence; VHF as required by the charter company.
pros: Wild nature and empty coves
Bonifacio and the Lavezzi Islands
Ajaccio airport 10 minutes from the marina
cons: Exposed coast, fewer shelters than Sardinia
Mistral and libeccio up to 30–40 kn
Expensive, overcrowded marinas in the south
ajaccio-south-corsica-bonifacio.charter_price_note: Estimate for 40–45 ft per week based on 12knots statistics for France (40–50 ft average: ~€4,900 in July, ~€2,700–2,800 in April and October); a catamaran costs roughly ×2
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: route and yachts in Ajaccio, Propriano, Porto-Vecchio
Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking yacht company and school: organises sailing trips round Corsica with its own skippers, helps with charters and berths in Ajaccio and Bonifacio
A cabin on a Lagoon 620 catamaran with captain and cook: a week Ajaccio — Gulf of Valinco — Bonifacio — Lavezzi Islands — Propriano; booking in Russian

antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.description: A week along the Côte d'Azur: the Lérins Islands off Cannes, the red rocks of the Esterel, Saint-Tropez and, if time allows, Port-Cros National Park. Winds are mostly light and hops short — fine for a first bareboat week, but marinas are expensive and cramped.
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.rating_basis: Glamorous harbours, Cannes and Saint-Tropez from the water, convenient Nice airport and short hops; but Navily and 12knots reviews mention high prices, crowded anchorages, noise and motorboats in summer, and light winds.
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.hazards: The mistral off Saint-Tropez and the Hyères Islands, the easterly levante with its seas, heavy motorboat and superyacht traffic, a ban on anchoring on Posidonia and restrictions in Port-Cros National Park.
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.crowd_note: In July–August hundreds of boats crowd the Lérins Islands and the bays of Saint-Tropez, with wash from motorboats, and marinas won't take you without a booking; June and September are much calmer.
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.region: Côte d'Azur: Antibes, Cannes and the Lérins Islands, the Esterel, Saint-Tropez; further on — Port-Cros and Porquerolles (Hyères Islands)
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.wind_desc: In summer mostly light daytime breezes of 5–15 kn, often calm in the morning. The north-westerly mistral is stronger off Saint-Tropez and the Hyères Islands, weaker off Antibes and Cannes; the easterly levante brings seas and rain. In winter and early spring — cold mistrals.
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.route: Antibes — Lérins Islands (Sainte-Marguerite and Saint-Honorat) — Cannes — Esterel (Agay) — Saint-Tropez — Port-Cros and Porquerolles — Saint-Tropez — Antibes, ~130–150 miles in a week; calmer — Antibes — Lérins — Esterel — Saint-Tropez and back
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.mooring: Very expensive marinas: in Saint-Tropez and on Porquerolles berths are scarce and pricey in summer, and Porquerolles takes no bookings. Antibes (Port Vauban, 1,700 berths) and Golfe-Juan are big ports with charter fleets. The main free anchorage is between the Lérins Islands, very crowded in summer; don't drop anchor on Posidonia.
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.licence: Under French rules no licence is needed for a sailing yacht, but the charter company requires proven experience (a sailing CV) and usually an ICC or national licence; VHF as required by the charter company.
pros: Nice airport 20 minutes from Antibes
Short hops and light winds in summer
Cannes, Saint-Tropez and Port-Cros National Park in one week
cons: Very expensive, overcrowded marinas
Little wind and lots of motor yachts in summer
Wash and noise from motorboats at anchor
antibes-lerins-saint-tropez.charter_price_note: Estimate for 40–45 ft per week based on 12knots statistics for France (40–50 ft average: ~€4,900 in July, ~€2,700–2,800 in April and October); a catamaran costs roughly ×2
highlights: Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez regatta for classic and modern yachts
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: bases in Antibes, Golfe-Juan, Cannes, Saint-Tropez, Hyères
Route around the Hyères Islands and Saint-Tropez

Russian-speaking yacht company with a French phone number: crewed trips from Baie des Anges marina (Villeneuve-Loubet) — a day at the Lérins Islands, Monaco and Villefranche, sunset sails, 2 days to Saint-Tropez
Charter agency: yachts and catamarans on the Côte d'Azur (Antibes, Cannes, Nice, Monaco, Toulon) with or without a skipper, routes tailored to the crew; advice in Russian

hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.description: The strait between England's south coast and the Isle of Wight is the home of British sailing, with dozens of marinas, legendary regattas and cosy pubs in Cowes, Yarmouth and Lymington. Hops are short and sheltered from ocean swell, but strong tidal streams and shipping demand good preparation; an ideal place for RYA courses.
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.rating_basis: The heart of British sailing: home to the RYA headquarters, the Hamble and Cowes clubs, Cowes Week and the Round the Island Race; a great place for RYA training and practising in tides. Downsides — tricky tidal streams, heavy shipping, cool and changeable weather, expensive marinas.
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.hazards: Strong tidal streams (especially in the Hurst Narrows at the western entrance), double high water, the Bramble Bank in the middle of the Solent dries at low water springs, steep seas with wind against tide, heavy big-ship traffic in the channels to Southampton and Portsmouth, Isle of Wight ferries.
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.crowd_note: On summer weekends and regatta days (Cowes Week in August, the Round the Island Race in June) the Cowes and Yarmouth marinas are packed, so book ahead; weekdays and the off-season are quieter.
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.region: Southern England, English Channel: the Solent — Cowes, Yarmouth, Lymington, Beaulieu River, Portsmouth, Chichester
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.wind_desc: South-westerlies of 10–20 kn prevail, with a sea breeze on top in clear summer weather; wind against tide kicks up a short, steep sea. In autumn and winter frequent gales from the west and south-west.
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.route: Hamble — Cowes — Yarmouth — Lymington — Beaulieu River (Buckler's Hard) — Newtown Creek — Portsmouth — Chichester Harbour — Hamble, ~100 miles in a week
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.mooring: Lots of marinas on both shores (Hamble, Cowes, Yarmouth, Lymington, Portsmouth) — convenient but expensive; there are buoys and anchorages in bays and estuaries (Newtown Creek, Beaulieu River). The Hamble River has more than three marinas; Yarmouth and Cowes are crowded in summer.
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.licence: UK law does not require a licence for pleasure yachts. For bareboat, charter companies usually require RYA Day Skipper (practical) or equivalent and a VHF SRC held by one crew member — check with the charter company.
pros: Short hops, a harbour at every turn
The best place for RYA courses and tidal practice
Famous regattas and a real sailing atmosphere
Chartering almost all year round, close to London
cons: Strong tidal streams and double high water — careful planning needed
Very heavy shipping: container ships, ferries, naval vessels
Cool and changeable, frequent rain
Expensive marinas
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.airport: SOU — Southampton, ~15 min; LHR — London Heathrow, ~1 h 15 min
hamble-solent-isle-of-wight.charter_price_note: Hanse 458 (2018, 46 ft, 3 cabins) from Port Hamble per week: high season ~£3,045 (≈€3,500) / low season ~£2,285 (≈€2,600); the broker doesn't specify the months, usually the peak is July–August and the charter season April–October. Older boats are cheaper: a Dufour 40 from Southampton costs ~£1,650. Cleaning and fuel usually extra; skipper ~€260 a day plus food and a cabin
highlights: Round the Island Race — a race round the Isle of Wight with more than a thousand yachts
Cowes Week — one of the world's oldest and biggest regattas
Southampton International Boat Show
school_notes: the largest bareboat fleet in the Solent (25+ yachts) at Port Hamble Marina, skippered days, RYA practical courses with partner Sailing Logic

oban-west-coast-scotland.description: Mountains plunging into the sea, empty lochs, castles, distilleries and seals — one of Europe's most beautiful cruising grounds. The weather and tides are serious, so this is an area for experienced or skippered crews; beginners are better off on a crewed cruise.
oban-west-coast-scotland.rating_basis: British sailing magazines and cruisers rank Scotland's west coast among Europe's best cruising grounds: mountains, empty anchorages, whisky and wildlife; downsides — wet, changeable weather, cold water, strong tidal streams and midges when there's no wind.
oban-west-coast-scotland.hazards: Strong tidal streams in the sounds: the Corryvreckan between Jura and Scarba (up to 8.5 kn, whirlpool, standing waves — pass only in calm weather at slack water), the Sound of Luing, Dorus Mòr; the Falls of Lora rapids at the entrance to Loch Etive near the base; rocks and reefs, Atlantic swell off the outer islands, squalls off the mountains.
oban-west-coast-scotland.crowd_note: It only gets crowded in Tobermory and Oban in July–August and during regattas; most anchorages have one or two yachts.
oban-west-coast-scotland.region: Inner Hebrides: Firth of Lorn, Sound of Mull, Mull, Tobermory, Iona, Staffa, Coll, Loch Sunart
oban-west-coast-scotland.wind_desc: South-westerlies of 10–20 kn prevail with frequent changes in the weather — Atlantic fronts come through even in summer; under a high there are calm days. The mountains bring gusts and squalls in the lochs. May–June are usually drier and sunnier; gales from autumn onwards.
oban-west-coast-scotland.route: Dunstaffnage — Tobermory (Mull) — Loch Drumbuie — Coll — Staffa and Ulva — Iona — Puilladobhrain — Dunstaffnage, ~130 miles in a week
oban-west-coast-scotland.mooring: Marinas at Dunstaffnage (250 berths), Oban and Tobermory, visitor moorings off many villages and pubs, countless empty anchorages in the lochs and between the islands — nights at anchor are the norm here.
oban-west-coast-scotland.licence: UK law does not require a licence for pleasure yachts. For bareboat, charter companies usually require RYA Day Skipper (practical) or equivalent and a VHF SRC held by one crew member — check with the charter company.
pros: The wild beauty of the Hebrides, empty anchorages
Short hops between sheltered lochs
Whales, sharks, puffins, seals
Pubs, distilleries and cosy Tobermory
cons: Frequent rain and rapid weather changes, gales even in summer
Cold water (12–14 °C in summer)
Strong tidal streams require planning
Midges in calm weather in July–August
oban-west-coast-scotland.airport: GLA — Glasgow, ~2.5 h by car or ~3 h by train to Oban
oban-west-coast-scotland.charter_price_note: Sun Odyssey 409 (2012, 42 ft, 3 cabins) from Oban per week: May–1 September ~€4,390 / April and September ~€3,950, March and October ~€3,510; Sun Odyssey 439 (2015, 4 cabins) — €5,150 / 4,640 / 4,120. Prices converted from pounds; final cleaning and a dinghy with outboard included, deposit ~€3,000. Skipper ~€1,510 a week plus food and a cabin; the fleet doesn't operate from November to early March
highlights: Puffins on Staffa and the Treshnish Isles
Basking sharks, minke whales and dolphins off Mull and Coll
school_notes: charter companies based at the marina: bareboat (Alba Sailing) and crewed cruises around the Hebrides

grenada-port-louis.description: Spicy Grenada and its small islands — Carriacou and Petite Martinique — are the southern gateway to the Grenadines: you can reach the Tobago Cays and get back within a week. Few people and a longer season than in the northern Caribbean, but the first passage to Carriacou is 30+ miles against the trades and the sea, so this is an area for confident crews.
grenada-port-louis.rating_basis: Valued for the lack of crowds, Carriacou and the proximity of the Tobago Cays, and a lower hurricane risk (south of the main belt); Sunsail puts the area in its top difficulty level because of the long upwind passage north; about 75 charter boats (12knots).
grenada-port-louis.hazards: The active underwater volcano Kick 'em Jenny north of Grenada (keep clear of the exclusion zone, especially at higher alert levels), seas and current in the channels, coral heads at the Tobago Cays (don't approach from the south), no anchoring off Grand Anse beach, hurricanes (Beryl devastated Carriacou in July 2024), no night sailing.
grenada-port-louis.crowd_note: Even in high season Grenada and Carriacou are uncrowded; only the Tobago Cays and Salt Whistle Bay get busy.
grenada-port-louis.region: Caribbean, Windward Islands: Grenada, Carriacou, Petite Martinique; to the north — Union Island and the Tobago Cays (St Vincent and the Grenadines)
grenada-port-louis.wind_desc: Easterly trades: January–May are the driest months with the best wind (~14 kn on average in April–May, stronger and with more sea in winter); from June rain and squalls, August–November light winds of ~10 kn. Grenada lies south of the main hurricane belt, but not outside it (Ivan 2004, Beryl 2024).
grenada-port-louis.route: Port Louis — Grenada's west coast — Carriacou (Tyrrel Bay, Sandy Island, ~35 miles upwind) — Petite Martinique — Union Island — Tobago Cays — Hillsborough (customs) — Grenada's south coast (Prickly Bay, Hog Island) — Port Louis, ~100 miles in a week
grenada-port-louis.mooring: Buoys EC$60–80 (≈$20–30) a night, no national park fees on Grenada; on Carriacou there are buoys at Sandy Island, Tyrrel Bay and Anse La Roche; often cash only (bring EC$800–1,000); Grenada's cruising tax is already paid for charters starting on the island; when entering the St Vincent Grenadines — customs at Hillsborough and on Union Island.
grenada-port-louis.licence: No formal licence is required: Sunsail asks for a Level 3 sailing CV (at least 20 days or 400 miles as skipper on a similar yacht), otherwise a paid skipper is mandatory. Clearance via SailClear ($25 subscription). No night sailing, keep clear of windward shores, don't approach the Tobago Cays from the south.
pros: Uncrowded, authentic islands without mass tourism
The Tobago Cays and Union Island within a week's route
South of the main hurricane belt, longer season
Airport 15 minutes from the base
cons: A long passage north against wind and sea
Rated as difficult by the charter companies
Few services, cash needed
The underwater volcano Kick 'em Jenny on the way to Carriacou — a restricted zone
grenada-port-louis.airport: GND — Maurice Bishop (Grenada), ~15 min to Port Louis marina
grenada-port-louis.charter_price_note: Oceanis 43 (2009, 43 ft, 4 cabins) from St George's per week: late January–February and holidays ~€3,200–3,300, January and March ~€2,550–2,950 / mid-April–early July ~€2,250, July–December ~€2,600. Plus a mandatory €310 package (cleaning, linen, towels, gas), deposit €3,200; fuel, mooring and local fees extra; the base doesn't provide skippers — go through outside agencies
highlights: Pure Grenada Sailing Week (Carriacou and Grenada)
Carriacou Maroon and String Band Music Festival
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~75 boats in St George's and Port Louis, a 7-day / 103-mile route
Base at Port Louis marina (St George's)

guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.description: Guadeloupe is a two-island “butterfly” ringed by small archipelagos: Les Saintes with its fort and bays, flat sugar-growing Marie-Galante and, next door, tropical Dominica. 15–25-mile passages across open channels with Atlantic swell are for experienced crews, but there are far fewer people than in the BVI.
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.rating_basis: Les Saintes is regularly named one of the most beautiful anchorages in the Caribbean, plus wild Dominica and French cuisine; about 90 charter boats at Bas-du-Fort (12knots). Reviews complain about open passages with big seas, the wind shadow off Basse-Terre, and dinghy thefts at Malendure.
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.hazards: Hurricanes June–November (Maria devastated Dominica in 2017), strong wind and seas in the channels and off the ends of the islands, sudden gusts off the Basse-Terre mountains, reefs off Grande-Terre and Marie-Galante, lines and buoys in the passage off Gosier, no anchoring in the national park, dinghy theft.
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.crowd_note: Les Saintes and the buoys at Pigeon Island are full in December–April and during the French school holidays; Marie-Galante and Dominica are uncrowded.
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.region: Caribbean, Leeward Islands: Guadeloupe (Basse-Terre, Grande-Terre), Les Saintes, Marie-Galante, La Désirade; to the south — Dominica
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.wind_desc: East–north-easterly trades: December–April 15–20 kn, sometimes 25 kn in January–February with a big Atlantic swell in the channels (to Marie-Galante, Les Saintes and Dominica); May–October lighter, south-easterly, with squalls; under high Basse-Terre — a wind shadow with calms and gusts; June–November is hurricane season.
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.route: Bas-du-Fort — Marie-Galante (Saint-Louis) — Les Saintes (Terre-de-Haut) — Dominica (Portsmouth, Prince Rupert Bay) — Les Saintes — Basse-Terre's west coast (Malendure, Cousteau Reserve, Deshaies) — Bas-du-Fort round the southern tip of Basse-Terre, ~150–180 miles in a week
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.mooring: Bas-du-Fort marina is the island's largest (a booked berth may be cancelled at the last minute, Noonsite reports); at Les Saintes and Pigeon Island — buoys; anchoring is banned in many places in the national park and there aren't enough buoys for everyone; customs clearance is electronic and free at Saint-François marina.
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.licence: As elsewhere in the French Antilles, charter companies usually don't require an official licence for a sailing bareboat — they look at your sailing CV and give a briefing; check details with the charter company. Night passages are prohibited. To visit Dominica, or to leave Guadeloupe for Martinique or Saint-Martin, you need customs clearance (checking out of one French department and into another).
pros: Les Saintes — one of the Caribbean's most beautiful anchorages
Dominica with its rivers and waterfalls one passage away
Direct flights from Paris, French infrastructure and cuisine
The Cousteau Reserve for snorkelling
cons: Open channels with 2–3 m seas in winter
Wind shadow and squalls off Basse-Terre
The Rivière Salée bridges are closed to masted yachts — you have to sail round the island to get west
Dinghy thefts and damage at the Pigeon and Malendure anchorages
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.airport: PTP — Pointe-à-Pitre (Pôle Caraïbes), ~15–20 min to Bas-du-Fort marina
guadeloupe-bas-du-fort.charter_price_note: Filovent benchmark for a monohull per week: 3 cabins — ~£2,550 (≈€2,950) in December–April, ~£1,900 in May, June and November, ~£1,300 (≈€1,500) in July–October; 4 cabins — £3,400 / £2,500 / £1,700 (≈€3,950 / 2,900 / 2,000). Extra — a package with final cleaning and linen, tourist tax, mooring fees; skipper £170–215 a day, food paid by the crew
highlights: Finish of the Route du Rhum transatlantic race in Pointe-à-Pitre (every 4 years, including 2026)
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~90 boats at Bas-du-Fort, prices by month, a Guadeloupe — Dominica route

labuan-bajo-komodo.description: Traditional Indonesian phinisi schooners and catamarans with crew: 3–7 days among the islands of Komodo National Park with dragons, mantas and pink beaches. Suits any group with no sailing experience; a cabin on a phinisi costs from ~$115 per person per day, a private luxury schooner from ~$31,000 a week.
labuan-bajo-komodo.rating_basis: Komodo dragons, pink beaches, mantas and some of the world's best reefs; Komodo is a UNESCO site and the main cruising ground for Indonesian phinisi and superyachts from May to October. Downsides: it's a crewed cruise, not independent sailing, crowds of boats at Padar and Pink Beach, and uneven safety standards on cheap boats.
labuan-bajo-komodo.hazards: Currents in the Sape Strait and around Komodo are among the strongest in the world (dangerous for inexperienced boat handlers; snorkel only with a guide), fresh trades and choppy seas in the open straits in July–August, reefs, uneven safety equipment on cheap tour boats.
labuan-bajo-komodo.crowd_note: In July–August dozens of boats sit off Padar, Pink Beach and Manta Point; it's quieter at dawn and at the outlying islands.
labuan-bajo-komodo.region: Komodo National Park: Rinca, Padar, Komodo, Pink Beach, Manta Point; western Flores
labuan-bajo-komodo.wind_desc: Dry season April–October (driest July–September, 20–25 mm of rain): south-easterly trades of 10–20 kn, fresher in the open straits. From October–November the westerly monsoon arrives: downpours (up to 270–290 mm in January–February), variable winds, thunderstorms; many phinisi head to Raja Ampat for the season.
labuan-bajo-komodo.route: Labuan Bajo — Kelor — Rinca (dragons) — Padar (viewpoint) — Pink Beach — Komodo (Loh Liang) — Manta Point and Taka Makassar — Kanawa — Labuan Bajo, 3–7 days
labuan-bajo-komodo.mooring: There are no marinas for charter yachts: phinisi lie in the Labuan Bajo roadstead and at anchor or on buoys off the park's islands. Entry to Komodo National Park is paid; fees and visiting rules for individual islands have changed in recent years — check with your operator.
labuan-bajo-komodo.licence: There is practically no bareboat — the fleet consists of traditional phinisi schooners and crewed catamarans, and guests need no licence. Even an experienced crew can't do without a local captain here because of the currents.
pros: Komodo dragons, mantas and world-class reefs
No licence needed — the crew does everything
You can book a cabin rather than the whole boat
Dry season from April to October
cons: Independent sailing is almost impossible
Crowds of boats at Padar and Pink Beach
Safety on cheap boats varies — choose an operator with reviews
December–March is the rainy season
labuan-bajo-komodo.charter_price_note: There is no bareboat here — price for a private phinisi with crew: Komodo Luxury from ~$1,800 per yacht per night (≈€10,700 for 7 nights), VIP phinisi from $5,800 a night; the price includes crew, three meals a day, soft drinks, fuel for the route and snorkelling gear. The operator publishes no seasonal discounts; peak demand is May–August. Extra — the Komodo National Park fee (~650,000 rupiah per foreigner), alcohol, diving and crew tips; 3–4-night tours are more common
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: crewed schooners and catamarans from Labuan Bajo, cabins from ~$115 a day
Cabins on a 41-metre crewed gaff schooner: Labuan Bajo — Komodo — Padar — Nusa Kode, with diving; booking and support in Russian
Broker: private crewed phinisi from ~$31,000 to $180,000 a week

portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.description: The granite islands of the La Maddalena archipelago, the coves of the Costa Smeralda and a hop across the strait to Bonifacio in Corsica — all within 10–20 miles of each other. Suits both a first bareboat week in calm weather and experienced crews, but you need to know how to sit out a mistral.
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.rating_basis: One of the Mediterranean's most beautiful areas: turquoise water, granite islands, short hops and the option of Corsica; it features in charter aggregators' top lists (Sunsail, Click&Boat, SamBoat, 12knots). Reviews complain about marina prices and the mistral.
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.hazards: The mistral and heaped-up seas in the Strait of Bonifacio, granite shoals and rocks between the islands, a ban on anchoring on Posidonia and closed zones in the park (fines), a 7 kn speed limit within 500 m of the shore, ferry traffic between Olbia and Corsica.
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.crowd_note: In July–August the coves of La Maddalena and Bonifacio are packed and marina berths are booked in advance; June and September are much quieter.
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.region: North-east Sardinia: the La Maddalena archipelago, Costa Smeralda, the Strait of Bonifacio and southern Corsica
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.wind_desc: In summer breezes of 7–15 kn, but the mistral regularly blows from the west–north-west: 25–35 kn, up to 40 kn in the Strait of Bonifacio, lasting 1–3 days. May–June and September are windier; frequent storms from October to April.
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.route: Portisco — Caprera (Cala Coticcio) — Spargi — Lavezzi Islands — Bonifacio (Corsica) — Budelli / Porto della Madonna — La Maddalena — Portisco, ~95 miles in a week
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.mooring: Marinas are expensive: €60–120 a night for 40–45 ft on La Maddalena and in Bonifacio, considerably more in Porto Cervo and on the Costa Smeralda in summer. In La Maddalena park a paid pass is required from June to September (40% discount for sailing yachts); anchor on sand only — Posidonia is off-limits; plenty of buoys and free anchorages off Caprera and Budelli.
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence issued by a government body or authorised organisation (ICC, national licences; most charter companies accept IYT, but in Italy it may formally not be recognised — check in advance) + a VHF certificate held by one crew member; send copies of your documents to the base 2 weeks ahead.
pros: Turquoise water and dozens of coves within short hops
Two countries in a week: Sardinia and Corsica (Bonifacio)
Huge charter fleet, Olbia airport 20 minutes away
cons: Mistral up to 30–40 kn in the Strait of Bonifacio
Expensive marinas and a paid national park pass
Crowded and expensive in July–August
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: August / April–May or October (Sun Odyssey 410 from Olbia ≈ $2,700–4,600); brokers quote €3,500–7,000 for 42–46 ft; a catamaran costs roughly ×2
portisco-la-maddalena-costa-smeralda.skipper_price_note: Skipper ≈ $259 a day from the Portisco charter company, plus food and a separate cabin
highlights: The Loro Piana Superyacht Regatta in Porto Cervo
The Round Sardinia Race
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~270 yachts in Portisco, bases in Olbia, Cannigione, Porto Rotondo
Dream Yacht Charter's Russian office: bareboat, skippered yachts and cabins in Sardinia and Sicily, turnkey trip organisation, Russian-speaking managers
Charter and flotillas from Cannigione
Detailed one-week Sardinia — Corsica route

portorosa-aeolian-islands.description: Seven volcanic islands 15–25 miles from the base at Portorosa: smoking Vulcano, Lipari, green Salina, fashionable Panarea and active Stromboli. Passages are longer and more exposed than in Sardinia and shelter is scarce — best for an experienced or skippered crew.
portorosa-aeolian-islands.rating_basis: Volcanoes, black beaches and Stromboli by night are a regular feature of the “best Italian routes” at Sunsail, Moorings, SamBoat and yacht.de; reviews criticise expensive pontoons, little shelter and rolling from ferry wash.
portorosa-aeolian-islands.hazards: A sudden sirocco, swell in the bays, deep rocky anchorages (you need a tripping line with a buoy), headland effects and gusts around the islands, ferries and hydrofoils, Stromboli's volcanic activity (observe the authorities' restrictions).
portorosa-aeolian-islands.crowd_note: In August Panarea and Lipari are packed with boats and ferries, and pontoon berths are booked in advance; June and September are calm.
portorosa-aeolian-islands.region: Tyrrhenian Sea, northern Sicily: Vulcano, Lipari, Salina, Panarea, Stromboli, Filicudi, Alicudi
portorosa-aeolian-islands.wind_desc: In summer light north-westerlies (tramontana/maestrale) and north-easterlies of 6–15 kn, sometimes over 20 kn; dying down by night. Calms are common in July–August. The south-easterly sirocco can arrive suddenly; in spring and autumn strong local winds, the mistral and the libeccio.
portorosa-aeolian-islands.route: Portorosa — Vulcano (Porto di Ponente) — Lipari — Salina — Panarea — Stromboli (night eruptions from the water) — Filicudi — Vulcano — Portorosa, ~130 miles in a week
portorosa-aeolian-islands.mooring: Pontoons on Lipari, Salina, Vulcano, Stromboli and Filicudi: from €50 to €300+ a night for 40–45 ft in summer; on Lipari ferry wash makes you roll. Paid buoys off Panarea and Filicudi; anchorages are deep and rocky, so you need a tripping line with a buoy.
portorosa-aeolian-islands.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence issued by a government body or authorised organisation (ICC, national licences; most charter companies accept IYT, but in Italy it may formally not be recognised — check in advance) + a VHF certificate held by one crew member.
pros: Active volcanoes and Stromboli's eruptions seen from the yacht
Warm water until the end of October
Large fleet in Portorosa, prices lower than in Sardinia
cons: Little shelter: in a storm only Lipari and Salina are protected
Deep rocky anchorages, swell and ferry wash
Expensive pontoons in summer
portorosa-aeolian-islands.airport: CTA — Catania, ~1 h 40 min; PMO — Palermo, ~2 h
portorosa-aeolian-islands.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week: August / April–May or October — estimate based on 12knots price statistics (40–50 ft average: €6,600 in August, €3,700 in spring); a catamaran costs roughly ×2
portorosa-aeolian-islands.skipper_price_note: Benchmark from Italian charter companies, per day, plus the skipper's food
highlights: Stromboli's night eruptions seen from the water
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: ~215 yachts in Portorosa, cabin cruises

Russian-speaking club: one-week skippered trips on a Lagoon 42 catamaran around the Aeolian Islands (Vulcano, Lipari, Stromboli, Panarea, Salina, Filicudi) in September; starting in north-eastern Sicily
Charter agency: yachts in Sicily with or without a skipper; if the crew has no skipper, they provide one experienced with Russian crews
Dream Yacht Charter's Russian office: bareboat, skippered yachts and cabins in Sicily, turnkey trip organisation, Russian-speaking managers
Bareboat and flotillas around the Aeolian Islands
Local charter company, reviews on 12knots

procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.description: Short hops between Procida, Ischia, Capri and the Amalfi Coast: a different famous town every evening. Easy navigation and light winds suit a first week, but be ready for high berth prices and summer crowds.
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.rating_basis: Sail Magazine and yacht.de praise Capri, Positano and Amalfi from the water and the short hops, but note the light summer winds, crowds and very expensive berths; the best months are May, June and September.
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.hazards: Gusts and squalls off the steep Amalfi coast, swell in Positano (no shelter), the narrow entrance to Amalfi harbour, ferries and fast boats around Ischia, Capri and Naples, thunderstorms in spring and autumn.
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.crowd_note: From late June to late August berths on Capri and in Amalfi and buoys in Positano must be booked well in advance; harbours are busy with ferries and motorboats.
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.region: Tyrrhenian Sea, Campania: Procida, Ischia, Capri, Sorrento, Positano, Amalfi; further on — Ponza and Ventotene
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.wind_desc: In summer mostly light winds: the north-westerly tramontana and thermal breezes of 5–15 kn, with gusts and squalls coming off the mountains along the steep Amalfi coast; you often have to motor. The libeccio (SW) and sirocco (S) build seas; in spring and autumn — thunderstorms with westerly lows.
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.route: Procida — Ischia (Casamicciola or Forio) — Capri (Marina Grande or buoys off Marina Piccola) — Positano — Amalfi — Sorrento — Procida, ~80–100 miles in a week
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.mooring: One of the most expensive places in the Mediterranean: €55–240 a night for 40–45 ft on Ischia, in Sorrento and Amalfi (Amalfi ~€120–200), up to €300 at Capri's Marina Grande. Positano has buoys only (~€100 including water taxi), there are few anchorages, and in summer berths are booked in advance.
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence issued by a government body or authorised organisation (ICC, national licences; most charter companies accept IYT, but in Italy it may formally not be recognised — check in advance) + a VHF certificate held by one crew member.
pros: Capri, Positano, Amalfi and Ischia in one week
Short hops and easy navigation
Base on Procida 1 h from Naples airport
cons: Light winds in summer, lots of motoring
Very expensive berths, few anchorages
Crowds and ferry traffic in July–August
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.airport: NAP — Naples, ~1 h including the ferry to Procida
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.charter_price_note: 40–45 ft bareboat per week from Procida: late July–August / April or October (Oceanis 41.1 ≈ $2,160–4,130, Oceanis 46.1 up to ~$5,900); a catamaran costs roughly ×2
procida-bay-of-naples-amalfi.skipper_price_note: ≈ $2,140 a week from Procida charter companies, plus food and a separate cabin
school_notes: Aggregator with a Russian-language version: sailing yachts and catamarans in Procida
Dream Yacht Charter's Russian office: new base in Naples — Capri, the Amalfi Coast, the Phlegraean and Pontine Islands; bareboat, skipper, cabins, Russian-speaking managers
Sailing trip platform: cabin cruise with a Russian-speaking skipper Salerno — Positano — Sorrento — Procida — Ischia — Capri — Amalfi; also IYT Bareboat Skipper courses in Naples
Charter agency: yachts in the Naples area with or without a skipper; they offer a skipper experienced with Russian crews
Bareboat charter and 7- and 14-day routes

punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.description: Elba and the small national park islands 15–25 miles from the mainland bases of Punta Ala and Scarlino. Moderate winds and Elba's sheltered bays suit a first bareboat week, while a hop to Capraia and Bastia adds some open sea.
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.rating_basis: A quiet alternative to Sardinia: green Elba, the national park and the option of Corsica; there are plenty of charter bases (Punta Ala, Scarlino, San Vincenzo, Castiglioncello), but it makes the top lists less often than southern Italy; Navily reviews mention expensive marinas.
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.hazards: The libeccio and steep seas in the Piombino Channel, national park no-go zones (Montecristo, Pianosa, Gorgona), Piombino — Portoferraio ferries, fishing nets around the islands.
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.crowd_note: In August the marinas on Elba and Capraia fill up, especially at weekends — book ahead; June and September are uncrowded.
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.region: Tyrrhenian Sea, Tuscany: Elba, Capraia, Pianosa, Giglio, Gorgona; nearby — Bastia in Corsica
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.wind_desc: In summer a moderate north-westerly maestrale and daytime breezes of 8–18 kn, often calm in the morning. The south-westerly libeccio kicks up steep seas and can blow hard, especially in spring and autumn; frequent storms from November to April.
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.route: Punta Ala / Scarlino — Elba (Portoferraio or Marciana Marina) — Capraia — Bastia (Corsica) — along Pianosa — Elba (Porto Azzurro) — Punta Ala; shorter — round Elba with a stop at Giglio, 100–190 miles in a week
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.mooring: Tuscan marinas are expensive (in Italy usually €50–200 a night for 40–45 ft), and reviews complain about prices on Capraia and in Punta Ala. Elba has plenty of anchorages; the islands are part of the Tuscan Archipelago National Park: Montecristo is closed, Pianosa and Gorgona by permit only.
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence issued by a government body or authorised organisation (ICC, national licences; most charter companies accept IYT, but in Italy it may formally not be recognised — check in advance) + a VHF certificate held by one crew member.
pros: The warm islands closest to northern Europe, easy to reach from Pisa and Florence
Elba has a bay for every wind
You can sail to Corsica (Bastia)
cons: Expensive marinas
Some national park islands closed or by permit only
The libeccio kicks up unpleasant seas
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.charter_price_note: Estimate for 40–45 ft per week: from ~$2,600–2,750 in spring (Hanse 415, Sun Odyssey 469 in Scarlino); in summer 1.6–1.7 times more according to 12knots statistics
punta-ala-elba-tuscan-archipelago.skipper_price_note: Benchmark from Italian charter companies (~$260–300 a day), plus the skipper's food
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: 37 yachts in Punta Ala
44 yachts in Scarlino, 5 miles from Punta Ala, one-week route
A cabin on a catamaran with captain and cook: a week San Vincenzo — Elba — Gorgona — Capraia — Pianosa — Montecristo; booking in Russian

riva-del-garda-lake-garda.description: The northern tip of Lake Garda, between the Alps, is one of Europe's windiest and most reliable lakes: in the morning the Pelèr blows from the north, in the afternoon the Ora from the south. A great place for training, racing and day sails; in a week you can cruise the whole lake down to Sirmione.
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.rating_basis: One of Europe's best lakes for sailing: the daily thermal winds Pelèr and Ora, dozens of clubs and schools, major regattas (Optimist, ILCA, world championships). As a cruising area it is limited — the lake is narrow, harbours and anchorages are few, and boats are more often rented by the day.
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.hazards: A strong Pelèr in the morning and Ora in the afternoon in the narrow northern part, squalls after thunderstorms (the Balinot, up to 40 kn), steep deep shores with no shelter, heavy traffic of windsurfers, kiters and ferries.
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.crowd_note: In summer Riva and Torbole are crowded with windsurfers, kiters and dinghies; visitor berths in the harbours are taken at weekends.
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.region: Northern Lake Garda (Trentino): Riva del Garda, Torbole, Limone, Malcesine; further south — Gargnano, Salò, Sirmione, Bardolino
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.wind_desc: Two reliable thermal winds: in the morning the northerly Pelèr (Vent) — from 2–3 a.m. until noon, up to 25 kn; from noon to sunset the southerly Ora, over 19 kn, strongest in summer and almost absent in winter. In autumn, after thunderstorms, the squally north-westerly Balinot can blow at 40 kn and more.
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.route: Riva del Garda — Limone — Malcesine — Gargnano — Salò — Sirmione — Bardolino / Garda — back north with the Ora; the lake is ~50 km long, so in a week you can cover the whole shoreline
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.mooring: The charter base is the port of San Nicolò in Riva del Garda; town harbours and clubs around the lake (Malcesine, Limone, Gargnano, Salò, Bardolino); visitor berths are few, book ahead in summer. The northern shores are steep and deep — there are almost no anchorages.
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.licence: Small yachts in Riva are rented even without a licence — GS Charter says a licence is “not necessarily required”; for larger yachts and multi-day rentals Italian companies and the Capitaneria di Porto usually require a government-issued licence (ICC or national); private certificates (IYT etc.) may not be accepted, Russian GIMS licences — check with the charter company. Motor navigation is banned in Trentino waters (except for regatta support).
pros: Predictable wind every day, from two directions
Alpine scenery and waterside towns
Lots of schools, clubs and regattas
Warm fresh water in summer
cons: Few harbours and almost no anchorages
Charters mostly by the day, few weekly offers
Crowded around Riva and Torbole in summer
Motor navigation banned in Trentino
riva-del-garda-lake-garda.charter_price_note: Lake yachts are smaller than seagoing ones: 30–33 ft, 2 cabins. A Beneteau First 31.7 from Malcesine — €349–399 a day or €1,500–2,000 a week (marina berths included); a Nautiner 30S there — ~€1,700 a week from late May to mid-October and ~€1,200 in winter, plus €80 cleaning, skipper ~€130 a day. Half-day rental in Riva (GS Charter) — from €220–430
highlights: Lake Garda Meeting — the world's biggest Optimist regatta (a Guinness record), Riva
Torboli Trophy and the Fraglia Vela Riva autumn regattas
school_notes: San Nicolò port: 25–34 ft yachts with or without a skipper, 3-day tours, sunset sails; open 1 April–30 November
Skippered half-day and full-day sails, courses, April–November
Courses for children and adults, yacht and catamaran rental, May–October
Riva's historic club: school for children and adults May–October, 20+ regattas a year

martinique-le-marin.description: Le Marin is the Caribbean's main charter port: hundreds of boats, French service, and a convenient start both north along Martinique and south to St Lucia and the Grenadines. In spring the area suits a first charter, but in winter the channel crossings with 20–25 kn trades and big seas are for experienced crews.
martinique-le-marin.rating_basis: The Caribbean's largest charter base and the start of routes to the Grenadines (12knots, Sunsail); praised for French infrastructure, the Pitons and variety; in winter the channel crossings require open-sea skills, while in spring the area suits beginners too.
martinique-le-marin.hazards: Wind acceleration and 2–3 m seas in the St Lucia and Dominica channels in winter, reefs and surf on Martinique's Atlantic coast, wind shadows and gusts under the mountains, sargassum seaweed in some years, hurricanes June–November; night sailing prohibited.
martinique-le-marin.crowd_note: Le Marin and Sainte-Anne host hundreds of yachts in December–April, but there's enough room to anchor; on St Lucia the buoys at Marigot Bay and the Pitons are taken by evening, and the “boat boys” are persistent.
martinique-le-marin.region: Caribbean, Windward Islands: Martinique (Sainte-Anne, Anses-d'Arlet, Saint-Pierre), St Lucia (Rodney Bay, Marigot Bay, the Pitons); further south — the Grenadines
martinique-le-marin.wind_desc: Trades: December 15–20 kn from the north-east, January–February the strongest winds (Sunsail quotes 25–30 kn) and big seas in the St Lucia Channel; March–April easterly 15–20 kn; May–October south-easterly 12–15 kn, warmer and wetter, hurricane season. April–May is the most comfortable time for beginners.
martinique-le-marin.route: Le Marin — Sainte-Anne — Anses-d'Arlet — Saint-Pierre — Anses-d'Arlet — Rodney Bay (St Lucia, ~25 miles across the channel) — Marigot Bay — Soufrière by the Pitons — Le Marin, ~130 miles in a week; in 10–14 days — one way to the Grenadines (Bequia, Tobago Cays, ~255 miles)
martinique-le-marin.mooring: Le Marin marina is the Caribbean's largest charter base (~270 boats according to 12knots); Martinique has plenty of free anchorages (the huge bay of Sainte-Anne). On St Lucia a cruising permit costs $7.5–20 and buoys $12–16 a night; anchoring is banned at the Pitons — marine park buoys only.
martinique-le-marin.licence: No formal licence is required: for Le Marin, Sunsail asks for a Level 1 sailing CV (at least 5 days or 100 miles as skipper on a similar yacht); if the base has doubts, a paid skipper is mandatory; for a St Lucia start — Level 3 (20 days or 400 miles). Minimum crew of 2, no night sailing, routes along the sheltered west coast; customs clearance between Martinique and St Lucia.
pros: The widest choice of boats in the Caribbean, flights from Paris
Martinique, St Lucia and the Grenadines can be combined, one-way routes available
Huge, safe anchorages (Sainte-Anne)
St Lucia's Pitons — one of the region's most spectacular anchorages
cons: Strong wind and seas in the channels in winter
Customs at every border crossing
Martinique's east (Atlantic) coast is not recommended for charter
Hurricane season, rainy August–October
martinique-le-marin.airport: FDF — Fort-de-France (Aimé Césaire), ~45 min to Le Marin; for St Lucia — UVF (Hewanorra) or SLU (Vigie)
martinique-le-marin.charter_price_note: Filovent benchmark for a 4-cabin monohull (~43 ft) per week: February–May ~€4,800, December–January (holidays) up to €5,800 / June–November ~€3,200; 3-cabin 39–41 ft boats are cheaper, from ~€2,100–2,700 in low season. Extra — Dream Yacht's mandatory package from ~€355 (final cleaning, linen, dinghy), mooring and fuel; skipper ~€210 a day plus food
highlights: Finish of the ARC Atlantic rally in Rodney Bay (St Lucia)
Tour des Yoles Rondes — a race of traditional boats round Martinique
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator: ~270 boats in Le Marin, Martinique — Grenadines cabin cruises
Base at Le Marin marina (run by the team from St Lucia)
Base at Rodney Bay marina, routes to the Grenadines

kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.description: Three islands a few miles apart: Valletta's fortresses, the fishing village of Marsaxlokk, Comino's Blue Lagoon and the cliffs of Gozo. Short hops and warm water from May to October suit a first week — just keep an eye on the forecast for the gregale.
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.rating_basis: A compact archipelago with clear water, the Blue Lagoon and Valletta's historic harbours; a long season (April–October according to 12knots). Downsides — a small charter fleet, few islands for a week-long route, crowds of motorboats at Comino.
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.hazards: The gregale (NE) with big seas in bays and harbours in autumn and winter, Malta — Gozo ferries in the Comino Channel, heavy tour boat traffic, large ships around Grand Harbour.
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.crowd_note: The Blue Lagoon off Comino is packed with tour boats during the day; the Grand Harbour and Gozo marinas are full in summer, but there are enough anchorages.
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.region: Maltese archipelago: Grand Harbour and Valletta, Marsaxlokk, St Paul's Bay, Mellieħa, Comino (Blue Lagoon), Gozo
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.wind_desc: In summer the north-westerly majjistral of 10–18 kn prevails — shelter on the south-east coasts; calms happen. The north-easterly gregale brings strong winds in autumn and winter and dangerous seas that roll into bays and harbours; in spring — the sirocco from the south.
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.route: Kalkara — Comino (Blue Lagoon) — Gozo (Mġarr, Xlendi, Dwejra, Ramla) — Mellieħa — St Paul's Bay — Sliema — Marsaxlokk — Kalkara, ~80–100 miles in a week
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.mooring: Marinas in Grand Harbour (Kalkara, Vittoriosa), in Msida and on Gozo (Mġarr); book ahead in summer. Plenty of anchorages, but choose by the wind: in a gregale the north-east coasts are exposed. The Blue Lagoon is very crowded with tour boats during the day — better in the evening and morning.
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.licence: For bareboat: a skipper's licence (ICC, national, Day Skipper) + a VHF certificate; according to 12knots, a licence is mandatory in the Mediterranean, and in Europe Day Skipper / ICC and VHF plus a sailing CV are usually requested.
pros: Long season: warm water until the end of October
Short hops and historic harbours
Clear water, excellent snorkelling and diving
cons: Few islands — a week-long route gets repetitive
Small charter fleet
Crowds of motorboats at Comino
kalkara-malta-gozo-comino.charter_price_note: Dufour 45 (2009, 46 ft, 3 cabins) from Birgu (next to Kalkara) per week: high season (July–August) ~€3,900 / low season ~€2,600, plus 18% Maltese VAT, cleaning, fuel and mooring. For comparison, a Dufour 450 GL (2014, 4 cabins) from Kalkara — $3,050–3,550 (≈€3,000) from October to December plus a ~€135 service package (cleaning, linen, gas); skipper €235 a day plus food and a cabin
highlights: The Rolex Middle Sea Race (starting in Grand Harbour)
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: bases in Kalkara, Valletta, Sliema
Charter company based in Kalkara port: yachts with or without a skipper, a Russian-speaking skipper available; cruises around Malta and Gozo

langkawi-malaysia.description: An archipelago of 99 islands on the Thai border: limestone cliffs, the Kilim mangroves, and the beaches of Ko Lipe an hour or two away. Calm water, light winds and empty anchorages suit a leisurely week or a delivery to Phuket; in the rainy season sudden squalls are possible.
langkawi-malaysia.rating_basis: A quiet alternative to Phuket: a UNESCO geopark, mangroves, cheap duty-free fuel and beer, few yachts. The charter fleet is small and scattered (mixed reviews on 12 Knots), and the wind is often light — it makes the top lists mainly as part of a Langkawi — Phuket route.
langkawi-malaysia.hazards: “Sumatra” squalls in the south-west monsoon (they hit without warning), strong tidal currents in the channels and at the Hole in the Wall, an uncharted underwater rock south-east of Pulau Seland (Bass Harbour), reefs at the entrance to Telaga and off Bumbon, fishing stakes and nets, ferry wash near Kuah.
langkawi-malaysia.crowd_note: Anchorages are empty even in season; it's only busy around Kuah (ferries) and in January during the regatta.
langkawi-malaysia.region: Andaman Sea: the Langkawi archipelago (99 islands), Tarutao and Ko Lipe in Thailand
langkawi-malaysia.wind_desc: December–March — the north-east monsoon: dry, NE 8–15 kn, calm seas, the best anchorages on the west and south sides of the islands. April–May — light variable winds, heat, thunderstorms. June–October — the south-west monsoon: downpours and sudden “Sumatra” squalls with strong gusts, often at night; with over 20 kn your anchor may drag.
langkawi-malaysia.route: Kuah — Dayang Bunting / Singa Besar — Ko Lipe (Thailand, Tarutao National Park) — Ko Butang — Ko Rawi — Ko Adang — Tepor — Kuah (you need to clear out and into Thailand); a no-border option — round Langkawi via Rebak, Telaga, Datai and the Kilim mangroves, ~80 miles
langkawi-malaysia.mooring: Two main marinas: Royal Langkawi Yacht Club in Kuah (234 berths, pricier than the rest) and Telaga Harbour in the north-west; also Rebak and Resorts World. Anchorages are free, with sand or mud bottoms and good holding; landing a dinghy at Telaga and Bass Harbour costs 5–8 ringgit a day.
langkawi-malaysia.licence: For bareboat, charter companies require an internationally recognised certificate: ICC, RYA Day Skipper / Yachtmaster, ISA, US Sailing Bareboat Cruising or equivalent. Without documents — skippered only. To visit Thailand you must clear out of Malaysia and clear in at Satun / Ko Lipe.
pros: Empty anchorages and calm water
Duty-free island: cheap fuel and provisions
Can be combined with the Tarutao islands (Thailand) or a run to Phuket
Warm water all year round
cons: The wind is often light — lots of motoring
A small, mixed charter fleet
June–October — downpours and “Sumatra” squalls
Murky water near Kuah, mud and fouling at the anchorages
langkawi-malaysia.charter_price_note: 40–43 ft bareboat (3 cabins) per week: December–March / May–October; the fleet is small, and some yachts alternate with Phuket
highlights: Royal Langkawi International Regatta (RLYC, Kuah)
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator, yachts on Langkawi
Charter agency: weekly yacht rental on Langkawi (base in Kuah) bareboat or skippered, routes around the archipelago, to Penang and into Thai waters
Marina and yacht club, regatta organiser
Broker: 38–48 ft bareboats, skippers

lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.description: The shallow freshwater IJsselmeer with its historic harbour towns, and an exit through the Afsluitdijk locks into the tidal Wadden Sea with its islands and seals. The lake suits a first bareboat week, the Wadden Sea those who can work tides; there are also traditional “brown fleet” sailing ships with crew for groups.
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.rating_basis: Lemmer is one of Friesland's best-known watersports centres, with a huge charter fleet; people love the cosy towns, fresh water and variety (lake + tidal sea, a UNESCO site). Downsides — shallows and a short chop, windy cool weather, crowded harbours in summer.
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.hazards: IJsselmeer shallows and a steep short chop at 20+ kn; on the Wadden Sea — tides, strong currents in the channels, drying flats and shifting channels (old charts are useless), closed nature reserves; heavy traffic at the locks and commercial shipping; wind farms on the lake.
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.crowd_note: In July–August and at weekends the harbours of the Wadden islands and popular IJsselmeer towns are packed, with boats rafted several deep; May, June and September are quieter.
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.region: Friesland: the IJsselmeer (Stavoren, Hindeloopen, Enkhuizen, Medemblik), the Frisian lakes, the Wadden Sea (Harlingen, Vlieland, Terschelling)
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.wind_desc: South-westerlies and westerlies of 10–18 kn prevail, with some calm days in summer; on the shallow IJsselmeer (average depth 4.5 m) a short steep chop builds quickly in a fresh breeze. On the Wadden Sea tidal currents rule everything, and passages are planned by the tide tables. In spring and autumn 20+ kn is more common.
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.route: Lemmer — Stavoren — Kornwerderzand lock — Harlingen — Vlieland — Terschelling — Harlingen — Makkum — Hindeloopen — Lemmer, ~110 miles in a week; a calm IJsselmeer-only option: Lemmer — Enkhuizen — Medemblik — Stavoren — Hindeloopen — Lemmer
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.mooring: Marinas and town harbours in every IJsselmeer town, berthing in boxes between piles; on the Wadden Sea the island harbours (Vlieland, Terschelling) are packed in summer, with yachts rafted several deep. Flat-bottomed or lifting-keel boats can dry out on the flats, but some areas are closed to protect seals and birds.
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.licence: On inland waters (including the IJsselmeer) a certificate (ICC/klein vaarbewijs) is only needed for boats over 15 m or faster than ~20 km/h — a normal 40 ft sailing yacht legally needs no licence; on coastal waters the flag state's requirements apply. You need to know the BPR rules, and VHF radios must have ATIS. Charter companies ask about experience, and for the Wadden Sea — confident navigation.
pros: Huge choice of yachts and marinas, long season (April–October)
No licence needed for a normal yacht on the lake
Two different areas in a week: a freshwater lake and a tidal sea with islands
Close to Amsterdam, traditional Dutch towns
cons: Shallow: a short steep chop in a fresh breeze, shallow draught needed
The Wadden Sea demands precise tidal planning, the flats dry out
Windy, cool weather, frequent rain
Crowded harbours in summer
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.airport: AMS — Amsterdam Schiphol, ~1 h 15 min by car
lemmer-ijsselmeer-wadden.charter_price_note: Varianta 44 (2012, 43 ft, 4 cabins) from Lemmer per week: late July–mid-August and Ascension ~€1,850, late March–early April ~€1,750 / May, June, October–early November ~€1,400, March and December ~€1,250; a Bavaria Cruiser 40 (2013) is €50 cheaper. Plus final cleaning €130–150, linen ~€25 per person; new boats from Lelystad (Bavaria C42, 2021) from ~€2,000. The base doesn't provide skippers
highlights: Skûtsjesilen — races of traditional Frisian skûtsje barges, with stages including Lemmer

svolvaer-lofoten.description: Jagged granite peaks rising straight out of the sea, fishing villages on stilts and the midnight sun — one of Europe's most beautiful and rugged sailing areas. Suits experienced crews with warm clothing; beginners only with a skipper or on a cabin cruise.
svolvaer-lofoten.rating_basis: Yachting World calls the Lofoten Islands one of the most beautiful places on the planet, and Yachting Monthly and PBO publish rave reports of cruises under the midnight sun; reviews complain about cold water, sudden gales, expensive food and few charter yachts.
svolvaer-lofoten.hazards: The Moskstraumen maelstrom between Moskenesøya and Værøy — give it a wide berth; strong currents between the islands; squalls and gusts off the cliffs and down the valleys; 2–3 m tides and shallow water in visitor harbours (rocks by the inner pier in Svolvær); the narrow Trollfjord, where cruise ships turn; cold water.
svolvaer-lofoten.crowd_note: From mid-July to mid-August (Norwegian holidays) the visitor pontoons in Reine and Skrova fill up; late May–June is the quietest time.
svolvaer-lofoten.region: Northern Norway, above the Arctic Circle: Lofoten, Vestfjord, Trollfjord, Vesterålen
svolvaer-lofoten.wind_desc: In summer the wind is changeable: under a high it's often calm and you motor; when lows pass through, south-westerlies of 20–30 kn arrive almost without warning. In the fjords the wind follows the valleys and shifts at every bend, and squalls drop off the cliffs. From September gales become more frequent.
svolvaer-lofoten.route: Svolvær — Henningsvær — Nusfjord — Reine — Å — Skrova — Trollfjord — Svolvær, ~150 miles in a week
svolvaer-lofoten.mooring: Visitor harbours at every fishing village (in Svolvær, Marinepollen — ~NOK 350 a night, showers and laundry extra), often moored alongside the pier; in Reine and Skrova the visitor pontoons are small and too shallow for deep draught, and may be full in summer. There are good anchorages (Sigerfjord, Trollfjord), but the shores are steep-to and deep.
svolvaer-lofoten.licence: Norway itself doesn't require a licence from foreigners on foreign-flagged boats; Norwegians born in 1980 or later need one for boats up to 15 m, and the ICC is only recognised with the coastal endorsement. Charter companies require an ICC or equivalent and experience for bareboat — check with the charter company.
pros: Fantastic scenery: Reine, Trollfjord, Henningsvær
Midnight sun — you can sail round the clock
Few yachts, quiet anchorages, excellent fishing from the boat
Visitor harbours in almost every village
cons: Short season — effectively June–August
Cold: water 9–12 °C, air up to 15–18 °C, waterproof gear essential
Sudden gales and squalls off the mountains, frequent calms
Few charter yachts, expensive food, restaurants and flights
svolvaer-lofoten.airport: SVJ — Svolvær (Helle), ~10 min; EVE — Harstad/Narvik (Evenes), ~2.5 h; BOO — Bodø + ferry/fast boat
svolvaer-lofoten.charter_price_note: There are only a handful of bareboats on Lofoten itself; the main fleet is in Harstad and Tromsø. Oceanis 423 (2007, 43 ft, 3 cabins) from Harstad per week: May–early September ~€4,950 / September to April ~€3,850. Plus final cleaning ~€270, linen ~€32 per person, gas ~€51 a week, deposit ~€3,200. In Svolvær BeBlue rents 3-cabin yachts from ~€2,200 a week plus fuel, cleaning and mooring fees
svolvaer-lofoten.skipper_price_note: BeBlue: skipper from €1,260 a week (~€180 a day), plus food
highlights: Midnight sun — the sun doesn't set (roughly late May to mid-July)
Northern lights at the start and end of the season
school_notes: yacht and catamaran charter from Svolvær, skipper, hostess
Norwegian sailing school: skippered Bodø — Svolvær trips, ICC assessment
cabin cruises on a Bavaria 50 Bodø — Svolvær with a skipper, beginners welcome
trip platform with Russian-speaking skippers; occasional routes in Northern Norway (Tromsø — Harstad)

opua-bay-of-islands.description: A hundred and forty-four islands in a subtropical bay in New Zealand's north: short hops, sheltered coves, dolphins and historic Russell. Suits a relaxed summer week (December–March) on a small yacht or an IYT course; winter is cold and windy.
opua-bay-of-islands.rating_basis: One of New Zealand's most popular sailing and fishing areas: 144 islands, sheltered coves, dolphins; the first port of call for yachts crossing the Pacific. The charter fleet is small (mostly 25–37 ft boats), and the water is cool even in summer.
opua-bay-of-islands.hazards: Rapid weather changes and south-westerly fronts, especially in winter; occasional remnants of tropical cyclones in January–March; tidal streams at inlet entrances, rocks and reefs around the islands, swell off Cape Brett outside the bay, Opua — Okiato ferries.
opua-bay-of-islands.crowd_note: In January (summer holidays) the popular coves of Urupukapuka and off Roberton Island are busy with local boats; the rest of the time it's uncrowded.
opua-bay-of-islands.region: Northland, North Island: the bay's 144 islands, Russell, Paihia, Urupukapuka, Cape Brett
opua-bay-of-islands.wind_desc: December–March — a warm summer: daytime breezes of 10–15 kn, dry and sunny; occasionally the remnants of tropical cyclones arrive (January–March). April–May — cooler and windier. June–September — winter: south-westerlies and fronts, rain (most in June–July), air 15–16 °C.
opua-bay-of-islands.route: Opua — Russell — Roberton Island (Motuarohia) — Urupukapuka (Otehei Bay) — Deep Water Cove by Cape Brett — Te Puna Inlet — Kerikeri Inlet — Opua
opua-bay-of-islands.mooring: Bay of Islands Marina in Opua (~250 berths, a port of entry into the country); the bay has plenty of sheltered anchorages for any wind direction, and apart from Opua there are almost no marinas.
opua-bay-of-islands.licence: New Zealand has no official licence for pleasure yachts — it's up to the charter company. Great Escape doesn't rent yachts to beginners: you need a sailing qualification and/or at least 6 months' experience on a similar boat, and your skills are checked at the briefing. No night sailing — be at anchor by dark.
pros: Plenty of sheltered anchorages for any wind
Short hops, calm water inside the bay
A school with IYT courses and flotillas
Few people outside the January holidays
cons: Small charter fleet, mostly yachts up to 37 ft
Water no warmer than 21–22 °C even in summer
Fronts, rain and cold in winter (June–September)
A long flight, via Auckland
opua-bay-of-islands.charter_price_note: The bareboat fleet in Opua is small yachts up to 31 ft (Great Escape): a Raven 31 (9.5 m, up to 4 people) — NZ$595 a day in December–February (≈€2,150 a week) / NZ$540 in February–May (≈€1,950); on Yachtico the same boat starts at ~€2,540 a week including fees, a Noelex 30 from ~€2,100. Plus fuel ~NZ$15 a day, deposit insurance NZ$25 a day, linen NZ$30 per person. 28–45 ft yachts with or without a skipper are available from FairWind Charters
school_notes: 25–37 ft bareboats and flotillas from Opua; Yachting NZ and IYT courses (Bareboat Skipper — 5 days, ICC, VHF)

raiatea-society-islands.description: Turquoise lagoons, Taha'a the vanilla island, Bora Bora and quiet Huahine: by day 25–33-mile open-ocean passages in the trades, at night calm water inside the reef. Well suited to an experienced crew on a catamaran and to anyone ready for a long flight for one of the world's most beautiful routes.
raiatea-society-islands.rating_basis: A tropical charter classic: the lagoons of Taha'a and Bora Bora, steady trades, a tide of less than 30 cm, well-marked reef passes; bases of The Moorings, Sunsail, Dream Yacht and local companies. Downsides — the long flight, high prices and the anchoring ban on Bora Bora.
raiatea-society-islands.hazards: Coral heads in the lagoons (sail in good light), currents in the narrow reef passes, ocean swell between the islands in fresh trades, rain squalls in the wet season, tropical cyclones November–April.
raiatea-society-islands.crowd_note: Not many yachts; buoys on Bora Bora and in Taha'a's popular bays may be taken by evening in July–August.
raiatea-society-islands.region: Leeward Society Islands: Raiatea, Taha'a (sharing a lagoon), Bora Bora, Huahine, Maupiti
raiatea-society-islands.wind_desc: May–October — the dry, cool season: steady easterly trades of 15–20 kn, June and August the driest; sometimes a reinforced south-easterly. November–April — the warm wet season: lighter, more variable winds, downpours (most in December), risk of tropical cyclones.
raiatea-society-islands.route: Raiatea — Bora Bora (30 miles) — Piti Aau — Taha'a, Hurepiti Bay — Huahine (33 miles) — Fetuna — Taha'a, Haamene Bay — Raiatea, ~160 miles in a week
raiatea-society-islands.mooring: Inside the lagoons — buoys and anchoring; a buoy costs ~$1–2 per foot for a monohull and $2–3 for a catamaran, and buoys off restaurants and pearl farms are free for customers. Anchoring is banned on Bora Bora — buoys only (~XPF 4,000 ≈ $40 a night). Marinas are at Uturoa and Apooiti on Raiatea.
raiatea-society-islands.licence: No official licence is mandatory — charter companies look at your sailing CV: The Moorings requires Level 3 experience (independent coastal navigation, ~20 days or 400 miles as skipper). You need to be able to handle reef passes; without experience — a skipper ($250 a day from The Moorings).
pros: Steady 15–20 kn trades in the dry season
Calm water inside the lagoons, tide under 30 cm
Bora Bora, Taha'a and Huahine in one week
Well-marked reef passes
cons: Very expensive and a long way to fly
January–March — wet season and cyclone risk
Paid buoys only on Bora Bora
Few monohulls for charter
raiatea-society-islands.airport: RFP — Raiatea, ~5 min (Air Tahiti flights from Papeete, PPT)
raiatea-society-islands.charter_price_note: Average weekly price for a 40–50 ft yacht (almost all catamarans) according to 12 Knots: July / January; monohulls are few — The Moorings bareboats from $4,199 a week in low season
raiatea-society-islands.skipper_price_note: The Moorings skipper — $250 a day, plus food
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: yachts from Apooiti marina (Raiatea), cabin cruises from $1,469 for 8 days
Charter agency: yachts in French Polynesia with a Russian-speaking skipper or bareboat, routes to Bora Bora, visa assistance
A cabin on a catamaran with captain and cook: a week Raiatea — Taha'a — Bora Bora and back; booking in Russian
Bareboat, skippers and crewed yachts from Raiatea
