horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.description: Ocean sailing among volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic: Horta with its painted harbour wall, the Pico volcano and whales right ahead. Passages between the islands are up to 50 miles of open ocean, so the area is for experienced or skippered crews.
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.rating_basis: A cult destination for ocean sailors: Horta and Peter Café Sport, the Pico volcano, whales, green islands; yet 12knots rates the routes as “experienced” — long open-ocean passages, few marinas and a small charter fleet.
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.hazards: Atlantic swell and fast-moving fronts, wind acceleration in the channels around Pico, exposed anchorages, hurricane remnants in September–October, whales in your path (keep your distance).
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.crowd_note: Horta marina is packed in May–July when the transatlantic yachts arrive; the other islands are uncrowded, but their marinas are small.
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.region: Central group of the Azores, Atlantic: Faial, Pico, São Jorge, Terceira, Graciosa
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.wind_desc: In summer, under the Azores High, the wind is usually moderate at 8–15 kn, with some calms; in the channel between Faial and Pico the wind strengthens because of Pico's height (2,351 m). In spring and autumn Atlantic fronts bring 25–35 kn and big swell; in September–October hurricane remnants occasionally reach the islands.
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.route: Horta (Faial) — Velas (São Jorge) — Angra do Heroísmo (Terceira, a day ashore) — Lajes do Pico (a day ashore, whales) — Horta, ~147 miles in a week; shorter — the Faial — Pico — São Jorge triangle (5–25-mile passages)
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.mooring: Horta marina is the legendary stopover for transatlantic yachts: crowded in May–July, with yachts rafted several deep. Small marinas in Velas (few berths for big yachts), Angra and Lajes do Pico (book ahead); anchorages are open to ocean swell.
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.licence: In Portugal a licence is required for any yacht, sail or motor (ICC or a national licence — check with the charter company) + a VHF certificate held by one crew member; 12knots marks the Azores routes as “experienced”.
pros: The atmosphere of ocean sailing and legendary Horta
Whales and dolphins almost every day
Few boats, wild nature
cons: Open ocean, swell and rapidly changing weather
Short season, water no warmer than 23 °C
Small fleet and few marinas
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.airport: HOR — Horta, ~10 min; PDL — Ponta Delgada (São Miguel), ~40 min flight
horta-azores-faial-pico-sao-jorge.charter_price_note: Dufour 410 GL (2016, 41 ft, 3 cabins) from Horta marina per week: 24 July–20 August ~€4,850, late June–July and late August–mid-September ~€4,500 / mid-October to mid-April ~€3,150 (€2,950 in autumn 2026), late April–June and late September ~€3,900. Plus final cleaning €220, deposit €2,000; skipper ~€1,200 a week plus food and a cabin
highlights: Transatlantic yacht season in Horta, the tradition of painting the harbour wall and Peter Café Sport
Watching sperm whales and other whales off Pico and Faial
The Semana do Mar sea festival in Horta
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: route and yachts in Horta

lagos-algarve.description: An Atlantic coastline of golden cliffs, grottoes and fishing towns; hops are short, but the wind is fresh and there's swell and tide. Suits an experienced crew who want a taste of the ocean without long passages.
lagos-algarve.rating_basis: Beautiful cliffs and grottoes around Lagos, steady wind and cheaper than the Mediterranean, but it's an exposed Atlantic coast with swell and tides, few sheltered coves and a small charter fleet; in recent years — the risk of orca encounters off the Iberian coast.
lagos-algarve.hazards: Atlantic swell and strong wind off Cape St Vincent, tidal streams and shallows at the lagoon entrances (Culatra, Faro), fish traps and nets along the coast, orcas that damage rudders (mostly near Gibraltar and in the Gulf of Cádiz; if you meet them, don't stop and head for shallow water).
lagos-algarve.crowd_note: In August the Lagos and Vilamoura marinas are full, but you can usually find a berth; anchorages are uncrowded.
lagos-algarve.region: Atlantic coast of southern Portugal: Lagos, Portimão, Albufeira, Vilamoura, the Ria Formosa lagoon; to the west — Sagres
lagos-algarve.wind_desc: In summer a north-westerly–westerly of 12–20 kn blows in the afternoon, up to 25 kn and more towards Cape St Vincent and off Sagres, lighter in the morning; east of Lagos — moderate sea breezes. Occasionally the easterly levante comes in from Gibraltar. From November to March Atlantic lows bring south-westerly gales.
lagos-algarve.route: Lagos — Alvor / Portimão — Albufeira — Vilamoura — Culatra (Ria Formosa) — Vilamoura — Portimão — Lagos, ~110–130 miles in a week; for experienced crews — a run out to Sagres and Cape St Vincent
lagos-algarve.mooring: Large marinas in Lagos, Portimão, Albufeira and Vilamoura; anchorages off Alvor, Ferragudo and in the Ria Formosa lagoon (Culatra). Anchorages are mostly open to Atlantic swell; take the tide into account at the lagoon entrances.
lagos-algarve.licence: In Portugal a licence is required for any yacht, sail or motor (ICC or a national licence — check with the charter company) + a VHF certificate held by one crew member; according to 12knots, in Europe Day Skipper / ICC and VHF are usually requested.
pros: The cliffs and grottoes of Ponta da Piedade from the water
Steady summer wind
Prices lower than in the Mediterranean
cons: Exposed coast, few sheltered coves, swell
Tides and currents at the Ria Formosa entrances
Risk of orca encounters off the Iberian coast
lagos-algarve.charter_price_note: Estimate for 40–45 ft per week based on 12knots statistics for Portugal (12–16 m average: ~€4,700 in July–August, €3,500–3,700 in April and October); the Algarve fleet is small
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: bases in Portimão, Cascais, Lisbon, the Azores
Charter agency: yachts in Portugal (Portimão, Lisbon, Cascais, the Azores, Madeira) with or without a skipper; a Russian-speaking skipper can be hired

seychelles-mahe-praslin.description: Granite islands with the best beaches in the Indian Ocean, 5–25-mile hops between Mahé, Praslin and La Digue, turtles and marine parks. Suits experienced skippers and groups on a skippered catamaran; beginners are better off in the transitional months or with a skipper.
seychelles-mahe-praslin.rating_basis: One of the world's most beautiful tropical cruising grounds: granite islands, the beaches of La Digue and Praslin, turtles and nature reserves; bases of The Moorings, Sunsail, Dream Yacht and Navigare. Reviews and guides mention high prices, strong trades in summer and currents, and few marinas.
seychelles-mahe-praslin.hazards: Unlit granite rocks and reefs, strong and unpredictable currents (up to 2.5 kn), squalls with 30–40° wind shifts, steep seas and southerly swell in the trade-wind season, tides of up to 1.5 m; night passages not recommended, serious medical care only on Mahé.
seychelles-mahe-praslin.crowd_note: Few yachts and empty anchorages; it's only crowded in La Digue's tiny harbour and at Christmas and New Year, when the best catamarans are booked 8–12 months ahead.
seychelles-mahe-praslin.region: Inner Islands: Mahé, Sainte Anne, Praslin, Curieuse, Cousin, La Digue, Félicité, Île Cocos
seychelles-mahe-praslin.wind_desc: November–March — the north-west monsoon: warm, NW 8–15 kn, calm seas, short heavy downpours (most rain in December–January). April and October–November — transitional months: 5–12 kn, flat water, the best visibility. May–September — the south-east trades: 15–22 kn, 20–28 kn with gusts of 30+ on open passages in July–August, a short steep sea and swell from the south. No cyclones — the islands lie outside the cyclone belt.
seychelles-mahe-praslin.route: Eden Island (Mahé) — Sainte Anne Marine Park — Praslin (Anse Volbert, Anse Lazio) — Curieuse — Cousin — La Digue — Île Cocos and Félicité — Mahé, ~80 miles in a week
seychelles-mahe-praslin.mooring: Marinas only on Mahé (Eden Island) and Praslin (Baie Ste Anne); elsewhere you anchor on sand (not on coral) or take paid buoys in the marine parks. Overnight costs $14–39: a buoy ~$35–39, anchoring off La Digue ~$14 (La Passe harbour has room for 3–4 yachts — call ahead); landing and reserve fees ~$117 per person per week.
seychelles-mahe-praslin.licence: For bareboat — a recognised certificate (ICC, IPC, ASA 103, US Sailing etc.); The Moorings requires Level 3 experience — at least 20 days or 400 miles as skipper on a similar yacht. Daytime sailing only (reefs, unlit rocks). Without experience — with a skipper or on a cabin cruise.
pros: Warm all year round, no cyclones
Famous beaches (Anse Lazio, Anse Source d'Argent) and nature reserves
Empty anchorages
April–May and October–November — light winds and flat water
cons: Expensive: catamarans, buoy and reserve fees
July–August — 20–28 kn trades and steep seas on passages
December–January — downpours and squalls
Daytime sailing only, few marinas
seychelles-mahe-praslin.charter_price_note: Average weekly price for a 40–50 ft yacht according to 12 Knots: April / June; the fleet is almost entirely catamarans, monohulls are few (the cheapest sailing yachts from ~$2,100 a week). Christmas prices are like August
seychelles-mahe-praslin.skipper_price_note: Skipper €150–200 a day ($225 a night with The Moorings), plus food

Russian-speaking club: skippered cabin cruises on a catamaran from Mahé — Praslin, Cousin, Curieuse, La Digue, Cocos; departures in March–April
Dream Yacht Charter's Russian office: bareboat, skippered yachts, catamaran cabins and turnkey tours in the Seychelles, Russian-speaking managers
Charter agency: yachts and catamarans with or without a skipper, route planning help; they offer a one-week cruise from Baie Ste Anne on Praslin

Charter from Eden Island marina

gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.description: Bare pink granite islands, white fishing villages, oysters and lobsters — Sweden's west coast is windier and saltier than the Stockholm archipelago. Short hops through inner passages alternate with runs out into the open Skagerrak; suits crews with basic experience.
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.rating_basis: The Ocean Cruising Club describes Bohuslän as red granite islands with white cottages and countless natural harbours; sailors value the steady wind and fishing villages; downsides — Marstrand and Smögen packed in July, a short season and rocks outside the fairways.
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.hazards: Underwater rocks and shallows outside the marked fairways, sudden summer squalls, Skagerrak swell off the outer islands, ferries and cargo ships on the approaches to Gothenburg; there's practically no tide, but in strong winds currents of 1–2 kn can run in the narrows.
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.crowd_note: From Midsummer to the end of July Marstrand, Smögen, Hunnebostrand and Lysekil are packed with Norwegian and German boats; early June and after mid-August (when school starts) are quiet.
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.region: Kattegat and Skagerrak: the Bohuslän archipelago — Marstrand, Tjörn, Orust, Käringön, Smögen, Lysekil, Fjällbacka
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.wind_desc: In summer westerlies and south-westerlies prevail, averaging 8–16 kn; in good weather a daytime sea breeze, with occasional calms and sudden summer squalls. Windier than the Stockholm archipelago: the outer islands are exposed to the Skagerrak and its swell. From September gales are more frequent.
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.route: Gothenburg — Marstrand — Klädesholmen — Käringön — Smögen — Lysekil — Mollösund — Marstrand — Gothenburg, ~110–130 miles in a week
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.mooring: Visitor harbours in every village (usually SEK 100–250 a night for 10 m, Marstrand and Smögen cost more) and a wealth of natural harbours among the bare granite islands: you moor bow-to the rock with a stern anchor under the right of public access (allemansrätten), but not next to houses or in nature reserves.
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.licence: Under Swedish law no licence is needed for boats under 12 m long and 4 m wide; yachts over 12 m long and 4 m wide require a skepparexamen/kustskepparexamen or higher. Charter companies require a recognised sailing certificate (ICC/IYT/RYA etc.) and experience for bareboat — check with the charter company.
pros: A steady westerly — more real sailing than in the Baltic
Natural harbours among the islands, bow-to-the-rock mooring
Picturesque villages: Marstrand, Käringön, Smögen, Fjällbacka
Seafood: oysters, prawns, lobsters
cons: Short season — June–August
Popular harbours packed in July
Rocks and shallows outside the fairways, outer islands exposed to swell
Expensive restaurants and visitor harbours in the trendy villages
gothenburg-bohuslan-west-sweden.charter_price_note: Bavaria Cruiser 41 (2022, 39 ft, 3 cabins) from Gothenburg (Eriksberg) per week: mid-July–mid-August ~€5,300, early July and from mid-August ~€4,800 / May ~€3,500, June ~€4,200; from October to April the fleet is laid up ashore. Plus final cleaning ~€310, gas ~€67 a week; skipper ~€2,200 a week including food. Older boats (Bavaria 39, 2007) from ~€1,750
highlights: Midsummer — the midsummer festival, harbours packed
Opening of the lobster season in Bohuslän (late September)
school_notes: Russian-language aggregator: Bavaria/Hanse sailing yachts at Göteborg City Marina

saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.description: Thousands of granite islands an hour from Stockholm: short hops in sheltered, tide-free water, pine trees, villages of red cottages and bow-to-the-rock mooring. A good place for a first bareboat week and a family holiday in the white nights.
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.rating_basis: The Ocean Cruising Club and sailing magazines praise the endless number of coves, free moorings and calm, tide-free water; downsides — a short season, light winds and rocks outside the fairways.
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.hazards: Underwater rocks and shallows outside the marked fairways (Swedes joke that sooner or later everyone hits a rock), ferries and cruise ships in the fairways to Stockholm, wind-driven currents of up to 1–2 kn in the narrows in strong winds, cold water.
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.crowd_note: From Midsummer to the end of July the popular harbours (Sandhamn, Vaxholm, Grinda) are packed with Swedish boats, but there's room in the coves; early June and August after school starts are empty except at weekends.
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.region: Baltic: the Stockholm archipelago — Vaxholm, Grinda, Möja, Sandhamn, Utö, Dalarö; north as far as Arholma
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.wind_desc: In summer a south-westerly of Force 2–3 prevails, with calms and a daytime sea breeze in good weather; gales in July blow about 2% of the time. In autumn the wind veers west and strengthens. Inside the archipelago there are almost no waves; off the outer islands (Sandhamn, Utö) it's the open Baltic.
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.route: Saltsjöbaden — Vaxholm — Grinda — Möja — Sandhamn — Utö — Dalarö — Saltsjöbaden, ~100 miles in a week
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.mooring: About 24,000 islands: free anchorages almost everywhere, and under the right of public access (allemansrätten) you can moor bow-to the rock with a stern anchor for a couple of days, as long as it's not next to private houses. Visitor harbours usually charge SEK 100–250 (€10–25) a night for 10 m, popular ones more. Discharging sewage is banned — pump-out stations only.
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.licence: Under Swedish law no licence is needed for boats under 12 m long and 4 m wide; yachts over 12 m long and 4 m wide require a skepparexamen/kustskepparexamen or higher. Charter companies require a recognised sailing certificate (ICC/IYT/RYA etc.) and experience on a yacht of that size for bareboat.
pros: Endless choice of coves and free mooring under the right of public access
No tides, almost no waves inside the archipelago
Excellent charts and navigation apps, everything well marked
White nights and easy access: the base is 20 km from central Stockholm
cons: Short season — June–August
Often light winds, lots of motoring
Countless rocks and shallows outside the fairways — careful navigation needed
Cool water (17–18 °C at the peak), expensive restaurants
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.airport: ARN — Stockholm Arlanda, ~1 h to Saltsjöbaden
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.charter_price_note: Yachtcharter Sweden (Saltsjö Pir), Bavaria 41 per week: mid-July–early August / May; Bavaria Cruiser 46 — €3,700–5,900. Aggregators list older 36–39 ft yachts from ~€1,500 a week
saltsjobaden-stockholm-archipelago.skipper_price_note: Yachtcharter Sweden: €1,950 a week plus food; on 12knots a skipper from ~$2,250 a week
highlights: Midsummer — the midsummer festival, the archipelago full of Swedish boats
White nights (roughly mid-May to late July)
The Gotland Runt offshore race (KSSS, Sandhamn)
school_notes: Charter agency: yachts in Stockholm and Gothenburg with or without a skipper, circular routes around the Stockholm archipelago; advice in Russian
charter base at Moranviken marina, bareboat and catamarans
Bavaria/Dufour bareboat fleet at Saltsjö Pir Marina (Fisksätra), Russian-language page on 12knots
large Bavaria/Hanse fleet at Saltsjö Pir Marina, skippers

bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.description: From Bodrum you head east into the long Gulf of Gökova — with pine-fringed coves, the fishing village of Çökertme, Cleopatra's Island with its golden sand and quiet anchorages at the head of the gulf — or south to ancient Knidos at the tip of the Datça peninsula. Inside the gulf the wind is gentler, while off the exposed peninsula it blows fresh in summer — an area for skippers with some experience.
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.rating_basis: Bodrum is a major yachting and gulet hub on Turkey's Aegean coast; the Gulf of Gökova is valued for its uncrowded pine-fringed coves, Cleopatra's Island and Knidos. Downsides — Bodrum's expensive marinas and a fresh meltemi off the exposed peninsula in July–August.
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.hazards: A strong meltemi and seas off the exposed Bodrum peninsula and in the strait towards Kos; the wind building in the afternoon in the Gulf of Gökova; southerly winds at the start and end of the season; heavy traffic of gulets, ferries and motor yachts around Bodrum; the Greek border (Kos) is close by.
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.crowd_note: In summer Bodrum and Yalıkavak are packed with motor yachts and gulets; at the head of the Gulf of Gökova there are plenty of free coves even in August, though Cleopatra's Island gets crowded during the day.
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.region: Aegean coast: the Bodrum peninsula, the Gulf of Gökova, Cleopatra's Island, Knidos, Datça
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.wind_desc: In summer an afternoon west–north-westerly, usually 10–20 kn; off the exposed Bodrum peninsula and heading out towards Kos the meltemi is noticeably stronger in July–August (up to Force 6–7), while inside the Gulf of Gökova it's gentler. Calm in the morning, dying down by evening. Strong southerlies can blow at the start and end of the season.
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.route: Bodrum — Orak Island — Çökertme — Şehir Adaları (Cleopatra's Island) — Söğüt (head of the gulf) — English Harbour (Değirmenbükü) — Knidos — Bodrum
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.mooring: Milta Bodrum Marina (425 berths) in the centre below the castle is the main base, along with Yalıkavak and Turgutreis; Bodrum's marinas are expensive. In the Gulf of Gökova — restaurant jetties and buoys (usually free if you dine), coves where you anchor with a line ashore, and the fishing village of Çökertme.
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.licence: For bareboat: ICC or RYA Day Skipper (practical) and above; IYT and other licences are accepted at the charter company's discretion together with a sailing CV. Charter companies often require a VHF certificate (SRC). The charter company issues the transit log from the crew list. Visiting Greek Kos on a Turkish charter yacht is usually prohibited by the charter contract.
pros: Uncrowded pine-fringed coves at the head of the Gulf of Gökova
Cleopatra's Island and ancient Knidos
Bodrum airport with plenty of flights
Season from May to October
cons: Expensive Bodrum marinas
A fresh meltemi off the peninsula in July–August
Usually no visiting Greek Kos
Bodrum is noisy and packed in summer
bodrum-gulf-of-gokova.charter_price_note: Sun Odyssey 40.3 (2005, 40 ft, 3 cabins) from Milta marina per week: July–early September ~€4,400, September ~€4,300 / January–March ~€3,300 including mandatory fees (transit log, final cleaning, linen). For comparison, a Sun Odyssey 380 (2022) from Turgutreis — €3,000–3,500 from May to October and €2,000 from November to early April, plus a €300 package. Skipper ~€165 a day plus food; Bodrum is more expensive than Göcek and Marmaris
school_notes: Platform with Russian-speaking skippers and schools: IYT and ISSA courses in Bodrum
Charter aggregator and school with a Russian website: yachts and gulets in Bodrum, Turgutreis, Türkbükü
Bodrum's main marina, 425 berths afloat

fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.description: The Gulf of Göcek with its twelve islands is a sheltered cruising ground of pine-fringed coves, Lycian ruins and restaurant jetties, 20 minutes from Dalaman airport. Short hops and gentle winds suit a first charter and training; from Fethiye you can sail along the open coast to Ölüdeniz, Kalkan and Kaş.
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.rating_basis: The Gulf of Göcek is one of Turkey's best sailing areas: 12 islands, dozens of enclosed coves with pine trees and restaurant jetties, short hops, no tides (12 Knots rates the route from Fethiye as easy). A popular training ground for Russian sailing schools. Downsides — expensive marinas and gulets in the coves in summer.
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.hazards: Gusts of up to 30 kn on the exposed Fethiye — Kaş stretch; thunderstorms and southerlies in spring and autumn; heavy gulet and water-taxi traffic in the coves; anchoring restrictions in some of Göcek's coves; fines for discharging sewage.
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.crowd_note: In July–August the popular coves (Bedri Rahmi, Cleopatra's Baths, Gemiler) are full of gulets and tour boats during the day; it's calmer by evening, and it's best to grab a restaurant berth before 4 p.m.
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.region: Lycian coast: the Gulf of Göcek (Skopea), Fethiye, Ölüdeniz, Kalkan, Kaş
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.wind_desc: In summer a steady afternoon west–north-westerly of Force 3–4 (up to 15–20 kn), calm in the morning; no tides or strong currents. The Gulf of Göcek is well sheltered; the open coast towards Kalkan and Kaş is tougher, with gusts of up to 30 kn. In spring and autumn occasional strong southerlies and thunderstorms, gales in winter.
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.route: Göcek — Yassıca Islands — Bedri Rahmi Bay (Tomb Bay) — Fethiye — Gemiler Island (St Nicholas) — Ölüdeniz — Sarsala — Göcek; eastern option: Fethiye — Soğuksu — Kaş — Kalkan — Ölüdeniz — Binlik — Fethiye, ~97 miles in a week
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.mooring: Göcek has several marinas (D-Marin ~388 berths, Skopea, Göcek Village Port and others) — expensive. In the coves — restaurant jetties and buoys (usually free if you dine at the restaurant) and anchoring with a line ashore; in some coves anchoring is restricted to protect nature. For comparison, a marina in Marmaris costs ~$50 a night. Sewage goes into the holding tank only and is pumped out at a marina (pump-outs are logged, violations are fined).
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.licence: For bareboat: ICC or RYA Day Skipper (practical) and above; IYT and other licences are accepted at the charter company's discretion together with a sailing CV. Charter companies often require a VHF certificate (SRC). The charter company issues the transit log from the crew list (details exactly as in the passports). Visiting the nearby Greek islands (Meis/Kastellorizo, Rhodes) on a Turkish charter yacht is usually prohibited by the charter contract.
pros: Dozens of enclosed coves 2–10 miles apart
Gentle, predictable wind, no tides
Dalaman airport ~20 minutes away
Restaurant jetties — free mooring if you dine
Long season: warm from May to October
cons: Expensive Göcek marinas
Gulets and tour boats in the popular coves
Usually no visiting the nearby Greek islands
Hot in July–August (34 °C)
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.course_price_note: Skipper training from Fethiye with a Russian-speaking instructor — about $1,500 for 10 days including living aboard (according to a T—Zh author's experience), food ~$250 extra
fethiye-gocek-twelve-islands.charter_price_note: Oceanis 40.1 (2022, 41 ft, 3 cabins) from Göcek per week: June–October €3,700–4,400 (September–early October the most expensive) / November–mid-April ~€2,700, late April ~€3,300. Plus a mandatory €200–350 package (transit log, final cleaning, linen); skipper ~€180 a day plus food
school_notes: Charter aggregator and school with a Russian website: yachts in Göcek and Fethiye, cabin cruises
Yacht catalogue for Skopea, D-Marin and Göcek Village Port marinas

marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.description: Marmaris is a major yachting base where the Aegean meets the Mediterranean. Nearby are the enclosed gulfs of Hisarönü and Bozburun, with pine-fringed coves and the villages of Söğüt, Selimiye, Bozburun and Orhaniye, and further on Datça and Serçe. Moderate winds and short hops make the area suitable for a first charter, courses and a relaxed week.
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.rating_basis: The Hisarönü and Bozburun gulfs are classic Turkish sailing: dozens of enclosed coves, restaurant buoys, moderate winds; 12 Knots rates the route as easy. Navily reviews: good moorings at Söğüt, Dirsek and Serçe, but the Orhaniye and Bozburun marinas are expensive.
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.hazards: Southerly winds and thunderstorms at the start and end of the season; limited depth at some jetties (Dirsek); floating litter in popular coves; gulet and jet-ski traffic; fines for discharging sewage — pump-out at a marina only.
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.crowd_note: In summer restaurant berths in the popular coves (Söğüt, Selimiye, Serçe) are taken by evening, with lots of gulets during the day; the coves of Bozburun and Datça are quieter than Göcek.
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.region: Aegean–Mediterranean coast: the Bozburun and Datça peninsulas, Çiftlik, Söğüt, Selimiye, Orhaniye, Serçe
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.wind_desc: In summer the meltemi from the north-north-west: it builds in the afternoon and dies at sunset, rarely over 24 kn. At the start and end of the season southerlies can be stronger. The classic daily rhythm: morning in a cove, set off around noon, sail the passage, anchor by evening.
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.route: Marmaris — Çiftlik — Söğüt — Bozburun — Dirsek — Orhaniye — Bencik — Datça — Serçe Limanı — Marmaris, ~115–140 miles in 7–10 days; in one week people usually stick to the Gulf of Hisarönü
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.mooring: Netsel Marina in central Marmaris is the main base (also Albatros, Yacht Marina, Adaköy); a marina costs ~$50 a night. In the coves — restaurant buoys and jetties with water and electricity (at Söğüt, Bozburun, Dirsek, Serçe), plus free coves to anchor in. Reviews say the Orhaniye and Bozburun marinas are expensive.
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.licence: For bareboat: ICC or RYA Day Skipper (practical) and above; IYT and other licences are accepted at the charter company's discretion together with a sailing CV. Charter companies often require a VHF certificate (SRC). The charter company issues the transit log from the crew list. Visiting the nearby Greek islands (Symi, Rhodes) on a Turkish charter yacht is usually prohibited by the charter contract.
pros: Lots of enclosed coves with restaurant buoys
A moderate meltemi and a steady “morning in a cove, afternoon under sail” rhythm
Wide choice of yachts and schools
Long season from May to October
cons: ~1.5 h to Dalaman airport
Expensive marinas in Orhaniye and Bozburun
Usually no visiting the nearby Greek islands
Hot in July–August
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.course_price_note: RYA Day Skipper (practical) in Marmaris — from €1,050 as a package, Competent Crew — from €1,500, one-day “Start Yachting” — from €270 (InSailing); IYT Bareboat Skipper courses also available — price on request
marmaris-hisaronu-bozburun.charter_price_note: Bavaria C42 (2024, 42 ft, 3 cabins) from Marmaris per week: June–October €4,100–4,300 (most expensive from late August to late October) / mid-November to late April ~€3,200, May ~€3,800. Plus a mandatory €300–350 package (transit log, final cleaning, linen, dinghy); skipper ~€175 a day plus food. Older boats are cheaper
school_notes: Platform with Russian-speaking skippers and schools: RYA and IYT courses in Marmaris and Adaköy
Charter aggregator and school with a Russian website: yachts at Netsel, Albatros, Yacht Marina, Adaköy

key-west-florida-keys.description: A chain of coral islands off southern Florida: from Key West a week's cruise takes you to the deserted Marquesas Keys and to Fort Jefferson on the Dry Tortugas — a reserve with reefs and turtles 70 miles offshore. Passages are long and exposed and the water is shallow, so you need experience; there are few sailboats for charter, mostly catamarans. The season runs from December to May.
key-west-florida-keys.rating_basis: Discover Boating includes south-east Florida with the Keys and the Dry Tortugas among the six best charter areas in the US; Fort Jefferson and the Marquesas Keys are unique anchorages. Downsides: shallow water, long open passages, few sailboats for charter and high prices.
key-west-florida-keys.hazards: Shallows, coral banks and seagrass beds — running aground and damaging coral are fined; shifting sands and shoals around Garden Key; cold fronts with 20–25 kn northerlies; summer thunderstorms and waterspouts; hurricanes June–November; lobster and crab trap buoys (they foul propellers); the Dry Tortugas have no water, fuel or shops.
key-west-florida-keys.crowd_note: Charter yachts are few; Fort Jefferson is busy during the day with ferry and seaplane visitors, but only yachts stay overnight.
key-west-florida-keys.region: Florida Keys: Key West, the Marquesas Keys, the Dry Tortugas
key-west-florida-keys.wind_desc: From November to May easterlies of 10–18 kn prevail, so the return trip from the Dry Tortugas is often a beat or under motor. In winter cold fronts sweep across Florida: after a southerly, a 20–25 kn northerly suddenly kicks in for 1–3 days. Summer brings light winds, heat and afternoon thunderstorms; June to November is hurricane season, with a real risk in August–September.
key-west-florida-keys.route: Stock Island — Marquesas Keys (25 miles) — Garden Key and Fort Jefferson on the Dry Tortugas (40 miles) — Loggerhead Key (6 miles) — Boca Grande Key (50 miles) — Wisteria Island (14 miles) — Stock Island, ~143 miles in a week
key-west-florida-keys.mooring: The base is The Perry Marina on Stock Island (fuel, pump-out). After that you spend the nights at anchor on sand: off the Marquesas (west side only — the east and north are closed as a reserve), off Garden Key next to the fort, off Wisteria. Dry Tortugas National Park fee — $15 per person plus a free boat permit; the dock at the fort is limited to 2 hours. Marina prices in Key West could not be found.
key-west-florida-keys.licence: The US has no official licence for sailing yachts; for bareboat, charter companies (per 12 Knots terms) require an international certificate: IPC/ICC, IYT Bareboat Skipper, RYA Day Skipper or ASA 104 with an IPC, checked in advance.
pros: Dry Tortugas: a 19th-century fort, reefs, snorkelling, turtles
Warm water and sunshine in winter, when the Mediterranean is out of season
Key West with its restaurants and sunsets at Mallory Square
Easy to fly in via Miami
cons: Few sailing yachts; a 42 ft bareboat catamaran costs about $13,200 a week
40–50-mile passages in open water
Shallow water and strict marine reserve rules
June–October — hurricanes and heat
key-west-florida-keys.airport: EYW — Key West, ~10 min; MIA — Miami, ~3.5–4 h by car
key-west-florida-keys.charter_price_note: There are few monohulls in Key West, and they're expensive: on Yachtico a Sun Odyssey 409 (2020) and Sun Odyssey 449 (2016, 4 cabins) start at ~$8,800–9,000 (≈€7,200–7,400) a week — the minimum price including mandatory fees; no seasonal breakdown is published. Catamarans of 38–42 ft there start at ~$4,000–6,400 a week (older Lagoon 380/42), new ones $12,500–16,000. The season is December–May; June–November is hurricane season
key-west-florida-keys.skipper_price_note: Captain $800 a day (Key West), plus food and a separate cabin
school_notes: Aggregator with a Russian-language website: catamarans and motor yachts at The Perry Marina, a route to the Dry Tortugas

st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.description: A chain of small islands between St Vincent and Grenada — one of the Caribbean's best places for a sailing holiday: turtles and reefs in the Tobago Cays, colourful Bequia, exclusive Mustique. Hops are short, but the channels bring strong trades and ocean swell, and navigating among reefs demands attention — an area for experienced or skippered crews.
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.rating_basis: The Tobago Cays, Bequia and Mustique are considered some of the Caribbean's best anchorages; 12knots names February–April as the steadiest time for the Grenadines; sailors love the wildness, the turtles and the water colour; downsides — passages with big seas, limited infrastructure, the aftermath of Hurricane Beryl (2024).
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.hazards: A tricky entrance to Blue Lagoon through the reef (Sunsail advises not to go in), coral heads in the Tobago Cays — enter from the north, not the south; wind acceleration and seas in the channels and off windward shores (keep well off), hurricanes June–November, night navigation prohibited.
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.crowd_note: The Tobago Cays and Salt Whistle Bay are packed with catamarans in December–April, and the best spots are taken before lunch; Canouan and Chatham Bay are quieter.
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.region: Caribbean, Windward Islands: St Vincent, Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Tobago Cays, Mayreau, Union Island
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.wind_desc: East–north-easterly trades of 12–20 kn from December to May, with the steadiest conditions in February–April; in December–January there are “Christmas winds” of 20–25 kn; in the channels between the islands (especially St Vincent — Bequia) the wind and seas are noticeably stronger than at anchor. Late summer and autumn are the peak risk for tropical storms.
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.route: Blue Lagoon — Bequia (Admiralty Bay) — Mustique (Britannia Bay) — Canouan — Tobago Cays — Union Island (Clifton or Chatham Bay) — Mayreau (Salt Whistle Bay) — Bequia — Blue Lagoon, ~100–110 miles in a week
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.mooring: Buoys at Mayreau, in the Tobago Cays and at Union Island — about €25 a night, on Mustique — about €75; Tobago Cays Marine Park fee EC$10 per person per day; elsewhere you anchor for free; arriving from St Lucia or Grenada, clear customs in Bequia or on Union Island (about €35 per adult for yachts from Martinique).
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.licence: No official licence is required — your sailing CV decides; the big companies class the Grenadines as a difficult area — Sunsail requires Level 3 for Grenadines routes from St Lucia and Grenada (at least 20 days or 400 miles as skipper), otherwise a paid skipper. No night sailing.
pros: Tobago Cays — snorkelling with turtles in the marine park
Islands “without crowds or hotels”, colourful villages
Short hops, steady trades
Can be combined with Grenada or Martinique on a one-way route
cons: Strong wind and seas in the channels
Reefs and coral heads, narrow entrances (Blue Lagoon)
Few shops and services, “boat boys”
Hurricane season; Hurricane Beryl badly damaged Union Island, Mayreau and Canouan in July 2024
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.airport: SVD — Argyle (St Vincent), ~20 min to Blue Lagoon; local flights to Bequia, Mustique, Canouan and Union Island
st-vincent-grenadines-blue-lagoon.charter_price_note: Sun Odyssey 419 (2018, 42 ft, 3 cabins) from Blue Lagoon per week: late January–mid-April and Christmas ~$5,400 (≈€4,600), January $4,600–4,950 / July–October ~$3,650 (≈€3,100), May–June and November ~$4,050. Plus a cruising permit of ~$14 per person; other boats at the base add mandatory cleaning and fees of ~$650–770; skipper $225–315 a day plus food and a separate cabin
highlights: Bequia Easter Regatta — the Easter regatta on Bequia
school_notes: Russian-language charter aggregator (website and support in Russian): ~60 boats in Blue Lagoon and on Bequia
Cabins on a catamaran with captain and cook: Bequia, Mayreau, Tobago Cays, Union Island

sylt-westerland-kite.description: Germany's best-known kite island: an open North Sea beach at Westerland that hosts a GKA wave world tour stop every summer. The west side brings surf and strong autumn winds, while the Wadden Sea side in the east has shallow flat water for learning. The water is cold even in summer, so you need a 4/3–5/4 wetsuit.
sylt-westerland-kite.rating_basis: Hosts a GKA Kite World Cup wave stop every summer; Sylt ranks near the top of German kite spot lists (surfertoday, Surf-Magazin)
sylt-westerland-kite.waves_note: In westerly storms, 1–3 m waves in several lines; the Wadden Sea side in the east has shallow flat water
sylt-westerland-kite.hazards: Strong longshore and rip currents in waves, groynes; on the Wadden side, low tide and sandbanks
sylt-westerland-kite.gustiness_note: Frontal sea wind is generally steady, gusty when fronts pass
sylt-westerland-kite.crowd_note: Brandenburger Strand has a zone for surfers and kiters; busy on summer weekends, mostly advanced riders in the waves
pros: Real waves and strong wind, especially in September–October
Flat-water Wadden side for beginners
Resort infrastructure, train from the mainland over the causeway
cons: Cold water: 5/4 wetsuit for most of the season
Windless weeks happen in summer
Expensive accommodation
sylt-westerland-kite.wind_dir: W–SW–NW, onshore / side-onshore; on the Wadden side (Rantum, Munkmarsch) easterlies give flat water
sylt-westerland-kite.airport: GWT — Sylt (Westerland), ~10 min; HAM — Hamburg, ~3 h by train

romo-lakolk.description: One of Europe's widest beaches: at Lakolk you can drive right down to the water, and there is room for everyone. At low tide, shallow lagoons with flat water form — handy for learning — and in westerly wind there is chop and small waves along the shore. The season runs from spring to autumn in a wetsuit; Sylt and the German coast are nearby.
romo-lakolk.rating_basis: Known among Northern European kiters as a huge beach with shallow water; listed among Denmark's spots next to Hvide Sande and Klitmøller
romo-lakolk.waves_note: Shallow flat-water lagoons at low tide; chop and small waves in strong westerly wind
romo-lakolk.hazards: Tides: sandbanks and channel currents at low tide; cars on the beach
romo-lakolk.gustiness_note: Wind off the open sea, steady
romo-lakolk.crowd_note: The beach is 1–2 km wide and tens of kilometres long — it never gets crowded
romo-lakolk.region: Rømø island, Wadden Sea, South Jutland
pros: Huge sandy beach, parking by the water
Shallow and safe for beginners
Kite buggy and land kiting on the sand
cons: Cold water
Tides change the spot within a few hours
Few schools and services
romo-lakolk.airport: BLL — Billund, ~1.5 h; HAM — Hamburg, ~2.5 h

hel-chalupy.description: Poland's kite capital: dozens of schools and campsites line the narrow Hel Peninsula between the open sea and the shallow Bay of Puck. In the bay the water is waist-deep for hundreds of metres from shore — a great place to learn — and in northerly wind advanced riders head to the waves on the sea side. In summer it is one of the busiest kite spots in Europe.
hel-chalupy.rating_basis: Polish and European guides call Chałupy and Jastarnia the best place on the Baltic to learn; dozens of IKO and VDWS schools
hel-chalupy.waves_note: Flat water and light chop in the bay; small waves on the sea side of the peninsula in northerly wind
hel-chalupy.hazards: Crowded water; stones and nets near shore in places, seaweed in summer
hel-chalupy.gustiness_note: Westerlies across the peninsula are gustier, northeasterlies are steady
hel-chalupy.crowd_note: In July–August hundreds of kites on the bay; zones are split between schools
pros: Shallow bay: you can stand far from shore
Lots of schools, rentals and campsites
Wind from both sides of the peninsula — pick your water
cons: Very crowded on the water and the beach in summer
Water is warm only in July–August
Traffic jams on the only road onto the peninsula
hel-chalupy.wind_dir: W–SW and N–NE; side-shore with flat water in the bay

neusiedl-podersdorf.description: The windiest place in Central Europe and Austria's main kite spot: a shallow steppe lake where you can stand almost everywhere. Podersdorf has a kite zone by the beach, schools and a campsite, and hosts the Surf Worldcup in spring. The best flat-water spot for learning and freestyle near Vienna, Bratislava and Budapest.
neusiedl-podersdorf.rating_basis: Home of the annual Surf Worldcup Podersdorf; Austrian and German guides call Neusiedl the country's main kite spot
neusiedl-podersdorf.waves_note: Shallow lake (about 1.5 m): flat water and short chop in strong wind
neusiedl-podersdorf.hazards: Reeds and mud near shore, sudden summer thunderstorms with squalls
neusiedl-podersdorf.gustiness_note: The northwesterly across the plain is moderately gusty
neusiedl-podersdorf.crowd_note: The kite zone fills up on windy weekends, quieter on weekdays
neusiedl-podersdorf.region: Burgenland, steppe lake on the Hungarian border
pros: Shallow and flat — ideal for learning
45 minutes from Vienna
Warm water in summer
cons: Not windy every day, calm spells in summer
Murky water and mud on the bottom
The lake freezes in winter
neusiedl-podersdorf.airport: VIE — Vienna, ~45 min; BTS — Bratislava, ~50 min

gizzeria-hang-loose.description: Italy's windiest summer spot: at the narrowest point of Calabria's 'toe' the wind from the Ionian Sea funnels across the isthmus, and from June to September the thermal blows almost every day. The Hang Loose Beach centre and neighbouring stations sit right next to Lamezia airport; along the shore there is chop and small waves.
gizzeria-hang-loose.rating_basis: Italian guides and thekitemag call Gizzeria Italy's most reliable summer spot; major competitions are held at Hang Loose Beach
gizzeria-hang-loose.waves_note: Chop and small waves up to 1 m in strong wind
gizzeria-hang-loose.hazards: Gets deep quickly near shore; shorebreak in strong wind
gizzeria-hang-loose.gustiness_note: The thermal across the isthmus is steady and predictable, picking up towards midday
gizzeria-hang-loose.crowd_note: Crowded around the centres in August, quieter in June and September
gizzeria-hang-loose.region: Calabria, Gulf of Sant'Eufemia, Tyrrhenian Sea
pros: Thermal wind almost every day in summer
Lamezia Terme airport 5 minutes away
Warm sea and Italian food
cons: Almost no wind in winter
Crowded in August
Untidy beach in places
gizzeria-hang-loose.wind_dir: W–NW thermal across the isthmus, side-onshore

mar-menor-los-narejos.description: Europe's largest saltwater lagoon, separated from the sea by the La Manga sand strip: the water is warm, shallow and almost always flat. One of the best places in Spain for learning and freestyle; there is wind for much of the year, and in winter kiters from all over Europe come here to train. Schools are in Los Narejos, Los Alcázares and on La Manga itself.
mar-menor-los-narejos.rating_basis: Spanish guides call the Mar Menor the country's best lagoon for learning; dozens of schools on yumping and in Los Alcázares
mar-menor-los-narejos.waves_note: The lagoon is closed off by La Manga: flat water, light chop in strong wind
mar-menor-los-narejos.hazards: Jellyfish in summer, rocks near the jetties, swimming-zone buoys
mar-menor-los-narejos.gustiness_note: The thermal and the levante are steady, with no obstacles over the lagoon
mar-menor-los-narejos.crowd_note: Busy around the schools at weekends, but the lagoon is big
mar-menor-los-narejos.region: Murcia, saltwater lagoon on the Mediterranean
pros: Shallow, warm, flat water
Wind almost all year and 300 sunny days
Lots of schools and inexpensive accommodation
cons: Lighter wind than Tarifa — often a big kite is needed
Jellyfish and seaweed in summer
Dense resort development
mar-menor-los-narejos.airport: RMU — Murcia-Corvera, ~25 min; ALC — Alicante, ~1 h

sant-pere-pescador.description: Catalonia's main kite spot: a long beach at the back of the Bay of Roses, where a sea breeze blows almost every day in summer and a powerful tramontana arrives for experienced riders in autumn and winter. Campsites and large centres, including ION Club, line the shore. Barcelona is an hour and a half away, France half an hour.
sant-pere-pescador.rating_basis: Catalonia's main kite spot with the IKO centre ION Club Golf de Roses; Spanish guides put Sant Pere next to Tarifa for windy days
sant-pere-pescador.waves_note: Chop and messy waves in the tramontana, light chop with the summer breeze
sant-pere-pescador.hazards: The tramontana blows offshore and carries you out to sea; gusts up to 40 kn
sant-pere-pescador.gustiness_note: The summer breeze is steady, the tramontana is strong and gusty
sant-pere-pescador.crowd_note: In July–August the beach is full of swimmers; kite zones are marked
pros: Reliable summer breeze and strong tramontana
Big beach, campsites right by the water
Girona and Barcelona nearby
cons: The tramontana is a gusty offshore wind, not for beginners
The beach is packed in summer
Cold water in winter
sant-pere-pescador.wind_dir: N–NW tramontana (side-offshore) and ESE summer breeze 'garbí' (side-onshore)
sant-pere-pescador.airport: GRO — Girona, ~40 min; BCN — Barcelona, ~1.5 h

dubai-kite-beach.description: A city kite beach with a view of the Burj Al Arab: in winter the shamal blows in from the Persian Gulf and a big local community gathers at Kite Beach. The wind does not blow every day, but the water is warm all year round and it is easy to combine with a holiday in Dubai. Riding is allowed only in designated zones.
dubai-kite-beach.rating_basis: A well-known city spot with a large community; ranks lower in world lists because the wind is light and irregular
dubai-kite-beach.waves_note: Chop and small waves up to 1 m in the shamal
dubai-kite-beach.hazards: Swimmers nearby, breakwaters, strong sun; fines for riding outside the zones
dubai-kite-beach.gustiness_note: The shamal is steady, the sea breeze light and unstable
dubai-kite-beach.crowd_note: On windy weekends lots of kiters and wing foilers on the water
pros: Warm water all year
Hotels, city life and direct flights
Russian-speaking instructors available
cons: Irregular wind, often 10–14 kn
Strict rules: ride only in permitted zones
Heat above 40 °C and little wind in summer

walvis-bay-lagoon.description: The legendary Atlantic speed spot: in season the southerly blows 25–35 kn almost every day, and kiters set world speed records on the shallow lagoon and a man-made channel. Around it are the Namib Desert, flamingos and seals, and the water is cold because of the Benguela Current. A place for confident riders who love strong wind.
walvis-bay-lagoon.rating_basis: World centre of speed kiting (Walvis Speed Spot and Lüderitz); wannakitesurf and kitejungle list it among the windiest spots in the world
walvis-bay-lagoon.waves_note: Flat water and chop in the lagoon; waves on the outer spots (Pelican Point, Guns)
walvis-bay-lagoon.hazards: Wind up to 40 kn, cold water, fog; oyster sandbanks in the lagoon
walvis-bay-lagoon.gustiness_note: Thermally boosted trade wind, steady, dying down in the evening
walvis-bay-lagoon.crowd_note: Few kiters even at the peak of the season
pros: Very strong, reliable wind in season
Flat lagoon water for speed and freestyle
Desert, flamingos and Sossusvlei nearby
cons: Cold water 14–17 °C and morning fog
Often too windy for beginners
Far away and expensive to reach
walvis-bay-lagoon.wind_dir: S–SW, side-shore; picks up in the afternoon

rodrigues-mourouk.description: A small island 600 km from Mauritius, where people come for an empty turquoise lagoon and a trade wind that blows almost non-stop from May to November. At Anse Mourouk there is a huge shallow lagoon with flat water, and beyond the reef waves for experienced riders. A kite festival is held here every year, yet there are still only a handful of kiters on the water.
rodrigues-mourouk.rating_basis: French and international guides (tropicalement-votre, InMotion, Air Mauritius) call Rodrigues one of the best and emptiest spots in the Indian Ocean
rodrigues-mourouk.waves_note: A huge lagoon with flat water; waves beyond the reef for experienced riders
rodrigues-mourouk.hazards: Coral heads and shallows at low tide, currents near the reef passes
rodrigues-mourouk.gustiness_note: The trade wind over the open ocean is steady
rodrigues-mourouk.crowd_note: Only a few kites on the lagoon even at peak season
pros: Huge empty lagoon
Strong, steady trade wind from May to November
Quiet island without mass tourism
cons: Long journey — only via Mauritius
Few places to stay and few schools
Coral and shallows at low tide
rodrigues-mourouk.airport: RRG — Rodrigues (Plaine Corail), ~20 min; flights from Mauritius

vilanculos.description: A quiet town on the Mozambican coast from which kiters set off on downwinders and to the sandbanks of the Bazaruto Archipelago with dunes, turquoise water and dugongs. At low tide tens of kilometres of shallows with flat water appear. The wind is most reliable from August to November.
vilanculos.rating_basis: Kitejungle and IKO centres call Vilanculos Mozambique's main kite spot; forums praise the downwinders to the Bazaruto islands
vilanculos.waves_note: At low tide, tens of kilometres of shallows and sandbars with flat water
vilanculos.hazards: Tides up to 3–4 m, currents in the channels, jellyfish; far from medical help
vilanculos.crowd_note: Just a handful on the water, mostly guests of the kite lodges
pros: Huge flat-water sandbanks at low tide
Downwinders and kite safaris to the Bazaruto islands
Hardly any other kiters
cons: Big tides: ride by the tide table
Basic infrastructure and a long journey
Malaria — prophylaxis needed
vilanculos.wind_dir: SE–S and NE depending on the season, side-shore
vilanculos.airport: VNX — Vilanculos, ~10 min; flights from Maputo and Johannesburg

watamu.description: A resort village on Kenya's north coast with a reef-protected lagoon: flat, shallow water at low tide, chop and small waves at high tide. Two monsoons — the kaskazi in winter and the kusi in summer — give two seasons a year. A marine park, the Gede ruins and Malindi are nearby.
watamu.rating_basis: IKsurfmag and kitejungle call Watamu one of Kenya's two main kite spots alongside Diani; several IKO schools
watamu.waves_note: A lagoon behind the reef: flat and shallow at low tide, chop and small waves at high tide
watamu.hazards: Coral reef and sea urchins; the bottom is exposed at low tide
watamu.gustiness_note: The monsoon winds off the ocean are steady
watamu.region: North coast of Kenya, Watamu Marine Park
pros: Two wind seasons a year
Warm lagoon behind the reef
Marine park and inexpensive accommodation
cons: Tides change conditions a lot
Seaweed in the kusi season
Light wind in April and November
watamu.wind_dir: Kaskazi NE (December–March) and kusi SE (June–September), side-onshore
watamu.airport: MYD — Malindi, ~25 min; MBA — Mombasa, ~2 h

south-padre-island.description: Texas's main kite resort: behind the island lies the Laguna Madre, a vast waist-deep shallow with flat water where hundreds of riders kite at the same time. National Geographic has listed South Padre among the world's best kite destinations. The season runs from March to June, when the southeasterly breeze blows almost every day.
south-padre-island.rating_basis: National Geographic listed South Padre among the world's best kite spots; MACkite and kitejungle call it one of the best spots in the USA
south-padre-island.waves_note: Flat, shallow water in the Laguna Madre; small waves on the Gulf side
south-padre-island.hazards: Stingrays and oyster beds in the lagoon (shuffle your feet), boats in the channel
south-padre-island.gustiness_note: The Gulf breeze is steady, especially in spring
south-padre-island.crowd_note: The lagoon is huge; it only gets crowded around the centres at the peak of spring

Reliable spring wind
Warm water and resort infrastructure
cons: Crowds during spring break
Calm spells and heat in summer
A US visa is required
south-padre-island.airport: BRO — Brownsville, ~40 min; HRL — Harlingen, ~50 min

oahu-kailua.description: One of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches and Oahu's main kite spot: the trade wind blows along a turquoise bay, and waves break on the outer reef. Because of swimmers, kiters have their own section of the beach and there are time restrictions. Best from April to September, when the trades are steady.
oahu-kailua.rating_basis: Together with Kanaha on Maui, the best-known kite spot in Hawaii (Fodor's, Oahu guides)
oahu-kailua.waves_note: Chop in the bay, waves on the outer reef
oahu-kailua.hazards: Reef and coral in the shallows, Portuguese man o' war, swimmers
oahu-kailua.gustiness_note: The trade wind is steady, with some gusts near shore due to the terrain
oahu-kailua.crowd_note: Crowded around the kite zone on windy weekends
pros: Steady trade wind most of the year
Warm clear water and reef waves
Honolulu is close by
cons: Zone and time restrictions for kiting
Lots of people on the beach
Expensive

squamish-spit.description: A kite spot among mountains and glaciers: in summer the cold air of the fjord and the warm valley create a thermal that builds to 20–30 kn almost every day. Riders launch from the Spit, a man-made jetty maintained by the local windsports society (entry fee). The water is icy and you need a thick wetsuit, but the view of the Chief and the snowy peaks is unforgettable.
squamish-spit.rating_basis: MACkite and 57hours call Squamish the best kite spot in Canada; the spot is run by the Squamish Windsports Society
squamish-spit.waves_note: Chop at the river mouth and in the fjord, no waves
squamish-spit.hazards: Cold water, the Squamish River current, logs in the water; the society's rescue boat operates at weekends
squamish-spit.gustiness_note: The thermal is steady, but there are gusts and lulls near the jetty and the mountains
squamish-spit.crowd_note: On sunny weekends there is a queue to launch on the jetty
pros: Strong thermal almost every day in summer
Mountain scenery
An hour's drive from Vancouver
cons: Icy water 10–12 °C
River current and tides
Only for confident riders
squamish-spit.wind_dir: S thermal blowing up the fjord, side-shore

los-barriles-kite.description: A village on the east coast of Baja California where kiters and windsurfers gather from November to March for 'El Norte', the northerly wind that blows along the shore. The famous La Ventana is nearby, but the wind here is usually stronger, with chop and small waves along the shore. Schools and hotels sit right on the beach.
los-barriles-kite.rating_basis: One of Baja's classic spots alongside La Ventana; East Cape guides and IKO centres
los-barriles-kite.waves_note: Chop and small wind waves in a strong norte
los-barriles-kite.hazards: Deep water close to shore, shorebreak in strong wind; stingrays and jellyfish
los-barriles-kite.gustiness_note: The winter norte along the coast is steady and stable
los-barriles-kite.crowd_note: Lots of kiters from the USA and Canada in winter, but there is room for everyone
los-barriles-kite.region: Baja California Sur, Gulf of California

Warm Sea of Cortez and whales in season
Relaxed village atmosphere

You need a car
Can be rough for beginners

holbox.description: A car-free island north of Cancún: sandy streets, golf carts and a shallow turquoise sea where you can stand far from shore. Kiters ride off the north beach and in the flat-water Yalahau lagoon, and in summer whale sharks pass nearby. The wind is most reliable from November to May.
holbox.rating_basis: Several IKO schools; Yucatán guides call Holbox the region's main kite spot after Isla Blanca
holbox.waves_note: Shallow sea with flat water and chop; flat water in the Yalahau lagoon
holbox.hazards: Sargassum, shallows and sandbars, boats by the pier
holbox.gustiness_note: The trade wind off the sea is steady
pros: Shallow warm water, easy to learn
Car-free island atmosphere
Whale sharks and flamingos

Weaker wind and hurricane season in summer
Getting there: car plus ferry
holbox.airport: CUN — Cancún, ~2.5 h + ferry from Chiquilá

bonaire-atlantis.description: A Dutch island off the coast of Venezuela, known for a trade wind that blows almost all year and crystal-clear water. Kiters ride at Atlantis Beach in the southwest: the wind comes off the low, flat shore, so it is steady and the water is smooth; schools back up students with a boat. On windless days the diving is excellent.
bonaire-atlantis.rating_basis: In the kitesurfingofficial top 25 and other world lists; famous for a steady trade wind almost all year
bonaire-atlantis.waves_note: The wind blows off the shore — smooth water near the beach, light chop further out
bonaire-atlantis.hazards: The offshore wind carries you out to sea; coral near the shore
bonaire-atlantis.gustiness_note: The trade wind over the low, flat island is steady

Smooth water and a clear sea
World-class diving on windless days

union-island-clifton.description: A small Grenadine island where kiters ride a turquoise lagoon behind the reef off the town of Clifton, with a view of the Tobago Cays. The trade wind is steady from December to June, and the local JT Pro Center and kite cruises around the Grenadines have made the island well known. It is a convenient base for catamaran trips to the neighbouring islands.
union-island-clifton.rating_basis: IKsurfmag, InMotion and Yachting Magazine call Union Island the main kite spot of the Grenadines
union-island-clifton.waves_note: A flat-water lagoon behind the reef; waves on the reef
union-island-clifton.hazards: Reef and coral, boats in Clifton harbour
union-island-clifton.gustiness_note: The trade wind off the Atlantic is steady
union-island-clifton.crowd_note: Small community, plenty of space on the water

Kite cruises around the islands

Hurricane season in autumn
union-island-clifton.airport: UNI — Union Island, ~5 min; flights from St Vincent and Barbados

icarai-de-amontada.description: A quiet fishing village on Ceará's kite route between Cumbuco and Jericoacoara: a long empty beach, a steady trade wind and good waves for wave riding. People come here for the calm that Jeri no longer has, and as a stop on downwind tours along the coast. The season runs from July to January.
icarai-de-amontada.rating_basis: A must-stop on Ceará downwinders; Brazilian and French guides call Icaraí a 'kite paradise'
icarai-de-amontada.waves_note: Good waves for wave riding off the point, chop near the shore
icarai-de-amontada.hazards: Shorebreak and currents, rocks in places
icarai-de-amontada.gustiness_note: The trade wind off the ocean is steady and strong in the second half of the year

Empty beaches and peace and quiet

noumea-anse-vata.description: The city beach of New Caledonia's capital, where the trade wind blows much of the year and almost every day from September to December. Kiters ride in Anse Vata bay and head out to Îlot Maître in the middle of one of the world's largest lagoons, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Cafés and all of Nouméa's infrastructure are close by.
noumea-anse-vata.rating_basis: Kitejungle and French guides call Anse Vata New Caledonia's main kite spot
noumea-anse-vata.waves_note: Chop in the bay, flat lagoon water near Îlot Maître
noumea-anse-vata.hazards: Coral shallows, boats and swimmers in the bay
noumea-anse-vata.gustiness_note: The trade wind over the lagoon is steady
noumea-anse-vata.crowd_note: On windy weekends the bay fills with local kiters and wing foilers

Huge UNESCO-listed lagoon
City with French cuisine nearby

French prices
